# Gates and environment variables (Railway)

One entry per documented `GATE_*` flag or env var family (not every variable has a paragraph, but every `GATE_*` the code reads has a line in the generated `docs/gate-index.md`): its default, where it is read, what on and off do, and how to kill it. Moved out of `CLAUDE.md` so it is read on demand instead of loading into every session.

Look a variable up by name (`grep -n 'GATE_NAME' docs/gates-and-env.md docs/gate-index.md`); each entry is one paragraph on one line. Add or change an entry in the same PR that adds or changes the variable.

Every dark `GATE_*` owes the same contract, which the entries below state as "Off = byte-identical": with the gate off the feature renders nothing, requests nothing, persists no new column or JSON key, and adds no row to a customer-facing document, and unsetting the variable restores the previous behavior exactly. Check the gate on EVERY path the feature reaches, not just the one that renders it. A gate read on the render path while the write path persists regardless leaves data behind that an ungated surface then consumes, so the documented kill switch no longer kills: saved-property coordinates persisted with `GATE_LAWN_RECLAIMED_HALF_N` unset (`server/services/customer-properties.js`, where scheduling and route-location resolution then read them), rule-derived classification keys the ungated Bank Import tab kept acting on after `GATE_TAX_LEDGER` was unset (`server/services/tax-ledger-rules.js`), and a `final_exterior_*` row added to a gate-off certificate. A control the gate should hide must be hidden by a server-provided, fail-closed capability rather than a client-only check.

Tips with facts (dark): `GATE_TECH_TIP_SOURCES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`server/config/feature-gates.js` `techTipSourcesLive`, read by `server/services/complete-scheduled-service.js` at the tips freeze and by `server/services/service-report/report-data.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, a library tip that names fact-register sources (`sources` in `server/services/service-report/tip-library.js`; the facts live in `server/services/email-division/fact-register-data.js`, knowledge-base only) freezes its `sourcedCopy` (else its copy) and `citations: [{ label, url }]`, and the live report's tech note prints each label as a link after the sentence, inside the quote, never the raw URL, after report-data re-checks the URL against the tip library's host rule. A fact past its `expiresOn` gives no citation, and the tip-library lint fails on it. The same gate matches the picker to the yard (`server/services/service-report/tech-tip-yard.js`, read from the visit address and the turf profile): a tip's `yard` filter (`grass`, `irrigation: 'system'`, `county`, `city`, `water` — the sprinklers' source as saved for this home, e.g. `reclaimed`) and `showMonths` leave out tips that do not fit; grass needs a trusted grass (staff or estimate set it, never a photo read), county and city need a known one (a straddling ZIP or city is unknown), an irrigation tip hides only where the yard is known to have no system, and the response carries a one-line `yard` summary. The same gate drives the office Complete Service form (owner 2026-10-24, decisions 2 and 6): the tips response adds `tipSources: true` and `blogPosts` (tip id → the live hub post its `blog.path` names, from `tipBlogPosts` in `report-blog-post.js`, never a post titled for one town); picking such a tip fills an empty blog slot ("Filled from the tip"; a restored draft or a post already picked wins, removing the tip keeps the post), each picked tip's chip prints its source labels, the field prints "Matched to this yard", the blog card offers Change, and a lawn visit gets the blog search (tree, shrub & palm still never ask). Off, the form is as before. A tip whose subject no such post covers may carry `blog.topic` instead; `server/scripts/seed-tech-tip-blogs.js` (tech-tip-blog-seeder, decision 3) lists every tip with a topic and what the blog queue would answer (a dry run, the default), and `--only <tipId,...> --execute` queues at most five a run through the office's own Suggest a post path (same checks, except that a post titled for one town never counts as covering a tip's subject; rows carry `signal_metadata.tech_tip_id` and `general_title`, which the brief turns into a title rule for the writer and the quality gate enforces with the hard `general_title` check). Writes are governed by GATE_BLOG_SEARCH_SUGGEST, the queue's own switch, not this gate. Tips written for this feature carry `sourcedOnly: true` (owner 2026-10-24, part 4): with the gate off the picker never lists or searches them and the freeze drops them, so none of their words reach a report until the gate flips; with it on they are likewise dropped from the day a fact they cite passes its `expiresOn` (`tipAvailable`; a freeze reports such a pick as `unknown_tip`). Off, the freeze and the report are byte-identical to before and frozen citations do not print. Owner 2026-10-24.

Inventory agent (dark): `GATE_INVENTORY_AGENT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`server/services/purchase-receipts/inventory-agent.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Requires `GATE_PURCHASE_RECEIPT_RESTOCK` ALSO on and a valid, offset-bearing `PURCHASE_RECEIPT_SINCE` — with either missing, the agent does nothing (`skipped: 'no_since'`/`'gated'`) exactly like the deterministic receipt sweep it rides behind. On, it resolves a `purchase_receipt_lines` row the deterministic sweep could only hand off (`agent_pending`: unmatched / needs_size / size_mismatch) with one bounded LLM call per line, then validates every number the model proposes against the purchased title in plain code before writing anything (`validateReading` / `validateExisting` / `validateNewProduct`) and applies in one transaction. Read fresh on every 15-minute scheduler tick (`server/services/scheduler.js`), right after the deterministic sweep — no redeploy needed to flip it. Kill behavior: unsetting the gate does NOT strand queued lines — the same scheduler tick calls `drainAgentQueue` instead, which restores every `agent_pending` line to the status it would have held WITHOUT the agent (its recorded `handoffFrom`, or `unmatched` when that's missing), ringing the same "not added" bell the deterministic sweep would have for `needs_size`/`size_mismatch`. Undo one agent-logged line (reverses the stock movement, restores an EXISTING product's container_size/inventory_unit/inventory_on_hand/default_unit, deletes an agent-created alias, never deactivates an agent-created product): `railway run --service Postgres node ops/agents/inventory-agent-undo.js --line=<id|8-char-prefix>` (dry run; add `--execute` to apply) — refuses when the product row or anything referencing it (a service's COGS mapping, a visit's applied product, a protocol, a restock request, …) changed since the agent's decision.

Pre-treat sticker report (ON in production since 2026-10-22): `GATE_PRETREAT_STICKER_REPORT` — off unless exactly `true` (`server/config/feature-gates.js` `pretreatStickerReport`, read at boot; served by `server/routes/reports-public.js` project `/data` and the admin project detail (`pretreat_sticker_report`, for the staff preview), which sends `pretreatStickerReport` only for `pre_treatment_termite_certificate`). On: the certificate page renders the Notice of Termite Protection label (form WV-001) with its blanks filled, then a "Treatment Record Details" block with the certificate fields the label has no blank for (`TermiteNoticeSticker` + `CertificateOfCompliance detailsOnly` in `client/src/pages/ProjectReportViewPage.jsx`). Off: today's field-grid Certificate of Compliance. Look only: the gate changes the layout, not data, send readiness or messages. Since #6490 (2026-10-23), independent of this gate: both layouts print a recorded final exterior treatment, and a staff send needs a lawful warranty choice and a clock-time `treatment_time` (the `final_exterior_*` fields never gate the send). Turning the gate off restores only the old layout, not the old send rules. Kill: unset (the variable change redeploys).

Autonomous editorial evidence: `GATE_EDITORIAL_EVIDENCE=true` enables mandatory answer plans, independent review/repair, and signed final-article evidence. Ships dark. `EDITORIAL_REVIEW_PRIVATE_KEY` (Ed25519 PEM/base64 DER) is restricted to the publisher/trusted reviewer; `EDITORIAL_REVIEW_PUBLIC_KEY` is shared with Astro validation. Setup, automated calibration, retry behavior, and coordinated activation are in `docs/autonomous-editorial-evidence.md`.

Astro brand-isolation merge guard: `ASTRO_REQUIRE_BRAND_ISOLATION` — default on; `false` disables it. Read in `server/services/content-astro/astro-publisher.js` (`assertBrandIsolationClear`). On, every portal merge of an astro PR (autonomous poller, internal-link lane, scheduler `mergeAstro` except unpublish PRs) waits for the astro repo's `brand-isolation` job to succeed on the PR head, read via the Actions API (the content token cannot read check-runs). It is not a `GATE_*` variable.

Voice relay manual eval: `npm run eval:voice-relay` runs the synthetic fixture through Sandy's live conversation loop in a dedicated CLI process, with deterministic grading and refused conversation database access. Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `--only=<id,...>` selects scenarios and `--fixture=<path>` supplies a custom fixture. Optional `--judge` grades completed transcripts through `TEXT_POLICIES.voiceJudge` (`MODEL_VOICE_JUDGE` pins the Anthropic primary; the registered OpenAI fallback is advisory). Judge calls may write ordinary LLM ledger/trace rows when their gates are on. Manual runs retry a failed scenario set once and send no notifications unless `--notify` is present. `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_EVAL` explicitly opts in (all environments) to Monday 03:50 America/New_York, under the existing exclusive cron lock and in a child process with `--judge --notify`; default off. Repeated failures or an inconclusive run use the existing admin regression bell and ops digest/email, controlled by `EVAL_REGRESSION_EMAIL` (`off` disables the email/digest channel). Rubric and fixture contracts: `docs/voice-quality-rubric.md`.

Lawn property history: `GATE_LAWN_PROPERTY_HISTORY` — dark in every environment; read with `gateEnvValue` once per operation. On, confirmed history resolves per property and visit, with reset windows, transactionally installed baselines, and history-bound PDF pins. Unset restores legacy readers and the insert-time baseline rule; baseline flags written while enabled remain. The property columns and proven visit-link stamping are additive and ungated.

Intelligence Bar record a payment: `GATE_IB_RECORD_PAYMENT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibRecordPaymentLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`. Owner ruling 2026-10-12 ("yes to all recommendations", Stage 3 purpose-built cards: "record payment"). On, the bar offers `record_payment` (admin only, platform path, customers / Invoices / dashboard pages and discovery, always a confirm card, never owner-direct, an `external_action`): it records money ALREADY RECEIVED outside the portal (cash, check, Zelle, Venmo, PayPal, other) against one open invoice by running the Invoices page's own Record payment handler (`POST /api/admin/invoices/:id/record-payment`) in process (`recordPaymentFromBar`, `server/routes/admin-invoices.js`, the `send_invoice` adapter pattern) with exactly the carded body. **It never charges a card, creates a Stripe payment, refunds or voids**: refunds and charging a saved card stay closed. The screen has no amount and no date field and settles the WHOLE amount due as of now, so `amount` must equal the balance due (an overpayment, a negative amount, a card method and a date other than today are refused; a partial payment is refused unless `GATE_IB_RECORD_PAYMENT_PARTIAL` and `GATE_PARTIAL_PAYMENTS` are both on). The card lists every change (invoice paid, ledger row, payment plan completed, reminders stop, an open pay-page card session cancelled, a billing pause that can clear, the linked visit a closeout completes, a review enrolment) and that no receipt is sent. **The card sends no receipt:** `record_payment` takes no receipt option (`send_receipt` is refused as `capability_unimplemented`: "record_payment does not send receipts; after recording, use resend_receipt or the Invoices page"), and the shim always hands the Invoices page handler `sendReceipt=false`. A receipt is a separate act with its own card and queue rules (`resend_receipt`, or the Invoices page); the receipt-queue review rounds on #6380 (take-over after a guarded claim, uncertain provider outcomes) are closed by removing the option, not by guarding it. Refused: paid / prepaid / void / refunded / canceled / processing invoices, payer-billed or statement-held invoices, annual-plan invoices, nothing due, a cancelled or no-show visit. The invoice's status and edit time, the amount due, the method / reference / note and the visit are pinned; any change before Confirm refuses with `preview_changed`, and the settlement (`recordManualPayment`, `expectedAmountCents` + `settlementFence` + `requireSelfPay`) enforces the edit time before the Stripe retirement and the status, the customer, visit link, service record, payer links, amount due and self-pay ownership on the LOCKED invoice row in the same transaction as the paid flip; the Invoices page sends none of these. The settlement also re-proves, only for the card (a `settlementFence` from `server/services/intelligence-bar/record-payment-fences.js`, run before the Stripe retirement and again under the invoice lock; the invoice notes are built from the locked row so a concurrent note edit is never erased): no annual-prepay term, the customer on the invoice, and (the ET day the card showed and the visit its closeout would complete (its edit time, scheduled date and service type, and that no job timer has started on it: the closeout's own `visitJobTimerRunning`) are re-asserted by the fence (a card shown before midnight ET refuses after it; an edited or missing visit refuses), and that visit (or none) is pinned, with the facts the card showed (service type, scheduled date, status, edit time), in the settlement transaction and handed to the closeout as its approved target and visit; the closeout re-asserts the facts on the locked visit row (`approved_visit_changed`), so a visit that became closable, or was edited, rescheduled, reclassified or cancelled, after the card is left open on the first run and on the retry sweep, the payment stays recorded, and the result says "the visit changed since the card; the payment is recorded, close the visit from its page"). Flip: `GATE_IB_RECORD_PAYMENT=true` (with `GATE_IB_PLATFORM` on). Rollback: unset it.

Intelligence Bar record part of a bill: `GATE_IB_RECORD_PAYMENT_PARTIAL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibRecordPaymentPartialLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-28/29 ("the bar should do what the Invoices page does"; partial payment was gap 8, plan approved "all"). It needs `GATE_IB_RECORD_PAYMENT` (which needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`) AND `GATE_PARTIAL_PAYMENTS`; with any of them off, `record_payment` refuses an amount below the balance due as before (`partial_not_supported`). On, `record_payment` accepts an amount LESS than the balance due. Everything else about the tool stays: admin only, always a confirm card, never owner-direct, no receipt from the bar, never a card charge. The card states the invoice, the customer, the method and reference, "Part payment of $X; $Y will still be owed", that the invoice stays open and its reminders continue, that no receipt goes out, and the amount owed it priced from. That amount owed and the part are pinned in the card's version; Confirm re-derives the card and refuses `preview_changed` on any drift (another part or credit moved the amount owed, an edit, a payer, a closed gate). The preview runs the Invoices page's own part refusals (`partPaymentRefusal` in `server/services/invoice-manual-payment.js`: payer-billed, an active payment plan, an unsettled card dispute, an annual prepay invoice, an Auto Pay customer, all fail closed), so they show on the card in the writer's words (`part_not_allowed`). The commit calls the SAME writer, `recordManualPayment`, through the same handler (`recordPaymentFromBar`), with `amountCents` and `owedCentsSeen` taken from the card's own pin (never from a request body, so a body `amount` is still dropped) plus an internal marker `barApprovedPart: true` that only the route's `cardPinsOf` sets from that approval. The writer allows a fenced part ONLY with that marker, both gates, the card's settlement fence, the self-pay re-proof, never `automated`, and `expectedAmountCents` equal to `owedCentsSeen` (so the under-lock fence compares the live amount owed with the card's, not with the part); the Zelle reconciler and notice Apply (`automated`, `expectedAmountCents`) and any other caller are still refused. The settlement fence keeps every check it has (edit time, status, customer, visit link, service record, payer links, money columns including `amount_paid`, the ET day, annual-plan term); a part carries no closeout visit. The writer's `owedCentsSeen` fence refuses a second Confirm of the same card (it meets a different amount owed), so one part is booked once. A part is not a settlement: no paid flip, no receipt, no reminder stop, no review ask, no visit closeout, no billing-pause clear, no plan completion; it adds the amount to `invoices.amount_paid`, writes one `payments` row and the same markers Undo (`GATE_UNDO_MANUAL_PAYMENT`) works from. Overpayment and a date other than today stay refused. Off = the bar behaves exactly as before. Kill switch: unset.

Appointment address choice: `GATE_EDIT_APPT_ADDRESS` — off unless exactly `true`, read per request via `isEnabled('editApptAddress')` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, the office chooses which of a customer's saved properties a visit is at: the Schedule screen's New Appointment "Service address" picker and the Edit-appointment address dropdown (`server/routes/admin-schedule.js`, `customer-properties.bookingPropertyStamp`), the customer page's change-address control, the Intelligence Bar's `switch_appointment_property`, and (2026-10-28) the bar's `create_appointment` `property_id`: a named property's address is pinned on the confirmation card and re-read under the booking lock (a change after the card refuses with `preview_changed`), and a customer with two or more active properties and none named is asked which one (`property_choice_required`, no card). Off = none of these offer a choice, `create_appointment` refuses a `property_id`, and a booking keeps the sole-active-property anchor (a customer with several properties gets no property on the visit; the office places it). Rollback: unset it.

Intelligence Bar convert a lead: `GATE_IB_LEAD_CONVERT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibLeadConvertLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`. Owner ruling 2026-10-12 ("yes to all recommendations", Stage 3 purpose-built cards). On, the bar offers `convert_lead` (admin only, platform path, always a confirm card, never owner-direct): it runs the Leads page's own Convert to Customer handler (`POST /api/admin/leads/:id/convert`, `convertLeadFromBar` in `server/routes/admin-leads.js`) in process with the operator identity. The screen links a lead to an EXISTING customer you name; it creates no customer and has no duplicate check, so the card does the matching read-only (the customer's phone and email against the lead's, and other customers that share them). The handler writes the lead only: status won, converted date, qualified, the customer link, the monthly / first-service value and WaveGuard tier you gave, a `converted` row on the lead's activity list, the lead's ad funnel row (to booked, when one exists), and the lead's estimates with no customer yet (its linked one, or every one tagged with the lead's id; the card lists them by id) are attached to the customer. The ad funnel row moves only when below booked, and a row already owned by another customer is not relinked. It sends NO text, email or call, books nothing, charges nothing, accepts no estimate and changes no autopay; the card says so. The lead (status, edit time, contact, links, values), the customer (name, phone, email, address), the estimates and funnel rows listed, and every figure on the card are pinned and re-asserted in the conversion's own UPDATE (the handler answers 409 on any difference); a change before Confirm refuses with `preview_changed`. Known limit: a customer edit in a column the card did not show still attaches to the same customer id. A lead already converted, a repeat quote-wizard lead (its conversion also settles the original lead's funnel row), and a preferred-time request with no funnel row (converting it creates one) are refused: convert those from the Leads page. After the commit the tool reads back the estimates attached and the funnel rows; anything the card promised that did not happen returns a partial result naming it, never success. Off = the tool is not offered and refuses every call. Rollback: unset the variable.

Intelligence Bar model failure notice: `GATE_IB_MODEL_FAILURE_NOTICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibModelFailureNoticeLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner request 2026-10-20, after the Anthropic monthly limit left a 2026-10-19 ask with no answer, no gap and no alert. On, a failed model call in `/admin/intelligence-bar/query` (a provider 4xx/5xx, a timeout, an overload) answers 200 with a plain reply: what failed in one sentence, whether any change was saved (read from the task's saved receipts; a saved or unknown change is named and `nothing was changed` is never claimed), and `try again in a few minutes`. The task ends `failed` (resumable) when nothing ran, `awaiting_approval` when a card is waiting, `outcome_unknown` when a change was saved or may have run. It records one gap row (source `ib-model`, kind `blocked`, code = the ledger's error code; no gap bell and no auto-build pickup, which only claims `intelligence-bar` and `tech-bar` rows) and posts one admin bell (`agents`, key `ib:model-failure`, rolling 1-hour window). It sends nothing to a customer. Off = the error reaches the error handler and the task is marked `outcome_unknown`, as before.

Intelligence Bar void an invoice: `GATE_IB_VOID_INVOICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibVoidInvoiceLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`. Owner ruling 2026-10-12 ("yes to all recommendations", Stage 3 purpose-built cards, "void" included). On, the bar offers `void_invoice` (admin only, platform path, always a confirm card, never owner-direct): it runs the Invoices page's own Void handler (`POST /api/admin/invoices/:id/void`, `voidInvoiceFromBar` in `server/routes/admin-invoices.js`) in process with the operator identity, so every refusal and rule is the route's own (`InvoiceService.voidInvoice`). The handler writes: the invoice becomes void; its payment-reminder sequence stops; account credit applied to it returns to the customer's balance; a payer statement that is still open drops it from its total; the invoice's own UNCONFIRMED Stripe PaymentIntent (no payment attempted) is cancelled. It sends NO text, email or call, changes no visit, and charges or refunds nothing; the Invoices page can restore a voided invoice to a draft. Money stays on the Invoices page (owner rule: refunds and charging a saved card stay closed): the card refuses with code `by_owner_rule` any invoice with money received or in flight (paid, processing, refunded, a payment recorded, a payment or Stripe charge on file, a PaymentIntent that is not unconfirmed or canceled, an unresolved saved-card attempt, a deposit already collected, a finalized payer statement, a payment plan), and with code `needs_invoices_page` the invoices whose void also unwinds other state (annual plan, membership dues, bait-station setup fee, a shared combined payment, a queued pay-link text). The invoice (status, edit time, total, credit, PaymentIntent and its Stripe status, statement, lines, visit) is pinned; any change before Confirm refuses with `preview_changed`, and `voidInvoice({ expected })` enforces the same pin on the row it reads (before any Stripe call) and as extra predicates on its own UPDATE; the page sends none (tested byte-identical). Tests: `server/tests/intelligence-bar-void-invoice.test.js`, `server/tests/admin-invoices-void-handler-replay.test.js`. Kill: unset `GATE_IB_VOID_INVOICE`.
Intelligence Bar schedule a text: `GATE_IB_SCHEDULE_SMS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibScheduleSmsLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`. **It texts a customer later, so flipping it is the owner's call.** Owner ruling 2026-10-28 (gap 5, and B1 below). On, the bar offers `schedule_sms` (admin only, platform path, always a confirm card on every login including the owner's, never owner-direct): one plain text to one customer's own number at one day and time. It runs the Communications page's own schedule handler (`POST /api/admin/communications/schedule-sms`) through the shared writer `scheduleCustomerSms` in `server/services/scheduled-sms-queue.js`, which the route now calls too and answers unchanged: every route guard (translation trial, applicant texts, explicit customer context, street-level hold, marketing and retention refusal, immediate-only link refusal, Waves from number, Agent Review draft claim, future time) and the one transaction under the suggest-thread lock. The bar never sends an Agent Review draft, reply context, linked visit or translation trial. The card shows the exact text, the customer, the number's last four digits (masked like the send_sms card), the From number, and the send day and time in words in Eastern Time ("Thursday, October 30 at 10:00 AM"). It pins the customer id, the number, the From number, a digest of the text and the send time; Confirm re-checks them, and inside the writer's lock re-reads the customer's phone, and refuses with `preview_changed` on any change with nothing written. A repeated Confirm queues one text, and an identical text already queued counts only when the bar could list and cancel it (the shared standalone rule `list_queued_messages` uses): a match tied to another workflow, such as an Agent Review decision from the Communications page, is refused with code `queued_text_not_cancelable` and nothing is written. The queued row is the page's own shape, so `list_queued_messages` lists it and `cancel_queued_message` cancels it. That promise holds only while no Agent Review suggestion is pending on the customer's thread (the writer would park it and stamp `parked_decision_ids` on the text, which the bar's list and cancel refuse), so the card is refused with code `suggestion_pending` while one waits, and Confirm re-checks inside the writer's lock; the operator handles the suggested reply on the Communications page first. **B1 time rule (owner 2026-10-28, binding), as the dispatcher really behaves:** a time from the bar between 8:00 PM and 8:00 AM Eastern is REFUSED and the bar asks for a time from 8 AM to 8 PM, because the bar is mostly voice and "at 9" can mean 9 AM or 9 PM. The scheduled-text sender (`scheduler.js`, node-cron every five minutes at minutes ending in 0 or 5) sends a queued operator text at the first run on or after its time and does not check quiet hours for operator rows, so a text for 10:01 goes at 10:05 and a text for 7:59 PM would go at 8:00 PM, at night; node-cron here also drops a tick under load. So the bar accepts **8:00 AM Eastern through 7:45 PM Eastern, inclusive**, and refuses 7:46 PM and later and midnight to 7:59 AM. 7:45 PM goes at the 7:45 run and still leaves before 8:00 PM if the 7:45 and 7:50 runs are both missed (7:55 is the third); 7:50 PM would survive only one missed run. 8:00 AM is the first accepted minute because a run never sends before the time. The refusal says this rule, and the card says the text "goes out on the first five-minute check on or after" the time (within about 5 minutes after it, never before), not at that exact minute. The dispatcher is unchanged. The Communications page keeps its behavior (it may schedule any minute), and "send now" at night is not part of this tool. The text sends from the scheduled-SMS cron at that minute, subject to the send path's own consent and suppression checks. **Security tightening that is NOT behind this gate (applies to the Communications page too):** the shared writer now runs the immediate send's own commit-phase link verification (`customerLinkSendRefusal`, `bearerSeamCheck` included) inside its thread lock, before the insert. A text that carries a link built for another customer (appointment page, service report, receipt, pay, estimate, and the other bearer links the immediate path verifies), or a link that matches no customer, is refused (409; 503 when the check cannot be read) with that check's own wording, and nothing is queued. Why: the scheduled-text dispatcher replays a queued row with no link check, so before this the page and the bar could queue another account's bearer link and the cron would deliver it. The dispatcher runs the same check again right before it sends a queued operator text (`scheduledLinkRefusal` in `server/services/scheduled-sms-delivery.js`, not behind a gate), so a row queued before the writer's check shipped, or whose customer's phone changed after queueing, cannot deliver another customer's link. It covers rows with no `metadata.entry_point`, which is every row the writer queues; system deferrals (quiet-hours holds and the other replays, each registered under an `entry_point`) are not checked, because they build their own links and have their own rechecks. A definite refusal is not sent: the row ends `blocked` with `metadata.blocked_code` `CUSTOMER_LINK_REFUSED` and `blocked_reason` set to the check's code, and the office gets one bell (category `alert`, Comms, dedupe key `scheduled-sms-link-refused:<row id>`, customer's first name and last initial only, never the text or a number) that links to the customer's thread. A check that cannot be read (the check's own "try again" refusal) returns the row to the bounded three-attempt retry rail with no alert, and the last attempt ends it blocked with the same alert. The bar also runs the same check when it builds the card. Off = the tool is not offered and not executable; the page route is otherwise as before.
Intelligence Bar Agent Review drafts: `GATE_IB_AGENT_REVIEW_DRAFTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibAgentReviewDraftsLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`. Round 45: a row's identity is service + name (its amount is reconciled, never keyed), so a mirror stating only its net meets its gross copy; an explicit setup row is read as the fee (waived at $0, no cached fallback) and never as work; an unreadable email opt-out says retry, never send by hand. Round 46: a blank higher amount alias never hides the accepted net below it; explicit setup rows are read from every container the extractor reads. Round 47: mirrored setup rows reconcile by net precedence (manual net, then sold-net alias over a same-gross copy) before a fee conflict. Round 48: a same-scope raw twin outranks an exact-amount twin whose stated scope differs. Round 49: the card classifies taxability with the canonical service_taxability table (loaded in the accept transaction); a frozen website-quote setup fee (setupFeeQuote.amount) is the fee line when no row and no cached fee exist. Round 50: a mapped manual net of 0 beside a twin's different manual net is a conflict; the visits line and the accepted message tell staff to schedule every visit of a one-time package. Round 51: a raw installation mirror reconciles taxability with its listed mapped copy (contradiction refuses; a one-sided explicit flag rides on); a same-gross raw twin outranks the first same-service row. Round 52: a non-numeric placeholder alias never hides an accepted zero; one_time.total is read as an aggregate; the tax note names commercial and business properties. Round 53: the visits line names every new recurring service to book; the fee line carries taxability (explicit setup-row flag, else the canonical default; disagreeing flags refuse). Round 54: the visits line names every one-time job; repeated same-price installations pair with their mapped copy by scope first. Round 55: the taxability-table read runs in a savepoint inside the accept transaction. Round 56: installations with two different stated scopes are two charges; a recurring accept naming no service refuses (`recurring_unnamed`); the card shows the service address (linked property, else the estimate snapshot). Round 57: the taxability read rejects inside its savepoint (fallback taken outside); a standalone installation line carries the row's scope. Round 58: the service address is pinned (`propertyPin`, re-checked under the accept's locks); clearing a saved lawn measurement is a card line. Round 59: a comped mapped row claims its own explicit-zero raw twin first; a manual-net twin is claimed by gross and scope, never any same-service row. Round 60: a one-time-only accept's visits line names only the one-time work; the converter's success log is labelled DRY RUN on a card preview. Round 61: twin rows match on any shared name (service key or display label); a legacy `oneTimePrice` mirror is a gross copy, never a second sold net. Round 62: rows that both carry a service key pair by that key alone; a shared label is the identity only when a side has none.
Intelligence Bar compose a new email: `GATE_IB_COMPOSE_EMAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibComposeEmailLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`. Owner ask 2026-10-28 (IB gap #9). **It emails a person, so turning it on is the owner's flip.** On: the bar's `compose_email` (`server/services/intelligence-bar/compose-email-tools.js`) sends ONE new email (not a reply) to ONE recipient, a customer on file (customer_id, the email on file) or any single address the operator names, on a confirm card every time, on every admin login, the owner's included (it is not on the owner-direct list; technician contexts never see it). Confirm runs `sendEmailMessage` (`server/services/email/send-message.js`), the same shared function the Email page's Send (`POST /admin/email/send`) calls: one Gmail message from the office mailbox (`GMAIL_USER_EMAIL`, From "Waves Pest Control"), a new thread, plain text sent as HTML with the page composer's own escaping (`encodeEmailBody`). The route adds no signature, attachment, tracking or unsubscribe link, saves no copy, links nothing to a customer and runs no suppression or opt-out check; the card says so. The card shows To (name and address), From, the subject and the exact body; those, plus the customer link and a digest of the body, are pinned, and Confirm re-derives them and refuses with `preview_changed` on any drift, then sends exactly the carded fields. A double Confirm never sends twice: the pending card is claimed by one atomic update, and the executor refuses a second run of the same operation. A portal link to a customer's account in the body (appointment, report, receipt, payment, estimate) is refused, as `send_email_reply` refuses it. One recipient, plain text only: no CC or BCC, no attachment, no list or bulk send. The bar's body is capped at 500 characters on both recipient paths (owner ruling 2026-10-26: customer emails are a few short lines; approved 2026-10-29): a longer body is refused at proposal time with no card, and the tool tells the model to shorten it; the Email page's own composer keeps its larger limit. If Gmail does not confirm, the result is `outcome_unknown` and nothing is retried: check the Gmail Sent folder. An email cannot be unsent. Off: the tool is not offered and a forced call refuses with `gate_off`, sending nothing.

Intelligence Bar target rules v2 (owner rulings 2026-10-12 decision 3, 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-22): `GATE_IB_TARGET_RULES_V2` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibTargetRulesV2Live()`; unset = off = today's behavior byte for byte). For the owner login in owner-direct mode (`GATE_IB_OWNER_DIRECT`) only; other admins keep today's flow. (1) Grounding (`task-context.js` `directGroundedIds`, `owner-direct.js` `targetGrounding`): a card-free internal customer edit (`update_customer`, `update_customer_property`, `set_primary_property`, `update_property_access`, `reschedule_appointment`, `assign_technician`) runs direct ONLY when its customer is (a) the one on screen (page context, never model input), (b) the sole match of one typed full name with nothing else identifying in the message, (c) the sole match of one phone or one email used alone (owner 2026-10-22), or (d) an operator pick. A name plus a contact, a city phrase, a second name or contact, a record id, a name or contact that resolves to nobody or several, and a reply to choice buttons all keep the confirm card. A value being set ("phone number to 941-...") never identifies anyone. A customer the model found itself (a call log, a search) is never grounded. (2) Taint: a request whose context carries more than one candidate customer cards every write (exempt tools included), and the thread is marked so the next 30 minutes of that thread are carded too; a read that returns customer-entered text taints the request (`TRUSTED_READS` lists the reads that do not). So does a message holding text pasted or dropped into the bar (owner 2026-10-24; the bar sends `pasted_text: true`, the saved task keeps it for a customer pick or a resume, `owner-direct.js` `notePastedText`): a full name inside pasted text would otherwise read as the owner naming that customer. Like a read, it leaves the v2 marker, so the rest of that thread is carded too. (3) Same-name lookup (`customerLookupLimit()`): up to 25 rows (it stopped at 10); the model sees only id, name, a checked city and last visit for each row and may offer them with `offer_choices` (4 buttons at most). More than 25 still asks for a phone or email. (4) Cap (`directCapThreshold`): a grounded customer tool may make 5 direct edits per request (it was 2), counted as each edit commits (carded calls never use the allowance); the 6th is refused with the bulk-card message. Lead tools, `create_customer` and the other exempt tools keep the 2-edit limit. Address text still always shows a card. Flip: `GATE_IB_TARGET_RULES_V2=true` in Railway → Variables; rollback: unset it (the v2 taint marker stops applying with the gate off).

Intelligence Bar new conversation after idle (owner 2026-10-12; not a gate): `IB_THREAD_IDLE_HOURS` — default **4**, read at call time (`idleHours()` in `server/services/intelligence-bar/threads.js`); 0, negative, non-numeric or empty = 4, and a value above one year is capped at one year. **The server is the only authority on starting a new conversation; the palette holds the thread it has and obeys.** Two server rules, both using this limit: (1) `GET /admin/intelligence-bar/threads/latest` (`latestThread`) returns no thread when the newest one has had no exchange for longer than the limit, so the palette opens a new conversation instead of resuming it; (2) a direct `POST /query` with an explicit `thread_id` whose thread is idle past the limit (`isThreadIdle`, middleware `startFreshWhenThreadIdle`) runs with no thread id and no client history, so the model never sees the old customer, and starts a new thread, unless the body carries `thread_reopened: true`. Every JSON reply to a rolled-over request carries `threadRolledOver: true`, whether or not a new thread id could be created, and no other reply carries it; the palette then runs its one reset (`startNewConversation`: thread, history, cards, open task, answer buttons, tool activity, gap prompts) before applying the reply, and holds the reply's thread id if it has one. The palette sends `thread_reopened: true` on the first question after a History open or after it loads a saved task that is not the one on screen (it clears after the exchange). The saved task's request key is matched against the request as the client sent it (`identityRequest` in `IbTasks.begin`), and the rolled-over request is stored with `thread_rolled_over`, so a retry after the thread went idle recovers its saved task instead of answering `request_changed`, and the snapshot it gets back replays `threadRolledOver`. A saved task resumed through `/tasks/:id/*` keeps its own thread. A failed idle lookup lets the request run unchanged. A `/query` with no `thread_id` always starts a new thread. The palette keeps no idle clock and never decides a rollover. The retention purge (`IB_THREAD_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 365) is separate. Why: one conversation ran from 2026-09-03 with 178 turns and an old customer bled into a new ask. Rollback: set `IB_THREAD_IDLE_HOURS=8760`.

Intelligence Bar confirm-card life (owner 2026-10-12; not a gate): a card stays open 10 minutes (`TTL_MINUTES`), except the tools in `LONG_TTL_TOOL_NAMES` (`server/services/intelligence-bar/pending-actions.js`), which stay open 60 minutes (`ttlMinutesFor(tool)`). The 60-minute tools each re-check at Confirm (live preview fingerprint, pinned version or pinned values) and send nothing to a customer, move no money and delete nothing: add_customer_property, update_customer_property, set_primary_property, update_property_access, create_customer, update_lead_contact, adjust_stock, create_restock_request, update_restock_request, update_lead_status, toggle_estimate_v2_view, toggle_show_one_time_option. Every other card stays at 10 minutes: customer messages (send_sms, reply_via_sms, send_email_reply, trigger_review_request, submit_review_reply), money (send_invoice, resend_receipt, approve_price, cancel_plan, remove_saved_payment_method), deletes and merges, bookings and schedule moves, outside-service writes, and legacy writes with no commit-time pin (update_customer, bulk_update_customers, bulk_update_leads, block_sender, create_pending_estimate, run_price_lookup, run_tax_advisor). The card countdown reads the server's `expiresInMs`, so it shows the right time for either life. Rollback: empty `LONG_TTL_TOOL_NAMES`.

Intelligence Bar tier-upgrade email: `GATE_IB_TIER_UPGRADE_EMAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibTierUpgradeEmailLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, one confirmed `update_customer` card that raises a customer's WaveGuard tier (Bronze < Silver < Gold < Platinum) AND changes the monthly rate that customer is billed emails them the `membership.tier_upgraded` template after the update is saved (owner 2026-10-08; `server/services/intelligence-bar/tier-upgrade-email.js`, sender `sendMembershipTierUpgraded` in `server/services/account-membership-email.js`, template seeded by migration `20261008100000`). The email's figures come from the pricing constants (`WAVEGUARD.tiers[tier].discount`, `WAVEGUARD.recurringCustomerOneTimePerk`, `PALM.flatCreditPerPalm` from `PALM.flatCreditMinTier` up); a monthly figure shows only to a customer billed monthly. Decided once at proposal time and pinned on the card (`_tier_upgrade_email`); the card shows the line "Emails {first name} the {tier} upgrade notice after the update is saved …" (worded as attempted, not guaranteed) in place of "No price-change notice is sent to the customer". At commit the email goes only when the pin is present, the gate is still on, and the committed before/after rows still pass the rules; it is fire-and-forget after the write commits, keyed on the pending action id, and never fails or undoes the update. The send is not waited for: the finished card says the email was started, the customer's interaction history records sent / skipped / failed, and a failure is logged; a promised email that is not even started (gate switched off, or the committed rows no longer qualify) shows as a warning on the finished card. Nothing is sent for: a bulk card, a first tier from none, a downgrade or the same tier, a tier change with no rate change, a rate the customer is not billed monthly (per-application, prepaid, per-visit), an auto-derived tier label, a customer who is inactive or churned, a card that also changes the stage or the active flag, or a customer with no email on file or with email turned off (the card then promises nothing). `membership.updated`, the customer page, `reprice_future_visits` and estimate acceptance are unchanged. Off = no pin, no card line, no email, exactly as before. Rollback: unset the variable.

Intelligence Bar staff Auto Pay-off: `GATE_IB_STAFF_AUTOPAY_OFF` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibStaffAutopayOffLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the bar's `remove_saved_payment_method` (admin only, always a confirm card) can turn a customer's Auto Pay off, then remove the card Auto Pay was using, as the two ordered steps of ONE card (owner ruling 2026-10-03: staff removal of the in-use card had no screen path, and staff had no way to turn Auto Pay off). The off step is the portal's own disable (`server/services/autopay-disable.js`, also used by `PUT /api/billing/autopay`): customer row locked first, `autopay_enabled=false`, pause cleared, every method's flag cleared, and the `autopay_disabled` log row committed in the same transaction (with `details.source = intelligence_bar` and the operator id; `enrollConsentedMethod` matches on event type only). The customer gets the same two emails the portal sends, each through its existing gate (`GATE_PAYMENT_METHOD_CHANGE_EMAILS`): Auto Pay turned off, then payment method removed. The removal keeps the Auto Pay guard ON and writes the `customer.payment_method.remove` audit row (`server/services/payment-method-removal-audit.js`, shared with `DELETE /api/admin/customers/:id/payment-methods/:methodId`). Off = the bar still removes a method Auto Pay is NOT using (one card, no Auto Pay change); for the method Auto Pay uses it answers that Auto Pay cannot be turned off from the bar yet and changes nothing. This gate covers only the Auto Pay-off step; the two customer emails stay behind `GATE_PAYMENT_METHOD_CHANGE_EMAILS`. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/billing-write-tools.js`.

Intelligence Bar send an existing invoice: `GATE_IB_INVOICE_ACTIONS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibInvoiceActionsLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the bar offers admins (Customers, Invoices / Revenue and dashboard pages; always a confirm card, never owner-direct, never the tech portal) one write on an EXISTING invoice only (owner ruling 2026-10-07, Q1): `send_invoice` sends ONE text to the customer, through the Invoices page's own send handler (`sendInvoiceFromBar` over the named POST `/admin/invoices/:id/send` handler, called with `channels: ['sms']`, an option the page never passes: the text leg runs, the email leg is never started, so there is no PDF email, no SMTP fallback and no attachment from the bar). The text is the invoice_sent pay-link text; the card shows the exact text, rendered by the same function the text leg sends with (base template row, pay link shown as a token). A hash of it is pinned, and the text leg refuses a different body at its provider handoff, so a template edited after the card is not sent. Ordinary send, no review request, no account-credit draw, no dispute-hold exemption. The card's total is the send's `expectedTotal`. The customer's phone is read again on the locked invoice row in the final provider handoff (`checkInvoiceDeliveryPreconditions`, where ownership and balance are rechecked) and compared to the approved phone; a changed phone refuses `recipient_changed` and the provider is not called. That final read and the provider request run under the same two locks the comms writers take, tried in the established order (customer-comms, then the SMS phone, then the invoice row, all on one connection); a writer holding either refuses `recipient_busy` (nothing sent, try again in a minute) instead of waiting. The card lists the lines the PDF lists (the PDF's own filter and numbers, `pdf/invoice-pdf.js visibleInvoiceLines` / `invoiceLineParts`, quantity x rate when the quantity is not 1) and the totals rows the PDF prints (`invoiceBreakdownRows`: subtotal, discount, commercial-only tax, deposit credit, total), and quotes the invoice notes. The totals rows depend on the customer too (a tax row only for a commercial property), so their digest is pinned and recomputed from the live customer row under the claim. The visit closeout is pinned by every fact the card shows (service type, date, resuming) and the visit row's edit time. The reminder cadence the card listed (`GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90` changes it) is carried through the send into `scheduleForInvoice(..., { approvedCadence })`, so a gate flip after the claim cannot change the schedule that was approved. A customer with no usable phone, or whose text template is switched off, refuses `invoice_no_channel` (send it from the Invoices page). A customer whose billing preference selects App, or App + Text, refuses `invoice_channel_unsupported`; the preference is read at the card, pinned, and rechecked under the claim and at the handoff (`preview_changed` if it moved), and the confirmed send never pushes. A queued pay-link text (`invoice_send_deferred`) and a send the Invoices page scheduled (status `scheduled` with a `scheduled_send_at` on the invoice; a parked row with no time is not queued) refuse `invoice_send_queued` at the card and at the claim, naming the scheduled time (the claim sees the row's prior status and time); the bar passes `adoptsQueuedInvoiceSend: false`, so it never cancels or adopts queued work. A lead lookup that cannot be read refuses the card with `lead_effects_unverified` (try again; an unread answer is never pinned as "no leads"), and the claim's recheck refuses the same way. Every refusal the route makes applies, with its text. The bar also refuses: any collections hold on billing messages (the route overrides it; the bar never does), an invoice with nothing due, an annual-plan invoice (found the way the pay page finds it, `invoice-prepay.js resolveInvoiceTermId`, so an untagged anchor invoice is caught; a failed lookup refuses; checked on the card, under the claim and at each provider handoff), a linked visit that never ran, an invoice with notes longer than 600 characters, and an invoice that is not verifiably the customer's own: who owes it is read from the live payer resolver (`invoice-payer-ownership.js`, not the payer columns minted with the invoice) when the card is built, again under the send claim (which holds the customer row `FOR SHARE` until it commits, so a payer assignment either lands first and is seen, or waits for the claim and then finds the invoice `sending`: the Bill-To writers' in-flight fence, `packetInvoiceSendInFlight`, refuses while a standalone invoice has a live send claim), and again at the text provider handoff; an unreadable answer refuses. A bar send never voids: a visit cancelled after the check makes the send refuse under its claim (`refusalOnly`, held for review as `INVOICE_VISIT_TERMINAL_UNVOIDED`), and a hold refusal is never requeued as a later scheduled send or queued as a deferred text. A text that did not send is not queued for a later replay (the page's partial-fan-out replay is off for the bar); the result tells the admin to send it from the Invoices page. Pins: invoice status, total, row version (edit time, amount due, lines, personal message, notes), recipient phone, billing channels, text and every effect the send also has (lead conversion, billing reminders, visit closeout, review outreach; for a reminder sequence the system stopped at a void, the card names the real outcome, decided by the one function the scheduler also uses: left stopped under a payment plan, restored paused, held for Auto Pay, resumed, or completed); drift refuses with `preview_changed`. The visit the card said the send closes (or none) is handed to the send's closeout (a different visit is left open and audited `approved_target_mismatch`) and is written on the invoice as an `audit_log` row (the claim's last write, after every claim-time refusal) (`invoice.send_closeout_target_approved`, naming the confirming admin and the claim token) inside the send claim; the claim that delivers adds an `invoice.send_closeout_target_delivered` row with the same token and the delivery stamp, and the delivery row is written in the SAME transaction that marks the invoice sent (a marker that cannot be written rolls the send's finalization back, the claim is held for review, and the bar reports `INVOICE_DELIVERY_RECORD_FAILED`: check the invoice by hand). The daily closeout retry sweep honors a pin only while that delivery is the invoice's newest; a pin whose claim was handed back is retired (`invoice.send_closeout_target_retired`) and ignored, and a pin with neither a delivery nor a retirement is unbound: the sweep closes nothing for that invoice and audits `invoice.closeout_pin_unbound`, until no live claim holds the pin and it is older than the 10-minute stale window (then it counts as retired). The retirement write is critical: when it fails the send reports `INVOICE_CLOSEOUT_PIN_RETIRE_FAILED` (the visit will not auto-close; close it by hand). The effects pin covers each effect whole except its wording, so the reminders' step days (`GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90`) are pinned too. The leads the card said it marks won are pinned the same way (an opaque set digest, or none): the conversion after delivery converts that set only, and a drifted set is skipped and audited (`invoice.send_lead_conversion_skipped`). An attachment upload writes a reservation row (`invoice.attachment_upload_reserved`, released at its insert, expiring after 10 minutes) before its first storage write: the bar's send claim refuses while one is live, and the upload's insert refuses when a delivery landed since the reservation. No invoice creation, amount edit, charge, refund or void. Off = the tool is in no tool list or platform action list and every call refuses with `gate_off`, changing nothing. The reminder re-arm decision for a void-stopped sequence is one function for the scheduler and the preview (`invoice-followups.js rearmDecisionFor`), kept at complexity 20 or below with the scheduler's other helpers. The reminder preview for a void-stopped sequence anchors the cadence the way the scheduler does (`invoice-followups.js voidStopRearmAnchor`, one function). A send-only refusal (`approved_target_mismatch`) never blocks the sweep's retry for a PAID invoice. The claim (`claimInvoiceForSend`), the provider-handoff checks (`checkInvoiceDeliveryPreconditions`, a table of checks run by a loop) and the closeout retry sweep (`retryIssuedInvoiceCloseouts`, with `pinDecisionFor` deciding skip / honor / unpinned) are kept at complexity 20 or below by a test. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/invoice-action-tools.js`.
Intelligence Bar email an existing invoice: `GATE_IB_INVOICE_EMAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibInvoiceEmailLive()`; also needs `GATE_IB_INVOICE_ACTIONS`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner ruling 2026-10-31 (gap #20). On, `send_invoice` also takes `channel: "email"` and an optional `cc_email` (one address): ONE invoice email (the `invoice.sent` template, PDF attached, pay link) to the customer's invoice email address, copied to that one CC, and no text, through the same send handler with `channels: ['email']`. The card shows the email as the customer reads it, built by the sender's own code (`invoice-email.js` `sendInvoiceEmail` with `previewOnly`: same recipient, CC rules, payload and template; pay link as a token; nothing written), and pins its digest, the template content hash, the address and the CC. The email leg refuses a different address (`recipient_changed`), a different rendered email or template (`email_content_changed`), and runs the card's live owner / annual-plan / delivery-choice / totals check again at the provider handoff. A bar email never falls back to SMTP. A CC is treated like a one-off recipient (no card-on-file label, no other invoices' balance). Refused: payer-billed invoices, no invoice email on file, a CC that is the recipient's own address or not one address, a customer whose invoice choice has no Email or has App. Off: `send_invoice` is text-only, exactly as before.

Intelligence Bar delete empty duplicate customer (owner ruling 2026-10-07, Q3: "soft-delete for empty stubs only (no visits, invoices, payments), carded, restorable"): `GATE_IB_DELETE_CUSTOMER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibDeleteCustomerLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, admin logins get `delete_duplicate_customer` (always a confirm card, never owner-direct; technicians never see it). **Archive only**: the commit is the customer page's own `DELETE /api/admin/customers/:id` handler (`archiveCustomerAsAdmin` in `server/routes/admin-customers.js`: billing wind-down guard, deletion gate, newsletter relink, `customer.archive` audit row). Nothing is merged or moved, and the other record (the one the duplicate queue keeps) is only read, never written, so no backfill, dunning release or payment-session change reaches it. Restore: `PATCH /api/admin/customers/:id/restore` (admin) clears `deleted_at`; the customer page has no Restore button yet. **What counts as empty is fail-closed** (`server/services/customer-empty-loser.js`): (A) every customer column outside the unknown-caller stub creator's list (the insert in `call-recording-processor.js`: id, account_id, is_primary_profile, profile_label, names, phone, email, address, referral_code, lead_source, lead_source_detail, pipeline_stage, pipeline_stage_changed_at, nearest_location_id, active, timestamps) must be NULL or its schema default, read from `information_schema` and compared at runtime, so a column added later refuses by default and the refusal names the column, never the value; (B) no linked rows: `loserAutoBlockers`, `previewMergeEffects` (declared FKs, every `*customer_id` column, polymorphic pointers), `nonFkMergeRewrites`, every merge-excluded table, and the customers table's own pointer columns (`referred_by_customer_id`); one untouched automatic primary property and the derived health score are allowed; a count that cannot be read refuses; (C) a primary profile with other live members in its account refuses. The record must also be a CONFIRMED same-identity duplicate the queue lists: one queue build (`duplicateWinnerFor(..., { requireSameIdentity: true })`) names the keeper; a record the queue keeps, does not list, links only by a shared email, or lists as a possible match (a different name, or a phone line holding more than one identity: "the queue lists this as a possible match, not a confirmed duplicate; use merge_customers") refuses. `merge_customers` keeps its own, wider queue rules. Inside the archive transaction, in order: BOTH customer rows (this record and the keeper) locked FOR UPDATE in one statement in ascending id order, the order the merge engine locks its pair in, and held until the archive commits; `acquirePairAdjudicationLock` (the lock the "not a duplicate" dismissal takes); the queue verdict again (pair still eligible and same-identity, same keeper); BOTH content pins, each a SHA-256 fingerprint of the allow-listed customer columns (not `updated_at` alone, because the Customer 360 save changes those columns without bumping it); and the emptiness scan again on the locked row; any change returns `preview_changed` with nothing deleted. The card names the record, the real customer it duplicates, every check, the restore line and "No customer message is sent"; dates are Eastern calendar dates. Remaining window, the same one the customer page delete and the merge engine have: no lock is shared by every history writer, so a foreign-key insert waiting on the row lock or a write to a pointer with no foreign key can commit just after the archive and attach to the archived row; the record stays restorable and the tool adds no post-commit snapshot. Off = the tool is not offered on either path and a forced call refuses. Rollback: unset `GATE_IB_DELETE_CUSTOMER`. Sends nothing to a customer. Code: `server/services/duplicate-customer-delete.js`, `server/services/customer-empty-loser.js`, `server/services/intelligence-bar/customer-lifecycle-tools.js`.

Caller demotion after an on-site contact's YES: `GATE_ONSITE_CALLER_DEMOTE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`onSiteCallerDemoteLive()`); also needs the recipient double opt-in rail on. On, when the on-site person a caller booked for answers YES to the opt-in text for a visit that is still confirmed and ahead: (1) the caller's appointment texts switch off account-wide (`notification_prefs.appointment_notify_primary = false`, and a saved property's own chosen `true` in `property_notification_prefs` goes back to not chosen; appointment emails to the holder are untouched: `appointment-email.js` reads `callerDemotedForTextsOnly` and keeps the holder on them), once per phone and only when that person is the account's only service-contact phone and a textable recipient; (2) that person gets the same booking confirmation text the caller got (`sendConfirmationToServiceContact`; same template, holds and confirmation choices; never sent twice for a visit). A 15-minute sweep retries a held or failed attempt for up to 14 days after the YES. A phone that already said YES on an earlier call gets no new ask at a later booking: its follow-up is re-armed on the new visit (`rearmOnSiteFollowUp`) and the sweep settles it within 15 minutes (the caller gets that call's own confirmation first; the contact gets the confirmation when no fan-out sent it, e.g. a reused booking). Off, a YES records consent exactly as before and the sweep closes the row, so a later flip never acts on an old YES. The demotion waits 10 minutes after the opt-in ask (or the later booking) and while the caller's own booking confirmation is pending, so the caller always gets that text first; the contact's confirmation does not wait. If that contact later replies STOP or NO, or is removed from the account, loses contact consent or has the phone suppressed another way (found by the sweep within 15 minutes), the caller's appointment texts switch back on (only where this flow switched them off; a holder's own earlier opt-out is never touched, and a preference the holder or the office saves after the demotion is theirs and is never switched back), also with the gate off. A renewed YES for a visit still ahead demotes again. Prerequisite: the retries, the later-booking re-arm and the restore backstop run on the 15-minute recipient opt-in sweep, which is registered only where `GATE_CRON_JOBS` is on (the same dependency the opt-in rail's own ask recovery has). Rollback = unset (callers already switched off stay off; the office or the customer turns appointment texts back on in notification settings).

Intelligence Bar billing type + per-application fee: `GATE_IB_BILLING_MODE_EDIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibBillingModeEditLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the bar's `update_customer` (admin, always a confirm card, never owner-direct) accepts `billing_mode` (per_application, per_visit, one_time, monthly_membership) and `per_application_fee` for one customer, alone on their own card. The billing type is checked with the customer page's own rules (`server/services/billing-mode-rules.js`, shared with PUT /api/admin/customers/:id): monthly membership needs a monthly rate, per application needs a fee, per visit / one time need every upcoming billable visit priced. Refused although the customer page allows them: annual prepay (to or from, or while a live annual-prepay term covers today), clearing the type to Not set, a change that makes the customer a member (the page sends the welcome email there), any edit for a customer with a Bill-To payer (on the customer or an upcoming visit), a move to monthly membership for a customer the monthly dues run would not charge (its own cohort and guards in `server/services/monthly-dues-eligibility.js`, shared with `billing-cron.js`: Auto Pay off or paused, inactive or service-paused, annual prepay covering or pending, no chargeable saved method), leaving monthly membership while a failed MONTHLY dues payment's retry is armed, and leaving it while this month's dues charge has an unsettled Stripe outcome (`hasUnresolvedSiblingStripeOutcome`: an unresolved invoice-less `stripe_orphan_charges` row or a dues attempt parked with `metadata.ambiguous_outcome`). The commit holds the customer's billing-collection claim (`customer-billing-lock.js`, the key the dues cron and retry sweep hold) takes the customer comms lock (the one a Schedule booking holds while it inserts visits) before the customer row lock, and locks the live visits FOR UPDATE (the Schedule save's row lock). Live visits are the lifecycle guard's own clause (pending, confirmed, rescheduled, en_route, on_site), also used by the customer page's unpriced-visit rule. The card does NOT project per-visit charges (price, tax, surcharge, prepayment, invoices and dues coverage all move completion's amount): it is refused (`billing_visits_priced`, at the card and again under the locks) when ANY live upcoming visit carries a price (or a base price a discount froze to $0, or a deliberate $0 stamp), a prepayment, create-invoice-on-complete, or an invoice of any kind (the invoices attached to the visit, `completion-invoice-candidate.js`, or the sibling / combined first-application invoice of its estimate, `estimate-first-application-invoice.js`); the count of such visits is pinned, so a visit priced after the card refuses as preview_changed, and the change is made on the customer page, which shows each visit's charge. The commit also takes the per-customer annual-prepay lock (try) before the customer row; lock order: property-preferences, comms, annual-prepay, customer row, billing claim, visit rows. A per-visit / one-time switch is refused for an ongoing recurring plan with no price (the nightly top-up's own series selector). The dues cron re-runs its guards on a fresh customer row under the collection claim, and completion re-reads the billing type inside the mint lock (409 BILLING_LANE_CHANGED on drift), so no lane writer is raced. The card shows the type and fee before → after in words, the rule each lane applies (no amounts; a move into monthly says how many upcoming unpriced visits are covered by dues), the saved method future charges go to by tender family and last four ("the saved card ending 1234" with the configured card-surcharge sentence, or "the saved bank account ending 1234 (ACH)"; invoiced when Auto Pay is off or, for per visit, GATE_COMPLETION_AUTOPAY_CHARGE is off), and that no customer message is sent; the billing fields, payer, Auto Pay state, each upcoming visit's billing columns and invoices, the tender family / last four / method id, the call-time state of GATE_COMPLETION_AUTOPAY_CHARGE and GATE_STAMPED_ZERO_FREE (the only gates `billing-lane.js` and the dues verdict read), and the customer version are pinned, and a change before Confirm refuses as preview_changed. Every live visit is pinned and locked (no row cut); a customer with more than 2,000 upcoming visits is refused (change it on the customer page). The visits' invoices are locked FOR UPDATE NOWAIT after the visits at confirmation and re-read, so an invoice edit in the window refuses; an ongoing plan is judged by the top-up's own billable-amount verdict for its next occurrences under the new lane; open membership-dues invoices (the line_items membership_dues_month stamp) are named on the card and pinned, replacing the flat "dues stop" line; the ongoing-plan verdict walks the complete top-up horizon (distinct add-on sets, not a date cap) and always validates at least the next occurrence, even past the horizon, and a walk too long to finish refuses as unverified; the dues-eligibility check reads annual-prepay coverage strictly (a probe error is unreadable); an unreadable Auto Pay lookup refuses the card (billing_autopay_unverified); and the unpriced-visit check reads every visit. A completion rechecks the billing type on the locked customer and visit rows of the transaction that marks the visit completed (a switch that landed first refuses the completion with a retryable 409; a completion that commits first has already moved its attempt to side_effects_running in that same transaction, and the card refuses `billing_completion_pending` while any of the customer's attempts is running or pending, at any age (`completion-attempts.js customerCompletionInFlightState`), so a completion that decides "no invoice" from the type it read at entry is never left behind by an edit), and a mint that finds the type moved releases the completion for a retry on the new lane. Writes the two columns only. Off = both fields are refused as unsupported, exactly as before. Rollback: unset the variable; a customer changed while on keeps the new values until set back on the customer page or by another card (visits completed meanwhile were billed under the new values). Round 13/15: leaving monthly membership while any monthly dues payment of this or last month is still `processing` by bank debit is refused (`billing_dues_processing`, no disclosure path: a debit that later fails arms a monthly retry that the lane change would supersede); the payment is pinned, so one that appears between card and commit refuses. The query is `findCollectedMonthlyPayment` (`retry-collectibility.js`, the dues cron's own predicate, now shared). A customer whose ongoing recurring plan (the top-up's `eligibleSeriesParentIds`) is stamped with a Bill-To payer is refused (`billing_visits_payer_owned`) even with no live visit; the roots are pinned and locked FOR UPDATE at commit. The commit also locks the customer's `payment_methods` rows FOR UPDATE NOWAIT before the final tender read and pins the full method id list, so an updated or added method refuses the card. Round 14: an ongoing recurring root whose extension price template (plus due add-ons) carries a positive price is refused (`billing_visits_priced`, naming the plan and the price) although it has no live priced visit, because the top-up copies that price onto the visits it mints and completion prefers it to the per-application fee; the price comes from the top-up's own resolver (`seriesNextOccurrencesPrice` in `admin-schedule.js`, sharing `seriesExtensionDatePrices` with the unbillable verdict), a series that cannot be verified is refused, and the price is pinned. A move into monthly membership for a customer with an active collections dispute hold is refused (`billing_collection_hold`): `monthlyDuesVerdict` now asks `assertNoCollectionHold` / `isCollectionHoldRefusal`, the charge guard the dues cron uses. The commit try-locks the advisory key `payment-methods` / customer id (`utils/payment-method-lock.js`) before re-reading the method rows; `StripeService.savePaymentMethod`, the only writer that inserts a method, takes the same key (blocking) around its insert, so no method insert can commit between the re-read and the commit. Open dues invoices show and pin the collectible amount (`invoiceAmountDue`: total less `credit_applied`). Round 17: the completion-in-flight fence has no age window for either state: a `side_effects_pending` row is resumed at any age and a stale `side_effects_running` row is reclaimed, both with the frozen required amount, so either fences the edit until it is finished or released (`customerCompletionInFlightState`; an abandoned row blocks by design). The unresolved Stripe outcome check covers both months the processing-dues check covers. The per-application line says each performed application is charged and discloses the outcomes that perform none (`NON_PERFORMED_VISIT_OUTCOMES` in `services/visit-outcomes.js`, the list the completion route's `visitPerformed` reads). Leaving monthly is refused (`billing_dues_draft`) while a stamped dues invoice is still a draft, because a draft has no pay link and the overdue reminders skip it. Round 18: the processing-dues refusal also covers a completion-stamped dues INVOICE paid by ACH and still `processing` (`findLiveStampedDuesInvoice` with `processingOnly`, the cron's own lookup), named by invoice number and month, and pinned. Round 19: ongoing roots are asked of the nightly top-up's own skip rules (`splitRootsByTopupSkip` in `admin-schedule.js`: `topupCustomerSkipReason` for deleted / held / inactive / churned customers, `topupSeriesSkipReason` for annual-prepay, plan-hold and duplicate series); a skipped root is listed on the card as not extended and its skip reason is pinned (round 22 below: a skip never removes the root from the checks). A root with an explicit $0 template override (`GATE_EDIT_APPT_PRICE_SERVICE_SCOPE` on and `recurring_template_overrides.estimated_price` exactly 0, the condition `applyStoredVisitFinancials` uses) is refused (`billing_visits_priced`, "it would bill nothing"), kept apart from an unpriced root, and the scope gate state is pinned. Round 22: no skip erases a root's terms. `splitRootsByTopupSkip` returns only `{ extend, skipped }` (no permanent or reversible list: any skip can clear), every ongoing root goes through the payer, price, zero and unbillable checks whether or not the top-up skips it (also in `billing-mode-rules.js` `unpricedOngoingSeries`), a skipped root is listed as "not extended now (reason)" with its terms applying if it resumes, and the skip reason is pinned so a skip that starts or clears after the card refuses as `preview_changed`. The price resolver `seriesNextOccurrencesPrice` returns `{ price, linePrice, zero }` with `zero` = `override` | `discounted` | `unpriced` | null (Round 21: `storedOccurrenceFloorVerdict`, read-only beside `storedOccurrenceFloorPrice`, which still decides what the top-up stamps); a known line price discounted to $0 is refused like the override (`billing_visits_priced`, names the plan, the line and the $0) and the kind and line price are pinned. Round 23: the line price behind that verdict is the parent line's gross plus each due add-on's gross (`base_price`, else net plus frozen discount dollars), so a $0 parent with a $100 add-on discounted to $0 reads `discounted`, not `unpriced`; the refusal names the add-on and its gross, and the add-on gross figures are pinned. What the top-up stamps is unchanged. The per-visit and one-time card copy says each performed visit is charged and discloses the same non-performed outcomes. Round 24: a live unpriced estimate-linked visit whose combined first-application invoice is void (or canceled without a setup fee) with no live recognized replacement is refused (`billing_visits_held`: "<visit> has a voided first-application invoice with no replacement; completion will park it for manual billing. Resolve it on the invoice page first"), because completion's lane-independent hold (`combinedInvoiceVoidedWithoutLiveReplacement` with `isSiblingCoverageEligibleVisit`, `billing-lane.js`) would park it; the same canonical function runs on the locked rows at commit (row-locked NOWAIT) and the voided invoice id is pinned per visit, so a void that appears or clears after the card refuses as `preview_changed`.

Service-line sheet price scope (owner 2026-10-26, bug 4 of the 10-24 price audit): `GATE_SERVICE_SHEET_PRICE_SCOPE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at module load (`isEnabled('serviceSheetPriceScope')`, answered to the client by `GET /api/admin/schedule/:id/series-summary` as `canScopeSheetPrice`; kill = delete the variable). Needs `GATE_EDIT_APPT_PRICE_SERVICE_SCOPE` on too: `canScopeSheetPrice` is true only when both are, because update-details honors a posted `priceServiceScope` only behind that gate. On, the service-line sheet (`client/src/components/schedule/MobileServiceEditModal.jsx`: phone Review & checkout → service line, and the Dispatch checkout's service line) shows "Apply price change to" with "This appointment only" (the default) and "This and following appointments" once a recurring-series visit's price differs from the price the sheet opened with — never on a one-time visit, a booster, or an unchanged price — and posts the pick as `priceServiceScope`, the same scope Edit appointment posts: this appointment only on the series' first visit pins the series template at the old price; following rewrites the upcoming visits and stamps the template, and the sheet then says how many visits changed. Only the price carries forward (the sheet sends no `serviceId`). Off, or while series-summary is loading or cannot be read, the sheet shows no choice and posts no scope: its save is exactly what it was before.

Series price guards: `GATE_SERIES_PRICE_GUARDS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at module load (`isEnabled('seriesPriceGuards')`, `server/services/series-price-guards.js`; kill = delete the variable and redeploy). On: (1) a series extension (completion auto-extend and nightly top-up, both `extendSeriesOnceLocked` in `admin-schedule.js`) compares the new visit's computed price with the pre-tax total (deposit credit added back) of the newest PAID invoice on a completed base visit of the series (boosters and callbacks excluded) whose positive lines are all that visit's own `scheduled_<visit>_primary` / `_addon_` charges (a setup-fee or multi-service invoice is not comparable and is skipped); more than 25% over still inserts and raises one office alert per series (Billing, deduped while open); (2) when the series root (the price template) is `cancelled` and that paid amount is missing or the price is more than 25% over it, the extension is skipped (top-up skip reason `cancelled_root_price`) and one office alert per series is raised (Schedule, deduped while open). Exempt: callback / always-free children, unpriced children, annual-prepay series (any visit of the series linked to a term, root or child), and children the prepay coverage stamps after insert. Alerts ring only after the extension's transaction commits, so the top-up dry run never rings. (3) A performed visit on ANY billing lane that completes with no billable amount (no reviewed price, no authoritative $0 per `hasAuthoritativeZeroPrice`, invoice amount ≤ 0) and no paid, existing or minted invoice, prepay or dues coverage raises one office alert per visit (Billing; not for callbacks, always-free types, backfill, recap-review or system quiet closeouts); the two existing `completed with no billable amount` log lines stay. Off = no extra reads, no skip, no alert. The seeder and the office-driven series writers (visit-count edit, alert extend/convert) are not covered.

Intelligence Bar OpenAI backup: `GATE_IB_OPENAI_BACKUP` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibOpenaiBackupLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
