On, when the /query tool loop's Anthropic call throws a provider error (HTTP 401/402/403/404/408/409/429, any 5xx including 529 overloaded, a connection or timeout error, or a 400 whose message says the account is out of room: usage limit, credit, billing, quota), the request switches to OpenAI with tool calling for its remaining rounds (`openai-tool-adapter.js`, Responses API, `store:false`, model = the OpenAI leg of the `highStakes` policy, `MODELS.OPENAI_REPORT_WRITER`, pin with `INTELLIGENCE_BAR_BACKUP_MODEL`; ledgered as provider `openai`, lane `ib_admin_backup`). Any other 400 (a request this server built wrongly) and every tool error are NOT intercepted. The switch turns tool search off (the ordinary page tool list plus `discover_capabilities`, plus any tool the request already loaded), drops the server search and thinking blocks from the history (client `tool_use` / `tool_result` pairs stay), and swaps the two prompt sentences that name the search tool for their `discover_capabilities` forms. Reasoning items from the backup's replies are replayed (with `reasoning.encrypted_content` requested) on its later rounds of the same request; the replay items are saved with the task checkpoint (a private `_openai` field on the reply's first block), so a resumed backup task replays them too, and a saved round whose reasoning cannot be replayed is dropped on resume; a function call that did not complete never runs (the round fails and the original error is rethrown); an incomplete or refused answer is filed as a failed ledger row. The answer ends with the line `(answered by the backup model)`. Confirmation cards are unchanged (the executors are server-side). The saved task is marked `request.model_provider = openai_backup`: a resume of it continues on the backup, and with the gate off it is refused as not resumable (start again). If the backup also fails, the original Anthropic error is rethrown unchanged. Off = no fallback, today's behavior. Rollback: unset the variable.

Intelligence Bar tool search for the owner login: `GATE_IB_TOOL_SEARCH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibToolSearchLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`). Has effect only on a model that accepts Anthropic's tool search (`MODELS.anthropicSupportsToolSearch`: Opus / Sonnet / Haiku 4.5 and later, Fable, Mythos; an older or unknown id keeps the ordinary list) and that does not think by default (`MODELS.anthropicThinksByDefault` on `INTELLIGENCE_BAR_MODEL || MODELS.FLAGSHIP`); with a thinking model the bar keeps the ordinary list, exactly as with the gate off (follow-up, not this gate). On, a full-access login (`ibFullAccess`, contact@ by default) on an ordinary admin page (not the tech portal, not the agent-estimate rail) is sent its page's usual tools up front (including `discover_capabilities`, the route to owner-workflow actions that are not tools; the prompt says to call it once when the search finds nothing; its result is `tool_reference` blocks only, at most 5, for the found deferred tools, or the plain JSON when it also holds an owner-workflow action, so the tools array never changes during a request), the Anthropic API's own tool search tool (`tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119`, no beta header; needs a model that supports it, which `MODELS.FLAGSHIP` does), and every other tool `allowed()` accepts (not `confirmed_endpoint`) with `defer_loading: true`, sorted by name, so the owner reaches the whole catalog without `discover_capabilities`. The system prompt line names the searchable areas. A request that continues after a card or an interruption (`/tasks/:id/resume`, `/tasks/:id/select-target`) continues on the ordinary tool list with `discover_capabilities`: the saved search blocks are stripped when the checkpoint is loaded. Other admins, technicians, the tech context and the agent-estimate rail are unchanged. Off = the page list plus `discover_capabilities` for everyone, today's behavior. Rollback if the API rejects the request shape: unset the variable.

Intelligence Bar reprice future visits: `GATE_IB_REPRICE_VISITS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibRepriceVisitsLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the bar's `reprice_future_visits` (admin only, always a confirm card, never owner-direct; offered on the Customers, Schedule / Dispatch and dashboard pages) sets one new per-visit dollar price on ONE customer's upcoming visits (scheduled today ET or later, pending or confirmed) of ONE service family (owner ruling 2026-10-07, Q8). The card lists each visit that changes (date, service, old price → new price), each visit left alone and why, and that no customer message is sent. Left alone: completed, in progress (en_route / on_site, or a visit tracker past scheduled), invoiced (any invoice row), prepaid, free re-service, $0 and add-on visits, a series' first (template) visit (the Schedule edit carries its price into visits the plan adds later), and any visit the Schedule screen's re-price block reports as holding money (`findBillingCoveredVisits`). A monthly-membership customer is refused (dues cover the visits; the price there is the monthly rate), and so is a customer with any annual prepay term the visit save's term refresh would process (`refreshableTermsForCustomer`, the refresh's own selection; the save refreshes those terms from the new prices, an effect the card cannot show) — "change visit prices on the Schedule screen". A visit's own annual-term link is judged by `findBillingCoveredVisits` (a voided term's visit is eligible). No percentage: the operator states the dollar price. At most 24 visits per card (`through_date` splits a longer schedule). Each visit is saved through the Schedule screen's own visit edit (`updateVisitDetails` over the named PUT `/admin/schedule/:id/update-details` handler, `server/routes/admin-schedule.js`) with the body its price-only edit sends (`estimatedPrice`, plus `expectedTotal`), so the handler's validation, re-price block, CAS and post-commit effects apply; a visit's discount stamp is replaced by the new full price, exactly as that edit does. Every listed visit's id, date, status, price and row version is pinned (`_verified_reprice_version`); drift on any refuses with `preview_changed` before the first save. Inside each save's transaction, under its customer and visit locks, the handler also rechecks the approved related state (`approvedRepriceState`: no add-on line, the same billing lane, no term the refresh would process; adapter-only, never an HTTP field) and refuses 409 on any difference; a refusal mid-batch stops and the receipt is partial, naming what changed. Off = the tool is not offered in any tool list or platform action list, and every call refuses with `gate_off`, changing nothing. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/reprice-visits-tools.js`.

Intelligence Bar several confirm cards in one answer: `GATE_IB_MULTI_CARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibMultiCardLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`, because the write frontier it relaxes exists only on the platform path). Off = one card per request: after the first card, every later write proposal in the request is refused with `dependency_unresolved`, exactly as before. On (owner request 2026-10-20), a later write may mint its own card when it is independent of every earlier unconfirmed card of the same request: it names its target record by id (customer, lead, visit, invoice, estimate, property), none of those ids matches an earlier card's, and no earlier card created a record. A same-record proposal is refused with `same_record_card_open` (the owner confirms the first card, then asks again). At most 5 cards per request (`card_limit_reached`). Only open edits join a set: `update_lead_contact`, `update_lead_status`, `update_customer` (name, phone, email, address, lead source and notes only), `update_customer_property`, `update_property_access`, `set_primary_property`, `add_customer_property`, `assign_technician`, `reschedule_appointment`, `send_sms`, `reply_via_sms` and `create_appointment` with no stated price. A refund, card charge, price, rate or tier change, setting, delete, merge, bulk, outside-service or record-creating card never joins a set: it closes the frontier as today. Address text in a write is still a card. Each card keeps its own pins and compare-and-set and confirms or cancels on its own; confirming one never alters another. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/multi-card.js`; the route admits cards in the tool loop of `POST /query`, and `loadTaskStep` (`pending-actions.js`) lets a task hold the request's own open cards.

Intelligence Bar general admin read: `GATE_IB_GENERAL_READ` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibGeneralReadLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`: with the platform gate off the reader is false, the tools are not offered and a forced call is refused). On, the owner login (`ibFullAccess`, contact@ or `IB_FULL_ACCESS_EMAILS`) gets two read tools (owner ruling 2026-10-12: "the Intelligence Bar may read what any admin screen reads, on the owner login, behind a gate"): `find_admin_reads` (searches the catalog by words, up to 10 entries, reads no rows) and `read_admin_data` (calls ONE catalog endpoint). The catalog is `server/services/intelligence-bar/admin-read-catalog.json`, a **hand-reviewed list that grows by review** (its size is `entries.length` of the catalog file; no count is committed). An endpoint is in it only when `admin-read-reviewed.json` has a row for it that a person wrote after reading the handler and every function it calls; the row holds the scan fingerprint (signals, unresolved callees, and a content hash of the handler chain), its allowed query keys (a row with none forwards no query), and its scope (`customer`, `invoice` or `broad`, which decides what a task for one customer may read), so any edit to that chain drops the endpoint from the regenerated catalog until it is reviewed again (the byte-for-byte catalog test then fails in the PR that edits it). `npm run ib:read-catalog` regenerates it; `-- --fingerprint <endpoint>` prints a row's fingerprint. The generator's scan (`scripts/build-ib-admin-read-catalog.js`) is a second lock: a reviewed endpoint is still left out when the scan finds a database write, an outside-service call, DDL, a signed-URL or credential signal, a file response, or middleware that does any of that; it follows calls across modules, named callbacks and the middleware that runs before the route, and the path deny rules (credentials, auth and identity flows, tokens, webhooks, sessions, files, downloads, streams, action verbs; `server/utils/admin-read-rules.js`) apply on top. `read_admin_data` takes the pattern and the parameter values separately, builds the path itself, and sends a GET to `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api<path>` with the Authorization header of the request that runs the bar, so every router middleware (auth, MFA, token version, technician scope, privacy filters, rate limits) applies as on the screen. The token travels only on the server-built action context (never model input, never logged, never stored in tasks, checkpoints, pending actions or telemetry). Only a JSON answer is returned; free-text fields a reviewed row marks `note` (typed by staff or customers) are withheld, and so is ANY response key whose name looks like free text (note, reason, description, message, details and similar; `FREE_TEXT_WORDS`) unless its row declares it `content`, shown only as `[note withheld: N characters]` with a `notes_withheld` count, and `content` fields (business-authored text) are returned scrubbed; the list includes the core record screens (customers, a customer's timeline and texts, estimates, schedule list, dispatch board, invoices, leads) through per-row `acceptSignals` (credential, signed-link and transaction signals the reviewer read), `omit` (response keys never shown, such as pay tokens and Stripe ids) and `keywords` for the finder, and free-text notes on those rows stay withheld exactly as above; credentials are removed before the answer is capped at 12,000 characters: a link that carries its own credential (presigned or signed URL, storage-host URL, `token`/`key`/`sig` query key) becomes `[signed link removed]`, a customer-facing link with a random 16+ character segment (pay, estimate, portal, unsubscribe links) becomes `[private link removed]`, and the value under any credential-named key (token, secret, password, pin, signature, hash, session, api key and similar, at any depth; gate and access codes are kept) becomes `[removed]` (arrays cut to the first items that fit with the total, long strings cut); 10 s timeout; redirects are not followed. It reads only; it cannot change anything. Scope class `broad`: inside a customer-scoped task it is refused (`customer_scope_required`) except on the owner-direct login, where the read widens. Off = the tools are in no tool list and every call refuses with `gate_off`, changing nothing. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/admin-read-tools.js`.

Intelligence Bar general read for the office login: `GATE_IB_GENERAL_READ_OFFICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibGeneralReadOfficeLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it needs `GATE_IB_GENERAL_READ` (so `GATE_IB_PLATFORM` too). Owner ruling 2026-10-28 ("A1", IB gap 3): the office (a non-owner ADMIN login, Virginia) gets `find_admin_reads` and `read_admin_data`, limited to the catalog rows a person reviewed as OFFICE rows. A row is an office row only when its entry in `server/services/intelligence-bar/admin-read-reviewed.json` says `"office": true`; `scripts/build-ib-admin-read-catalog.js` carries it into `admin-read-catalog.json` and FAILS the build for an office row on the never-office list (banking, payouts including `/admin/referrals/payouts`, payroll, tax, the SEO pipeline, revenue settings, pricing configuration and discounts, settings and integrations, credentials and tokens) or a row reviewed to return notes (`keepNotes`). The first office rows are `/admin/dispatch/alerts`, `/admin/email-templates`, `/admin/email-templates/automations` and `/admin/schedule/blackout-dates`. On her login `find_admin_reads` lists only office rows and `read_admin_data` refuses every other reviewed row with "That read is not available on this login." before any request is made; free-text notes are ALWAYS withheld there, whatever `GATE_IB_READ_NOTES` says (that gate is the owner login's ruling); the loopback GET still carries her own bearer token, so each endpoint's own auth applies. The access path is `allowed()` in `server/services/intelligence-bar/action-registry.js` (offers exactly those two tools, never `find_admin_edits`, to a non-owner admin while the gate is on) and `executeAdminReadTool` in `admin-read-tools.js` (the office limit and the admin check). Every later write on her login is carded as before: owner-direct is owner-only. The owner login keeps the whole catalog and technicians never get either tool. Off: the two tools are offered to the owner login only and a forced call from her login is refused, byte-identical to before.
Intelligence Bar read notes: `GATE_IB_READ_NOTES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibReadNotesLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `GATE_IB_GENERAL_READ`, so `GATE_IB_PLATFORM` too). Owner ruling 2026-10-13: the general read RETURNS free-text notes and access instructions (gate codes, lockbox instructions), scrubbed of secrets, on the owner login only. On, a value the general read would withhold as `[note withheld: N characters]` (a key a reviewed row declares `note`, or any key named like free text and not declared `content`) comes back instead, with `notes_returned` counting them. Each returned string passes the existing structural link redaction (signed and private links become markers) and ONE fixed-format scrubber (`server/utils/note-secret-scrubber.js`): PEM blocks, key prefixes (`sk-`/`sk_`, `pk_`, `rk_`, `whsec_`, `ghp_` family, `github_pat_`, `xox*-`, `AKIA`/`ASIA`, `AIza`, `SG.`), `Bearer <token>`, JWTs, credential-named query parameters and `user:password@` in a URL, card numbers (Luhn, `pan-scrub.js`), SSN pattern and any run of 32+ base64/hex characters become `[removed]`. One structural rule covers labelled credentials: a credential key (password, secret, token, api key, auth, authorization, cookie, `*_key`, an env-style name such as DB_PASSWORD) followed by `:` or `=` loses EVERYTHING after the separator to the end of that note string (one `[removed]`; the text before it, the key and the separator stay; no value format is parsed). It has NO other prose rules: a code or password written as plain words ("the gate code is 1234", "lockbox 4521, key under the mat", "password is hunter2") comes back as written; that is the known limit and the ruling. Each note is cut at 1,000 characters (`[cut]`). The read keeps its untrusted-data marker, so every later write in the thread shows a confirm card. Other strings in the answer go through the same scrubbers as before. Off = notes are withheld byte-identically to before. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/admin-read-tools.js`, `server/utils/signed-link-redaction.js`.

Intelligence Bar general admin edit: `GATE_IB_GENERAL_EDIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`ibGeneralEditLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `GATE_IB_PLATFORM`: with the platform gate off the reader is false, the tools are not offered and a forced call is refused). On, the owner login (`ibFullAccess`, contact@ or `IB_FULL_ACCESS_EMAILS`) gets two tools (owner ruling 2026-10-12: "a general EDIT tool is allowed for a reviewed allow-list of small internal edits only ... owner login only, ALWAYS a confirm card, its own gate"): `find_admin_edits` (searches the catalog by words, up to 10 entries, changes nothing) and `propose_admin_edit` (validates ONE edit and mints a confirm card; the card is never owner-direct and never skipped). The catalog is `server/services/intelligence-bar/admin-write-catalog.json`, a **hand-reviewed list that grows by review** (its size is `entries.length`; no count is committed), generated by `npm run ib:write-catalog` from `admin-write-reviewed.json`. An edit is in it only when that file holds a row a person wrote after reading the PUT or PATCH handler and every function it calls: the row holds the scan fingerprint (signals, unresolved callees, the tables the chain writes, a content hash of the handler chain), the body fields the edit may carry (type and size; any other field is REFUSED, never dropped), the scope (`customer` and `visit` rows also need the customer id, which the tool checks against the record in the path; the task-context guard then checks it against the task customer), a reason and the line the card shows about what the edit does not do. Any change to the handler chain drops the endpoint from the regenerated catalog until it is reviewed again (the byte-for-byte catalog test fails in the PR that edits it). The generator is stricter than a reviewer for a write (`server/utils/admin-write-rules.js`): only PUT or PATCH; no delete, bulk, send, money, settings, user or credential word in the path; an outside call, a messaging, payment or alerting module, a signed or customer-facing link, a file response, a delete, DDL, a raw SQL write or a bulk insert keeps the route out with no waiver (a sender-, charge- or delete-named call and a credential field stay out unless the row waives them with a reason); no money, message or queue table may be written. Batch 1 covers: SMS template wording, email template name and description, email draft version wording, email preview data, email automation step wording, one timesheet entry, one customer's text and report preference flags, a visit note and a product-use note. `propose_admin_edit` takes the method, the catalog pattern, the path parameters and the body, never a URL. Its card names the record in words (a read-only snapshot per edit supplies the label, the current value of every carded field, the row version and the record state; an email version must be a draft) and lists every field's current and new value, shows an ADDRESS CHANGE line when a field looks like address text, and pins the reviewed row's digest, the filled path, the exact body, the customer binding, the label, the current values and the version. On Confirm the route re-runs the preview (it must equal the card), the executor rebuilds the plan and refuses with `preview_changed` unless it still equals the approved pin, then re-reads the record and sends exactly the carded body as a loopback PUT or PATCH to `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api<path>` with the Authorization header of the confirming request (set on the action context by the route, never model input, logged or stored), so every router middleware and the handler's own validation and locks apply as on the screen. The handler's response body is never returned (a receipt of endpoint, record ids and field names only); a 4xx answer is a refusal, a 5xx, timeout or transport error is `outcome_unknown`, and a 2xx is checked by reading the record again (every carded field must hold its new value, else `outcome_unknown`). Off = the tools are in no tool list and every call refuses with `gate_off`, changing nothing. Code: `server/services/intelligence-bar/admin-write-tools.js`.

Contact login (owner 2026-10-20): `GATE_CONTACT_LOGIN` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`contactLoginLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, an on-location contact (a `customers.service_contact*` phone) signs into the customer app with their OWN number through the same SMS-code login (`server/routes/auth.js` `resolveLoginIdentity`: the account holder's own number always wins; a contact number is tried only when no holder row matches; a contact on several rows lands on the primary profile, then the oldest, no chooser) and holds a CONTACT session on that customer row: the access and refresh tokens carry `contactKey` (the last-10 phone key), `server/middleware/auth.js` re-checks on every request that the gate is on, the row is active (no cancelled allowance) and the number still occupies a slot (the holder removing the contact ends the session at its next request or refresh; the only profile switch admitted is to another row that lists the number as a contact, below), and only the routes in `CONTACT_SESSION_ROUTES` answer — `/auth/me` (narrowed: the contact's own name/phone/email, the property address, no referral code, credits, prepay, rate or holder prefs), `/auth/properties` (every row the number is a contact on) and `/auth/select-property` (a listed row only), the push device routes, the schedule and visit-history reads, technician tracking, the documents reads (service reports only; nothing for a contact `slotWithheldFromReports` applies to), the activity beacons and `GET/PUT /api/notifications/contact-preferences`; everything else answers **403 `ACCOUNT_HOLDER_ONLY`** (never a 401 the client would read as a dead session). The app narrows to Visits + Documents, view-only: no confirm, reschedule, request, chat, bell or account deletion; the contact's app device registers through the push routes stamped with their phone key (below), never as the holder's device. Per-contact notification choices live in `service_contact_notification_prefs` (migration 20261020120000; keyed by customer + phone key so a slot reorder keeps them; the holder's contact save prunes a removed phone's row): the six purposes (`appointment_confirmation`, `service_reminder_72h`, `service_reminder_24h`, `tech_en_route`, `tech_arrived`, `service_completed`), a per-purpose channel (`sms` / `email` / `both`; NULL = whatever the account sends), `sms_enabled` / `email_enabled` and `consent_attested_at`. `server/services/contact-notification-prefs.js` `filterContactsByOwnPrefs` runs at every fan-out seam right after `filterRecipientsByOptin` (appointment reminders and their replay, en-route, arrived, the appointment email, the contact report text, the service-report email recipients, the slot-1 summary text, the call-booking secondary confirmation) and only NARROWS: the customer row's toggles and the consent validator stay authoritative, so a purpose the holder turned off stays off (the card shows it locked); fail-CLOSED on an unreadable table (service contacts held, the holder kept; a missing table is the absent state). Turning texts on from the card needs the contact's own consent statement once (`CONSENT_REQUIRED` otherwise); that attestation confirms THIS customer's `recipient_optin` row when it is `pending` or `ask_failed` (the YES reply it stands in for) and never a `declined` (STOP) row. A contact listed on several rows lands on the primary profile, then the oldest, and sees every row their number is a contact on in the ordinary property switcher (`GET /auth/properties` lists them; `POST /auth/select-property` re-mints the family for the target row, same contact claim, refused for any row that does not list the number). The contact's app device registers through the ordinary push routes with `push_subscriptions.contact_phone_key` stamped (migration 20261020130000); `sendToCustomer` excludes contact-stamped devices from every push except the appointment and report purposes `contactPushPurpose` names (`services/contact-notification-prefs.js`), and then only while the key still occupies a slot and the contact's text choices allow it — billing, receipts, requests, estimates, weather and untyped bells never reach a contact device; the holder's status and freshness checks never count a contact device; the holder's contact save deactivates a removed contact's devices. Customer 360 (Contacts & Recipients) reads each contact's effective choices (`GET /api/admin/customers/:id/contact-notification-prefs`) and may narrow them (`PUT …/:slot`, admin, audited as `customer.contact_notification_prefs.update`); staff never stamp the contact's attestation and cannot turn texts on for a contact who has not agreed in the app. Off = a contact number never logs in, an existing contact token is refused (401), the senders ignore the per-contact table and contact devices, byte-identical to before. Sends nothing to a customer.

Inbound referral confirm (dark): `GATE_REFERRAL_INBOUND_CONFIRM` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`referralInboundConfirmLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-26: "YES GO" (review and referral lane, decision 2). The Referrals Queue (`/admin/referrals`, Queue tab) gets a "Needs confirmation" section (`server/services/referral-inbound.js`): active WaveGuard plan customers (real tier, `monthly_rate` > 0, valid phone) who came in through a referral link (`?ref=CODE` on `customers.landing_page_url`, as the website forwards it) or told the call reader who referred them (`lead_source_detail` "Referred by …" or "Referral (unnamed)"), with no referral row for their phone and no office answer yet. Each card shows that evidence and the likely referrer: the owner of the link code (an active promoter, a merged promoter's target, or the customer whose own code it is), or customers matching the spoken name; a search finds any other customer. Confirm (`POST /api/admin/referrals/inbound/:customerId/confirm`) refuses a referrer in the customer's own household (same row, account or phone), enrolls the referrer as a promoter, makes the referral row (`source` `inbound_link` or `inbound_call`, no invite text) and runs the existing conversion (`convertReferral`). When a performed recurring visit is on record (its current closeout is not inspection-only, declined, incomplete or a quiet backfill; an issued-invoice closeout counts), it runs the existing first-service credit at once: $25 to each account (live settings). Otherwise the completion flow credits at the next performed recurring visit, as for any referral. Either way the referrer gets one thank-you email at the next 9:00 AM ET and no reward text (owner 2026-10-29; `sendDueReferralRewardEmails` in `server/services/referral-engine.js`, cron every 15 minutes 9:00-11:45 AM ET, job `referral-reward-email`). A confirm takes an advisory lock on the friend's phone, so two profiles that share it cannot both make a referral. The conversion keeps its own milestone text at 3, 5 and 10 conversions. "Not a referral" (`POST …/dismiss`) records the answer. Each answer is one `referral_inbound_reviews` row (migration `20261026150000`), and that customer is never listed again. Off: `GET /api/admin/referrals/inbound` answers `enabled:false` with no list, both actions answer 404, and the page shows no section. Rollback: unset the variable; referral rows already made stay, and a posted credit is a ledger movement.

New-referral bell (dark): `GATE_REFERRAL_INBOUND_BELL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`referralInboundBellLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-29: "ok go" (plan: a notification with a Confirm button for each new referral card). Acts only while `GATE_REFERRAL_INBOUND_CONFIRM` is on. Every 15 minutes (scheduler job `referral-inbound-bell`, `syncReferralInboundBells` in `server/services/referral-inbound-bell.js`) each card in Referrals → Queue gets one admin bell row (category `customer`, `dedupeKey` `referral-inbound:<customerId>`), "Customers — confirm <name>'s referrer", linking to `/admin/referrals?tab=queue`. It rings once per card; a changed card rewrites the row quietly; a card that leaves the list and comes back rings again. The row carries buttons (`docs/admin-notifications.md` section 2, part 9). **Confirm <referrer>** runs the Queue's own `confirmInboundReferral` with that referrer. It is offered only for one sure referrer (the link code's owner, or the one customer whose first and last name match the name the caller gave), only while the program defers rewards to the first visit (`require_service_completion`), only before the friend's first performed plan visit, and only when the confirm would not earn the referrer a milestone (3, 5 or 10 conversions pay a bonus and send a text at once). So the tap sends nothing and moves no money: the $25 credits and the referrer's one 9:00 AM email follow the first plan visit. The tap runs the confirm with `deferredOnly`: under the customer's row lock it checks again that the referrer is still the one sure referrer and that no plan visit is on record, then converts on the same transaction (`convertReferral` with the caller's transaction), and the conversion refuses an at-once reward or a milestone under the promoter row lock. So a refusal saves nothing, and two taps at the same moment cannot pay a milestone. A plan visit that completes while the confirm runs is credited right after it, as the Queue's confirm does, so that visit's credit is not lost. **Not a referral** runs `dismissInboundReferral`. Each tap reads the card again and answers 409 with a short message when the card was answered, the referrer changed, or one of those holds applies. The row closes when the card is answered anywhere (`closeReferralInboundBell`, called by both Queue steps) or leaves the list; with `GATE_REFERRAL_INBOUND_CONFIRM` off, open rows close. Only admin logins see the row and its buttons. Off: no row is raised, open rows serve no buttons, and a tap answers 409. Rollback: unset the variable; answers already given stay.

Close-only bell buttons (dark): `GATE_ALERT_CLOSE_BUTTONS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`alertCloseButtonsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-29: "ok go" (bell buttons plan, PR 2: close buttons next). Three admin bell rows carry one server-set button (`docs/admin-notifications.md` section 2, part 9, kind `close_note`): **Handled** on a customer's text thread (trigger `sms_reply`), **Called back** on a text call-back follow-up (`sms_operational_followup`, call-back promises only; an email follow-up gets none, because Done settles text follow-ups only) and on a missed call (`customer_missed_call`). A tap is the bell's own Done with the button's label as the resolution (`markAdminDone` by the person, fenced on the version the tap claimed, so a new text that rewrote the row meanwhile answers 409 and stays open), then it settles a text follow-up the row speaks for, as Done does (`settleCommitmentsForDoneAlert`). A follow-up row that is no longer call-back only writes `buttons: null`, so its refresh drops the button. It sends no reply and places no call. The emitters write the button when they raise the row, so rows raised before the change carry none. Only admin logins see the buttons; technicians keep Done. Off: the rows serve no such button and a tap answers 409. Rollback: unset the variable; rows already closed stay closed and can be reopened from Recently done.

Bid invite bell buttons (dark, a trial): `GATE_BID_ALERT_BUTTONS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidAlertButtonsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and only while `GATE_BID_DESK` is on too. Owner 2026-10-29: "bid buttons, as a trial, make sure to add an admin bell, a week out, to see how they are in production" (week-1 read-out: ops job `bid-buttons-trial-week1`, Nov 5 12:30 ET). A new bid invite's bell row (`bid-desk:new:<bid>`) stores **No bid** and **Bid** (`docs/admin-notifications.md` section 2, part 9, kind `bid_decision`); when the bell list is served, one read of the page's bids shows No bid while the bid is still new and Bid only once its due date is confirmed on the Bid desk. A tap runs the Bid desk's own save step (`saveBidUpdate`, the page's Save decision) under the bid-row lock, refusing a bid already decided (the row closes with that note) and Bid without a confirmed date (the row stays open). A decision closes the bid's bells exactly as Save does. It sends nothing to a buyer or customer and moves no money. Only admin logins see the buttons. Off: the rows serve no such button and a tap answers 409. Rollback: unset the variable; a wrong decision is set back on the Bid desk.

Report text to on-location contacts: `GATE_CONTACT_REPORT_TEXT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`contactReportTextLive()`). On, when the account holder's visit-complete text goes out (sent, or queued for the send window), each confirmed on-location contact gets one plain text with the report link (`contact_report_ready` template; no pay link, no review ask). "Confirmed" is the appointment-text rule: consent-stamped, not the account holder's own number, not held by an unconfirmed opt-in ask. The text rides the scheduled-SMS rail (`sms_log` status `scheduled`, entry point `contact_report_ready_deferred`): the executor rechecks the gate, the contact, the report age (24 hours) and a combined-stop summary's token before the send and again at the provider boundary. One text per contact per report (`metadata.contact_report_key`). On, the combined-stop summary text goes to the account holder instead of Contact 1. Known limit: an account holder with texts off, or on the App channel for visit-complete notices, gets no visit-complete text, so contacts get no report text (a contact with an email still gets the report email); the portal contact card states that condition in its wording. Off = no contact text is queued, a queued one is dropped at its recheck, and the summary recipient is unchanged. Rollback: unset the gate. That is the only supported switch: deactivating the `contact_report_ready` template row stops the contact text but leaves the summary recipient and the portal wording on.


Staff onboarding documents (owner 2026-10-08): `GATE_STAFF_ONBOARDING_DOCS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`staffOnboardingDocsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`); also needs `GATE_CONTROLLED_STAFF_DOCUMENTS`. An admin ticks "Required at onboarding" on a staff document in the staff documents page (migration `20261008120000_staff_document_onboarding_required` adds `document_templates.onboarding_required`, default false, staff documents only, nothing seeded; the checkbox works with the gate off). On, the required documents are DERIVED on every read in `server/services/staff-onboarding.js`, with no assignment step and no writes: a document is outstanding for an active staff member who can open it (admin-only documents reach administrators only) until they have an acknowledgment (policy) or a COMPLETED record (form, procedure) on its CURRENT issued version, so a newly issued version is outstanding again by itself and a deactivated hire leaves no open row. `GET /api/tech/staff-documents/onboarding` answers the caller's outstanding documents `[{document_id, title, kind, version_id, due_at}]` and counts; `GET /onboarding/team` (admin) lists each active member's signed and outstanding documents on the staff documents page. `due_at` is display only (hire date or version effective date, whichever is later, plus 7 days; null for a policy). The Today page shows an in-page card "Sign N documents to finish setup" (`client/src/components/staffDocuments/OnboardingCard.jsx`) that opens the first outstanding document in the reader. Off = both endpoints answer `{ enabled: false, documents: [] }` with no query and no card. Sends nothing to a customer or staff member. Rollback = unset.

Truck clock-in (owner 2026-10-25, "this works"): `GATE_TRUCK_CLOCK_IN` — **ships DARK and RECORD-ONLY: `shadow` is the only value that does anything; anything else, `true` included, is off**, read at call time (`truckClockInMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`, exactly `shadow`, trimmed, any case). The rule being measured: a technician's shift starts at the truck's first GPS arrival at one of their visits that day, or at the start of the truck's first trip of the day when that trip starts within 200 m of the office (`RouteOptimizer.HQ`); "first trip" means no earlier trip-start of a DIFFERENT trip for the same truck (vehicle IMEI) in `bouncie_webhook_log` since the start of that Eastern work day, matched through the receiver's own event-name normalizer. Both Bouncie receivers log a copy of the same event, so trips are told apart by identity (`transactionId`/`tripId`; with none, an identical payload or a trip-start time within 2 minutes is the same trip; if that cannot be shown the row counts as a different trip, which suppresses the office trigger and leaves a later arrival to fire). It would only clock in a technician with no active shift who has a completed Vehicle Use & Commuting Agreement (`staff.vehicle-use-commuting-agreement`, checked with `hasCompletedIssuedRecord` in `server/services/staff-onboarding.js`). Home-to-first-stop driving is unpaid commute under that agreement. Training days stay by hand: a trainee rides in the trainer's truck, so no Bouncie device maps to the trainee. The hook is `server/services/truck-clock-in.js`, called from the Bouncie webhook receiver (`server/routes/webhooks-bouncie.js`) after the arrival detector, in its own try/catch. The FIRST trigger per technician per Eastern work day wins: it writes one `truck_clock_in_shadow` row (`technician_id`, `work_date`, `trigger` = `first_arrival` or `office_trip_start`, `event_at`, `would_clock_in`, `skip_reason`, `lat`, `lng`; unique on technician + work date), and later triggers that day do nothing. `skip_reason` is `already_clocked_in`, `agreement_not_signed` or `agreement_unknown` (the agreement check failed to read). This release NEVER writes `time_entries` and never calls the time-tracking service; live clock-in (the shift write at the GPS time, an atomic claim and a retry) is a separate later change that will add its own value. Clock-out, the 9 PM reminder and the 11 PM close are unchanged. Sends nothing to a customer or staff member. Rollback = unset.

Series moves skip closed days: `GATE_SERIES_MOVE_SKIP_CLOSED_DAYS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`seriesMoveSkipClosedDaysLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-22 ("fix series edit"): staff moved one visit of a monthly plan to a fifth Thursday, the move re-anchored the plan to the last Thursday, and the next visit landed on Thanksgiving, a closed day nobody picked. A staff series move (`rescheduleSeries` with initiator `admin`: the dispatch board, Edit appointment, a collective single-visit move, the call-proposal review card) re-dates the plan's later visits; staff moves skip the closed-day refusal by design so the owner can book his own day off, so those later dates were never checked. On, each later visit that lands on a closed day (an owner blackout date, a weekly day off or a closed holiday, `scheduling/blackout-dates.js` `getBlackoutLayers`) moves forward to the next open day with the shared nudge the Edit appointment cadence rewrite and the recurring seeder use (`scheduling/blackout-nudge.js` `clearOfBlackout`, re-applying the weekend rule; three closed weeks in a row keep the date). The date the staffer picked stays as picked. The staff preview (`previewSeriesMove`) shows the same dates, so a reviewed apply matches. Owner 2026-10-24 ("FIX") extended it to a customer web move that hands its later visits to dispatch (deferred placement, `GATE_CUSTOMER_RECURRING_DISPATCH`): that move checks only its picked date against closed days, so a hand-off took a closed day as its due date (10-23: a customer's move to a Friday put an untimed visit on Christmas). Its later visits now skip closed days the same way, due date included, and the page that names the next visit's date (`projectNextVisitDates`) projects the same way, so it never names a date the move will not write. Other customer, SMS, call-pipeline and technician series moves are unchanged (they still refuse a closed projected date). The closed days are read once per move or page (`loadSeriesClosedDays` in `rebooker.js`, which holds the rule for who skips them). The read covers one-off closed dates for 3 years ahead; weekly days off and closed holidays hold on every date. A failed read projects as before. Inside the move's transaction the closed days are read again under the closure fence (`lockClosureState`, shared); a day closed while the move waited for its locks refuses the move (409 `SERIES_CHANGED`, reload and try again). Off = every projected date is byte-identical to before, with one exception that applies with the gate on or off: at the Feb–Oct season edge, the collision walk that moves a visit off a date another visit of the plan already took now skips taken dates when the season clamp walks a November date back into October (before, it could settle on the taken Oct 31 and write two visits on one day; Codex #6500 r1). Sends nothing by itself (the move's own text, if any, names the dates it wrote). Code: `makeSeriesProjector` in `server/services/rebooker.js`.

Hired button (dark): `GATE_HIRED_PACKET` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`hiredPacketLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-25 (D7): on a prospective placeholder row, an admin's "Hired" action on the Staff page (Team tab) takes the hire's name, email, first day and pay, makes the row an active staff account (`POST /api/admin/timetracking/technicians/:id/hire`: `employment_status` active, `field_dispatchable` stays false, `must_change_password` true, a 7-day set-password token, audit event `staff.hired` with ids only) and emails the hire ONE welcome message with a "Set your password" link and a pointer to the Onboarding card. "Resend link" (`.../hire/resend`, 60-second cooldown) shows for an active staff member who has not set a password yet. Off: no button, both endpoints answer 404 `{ enabled: false }` before any database work, and `GET /technicians` carries no new fields. Each click sends one email to one staff address, never a customer; an email failure never undoes the hire (the answer says `emailed: false` or `'uncertain'`). Rollback = unset the variable; the manual steps (rename, email, Active, Forgot password) always still work. Form prefill from the staff record is `GATE_STAFF_DOC_PREFILL` (next paragraph).

Staff form prefill (dark): `GATE_STAFF_DOC_PREFILL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`staffDocPrefillLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy; also needs `GATE_CONTROLLED_STAFF_DOCUMENTS`). Owner 2026-10-25: the hiring paperwork is prefilled from the staff record. A NEW record on a staff form opens with fields filled from the owner's `technicians` row through a table in `server/services/staff-documents.js` (`PREFILL_MAP`, template key to field id to column); the only entry is `staff.vehicle-use-commuting-agreement`: `vehicle` from `vehicle_name`, `home-address` from `address`, `start-date` from `hire_date` (YYYY-MM-DD). Code never fills a checkbox or a `signed-name` field, only fields the version has, and skips empty values. `GET /api/tech/staff-documents/versions/:id/prefill?owner_id=` (same auth as the record routes; current issued form version only; a non-admin may only ask for themselves, else 403) answers `{ answers, fields }` and reads only. `GET /:id` carries `prefill: true` while the gate is on, and `DocumentRecord.jsx` then fetches it, fills only empty fields (a typed value always wins), refetches when the admin changes the owner (replacing only values the last prefill put there) and shows "Filled from the staff record: <labels>. Check each before you save." Nothing is saved or sent until the signer saves; the typed signature stays the signer's. Off: the endpoint answers 404 `{ enabled: false }` before any query and the form opens empty. Fields the Hired dialog does not collect (vehicle, home address) stay empty until an admin sets them on the staff record. Rollback = unset the variable.

Review bonus credit (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_BONUS_ASK_FIRST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`reviewBonusAskFirstLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Census M8 (second technician, 2026-10-25): `services/review-incentives.js` `resolveTechnicianForGoogleReview` names the technician a Google review bonus goes to. Today it takes the latest service record in the 45 days before the review, so a pest + lawn customer who saw both technicians that week credits whoever came last, and two visits on one date tie. On: the review ask that reached the customer comes first, the latest `review_requests` row with a technician DELIVERED in the 45 days before the review, by email (`sent_at`) or by text (`sms_sent_at`; the completion-SMS and composer asks stamp only that one); nothing found = today's order (latest service record, latest completed visit, latest ask). A click on the ask link (`redirected_at`) is not used: nothing proves the customer made it, and an undelivered ask's link can be opened by anyone who holds it (Codex #6755 security review). The payout row then also carries that ask's id. All three callers follow it: the payout writer, the attribution queue and the manual confirm. Existing payout rows are never re-attributed. Bonus pay, so the owner flips it. Sends nothing. Off = today's order byte for byte. Rollback: unset it.

Leaderboard callback credit (dark): `GATE_CALLBACK_SOURCE_TECH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`callbackSourceTechLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Census M9 (second technician, 2026-10-25): the admin dashboard leaderboard (`routes/admin-dashboard.js` `computeCoreKpis`) counts a callback (`service_records.is_callback`) against the technician who did it, so the owner who fixes the hire's visit shows the callback and the hire shows none. On: `services/callback-credit.js` credits each callback in the window to the technician of the newest earlier regular record (not itself a callback) of the same customer, in the same service category (`auto-dispatch/service-category.js` `classifyServiceCategory` on the names), within 60 days (on the callback's own date, only a record created before the callback's record); none found = the callback's own technician. Jobs, revenue, revenue per hour and margin stay with the technician who did the work; only the callback count and rate move. A credited technician with no job in the window gets a row; an id with no technicians row joins "Unassigned". Reads only, on an owner-only screen; the company-wide callback rate is unchanged. Off = no extra query, same leaderboard. Rollback: unset it.

Visit tech relay (dark): `GATE_CUSTOMER_TEXT_TO_VISIT_TECH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`customerTextToVisitTechLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Census M3 (second technician, 2026-10-25): every automated text (on-the-way, arrived, reminders) leaves from the location line (`services/twilio.js` `deriveOutboundNumber`), so a reply such as "the gate is open" or "the dog is out" reaches the office inbox and the owner only, never the technician on the way. On: `routes/twilio-webhook.js` calls `services/visit-tech-relay.js` for a known customer's text to any office line (not a technician line; `services/tech-line.js` handles those), when the sender's number belongs to exactly ONE live customer across every identity phone slot (primary, service contacts, second phone); a number on two customers relays nothing, even when the webhook matched one by the primary phone. The call is registered before the consuming branches (reschedule reply, lead intake), so a consumed reply is relayed too, and runs after the response is sent. The technician of each of the customer's visits TODAY (Eastern) that is en route or on site, or is that technician's next open stop (the first open visit of the technician's day plan not already en route or on site, ordered COALESCE(route_order, 999), COALESCE(window_start, '23:59'), created_at, id as in `services/stops-ahead.js`), gets the tech-home text card (`tech_line_sms`, headline "Text from your customer") and one push. One card per technician per text. A visit counts only while it is a live stop, by the `services/stops-ahead.js` predicates: no terminal or rescheduled status, no tracker-terminal `track_state` (`complete` / `cancelled`), no expired estimate-slot hold; en route or on site reads from the status or the tracker (`track_state` `en_route` / `on_property`). The rows of one appointment (technician, date, customer, window) are one stop: a row whose sibling is underway belongs to the current stop, never the next one. No copy for an admin technician (the owner already gets the office bell), an inactive or office-only (not field-dispatchable) account, a text to the AI customer-chat line, a STOP / START / HELP keyword, a reaction, a courtesy-only text or a staff sender. The office inbox, bell and owner forward are unchanged. Sends nothing to a customer. Inert today: the only technician is an admin. Off = no visit read. Rollback: unset it.

Series-move text hold: `GATE_SERIES_MOVE_TEXT_COALESCE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`seriesMoveTextCoalesceLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner ruling 2026-10-06: staff moved one recurring series twice a minute apart and the customer got two texts (`appointment_recurring_placement_confirmed` for Thursday Oct 15, then Wednesday Oct 14). On, the customer text of a staff series move from the dispatch board or the Edit appointment modal (`series_moves.source_surface` `dispatch_board` or `edit_modal`) is held 3 minutes from that move's commit, then sent only if no newer move exists. A newer move = a committed `series_moves` row for the same customer, text requested, from one of those two surfaces, that moved the same anchor visit or whose recorded shifted set (`result.rescheduledOccurrences`) includes it. Sharing a recurring parent is not enough: a series move shifts only the picked visit and later ones, so moving a later occurrence does not drop an earlier move's text. If one exists, the older text is dropped: the row concludes as a non-send (`notified_at` set, `customer_notified=false`), `result.textSupersededBy` names the newer move, and the log says so. Each move holds from its own first effects pass after the commit (recorded as `result.textHoldStartedAt`; `series_moves.created_at` is the transaction start, so a move that waited on locks would otherwise reach its hold already expired), so a chain of moves less than 3 minutes apart ends in one text, for the last move, about 3 to 4 minutes after it. If the lookup for a newer move fails, the text stays held (`notified_at` empty) and the next pass tries again, until the move is 30 minutes old; then the text is sent anyway. The release sweep and the 15-minute reconciler follow the same rule. Only the customer text waits: reminder rows, the conflict card, board broadcasts and the reminder-window cover all run at once, and the covered reminder windows stay covered while the text is pending. A held or superseded pass returns `notificationSent: null` (not `false`, so no "text failed" notice shows on a staff screen). The hold uses the existing series-move deferral, not a new queue: `notified_at` stays NULL and the existing `series-move-effects-reconcile` job in `server/index.js` re-runs the pass when the hold ends. That job now ticks every minute under its one lock. With the gate off it returns before the lock except on the quarter hour, so it selects exactly what the old `*/15` schedule did. With the gate on, the quarter-hour tick selects the normal rows plus held staff texts (`reconcileSeriesMoveEffects({ heldTexts: 'with' })`), and the ticks between select only held staff texts (`'only'`): committed, text requested, `notified_at` empty, 3 to 30 minutes old, tried at most every 2 minutes, whatever else is unfinished on the row (a failed reminder sync is retried by the same pass). Not held: Quick Move (its own moved text), customer web page, SMS reply and call moves, and single-visit moves. Off = the text goes out the moment the move commits, as before. Rollback: unset the gate. Code: `server/services/series-move-text-coalesce.js`, `applySeriesMoveEffects` and `reconcileSeriesMoveEffects` in `server/routes/admin-dispatch.js`.

New client booking confirmation by text AND email (dark): `GATE_NEW_CLIENT_CONFIRM_EMAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`newClientConfirmEmailLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-24: "send SMS/email as the default for new appointment bookings for new clients". The trigger was a new commercial lead whose office line was a VoIP number that cannot take texts. Today a booking confirmation is text first, with an email only when the text fails. On, `resolveConfirmationChannel` (`server/services/appointment-reminders.js`) promotes a confirmation whose channel resolves to the default `sms` to `both`, so the existing text + email path delivers it (no second send path). Both confirmation senders use it: `deliverConfirmation` (admin and inline bookings) and `deliverConfirmationByChannel` (self-service, estimate accept, call-created). It promotes only when ALL hold: the customer has no `scheduled_services` row with status `completed`, and `customers.member_since` (the became-a-customer date) is unset or within the last 90 days (both read at send time; the April 2026 import brought about 500 active customers whose visits predate the portal, so they have no completed row but an old `member_since`); the notification settings were readable; the customer did not pick the confirmation channel in the portal (`notification_prefs.appointment_confirmation_channel_explicit`, stamped by `server/routes/notifications.js` on any customer write of `appointmentConfirmationChannel`; migration `20261024210000_confirmation_channel_explicit.js`, default false; `20261024230000_confirmation_channel_explicit_backfill.js` marks every row that existed before the stamp as picked, because a stored `sms` from before it may be a deliberate Text choice, so only a customer created after this change can be promoted); portal-wide email and the New Appointment Confirmation toggle are on; and the confirmation email's own recipient resolution finds a usable address. Anything else, and any failed lookup, keeps today's text-first behavior. The 72h and 24h reminders, en-route, reschedule and cancellation notices are unchanged. Door: two-way (unset the variable). Blast radius: every new client's booking confirmation gains an email; no existing client changes. **Who flips: owner** (it sends customer email). Rollback: unset `GATE_NEW_CLIENT_CONFIRM_EMAIL`.

Reschedule and cancellation notices by email (dark): `GATE_MOVE_NOTICE_EMAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`moveNoticeEmailLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-24: "reschedule email". A customer whose line cannot take texts (a landline, or a number a carrier bounced) heard nothing when a visit moved or was cancelled: those two texts had no email version (production 2026-10-24: 24 active customers have such a line, all with an email on file; 2 of their visits were cancelled in the last 60 days with no notice). On, `deliverMoveNoticeEmail` (`server/services/appointment-reminders.js`) sends the same notice by email (`appointment.rescheduled` / `appointment.cancelled`, seeded by `20261025030000_seed_move_notice_email_templates.js`, stream `transactional_required`) when the reschedule text (`handleReschedule`, and `sendRescheduleNoticeForVisit` in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js`) or the cancellation text (`sendCancellationNotice`) reached no recipient, or when a carrier later bounces it (`handleUndeliveredSms`; a bounced reschedule text gets this email instead of the confirmation email it gets with the gate off). Never for a held text (send window, visit move, unreadable settings, an App push in flight): those are deferrals. Never for a text its own pre-dispatch check refused (a reclaimed cancellation lease, a restored visit, a failed fence read, a reschedule that moved again, ended or is gone). The email is sent only while the notice is still true (a reschedule: the visit is live, the quoted slot is ahead and unchanged, no grouped move holds it; a cancellation: the visit is still cancelled), checked before the send and again at the email's dispatch boundary. One email per notice: a reschedule is keyed by the notice's own stamp (`move_notice_at` on the text's audit rows); a cancellation is bound to its own notice: the text is stamped with the notice's claim token (`cancel_notice_at`) and the visit's restoration count (`cancel_restorations`), and the email needs the reminder row to still carry that token and the count to be unchanged, checked before the send and at the dispatch boundary (a newer cancellation re-claims with its own token and may have asked for no notice); the key is the restoration count, so the sweep's retries of one cancellation share it. A bounced text's email quotes the slot that text quoted (`rendered_slot_ms`, or `move_notice_slot_ms` for a windowless text); with neither on record, no email. No stored-copy rail re-sends these emails (category `appointment_move_notice`, `server/constants/email-replay-exclusions.js`): a provider-blocked or bounced one settles as not sent, because a later replay would skip the still-true check. The no-show detector counts a delivered reschedule email as the new arrival promise (`APPOINTMENT_EMAIL_EVENTS`; its key keeps the slot in segment 3, `na` for a windowless visit, which promises no slot; a notice that moved a grouped stop records the text's `notificationEventKey` and ends its key in `:stop`, so it speaks for every member), and migration `20261025040000` puts `appointment.rescheduled` back in the detector's partial index. No usable email raises the no-channel admin alert. Operator results say when the email went out. Off = today's behavior, no reschedule or cancellation email. Who flips: the owner (customer email).

Second technician, same hour (dark): `GATE_MULTI_TECH_CONFIRM` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`** (`gateEnvValue`), read at call time via `multiTechConfirmLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner-approved 2026-09-29 for capacity mode; owner 2026-10-30 ("so techs can and will book the same hr"): it now works with `GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` OFF too, which is how production runs today. On, each technician's route is separate: a row blocks a technician only when it carries that technician's id or no technician id, and unassigned rows still block every technician. One reader decides it, `techScopedConfirmActive()` in `server/services/scheduling/occupancy.js` (the gate alone, hour mode or capacity mode). Sites: `findConflictingVisits` takes an opt-in `technicianId` (the commit probe of /book, estimate holds in `slot-reservation.js`, the phone agent, admin and rebooker saves); `/book`'s offer mirror and confirm legs (`routes/booking.js`; capacity mode already scoped the offer with the gate off, kept byte for byte); the estimate offer filter and ASAP packing dates (`estimate-slot-availability.js` `filterCollidingSlots`, `stopDatesInRange`); the whole-route fit in hour mode (`arrival-route.js` `rowIsFixedBlock`: another technician's stop or hold is no fixed block); the open-hours hint (`find-time-hints.js`); and the pick that names a technician for a new visit (`pick-technician.js`, office Auto, phone agent). Not covered: the old by-city engine for lead replies and text drafts (`availability.js`, its own gate `GATE_MULTI_TECH_TEXT_TIMES`), the assistant's open-times list (`assistant-route-times.js`, stays tech-blind and only offers fewer hours), the grouped-visit mover and tech-out move. Concurrency is unchanged: every writer takes the date-wide occupancy lock first. Off = every probe is tech-blind, byte for byte. Rollback = unset.

Text-side appointment times from the website booking engine (multi-technician booking PR 4; `server/services/scheduling/text-offer-times.js`): `GATE_MULTI_TECH_TEXT_TIMES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `multiTechTextTimesLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-06 ("go PR 4"; lead replies know only a city, so use the city centre). Three read-only callers still asked the old by-city engine (`services/availability.js` `getAvailableSlots`: a city maps to a zone, hourly slots, no technicians, no routes). On, they ask the engine the website offers from (`routes/booking.js` `availabilityForPin`, per technician and route-aware), so a text offers the times /book would, including a second technician's free time: (1) the lead reply agent's `check_next_availability` (`lead-response-tools.js`); (2) the text drafter's city-based OPEN TIMES fallback and its send-time recheck (`sms-shadow-drafter.js`, used when `GATE_SMS_OFFERS_SCHEDULER` has no picker for the text; the scheduler path already reads the website engine and is unchanged). The fallback is one more offer source, `website_engine`, on the scheduler plumbing: an estimate-linked draft takes its service from the linked estimate through `funnelKeyForEstimate` (an estimate the website engine cannot represent keeps the old finder), and the draft's `open_times_snapshot.lookup` is stamped `source: 'website_engine'` plus its `serviceKey`, so the send-time recheck asks the engine that built the snapshot whatever the gate says by then; a snapshot with no source is the old finder's and is rechecked there (a gate-off draft carries no stamp); (3) the estimate converter's first service day (`estimate-converter.js` `pickFirstServiceDate`), only when the accepted estimate is ONE website funnel service (`funnelKeyForEstimate`, through the `sms-book-funnel-map.js` table: every sold recurring line must map to the same key); a multi-service, combined or unmapped estimate keeps the old engine, and the converter asks `internal`, so it does not depend on `GATE_SELF_BOOKING` or the account being signed in. A known customer is offered times only if `bookableOfferCustomer` (`routes/booking.js`, shared with `availabilityForExistingCustomer`) allows it: an active account, and no blocked pre-customer stage under `bookingCustomersOnly`; otherwise, or with no resolvable pin, no times (never the city centre). The pin is the customer's own booking pin when there is one, else (a lead with no customer record) the CITY CENTRE: the city's fixed point in `services/pest-forecast/locations.js` (Manatee, Sarasota and Charlotte rows), else the centre of its service zone (`service_zones.center_lat/lng`, what /book uses for a bare city), else nothing (a city Waves does not serve gets no times). The drafter's service is mapped to a /book funnel service through `sms-book-funnel-map.js`: a text naming none gets general pest times, a named service /book does not book gets none. Old-engine rules that do not exist in the website engine go away for these callers: the per-city zone day list and the 15-minute `booking_config` buffer; the website engine's route-day, travel and notice-window rules apply. Dropping the gate returns all three to the old engine, byte for byte. Not covered, on purpose: the customer assistant's `check_availability` and `book_appointment` in `ai-assistant/tools-expanded.js` (loaded only by `managed-assistant.js`, which no runtime path loads; the live assistant has no booking tool), and `getAvailableSlots` / `confirmBooking` stay in `availability.js` until the gate has held a quiet week.

Managed Agents session cost guards: `GATE_AGENT_SESSION_GUARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`agentSessionGuardLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, two things change (`server/services/agent-control/session-guard.js`). (1) The blog writer, refresher and content engine (`agent_content`), the meta rewriter (`agent_meta`), the backlink strategy agent (`agent_backlink`), the weekly briefing (`agent_bi`) and the lead response agent (`agent_lead`) create each session with a hard spend cap at list price: 1000, 100, 500, 300 and 100 cents; `AGENT_SESSION_BUDGET_CENTS_<LANE>` (for example `AGENT_SESSION_BUDGET_CENTS_AGENT_LEAD=250`, a whole number of cents) overrides one lane. At the cap the platform pauses the session and the runner ends the run as `budget_exhausted` in the call ledger, the same way as any other failed run (the lead agent's standard reply fallback still applies). The customer assistant (`agent_assistant`) has no cap: its session is one conversation over many turns. (2) When a runner ends a session with a failure (its own deadline, its own event cap, a broken stream), `recordSessionUsage` first sends that session a `user.interrupt` and waits up to 10 seconds for it to stop, so it makes no more model requests nobody reads and the ledger reads its settled usage; a failed interrupt is logged and changes nothing. The customer assistant is never interrupted: its session takes the customer's next turn. Off = sessions are created with no cap and are not interrupted, as before. First flip: watch the next session of each lane; a model with no list price makes a capped create answer 400, and unsetting the gate restores the old body. Sends nothing to a customer.

Draft estimates retired after a send: `GATE_ESTIMATE_DRAFT_RETIRE_ON_SEND` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`estimateDraftRetireOnSendLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-06: a call left an auto draft, staff built and sent a second estimate, and the old drafts stayed in the list. On, a job every 15 minutes (`estimate-draft-retire` in `server/services/scheduler.js`, under `GATE_CRON_JOBS`) archives a draft when the same customer has an estimate that was really delivered and was created after the draft, at the same door, nobody edited the draft after that delivery, and the draft is at least 30 minutes old. Any service line counts (owner 2026-10-06). Delivery: `deliveryState.lastDeliveredAt`; the older tracking shape (non-empty `sentChannels`) only when the customer viewed the estimate; `sent_at` only for rows with no delivery tracking. Never a send: website quotes (`quote_wizard`, unauthenticated), report or plan-restart mints with no delivery, a row reset to draft or carrying a call-linkage invalidation marker. Same door: same `property_id` when both rows have one, else `samePremiseDisplay` with city and ZIP plus the same unit; up to 5 later sends are checked per draft, same door first. Kept: a draft linked to any lead (`leads.estimate_id`, or the draft's `estimate_data.lead_id` while that lead has no estimate link), open or closed, unless the lead is soft-deleted (owner 2026-10-08: staff delete it by hand; the sweep writes nothing to `leads`), drafts in an estimate group, with a scheduled send, a price lock, a live delivery claim, an estimator-engine hold, a live address hold, an uncertain send attempt, a booking-page handoff (`booking_intents`), a live clarification text, an assessment link, and one-tap or website quote drafts. Archive, not delete: `estimate_data.retiredBySentEstimate` names the sent estimate and the normal Unarchive action restores the draft; open notifications whose `metadata.estimateId` is the draft are closed through the notification done contract (`done_by = 'estimate-draft-retire'`). The sweep never waits on a lock (draft, its leads, then sent estimate, each `NOWAIT`; a busy row is retried next run), 200 archives per run. The first run after the flip clears the backlog (see the PR for the dry-run count). Sends nothing to a customer. Code: `server/services/estimate-draft-retire.js`.
Office alert after a report-only completion: `GATE_REPORT_ONLY_PAYMENT_ALERT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`reportOnlyPaymentAlertLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-30 (tech portal gaps audit, option A): a technician cannot record cash or a check (`/admin/invoices/:id/record-payment` is admin-only), so a completion that chose "report only, no pay link" can leave money the office never records. Every completion with `includePayLink === false` (visit completed, not backfill, not a system or issued-invoice closeout, no invoice already sent) saves `structured_notes.payLinkOmitted: true` on its service record, whatever the gate. On, a job hourly 8 AM–8 PM ET at :41 (`report-only-payment-alert` in `server/services/scheduler.js`, under `GATE_CRON_JOBS`; `server/services/report-only-payment-alert.js`) finds those records from before today (ET) within 30 days, takes each visit's newest live invoice (`completionNewestLiveInvoiceLookup`), and raises one needs-you Billing alert per invoice that is still owed (collectible status, balance due > 0, no payer, not withdrawn): "Billing — record <customer>'s $<due> payment", linked to the invoice, dedupe key `report-only-payment:<invoiceId>`, raised through `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen` (one ring per episode). The same pass closes an open alert whose invoice is paid, voided, processing, handed to a payer or no longer owed; a bill that is owed again (a returned bank debit) reopens and rings. Off: the marker is still saved; no alert is raised or closed. Office-side only: it sends the customer nothing.

Lawn watering forecast and rain close-out: `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_FORECAST` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `lawnWateringForecastLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); also needs `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_RULE` (no instruction exists without it). Lawn report rebuild P30, owner rulings 2026-09-30 (the report is a record, not a clock) and the robustness-ideas "must not" list. For a plain `water_in` instruction only (never a hold or hold-then-water-in): (1) at completion the write gate (`lawn-report-write-gate.js`) reads the property's hourly forecast (`fetchPropertyForecast`, 3 s deadline, fail-open) for the window completion to water-in deadline and, when the known total reaches the label amount, freezes ONE sentence in INCHES beside the instruction (`instruction.forecast`; it asks the customer to check the rain at a checkpoint six hours before the deadline, so it needs a forecast total to that checkpoint that reaches the label amount and at least six hours from completion to it, first writer wins, never inside `lines`, so the PDF, the watering text, the hero task and Ask Waves are unchanged); an unavailable, incomplete or below-amount forecast writes exactly today's instruction. (2) On the LIVE web view only, `attachLawnWateringCloseOut` (report-data.js, called from the `/data` route) asks MRMS radar (`mrms-qpe.js` daily rain) for whole Eastern days inside the frozen window and, when the measured total reaches the water-in amount, adds `banner.observedRain`, a qualified "near your address ... local totals may vary" note the client shows UNDER the instruction (the instruction stays visible); the radar request is aborted at the 2.5 s page deadline. Forecast never closes a water-in; no probability or percent anywhere; no model call; no new customer SMS or email. Both banner keys are removed from every non-live render, so PDF cache keys are untouched. Off: no forecast read, no radar read, payload and PDF byte-identical. Rollback = unset the variable; frozen `forecast` blocks stay in the record and are ignored. Contract detail in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`.

Lawn watering text for every product combination (owner 2026-10-22: "for all combinations, a text goes out, but the text is accurate"): `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_EVERY_VISIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnWateringEveryVisitLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); also needs `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_RULE` and `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_SMS`. On, six things change: (1) a catalog watering rule may carry `by_target` entries and the visit's logged targets pick them (`rulesForTargets` in `server/services/service-report/lawn-watering-rule.js`; Acelepryn: water in for grubs, hold for caterpillars; no covered target = the top-level rule, or for a target-only rule its first entry, the product's main use), and a hold's `then_water_in` (the label's "if no rain within N days, irrigate 0.5 inch") becomes a rain-counting water-in; (2) rule E in `lawn-watering-instruction.js`: a water-in the label requires the same day (Dylox) beside a hold that leaves it no deadline shortens each hold that carries a `label_minimum` (the owner's 24-hour herbicide hold, a "for best results" line) to that minimum and judges drying with 2 hours, not the 6-hour floor; a hold with no `label_minimum` is the label's own direction and stays; (3) a visit whose products need no watering change (state `none`) gets the "No watering change" text too (`lawn-watering-sms.js`); (4) a lawn visit that still has no instruction while the text was otherwise due raises ONE office alert (Comms, needs-you) naming the product with no rule or the clash, and marks the visit `skipped_no_instruction`; since 2026-10-27 (owner ruling) a visit closed on a later ET day than it was worked gets no instruction, no text and no alert and is marked `skipped_late_close` (`server/services/service-report/lawn-watering-late-close.js`: the first arrival stamp the report's staleness rule keeps, else the scheduled day, else the first raw arrival stamp, is on an earlier ET day than the completion, and an arrival is 12 or more hours before it; the report, its completion freeze and the Fast Complete preview all judge it so, and the report renders no watering steps for that visit), and a visit closed with no tech-confirmed photo read alerts as `no_lawn_read` (the steps are built with the lawn report, which needs the read), so `report_not_built` again means a failed build; (5) since 2026-10-24 a guessed rule (source `default`: the catalog derivation for a product with no stored label or owner rule) is no claim (`unchecked_rules`): no instruction, no text, and the alert names the guessed product, so a guess never reaches the customer; (6) since 2026-10-24 the label ladder for products whose watering clashes (owner: "if products clash, we need to develop a strategy ... check labels", and no office alert for a clash): a water-in whose window the label writes (`label_window` `directs` or `best_results`, and every same-day rule) counts from the application and never follows a hold, and one that also carries `rain_counts` (T-Storm 2G, one day) is written as a run, not the long rain line; rule E shortens a hold to its `label_minimum` for a label direction, and for a `best_results` window (T-Storm 2G) only when the hold is our own rule (`label_best_results` marks a hold whose part above the minimum is the label's own "for best results" line: that hold goes first and the window follows it, as in rule C); late in the day a same-day deadline may run to 11:59 PM, still with a 3-hour run, and an hours minimum the data marks `label_minimum.advisory` (label advice such as a rainfast figure, never a "do not irrigate" direction like SpeedZone's 3 hours) may end by 9 PM to make room; a hold with `yields_to_label_water_in` (Advion Insect Granule, whose label only warns that water may weaken the bait) gives way to a water-in the label directs, and the instruction records `yielded` (the bait and the water-in); a water-in with `beside_hold_by_hours` (a humectant's 24-hour root-zone step) uses that window whenever a hold shares the visit. The catalog data is migration `20261025020000_watering_rule_clash_keys` (25 products, each written only while its rule is still the value read on 2026-10-24, audited; every v13 program mix reads exactly as before): label windows for Acelepryn, Acelepryn Xtra and Tetrino on grubs, Armada, Headway G and Heritage G on fairy ring, and the root-dysfunction uses; T-Storm 2G as a best-results window; best-results holds for Talak, Blindside, Dismiss NXT, Drive XLR8, both irons, Three-Way and the Acelepryns on caterpillars; advisory minimums for Certainty, Fusilade II, Recognition, both SedgeHammers and Three-Way (SpeedZone's 3 hours is a direction and stays); Advion Insect Granule yields, and its precaution's skip-watering sentence becomes "Follow the watering steps on this report."; Hydretain and Moisture Manager take a 24-hour window beside a hold. A clash no label lets one text meet (two label directions with no full run left, such as Dylox with Anuew EZ after about 5 PM) stays no claim, and its no-claim names `holdProducts` and `waterInProducts`. Owner 2026-10-24: for the two clashes the technician fixes on site (`water_in_conflict`, `same_day_too_late`), the visit's technician gets a `lawn_watering_tech_note` card on the Today screen (`lawn-watering-tech-note.js`; once per visit: the marker `lawnWateringTechNoteAt` is claimed in the card's own transaction) instead of the office alert (too late with no hold: water the product in on site; a clash: "Do not water now", never water during the hold, and ask the customer to water in as soon as the no-water time is over), and the office alert is only the fallback when the visit has no technician or the card cannot be written.
