When a bait's no-water hold (Advion Insect Granule) gave way to a water-in its label requires (the frozen instruction carries `yielded`), one staff note goes on the customer's next live lawn visit saying the bait went down with a product that must be watered in, so it may get wet and may need to go down again (`lawn-watering-yield-note.js`). Off: today's instruction, text and no alert, byte for byte (a stored `by_target`, `label_minimum` or clash key is ignored; a rule with no top-level mode is no rule).

Lawn watering forecast from two sources, in the watering text: `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_TEXT_FORECAST` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `lawnWateringTextForecastLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); needs `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_FORECAST` (and so `GATE_LAWN_WATERING_RULE`). Owner 2026-10-22 ("account for weather ... we have two sources now"). If at least ¼ inch falls in that time, it counts as watering in today's treatment. If it does not, run the watering above right away." (`afterHold: true`). Rain inside the hold never counts; a hold that waits for drying, a long window, and a short water-in beside a long one get none. Estimate consumer notice: `GATE_ESTIMATE_CONSUMER_NOTICE` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `estimateConsumerNoticeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). (eff. 4-29-2025): the licensee first obtains the property owner's signed Consumer Notice Form FDACS-13692 Rev. 07/21 before a wood-destroying-organism treatment. Residential service agreement on the accepted estimate page: `GATE_ESTIMATE_SERVICE_AGREEMENT` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time (`estimateServiceAgreementLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). A signed service agreement for every residential recurring plan. On, the ACCEPTED estimate page (`cta.terminalState === 'accepted'`) of a residential estimate whose recurring plan carries a pest lane (recurring keys `pest_control`, `mosquito`, `rodent`, `rodent_bait`) or a lawn lane (`lawn_care`, `tree_shrub`, `palm_injection`) shows **Review and sign your service agreement**, one button per lane; a commercial estimate (authored proposal, auto-priced commercial, any `commercial_*` line), a termite-only plan, a one-time-only estimate and an estimate accepted as one-time service (`accepted_service_mode = 'one_time'`, which a mixed estimate keeps beside its quoted recurring rows) get nothing (commercial and termite programs have their own agreements). A second tap returns the same open agreement with a fresh link (only a link hash is stored) when it reads exactly as one issued now (same template version and text); any change cancels the stale open agreement and issues a new one; a signed agreement answers 409 `already_signed`; an estimate with no customer account 409 `no_account` and the page says to call. Merge values: `customer.name` from the account, `customer.address` is the estimate's own service address as written (the property the plan was accepted for, which may differ from the account's primary), else the account address, and with neither the route answers 409 `template_unavailable`; `service.name` is the lane's recurring line names joined with ` + ` (`Pest Control + Mosquito`), with no cadence (a bundle's `accepted_frequency_key` is the primary pest cadence while lawn keeps its own program, and both templates confirm service frequency before service begins); `agreement.start_date` is the first visit booked from the estimate, else `Your first scheduled visit`. The contract snapshot carries `estimate.id`, `estimate.lane` and `estimate.source = estimate_service_agreement`, so only an agreement issued here is reported or reused (one staff issued by hand is never re-linked). Signing changes nothing: the estimate, the booked visit, the invoice and the payment are never touched, and this route sends nothing to the customer (the existing signed-contract email then sends the signed copy, and the customer portal lists it under Documents → Agreements). `GET /api/estimates/:token/data` adds `cta.serviceAgreements` (`[{ lane, title, state, canSign, reason? }]`) for an accepted estimate only, never a staff preview, a draft preview or the document render. **Before the owner flips it**: the Residential Pest Service Agreement seeded by `20260601000009` is a scaffold (its cancellation paragraph says the terms "should be reviewed before sending") — publish the final residential terms as a new template version on the Contracts → Templates tab first; the Lawn & Ornamental agreement carries owner-approved terms already. The gate is re-read after the issuing locks and before any write, so a kill thrown mid-request writes nothing. Off = the route answers the generic 404 with the privacy headers from a pre-guard mounted before the global limiter (and skips its rate limit), `/data` carries nothing new, and the accepted page is byte-identical. Rollback: unset the variable.
Commercial agreement renewal reminder: `GATE_AGREEMENT_RENEWAL_REMINDER` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time (`agreementRenewalReminderLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Prepaid year end bell: `GATE_PREPAY_YEAR_END_BELL` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time (`prepayYearEndBellLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the daily renewal-reminder workflow (`server/services/workflows/renewal-reminder.js`, one extra leg after the annual prepay legs) runs `runPrepayYearEndBell` (`server/services/prepay-year-end-bell.js`). The PDF cache key gains `:photoset=1` only while the gate is live AND the visit's assessment carries the marker, so a marked visit's PDF cached before a flip is never served after it and a legacy visit keeps its stored PDF. Off: no model call, no read, and the payload, the PDF and its cache key are byte-identical. On, the AI picks facts and code writes every word: every sentence comes from the `TS_SENTENCES` constant (the owner reads and approves that one constant), filled only with display names from closed code-owned lists (conditions, plants and places, photo-finding labels) and the catalog names of the applied products. The completion step (`freezeTreeShrubTechParagraph`, called from `complete-scheduled-service.js` next to the lawn write gate, tree & shrub visits only) makes at most ONE model call per visit (lane `ts_tech_paragraph`, `TEXT_POLICIES.report`, one 15-second deadline across the whole step: assessment lookup, report build (no treatment-narrative call), input gather, model call and freeze; owner-visible in the AI cost ledger and `llm_dispatch_log`), and only when the technician left a note. The model's only job is extraction: it returns up to 3 `{ condition, plant }` pairs of closed-list ids from the note (structured-output enums, no numeric bounds) and nothing else; none of its text is ever printed. Code then verifies each pair against the note: the model judges whether it was a sighting today (seenToday) and gives the technician's exact words (quote); code keeps the item only when seenToday is true and the quote is word for word part of one note sentence that names the condition and no palm-banned term, and keeps the plant only when the quote names it (owner 2026-10-05: the model judges, the code verifies, no word list); a failing pair is dropped, never the whole paragraph. (product display names only; never an active ingredient), and "Your landscape looked excellent|good today." only when nothing else applies, the technician rated the landscape Excellent or Good and the visit has no technician note (any note keeps it out). A hidden or rewritten photo finding never enters. Not inputs: the seasonal watch list (`GATE_TS_WATCH_LIST`, tech-facing), the last visit, the report headline, product ingredients, targets and methods. A visit with no note gets the deterministic lines only (no model call); when the model call fails, times out or answers malformed the deterministic lines are frozen without any "saw" line or all-clear; with no sentence at all only a text-less marker is stored (never printed; a resumed completion makes no second call). A survivor freezes first-writer-wins under `structured_notes.treeShrubTechParagraph[assessmentId]` as `{ text, slots }`, is never regenerated at render, and at read time must equal the render of its slots under the CURRENT `TS_SENTENCES` and pass the palm rules (never Ganoderma, a conk, lethal bronzing or fusarium, never crown, spear leaf or newest fronds) and the customer-copy screen, else nothing prints. It prints as `reportV2.techParagraph` ("From your technician", under "What we applied today") on the web report and the PDF. Tree & shrub yearly neonicotinoid cap (owner 2026-10-09; `server/config/tree-shrub-neonic-caps.js`, `server/services/tree-shrub-neonic-ledger.js`, `server/services/tree-shrub-fast-context.js`, `client/src/lib/tree-shrub-neonic-cap.js`, `client/src/components/tech/FastCompleteTreeShrubSheet.jsx`): `GATE_TS_NEONIC_CAP` — **ships DARK: strict opt-in, exactly `true`**, read at call time via `tsNeonicCapLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). Tech-facing; no customer text changes. The cap is a label amount per acre per calendar year, scaled to the visit property's ornamental bed area (`customer_properties.bed_sqft`): Zylam 78.9 fl oz per acre (1.811 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft) and Safari 20 SG 43.2 oz per acre share ONE dinotefuran cap (an application is its amount over its own product's yearly amount, and the shares add up to 1); Merit 2F 25.6 fl oz per acre (0.588 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft) is a separate imidacloprid cap. Dominion 2L (same strength, same label limit) shares that imidacloprid cap. Zylam also has the label's count limit: an active Zylam row holds when three visits already applied it at the property this year. An active ingredient is matched anywhere in a product's ingredient text, so a two-active product (Temprid FX) is held too. A catalog product of either ingredient with no strength in the config (`uncapped`, for example another Merit formulation) holds an active row: it is never passed unchecked. The one exception is a trunk-injection product (Arborjet Ima-Jet): it is dosed per tree, so it gets a line, no hold, and its rows are not bed applications. Rows counted (`property_application_history`, that property, the calendar year in ET, retracted rows out, the visit being completed out): Zylam and Safari from ANY visit (ornamental products only here, so a lawn visit that also treated shrubs spends the allowance); every other row only from tree & shrub visits (a lawn imidacloprid application is another treated area, and Alpine WSG on a pest visit is structural). A row is classed by the name and ingredient FROZEN on the application, not the catalog's current ones. A row that cannot be sized (no quantity, a unit that does not convert, a product with no strength in the config) is counted as `unsized` and named on the sheet, never as zero in silence. Off: fast-context has no `neonicCap` key and the sheet shows nothing new. On: fast-context adds `neonicCap` ({ year, bedSqft, ingredients }, the year being today's in ET), and the sheet shows what is left under each capped product's amount and HOLDS Complete on an amount over it or one it cannot size. No bed area on file: the yearly AMOUNT cannot be computed, so the sheet says the bed area is needed and the amount check holds nothing. Lawn report "What the photos showed" (lawn report rebuild P23b; `server/services/service-report/lawn-photo-findings.js`, `report-data.js`, `LawnPhotoFindings` in `client/src/components/report/lawnV2/LawnReportV2.jsx`, `ServiceReportDocument` in `client/src/pages/ServiceReportDocument.jsx`): `GATE_LAWN_REPORT_PHOTO_FINDINGS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnReportPhotoFindingsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). Lawn score scale 2 (owner 2026-10-24, lawn scoring review; `server/services/lawn-visit-input.js`, `lawn-visit-result.js`, `lawn-visit-scores.js`, `lawn-visit-assessment.js`, `lawn-assessment-history.js`, `lawn-last-visit-scores.js`, `lawn-treatment-guide.js`, `server/routes/admin-lawn-assessment.js`; migration `20261024233000_lawn_assessments_score_scale.js`): `GATE_LAWN_SCORE_SCALE_V2` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnScoreScaleV2Live()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). Needs `GATE_LAWN_VISIT_ASSESSMENT` and `GATE_LAWN_PROPERTY_HISTORY` also on (the reader reports off without either). On: (1) the lawn visit assessment reads under its prompt version plus `-scale2` (`lawn-visit-v1-lighting-scale2`, `lawn-visit-v1-shot-list-lighting-scale2` and so on): the SCORES block asks for four 0-100 ratings against written anchors at 100 / 90 / 75 / 50 / 25 (`turf_density`, `weed_control`, `color_health`, `condition`; Condition counts thatch only where a photo shows the thatch layer) in place of scale 1's weed share of the lawn (stored as 100 minus it, so 95-99 on almost every lawn), color 1-10 x10 and the severity-word map for Condition. So at a lawn's first scale-2 visit everything that compares visits starts fresh, like a baseline reset: the report's since-last lines, prior-visit score line, before/after and trend chart, the paired-photo recheck and treatment memory (no prior visit), the baseline, the property score, the lawn health signal, the portal lawn health card and its `/history` timeline, and the technician's Last visit row (which follows the scale of the visit's own read: none at the first visit on a new scale). Reports of scale-1 visits keep their own scale-1 history. Outside property history the same rule holds: a treatment outcome's pre-assessment (`agronomic-wiki.js`) is on its post-assessment's scale, else the outcome has no deltas; the ROI improvement buckets and the neighbor benchmarks (`assessment-analytics.js`) compare within one scale, with one benchmark segment per scale (`<zip>|<grass>|s2` for scale 2; a scale with fewer than 3 customers in a segment shows no ranking); and the assistant's `get_lawn_health` compares the first and latest visit on the latest visit's scale; (4) the treatment guide's weed card reads a scale-2 row's rating ("Weed control scored N today.", the same line: 90 or lower), never a share of the lawn. Old rows are never rewritten. Off = byte-identical prompt, schema, stored run and scores; the history filter is a no-op while no row has `score_scale = 2`. Migration: nullable `lawn_assessments.score_scale` smallint, additive, no backfill. Rollback: unset the variable; rows already on scale 2 stay on it and compare only with each other.

Lawn paired-photo recheck (`server/services/lawn-paired-recheck.js`, lawn report rebuild P19b, owner ruling 2026-09-29 round 3b): `GATE_LAWN_PAIRED_RECHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `lawnPairedRecheckLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and false unless BOTH prerequisites are live too: `GATE_LAWN_VISIT_MEMORY` (it writes onto that store) and `GATE_LAWN_PROPERTY_HISTORY` (the prior visit exists only from the property-scoped history; without it the first render freezes `sinceLast: null` and that visit's one chance would be spent for nothing). With any of the three off it reads off. On, the report render that CREATES a visit's frozen memory entry (first healthy render; never a replay, a lost race or a degraded read) hands a background job (setImmediate, after the render returns; nothing the technician's Analyze or the render waits on) the entry. The job pairs last visit's and today's photos of the SAME shot, and only shots flagged `recheckPairable` in `shared/lawn-photo-shots.json` (front always; back only when both visits carry the `shot_list_v1` photo marker; `side` never, because it records no side of the property so two visits can show opposite sides; the report's before/after slider keeps its own wider `pairable` set, unchanged) for the same customer and the same recorded property, the prior being the entry's FROZEN `sinceLast.priorAssessmentId` (never a live latest lookup), usable photos (adequate or limited) on both sides only; problem-area and the other detail shots never pair (a different spot every visit and nothing identifies a watch item: no guess). ONE call per visit (at most 2 pairs, four images; `TEXT_POLICIES.lawnPairedRecheck`: Gemini then GPT-6 Sol, same models as `lawnVisitAssessment`, lane `lawn_paired_recheck`, prompt `lawn-paired-recheck-v2`) sees only the photos, the view names and the watch topics' plain names (no scores, products or prior verdicts) and answers better / same / worse / cannot_tell per pair and per watch topic with `what_changed` from a closed set (patch_size, color, edge, density). A better / same / worse answer that cites a pair the model could read (and, for better / worse, names a changed dimension) is written once, first writer wins per check, onto `structured_notes.lawnVisitMemory[assessmentId].sinceLast.checks[].recheck` as `{ verdict, source: 'photo_pair', whatChanged, pairs, promptVersion }` (the whole-lawn pair verdicts beside it as `sinceLast.photoPairs`), where the progress engine (`lawn-progress.js`) already reads it; cannot_tell writes nothing (the engine says unclear). Precedence in the engine: an `office_review` override (`check.recheckOverride`; no writer exists yet) beats `photo_pair`. Kill switch on the READ too: the progress engine takes a `photoPair` flag from its one production caller (`report-data.js`, which passes `lawnPairedRecheckLive()`), and with the gate off a stored `photo_pair` verdict is ignored (the check reads unclear, as before the feature) while an `office_review` decision still stands; the stored entry is left untouched, so turning the gate back on uses the verdict again. Watch topics are labelled neutrally (the frozen check stores only key and status, no cause or moisture direction): water is "a watering problem (too dry or too wet)"; mowing is never put to the model (a measured height, direction unknown). The answer must cover EXACTLY the pairs and watch topics sent (no missing, extra, unknown or duplicate entry, no empty list), else that provider leg is rejected and the fallback provider runs; if every leg fails nothing is written. A photo_pair verdict on a visit whose photos are not comparable still reads as unclear. The recheck fields never appear in the public report payload (`publicSinceLast`) and the job adds no customer sentence. Any miss (no pair, provider error or timeout, garbage, no entry) writes nothing and is logged. Off = no extra model call, no photo read, no stored field, every payload byte-identical.
Lawn rainfast breach watch (`server/services/service-report/lawn-rainfast-watch.js`, lawn report rebuild P31): `GATE_LAWN_RAINFAST_WATCH` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `lawnRainfastWatchLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); also needs `GATE_LAWN_VISIT_MEMORY` (it writes onto that store's frozen entry). LIVE web view only. A product is judged only when its catalog row states a rainfast interval (`products_catalog.rainfast_minutes`, read ONLY from the facts frozen with the visit in `reportIdentitySnapshot.productFacts`, never the live catalog; a frozen "no interval" is known-absent and not judged, while any applied product whose interval is unknown (no snapshot on an older record, a product the snapshot never saw or froze as not approved for reports, an unusable frozen interval) holds the whole verdict; seed data: Celsius WG 60, SpeedZone Southern 180, Primo Maxx 60, Chelated Iron Plus 60); no interval = never judged, nothing is inferred. Only the rendered `/data` view opts in (the Ask Waves build, also `mode: 'live'`, makes no weather call and no write). Nothing is judged until every interval on the visit is over: one hour after the LONGEST interval ended (and for 7 days at most), all intervals are judged in one pass and one item names every breached product; an interval that cannot be read holds back the whole verdict, and so does a failed read of the visit's products or their catalog facts (a stored verdict still replays; nothing new is judged or written until a healthy view). The live view reads the property's hourly weather-model rain for the past hours (Open-Meteo through `fetchPropertyForecast`, 2.5 s deadline; a model analysis, not a gauge) for the whole hours inside completion to completion + interval. A total of at least 0.25 inch records ONE `retreatCheck` item on the visit's frozen memory entry (`structured_notes.lawnVisitMemory[assessmentId].retreatCheck`: first writer wins, compare-and-set on the entry, never creates an entry, no row lock; the same UPDATE also re-asks the token route's read eligibility, `report_template_version = 'service_report_v1'` and not a suppressed typed report) and adds ONE fixed sentence to the lead's Watching line ("Our weather data shows rain soon after your treatment, which can reduce its effect. Tell us if results look weak."; 20 words, exactly the Watching word cap, so when it does not fit beside the writer's sentence it replaces that sentence; no number, no product name, and it commits Waves to no action). Every later view replays the stored item with no weather call. The next visit's `sinceLast` carries the item as engine input only (`publicSinceLast` leaves it off the payload); a retreat-check alone is enough to build that internal block (a support-product-only visit), and the engine, the since-last copy and the payload see no block for it. The first eligible `/data` view is enough (it reads the record again after its own memory step). As a helpful extra (the customer sentence promises nothing, so nothing depends on it), with the same gate and `GATE_LAWN_PROPERTY_HISTORY`, the lawn Fast Complete context (`GET /admin/dispatch/:serviceId/lawn-fast/context`, `lawn-fast-complete.js` `loadReCheckNote`) adds `reCheck: { line }` or `reCheck: null`, and the sheet shows the line ("Re-check last visit's treatment: weather data showed rain soon after it (<product names>).", at most three names) when the PRIOR lawn visit at the same property (the property-scoped `historyBeforeVisit` resolver) stored a retreat-check, read from that visit's own record for the same customer. Advisory and fail closed: any miss or failed read is `null` and never a read failure or a refusal; gate off or property history off leaves the key off, so the context is byte-identical. The job card has no natural slot for it. Any missing hour, failed or slow fetch, missing coordinates or missing completion time = no item and no sentence; intervals under 2 hours are read from Open-Meteo's quarter-hour series (`fetchPropertyRainQuarterHours`, same model), longer ones from the hourly series; the 0.25 inch test is on the unrounded sum, and a window with no whole slot inside it is never judged. The PDF, static builds, SMS and email never change; nothing is sent to a customer. Off: no weather read, no write, payload byte-identical. Rollback = unset the variable; stored `retreatCheck` items stay in the record and are ignored.

Lawn Fast Complete, server half (`server/services/lawn-fast-complete.js`, lawn report rebuild PR-C1): `GATE_LAWN_FAST_COMPLETE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnFastCompleteLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-03: every regular lawn visit type is eligible (recurring program visits first, then per-application and one-time lawn visits); the lawn re-service keeps its own sheet and gate (`GATE_LAWN_RESERVICE_FAST_COMPLETE`), Tree & Shrub (it shares the `lawn_care` category; reason `tree_shrub`, decided by the Tree & Shrub sheet's own predicate on the completion profile's findings type) keeps its sheet, the Waves Assessment visit its own diagnostic lane, and project-backed, companion-section and grouped visits take the full form (`lawnFastIneligibleReason` is the one eligibility function). The sheet must echo the context's whole `service` object as `expectedVisit` AND send `lawnFast: { visitType }` from the same context; the preflight recomputes the visit type with the same strict reads and refuses a change since open (409 `visit_identity_changed`, reason `visit_type_changed`) or an unreadable billing lane (503 `lawn_fast_visit_type_unavailable`, retry). The gate is checked first for every body carrying `lawnFast`, an `incomplete` outcome included; an incomplete outcome is then exempt from the identity, visit-type, eligibility and assessment checks. The photo minimum is advisory: a warning in the context, never a refusal. The schedule payload carries `lawnFastCompleteEnabled` per service. Customer-silent: sends no text or email; completion keeps its own messaging. Off = both routes answer 404 `{enabled:false}`, a `lawnFast` block is refused 409, the flag is false and nothing else changes. No migration. Lawn Fast Complete weed-spot rules (owner 2026-10-08; `server/services/lawn-weed-mix.js`, `lawn-fast-complete.js`, the sheet `FastCompleteLawnSheet.jsx`): `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_RULES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnSpotRulesLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_LAWN_FAST_COMPLETE` and the completion-defaults gates (the add-ons come from the plan); the weed entry also needs `GATE_LAWN_V13` (the group is read from the staged v13 protocol rows' `gates`, which exist only then). On, the lawn Fast Complete context (technician sheet only, no customer message, no public payload) carries `spotRules: true` and, in a window with weed spots, `plannedProducts.weedMix`: the add-on other add-ons name in `gates.tankMixWith` (Celsius WG) is the lead, those that name it are its members (Certainty, the nonionic surfactant), and the add-on whose `gates.trigger` is `celsius_annual_cap_reached` (Blindside) is the replacement. The sheet lists them as ONE "Weed spots" entry: one tap opens the lead and its members while the lead is under its yearly cap, and the replacement in their place once the plan's own limit reader (`v13VisitLimits`, any hard block reads as capped, a failed read reads as capped) shows the lead at its cap; with the replacement capped too the entry is a line saying the yearly weed-spray limit is reached, and a limit read that fails offers nothing. The surfactant (the member that states a concentration) is left out when the property's current air temperature (FAWN `getCurrent`, 2.5 s bound, a reading over 90 minutes old or any failure = unknown) is 90 F or hotter (`SURFACTANT_MAX_TEMP_F`, Celsius WG label: no adjuvant at 90 F or above), and is added with the note "Leave the surfactant out if it is 90°F or hotter." when the temperature is unknown. Off = the context and the sheet are byte-identical to before: no `weedMix`, no `spotRules`, no weather read, no limit read. Kill: unset the variable.

On, the lawn Fast Complete context carries `treatmentGuide: true` (a recurring visit with a plan) and `plannedProducts.chinch`, and once the technician confirms the lawn assessment the sheet reads `GET /api/admin/dispatch/:serviceId/lawn-fast/treatment-guide?assessmentId=` (404 `{enabled:false}` while off) and (the answer also carries the Weed spots decision, `weedMix`, and the standing chinch tap's decision, `chinch`, both read fresh; the sheet then follows them for the weed entry, the weed card, the search exclusion and the chinch entry, so a cap reached since the sheet opened, or a failed fresh limit read, is never overruled by the context's older offer) shows a group **"Suggested from this lawn"** between the plan's rows and "Also in <Month>'s protocol": one card per finding with the finding line, the check to do first, the product and one tap. The technician taps every product; nothing is added by itself. Until the fresh guide has answered for the confirmed assessment, the guide-governed taps wait (the Weed spots entry, the standing chinch tap and the add-ons a card may own, named in the context's `plannedProducts.guidedProductIds`) and read "Confirm the assessment first."; a failed or malformed guide read unlocks them with the context's decisions; a second answer after a retake drops the rows the guide opened that it no longer offers and says "Removed: <names>. The limits changed.". One invariant governs it all: a product of a guide-governed kind (the weed group, the chinch rungs, and the month's fungicide, caterpillar and dry-spot picks) may be on the sheet only if the LATEST decision offers it (the fresh answer, or the context's own decisions when the read failed), and the entry or card that decision offers adds the program's own row, while Search adds a plain row of any governed product its own read limit does not forbid (owner 2026-10-09; see the search rule later in this entry). The answer names what the read kept out (`blockedProductIds`: a limit, a city hold or a failed limit read, per kind, and the chinch rung ids ride `chinch.rungIds`); a pick with no card is blocked or not: blocked stays out of the list and the search, while a pick with no finding and nothing blocking it returns to the generic list (the technician can still treat what he sees). Every new decision (answered to answered or failed, failed to answered, after a retake) drops the rows it does not offer ("Removed: <names>. The limits changed." or "…could not be checked."), Complete waits while the guide is reading, and a row the latest decision does not offer blocks Complete with "Remove <name>: it is not offered for this lawn right now." A read that THROWS is never turned into "nothing found": the treatment-guide request fails (the staged chinch lookup, the assessment and its run, the plan, the weed mix), and the sheet then follows the context's decisions; a staged chinch lookup that throws while the CONTEXT is built leaves that visit with no guide at all (`treatment_guide` in `readFailures`, no `treatmentGuide`, no `chinch`), while a lookup that succeeds and finds no chinch row is a real "nothing to offer". "Blocked" means the read found a limit or hold that forbids the product (`blockedProductIds`); when the limit read itself FAILED the product is UNREADABLE instead (`unreadableProductIds`: the picks, the chinch rungs, the weed group in mode 'unavailable'): its entry or card offers nothing, but it is released to the search (and a pick to the list), and a row of it is neither dropped nor holds Complete, because the lawn sheet has no Full form control and hiding it would leave no way to record a real application (completion records the visit and flags it to the office). Unreadable is judged PER product: a chinch rung whose limit was read (blocked) stays hidden when the other rung's own read fails; the chinch ladder offers the first clean rung, skips a yearly-capped one, offers nothing at an unreadable rung (it cannot be called exhausted, so the next rung is not offered either), and a rung after an offered rung is only "not offered"; picks are judged one by one; an unavailable weed mix still withholds the tap as a whole (the #6129 rule) but its members read as forbidding stay blocked (`blockedIds` on the mix) and the others are released. The one wording, with the guide live: "The limits could not be checked. Use Search products for what you applied; the office will review it." (the weed entry, the chinch entry and an unreadable pick's line; with the guide off the merged spot-rules note "…Use Other product for what you sprayed." stands). Take-all fungicide (the month's `fungicide_spot` rows whose trigger starts with `mapped_take_all`, or whose protocol line is about mapped take-all; March and September Artavia, April and October Headway; named in the context's `plannedProducts.takeAllProductIds` and read again in the guide answer's `takeAllProductIds`, which the sheet prefers once it settles) is preventive on mapped areas only: it is never in the add-ons list and no tap offers it; once the guide has decided, the search alone reaches it (unless a limit that was read forbids it), and the row says "Take-all fungicide is for mapped take-all areas only." (after the unreadable-limit warning when the limit read failed). A product a visible card owns is not listed in the add-ons list. The search lists every lawn product (owner 2026-10-09, "add all lawn products to the drop down"): once the guide has answered or failed, every governed product (the weed group, the chinch rungs, the picks) that no check-only card holds and that its OWN read limit does not forbid (the weed decision's `blockedIds`, the chinch decision's `limitedIds`, the answer's `blockedProductIds` for a pick; with places, forbidden only when every place forbids it), as a plain row; before the answer the search waits as the taps do; the check-only take-all card's product is searchable as above; "Nothing found" releases a pick, except the held take-all product (a chinch rung comes back through the standing entry). The cards, the standing chinch entry and the rows they open show the plan's gate notes (a watering hold). The rule table is fixed in code: **weeds** = weed coverage 10% or more and the Weed spots entry can add something (the tap is that entry's; a month whose add-ons hold a weed herbicide with no tank-mix group, or whose lead is capped with no replacement row, has no weeds card); **fungus** = worst fungal activity minor or worse and the month's add-ons hold a fungicide (the staged row's `role` `fungicide_spot`; the first in program order; the card names it with its own protocol line, "Check first: look at the blades and the edge of the patch."; in a take-all month, where the staged row's `gates.trigger` starts with `mapped_take_all` (or the protocol line is about mapped take-all), the card is the check only with the line "Take-all is treated on known trouble areas only. None is on file for this lawn." and no add button, until a later change fills `troubleAreasOnFile` in `lawn-treatment-guide.js`); **chinch bugs** = insect damage moderate or severe, April through September; one look at the sunny edge of the damage, not a count (owner 2026-10-08; "Check first: part the grass at the sunny edge of the damaged patch. Do a float test only if you are unsure.", button "Found at the edge. Add it"); **caterpillars** = insect damage moderate or severe and the month holds the row whose `gates.trigger` is `caterpillars` ("Check first: soap flush to bring them to the surface."); **dry spots** = drought stress minor or worse and the month holds the row whose `gates.trigger` is `dry_spots`. There is no overwatering card. Where the levels come from: a run-backed assessment (`GATE_LAWN_VISIT_ASSESSMENT`) reads `lawn_assessment_runs.severities`, a legacy one the WORST level across the per-photo reads in `claude_raw` / `gemini_raw` (the photo merge's `worst_fungal_activity` rule); weed coverage is 100 minus the confirmed `weed_suppression` score, drought stress is `composite_scores.drought_stress`. A product at a limit, whose limit could not be read, or that the city holds is never suggested (the plan's own `v13VisitLimits`). Chinch bugs are treated in ANY month without asking the office: the sheet also lists a standing **"Chinch bugs found at the edge of damage"** tap in every month, and both it and the card add Arena 50 WDG as a spot row, or Atticus Talak 7.9 F when Arena is at its yearly count cap (the product ids come from the visit's protocol's staged rows by `gates.trigger` `chinch_20_to_25_per_sqft` then `chinch_second_product_or_caterpillars`, any window; any other limit on Arena holds the offer, a failed limit read offers nothing, same as the weed mix); a product outside the month's plan completes like any catalog product the technician adds (the off-protocol check is advisory). At completion the sheet echoes `lawnFast.treatmentGuide` and the server freezes the validated `structured_notes.lawnTreatmentGuide = { v: 1, cards: [{ kind, shown: true, checked: 'found'|'none'|null, taken, productIds }] }` (`taken` = every product the card offers is on the sheet at completion) only while the gate is live; no customer, report or public path reads it. Off = the context, the route, the sheet and the completion are byte-identical to before. Rollback: unset the variable.
Lawn Fast Complete spot target (owner 2026-10-09; `server/services/lawn-spot-target.js`, `client/src/lib/lawn-spot-target.js`, `client/src/components/tech/LawnSpotTarget.jsx`): `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_TARGET` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnSpotTargetLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and live only while `GATE_LAWN_TREATMENT_GUIDE` is also live. The lawn "What to expect" line reads curative only from a tagged target, a named issue or a finding-to-product tie, and the sheet sent `targets: []`, so a spot fungicide or insecticide applied to a found problem printed the protective sentence. On, the context carries `spotTargets` (the closed lists of a spot fungicide / insecticide row's target, read from the expectations engine's own table `TARGET_CLASS_BY_NAME`, so a name the engine does not know is never offered), the sheet shows one optional `Treating (optional)` choice on a spot fungicide or insecticide row (none on a whole-lawn row) and a `Recorded for:` line, with no tap, on a row a chinch find opened, and `/complete` stores `service_products.targets` for those rows of a `lawnFast` completion from the SERVER's verdict, never the sheet's: the trouble-area type (`troubleTypeFor`, confirmed by the staged sets `troubleTypeIdsFor`) decides and the tag is kept only when it stands for that same type (a chinch-only rung, or a ladder rung opened by the chinch entry, is stored as `Southern chinch bugs`; the month's take-all product accepts only `Take-all root rot`, never set by itself; any other fungicide or insecticide row accepts only a name of its own family); a staged-set read that fails stores no tag; free-text tags on these rows are dropped; a chinch find also comes from the submitted guide record (a chinch card or the standing Found tap, checked found and taken) for a shared rung already on the sheet, with the same ladder confirmation; a fungicide or insecticide row the server does not resolve as a spot row (the completion's own method inference) stores no tag, whatever the sheet sent, and the sheet itself sends none for a row moved off spot or onto a product of another family. A stored tag changes LIVE customer text with existing sentences only: the product's `What to expect` row reads curative, and the product card's purpose line names the recorded target; no new sentence. Off = no `spotTargets` key, no control and no line, and the sheet sends `targets: []`, as on main. A `lawnFast` completion with the gate off (a sheet loaded while it was on, submitted after it was turned off) stores NO target and ignores `targetFind` and `troubleType` for a chinch find, and the report facts freeze reads the same none; it is not refused. A completion with no `lawnFast` block (the full form, other sheets) is untouched and keeps its own tags. Rollback: unset the variable.
Lawn Fast Complete photo label (owner 2026-10-09; `server/services/lawn-photo-shots.js`, `server/routes/admin-lawn-assessment.js`, `server/services/service-report/report-data.js`, `client/src/components/lawn/LawnAssessmentCompletionBlock.jsx`): `GATE_LAWN_PHOTO_LABEL_PICK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnPhotoLabelPickLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The report prints the label of the photo's SLOT (the shot list's `reportLabel`), so a close-up of bare soil put in the Shaded area slot reached the customer as `Shaded area`. On, and while the shot list (`GATE_LAWN_SHOT_LIST`) is also on, each photo that sits in a slot gets a `Customer sees` chooser on the lawn sheet over the eight customer wordings (Front yard, Back yard, Side yard, Close-up, Blade close-up, Sunny edge, Shaded area, Trouble spot), defaulting to the slot's own wording. A changed pick rides with the photo to `POST /admin/lawn-assessment/assess` as `labelKey` (a shot key; the lookup `GET /admin/lawn-assessment/service/:id` carries `labelPickEnabled: true` so the sheet shows the chooser) and is stored beside the photo in `lawn_assessments.photos` (no migration). Only a real shot key on a photo that sits in a slot, and only one that differs from the slot, is stored; anything else is dropped and the slot's wording stands. The report (web photo strip, the labeled photo set and the PDF) prints the pick instead of the slot wording; the slot key (the recorded zone, the model's shot guide, before/after pairing, lead-photo order, findings thumbnails) never changes, and the 8-key shot list order is unchanged. The customer portal lawn health gallery and per-visit photo list (`server/routes/lawn-health.js`) carry the same pick as `labelPicked` and the portal gallery prints it. The chooser lives only on the pre-analysis photo step, so it is gone once an assessment result exists. The PDF cache key carries `:labelpick=1` only while the gate is live. Off = no `labelPickEnabled` key, no chooser, no `labelKey` sent or stored, no `labelPicked` payload key, and the sheet, payload, PDF and PDF cache key are byte-identical to before. The trace-step hint on the lawn treatment-area tracer (`Trace the grass only — leave the house, driveway and pool out.`) is technician-only text and is not gated. Rollback: unset the variable.
Lawn Fast Complete places and trouble areas (owner 2026-10-09, "start building these"; `server/services/lawn-trouble-areas.js`, `application-limits.js`, `lawn-weed-mix.js`, `lawn-treatment-guide.js`, `lawn-fast-complete.js`, `complete-scheduled-service.js`, `compliance.js`, `routes/admin-dispatch.js`, the sheet `FastCompleteLawnSheet.jsx` with `LawnSpotPlace.jsx` and `lib/lawn-trouble-places.js`, migration `20261009110000_lawn_trouble_areas`): `GATE_LAWN_TROUBLE_AREAS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnTroubleAreasLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and **live only while `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_RULES`, `GATE_LAWN_V13` and `GATE_LAWN_TREATMENT_GUIDE` are also live** (fail closed; the guide is live in production, and without it the sheet has no take-all or chinch ids to classify and hold the places by). Technician sheet and office only: no customer text, no report or public payload change, no model call. This is the first half of the next tech PR (the new-sod month question, the Monday weed jug, the mix line and take-all cards that read the store are later PRs). On, (1) **a place on every spot row**: the context carries `troubleAreas: { v: 1, places, known, knownUnavailable, blocked }` (the closed list is `front`, `back`, `left_side`, `right_side`; the lawn has no named zone model, so the list is fixed); every spot-treatment row asks WHERE in one tap, under its area (the Weed spots rows share one place, as they share one area), Complete waits for it the way it waits for the area, and the place rides the /complete product row as `areaPlaces`, a list (owner 2026-10-30: the chips are multi-select, one spray on the Front and the Back is ONE application recorded once at both; an older client's single `areaPlace` still reads as a list of one; stored in `treated_places` on `service_products` and the ledger, migration 20261030120000, with the first place also in `treated_place`; the limits are judged at each place, and a row with no place counts at every place), with `troubleType` and `troubleSource` hints; the Weed spots and Chinch-found entries take the place in the tap that adds the products, so the place costs no extra tap there, and a lawn's single known trouble area of the row's type is the default place (no extra tap); (2) **a per-property trouble-area store**, `lawn_trouble_areas` (place, type weeds | fungus | take_all | chinch | other_insect | dry_spot, status active | cleared, source tech_tap | guide_card, first seen, last seen, last treated, first and last service record): written inside the completion transaction from spot rows that carry a place (the first writer wins per property, place and type; a later treatment moves last seen and last treated and reactivates a cleared area; a failed write is logged and never fails the visit), read by the context for a compact "Known trouble areas" line above the guide cards, and cleared by one tap and one confirm (`POST /api/admin/dispatch/:serviceId/lawn-fast/trouble-areas/:areaId/clear`, 404 `{enabled:false}` while off; the visit must be one the lawn sheet can complete, the same eligibility the context applies (a pest, re-service, assessment, project, companion, grouped or closed visit is refused 409 `lawn_fast_not_eligible`), and the area must be an active one of the visit's own property; a treatment dated before the clear keeps the area cleared, one dated on or after it brings it back); the place is stored on the product record (`service_products.treated_place`) and on the application ledger (`property_application_history.treated_place`), spot rows only; (3) **the v13 yearly limits per place**: for a spot row that carries a place, the product's own yearly count, its minimum interval (Arena 56 days) and its v13 yearly amount (Arena 0.294 oz per 1,000 sq ft) are judged per (property, place) by the same reader the plan uses (`application-limits.js` `checkLimits` `opts.place`); a ledger row with NO place on record (all history before this gate, and every whole-lawn row) counts against EVERY place of that lawn; no limit value was added or changed; the shared active-ingredient cap, MOA rotation and every whole-lawn (broadcast) row keep the per-lawn logic. The sheet decides instantly: the Weed spots mix (`plannedProducts.weedMix.byPlace`) and the chinch ladder (`plannedProducts.chinch.byPlace`, also in the treatment-guide answer) carry a decision per place (a place at the lead's yearly count takes the replacement, a place at the Arena yearly count takes the bifenthrin product), and every other planned or add-on product a limit closes at a place is listed in `troubleAreas.blocked`; a closed place is off for the row with the limit's own words. The server stays authoritative: the /complete preflight refuses a spot row with no place (400 `lawn_place_required`), a place off the list (400 `lawn_place_invalid`) and a place the cap forbids (400 `lawn_place_limit`, correctable: the sheet stays editable; only the product's own count, minimum interval and v13 yearly amount refuse, and the row is sized the way a recorded ledger row is, so a typed quantity over the row's own spot area counts at that dose; the shared active-ingredient cap and every other limit stay advisory after the fact), and the closeout's after-the-fact limit audit judges a recorded spot application at its place. A limit read that FAILS refuses nothing and allows nothing new: it is the existing "unknown" (the visit is recorded and the office is flagged). The context reads limits once for the lawn and again per place only for what is capped lawn-wide (a place can only be more open than the lawn), and the air temperature once. The guided add-ons follow the same rule: the fungicide, caterpillar and dry-spot picks (and their cards) are checked per place in the treatment-guide read, and a pick is held back (`blockedProductIds`) only when NO place permits it, so a product capped at one place but open at another stays reachable and its place chips close only the forbidden places with the limit's words; the weeds and chinch cards carry a set per place (`byPlace`) and add a place's own set with one tap on the place, as the entries do. A limit read that fails at SOME place is the unknown at that place only: the product stays unreadable at the top level (released to the search with the unreadable note, never dropped by reconciliation, `unreadableIds` on the chinch and weed decisions and `unreadable` on the add-on offers), the place that read as capped stays closed, and the place whose read failed is allowed and recorded, with the closeout audit flagging it as today. Which rows are spot rows is decided by the very function the completion stores the method with (`inferServiceReportApplicationMethod`: the submitted `applicationMethod` or its `method` alias, else the catalog default for the lawn line), so a row with no method on a spot-default product asks for a place and is limit-checked like any spot row, and an explicit non-spot method does not. Take-all rows: a take-all row opened by the guide CARD (`troubleSource` `guide_card`) must sit on a place with an active `take_all` area (the card carries `allowedPlaces`, the sheet offers only those, and `/complete` refuses another with 400 `lawn_place_not_mapped`); a take-all row added through Search (`troubleSource` `tech_tap`) is the deliberate path that maps a NEW take-all area and may take any open place. Only a product the server itself identifies as a take-all row is held to it. Dose-dependent blocks: the context's `troubleAreas.blockedTypes`, the guide answer's `placeBlockedTypes` and the weed and chinch decisions' per-place `amountBlocked` say which closed place is a yearly AMOUNT block (`annual_max_rate`). The reads judge the program dose, so the sheet drops such a block (from any map, or from a refusal) once the tech changes that row's dose, and a count or interval block is never dropped; `/complete` judges the entered dose and stays authoritative (worst case one more refusal with its reason). Property: the places work on the visit's property: its own `property_id`, else the one the property-area flow resolves from the visit's address or the customer's sole property (`property-service-areas.resolveVisitPropertyId`, the one shared resolver, used through `lawn-trouble-areas.propertyOf`) for the context's known areas and per-place limit reads, the preflight, the closeout audit, the clear route, the store write, and the ledger's property on a PLACED row (a row with no place keeps the property it always had, none on an unlinked visit). A visit whose property cannot be resolved has the places OFF (no `troubleAreas`, no place asked, none stored or judged), as with the gate off. Classification: the server's staged sets decide the special products whatever the sheet sent: a take-all row is always `take_all`, the chinch-only first rung is always `chinch`, and the shared rung (Talak) is `chinch` only when the sheet says so and the ladder confirms it; the sets are read once per completion and only when a placed row could need them (a fungicide or an insecticide row, or one the sheet tagged), and a failed read stores no area for such a row (the application is still recorded, and nothing is ever refused for a read failure). The card/Search rule is decided by `troubleSource` alone. The sheet follows a cleared take-all area at once (the card drops the place, or turns check-only), and a `lawn_place_not_mapped` refusal reads the maps again like a limit refusal. A place's limit answer (the context's `blocked` and `blockedTypes`, the guide's `placeBlocked`, the searched products, the weed and chinch decisions) keeps only what `/complete` would refuse there (`refusesAtPlace`, applied through `blocksAtPlace`): the product's own count, interval and v13 amount; a lawn-wide limit such as the shared active-ingredient cap closes no place and stays an advisory. A row the tech enters is sized for the preflight by the very function that sizes a recorded ledger row for the closeout audit (`v13AmountShare`: the stated rate, else the quantity over the spot area, else the cap row's fixed fallback), so a quantity with no spot area counts the same in both; the reads that have no entered dose (the plan's proposal, the sheet's per-place reads) count the program's dose. An unmapped take-all refusal holds for the guide-card row only. The clear route runs its eligibility, property lookup and clear in one transaction that first locks the visit (`lockOwnedLiveVisit`), so a reassignment or a terminal status after the first check stops the former technician. The store makes every read and write it needs on the completion's transaction inside one savepoint (the staged-set read runs on its own connection), so a failed store aborts only itself and the completion still commits. A guide record names the place of the row the card added, for every card. Known limit: one place per product per visit. The sheet and the completion keep one row per product, so Celsius cannot be recorded at Front and Back in the same visit. Off = the context, the routes, the sheet, the limits and the completion are byte-identical to before.
Lawn Fast Complete new sod (owner 2026-10-09, new-sod holds PR 2b; `server/services/lawn-sod-sheet.js`, `lawn-sod-holds.js`, `lawn-fast-complete.js`, `routes/admin-dispatch.js`, the sheet `FastCompleteLawnSheet.jsx` with `LawnSodParts.jsx` and `lib/lawn-sod-sheet.js`): `GATE_LAWN_NEW_SOD_NOTE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnNewSodNoteLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); technician sheet only: no customer text, no report change, no model call, no migration. On, for a lawn visit at the home that has a sod record (`property_preferences.sod_laid_on`, set by the office in Customer 360; the visit must be provably at that home by the shared scope chain `visit-property-scope.js`, else no holds), the lawn Fast Complete context carries `newSod` while any hold is active on the visit's day: the banner words (day N and the sod date, whole lawn or the named part, the held classes, `Watch for large patch.` as a note only, never a fungicide line), `lines` (by product id: held with a plain reason, or a part-of-lawn `Skip the new sod: <area>` note) and, when the weed killer hold has passed its 30 days without a saved check, `rooted` (the tick). Every date and scope comes from `lawn-sod-holds.js`; nothing is restated. Product to hold class comes from the catalog row: pre-emergent = a pre-emergent active ingredient (a combination bag such as Dimension 18-0-10 is a pre-emergent and a fertilizer), fertilizer = nitrogen analysis on a granular (spreader) bag, weed killer = a herbicide that is not a pre-emergent plus the whole Weed spots group, Tetrino, Dylox and Gravex by active ingredient (brand name as the fallback); Nutra-TECH, Artavia, Headway and Velista are never held. A whole-lawn hold takes the line off the sheet (shown greyed with its reason; the technician can still add it by hand and sees a warning); a part-of-lawn record keeps every line on and notes the skip on the weed, pre-emergent, Tetrino, Dylox and Gravex lines (Dylox is held 30 days on the sod area, whole or part, label: not on water-logged or saturated turf), and through day 30 the fertilizer line carries `Keep fertilizer off the new sod: <area>.` While the pre-emergent hold is on and the fertilizer hold is over, the combination bag is replaced by LESCO 24-0-11 at 2.5 lb per 1,000 sq ft in October, or 2.1 lb (0.50 lb N) in April on the 9-visit plan (`swapBagFor`, keyed on the visit's month because the sheet line carries no targetN; resolved to the catalog row by name; if it cannot be resolved the bag is held with `Use LESCO 24-0-11 by hand.`); when every primary line is held the sheet says `No whole-lawn product today. Spot work only.`, and on a whole-lawn record with nothing left to spread by hand it adds `If there is no spot work, complete the visit with no product.` and the context carries `noProductAllowed` with `noProductNote` (`No product applied: new sod is rooting (laid <date>). Held: <class> until <date>.`): the sheet then drops the Products applied required rule, still asks for the photo and the confirmed assessment, and appends that sentence to the technician note; `/complete` is described under No product below The tick `POST /api/admin/dispatch/:serviceId/lawn-fast/sod-rooted` with `{ sodLaidOn }` saves `sod_rooted_on` = the visit's ET day: it takes the customer's property-preferences advisory lock first, then the visit row lock, then the preferences row; it is idempotent, never moves or clears a saved day, refuses (409) when the sod date differs from the one the sheet rendered or the sod is inside 30 days, and 404 `{enabled:false}` while off. A failed sod read shows `Could not check this lawn for new sod` on the sheet and adds `new_sod` to `readFailures`. Not in this PR: the customer report card, the last pre-emergent line, any customer message and the automatic watering pause. Known limit: only products the context already names (planned lines, add-ons, the Weed spots group, the chinch offer) are classified, so a product found only through the search box gets no hold warning. Capability signal: the hold-adjusted context (held lines, the swap bag, `newSod`) goes ONLY to a sheet that sends `sodAware=1` on GET `/lawn-fast/context` (and on the tick); without it, with the gate on, the context is the legacy one exactly (the same planned items, nothing appended or removed, no `newSod`, the sod record never read), so an older or cached sheet that would pre-pick every planned item behaves as it does with the gate off (the accepted status quo until it reloads). The tick refuses a visit dated after today (ET): 409 `sod_rooted_future_visit`. No product: a `/complete` with an EMPTY product list whose technician note carries `No product applied: new sod` is re-judged by rebuilding the context as a sod-aware sheet and answers 409 `lawn_sod_no_product_stale` unless that context sets `noProductAllowed` and generated the same note; an empty list without the sentence is judged as before. Off = the context, the route and the sheet are byte-identical to before.
Lawn report New sod card (owner 2026-10-09; `server/services/lawn-sod-report-card.js`, hooks in `complete-scheduled-service.js` and `service-report/report-data.js`, the page card `LawnNewSodCard.jsx`): `GATE_LAWN_NEW_SOD_REPORT_CARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnNewSodReportCardLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and it also needs `GATE_LAWN_NEW_SOD_NOTE` (fails closed); customer web report only: no PDF, SMS or email change, no model call, no migration. On, a lawn Fast Complete completion (not an incomplete visit, not a resumed one) at a home with an active sod hold rebuilds the sod-aware sheet context on the completion transaction, inside a savepoint, and freezes `structured_notes.lawnNewSod { v: 1, visitDay, sodLaidOn, covers, planRan, held: [{ kind, until, rootedCheck }], swap: { name } | null }` (first writer wins). The sheet echoes the sod record it showed (`lawnFast.sod = { laidOn, covers, held: [kind, ...] }`); the freeze writes nothing when the echo is missing, or the record or a hold decision (the rooted check included) changed since. The office's free-text area name is never frozen or printed. A held class the technician applied anyway (the planned product or another product of that class) is not listed. The public payload is in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`. `held` lists only the classes that kept a PLANNED primary line off the visit (`plannedHeld` on the sheet context's `newSod`, from `lawn-sod-sheet.js`), in the order fertilizer, weed killer, pre-emergent, Dylox; Tetrino and Gravex are held on the sheet but never named to the customer; a whole-lawn class the technician applied by hand anyway is left out; a part-of-lawn record names the classes skipped on the sod area (fertilizer through day 30). Nothing held = nothing frozen, no card. A failed read (sod record unavailable, any query error) freezes nothing, logs a warning and never fails the visit. The report payload carries `lawnNewSod` (title, lead, items, rest, swap, close: fixed sentences built by the server from the frozen block alone, never from the live sod record) only while the gate is live and the block is valid; the page prints strings only and only in live mode (the PDF and static views are unchanged). Off = no freeze and a byte-identical payload and page. A record frozen while on keeps its block after a rollback, and prints nothing while off.
Lawn v13 November large patch nitrogen (owner 2026-10-09; UF/IFAS Large Patch SS-PLP-5: reduce nitrogen and use slow-release in the disease window, November to May; it does not say zero; `server/services/waveguard-plan-engine.js` `visitNutrientTargets`, the rule in `server/config/lawn-v13-nitrogen-targets.js`, the tank sheet in `server/routes/admin-protocols.js`): `GATE_LAWN_NOV_LARGE_PATCH_N` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`** (a different spelling such as `TRUE` is off), read at call time via `lawnNovLargePatchNLive()`, and live only while `GATE_LAWN_TROUBLE_AREAS` (which needs the v13 program, spot rules and treatment guide) and `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_TARGET` are live (owner-visible, 2026-10-23: the large patch evidence is the target the Fast Complete sheet records on the fungicide application, which only `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_TARGET` captures, so the rule fails closed without it). On, a v13 November visit at a lawn with an ACTIVE mapped LARGE PATCH (owner-visible change 2026-10-23: the rule used to read any "fungus" area, which also stands for gray leaf spot, Pythium, dollar spot, fairy ring and rust; it now asks `loadActiveLargePatch`: the newest fungicide application at the area's place must record the target Large patch, Brown patch or Rhizoctonia, and an unknown disease keeps the normal target) sizes its nitrogen bag for 0.5 lb N per 1,000 sq ft instead of the visit's 0.75 lb N (LESCO 24-0-11: 2.1 lb per 1,000 sq ft instead of 3.1). The one reduced target is read by the plan, the tank sheet, the completion defaults, the yearly limit check and the Fast Complete planned amount, and the nitrogen line carries the note "Active large patch mapped: nitrogen reduced to 0.5 lb N (2.1 lb per 1,000). Close the spreader over the patch and 6 ft around it." A target is never raised (a visit already at 0.5 or less is unchanged), potassium is untouched, and December (10-0-22, 0.45 lb N) is unchanged. A failed or empty trouble-area read, a lawn with no property, or the reference tank sheet (no visit) keeps the normal target. No migration: the rule is code config. Off = the plan, the tank sheet and the Fast Complete planned amounts are byte-identical to before. The recipe text in `lawn-protocol-v13.json` does not state this rule (it would be false with the gate off); the line note carries it. Removing the gate later deletes the reader, the config file and the gate check. Since 2026-10-23 the large patch evidence and the area are both dated to the visit's day, the newest fungicide day at the place must name large patch on every row, and the area read fails closed (see the December row, `GATE_LAWN_DEC_LARGE_PATCH_K`, for the exact rule).
Lawn v13 December large patch potassium bag (owner 2026-10-23, "do whatever is going to make the grass look its best, based on the research we did"; UF/IFAS Large Patch SS-PLP-5: reduce nitrogen in the disease window; healthy lawns keep feeding, so only a mapped large patch changes; `server/services/waveguard-plan-engine.js` `visitNutrientTargets` and `troubleProductSwap`, the rule in `server/config/lawn-v13-trouble-product-swaps.js`, the tank sheet in `server/routes/admin-protocols.js`, the brief in `server/services/previsit-brief.js`): `GATE_LAWN_DEC_LARGE_PATCH_K` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`** (a different spelling such as `TRUE` is off), read at call time via `lawnDecLargePatchKLive()`, and live only while `GATE_LAWN_TROUBLE_AREAS` (which needs the v13 program, spot rules and treatment guide) and `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_TARGET` are live (owner-visible, 2026-10-23: the large patch evidence is the target the Fast Complete sheet records on the fungicide application, which only `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_TARGET` captures, so the rule fails closed without it). On, a v13 December visit at a lawn with an ACTIVE mapped LARGE PATCH puts down LESCO Black Out 0-0-24 AM Spar-TECH (SiteOne 511512, 50 lb; 0 N, 0 P, 24% K2O) at 4.125 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.99 lb K2O, the same potassium as the 10-0-22; the plan derives 4.125 lb) with a nitrogen target of 0, instead of LESCO 10-0-22 at 4.5 lb (0.45 lb N). Every other lawn keeps the 10-0-22. The swapped line carries the note "Active large patch mapped: potassium-only bag, no nitrogen (4.125 lb per 1,000 sq ft = 0.99 lb K2O). Used in place of the LESCO 10-0-22." and the pre-visit brief marks the 10-0-22 as replaced. The one swapped bag is read by the plan, the tank sheet, the completion defaults, the yearly limit check and the Fast Complete planned amount. The bag has no nitrogen, so the nitrogen ordinance checks (North Port from April 1, the county window June 1 to September 30) do not read it. Watering: the 0.25 inch within 24 hours rule of the other granular fertilizers, and the product is approved for the service report, so the customer watering text goes out. A failed or empty trouble-area read, a lawn with no property, or the reference tank sheet (no visit) keeps the 10-0-22. The figure is one number everywhere staff read it: the recipe, the line, the technician note, the Protocol Reference and the prefilled amount all say 4.125 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.99 / 0.24, exactly 0.99 lb K2O). The 0-0-24 catalog row's own default rate (4.1 lb, written by the migration) is only a fallback the planner uses when the K target is missing. Evidence is dated: only fungicide applications on or before the visit's scheduled day count (a later application never changes an earlier visit). The AREA is dated the same way (`loadActiveAsOf`): the table keeps no status history (a reactivation erases `cleared_at`), so it fails closed. An area counts for a visit only if it was first seen on or before the visit's day, has no activity (`last_seen_on`, `last_treated_on`) after it, and is active now or was cleared after that day (a clear on the visit day or before, or with no timestamp, does not count). So a clear after the visit still counts for it, and a reactivation or a later treatment does not retroactively qualify an earlier visit; the cost is that an area treated again after a past visit no longer reads as active on that earlier day. The newest application day at the place decides, and every fungicide row of that day must name large patch (several fungicides in one completion share the day, so a mix of targets or a blank one is ambiguous and fails closed). Migration `20261023121000_lawn_v13_dec_large_patch_potassium_v2` inserts the catalog row (it THROWS and writes nothing if any catalog row already matches the name or an alias; no price is written, set $30.06 in Inventory) and one non-default `lb_k` row in each v13 December window; its `down()` is all or nothing. **Large patch means large patch (owner-visible rule, shared with `GATE_LAWN_NOV_LARGE_PATCH_N`):** a "fungus" trouble area also stands for gray leaf spot, Pythium, dollar spot, fairy ring and rust, and the store records no disease, so the rule asks `lawn-trouble-areas` `loadActiveLargePatch` for the evidence: the NEWEST fungicide application at the area's place (`property_application_history`, retractions left out) must record the target Large patch, Brown patch or Rhizoctonia (`service_products.targets`, written by the Fast Complete sheet while `GATE_LAWN_SPOT_TARGET` is live). Another disease, no target, no application or an unreadable ledger = no swap (fails closed). The recipe states the conditional bag in `lawn-protocol-v13.json` (December visit, `swaps.largePatchPotassium`, all three tracks), `lawnProtocols()` hands it out only while this gate is live, and `server/config/lawn-v13-trouble-product-swaps.js` reads it, so the overlay and the recipe cannot drift (`swapRecipeProblems()` is tested). Migration `20261023120000_lawn_v13_dec_large_patch_potassium` is an inert no-op kept so databases that recorded it stay valid. Another lane's alternative, no December nitrogen on every lawn, is a change in the rule file (drop `evidence` and `troubleType`, and the area read goes away). Off = the plan, the tank sheet, the brief and the Fast Complete planned amounts are byte-identical to before. Removing the gate later deletes the reader, the rule file and the gate check.

Lawn reclaimed water, half nitrogen (owner 2026-10-05 adopted half N for reclaimed lawns; 2026-10-23 "do whatever is going to make the grass look its best"; UF Mobile Irrigation Lab: 38% of 3,177 Manatee reclaimed-water evaluations got more than the recommended N from the water alone): `GATE_LAWN_RECLAIMED_HALF_N` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`** (a different spelling such as `TRUE` is off), read at call time via `lawnReclaimedHalfNLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The fact: `customer_properties.reclaimed_water` (boolean, NULL = unknown), `reclaimed_water_source` (`county_meter` | `office` | `customer`) and `reclaimed_water_checked_at` (migration `20261023100000_reclaimed_water.js`, additive and nullable). An office or customer value always wins; the county job only writes rows whose source is NULL or `county_meter`. The office sets it in the Customer 360 service-address panel (`PUT /api/admin/customers/:id/properties/:propertyId/reclaimed-water`, body `{reclaimed: true|false|null}`; null hands the property back to automatic; 404 while the gate is off). Plan: on, a v13 visit whose property is reclaimed has its nitrogen target halved (`nitrogenDecision` in `server/services/waveguard-plan-engine.js`; the fraction is `RECLAIMED_N_FRACTION` in `server/config/lawn-v13-nitrogen-targets.js`). The amount derives from the halved target for the plan, the tank sheet, the completion defaults, the yearly limit check, the previsit brief and the Fast Complete planned amount, and the line carries the note "Reclaimed water: half nitrogen today (0.375 lb N, 1.6 lb per 1,000)." With the November large-patch cut (`GATE_LAWN_NOV_LARGE_PATCH_N`) also in effect the SMALLER target wins (not both), and the line carries BOTH notes: the half-nitrogen note and the fungus spreader instruction ("Active fungus mapped. Close the spreader over the patch and 6 ft around it.", without the fungus rule's own larger figures), in the plan, the tank sheet and Fast Complete; the visit text names both reasons: half of 0.75 is 0.375, already under the large-patch 0.5. A visit with no nitrogen target above zero is unchanged. Two kinds of bag are NOT halved, because their rate is set by something other than their nitrogen: a pre-emergent plus fertilizer bag (October Dimension 18-0-10 at 4.04 lb, the 9x April Dimension), because halving it would halve the pre-emergent (dithiopyr), and a visit that states a potassium target (the December 10-0-22), because reclaimed water adds N, not K, and the potash is for cold weather and large patch. Those lines say "Reclaimed water: this bag carries the pre-emergent, so its full rate stays today." or "Reclaimed water: this bag carries the winter potash, so its full rate stays today." The new-sod bag swap (`server/services/lawn-sod-sheet.js`, October and 9x April: plain 24-0-11 in place of the held Dimension bag) carries no pre-emergent, so on a reclaimed lawn it is halved by the same `nitrogenDecision`: 1.25 lb per 1,000 in October (0.3 lb N), 1.05 lb in April (0.25 lb N), with the same half-nitrogen line note. With the gate on and the visit pinned to v13, the swap bag's baseline follows the plan window the bag replaces (under the completion defaults a 9x April visit rescheduled into May still replaces April's 0.5 lb N pass: 2.1 lb, 1.05 halved); with the gate off the sod sheet keeps choosing the baseline by the visit day's month, as it always did. A county verdict never outlives its coordinates: migration `20261023110000_reclaimed_water_coordinate_reset.js` adds one BEFORE UPDATE trigger on `customer_properties.latitude/longitude` that clears the three columns when the coordinates change while the answer is still `county_meter` (the geocode review, a re-geocode, a manual pin and `syncPrimaryAddress` all pass through it; an office or customer answer is untouched). The office edit goes through the audited `editManualProperty` writer (`reclaimed_water` field; source `office` and the time are written with it; the audit event carries the actor, the new answer and the old one); with the gate off the property list, add and edit answers are the old payload (no `reclaimedWater` key, none of the three columns) and the writer refuses the field. The tank sheet (`/lawn-mix`) and the new-sod swap decide v13 eligibility the planner's way (`GATE_LAWN_V13` live and not pinned to another protocol version), independently of `GATE_LAWN_NOV_LARGE_PATCH_N`: each nitrogen gate activates its own adjustment. A genuine street, city, state or ZIP move on the primary property (`syncPrimaryAddress`, the same canonical test as the neighborhood reset; a unit-only or format-only edit changes nothing) clears all three reclaimed columns, whoever set them, so the next county tick settles the new address. A visit whose property a customer merge deactivated (the visit keeps the loser's property id) is judged by the winning customer's ACTIVE property at the same address key; none means no halving. A staff-added service address saves the address picker's coordinates (validated pair, 7 decimals; a bad or partial pair is ignored), so the county match can judge it; the coordinate-change trigger is BEFORE UPDATE only, so the insert is untouched. The empty-duplicate check (`customer-empty-loser.js`) treats a `county_meter` reclaimed answer as derived, like the neighborhood stamp; an office or customer answer is real history and blocks the delete. A failed property read, a visit with no resolvable property, or a gate that is off keeps the normal target. Automatic detection (Manatee only): `server/services/reclaimed-water-meters.js` downloads the county's public reclaimed meter layer (`Reclaim_UN_Breakdown/MapServer/5`, about 40,000 points, fields OBJECTID, LIFECYCLESTATUS and RETIREDDATE, paged 2,000 by OBJECTID, plain browser user agent because the server answers 403 to some others) into `reclaimed_water_meters` and marks every active property with coordinates within 30 m of an in-service meter (`RETIREDDATE` empty and `LIFECYCLESTATUS` 8 or empty: on 2026-10-23 all 40,347 points read RETIREDDATE empty and LIFECYCLESTATUS 8, and the county publishes no code list for the field, so 8 is the layer's in-service value and any other code or any retired date drops the meter) `reclaimed_water=true, source=county_meter`. The county only ever says YES: a property with no meter within 30 m is left unknown (no county value written, full nitrogen), whether it is in Manatee, over the line in Sarasota or Charlotte (no layer there), or a lawn whose meter sits farther away; a property marked earlier whose meter a new layer dropped goes back to unknown. The match runs on our own copy: no customer coordinate is ever sent to the county. The 30 m radius is one front setback (7 to 10 m) plus geocoder error (5 to 15 m) to the lot's own curb meter, short of the next lot's meter. Job: cron `reclaimed-water-meters`, daily 3:47 AM ET, through `runExclusive`; it downloads only when the stored layer is older than six days (a short, malformed or failed pull keeps the stored layer) and matches every property after a download, else only the properties with no county value and those marked before the stored layer was fetched; it does nothing while the gate is off. The recipe file `server/config/lawn-protocol-v13.json` keeps the original, gate-off wording of the two reclaimed-water sentences (every track's `notes[2]` and `safety_rules[6]`: "the tech logs half ... the app does not adjust it yet"); `lawnProtocols()` (`server/services/lawn-program.js`) swaps in the gate-on wording (half N at every N visit except bags that carry the pre-emergent or the winter potassium; a line that shows "Reclaimed water: half nitrogen today" is already halved) only while `lawnReclaimedHalfNLive()` is true, so job cards and the Protocol Reference never promise behavior the gate has not switched on. Off = the plan, the tank sheet, the Fast Complete planned amounts, the property routes and the cron are byte-identical to before. Removing the gate later deletes `lawnReclaimedHalfNLive`, the checks in the plan, the route and the cron.
Lawn assessment without the season boost (owner 2026-10-24, lawn scoring review "GO", step 4): `GATE_LAWN_NO_SEASON_BOOST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnNoSeasonBoostLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `POST /admin/lawn-assessment/assess` stores `turf_density` and `color_health` exactly as the model derived them, with no cool-week season multiplier (`seasonAwareAdjustment` or `applySeasonalAdjustment`), on both the one-call (`lawn-visit-scores.js` `scoreVisit`) and the legacy path; the prompt already asks for color "for the season", so the boost counted the season twice and could make the report's overall "up" line fire alone. Only new assessments change; report wording (`dormancyLikely`, the seasonal color line), the progress-engine season gates and the diagnostic funnel (`lawn-diagnostic-analyze.js`) are unchanged. Off: today's boost, byte for byte. Rollback: unset it.


Lawn cost-plus list price (owner 2026-10-09; `server/services/pricing-engine/service-pricing.js` `priceLawnCare`, `estimate-engine.js`, `lawn_pricing_v2.costPlusList` in `constants.js`): `GATE_LAWN_COST_PLUS_LIST` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `gateEnvValue` (unset = kill, no redeploy). On, a residential recurring lawn plan is priced at annual cost / (1 - 0.45), in whole dollars per application, never below the market table and at least $55 a visit; cost is the v13 program product cost at SiteOne account prices plus 10 more labor minutes a visit for spot work; the lawn size is not rounded. Tier rows carry `pricingSource` `COST_PLUS_LIST` or `MINIMUM_PER_VISIT`, `costPlusListApplied`, `listMargin` and `costPlusListAnnual`. The mode also arms the lawn cost floor, so WaveGuard tier and manual discounts on the lawn line stop at a 35% margin (`minimumCollectedAnnualPrice` = cost / 0.65). `pricingMetadata.lawnCostPlusList` records the state for each run, with the full cost basis it priced with (`lawnCostPlusListBasis`: the knobs plus labor minutes, loaded rate, drive minutes, reserves, admin cost and margin floor): an estimate priced on replays on at the same basis after the gate goes off or any of those numbers change. In this mode the request options `targetLawnGrossMargin`, `lawnMaterialCostPerK`, `lawnLaborMinutesBase`, `lawnLaborMinutesPerK` and `routeDriveMinutes` are ignored, and one that priced a lawn off (or before this gate, with no stamp) replays off after the gate goes on. An estimate that never priced a lawn pins nothing: a lawn added later follows the live gate. A posted `lawnCostPlusList`, `services.lawn.costPlusList` or snapshot is stripped (`estimate-client-identity-fields.js`); only the gate and the saved stamp set the mode. The knobs live in `pricing_config.lawn_pricing_v2.costPlusList` (seeded by migration 20261009150000, validated on admin save). The one-time lawn anchor and commercial lawn stay on the market table. An invalid `costPlusList` knob or cost basis fails the calculation closed (400 `LAWN_COST_PLUS_LIST_KNOBS_INVALID`). Off = every price is byte-identical to before. ON in production since 2026-10-26. The client preview mirror proved unneeded (no live screen prices with the client engine), and #6226 tested the estimate page with the gate on.
