Multiple discounts per service: `GATE_DISCOUNT_STACKING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `discountStackingLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`) — the canonical reader; the `gates.discountStacking` map entry is for `logGateStatus` only and must never be read directly for a live decision. The one stacking rule (owner ruling 2026-09-11, "the lesser of the two") lives in `server/services/discount-stack.js`: dollar credits come off first, then percentages compound on what is left (10% then 5% off $111 is $16.10, never an additive $16.65), with EVERY discount-carrying surface reading the same gate together — schedule creation/extension (`server/routes/admin-schedule.js`), and invoice/document calculation: `InvoiceService.create`, the existing-draft edit/retotal path (`calculateUpdateFinancials`), and discount-engine.js's `/api/admin/discounts/calculate` preview all flip to `discountStackingLive()` in the same change, so preview and save can never disagree ($111 at 10%+5% previews AND saves $16.10 either way — no half-migrated state where only one side compounds). `GET /api/admin/discounts/stacking` calls `discountStackingLive()` and reports it for a picker to read. The corrected cent-exact rounding (5% of $20.70 is $1.04, never the old float formula's $1.03) is live regardless of the gate. Invoice document-stack specifics (server/services/invoice.js): an unparented negative line item — a stored stamp (`scheduled_service` / `validated_checkout` / the builder's own "Scheduled price adjustment" reconciliation row) OR a plain literal credit with no `discount_id` — always joins the document stack, reducing the base a fresh percentage compounds against; a scheduled appointment discount's service-key/category scope (`scheduled_services.discount_service_key_filter` / `_category_filter`) narrows its document term to the line(s) it reaches, with "no service-key snapshot anywhere on this invoice ⇒ unscoped" (pre-lane invoices) and "a snapshot present but matching no line ⇒ the credit resolves to $0" (orphaned, never a silent overcharge replay of a frozen amount). Gate off keeps every one of these paths byte-identical to before this lane, in its own untouched branch. `slot-reservation.js` carries no discount arithmetic.

Staff two-step sign-in (`server/services/staff-mfa.js`): `GATE_ADMIN_MFA` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `adminMfaLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`, resolved through `staff-mfa.js`). On, a staff member who set up an authenticator app at `/admin/two-step` (TOTP, RFC 6238; secret pgcrypto-encrypted with `STAFF_MFA_KEY`, falling back to `DATA_HYGIENE_VAULT_KEY`; ten single-use SHA-256-hashed recovery codes) gets only a 5-minute challenge from `POST /api/admin/auth/login` and a session from `POST /login/mfa` after a code passes (dark = a generic 404 from `server/middleware/staff-mfa-guard.js` ahead of every limiter; a code is accepted once per 30-second step; 5 wrong codes lock the account 15 minutes; every factor check and write is fenced on the session's credential version and atomic with recovery-code use). Every staff check (`adminAuthenticate`, `verifyStaffBearer`, staff sockets, the report staff peek, terminal auth, staff OAuth states, staff push lookups) refuses an enrolled account's session that never passed the code (401 `MFA_REQUIRED`); enrolling and turning it off move the credential version and deactivate push devices. `GATE_ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCE` (needs the master gate) holds an admin with no authenticator on the setup page (403 `MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED` elsewhere). WavesPay needs the build with `API.loginMfa` before an enrolled account signs in there. Unset `GATE_ADMIN_MFA` = the kill switch: login and every session are exactly as before, whatever was enrolled.

Core: `DATABASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` / `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` / `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET`.

Optional model overrides: `MODEL_DEEP` / `MODEL_EXTREME` / `MODEL_FLAGSHIP` / `MODEL_WORKHORSE` / `MODEL_ROUTINE` (default Sonnet 5.5 at low effort; owner 2026-10-04: staff wiki Q&A, vendor invoice PDFs and lead synopsis moved off the flagship; owner 2026-10-25: the wiki compiler, agronomic wiki pages, voice-profile distiller and KB nightly audit moved off `MODEL_DEEP` through `llm/deep.js`, each keeping its own effort; expense categories stay on `MODEL_FLAGSHIP` (2026-10-04 bake-off: Sonnet 5.5 filed equipment as Depreciation); customer-facing wiki Q&A stays on `MODEL_FLAGSHIP` and published hero alt text on `MODEL_VISION`; set `MODEL_ROUTINE=claude-opus-4-8` to roll back the model and the effort; never Fable / Mythos) / `MODEL_FAST` / `MODEL_VOICE` / `MODEL_VISION` (global), `INTELLIGENCE_BAR_MODEL` / `INTELLIGENCE_BAR_TECH_MODEL` (IB-specific), `MODEL_ADS_ADVISOR` (daily ads advisor, `TEXT_POLICIES.adsAdvisor` primary leg; default Claude Fable 5.1 at effort `high`, OpenAI report writer as backup — owner ruling 2026-10-01), `BLOG_IMAGE_PROVIDER` (blog image chain, default `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst,gpt-image-2,gpt-image-1.5,gpt-image-1` — Images 2.5 leads since 2026-09-25) / `SOCIAL_IMAGE_PROVIDER` (social image chain, its own older default `gpt-image-2,gpt-image-1.5,gpt-image-1`, no Images 2.5 leg; an override with no valid slug falls back to that social default, never the blog one) (both **OpenAI only** since 2026-09-24: every Gemini image model is SynthID pixel-watermarked and `parseChain` drops those slugs from any chain; `ALLOW_PIXEL_WATERMARKED_IMAGE_PROVIDERS=true` is the only way to reach them and also restores the pre-09-24 interleaved defaults — deliberate runs only, never a prod default; the same override gates Veo social video, which is SynthID-marked too and refused without it), `MODEL_GEMINI_IMAGE_PRO` (Nano Banana Pro model id, unreachable without that override; `BLOG_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` per request, `BLOG_IMAGE_CHAIN_BUDGET_MS` for the whole chain incl. the screen retry; `BLOG_IMAGE_UNIFORM_LOGO=false` is the kill switch for the Waves logo reference image — since 2026-09-24 the blog publisher opts in with `generate({ uniformLogo: true })` and its OpenAI legs post `server/assets/brand/waves-logo.png` to /v1/images/edits so a generated technician carries the real logo on the cap and right chest; the publisher's text/logo screen allows it there only. `BLOG_IMAGE_VAN_WRAP=false` is the independent kill switch for the Waves van wrap reference — owner ruling 2026-09-24: a generated van shows the REAL current wrap (it reads the retired "WAVES" / "Lawn & Pest" name) rather than wait for a re-wrap; the publisher opts in with `generate({ vanWrap: true })`, and when the image's plan places a van in the scene (`plan.van`) its OpenAI legs post `waves-van-side.png` + `waves-van-rear.png` to /v1/images/edits so that one van carries the wrap; a separate vision question judges that van (wrong body, plain van, missing mascot, or a readable phone number / web address that is not Waves' own fail; other lettering drift passes) and the main screen fails the same marks anywhere else; the chest-badge side is judged from the badge's and button placket's positions, never the screen's own left/right words; the whole screen runs on GPT-5.6 Sol first (`TEXT_POLICIES.imageScreen`, `MODEL_OPENAI_IMAGE_SCREEN`, owner ruling 2026-09-25) with Claude VISION as the backup when OpenAI misses. Social tiles and newsletter images do not opt into either reference — they have no screen to catch a mark pasted elsewhere). Fable is never automatic; opt in explicitly through `MODEL_EXTREME` or a deliberate feature route.

Ask Waves turn budget: `ASK_WAVES_TURN_BUDGET_MS` (default 22000ms) — the whole customer-turn wall-clock budget for `TEXT_POLICIES.askWaves` (`dispatchWithFallback`, `hardDeadline: true`), covering the OpenAI primary AND the Anthropic fallback combined, never each getting the full amount. Read fresh on every call, no restart needed. A bad, non-positive, or out-of-range (>120000ms) value falls back to the 22000ms default rather than reaching the dispatcher as a real budget.

Ask Waves topic routing: `GATE_ASK_WAVES_TOPIC_ROUTING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `askWavesTopicRoutingLive()` (unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the intake model also classifies what the visitor asked (`topic`), and a medical-emergency, product-safety or re-entry question gets reviewed copy instead of the model's own answer; routing follows the model's topic only — no regex floor, never a regex-only emergency override (#4899). Off, prompt, schema and replies are byte-identical. Contract detail in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`.
Ask Waves emergency second opinion: `GATE_ASK_WAVES_EMERGENCY_CHECK` — **ships DARK**, read at call time via `askWavesEmergencyCheckLive()`. On, a fast classifier (`fastStructured`) asks "is anyone in medical danger?" alongside every chat turn (waits at most 1.5 s past the answer); a yes turns a non-emergency answer into the emergency script. Adds only, fails open (#4899).
Ask Waves Jev second check: `GATE_ASK_WAVES_JEV_CHECK` — **ships DARK: `off` | `shadow` | `enforce`, anything else reads as off**, read at call time via `askWavesJevCheckMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy; `askPackage` still needs `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS`). A model-written website chat reply (not reviewed copy, not an emergency turn, not a deterministic fallback) is also put to Jev as `ask_waves_safety.v1` (`typed-decisions/packages.js`; two yes/no reads of the reply: `safety_claim`, a blanket safety or approval claim, and `access_timing`, a re-entry or use time), beside the existing word list (`intakeSafetyClaimSupplement`). Owner-approved 2026-10-28 after a replay of 24 new unsafe replies: word list 22, Jev 23, both 24. `shadow` changes nothing a visitor sees and adds no wait: after the chat log writes the assistant `agent_messages` row (`logIntakeExchange` now returns its id), Jev is asked and both answers are recorded in `decision_reviews` (subject type `agent_messages`, migration `20261028200000`; `subject_hash` = `askWavesSubjectHash` of the cleaned visitor message + the reply; baseline `production: false` because the word list passed it). `enforce` waits at most 800 ms (`ASK_WAVES_JEV_CHECK_GRACE_MS`) for the answer; a yes on either question serves the same reviewed copy the word list serves (emergency guidance when it applies, else the safety-label copy in the reply's language) and logs the swap without the reply text; a timeout, error or `ok:false` keeps the reply (fails open). The review route reads an `agent_messages` subject back as the visitor message + the reply (`admin-typed-decisions.js`). Adds one Jev call per model-written reply; no customer send.

SMS operational actions: `GATE_SMS_OPERATIONAL_ACTIONS` is opt-in and read again before writes; `GATE_SMS_OPERATIONAL_ACTIONS_SINCE` must be an ISO instant with an offset, selecting only messages from the authorized activation onward. Unset/disable the gate to stop extraction, profile writes and exception bells. No customer sends. Scope and pending timing/scheduling rules: `docs/sms-operational-actions.md`.
Access codes section (server half): `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_SECTION` is opt-in and read at call time. On, a five-minute sweep (`services/access-code-capture.js`, cron lock `access-code-net`) reads each inbound customer text that mentions a gate, door, lockbox, garage, call box, pass or code, asks one model call what access information the text states, verifies every item in code (the quote is in the text, a code sits in the quote as a whole token and is not the house number, ZIP or a phone number), and files it as a `found` row in `customer_access_codes` (a door code for a one-time job included). The office accepts, dismisses or retires each one through `/api/admin/access-codes` (every route 404 while the gate is off); accepting (or adding) a standing neighborhood gate, property gate, lockbox or garage code on a one-home account also writes the matching profile field, replacing an older value, so the neighborhood directory sweep files it. One list (owner ruling 2026-10-05): the same tick mirrors those four profile fields into `profile` rows for every customer with exactly one active home (`access_code_profile_mirror` holds a per-customer receipt: the profile edit time seen, the home count and a hash per kind, never a code). A filled field gets one active `profile` row bound to the home and retires every other active code of that kind there; an emptied field retires the home's codes of that kind when the sweep had mirrored a value, and a `profile` row always; directions-only rows are left. The mirror never writes the profile field, runs only with the gate on, skips multi-home customers and needs no activation time. The technician's visit read (`GET /api/admin/access-codes/visits/:visitId`) returns every row, and marks a standing code row of those four kinds `profileBacked: true` when the customer has one home; the visit card hides such a row only when the brief's profile code of that kind reached it (so a brief with facts off or failed soft still shows the row), and keeps a row that adds directions to the same code; a multi-home customer's rows are never marked. The mirror also retires its rows when a field becomes a value the table cannot hold, or when the customer's only home changes (the receipt keeps the sole home id), and a failed mirror fails the job on the no-activation-time path too. The office list keeps every row, a mirrored one labelled "From the profile"; retiring it clears the same value from the profile field. Audit rows for the mirror use actor `system` and carry no code. `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_SECTION_SINCE` must be an ISO instant with an offset: the sweep reads only texts from that moment on, so turning the gate on never reads history. Nothing is sent to a customer and the sweep rings no bell; the codes waiting on the office are listed by the found-codes bell (`GATE_ACCESS_CODES_FOUND_BELL`, below). Owner ruling 2026-10-05: every code is saved, customer or not. An inbound text from a number with no customer record is read the same way and filed unlinked (`customer_id` null, the sender's phone, and a suggested customer when the text names exactly one home); an unlinked row never reaches the profile mirror. The office links it with `POST /api/admin/access-codes/:id/link` (admin only) before it can be accepted (`link_required`), and may dismiss it unlinked; a linked row behaves like any other. A visitor or QR pass keeps its link whole (a link cropped part-way is refused). A visitor or QR pass is shared with its neighborhood at READ time, never copied into the neighborhood directory: the technician's visit read (`GET /api/admin/access-codes/visits/:visitId`) adds the active standing passes (kind `pass`, directions only, no keypad code) of OTHER live customers whose home is in the same neighborhood as the visit's home, when `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ACCESS` is on, as `{ id, kind: 'pass', code: null, instructions, life: 'standing', scheduledServiceId: null, shared: true }` (identical directions listed once, never the other customer's id, name, quote or address). A pass follows its home's current neighborhood, leaves when its owner retires it and disappears when either gate is off; a visit-life pass stays on its visit. The Gate codes page shows an unlinked row's sender phone, a one-tap "Link to <suggested name>" and a customer search. The suggested customer needs the house number, full street name (suffix and directional) and, when the text names one, the unit to match one live home. Linking, and accepting a code the text itself gave, refuse a numeric code equal to a house number or ZIP of the customer's live homes (`code_is_address`). The visit card shows a pass row's https link as an Open visitor pass button (only rows the server marks kind `pass`; alerts and other notes keep their raw text). Rollback: unset `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_SECTION`; the table, the receipt table and their rows stay.
Setup fee settled anywhere (`services/setup-fee-obligation.js` `setupFeeSettledElsewhere()`, owner 2026-10-24 notification audit: 4 of 4 setup-fee alerts since 08-25 were false): `GATE_SETUP_FEE_SETTLED_ANYWHERE` ships DARK, read at call time via `setupFeeSettledAnywhereLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; strict `true`, unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the one predicate also reads the customer's own invoices that do not cite the accepted estimate. The fee is settled when a PAID line named setup fee, membership fee or WaveGuard Membership sums to the frozen fee, when a live invoice has a waived or $0 setup-fee line, or when a covered non-termite annual-prepay term or a paid annual-prepay invoice from the last 13 months exists. Settled means `unminted_setup_fee_manual_billing` is not raised, the completion hold (`unmintedSetupFeeHold`) is not set so the normal visit invoice is made, and `setup-fee-alert-reconcile.js` counts the fee as covered so billing the visit closes or shrinks a standing alert instead of reopening a fee instruction. Sends nothing to a customer and creates no invoice. Off = exactly the old behavior. Rollback: unset the variable.
Setup-fee application settled (`services/setup-fee-alert-reconcile.js`, owner 2026-10-28, the three false alerts of #6830): `GATE_SETUP_FEE_APPLICATION_SETTLED` ships DARK, read at call time via `setupFeeApplicationSettledLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; strict `true`, unset = kill, no redeploy). On, the reconcile of the `unminted_setup_fee_manual_billing` alert counts a parked visit's application as billed in two more cases. First, a prepay year of the customer bought the visit (`annual-prepay-renewals.js` `prepayYearBillingVisit()`: the year's sold selection, the same test the pay-after-first-visit hold uses) and its bill is live: paid coverage, or `payment_pending` on a prepay invoice that is not void, cancelled or refunded and not dispute-suspended. That covers a year from another estimate, a year paid after the visit was completed (never stamped prepaid), and a same-day sale whose prepay invoice carries the visit. Second, the visit's own invoices bill its frozen charge counting its own add-on lines (`scheduled_<visit>_addon_*`) beside its base line (`estimate-first-application-invoice.js` `sumVisitChargeCents()`): a first visit carrying the setup fee as a WaveGuard Membership add-on is frozen at base + fee. The completion that parks a new alert also runs the reconcile right after commit, so a covered visit's alert closes in the same closeout instead of at the next daily sweep. Billed = the alert resolves (done), or shrinks to the charge still owed; a coverage regression (the year voided, the invoice voided) reopens it. Sends nothing to a customer, creates no invoice and changes no completion billing. Off = exactly the old behavior. Rollback: unset the variable.
Setup fee on an open invoice (`services/setup-fee-alert-reconcile.js`, owner 2026-10-31 "do these": a setup fee booked as the plain WaveGuard Membership add-on on a visit invoice that is not paid yet still read "fee owed, bill it"): `GATE_SETUP_FEE_OPEN_INVOICE_NOTICE` ships DARK, read at call time via `setupFeeOpenInvoiceNoticeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; strict `true`, unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_SETUP_FEE_SETTLED_ANYWHERE` on (it is the rule that counts the fee once paid). `setup-fee-obligation.js` `setupFeeSettledElsewhere()` also lists, when the fee is not settled, the customer's open invoices (`scheduled`, `sent`, `viewed`, `overdue`, `partially_paid`; never a draft or a `prepaid` one) whose lines that same rule counts as paid fee money once the invoice is paid (`open`). On, when the fee is not covered but the money already counted plus those open lines reach the frozen fee, the reconcile of the `unminted_setup_fee_manual_billing` alert keeps the alert open but rewrites it to say the fee is already on that open invoice (its number) and must not be billed again, still listing any application charge owed, and stamps `metadata.feeOnOpenInvoice` true. The fee still counts as covered only once paid: paying the invoice resolves the alert at the next reconcile (the daily sweep at the latest), voiding it brings the fee instruction back. The ops-crons morning digest check `b13-setupfee-parks.js` (on the Mac, not in this repo) reads the stamp: it no longer lists an alert with nothing left to bill and names the fee as already invoiced on one that still owes an application. Partial coverage (open lines short of the fee) and the terminal-lane fee clause keep today's text. Sends nothing to a customer and creates no invoice. Off = today's alert text; a standing notice is rewritten back to the owed instruction, with the stamp false, on the next reconcile. Rollback: unset the variable.
Call address family card (`services/call-family-name-link.js` `matchStatedAddressAccounts`, owner 2026-10-24 "yes build"; audited case: a daughter called from her own number for her mother, the names came through spelled a little differently, and the pass minted a third record for one house): `GATE_CALL_ADDRESS_FAMILY_CARD` ships DARK, read at call time via `callAddressFamilyCardLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; strict `true`, unset = kill, no redeploy). On: (1) when no other basis fires, a live customer at the stated house number and street (the existing `sameHouseNumberStreet` rules; a stated unit must equal the unit on file; the stated ZIP or city must agree; at most 3 accounts, more is not evidence) becomes the suggest-only `family_account_candidates` card, basis `stated_address_on_account`, asking "<caller> called about <customer>'s home. Add as a contact?" with the role the call gave; vendor and job-applicant calls are skipped. (2) A card that was filed (any basis except the callback voicemail one, which has its own hold) now also stops the pass from creating a customer for that call: the call stays customer-less like the shared-phone case and the workable-lead path still captures the prospect. (3) Two admin-only card actions: `POST /api/admin/triage/:id/attach-contact` puts the caller's name, number and role in the FIRST FREE service-contact slot of the chosen account through `persistCallSecondaryContact` (`operatorAttach`; the slot write, the relink and the card transition are ONE transaction; never overwrites, all three slots full = 409 and nothing changes; the account's consent stamp is kept and the new number is held out of every text until that person's own YES; no text, email or opt-in ask is sent. The Attach tap is recorded as the office's confirmation that the person belongs to the account (`service_preferences.office_confirmed_slot_phones`: who and when), and the inbound call-identity reader (`slotOnlyLinkAllowed`) links that person's next call only while that confirmation is on the slot; every other slot is read as before) and relinks the call by the shared relink (`services/call-customer-relink.js`, the same code as `PUT /api/admin/call-recordings/calls/:id/customer`); `POST /api/admin/triage/:id/new-customer` closes the card as a person's decision and reprocesses the call (as the Reprocess button does), which creates the customer the old way. Off = both new behaviors and both routes (404) are absent and nothing else changes. Removal: delete the gate with the old (mint-around-the-card) path.
Neighborhood naming (`services/neighborhood-naming.js`, owner 2026-10-24 "ok go"): `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_NAMING` ships DARK, read at call time via `neighborhoodNamingLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy) and honoured only while `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ACCESS` is live. On, the 15-minute gate-code sweep runs a naming pass before it files: (1) it asks the county about 20 live homes per tick (customer active, customer stage, with a pin) that were never checked, plus a one-time second look at checked homes whose `county_subdivision` is a bare Sarasota plat number, and names a Sarasota number from the county's PlatBoundary layer (`max_sub_id` = the number; phases fold into one community; `county_subdivision` keeps the number, so the estimator's subdivision median is unchanged); (2) for a home the county could not name it takes the community the customer said on a call about that same address (`call_log.ai_extraction_enriched` `subdivision_or_community`), matched to the county's directory entry of that name or added as a `customer` neighborhood, and links the home as `neighborhood_source='caller'`, which is UNCONFIRMED and kept out of every shared neighborhood credential, read and write, until the county or the office confirms it: a gate code saved on such a home is not filed (no entry added, no other entry demoted, nothing retried); a visit at it gets no directory entries, no tech add or mark-wrong action, and no shared visitor pass (none shared out of it either); the Customer 360 row lists no entries for it. The link itself stays, naming the community for the office. The county naming the home later replaces it, and the office confirms it with the Confirm button on the neighborhood row (the existing office pick on the same neighborhood), after which filing and reads work as for any home. A call counts as about the home only with the same street and number AND a matching 5-digit ZIP, or, with no usable ZIP on the call, the same city. The county always wins over a caller link, an office pick is never touched, and a county or plat outage leaves the home unchecked (an hour off the batch; three in a row end the pass). Where each home got to is stored on the row (`customer_properties.neighborhood_naming`, jsonb, one migration): a home is picked only once its wait has passed (county answer with no name or a caller try: a day), least recently tried first, in SQL before the batch limit, so unnameable homes never block the ones behind them, restarts included; state written for an old address is ignored after a move. Towns and counties are never taken as a community. The Customer 360 neighborhood row reads "From the customer, confirm" for a caller link. No message, no bell; logs carry counts only. Rollback: unset `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_NAMING` (the sweep is then byte-identical to before); links already written stay, and a wrong caller link is fixed by an office pick on the property.

Neighborhood address lookup (`services/neighborhood-access.js` `homeParcel`, owner 2026-10-24 "Build it"): `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ADDRESS_LOOKUP` ships DARK, read at call time via `neighborhoodAddressLookupLive()` (unset = kill, no redeploy) and honoured only while `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_NAMING` is live. A stored pin often sits on another lot (a ZIP centre, or a few doors off: 29 of the first 40 never-checked homes the naming pass asked about on 10-24). On, when the parcel under the pin is not the home's own (or there is none), the naming pass and the saved-code sweep ask the county roll for the home's own address (`lookupCountyParcelsByAddress`: one `LIKE '<house number> %<street word>%'` on the situs field, no AND/OR for the Manatee WAF) and link by a lot only under the pin path's own proof (`parcelMatchesProperty`: the home's house number, full street with suffix and directional, and equal ZIP); when several lots pass (one building's units), they must all name one community (a Sarasota plat by its number), else nothing is linked. A failed or timed-out search is an outage (the naming pass waits an hour; the sweep tries again next pass), a page-capped answer is no lot. On, a `#` unit tail ("500 Sample Loop #201") is also read as a unit, like `APT` or `UNIT`. Known limits: a home with no pin is not searched; a street spelled differently from the roll ("Bay Side" for BAYSIDE, "Pl" for DR) still does not match; a Sarasota unit row written "<number> <street> <unit> BLD <n>" keeps its bare unit number in the street, so it does not pass; Charlotte has no situs ZIP, so it never links this way. No message, no bell; logs carry counts only. Rollback: unset `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ADDRESS_LOOKUP` (the pin-only match as before); links already written stay, and a wrong one is fixed by an office pick on the property.

Neighborhood merge (`services/neighborhood-merge.js`, owner ruling 2026-10-25): `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_MERGE` ships DARK, read at call time via `neighborhoodMergeLive()` (unset = kill, no redeploy) and honoured only while `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ACCESS` is live. The directory makes one entry per county plat name, so one gated community can show up several times and a code saved on one entry never reaches stops on the others. On, Customers → Gate codes shows Merge into… on each entry: the office picks another entry of the same county, reads a dry run of what moves (`POST /api/admin/neighborhood-access/:id/merge` with `dryRun: true`, which writes nothing), then merges (admin only). A merge moves every home (`customer_properties.neighborhood_id`), every gate entry and every filing-ledger row of the merged entry to the kept one; a live code both hold is kept once (the copy confirmed more recently stays, the other is retired); when the kept entry has a live entry of its own, each moved live entry's label gets the old name in brackets; statuses never change. The merged entry stays as an inactive row pointing at the kept one (`neighborhoods.merged_into_id`, migration `20261025230000`), under its own name, so `lockCommunity` sends a new home with that name (county upsert, caller link, Customer 360 create) to the kept entry, and a search by the old name finds it. Each merge writes a `neighborhood_merges` row (who, when, and a journal of ids, labels and statuses; never a code). Undo merge (`POST /api/admin/neighborhood-access/merges/:mergeId/undo`) puts back what the merge moved and nobody changed since, and switches the merged entry back on; a merge whose kept entry was merged again waits for that later undo. Both routes yield to every other writer (300 ms lock wait, three tries, then busy). Refused: another county, the same entry, an entry already merged or switched off, two entries that both have a gate pin. Suggested merges (owner ruling 2026-10-25: a list, a person always taps Merge): the page lists "Possible duplicates" from `GET /api/admin/neighborhood-access/merge-suggestions`, pairs of live entries in one county whose names read as one community by two rules only (the same name once phase words, a trailing numeral or letter tag, "Lwr", "Sub", "Condo", "Townhomes", "Villas" or "Homes" are taken off, spaces ignored; or "X at Y" where Y is such a name of another entry), the entry with the most homes kept; Review merge opens the same dry run and Merge, and Not the same (`POST /merge-suggestions/dismiss`, table `neighborhood_merge_dismissals`, migration `20261025233000`) keeps that pair out for good. Nothing merges by itself. No message, no bell; logs carry ids only. Rollback: undo the merges you want back, then unset `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_MERGE` (the buttons go; merges already made stay, and new homes keep following them).

Homes not placed (`services/neighborhood-naming.js` `unplacedHomes`, owner ruling 2026-10-26): `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_UNPLACED` ships DARK, read at call time via `neighborhoodUnplacedLive()` (unset = kill, no redeploy) and honoured only while `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ACCESS` is live. On, Customers → Gate codes lists "Homes not placed" (`GET /api/admin/neighborhood-access/unplaced`, admin only): live homes with no neighborhood where the county's lot at the pin carries the home's house number and full street but another ZIP (ours is wrong or blank, or the roll's postal ZIP differs), and live homes with no neighborhood whose customer saved a gate code (it reaches only that customer's stops until the home is placed). The naming pass keeps the ZIP-only lot on the home's naming state (`customer_properties.neighborhood_naming.zip_mismatch`: the county's ZIP, county and plat; written for the current address only, cleared by any other answer; this stamp runs whatever the gate says and has no other reader). A ZIP-only lot is never linked by itself (a pin dropped in another town can sit on the same number and street); the office taps Link to the county's community, which is the existing office pick (`PUT /properties/:id/neighborhood` with `create`), after a confirm. An office decision (linked or cleared) never appears. The list carries no code values. Add entry also gets "I have not seen this work": `POST /:neighborhoodId/entries` with `unconfirmed: true` files the entry `needs_confirm` with no confirmation date and demotes no other code; with the gate off the flag is ignored (the entry is active and confirmed now, as before); a non-boolean is 400. No message, no bell; logs carry ids only. Rollback: unset `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_UNPLACED` (the list and the box go; links made stay, and a wrong one is fixed by another office pick).

Gate codes on the office schedule (owner ruling 2026-10-26): `GATE_SCHEDULE_ACCESS_CODES` ships DARK, read at call time via `scheduleAccessCodesLive()` (unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `GET /api/admin/schedule` sets `scheduleAccessEnabled: true` on each day row, and Dispatch → Schedule draws the row's gate lines — the `propertyAlerts` of type `gate` the tech app's stop brief already shows (`services/nextstop-alerts.js`: the customer's own gate code, else the neighborhood's code tagged "neighborhood" or "neighborhood, confirm on site"; yard, garage and lockbox from the profile) — in four places: the phone list row (one line; amber while a neighborhood code is unconfirmed), the Complete service header of every Fast Complete sheet (the tech app's too; `SheetAccessCodes`), a new Access section in Details, and the desktop side panel. Details and the panel also list the office's accepted codes for the stop from `GET /api/admin/access-codes/visits/:visitId` (404 while the access codes section is off = the lines alone). Details offers Wrong code and Add gate code through the routes the tech app uses (`POST /api/admin/neighborhood-access/visits/:visitId/entries[/:entryId/wrong]`, `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_TECH_ACTIONS`; an admin's add is filed as source `office`). Codes still waiting on the Found list never show. The week payload carries no gate lines, so the week list shows none. Staff screens only; nothing is sent to a customer. Rollback: unset `GATE_SCHEDULE_ACCESS_CODES`.

Access codes from calls (owner 2026-10-23): `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_CALLS` is opt-in (off unless `1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time, and needs `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_SECTION` on too. `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_CALLS_SINCE` must be an ISO instant with an offset: the sweep reads only calls created from that moment on, and with it unset or malformed calls are never read, so turning the gate on never reads history. On, the same five-minute sweep (`services/access-code-capture.js`, cron lock `access-code-net`) runs a second pass after the texts, with its own batch of 10 and its own receipts (`data_hygiene_source_extractions`, source type `call_log`, extractor version `access-net-call-v1`, hashed over the call's owner, direction, both numbers, spam verdict, transcript status, sandbox flag and transcript, identically in JavaScript and SQL, so a re-transcription, relink, phone remap or status change reads the call again; the write rechecks eligibility under the row lock). It reads every `call_log` row with a finished, non-empty transcript, inbound or outbound, voicemails included, whatever its `processing_status` (`extraction_failed` too); it skips spam, pending or rejected transcripts, sandbox calls, a far-end number that is one of ours and a line that is not a Waves line. The call's customer is `call_log.customer_id`, else the one live customer whose phone is the far-end number (outbound: `to_phone`, inbound: `from_phone`), else the code is filed unlinked under that far-end phone, the same rules as an unlinked text. That one owner rule (`callOwnerId` / `callOwnerSql`) is used everywhere: a call's rows belong to its owner now, so clearing a call's link, or a phone that now belongs to another customer (or to nobody), hides the old account's rows at once, retires its active codes with their profile copy on the next tick and files the code again for the new owner; an explicit office link on an unlinked row stays. A keyword net, then one model read (the same reader and schema as texts): only a code the CUSTOMER states counts, and a staff read-back confirms but is not a source. Spoken numbers (`pound, four four one seven`, `double five`, `oh` for 0 between digits) are normalized in code before verification, so the model's `#4417` verifies against the verbatim quote. The verifier keeps the text rules (quote verbatim, house number, ZIP, phone numbers and 10 or more digits refused) and adds: the quote is inside one non-staff turn (staff on an outbound call is the speaker who introduces themselves as Waves, never one who only mentions it) and the code must be the whole spoken run of that complete customer turn with its pound/star symbols (so `4417` fails when the customer said `pound, four four one seven`), the first turn that says the code is the quoted speaker's, a numeric code has at least 3 digits, and a card number (13 to 19 spoken digits), card, CVV or expiration words, or a Google, Bing or bank verification code within 300 characters of the quote refuse the item. A plain `gate` is the neighborhood gate (a front, main or side gate is the property gate), and a gate code given while a technician is at the gate stays standing unless the customer calls it temporary. A calls failure never blocks the texts: the texts are filed first, and a failed call read or calls query fails job health with `ACCESS_NET_FAILURES` (the tally carries `calls`). Nothing is logged but ids and error codes, and nothing is sent or belled. A found row from a call shows as `Call, <day>` on the Gate codes page. Rollback: unset `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_CALLS` (or `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_CALLS_SINCE`); the rows, receipts and the texts net stay as they are.
Access codes from emails (owner 2026-10-24): `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_EMAILS` is opt-in (off unless exactly `true`), read at call time, and needs `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_SECTION` on too. `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_EMAILS_SINCE` must be an ISO instant with an offset: the sweep reads only emails received from that moment on (and at most 30 days back), and with it unset or malformed emails are never read, so turning the gate on never reads history. On, the same five-minute sweep (`services/access-code-capture.js`, cron lock `access-code-net`) runs a third pass after the texts and the calls, with its own batch of 10, its own receipts (`data_hygiene_source_extractions`, source type `email`, extractor version `access-net-email-v1`, hashed over the email's owner, sender address, subject, classification, the SENT/DRAFT/SPAM/TRASH labels, the bulk and bid-desk marks, the authentication result and both stored bodies, identically in JavaScript and SQL, so a relink, an address change, a reclassification or a spam label reads the email again; the write rechecks eligibility under the row lock). It reads inbound mail stored at least 15 minutes ago (so the classifier and the bid desk have had their say) and skips: our own addresses and domains (`wavespestcontrol.com` and the other Waves domains, `wavesflorida.com`), no-reply, mailer-daemon and postmaster senders, auto-reply and bounce subjects, anything with a List-Unsubscribe header, mail classified spam, newsletter, vendor, internal or review notices, mail the bid desk filed, mail labelled SENT, DRAFT, SPAM or TRASH, and mail whose sender Gmail did not authenticate as the domain it claims (the same alignment check the new-email bell trusts). The email's owner is `emails.customer_id` (the Gmail sync's match on `customers.email`), else the one live customer whose email is the sender address, else the code is filed unlinked under that address in `customer_access_codes.sender_email` (new nullable column, migration `20261024130000_customer_access_codes_sender_email`; the owner check now accepts a sender phone or a sender email). That one owner rule (`emailOwnerId` / `emailOwnerSql`) is used everywhere, as for calls: a relinked or moved email hides the old account's rows at once, retires its active codes with their profile copy on the next tick and files the code again for the new owner; an explicit office link stays. Only the customer's NEW words are read: quoted history (`>` lines, `On ... wrote:`, Outlook and forwarded headers) and the signature are stripped before the keyword net and the model, and an item whose quote repeats text we sent in the same Gmail thread is dropped. The reader and schema are the texts' (one model call per flagged email), with a prompt that says signatures, phone numbers, street addresses and order, confirmation, invoice, account or tracking numbers are never codes. The verifier keeps the text rules (quote verbatim in the new words, house number, ZIP, phone numbers and 10 or more digits refused) and adds the calls' card, CVV, expiration and Google/Bing/bank sign-in refusals within 300 characters of the quote, and refuses a numeric code that appears only inside a phone number (a signature). An email failure never blocks the texts or the calls: they are filed first, and a failed email read or emails query fails job health with `ACCESS_NET_FAILURES` (the tally carries `emails`). Nothing is logged but ids and error codes, and nothing is sent or belled. A found row from an email shows as `Email, <day>` on the Gate codes page, and an unlinked one shows the sender address. Rollback: unset `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_EMAILS` (or `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_EMAILS_SINCE`); the rows, receipts and the texts and calls nets stay as they are. Known limits: a bare code sent as the whole reply to our question is not read for emails (texts read it), a body over 6000 characters after stripping is not read, and the subject line is not read.
Found-codes bell (owner ruling 2026-10-24): `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_FOUND_BELL` is opt-in (off unless exactly `true`) and read at call time. On, a five-minute cron (90 seconds after each access-codes sweep tick; `services/access-code-found-bell.js`) keeps one standing admin row (category `access_codes`, key `access-codes-found`, area Customers, needs-you, done when the count is zero) for the codes on the Gate codes page's Found in messages list (`listFound`, so the row's count is the tab's count, from texts, calls and emails alike). It rings when a code joins the list (checked against the id of every waiting code, not only the 50 newest the row names; `listFoundWaiting`, which also gives the day of the oldest waiting message the row names, whatever the filing order) and moves to the top of the bell, refreshes quietly when one leaves (a person's read and done stay), closes itself done when the list is empty, and rings again when a code waits after that. The row names the kind of code, who sent it (the linked customer, else an unknown sender) and the day; it never carries a code, the customer's words, a phone number or an address. Its link opens the page on Found in messages (`/admin/customers/gate-codes?view=found`, also on a page already open). The category rings by default under `GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY` and can be silenced in Settings → Notifications (Gate codes found in messages); silenced, the cron reads no codes and closes the row, so no refresh or reopen rings it (the override is read while the bell policy is on, as on a fresh insert). With `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_SECTION` off the list is not served and the row closes. One sync runs at a time: it holds the row's advisory lock and reads the list inside one transaction. Differing codes in one neighborhood still never ring (owner ruling 2026-10-03). Rollback: unset `GATE_ACCESS_CODES_FOUND_BELL`; the cron then does nothing, and a row left open stays until someone marks it done.

Access code capture: `GATE_ACCESS_CODE_CAPTURE` (off by default, read at call time) lets the SMS operational lane save a gate, lockbox or garage code when the whole text is one plain sentence: an optional greeting, the kind of code, a credential word (code, pin, combo, keypad), the code, an optional thanks ("Gate code is 1234", "Our new side gate code: #1234. Thanks"). Any other word in the message saves nothing. A plain "gate" is the neighborhood gate; a front, main, side or back gate is the property gate. The property's house number or ZIP is refused. Off = only the strict sentence form ("Lockbox code is 1234") saves. It needs `GATE_SMS_OPERATIONAL_ACTIONS`. Rollback: unset it.

LLM mention prober (AEO): `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` enables the Perplexity probe (`PERPLEXITY_MENTIONS_MODEL`, default `sonar`) alongside the existing `OPENAI_MENTIONS_MODEL` / `GEMINI_MENTIONS_MODEL` / `MODEL_MENTIONS` / `LLM_MENTIONS_MAX_PROBES` overrides. Measurement probes call each answer engine directly by design — no ROUTES entry, no Claude fallback (a fallback would falsify the visibility measurement). `LLM_MENTIONS_APP_SCRAPER` (default ON whenever `DATAFORSEO_LOGIN` and `DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD` are both set; `false`/`0`/`off`/`no` restores the API probes) makes the ChatGPT and Gemini rows measure the consumer apps through DataForSEO's LLM scrapers (`llm-app-scraper.js`, ~$0.004 per request, ChatGPT US-level only, Gemini by city); app rows record `model_version` `dataforseo:chatgpt_app:<model>` / `dataforseo:gemini_app:<model>`. The same switch also adds the `google_ai_mode` platform (Google AI Mode via `/serp/google/ai_mode/live/advanced`, model `dataforseo:google_ai_mode`, city `location_name`, Parrish by coordinate), kept beside `google_ai_overview` since they are different Google features; with the switch off it disappears (no API equivalent). `LLM_MENTIONS_MAX_PROBES` defaults to 300: the six platforms x 40 benchmark questions (240) run daily, and a fifth of the ceiling is reserved for rotating ancillary queries. `rank_position` is Waves' place among every company the answer names (`companies_named`): `rank_method` `all_named_v2` when the scraper supplied brand entities (ChatGPT app), `all_named_text_v2` when names were read from the answer text (a company can be missed, so the rank is a conservative bound: every brand-like span before Waves counts against it); rows without a `rank_method` are the older `known_list_v1`, ranked against the `COMPETITORS` list only — see `llm-mention-companies.js`. Readers of the competitor columns (dashboard, gap miner, backlink strategy tools) go through its `rivalsOf` / `rivalEntries` (companies_named when present, else competitors_mentioned, canonicalised, Waves excluded); `competitors_mentioned` itself stays known-list only.

Open-Meteo paid key: `OPEN_METEO_API_KEY` — read at call time in `server/services/open-meteo-endpoint.js`. Set (owner 2026-10-06, Standard plan $29/mo): every Open-Meteo call (`application-conditions.js`, `irrigation-weekly-email.js`, `scripts/sync-lawn-area-weather.js`, and the NWS-outage backup in `weather-forecast.js`, which the pest forecast (`pest-forecast/weather.js`), the dispatch forecast analyzer and the portal weather tile (`routes/feed.js`) also fall back to) uses `customer-api.open-meteo.com` with the key as `apikey`, and the service-week rain skips the archive API (not in Standard; NOAA MRMS already supplies closed-day rain first). Unset: the free endpoints, which are non-commercial only. Never log an Open-Meteo URL: the key rides in it. Owner 2026-10-06: the plan stays; NWS hourly chance stays the primary rain forecast, Open-Meteo is its backup.

AI Overview pinned captures (`server/services/seo/aio-pinned-capture.js`): no gate. An admin pins a managed query (`PATCH /api/admin/seo/llm-mentions/queries/:id` with `pin_daily`, `pin_until`, `pin_location`). Behind `seoIntelligence`, crons at 3:40 AM and 3:00 PM ET (`aio-pinned-capture-am` / `-pm`, runExclusive) make one DataForSEO SERP call per pinned query per device (desktop, mobile), hard cap 12 calls per pass. Every attempt is stored in `seo_aio_captures` (shown / none / task_error / request_error) with the overview text, cited elements, aio_references, organic top 10, People Also Ask and local pack. Read with `GET /api/admin/seo/llm-mentions/captures?query_id=&days=` (`raw=1` adds the full overview item). With no pinned query the job makes no call. `seo_llm_mentions` and `runDaily` are unchanged.

AI Overview gap sweep (`server/services/seo/aio-gap-sweep.js`): `GATE_AIO_GAP_SWEEP_MONTHLY` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `aioGapSweepMonthlyLive()`; unset = off) lets the scheduler start the monthly sweep on the 2nd at 4:10 AM ET. Manual starts need no gate: `POST /api/admin/seo/aio-sweep` (`maxCostUsd` at most 25, default 10; `minImpressions`, default 20; `max` at most 5000, default 2500). A sweep lists every candidate search (Search Console queries of the last 90 days with at least `minImpressions`, branded and "waves" queries left out; competitor-gap queries; active managed questions), stores each as a pending row in `seo_aio_sweep_results`, then a job every 10 minutes behind `seoIntelligence` (`aio-gap-sweep`, runExclusive, no call when no run is open) makes one mobile DataForSEO SERP call per row, 40 rows per tick. Cost is bounded by the run's `max_cost_usd` (the run stops as `stopped_budget` once its cost reaches it) and by `max` rows; only one run can be open at a time. Read with `GET /api/admin/seo/aio-sweep/runs` and `GET /api/admin/seo/aio-sweep/:runId/gaps` (overviews that show without a Waves citation, web citations first, then impressions); `POST /api/admin/seo/aio-sweep/:runId/cancel` stops an open run. Nothing is sent to a customer.

Basic payroll settings (`server/services/payroll-w4.js`, `server/routes/admin-payroll.js`): `GATE_PAYROLL` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollLive()`; unset = off). On, an admin sees a Payroll tab on the Staff page where they type the elections from a signed paper Form W-4 for each W-2 technician (a correction is a new row; rows are never edited) and record how each is paid: paper check, or bank transfer with the date the employee's written OK was received (Florida law). Stores no SSN and no bank account number; the paper W-4 keeps both. Pay runs (`server/services/payroll-runs.js`, `/api/admin/payroll/runs`): a weekly run works out each W-2 technician's paycheck from the approved timesheet with `computePaycheck`, lists anyone blocked (no pay rate, a pay rate below the Florida minimum wage on the pay date, no tables for the year) or waiting for approval, and cannot be finalized until none are left; a technician with no W-4 on file, or whose exempt W-4 lapsed (after February 15 of the next year, or the next business day when that is a weekend or legal holiday), is not blocked: the check is withheld as the IRS default (single, no adjustments; Tax Topic 753), stored with no W-4 election and flagged on the run and the stub; a finalized check is evidence (trigger), void the run to redo a week, and unlocking an approved week is refused (409) while a finalized check exists. A stub per check (employee view, SSN last 4 only) and a CSV export; the owner still pays the technician and makes every tax deposit himself, and the portal moves no money and sends no message. Off, every `/api/admin/payroll` route except `/status` answers 404 before any query and the tab is hidden. Sends nothing to a customer or staff member. Rollback = unset.
Payroll tax calendar (`server/services/payroll-tax-calendar.js`): `GATE_PAYROLL_TAX_CALENDAR` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollTaxCalendarLive()`; unset = off; needs `GATE_PAYROLL` for the finalized pay runs it reads). On, `syncPayrollFilings` writes one `tax_filing_calendar` row per payroll tax duty (column `source_key` `payroll:...`): the monthly federal deposit (941 withholding plus both halves of Social Security and Medicare, due the 15th of the next month), Form 941 and Florida RT-6 every quarter (RT-6 even with no wages; its amount is RT-6 line 5, the quarter's wages under the $7,000 base times the rate each check stored, rounded once, from `payroll-rt6.js`, which the tax form figures share, so the amount to pay matches the return), one FUTA alert row for a year once its FUTA passes $500 (FUTA deposits are out of scope: the row says a deposit is due and leaves the amount to the owner and the accountant), Form 940 (full year FUTA) and W-2/W-3 yearly (Jan 31), and a Florida new hire report 20 days after the hire date of a W-2 technician hired on or after 2026-10-25. Periods follow the pay date. Due dates move to the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or holiday (IRS: DC legal holidays; Florida: federal holidays plus the Friday after Thanksgiving). Semiweekly depositors, the $100,000 next-day rule and FUTA deposits are out of scope. It runs after a pay run is finalized or voided and daily at 8:23 ET before the existing 14-day tax deadline text to the owner (no new notification). It adds rows and updates or deletes only rows still `upcoming`; a row the owner marked prepared, filed, paid or late is never touched. If a pay run later raises an amount above what the marked rows of that duty cover (amount paid, else amount due), a new `upcoming` row `<key>:balance:<n>` holds the difference; a lower amount adds no row. Each row built from pay checks stores `source_digest` (a hash of exactly those checks, migration column on `tax_filing_calendar`). If a Form 941, RT-6, Form 940 or W-2/W-3 row was marked done and its checks later change (a void and replacement), a new `upcoming` review row `<key>:review:<n>` ("figures changed after it was marked done"; n is one above the highest marked review) asks the owner to check the figures when the digest differs from the latest acknowledged state (the marked review row with the highest n, else the marked base row; never ordered by time); marking it done makes it the latest acknowledged state, so a later return to an earlier digest raises a new review (a payment on a balance row does not acknowledge), and a period with a marked row stays covered even when every check in it is voided. Deposits never get review rows, and a marked row without a digest never does. Marking a row filed or paid can store a confirmation number; `paid` now counts as done on the dashboard, Intelligence Bar and tax advisor deadline lists. Off, the sync returns before any query and nothing else changes. The owner makes every deposit and filing himself; sends nothing to a customer or staff member. Rollback = unset; rows already written stay as ordinary calendar rows, remove with `DELETE FROM tax_filing_calendar WHERE source_key LIKE 'payroll:%' AND status = 'upcoming'`.
Payroll Mercury status (`server/services/payroll-mercury.js`, `payroll-mercury-poller.js`, `mercury-client.js`, the `payroll-mercury-poll` job in `scheduler.js` every 15 minutes at :11, `server/routes/admin-payroll.js`): `GATE_PAYROLL_MERCURY_STATUS` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollMercuryStatusLive()`; unset = off and the kill switch; needs `GATE_PAYROLL`). Owner plan A, 2026-10-30: Waves works out each W-2 paycheck and Mercury sends it only after the owner approves the request in the Mercury app; the owner still pays the taxes and files by hand. This is the read-only half: the poller moves each `payroll_payments` row on from Mercury's answers (request pending, approved, rejected, cancelled; transaction sent or failed; a sent payment is read again once a day for 60 days and a failed, reversed or refunded transaction makes it `returned`; an unknown one is looked up by the recipient and the `waves-pay:<id>` note), the payroll bells ring (category `payroll`, `bellDefault`, the owner's Settings override wins: failed, rejected, cancelled, returned, unknown for 30 minutes, a request still pending at noon ET on the business day before pay day, a posting in another month than the pay date, a refused key), saving a technician's Mercury recipient id (`PUT /technicians/:id/mercury-recipient`) reads the recipient and shows its NAME only, `GET /runs/:id/send-preview` gives the three warnings (funding, key health, approve-by day) `POST /checks/:id/paper` records a paper check instead, and `POST /payments/:id/link-request` names the Mercury request that belongs to a payment whose outcome is unknown (it must match the attempt's recipient, account and exact amount and be made no earlier than 10 minutes before the attempt; it moves no money and writes one `payroll.mercury_request_linked` audit event with ids only). Env: `MERCURY_API_TOKEN` (a CUSTOM token: read scopes plus Send Money with Approval; no IP allow-list needed; paste the whole token, with its `secret-token:` prefix), `MERCURY_ACCOUNT_ID` (the account money leaves), `MERCURY_API_BASE` (default `https://api.mercury.com/api/v1`, sandbox `https://api-sandbox.mercury.com/api/v1`; must be https on a mercury.com host). No default can send. Mercury deletes a token unused for 45 days and lowers a token's permission to what it used in 45 days, so the first payment of a pay cycle may need a new key. The token, account number, routing number and every Mercury answer are never logged or stored; the code never calls Mercury's direct send. Voiding a pay run is refused while any of its payments is queued, requested, unknown, approved or sent, with the gates on or off. Off = no Mercury call at all and every payroll output and route is byte for byte today's, except that a paper check recorded while the gate was on still shows on its stubs and in the run CSV. Sends nothing to a customer or staff member.
Payroll Mercury pay (`server/services/payroll-mercury.js`, `POST /api/admin/payroll/runs/:id/send`, `POST /api/admin/payroll/checks/:id/send-again`): `GATE_PAYROLL_MERCURY_PAY` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollMercuryPayLive()`; also needs `GATE_PAYROLL` and `GATE_PAYROLL_MERCURY_STATUS`; unset = no request is ever made). On a finalized run, Send to Mercury writes a `queued` payment row and commits it, then asks Mercury for an approval request (`POST /account/{id}/request-send-money`, ACH, with an idempotency key and the note `waves-pay:<payment id>`) for each bank-transfer check that has a Mercury recipient id and no payment row yet, all under the payroll advisory lock; a partial unique index keeps one open or paid row per check, so a double click is one row. A 2xx is `requested`; a definite 4xx is `failed` (only the HTTP status and a short Mercury error code are kept); a timeout, 5xx or network error is `unknown`, and code NEVER re-POSTs. Send again is allowed after failed, rejected, cancelled or returned, or after unknown when the owner confirms nothing is waiting in Mercury and a fresh read finds no live request or transaction of the same amount to that recipient in the last 7 days; each retry is a new attempt with a new key. Money leaves only when a different Mercury user approves the request in the Mercury app (approve by Wednesday 5 PM ET before pay day; the business day before when pay day is the 1st of a month). Out of scope: a Plaid bank-feed match for Mercury, TaxBandits, any direct-send call, tax deposits. Rollback = unset; existing payment rows stay and still block a void. Sends nothing to a customer or staff member.
Tax deadline bells (`server/services/tax-deadline-reminders.js`, the 8:23 ET `tax-deadline-alerts` job in `scheduler.js`, `PUT /api/admin/tax/filings/:id`): `GATE_TAX_DEADLINE_BELLS` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `taxDeadlineBellsLive()`; unset = off). Owner 2026-10-30, "All tax deadlines ring". The old job texted the owner phone; the text path turns an owner-phone internal alert into the `internal_admin_alert` trigger, which the bell policy (`GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY`) denies, so from 2026-09-01 the owner got nothing while the job still marked each row reminded. Off, that text and the `reminder_sent` marks are unchanged. On, the text is replaced by one bell per row and stage, raised with `raiseAdminAlert` in category `tax` with `bellDefault: true` (rings by default; a saved Settings override for the category still wins). Payroll rows (`source_key` `payroll:%`) not marked filed or paid ring at `d14`, `d3`, `d1` (the business day before the due date, skipping weekends and that row's holidays: IRS rows use the DC legal holidays, Florida RT-6 rows the Florida set, both from `payroll-tax-calendar.js`) and `overdue` (each morning after the due date until marked, one bell a day). Other rows (sales tax, estimated tax) ring once at `d14` and never after the due date. A row first seen inside a window rings only the latest stage due. Stages sent are stored in `tax_filing_calendar.reminder_stages` (jsonb, stage to ISO time); the first stage also sets `reminder_sent` and `reminder_sent_at`. A bell closes (done, `done_by` `episodes`) when its row is marked filed or paid, and the 8:23 run closes any still open for a marked or removed row, and for a non-payroll row once its due date passes. Not behind the gate, same release: `PUT /api/admin/tax/filings/:id` refuses a status outside `upcoming`/`prepared`/`filed`/`paid`/`late`, refuses `paid` or `filed` on a payroll row with no confirmation number, and defaults `paid_date` to today ET on `paid`. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback = unset (rows already written stay).
Payroll tax form figures (`server/services/payroll-form-figures.js`, `GET /api/admin/payroll/forms?year=YYYY&quarter=N`): `GATE_PAYROLL_FORM_FIGURES` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollFormFiguresLive()`; unset = off; needs `GATE_PAYROLL`, which the route already checks). On, the Payroll tab shows a Tax forms section with the line-by-line figures to type onto Form 941 and the Florida RT-6 (one quarter), Form 940, and each employee's W-2 with the W-3 totals (one year), with a copy button on each amount. Figures are added up from finalized, not-voided pay checks (`payroll_checks.status = 'finalized'`) by pay date, from the stored check rows only (no paycheck is worked out again); rates and wage bases come from `payroll-calc.js`. RT-6 line 5 is line 4 times the rate, rounded once (a note shows the paychecks' own sum when per-check rounding differs); the rate is the one each paycheck stored (`floridaReemploymentRateBp`, now returned by `computePaycheck`), else the calculator's new-employer rate, the only one pay runs pass, and is never rebuilt from a rounded tax; 941 line 7 is the fractions of cents in the employee share only (the Social Security and Medicare the paychecks withheld, less the employee share of line 5e; Form 941 instructions), and the employer share is what line 5e leaves; the 941 monthly schedule and 940 Part 5 must total line 12, so a rounding difference goes to the last month or quarter with tax, or comes off the latest ones, never below zero. The W-3 carries no box 12 TT total: qualified overtime stays on each W-2. 941 line 13 and 940 line 13 are the Tax page calendar deposit rows (`payroll:941_deposit:<YYYY-MM>`, `payroll:940_deposit:<year>`) marked `paid`; layer 2 writes no 940 deposit row, so 940 line 13 reads 0. 940 line 10 reads $0 only when every quarter's Florida reemployment tax (all of RT-6 line 5) is covered by `payroll:rt6:<year>-Q<n>` rows (balance rows too) marked `paid` with a paid date on or before the Form 940 due date (January 31 of the next year, moved past a weekend or legal holiday); otherwise lines 10, 12, 14, 15 and Part 5 read "Needs your check" with no amount to copy, because tax paid late or not paid cuts the FUTA credit (IRS line 10 worksheet, not worked by the portal). The section asks for its figures again after a pay run is finalized or voided. 941 line 16 follows the Pub 15 depositor rules from the stored checks: no schedule when line 12, or the prior quarter's line 12 with this one under $100,000, is under $2,500; semiweekly when the lookback period (July 1 two years back to June 30 last year) holds more than $50,000; a check when a month or any four days in a row reached $100,000 of tax since January of last year (whether that was a next-day deposit obligation depends on the depositor status then, which the portal cannot always tell); both read "Needs your check" on line 16 because the portal does not fill Schedule B; monthly otherwise. Employee counts use the 12th rule. No PDF is filled in. No full SSN, EIN, bank account or routing number is held or shown: those fields read "Enter from your records". Off, the route answers 404 and the section does not render. It files, pays and sends nothing. Rollback = unset.
Payroll time off (`server/services/payroll-time-off.js`, `server/services/payroll-runs.js`, `server/services/payroll-calc.js`, `/api/admin/payroll/time-off`): `GATE_PAYROLL_TIME_OFF` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollTimeOffLive()`; unset = off; needs `GATE_PAYROLL`, which the routes already check; owner ruling 2026-10-26, "Paid days off ... add this before the tech's first day off"). On, an admin records one paid day off per W-2 technician per date in `payroll_time_off` (kind `pto` or `holiday`, hours up to 24 with 2 decimals, a note), and a pay run for that week pays the hours at the straight hourly rate on the same check, taxed on the full gross like any wages. Time off is hours not worked, so it never counts toward overtime (overtime stays as the weekly timesheet worked it out); 40 hours worked plus a 10 hour holiday pays 10 hours of holiday and no overtime. A W-2 technician with time off and no worked time that week gets a check for the time off alone; a technician whose worked time is not approved stays waiting, and time off never bypasses the timesheet. A draft stores `pto_minutes`, `holiday_minutes`, `pto_pay_cents` and `holiday_pay_cents` on the check (frozen with it by the existing trigger), the review token covers them so a time-off change after drafting forces a reload, and the pay run table, the stub and the pay run CSV (four columns at the end: PTO Hours, PTO Pay, Holiday Hours, Holiday Pay) show them. A yearly allowance per technician (`technicians.pto_hours_per_year`, a setting; `PUT /technicians/:id/pto-allowance`; the draft policy is 80 hours of paid time off a year plus 6 holidays and 1 floating day, not final) only warns: paid time off past it is saved and the response carries a plain warning. `GET /time-off/balance` shows hours booked and hours paid for a year. Create, change and delete answer 409 once the pay run for the week that holds the date is final, whichever technician it paid (a run finalized without a check for a technician would otherwise never pay a day added later; void the pay run first); the write takes the same lock `finalizeRun` takes. The tax package `w2-payroll.csv` (`GATE_TAX_PACKAGE_W2_LABOR`) adds `Paid Time Off Hours` and `Holiday Hours` after `Overtime Hours`, with the totals row footing them, so the hours reconcile with gross. Recording time off does not mark the technician out on the schedule (`technician_absences` is separate). Off, every output is byte for byte today's: same checks, `calc_snapshot`, token, stub and CSV; the new routes answer 404 `{ enabled: false }`; nothing new renders; the new columns are not read. Pays, sends and files nothing; the owner still pays the technician. Rollback = unset (finalized checks that included time off keep their gross).
Payroll pay lines (`server/services/payroll-pay-lines.js`, `server/services/payroll-regular-rate.js`, `server/services/payroll-runs.js`, `server/services/payroll-calc.js`, `server/services/payroll-form-figures.js`, `/api/admin/payroll/pay-lines`): `GATE_PAYROLL_PAY_LINES` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payrollPayLinesLive()`; unset = off; needs `GATE_PAYROLL`, which the routes already check, and reads paid time off when `GATE_PAYROLL_TIME_OFF` is also on; owner ruling 2026-10-29, D5 part 1 of the first-technician pay plan, "Build the payroll pieces now, switched off"). On, an admin adds pay lines (`payroll_pay_lines`: kind `review_bonus`, `commission`, `health_allowance` or `hsa_employer`, whole cents up to $100,000, the earned week (a Monday), an optional span `covers_from`/`covers_to` for a commission or monthly allowance that covers several weeks, a note) with `POST /pay-lines`, lists them with `GET /pay-lines?technicianId=&status=`, lists the employees a line can be for (every W-2 technician, one who has left too) with `GET /pay-lines/technicians`, and removes an unpaid one with `DELETE /pay-lines/:id`; the Pay runs section of the Payroll tab has the form and the new lines show on the check row, the stub and the pay run CSV (five columns at the end: Review Bonus, Commission, Health Allowance, Overtime On Bonus And Allowance, HSA From Waves). Every open line earned in or before the run's week goes on that technician's check, even for a technician who has left (a lines-only check; a technician whose worked time is still waiting for approval stays waiting). A bonus, commission and allowance are taxable wages: gross, federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, FUTA and RT-6 all read them. The employer HSA money is Section 125 cafeteria-plan pay: not gross, not net pay, in no wage base, reported in W-2 box 12 code W. Every line, the HSA one too (a cash-or-HSA choice counts), is in the federal regular rate (29 CFR 778.109, 778.208-778.215): each overtime hour is owed one more half of the line pay per hour worked, `1/2 x (line pay allocated to the week / hours worked) x overtime hours`, rounded half up once per week and paid on the same check as `line_overtime_premium_cents`. A line with a span is split equally over the workweeks of the span (778.120) and priced from the APPROVED weekly timesheet of each of those weeks (a week with no worked time counts as no hours; a covered week that holds worked time not yet approved makes the technician wait, so a line is never paid without that week's overtime, and with `GATE_SHIFT_CLOSE_REVIEW` on a covered week with an automatic clock-out no admin has reviewed holds the check like the run's own week); a one-week line stays in its week, even when it is paid on a later run. The base hourly rate is not an input, so a raise between weeks never changes the figure; paid time off and holiday hours are not hours worked and never enter it. The extra overtime is paid whether or not the employee is FLSA-covered. W-2 box 12 code TT is filled only for a technician set covered (`technicians.flsa_overtime_covered` true, `PUT /technicians/:id/flsa-coverage { covered: true | false | null }`; null = not set yet = no code TT) from `payroll_checks.qualified_overtime_cents` (base premium plus the line premium); a check made with the gate off stored none, so it counts its overtime premium only when the employee is marked covered now. Form 940 line 3 includes the employer HSA money and line 4 lists it (box 4a, fringe benefits); Form 941 and RT-6 wages exclude it. Finalize marks the lines paid with the check inside its transaction and payroll lock; void reopens them (also after the gate is turned off); a paid line can never be edited or deleted (trigger). Once a line is paid, every week it priced (its earned week, or each week of its span) is closed to timesheet edits, voids and unlocks like a paid week, even when that week had no check of its own, until the paying run is voided (`server/services/payroll-paid-line-weeks.js`, read by `time-tracking.js` and `timesheet-approval.js`; not behind the gate). Adding or removing a line, or moving its span, makes a draft stale. Migration `20261029130000_payroll_pay_lines.js` adds the table, seven nullable `payroll_checks` columns (null with the gate off) and the technician setting. Off, every output and route is byte for byte today's for checks drafted with the gate off (the pay-lines and coverage routes answer 404 `{ enabled: false }`); a check drafted with it on keeps showing and reporting what it stored (check row, stub, pay run CSV columns, W-2 codes TT and W, Form 940 lines 3 and 4), so turning the gate off never changes a paid year. Pays, sends and files nothing; the owner makes every payment and filing himself. Rollback = unset.
Monday briefing technician scorecard (`server/services/bi-tech-scorecard.js`, `server/services/bi-agent-tools.js` `get_operations_snapshot`, `server/services/bi-agent-config.js`): `GATE_BI_TECH_SCORECARD` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `biTechScorecardLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = off = kill, no redeploy). Second technician build 7, owner GO 2026-10-29. On, `get_operations_snapshot` also returns `techScorecard` for the last full week (Monday to Sunday ET, before the Monday the briefing runs): one row per technician with 1+ completed visit. Stops, days worked, on-site minutes per stop (against 25; the repo stores no on-site target) and drive minutes per stop come from `getDayScorecard` (`services/scheduling/day-scorecard.js`, which does not check `GATE_ROUTE_SCORECARD`; that gate guards its route only); drive is the Bouncie `mileage_log` day total, so it includes the legs to and from the first and last stop, and only a day whose every trip has a duration counts (a partly timed day is left out of drive per stop and counted in `driveCoverage.partialDays`). Callbacks come from `callbackCreditByTechnician` (`services/callback-credit.js`): a callback counts for the technician whose visit it corrects, whatever `GATE_CALLBACK_SOURCE_TECH` says. Review asks count `review_requests` rows for the technician's visits that week with a delivered text or email, excluding the no-link check-in templates (`ASK_TOUCH_SQL`). Revenue per tech-day is the dashboard leaderboard's revenue for the technician (`computeCoreKpis` leaderboard, `service_records.revenue`) divided by days worked. Cost per tech-day is the cost card in effect on each worked day (`tech-cost-rates.js`): labor cost per worked hour times the card's paid hours per day, labor only, and only when `GATE_TECH_COST_RATES` is on. A value with no source is `null` with a reason in the row's `reasons`, never 0; a row under 5 stops carries `lowSample`. The BI agent's session takes its prompt and tools from the checked-in `BI_AGENT_CONFIG` on every run (`agent_with_overrides`), so the change ships with the deploy and needs no agent sync; the gate must be set on the service that runs the Monday 05:00 cron. Reads only; sends nothing. Off = the tool output and the agent prompt are byte for byte today's. Rollback: unset it.

Truck views per vehicle (`server/services/intelligence-bar/bouncie-ops-tools.js`, `server/services/bouncie-mileage.js` `getDashboard`, `client/src/components/equipment/MileageTab.jsx`, `GET /api/admin/mileage/dashboard`): `GATE_TRUCK_VIEWS_PER_VEHICLE` (**ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `truckViewsPerVehicleLive()`; unset = off; tech roadmap build 6, owner "GO" 2026-10-29, "Every truck in the truck views"). Today the Intelligence Bar answer to "what did the truck drive today?" reads one Bouncie vehicle and the admin Mileage tab sums every vehicle with no split. On: `get_truck_trips` answers `{ date, vehicles: [{ vehicle, technician, trips (30 shown each), total, total_miles, truncated }], total_miles, note }` for every vehicle, or for the one named by the optional `vehicle` input (a vehicle nickname or the name of the technician whose `technicians.bouncie_imei` is that vehicle's IMEI, not case-sensitive); a `vehicle` that matches nothing answers a plain note that lists the known vehicles (not an `{ error }`, so the circuit breaker does not count it); the tool description and schema are static text, true with the gate on or off (the registry copies them once at load), and with the gate off `vehicle` is ignored. `get_truck_status` adds `technician` to each vehicle (null when no technician is linked). The dashboard adds `vehicles` (one entry per `mileage_log.vehicle_id`: `vehicle_id`, `vehicle_name`, `technician`, `today` and `mtd` with the same fields as the existing totals, ordered by month-to-date miles) built from the same two `mileage_log` reads plus one `technicians` read, and `live_vehicles` (every Bouncie vehicle, same shape as `live_vehicle`, plus `technician`); `today`, `mtd` and `live_vehicle` do not change. The Mileage tab dashboard shows a Vehicles table (vehicle, technician, today miles, month-to-date miles, month-to-date business miles, month-to-date IRS deduction, live state; a tracker with no trips yet shows at zero) and labels the existing totals "All vehicles". Not changed: the IRS report and CSV (a per-vehicle deduction method is a separate owner question), trip linking, cost cards. Read-only: calls Bouncie only through the tools that already did, writes nothing, sends nothing. Off, every response and the Mileage tab are byte for byte today's. Rollback = unset.

Payroll family employee (`server/services/payroll-family-employee.js`, `server/services/payroll-runs.js`, `server/services/payroll-calc.js`, `server/services/payroll-rt6.js`, `server/services/payroll-form-figures.js`, `server/services/payroll-tax-calendar.js`, `PUT /api/admin/payroll/technicians/:id/family-employment`): `GATE_PAYROLL_FAMILY_EMPLOYEE` (strict `true`; unset = off; read at call time via `payrollFamilyEmployeeLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; needs `GATE_PAYROLL`). Owner ruling 2026-10-29, D5 part 2: first use is the owner's mother (a parent), from the first 2027 pay run. On: an admin records, per W-2 technician, the relationship (`parent` or `spouse`), the employer entity (`sole_proprietorship` or `single_member_llc`, no S election) and the start date (`technicians.family_relationship`, `family_employer_entity`, `family_exempt_from`; all three set or all three empty). A pay run whose pay date is on or after the start date skips federal unemployment tax (26 U.S.C. 3306(c)(5)) and Florida reemployment tax (F.S. 443.1216(13)(d)) for that person and nothing else: federal income tax withholding, Social Security, Medicare, Form 941 and the W-2 are unchanged. The check stores `unemployment_exempt` and `unemployment_wages_cents` (the FUTA and RT-6 wages it counted; 0 when exempt). Form 940 line 3 still holds the pay and line 4 lists it as exempt (box 4e, with box 4a for the HSA money); line 5 uses only the non-exempt pay; the RT-6 wages, monthly covered-employee counts and wage list leave the person out. Exempt pay never counts toward the $7,000 base. The relationship child is not supported (the under-21 test needs a birth date); clear the setting if Waves elects S corporation status or takes a partner. Off = every output and route is byte for byte today's for checks drafted with it off (the setting route answers 404 `{ enabled: false }`), and a check drafted with it on keeps reporting what it stored (forms, Tax page calendar, stale-draft token). After it is turned off, a technician whose year already holds exempt pay is paid with no exemption but still stores the two figures, so the earlier exempt pay never uses up the $7,000 base and the RT-6 reads the right taxable wages; rollback = unset. Pays, sends and files nothing; the owner makes every payment and filing himself.

Payroll review bonus import (`server/services/payroll-review-bonuses.js`, `server/services/payroll-pay-lines.js`, `server/services/payroll-runs.js`): `GATE_PAYROLL_REVIEW_BONUS_IMPORT` (strict `true`; unset = off; read at call time via `payrollReviewBonusImportLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; needs `GATE_PAYROLL` and `GATE_PAYROLL_PAY_LINES`). Owner ruling 2026-10-29, D5 part 3a: review bonuses flow into pay runs.
