On: each time a pay run is drafted, recomputed or finalized (inside its transaction, after the payroll lock, before the run is worked out), every `review_incentive_payouts` row with status `earned` that belongs to a W-2 technician and was earned (Eastern calendar date) on or before the run's week end becomes one open `review_bonus` pay line (`source_type` `review_incentive_payout`, `source_id` the payout id, earned week = the Monday week of that date, note `Google review bonus`); the unique index on the source stops a second line. A change the sync makes during a finalize changes the review token, so the finalize is refused as stale and shows the new numbers. Finalizing a run marks each payout it paid `paid` (`paid_at` now, `paid_by` the finalizing admin); if one is no longer `earned` or no longer the technician's, the finalize answers 409 and rolls back. Voiding the run puts those payouts back to `earned`, and the next run imports them again. Stale-line cleanup runs whenever `GATE_PAYROLL_PAY_LINES` is on, whatever this gate says: an open imported line whose payout was marked paid by hand on the Reviews page, moved to another technician, or changed is deleted at the next draft, recompute or finalize, so payroll never pays a bonus the owner already paid. Finalize and void keep the payouts in step with the lines they paid whatever the gates say. The sync writes one critical audit event (`payroll.review_bonus_lines_synced`, ids and counts only) when it changes anything. Off = nothing is imported and every pay run output is byte for byte today's; rollback = unset: the next draft, recompute or finalize takes every open imported line off (a finalize of older numbers is refused as stale), and the bonuses wait on the Reviews page again as earned. Pays, sends and files nothing; the owner makes every payment himself.
Commission Sold by (`server/routes/tech-field-lead.js`, `server/services/field-lead-gps.js`, `server/services/estimate-sold-by.js`, `server/services/admin-estimate-persistence.js`, `server/routes/admin-estimates.js`, `client/src/components/tech/FieldLeadModal.jsx`): `GATE_COMMISSION_SOLD_BY` (strict `true`; unset = off; read at call time via `commissionSoldByLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`). Owner ruling 2026-10-29, D5 part 3b-1: "the technician's flag, checked by the truck GPS, fills in 'Sold by'". It records who sold; the commission ledger that pays it is part 3b-2, and nothing here pays, texts, emails or charges anyone. On: `POST /api/tech/field-lead` also records a GPS check on the lead (`leads.gps_verified`, `leads.gps_check`; the lead is made whatever the result). A flag from a visit is verified when that technician's own truck logged a `gps_arrival.mark_on_property` arrival at the visit (or another stop of its grouped visit) in the 12 hours before the flag AND the truck stands within the radius of the visit's destination now (the arrival detector's own destination rule, `extractDestination`), so an address moved after the arrival never verifies. A new-customer "Neighbor" flag (`prospect`: first name, 10-digit phone, address, ZIP) is verified when the technician's truck (`technicians.bouncie_imei` to `vehicle_locations`, position under 6 hours old, reported and received after the device was last mapped to that technician, the tracker's shared remap rule) is within `system_settings` `field_flag.gps_radius_m` meters (whole number, default 300) of the geocoded address. `gps_check` holds the result and the distance, never the truck's coordinates; the lead activity gets one line such as `GPS: verified, 40 m`. The tech app learns the gate from `commission_sold_by` in `GET /api/admin/feature-flags` and shows the Neighbor mode only then. Saving or revising an estimate fills `estimates.sold_by_technician_id` (source `flag`) from the newest GPS-verified field lead made in the last 60 days by an active W-2 technician (the flagging technician, `gps_check.technician_id`, not the lead's current assignee) that the office built the estimate from (`leads.estimate_id`, set when the office makes the estimate from the flagged lead) and that proves the estimate's place, read from the premise the GPS check stored with its result (`gps_check.premise`, never the lead's editable columns): a visit flag for the visited property (the visit's customer row, and the visit's stamped service address, else the customer's primary address, as the arrival detector uses), a Neighbor flag for the typed address the truck was near; the estimate's service address must match that address (same street and the same unit, no conflicting ZIP, city or state); the same customer, a typed phone or a changed estimate address never binds, and one flag credits one estimate (a lead already filling another estimate is skipped, under a lead row lock); it never fills an accepted estimate or one with an office choice or a clear; a flag credit is re-checked on every save and comes off when a revision moves the estimate to a place the flag never proved, or the office moves the lead to another estimate. `PUT /api/admin/estimates/:id/sold-by` (admin only) sets an active W-2 technician (source `office`) or clears it with `null` (source `cleared`, so the flag never refills it); 409 once the customer accepts; one critical audit event `estimate.sold_by_set` (ids and sources only). The admin estimate list returns `soldBy` and shows a Sold by row. Off = the flag route, the flag modal and every estimate path are byte for byte today's, and nothing is read, written or shown. Rollback = unset: stored Sold by values stay, but nothing reads or shows them until part 3b-2's ledger reads them under its own gate.
Commission ledger (`server/services/payroll-commission.js`, `server/services/payroll-runs.js`, migrations `20261029200000_commission_ledger.js`, `20261029203000_commission_ledger_merge_statements.js` and `20261029204000_commission_entries_payment_source.js`): `GATE_PAYROLL_COMMISSION_LEDGER` (strict `true`; unset = off; read at call time via `payrollCommissionLedgerLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`). Needs `GATE_PAYROLL_PAY_LINES`; reads `estimates.sold_by_technician_id` (filled under `GATE_COMMISSION_SOLD_BY`). Owner rulings 2026-10-29, D5 part 3b-2: the technician earns 10% of what Waves collects for the NEW service only, in its first 12 months, on work the technician brings in; paid in the next payroll after each payment, even after the technician leaves; office-booked calls and web plans do not count; collected = net of sales tax, the card surcharge and refunds. A new customer pays on every payment on the new plan; an existing customer's add-on pays only the add-on's own invoice lines (a $240 add-on on a $600 plan earns $24); a payment that covers several lines is split by each line's share. A refund inside the 12 months comes off the technician's next commission, never below $0 and never from wages; a refund dated after the 12 months is not taken back. Refunds are read from the payment row (`status`, `refund_amount`, `refunded_surcharge_cents`); Waves keeps no reliable refund date (`payments.refunded_at` is never written, and refund writers do not all stamp `updated_at`), so a refund is dated the day a pay run first sees it: one seen while the sale's 12 months still run (today's Eastern date <= `window_end`) is taken off, one first seen after them is never taken back (a pay run syncs at every draft, recompute and finalize, so only a refund in the last days of the 12 months can be seen late, and that errs toward the technician). The first sight of a payment always counts it net of what is refunded then, and an entry is written even when that is $0 (a payment refunded in full when first seen), with its refund, so no later sync takes it for new money. Each entry stores the refunded base it has deducted so far (`commission_entries.refund_counted_cents`); when the row shows less refunded than that (a refund failed, a dispute was won) the money kept counts again. The refunded base of a `paid` or `refunded` row is the refunded cash without the card surcharge share of it (`refunded_surcharge_cents`; on a payer statement row, whose refund writer records no share, at least the surcharge's proportional share of the refund, as the webhook prorates a dashboard refund), at most the base; a `refunded` row with no refund amount and a `disputed` row count as refunded in full; every other status counts 0. Entries recompute on every sync, so a refund inside the 12 months comes off the technician's next commission, never below $0 and never from wages; nothing is taken back when no later commission comes. A full refund of a combined charge is stamped on each per-invoice payment row at its own share, so it reduces each invoice; a partial refund of a combined charge touches no payment row (operator note) and is not seen. Attribution is fixed when a payment is first counted: the entry stores the invoice the payment belongs to and that invoice's share of the estimate and its cash figures (`invoice_id`, `share_own_cents`, `share_all_cents`, `pre_tax_cents`, `tax_cents`) as they were then, and from then on is computed from that snapshot and the payment's own status and refunds, never from today's visits, add-on rows or invoice lines (Update Details deletes and re-inserts a visit's add-on rows with new ids, so a later edit must not move money already counted or paid); a payment or add-on row that is gone leaves the entry as it was (a missing payment counts 0). A line not yet counted belongs to a sold add-on by its row id, or by the pair of the host visit in its `client_id` and its service key matching a current add-on row of the estimate, and invoices are searched through the add-on rows' host visits as well, so an invoice billed before a row was replaced and paid after is still found. Discounts: an invoice line is worth its amount less its discounts as the invoice writer allocates them: the saved discount lines are replayed through the writer's own engine (`stackDocumentDiscounts`, `server/services/discount-stack.js`) the way `invoice.js` replays them on every later save, each at its frozen dollars in its frozen canonical order (fixed credits before percentages); a line discount comes off its line, one whose line is gone is $0, and a document-wide one reaches the lines matching every scope it names (`document_scope_service_key` AND `document_scope_service_category`). A `deposit_credit` line is a prior payment, not a discount, and an invoice-level discount that never became a line changes no line's share. The sold lines' share of the invoice is their value over all lines (a $240 add-on with a $120 discount on a $600 plan earns $12). On: draft, recompute and finalize of a pay run (after the payroll lock, before the run is worked out) make `commission_sales` (one per accepted estimate sold by a W-2 technician, 12 months from the Eastern acceptance date; insert-only, except that a customer merge and its revert move `customer_id`), `commission_entries` (one per sale, payment and invoice: what counted and the commission) and one open `commission` pay line per entry (`source_type` `commission_payment`, `source_id` `<entry id>:<n>` with n the highest suffix the entry has on any line + 1, and an entry's open line (for example one a void reopened) keeps its own id, note `Commission: <customer first name> <last initial>., payment <Mon D>`, no amounts). Payments reach an invoice by `metadata.invoice_id`, else the same PaymentIntent, else the manual description `Invoice <number> — <method>`; a payer statement's settlement row (`GATE_PAYER_STATEMENTS`: one payment for the whole statement, `customer_id` NULL, `statement_id` set, described `Payer statement S-<id> settlement (<method>)` by `settleStatementPaid`, card and offline alike; any other row on a statement is a webhook marker written before a validated settlement and never counts) pays each child invoice that is not void its total over the positive totals of the statement's invoices that are not void (`statement_part_cents` / `statement_total_cents`, fixed with the rest of the snapshot). An estimate deposit has no payments row: the writer applies it to an invoice as a `deposit_credit` line naming the estimate, after tax, as a prior payment, and one deposit can be applied in parts to several invoices, so each application (the deposit credit an invoice carries for one estimate) counts as a payment on that invoice (`payment_source` `estimate_deposit`, `payment_id` = the deposit's estimate id, `invoice_id` = the invoice), shared like any payment by every sale with lines on it and dated the day the invoice was made, never before the sale. The deposit ledger (`estimate_deposits`) records a refund or dispute of a deposit (`refunded_amount`, status `refunded`) while the invoice keeps its credit line, so each application loses the part of the estimate's applied money the ledger shows reversed (a refund returns the never-applied remainder first); an application on a voided invoice, or with no applied money in the ledger behind it, counts as refunded in full (the 12-month refund rule applies). A deposit never applied to an invoice is not counted. Only the acceptance mint (stamped `Auto-generated from accepted estimate #<id>`) counts whole. Any other invoice counts line by line: the estimate's visit lines (the primary line and the `scheduled_price_topup_<visit>` top-up) and add-on lines; lines with no line id when no line of the invoice has one and the invoice is the estimate's prepay term or first application invoice or bills only its visits; and its setup fee and first application lines when the invoice carries the estimate's setup fee claim or names `accepted estimate #<id>` in its notes (a completion invoice that carries a setup fee can also carry another estimate's add-on). A payment a visit's prepaid stamp recorded (`metadata.source` `scheduled_service_prepaid`: cash or Zelle the technician assigned to the visit can mark on their own visit, with no processor settlement and no independent approval) is never counted, so the selling technician cannot earn on money only they attest; the owner adds a manual commission pay line once the cash is confirmed. Office-recorded payments (record-payment, admin only) and processor payments count. Payments, invoices and visits are only read, never row-locked. One critical audit event `payroll.commission_lines_synced` per sync that changes lines (ids and counts only). Off = no sales or entries are written, every open commission line comes off the next run, paid lines stay; with pay lines off nothing at all runs and every pay run is byte for byte today's. Rollback = unset. Not built: monthly-membership dues (payments with no invoice) are not counted, so the owner adds a manual commission pay line for them; there is no ledger page, each commission is a line on the pay run.

First-touch auto-release: `GATE_FIRST_TOUCH_AUTO_RELEASE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, layered on `GATE_TRIAGE_AUTO_RESOLVE` + `GATE_TRIAGE_AUTO_RESOLVE_EVIDENCE`. On, an open `email_unverified` card whose dictation was unambiguous — no arbiter doubt, V1 + V2 + the release target agree, one candidate ≥ 0.9 (a clearly spelled address with no candidates qualifies only under `GATE_FIRST_TOUCH_AUTO_RELEASE_SPELLED`, below), no `name_email_mismatch`, the domain has MX, the pending hold targets that exact address, card younger than `FIRST_TOUCH_AUTO_RELEASE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 7) — auto-resolves (`email_dictation_unambiguous`), and the ledger sweep then releases the hold: the new-lead drip and newsletter opt-in go out. Sends customer email — owner-flip only. The gate is re-asked at the send: a card the resolver closed under it approves a release only while the gate is still on (flip it off and queued auto-releases stop), and every release re-checks the hold's customer binding, the customer's liveness, and address ownership under the hold's row lock. Independent of the gate: the ledger sweep retires any pending hold older than `FIRST_TOUCH_HOLD_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 14) as `blocked` / `first_touch_stale` — a first touch weeks late is never sent.

First-touch auto-release, spelled addresses: `GATE_FIRST_TOUCH_AUTO_RELEASE_SPELLED` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time, and it only matters while `GATE_FIRST_TOUCH_AUTO_RELEASE` is also on. A caller who spelled the email letter by letter files an `email_unverified` card with NO `email_candidates` (the payload holds only `confidence` and `email_release_target`), so the one-candidate rule never fires and a person must press Resolve. On, such a card qualifies when `confidence` ≥ 0.9, `email_release_target` is a valid address and the payload has no `email_disagreement`; every other check above still applies unchanged (V1 + V2 + target agreement, no arbiter doubt, no `name_email_mismatch`, domain has MX, pending hold on that exact address, card and call younger than `FIRST_TOUCH_AUTO_RELEASE_MAX_AGE_DAYS`). `email_invalid` cards and multi-candidate cards behave as before. Sends customer email — owner-flip only. Rollback: unset it; new cards stop auto-resolving (a card already closed under the rule keeps its release, since both shapes share the `email_dictation_unambiguous` key).

Backlink signup worker URL guard (security audit run 2, 2026-10-22): `GATE_BACKLINK_SIGNUP_URL_GUARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`backlinkSignupUrlGuardLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Only matters while `GATE_BACKLINK_AGENT` is on. On, `server/services/backlink-agent/signup-worker.js` locks its browser to the queued site the way the citation filler (`server/services/seo/browser-form-filler.js`) does: before launch the queued URL must be http(s) with a hostname that matches a strict DNS-name grammar (letters, digits, hyphens and dots only; no IP literals, `;`, `,` or `*`, because the pinned names go into Chromium's resolver and proxy-bypass flags) and is not blocked (`contact-finder` `isBlockedHostname`), and the host plus its apex/www sibling are resolved to verified public IPv4 (`resolvePublicIps`, 5 s deadline per lookup so a silent resolver cannot hold the queue) and pinned with `--host-resolver-rules`; a host with no public IPv4 marks the queue row `failed` and no browser starts. A context-level route aborts every request (redirects, sub-resources, popups) whose host is not pinned (`requestAllowed`), service workers are blocked, WebSockets are closed, and `PROXY_URL` is not used (a proxy would do its own DNS). Because Chromium follows redirect hops without calling the route, the network layer is locked too: `--proxy-server` points at a dead local port and `--proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>;<pinned hosts>` lets only the pinned hosts connect directly, so a redirect to a literal IP, loopback or any other host never connects; after the first navigation a page that landed off the pinned hosts marks the row `failed` (`redirected_off_host`). The model-chosen `signup_url` must be one of the pinned hosts, else the row is marked `failed`; a signup page on another sub-domain is therefore not followed. Why: the audit found the worker opened a third-party-steered URL in the server's Chromium with no scheme, host or private-address check. Off = navigation exactly as before. Sends nothing to a customer.

Newsletter sends itself (owner 2026-10-30, option A, after "do we still have the manual newsletter code? if so we need to remove it, this should be fully autonomous"): `GATE_NEWSLETTER_AUTO_SEND` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`newsletterAutoSendLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_NEWSLETTER_PROOF_APPROVAL` on and `NEWSLETTER_PROOF_APPROVERS` set (the proof step it rides). On, (1) the Monday proof step (`sendNewsletterProof`, `services/newsletter-proof.js`) emails the owner an `FYI: [PROOF-…]` copy ("reply HOLD to skip this week") of a weekly flagship that passed every check (recipients, claim validation, calendar target, event lineup, live page recheck), and only after that copy went out queues it for its Tuesday 6:00 AM ET target (`status='scheduled'`, `proof_approved_at` set, `proof_approval_email_id` null: that null is how the dispatcher and the reply handler tell an auto-queued issue from a reply-approved one); until then the claim is a draft the dispatcher never picks up, a failed copy releases the claim so the catch-up retries, and an issue that changed between the copy and the queue stays unqueued and raises a `newsletter_proof_blocked` alert; (2) a HOLD reply (hold / stop / cancel / pause / abort / skip / don't send in the un-quoted text, from an approver) on an auto-queued issue still scheduled returns it to draft and marks its calendar week `skipped`, and no later reply or catch-up proofs or queues a skipped week; (3) Cancel schedule in History (`POST /sends/:id/cancel-schedule`) marks the week `skipped` instead of `drafted` (also for an issue the switch queued when the switch is off at cancel time), so the 4:30 AM catch-up cannot re-queue it; (4) the inactive-reader check-in email the sunset job stages (`services/newsletter-sunset.js`) is scheduled for the next scheduler tick instead of parked, with the same auto-queued marker, and its "win-back waiting" alert stays quiet; a win-back draft parked before the switch (it may have been edited) stays parked and keeps the alert, and a new win-back waits while an earlier cohort is still in its grace window (it goes to the whole `reengagement_due` tag, which they keep until they recover or are sunset) (the safety-valve alert still fires); (5) the autopilot's "draft ready" bell is skipped for a queued issue. The Tuesday tick re-runs the checks; a send it stops (lineup, live recheck, missed 6:00–6:14 window, validation) goes back to draft and raises one `newsletter_proof_blocked` alert that says why (this alert fires with the switch off too). Off: the issue waits for an APPROVED reply, as before, and an issue or check-in email the switch already queued stays queued unsent (the dispatcher skips it) until the switch is back on or its schedule is cancelled in History. Emails the list (625 active readers, Tuesdays).
Newsletter event-click redirect bound to the send (security audit run 2, 2026-10-22): `GATE_NEWSLETTER_CLICK_BOUND` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`newsletterClickBoundLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, (1) at send time the sender stores the lineup's URLs on the send (`newsletter_sends.event_url_snapshot`, jsonb `{ eventId: url }`, written once; a resumed send reuses it and adds any event joined to the lineup since, with its URL as of then; a failed write is logged and the send goes on with live URLs); (2) `GET /api/public/newsletter/e/:token/:eventId` redirects only when `:token` is a real `newsletter_send_deliveries.engagement_token` and the event is in that send's `event_ids` or `alternate_event_ids`, to the URL the send carried (the snapshot), or the live `event_url` for a send made before snapshots existed; an unknown token, an event outside the lineup, a send whose snapshot has no URL for the event (or lacks the event), or a failed membership lookup goes to the homepage (`https://www.wavespestcontrol.com/`); a token that is not a uuid goes home before any query. The per-IP over-budget path applies the same rules and records nothing. Feed pulls are unchanged: a feed can still update or re-use an event row for the next newsletter, but it cannot change where an already-sent email's link goes. Why: the audit found the portal host redirected to whatever URL a third-party feed held at click time for any event id, an open-redirect shape next to the login and pay pages that URL-reputation services (Norton Safe Web rates the domain "Warning") score. Migration `20261022150000_newsletter_send_event_url_snapshot` adds the nullable column. Off = redirect exactly as before; the column stays empty. Sends nothing. Code: `server/services/newsletter-event-clicks.js`, `server/services/newsletter-sender.js`, `server/routes/public-newsletter.js`.

Shared daily cap for public paid-LLM routes (security audit run 2, 2026-10-22, #13): `GATE_PUBLIC_LLM_SHARED_CAP` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`publicLlmSharedCapLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The per-IP daily limiters in `server/index.js` (`askWavesDailyLimiter` 120/day on POST `/api/public/ai-intake/message`, `photoAssessmentDailyLimiter` 40/day on POST `/analyze` for lawn-assessment and pest-identifier) keep their counts in process memory: the counts reset on every deploy or restart, and nothing caps the total, so many IPs (or IPv6 /64 rotation) can each spend a full per-IP budget of paid LLM and vision calls. On, `consumeSharedDailyCap` in `server/middleware/public-llm-shared-cap.js` counts one unit in the Postgres table `public_llm_daily_usage` (one row per bucket and Eastern calendar day, one atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING count`) and the route answers 429 with the same message once the day's count passes the cap. Each route calls it once per request, at the last point before the paid model call (`public-lawn-assessment` and `public-pest-identifier` `/analyze` after the honeypot, Turnstile, photo validation and in-route hourly limiter; `public-ai-intake` `/message` after the gate, in-route limiter and body validation), so a request rejected earlier never burns the shared budget, and a retry or fallback model inside the paid call does not count again. Caps: `PUBLIC_LLM_DAILY_CAP_ASK_WAVES` (positive integer, default 1500 a day, one bucket `ask-waves`) and `PUBLIC_LLM_DAILY_CAP_PHOTO` (positive integer, default 300 a day, one bucket `photo-assessment` shared by both photo funnels); an unset or invalid value uses the default. A database error fails open (warning logged at most once a minute) and the per-IP limiter still applies. Off = byte-identical behavior: no database call. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback = unset the gate. The Chrome extension's bucket `bug-id-extension` (`GATE_BUG_ID_EXTENSION`, below) is the one exception: it is a `failClosed` budget, counted whatever this gate says and refused on a database error.

Chrome extension bug identifier (owner 2026-10-31, "Let's do the insect identification"): `GATE_BUG_ID_EXTENSION` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bugIdExtensionLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `POST /api/public/bug-id-extension/identify` (`server/routes/public-bug-id-extension.js`) takes 1–3 base64 JPEG/PNG/WebP photos from the Waves Bug Identifier Chrome extension and answers with the v2 species-catalog engine's customer-facing object only (`identifyPestV2` on the Gemini-only ladder, as the customer app calls it; never the engine's `internal` or `v1` blocks). Callers are anonymous and worldwide, so there is no lead capture, no pricing, no database row and no stored photo, and no Turnstile (the widget cannot render on a chrome-extension:// page). Spend guards: 6 requests an hour and 15 a day per IP (IPv6 collapsed to its /64, in memory, skipped outside production), then one worldwide daily cap counted in `public_llm_daily_usage` under the bucket `bug-id-extension`: `PUBLIC_LLM_DAILY_CAP_BUG_ID_EXTENSION` (positive integer, default 100 a day, owner 2026-10-31; an unset or invalid value uses the default). That cap is `failClosed`: it counts whatever `GATE_PUBLIC_LLM_SHARED_CAP` says, and a database error refuses the request (429) instead of allowing it. It never touches the website funnels' `photo-assessment` bucket. Off = every request to `/api/public/bug-id-extension`, any method, answers the generic 404 in `server/index.js` before the global `cors()` (so an OPTIONS preflight reads 404 too), the global limiter and the 50 MB photo parser. Sends nothing to anyone. Rollback = unset the gate.

Public lawn watering calculator (owner 2026-10-31, backlink tools plan step 2, "ok go, approved"): `GATE_PUBLIC_WATERING_PLAN` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`publicWateringPlanLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy; also a boot-log entry in `gates`). On, `GET /api/public/watering-plan` (`server/routes/public-watering-plan.js`, logic in `server/services/public-watering-plan.js`) answers one JSON plan per curated Florida location or ZIP for the free embeddable calculator: last 7 days of observed rain (NOAA MRMS merged with Open-Meteo), the plan-week forecast (Open-Meteo), the turf's weekly need (ET0 x crop coefficient, seasonal fallback) and the run/hold decision from the Monday irrigation email's engine. No paid AI, no customer row, no database access, nothing sent to anyone. The legal ceiling is `currentRestrictionPolicy` and it fails closed: outside established coverage the answer is `need_only` (inches only, no event count, no legal maximum) with a link to the county's water management district rules page. 120 requests per 15 minutes per IP (skipped outside production); weather cached per location until the earlier of 3 hours or ET midnight. Wildcard CORS (GET only, no credentials) through the same app-level handler as `/api/public/pest-forecast`. Off = every request to `/api/public/watering-plan`, any method, answers the generic 404 in `server/index.js` before that CORS handler (so an OPTIONS preflight reads 404), the global limiter and the route's own limiter. Contract: `docs/public-route-contracts.md`. Rollback = unset the gate.

Text follow-up alert false alarms (admin notifications audit, owner 2026-10-24): `GATE_SMS_FOLLOWUP_WITNESS_FIX` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `smsFollowupWitnessFixLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Fixes three ways a text follow-up alert (`sms-commitment-source:` bells from `server/services/sms-operational-actions.js`) stayed open or came back after the work was done. (1) A callback witness counted only an outbound call to the exact number that texted; on, a completed staff call of 60 seconds or more to ANY phone on that customer's call rows (`loadSmsFulfillmentEvidence` drops the `to_phone` match for calls) answers it. (2) An estimate witness needed `commitment.sms_context.property_id` to equal the estimate's property, and that id is null when the customer has two or more properties, so the check ended `invalid_witness`; on, a request that names no property accepts any estimate handed to that customer after it (`scopedToProperty` in `server/services/sms-commitment-fulfillment.js`; the model still judges whether it covers the requested service, and a request that names a property keeps the property rule). (3) Done on the bell wrote only the `notifications` row, so the next 5-minute sweep tick saw the follow-up still open and rang again; on, `PUT /api/admin/notifications/:id/done` also calls `settleCommitmentsForDoneAlert`, which marks every open promise the alert speaks for as done by that admin through `applySmsCommitmentUpdate` (the profile panel's Mark done: `status`, `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_at`, an audit event; the emitter owns clearing, `docs/admin-notifications.md`). A follow-up that changed since is skipped and logged, never a failed Done click. Email follow-up alerts are not touched. Sends nothing to a customer. Off = byte-identical to today. Rollback: unset the variable.
Call promises close on their own (owner 2026-10-24: "open promises should close automatically ... a text is sent, the customer confirms it has been resolved, or appt booked, rescheduled — all these should be checked by the agent for all the communication lines"): `GATE_CALL_PROMISE_AI_CLOSE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callPromiseAiCloseLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and needs `GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS` and `PROMISE_EVIDENCE_CLOSE` (default on). `server/services/call-promise-ai-close.js` hands an open, untouched Waves call promise (`call_commitments`, `party = 'waves'`, a call with a customer) that the fixed rules in `call-commitments.js` left open to the text-follow-up checker, as a staff promise made at the end of the call: `loadSmsFulfillmentEvidence` reads every line after the call (texts both ways, calls with transcripts, emails, visits booked, moved or completed, estimates, payments), `verifySmsFulfillment` (with `requireModel`, so a person's later text is evidence for the model and never a close of its own) judges it on `TEXT_POLICIES.highStakes`, and `sms-commitment-thread-close.js` closes it on a later text where the customer says it is done. Only a grounded `fulfilled` verdict closes: the model cites one record and quotes it exactly, and for a call record the quote must sit in Waves' own turns; open, uncertain or a failed read leaves the promise open. A promise with no admissible later record costs no model call. Runs: the nightly overdue watchdog (`call-commitments-watchdog.js`, up to 60 model calls: about $1.50 on the first night over a backlog of about 200 open promises, far less after, because unchanged evidence is cached) and, behind the response, the Owed queue read for the calls on the page (`GET /api/admin/call-recordings/commitments/open`, up to 5 model calls, one run at a time). Verdicts are cached on the row by evidence hash (`call_commitments.contact_check.ai_close`), so unchanged evidence costs no second call. The close writes the same association proof every automatic close carries (`closed_by: promise_evidence`) with `kind: ai_check`, `closed_agent: ai-check`, the cited `record_type` / `record_id` and a short `label` (never the quote: the Owed feed is staff-wide and a quoted line can carry a private link, card number or gate code); the Owed tab lists it under Closed automatically with a Reopen (the existing `reopen` action, a human verdict this job never overrides). `refreshFulfillment`'s re-judge keeps the close only while `aiCloseStands` re-runs the SAME evidence path that admitted it: the cited record must still be an admissible witness under `loadSmsFulfillmentEvidence` / `admissibleWitness` (ownership, property, recipient, delivery and status rules all apply as for the text lane) and must fingerprint (`witness_fp`, an md5 of the record as the verifier saw it, minus fields that only move forward) as it did at close; a truncated source that may hide an old record keeps the close, a source that failed leaves it as it is. There is no per-type column list. The watchdog's lapse scan adds a bounded recheck (`listRecheckCallIds`: AI closes of the last 30 days not read for 12 hours, oldest first, 100 a run), and an Owed queue read rechecks at once. Known limit: `send_report` / `send_paperwork` promises close only on a customer's or a person's later text in the thread (the text lane's rule: no record witnesses them). Off = exactly today's behavior (the run returns before any read). Internal ledger writes only: no customer text, email or call. Read-only dry run: `ops/agents/call-promise-ai-close-dryrun.js`. Remove the gate (and the fixed `other` contact check it overlaps, `PROMISE_CONTACT_CHECK`) in a later PR once it has held.

A later text no longer holds an AI close for good (owner 2026-10-25 "build it", after 16 of the 40 proofs the AI close had found sat held): `GATE_CALL_PROMISE_LATER_TEXT_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callPromiseLaterTextCheckLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), honoured only while `GATE_CALL_PROMISE_AI_CLOSE` is live. Today `call-promise-ai-close.js` holds a record proof the AI accepted whenever any human text came after it (`latestHumanTextAt`: a customer's text, or one a person from Waves sent, which includes a template a staff member sent from the portal), and only the thread check's clear "it was done" releases it, so a plain "Ok" or a text about another job keeps the promise open for good. With the gate on, `server/services/call-promise-later-text-check.js` reads every human message that came after the proof, whole, with exactly the rules the hold counts (`humanTextQueries`, exported from `sms-commitment-thread-close.js` for this; no page and no text cut) and asks one question on `TEXT_POLICIES.fastStructured` (lane `call-promise-later-text-check`): does any of them say this promise was not kept, was undone, went wrong or is still needed? Only `not_contradicted` lets the record proof close the promise, through the same close as every AI close (the proof also records `later_text_check`). `contradicted`, `unclear`, a failed or invalid read, any later message with no words (a photo) wherever it sits, a text longer than 2,000 characters, more than 30 later texts on one side, card-number fragments the scrubber cannot attribute, and a newest message that is not the one the hold counted keep it held exactly as before, and the thread check still runs. The verdict is cached on the row (`contact_check.ai_close.later_text_check`) by a hash of the promise, the proof, the newest human message and the later texts, never with a quote; a held proof now keeps the record it rests on (type, id, time; bookkeeping, written with the gate off too and read only while it is on) in its cached verdict, so an unchanged hold costs no model call and a hold cached before this change is judged again once. A newer human text after such a close reopens it as before (`aiCloseStands`), and the next run asks again. The text follow-up lane is untouched. Off = today's closes, holds and model calls. Internal ledger writes only: no customer text, email or call. Dry run: `ops/agents/call-promise-ai-close-dryrun.js` with `GATE_CALL_PROMISE_LATER_TEXT_CHECK=true` in its own process.

Lawn estimate limits (owner 2026-10-22, "lets go ahead and do this"): `GATE_ESTIMATE_LAWN_LIMITS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `estimateLawnLimitsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy; every output with it off is the old output). On, a RECURRING lawn estimate (the lawn guide packet's own detector: `recurringServicesWithSupplements` + `recurringServiceKey` = `lawn_care`; a one-time-only lawn row does not count) carries a "What we can and can't fix" block: one fixed paragraph on every such estimate plus one line for each flag the office set on the customer's turf profile. The wording is the owner's, word for word, in one module (`server/services/estimate-lawn-limits.js`) that every surface reads: the `/data` payload (`lawnLimits` = `{ heading, paragraphs: [{ key, text }] }`, absent with the gate off and on any non-lawn estimate) which the React estimate page (`LawnLimitsCard`) and the browser-rendered PDF (`EstimateProposalDocument`) print, the legacy server-rendered page (`/api/estimates/:token`, `data-lawn-limits` card), and the pdfkit fallback PDF (customer download, admin download and the email attachment builder). Copy only: no prices, no send logic touched. Flags (migration `20261022192000`, two nullable columns on `customer_turf_profiles`, safe down): `other_grasses` (text[], any of carpetgrass, bahiagrass, bermudagrass, torpedograss, dallisgrass; stored as a clean ordered list, an empty list is NULL) and `virus_streaks_suspected` (boolean). The general turf profile `PUT /api/admin/customers/:customerId/turf-profile` reads and writes them (400 on an unknown grass or a non-boolean) and its GET answers `lawnLimitsAvailable` + `otherGrassOptions` only while the gate is live; with the gate off the columns are neither written nor returned and the editor shows nothing (Field Assessment turf profile editor, "Seen in the estimate photos"). Which profile counts (Codex #6487 r1): only the ACTIVE turf profile (active, or the legacy NULL: `loadTurfProfile`, the canonical loader), and only when it speaks for the estimate's or visit's property. `customer_turf_profiles` has no property column (one row per customer), so the rule is the one the bermuda removal switch uses (`profilePropertyScope`): the profile speaks for the customer's only active property, else the primary one; an estimate or visit for another property, or one that names none at a customer with several properties, or a failed read, gets the fixed paragraph only and no tech warning (fail closed); a customer with no active property rows and no named property is a legacy single home and counts. A lawn recorded as bermuda, zoysia, bahia or mixed (profile grass, then track, then the customer's legacy lawn text) gets NO block, because the fixed paragraph is about St. Augustine; an unknown or blank grass keeps it. Frozen at accept (Codex #6487 security P2): an OPEN estimate follows the live profile, but the customer accept (`PUT /api/estimates/:token/accept`, in its transaction, after the status flip) and the staff manual accept (`markEstimateManuallyAccepted`, after the claim) write the block as rendered into `estimate_data.lawnLimitsAtAccept` (no new column), and an accepted, declined, expired, price-locked, past-expiry or archived estimate prints ONLY that stored block on every surface (`/data`, the React page, the browser PDF, the legacy page, the pdfkit PDF, the email attachment); nothing stored (accepted before this shipped, the gate off or no lawn at accept, a one-tap purchase) means no block, never the live profile. Stale accepts are refused (Codex #6487): `/data` carries `lawnLimitsHash` beside `lawnLimits`, the React page (and the legacy page's script) echoes it as `lawnLimitsHash` in the accept body, and `PUT /api/estimates/:token/accept` recomputes the live block's hash before any write and answers 409 `LAWN_LIMITS_STALE` ("This estimate was refreshed. Please reload the page and review the updated terms before accepting.") on a difference. No block on both sides matches; an old tab that sends no hash is refused exactly when a block exists now; a tab that rendered a block when none exists now is refused; gate off = no check. The staff manual accept sends no attestation (the office accepts on its own screen); it stores the block live at that moment. A customer with no linked profile (or an estimate with no customer) still gets the fixed paragraph. Tech sheet: with carpetgrass on the profile the lawn Fast Complete context carries `carpetgrassCelsiusWarning` ("Carpetgrass on this lawn: Celsius kills it. Spot only, off the carpetgrass.") and a Celsius WG row on the sheet shows it as a note under the product: no new tap, no new step, never a block (the full form is not covered). Kill: unset the variable.
Satellite palm count typed before send (owner 2026-10-24 "ok go", follow-up B to #6562): `GATE_SATELLITE_PALM_COUNT_TYPED` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `satellitePalmCountTypedLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, a never-sent estimate whose stored Tree & Shrub line priced a palm count read from the satellite image (`palmCountFromLookup` with a count above 0, found by `satellitePalmCountToConfirm` in `server/services/estimator-engine/lookup-palm-review.js`) is sent only with the admin's own count: `assertEstimateSendable` in `server/routes/admin-estimates.js` refuses with 409 `PALM_COUNT_REQUIRED` until `POST /api/admin/estimates/:id/send` carries `confirmedPalmCount`, and with 409 `PALM_COUNT_MISMATCH` when that count is not the priced one (the quote is rebuilt with the real count first). Acknowledging the AI review (`acknowledgeEngineReview`) no longer clears it. `GET /:id/send-preview` returns `satellitePalmCount` (the priced count) so Review and send shows a "Palms you counted on the aerial photo" field and refuses a different number before an attempt starts; the Agent Estimate page asks with a prompt. Per estimate: a grouped sibling is never cleared by the anchor's count. A scheduled or sending row cleared it at request time, like the review acknowledgment; a row already sent is never asked. Off = the one-click acknowledgment as before. Never sends, never changes a price.

First-touch hold shelf life: `FIRST_TOUCH_HOLD_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 14). The ledger release engine retires any held first-touch send whose hold OR source call is older than this as `blocked` / `first_touch_stale` — on the canonical claim path every release takes and in the ledger sweep's pre-pass — so a "welcome, new lead" email is never sent weeks late. An unreadable source-call age re-pends the hold (`call_age_unavailable`) rather than passing.

Email bounce rescue: `EMAIL_BOUNCE_TRANSCRIPT_RESCUE` (`off` disables the transcript-evidence rescue; default on, same convention as `EMAIL_BOUNCE_RECOVERY`), `RESCUE_SUGGESTION_EMAIL_TO` (ACT: suggestion recipient, default contact@).

Content publish gates: `GATE_COMPLIANCE` — the semantic compliance gate, an LLM second layer for `REENTRY_SAFETY_CLAIM` / `BANNED_TOPIC` catching the paraphrases regex cannot express. **Ships DARK: off unless set to exactly `true`.** It P0-blocks a publish, so calibrate before enabling — `node ops/agents/compliance-gate-eval.js --document --all` (live API keys required) reports recall/precision over the labelled corpus 23 Codex rounds produced. **`--document` is required for an activation decision**: without it the harness sends isolated sentences, which measures discrimination but not long-document recall or whether a banned topic reads as offered-by-Waves vs merely discussed — the context production always supplies. Treat the first clean run as provisional and hand-check a sample of both verdicts before flipping the flag. Once on, `GATE_COMPLIANCE=false` is the revoke. The regex layer in `content-guardrails.js` is unaffected either way and stays fail-closed. Also `MODEL_COMPLIANCE` (swaps the Anthropic leg only; OpenAI fallback stays) and `COMPLIANCE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 60000, no retry — same ceiling as the fact-check gate).

Estimate sent ⇒ Waves Assessment closed: `GATE_ESTIMATE_SENT_CLOSES_ASSESSMENT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`estimateSentClosesAssessmentLive()`), owner ruling 2026-10-04. On, a sweep every ten minutes (`assessment-estimate-closeout.js`, cron lock `assessment-estimate-closeout`) completes an open Waves Assessment visit once an estimate was handed off to its customer after it (a real delivery or the customer's own acceptance, `LATEST_HANDOFF_SQL` — never a bare `sent_at`), through the canonical completion — the assessment's internal-only profile means no service report, completion text, review ask or invoice. It reads durable state (open assessment visits of the last 30 days, estimates with `sent_at` in the last 14 days), so no estimate send path is hooked. "After": a visit its technician set out for or reached (`en_route` / `on_site`) closes when the estimate was sent after `arrived_at` (else `en_route_at`); a visit nobody is known to have gone to closes only when the estimate was sent on a later ET day; an estimate sent before the visit closes nothing. One estimate closes one assessment: the visit its booking link (`estimate_data.scheduled_service_id`) names, else the newest of that customer on or before the estimate's day. An assessment with a visit price, a prepayment or a linked invoice is never closed (money is a person's); the close passes `systemQuietCloseout` so the completion mints, adopts, credits or charges no invoice and writes no technician activity line or `job_complete` notification. It records no inspection credit offer (`offerInspectionCredit: false`, owner ruling 2026-10-04): the $75 credit comes only from a hand completion. A running job timer or a grouped stop leaves it open. The whole decision (assessment identity, estimate, rule, timer) is re-made on the row the completion locks (`recheckLockedAssessment`, called by `completeScheduledService` for an `assessmentEstimateCloseout` request: a refusal is a 409 `assessment_estimate_close_refused` before any write). Every close runs in the backfill posture, the visit day included, so time on site stays unknown. Audit: `visit.assessment_closed_on_estimate_sent` / `visit.assessment_close_on_estimate_sent_refused` (a refused visit rests 6 hours; a failure is retried on the next tick). It records no consultation outcome. Rollback: unset the gate; visits already closed stay closed.

Invoice issued ⇒ visit completed: `GATE_INVOICE_ISSUED_CLOSES_VISIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`** (owner ruling 2026-09-07). On, an invoice that bills an open, not-future visit and is SENT to the customer (any surface) or PAID by hand closes that visit out through the canonical completion in its quiet backfill posture — no service report, completion text, review ask, or charge; the invoice is reused, none minted. Linked invoices ONLY (`scheduled_service_id`, or through its service record) — an unattached office invoice is never paired by inference (owner ruling 2026-09-07; link it at creation instead). Project-backed visits (completion profile `requiresProject` / `projectBacked`) are excluded — they complete only through their project's close route — and are audited with reason `project_backed`. Audit rows for every linked visit: `visit.completed_on_invoice_issued` / `…_refused` (with the reason; a thrown failure is `code: 'error'`); an invoice with no visit link is logged only. Automated triggers act as the system, never as the visit's technician. **Which visit closes (owner ruling 2026-10-04, `issuedCloseoutVisitRefusal`):** a visit its technician arrived at (`on_site`) closes on a send or a payment once its day has passed, and TODAY only on a payment. A visit nobody arrived at (pending / confirmed / legacy NULL) closes only on a past day AND only when the invoice's own stamp (`paid_at` for a payment, the newest delivery stamp for a send) is on a later ET day than the visit — settled or delivered on or before the visit day it is a prepayment and stays open (`visit_prepaid`; `visit_scheduled_today` on the day itself). The proof is the durable stamp, not the clock at call time, so a live trigger, a redelivered webhook and a retry sweep reach the same verdict; with no stamp the call day stands in. `en_route`, future and terminal visits never close. A visit whose job timer is still RUNNING stays open (`visit_timer_running`) — the closeout only reads `time_entries`, never ends or re-times one; a closed arrived visit's time on site stays unknown (backfill duration policy). Card and bank payments trigger it too: the Stripe webhook runs the closeout for every settled invoice (office card-on-file charge, pay page, Auto Pay, cleared bank debit), before its review step. Retry: `retryIssuedInvoiceCloseouts` runs daily at 11:37 ET (cron lock `invoice-issued-closeout-retry`) over delivered or settled invoices of the last 7 days that are still linked to an open visit, with the trigger the invoice's state proves (`paid` when settled, else `sent`). An ARRIVED (`on_site`) visit is retried whether or not a closeout ever ran. An UNSTARTED past-day visit is retried under the same prepayment rule (the sweeps prefilter it so a prepaid visit is not re-audited daily). Statement children (`retrySettledStatementCloseouts`: settled statements with `paid`, delivered unpaid ones with `sent`; a child's delivery proof is its statement's `sent_at`) run in the same daily cron.

LLM call ledger (agent control S2a): `GATE_LLM_CALL_LEDGER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = kill). On, every provider call through `server/services/llm/call.js` / `deep.js` and every Managed Agents session writes a `row_kind` `call` / `session` row to `llm_dispatch_log` (tokens incl. cache read/write + reasoning, latency, served model, lane / run correlation). The chain rows and digest under `GATE_LLM_DISPATCH_METRICS` are unaffected either way. `GATE_AGENT_CONTROL_READ` (S2d, **dark**, read at call time) serves the Agents hub Control center reads — `/api/admin/agents/control/areas` + `/control/lanes` over the ledger (ET windows today/7d/30d, per-lane ok / fallback rate, p50/p95 latency, tokens, attention status) and flips `features.ledger` on the hub probe; off = both 404.

Estimated AI spend (dark): `GATE_LLM_COST_TRACKING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `llmCostTrackingLive()` (`server/services/llm-cost.js`). Prices are pulled from OpenRouter's public model list into `llm_model_prices` (never hand-typed, owner ruling 2026-09-03), refreshed when a week old (each pull replaces the table: a model the feed dropped goes unpriced). On, the Agents hub Control center shows each lane's estimated cost for the window (`estCostUsd`, `unpricedCalls`; the ledger's tokens from `GATE_LLM_CALL_LEDGER` times list price, provider token semantics respected; a call past a long-prompt threshold bills at the feed's tier rate; where the ledger cannot tell which listed rate applied, e.g. a cache write's lifetime, the higher one is used, so the estimate may run high, never low; a model the feed does not list, a call with no usage (except a single call the provider refused with a status the SDKs never retry, 400/401/402/403/404/413/422, which bills nothing; a timeout, a retryable 408/409/429/5xx and any session turn with no usage stay unpriced), Anthropic cache writes with no listed write rate, or a session turn whose total prompt reaches a tier is counted unpriced, never guessed; image / audio / embedding calls write no ledger row, and per-request fees such as web search are not recorded, so neither is included), and a daily 7:40 AM ET check raises ONE `llm_cost` admin item when a lane's spend yesterday is at least `LLM_COST_ALERT_MIN_USD` (default 5) and `LLM_COST_ALERT_MULTIPLIER` (default 3) times its average day over the week before, closing it once spend is normal; with `GATE_LLM_CALL_LEDGER` off, or no ledger rows at all yesterday, it neither raises nor closes, an item stays open while a lane it names had unpriced calls yesterday, and a lane with unpriced calls in its baseline week is not checked for a spike. Internal only. Off = no fetch, no item, cost null on the hub.

Terminal content writer (dark): `GATE_CONTENT_WRITER_TERMINAL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `terminalWriterLive()` (`server/services/content/terminal-writer.js`; owner ruling 2026-10-08: content that can wait is written in the owner's terminal on the Claude plan, not by a paid agent session). Only the draft step of `autonomous-runner.js` `runNext` changes: the claim, the brief, every gate, the publish and the PR poller's post-merge chain are the same as for an agent draft. On, where the runner would dispatch the writer or refresher agent it reads `terminal-drafts/<opportunity id>.json` on the branch `terminal-writer/<opportunity id>` of the Astro repo (the agent's `emit_draft` input plus `opportunity_id` and `brief_id`; at most 400 KB; shape-checked). A row that waits keeps the brief it was handed: while its latest run ended waiting, each look at the row loads that stored brief instead of composing a new one (for up to 7 days), from the top of the run. The file must name that brief, so the draft is judged against the brief it was written from. That binding makes a draft read-once (the run that takes it becomes the latest run, so the file's brief is no longer the one the row waits on), so a gate retry asks for a fresh draft; the branch is deleted as best-effort cleanup at the end of the batch, after the run that took the draft is stored, and only while it still points at the commit that was read. No file, or a rejected one, records the run as `deferred_terminal_draft` (`skip_reason` `terminal_draft_missing` / `terminal_draft_invalid` / `terminal_draft_unreadable` when GitHub could not be read; the brief stays on the run) and defers the claim 3 hours with the attempt refunded; no agent session starts. The 1:00 PM catch-up claims blog rows only (written blog drafts first, then by score), so only the next 9:00 AM batch looks again at a refresh. Written drafts go first (owner rulings 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-29; kill switch `AUTONOMOUS_CONTENT_TERMINAL_DRAFTS_FIRST=false`, default on): before it claims by score, and before its reserved citability backfill slots, every batch spends its first slots, inside the same batch limit (`AUTONOMOUS_CONTENT_DAILY_BATCH_SIZE`, default 5), on the rows whose usable draft is pushed (`awaitingTerminalDrafts().written`, best score first; a row whose brief is past its 7 days is briefed again instead). Each of those claims is scoped to the written rows not yet taken (`claimNext({ onlyIds })`) and keeps every claim rule, and each of those runs still checks the publish caps and every gate; when none of them is claimable, the slot returns to the score order. A scoped pass takes only its own lane's drafts: the 1:00 PM blog catch-up takes the written blog drafts first (2026-10-29: a deploy cut the 9:00 AM batch after two claims, and the catch-up spent all ten slots by score on blog rows with no draft while four blog drafts waited), and the blog fallback after a failure streak keeps taking the blog drafts left. With none written, or the switch off, the batch claims by score as before. After each batch ONE admin item (`Content — write N website posts in the terminal`, dedupe key `content-terminal-due:<ET date>`, raised through `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`: rewritten quietly when the list changes, closed when nothing waits, reopened and rung when work comes back the same day) lists the pending rows whose latest run is `deferred_terminal_draft` and that have no usable draft yet; a row whose terminal draft failed a gate (`deferred_gate_retry`) is counted in the item's detail and becomes writable when the next run composes its retry brief. The item is raised with `bellDefault: true` (the `content` category is off the bell policy's default list). The blog drought alert is not sent while a blog waits for its draft and today's item stands (`blogDraftRequested`); other page types waiting, a suppressed item or a failed read leave the drought alert in place. Title/meta rewrites (`rewrite_title_meta`) keep their agent, and so do blog, customer-question and refresh briefs while `GATE_EDITORIAL_EVIDENCE` is on (the agent session's approved answer plan cannot be carried by a terminal draft). `ops/agents/content-terminal-due.js` prints the list and, with `--brief=<id>`, the brief (with `seo_requirements`, without phrases customers typed in texts), the writer agent's system prompt, the draft shape and, for a refresh, the live page, read-only. Off or unset = the agent drafts as before; a `deferred_terminal_draft` row is claimed by the next batch like any deferred row, and the next run closes any open terminal item. The daily batch, the admin Run now button and `run-autonomous-next.js --live` all end with the same step (`settleTerminalWork`): branch cleanup for drafts the run took, then the item. Needs `GATE_AUTONOMOUS_CONTENT` on.

Zelle payment-notice reconciler: `GATE_ZELLE_NOTICE_RECONCILE` — **ships DARK: off in prod unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = live kill). On, the Gmail sync settles an authenticated Capital One "sent you money with Zelle" notice against the ONE open self-pay invoice it matches (exact cents + payer name or memo invoice number) through `recordManualPayment` — receipt email + SMS included (owner ruling 2026-09-02) — and parks everything else on the Invoices page for one-click Apply / Ignore.

Zelle payments from the bank feed: `GATE_ZELLE_BANK_RECONCILE` — **ships DARK: off in prod unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = live kill). On, the hourly Plaid sync job (`GATE_BANK_IMPORT` + `GATE_PLAID_SYNC`) then reads each new "Zelle money received from <payer>" credit on a Plaid bank account (Capital One names the payer in the bank's own wording, stored as `bank_transactions.original_description`) and runs the same decision table as the email reconciler: the ONE open self-pay invoice at the exact cents whose customer name corroborates the payer is settled through `recordManualPayment` with the receipt email + SMS; everything else parks on the Invoices page. Only credits dated in the last 14 days and no earlier than 2 days before the account was linked are read; a credit posted more than 72 hours before the pass parks as too old. A parked bank credit with no candidate invoice is listed on the card without an alert. Owner flips it (a customer receipt goes out). Kill = unset.

PostHog ingest proxy: `GATE_POSTHOG_INGEST_PROXY` — **ships DARK: off unless `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at request time via `gateEnvValue` (unset = kill, 404). Railway injects variables at process start, so let the variable change trigger its automatic redeploy — never set this gate with `--skip-deploys` (the running process keeps the old value until `railway redeploy`). On, `/ingest/*` on the portal origin forwards verbatim to PostHog Cloud (fixed upstream hosts, cookies/auth/referer stripped, visitor IP in `X-Forwarded-For`, per-IP limiter after the gate, in-flight cap before buffering, 2 MB / 10 s caps, nothing from the request logged) so ad blockers stop dropping the hub's and `/book`'s funnel events. Inert until a caller points its SDK at it: hub `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=https://portal.wavespestcontrol.com/ingest` (+ Pages redeploy), portal `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST=/ingest`; both SDKs take `*_POSTHOG_UI_HOST` (default `https://us.posthog.com`) for toolbar/replay links. Kill = unset the gate AND revert the caller's host env — an SDK pointed at a 404 just drops events.

Affiliate links (blog monetization pilot): `GATE_AFFILIATE_LINKS` — strict opt-in; blog bodies reference owner-approved products by id through `<AffiliateLink product="…">`, resolved against the vendored `packages/affiliate-registry` (source of truth in the astro repo; `npm run sync:affiliate-registry`). Gate off = every AffiliateLink is a P0 and the lane is dark; raw tracking URLs are always `DISALLOWED_EXTERNAL_LINK`; newsletter/social strip affiliate material regardless of the gate. Risk classes, page eligibility, disclosure, density, and refresh rules are in `content-guardrails.js`; autonomous supporting blogs need no per-post approval (the PR poller validates the current head against the live registry; other content lanes retain their existing approval contract); playbook in `docs/affiliate-links-pilot.md`.

Lead Response agent run deadline: `LEAD_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (milliseconds, default 180000 = 3 min), read once per run. Bounds the whole run (session creation, every events POST, each tool wait) and is recorded as `session_timeout` on the ledger; a tool with a customer-visible side effect (the lead text, the owner draft) is never abandoned mid-flight — it finishes before the run returns. Unset, blank, non-numeric or non-positive falls back to the default. Kill the agent entirely by unsetting `LEAD_AGENT_ID`.

Sandy unbooked-call hand-off (`server/services/voice-agent/relay-unbooked-handoff.js`, hooked in `relay-conversation.js` end(), trigger `relay_unbooked_call` in `notification-triggers.js`): `GATE_RELAY_UNBOOKED_HANDOFF` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `relayUnbookedHandoffLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, a PRODUCTION relay call (never the `voice_relay_sandbox` source) whose close-time reconcile stamps `ai_handled` with at least one caller turn, no booking, no lead (including a capture floor that stood down or failed), no re-service and no transfer, claims ONE stamp (`call_log.metadata.relay_unbooked_alerted_at`, a single guarded UPDATE that re-proves those facts on the row), writes a lead from the call through `createLeadFromExtraction` (when the caller number is a valid E.164; the lead activity carries `source: sandy_unbooked`) and rings ONE admin bell `relay_unbooked_call` (high, Communication, category `missed_call`, dedupeKey `relay-unbooked:<CallSid>`, opens the call) with the call summary and the caller number. A relay call has no Twilio recording, so the recording processor never picks it up; the lead is written directly. A second reconcile, a reconnect close or a late-segment repair matches 0 rows and does nothing. Off, the close is byte-identical to today. Kill: unset.

Voice recovery evidence: `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_RECOVERY` — off unless exactly `true`, read at write time. Verified lead capture and re-service filing stamp their call metadata in the artifact transaction so a later session can distinguish a committed artifact from a failed write. Unset to disable.

SMS solicitation screen: `GATE_SMS_SPAM_CLASSIFIER=shadow` records evidence only; `true` also marks confident unknown-sender pitches read and stops their alerts, replies, lead creation and estimator handling. Default off; unset to disable. Known relationships, genuine opt-out requests, carrier commands, reactions, empty bodies and the AI line bypass enforcement. Both message records retain `metadata.spam_verdict`; only an enforced latest inbound is omitted from the unanswered digest. See the Twilio entry in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`.

SMS scheduling by text (sms-booking-complete-scope 2026-10-02; `server/services/sms-scheduling-decide.js`, `server/services/sms-scheduling-act.js`): `GATE_SMS_SCHEDULING_DECIDE` — off unless exactly `true`, read at call time via `decideLive()`. On: when a customer texts from a phone that holds an open offer of picker times (`sms_offers`), one model call reads the reply and code checks it; the result is recorded in `sms_offer_decisions` as what it would do. Records only. `GATE_SMS_SCHEDULING_ACT_MOVE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `actMoveLive()`; needs the decide gate. On: a recorded `would_move` from a reply at most 15 minutes old is carried out through the reschedule link's own eligibility, picker rebuild and mover (`routes/reschedule-public.js` `_internals`), with the offer, logged-move, portal-request and reminder reply-1/2 fences read again under the move's locks; the customer gets the standard rescheduled text (the series text when a recurring visit's date move shifts later visits). Every refusal leaves the visit untouched and the text to staff. Result on the decision row: `execution_status` `moved` / `refused` / `failed` / `claimed`. Kill: unset; no decision is retried.

Call transcription tunables: `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` / `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEYWORDS` (CSV of literal keyword hints, gpt-transcribe family only), `CALL_PROC_MIN_AUDIO_BYTES_PER_SEC` (partial-download floor, default 3000), `CALL_PROC_EARLY_PROCESS_DELAY_MS` (early verified attempt, default 2 min).

Voice relay (Sandy) tuning: `VOICE_RELAY_INBOUND_MODEL` — inbound-only override, checked once per session at conversation construction and pinned on that session; takes precedence over the shared `VOICE_RELAY_MODEL` (which collections-conversation.js also reads and this override never reaches) and falls back to it, then `MODELS.VOICE`. `VOICE_RELAY_SANDBOX_MODEL` outranks it, but only for a sandbox session (`VOICE_RELAY_SANDBOX_NUMBER` calls below) — never production inbound. Both are checked against the live `config/models.js` MODEL_CATALOG — Anthropic text models excluding `requires: 'deep'` ids AND thinking-always-on ids (`MODELS.anthropicThinkingAlwaysOn` — Opus 5.5+ and Sonnet 5.5+, which reject this lane's always-on `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }`), ALWAYS; a voice-eligible OpenAI id (a `voice` object on its catalog entry, e.g. gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna/gpt-5.6-luna/gpt-5.6-terra) OR one of those thinking-always-on Anthropic ids ADDITIONALLY, but only for a sandbox session or an eval-harness session (`evalHarness`, set by `voice-relay-replay.js` alone — the shared `VOICE_RELAY_MODEL` is Anthropic-only under every gate); the OpenAI id also requires `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_OPENAI` exactly `'true'` (read at call time via `feature-gates.js`'s `voiceRelayOpenaiLive()`), while a thinking-always-on Anthropic id needs no gate — a session pinned to one sends its catalog `voice.thinking` floor when that is `between_tools` (Sonnet 5.5), otherwise omits `thinking` and sizes `max_tokens` off the same floor `anthropic-wire.js` uses elsewhere. An ordinary production inbound call takes a voice-eligible OpenAI `VOICE_RELAY_INBOUND_MODEL` only under the SEPARATE `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_OPENAI_INBOUND` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at session construction via `voiceRelayOpenaiInboundLive()`; `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_OPENAI` never opens production inbound (owner ruling 2026-09-28: GPT-6 Luna). A rejected value, or any ineligible id, falls back down the chain with one logged warning and a `model_fallback_reason` stamp in `_versionStamps()`, never a silent substitution. A session pinned to an OpenAI model runs through `server/services/voice-agent/relay-openai-client.js` (Responses API, SSE) instead of the Anthropic SDK — same tool-use loop and stream/finalMessage surface, its own request/response translation. An OpenAI round that fails for a provider reason (request error, non-2xx, stream error, the 20 s stream timeout — never a caller barge-in) switches the rest of that call, once, to the model the shared Anthropic chain resolves (`VOICE_RELAY_MODEL` → `MODEL_VOICE` → default), and retries that round on Claude only when none of it has reached the caller yet; otherwise the round fails as before and the next turn runs on Claude. The switch is stamped `model_switch` in `_versionStamps()` and `modelSwitched` on the turn. Eval-harness sessions never switch, so the benchmark measures the model alone. See `docs/sandy-benchmark.md`'s "OpenAI candidates" section for the benchmark runner's own gate handling. `VOICE_RELAY_PROFILE` — the id of a code-reviewed `RELAY_PROFILES` entry (`server/services/voice-agent/relay-profiles.js`, the only place `<ConversationRelay>` STT / turn-taking attributes are chosen); unset = the untuned relay, byte-identical TwiML; an unknown or sandbox-only id falls back to unset with one warning. `VOICE_RELAY_SANDBOX_NUMBER` — E.164 of the test number; enables `POST /api/webhooks/twilio/relay-sandbox`, the ONLY Sandy test path. **Enforced: a number `config/twilio-numbers.js` registers as a live line is refused** (403 on every call, one error log) — only an unregistered number or one parked under `unassigned` is eligible (the former GA# is still registered as Google Ads — Pest; park it first): every sandbox call gets a `call_log` row with `source='voice_relay_sandbox'` that the calls tab, unified inbox, and audits exclude, and a two-digit DTMF cell code inside the first 3 s selects a profile (`SANDBOX_CELLS`). `VOICE_RELAY_SANDBOX_ATTRS` — raw attribute JSON for sandbox cell `99` only. Per-call latency and version stamps land in `call_log.transcription_metadata.latency` / `.versions`; per-turn timings (no text; model ms, each tool's name + ms, a wall-clock prompt stamp) in `.turn_stats`. `node server/scripts/voice-relay-turn-timing.js --call=CA… | --sandbox --since=7d` (read-only) joins them with Twilio Voice Insights' per-turn ConversationRelay timeline (`relay-insights.js`; needs Voice Insights Advanced Features, on for this account) and splits caller-stops → Sandy-heard into STT / app / TTS, plain vs tool turns (model and tool ms are whole-turn totals, not slices of the gap). `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_INTERRUPT_CONTEXT` — **ships DARK: off unless set to `true`**, read at call time (a flip needs no redeploy): on, a barge-in rewrites the cut reply in the model's history to the played-text record (`… [interrupted]`) and prefixes the next caller message with what the caller heard, so Sandy resumes instead of repeating the unheard clause; off, a barge-in only aborts the generation and the model's messages are byte-identical to today. Transcript and stored record are unaffected either way. `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_RECOVERY` — **ships DARK: off unless set to `true`**, read at call time: on, a relay socket that fails mid-call is reconnected ONCE (`/relay-complete` re-renders the relay with a resumed greeting; the new socket takes the claim), every socket's turns land as a segment in `call_log.metadata.relay_segments` and the owning close composes the whole transcript, a second failure hands the caller to the office (transfer gate on, office open) or voicemail, and a second consecutive model / tool failure hands off instead of re-prompting; off, `/relay-complete` and the close-time writes are byte-identical to today. `GATE_VOICE_RELAY_TRANSFER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time: on, and only while the office is open at the session's first turn, Sandy gets `transfer_to_office` — the caller is handed to the existing staff simul-ring (press-1 screen, then a ≤20-word whisper read from the row) with a server-built packet on `call_log.metadata.relay_handoff` and `call_outcome='ai_transferred'`; after hours the tool is absent and she offers a callback through `capture_lead`. A packet write failure still transfers and rings the `sandy_transfer_no_context` bell. Off ⇒ no tool, prompt and `/relay-complete` byte-identical to today. Sandbox transfers hang up instead of ringing staff. `VOICE_RELAY_RENDERER=block|stream` (PR C) — resolved once per session and pinned on `this.renderer`, same allowlist/pin/warn-once shape as the model override above; `VOICE_RELAY_SANDBOX_RENDERER` outranks it for sandbox sessions only; an unrecognized value falls back to `block` with one logged warning. `block` (default, unset) is byte-identical to this lane's original one-utterance-per-frame behavior. `stream` sends a sentence progressively ONLY when it is ALLOWLISTED-safe (`isStreamSafe`: an ack + at most one read-only clause like "let me check on that", or a question — a commitment BLOCKLIST never converges, so an ordinary statement now holds by default too) AND not vetoed by `needsHold` (a dollar amount, any digit or a date/time expression, a negation, a commitment-or-success claim, or a future/modal write commitment like "I'll book that"/a bare "-ing" write verb — read-only verbs like check/look/pull up never hold) until `finalMessage()` is known and the existing write-tool suppression check has cleared it (never spoken or stored ahead of a pending write); a sentence boundary is abbreviation-aware (Mr/Dr/St/a.m/U.S/etc/a single-letter initial never end it early); the round loop also stops flushing the instant any `tool_use` content block starts streaming, and EVERY progressive flush — not just the round's first — revalidates session ownership via the same late-supersession recheck the block renderer runs immediately before speaking, serialized in order through a chain that never stays rejected on a throw (a step that fails logs it and withholds the rest of the round instead of skipping later sentences or leaking an unhandled rejection); found superseded ⇒ the rest of the round speaks nothing and ends through the existing superseded path; a barge-in landing mid-finalize, or a genuine mid-stream failure, closes the round with only the actually-sent prefix in history (never the model's full generated text), tool_use paired with a synthetic result rather than left unpaired. See `server/services/voice-agent/relay-stream-renderer.js` and `docs/conversationrelay-booking-plan.md` for the chunking policy and interruption handling.

Job card (dark): `GATE_JOB_CARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = kill). On, the Service Protocol drawer gets a first "Job card" tab (`GET /admin/protocols/job-card/:serviceId`, `services/job-card.js`): customer strip with plain `tel:`/`sms:` links, a 1–3 sentence paragraph that is the deterministic template of portal facts, built on each read (the model rewrite and its `scheduled_services.job_card` cache were removed 2026-10-03: the grounding validator rejected every attempt; raw access codes never enter the paragraph — they ride only in `strip.access.codes`, tap-to-reveal), a per-product spray check from NWS hourly at the property, the 110 / 1 gal tank mix helper, and product cards whose Order more posts the existing tech-allowed restock request. With the separate dark `GATE_JOB_CARD_CUSTOMER_CONTEXT` (exact `true`, read at call time) the card also carries `notes.customerRequest` — why the customer booked this visit (`scheduled_services.customer_request*`), shown as a "Why they booked" box — plus `notes.customerTexts` (the customer's inbound texts from the 14 days up to the visit's day, newest three; `null` = unreadable) and, with `GATE_VISIT_PREP_PHOTOS` live too, `notes.prepPhotos` (the Visit Brief's customer photos, thumbnails via `GET /admin/schedule/:id/visit-prep-photos`); display only, never the paragraph or a model call. Off → the endpoint answers `{enabled:false}` and the tab hides. No comms either way.

Label weather review: `GATE_LABEL_PIPELINE` — opt-in, read at call time. Inventory product details can fetch the exact EPA PDF and stage weather facts for admin source review. Approved weather evidence feeds the Job Card without changing the general label/rate verification stamp. When the EPA check fails, the Job Card and the rate check use the last check that got an answer for the same label file and checksum, up to 7 days old (owner 2026-10-30; `epa-label-check-keep.js`, kept in `system_settings` under `epa_label_check:*`, ordered by the time EPA answered); EPA's record of a cancelled registration or removed label is an answer (`inactive`), not an outage; approval always checks fresh, and its answer is kept too. Unset restores the legacy spray check; per-product revoke withdraws a review. Scope and boundaries: `docs/product-label-weather-review.md`.

Spray rain rules: `GATE_SPRAY_RAIN_RULES` — `shadow` or `true`, read at call time (`sprayRainRulesMode()`); anything else is off. Owner 2026-10-26 (plan page "Visit-Day Rain Rule", D1 = A, D2 = A). On, the visit-day spray check (`job-card.js` `buildSprayCheck`) judges each product's label rain rule from `server/config/label-rain-rules.js` (hand-read EPA labels with file and page): "Do not make applications during rain" on the start hour (the current hour once the window opened), a label's dry-before-rain advice (a caution above 60%, the Warning level above 80%), and no rain check for water-in products. A tank spray whose label has no rain rule gets the Waves rule of its service (`reschedule-rules.js` `serviceSensitivity`, via the weather rebooker's `classifyServiceType`): the strictest among the services whose lines name it on the visit, so an add-on's product takes its add-on's rule (Tree & Shrub 3 h on a pest visit), on the card and in the tank search. Every rain number, catalog `rainfast_minutes` / `rain_free_hours` included, uses one odds table: caution above `caution_if_rain_prob_above` (60%). Owner 2026-10-29 ("i just want to warn techs"): no weather reading withholds a dose. A reading past `reschedule_if_rain_prob_above` (80%), or past a wind or temperature limit, is a caution that names it (it still outranks a missing hour); the job card, the tank search and the Tree & Shrub field guide keep the amount. Step 2 (plan page "Spray Weather Warnings"): rain past 80% is the Warning level (`level: 'warning'` on a caution; a dark chip on the card, still no red); wind and temperature are judged at the start hour and the next one and name the reading and its hour; a tank spray whose label gives no dry time (not listed, or listed with the during-rain line only; not a dust, a tablet or an adjuvant) gets the Waves hours as its dry time; a label `heat` line (Celsius WG: "DO NOT use a spray adjuvant at temperatures above 90 degrees", current Envu label p5) is a caution above 90°F that replaces the catalog 95°F; every caution carries one `action` (the label's words, else spray it first, or at the Warning level skip it and note why, or plan a re-treat), shown under the reason on the card and in the tank search.
