Owner 2026-10-30 (A, A, A): a label `wind` line is a caution at each label's own number, at the start hour and the next one (Artavia, Heritage WDG, Headway, Onslaught, Tekko Pro, Permethrin SFR and Scion at 15 mph; Bifen XTS, Sedgehammer 75% and Blindside at 10 mph; Cyper TC's 10 mph on-grade line on termite visits only), and Florida's fertilizer line "Do not apply if heavy rain is expected" (Dimension 18-0-10, High Manganese Combo, Green Flo Phyte Plus; the two with no EPA number match by catalog name) is a caution when the start hour's NWS words say heavy rain or thunderstorms, above 60% (the Warning level above 80%); Green Flo's "not on foliage above 90°F" is a heat caution. The field guide also shows its mix when the only gap is a missing forecast (`forecastGap`); an open label review (`reviewedWeather` unresolved) still withholds it. Unverified catalog weather values are skipped, not "unknown". Dispatch chips name the caution and the product ("Rain likely 2 pm · Talak", "Rain warning · Celsius WG", "Wind caution · Celsius WG"), a Warning first, ahead of "Weather unknown" (a missing forecast), and are never red. `shadow` keeps today's check live and upserts the rain-rule verdict of each visit-day card or readiness build into `spray_rain_rule_shadow` (worst read per visit per day, with that read's start time and service); `true` keeps upserting the same row, which then counts the real rain odds behind each caution. Off is byte-identical to today. Kill switch: unset.

Call commitments (dark): `GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS` — every processed call records what Waves promised and what the caller agreed to as evidence-linked `call_commitments` rows (seeded from the V2 extraction plus one bounded FLAGSHIP model pass over the transcript), links each promise to the later record that fulfils it, and surfaces it all in the Calls tab "Call intelligence" panel. Off (default) → nothing is written; rows already recorded stay visible. The model leg reads `CALL_PROC_EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_MS` but is NOT counted in the claim ceiling (`server/utils/claim-ceiling.js`): it runs after finalization has cleared the claim, so it cannot extend a held one. See `docs/call-intelligence-audit-and-expansion.md`.

Call last-name suggestion (dark): `GATE_CALL_LAST_NAME_LOOKUP` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`callLastNameLookupLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, after a phone call finalizes, a background job looks for the last name of a caller who gave a first name and no last name, when the caller is that customer (call contact phone = `customers.phone` on the phone identity key), the customer is live with a blank `last_name`, and the valid V2 extraction has no caller last name. It NEVER writes `customers.last_name` (owner 2026-10-08, after a real-data test: the county rule disagreed with the name on file about 4 times in 100 answers). It posts ONE admin notification (category `customer`, `bell: true`, link `/admin/customers?customerId=<id>`, dedupe key `call-last-name-suggestion:<customerId>`) and the office saves the name. All four sources run and every answer is collected: (1) the county parcel owner record, ONLY when the V2 `caller.relationship_to_property` is `owner` or `unknown` — the customer's coordinates give the parcel, the parcel's house number must equal the customer's, and the caller's first name must match one owner's first name (Manatee, Sarasota, Charlotte formats; an entity owner or a stacked condo association gives nothing); (2) another live customer or lead with the same email or phone, the same first name and a last name; (3) the caller's email as `first.last@`, `first_last@` or `first-last@` (never a run-together address); (4) the Twilio Lookup v2 `caller_name` for a US number (about 1 cent a lookup; skipped for no name, `UNKNOWN`, a BUSINESS type, a name of 15 characters or more, no or several first-name tokens, or other than one leftover token). A realtor, tenant, buyer, family member or any other non-owner never gets the county owner's name. Answers are grouped by surname: agreeing sources are one suggestion; different surnames are all listed in the full text and none is picked. The last name is checked blank again just before posting. The notification closes itself through the relevance sweep (`admin-alert-relevance.js` class `call_last_name_suggestion`) once the customer has a non-blank last name or is gone (deleted or soft-deleted), and the sweep puts it back if the name is blanked again within 14 days. Owner names are never logged or cached; logs carry ids and outcome codes only (the notification text may name the customer, a staff-only surface). See `server/services/call-last-name-lookup.js`.

Bait station visits on the Fast Complete sheet (dark): `GATE_STATION_FAST_COMPLETE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`stationFastCompleteLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_REPORT` and `GATE_TYPED_VOICE_FILL`. Owner 2026-10-08. Today a termite or rodent bait station visit opens the one-screen sheet in admin Dispatch only while the station map (`station-map-v1`) is known OFF, because with the map on the full form records a check for every station. On, the schedule row carries `stationFastCompleteEnabled` (true only for a `termite_bait_station` or `rodent_bait_station` form with no companion form) and admin Dispatch also opens the sheet for such a visit while the map is known ON. The sheet (`FastCompleteStations.jsx`) loads the station registry from `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/property-map`, shows "N stations, all OK", and the note names exceptions by station number ("station 4 had activity, I replaced the bait in 7"). `POST /admin/dispatch/:id/typed-facts` reads them when the request carries the sheet's `stations` (`services/visit-station-facts.js`, lane `visit_typed_facts`): the server loads the registry itself, and a station number must be an ACTIVE station of the visit's program that the sheet showed, the status one of activity / serviced / inaccessible, and the quoted words in the note and stating that number, else the exception is dropped (the tech can still tap the station). Each exception is a chip the tech taps to correct (ok / activity / serviced / no access; rodent reads "Consumption"). The completion posts `termiteStations: [{ id, status, touched? }]` exactly as the full form does (an entry per pinned station, `touched` on exceptions) and the typed station counts from the one shared rule (`client/src/lib/station-checks.js`, also used by the full form). The sheet hands the visit to the full form (a hold that says so) for a registry that failed to load, no station on record, or a station with no pin (drift-hidden); adding, moving and retiring stations, a companion form, an inspection-only outcome and `rodent_trapping` (its setup and serviced rules differ; not in this scope) stay on the full form. "All stations OK" is asserted (to the report writer as `stationChecks`, and to the record as `termiteStations`) only when the note's station read is KNOWN to have succeeded for the current note text, or the tech marked the stations by hand and tapped "Stations checked by hand". The typed-facts answer carries `stationRead: 'read' | 'failed'` (a model failure, timeout, registry error, throw or too-long note is `failed`, with no exceptions; an answer with no verdict also counts as failed); a failed or unread note holds the report and Complete with a plain message and Try again. Verification fails closed: if the model returned any exception that did not verify (an unknown or ambiguous number, a quote that does not state the number, a status outside the allowed set, two statuses for one station, a malformed entry or answer) the read is `stationRead: 'failed'` with detail `unresolved`, the exceptions that did verify ride along to be pre-marked, and the sheet holds with "Couldn't match everything you said about the stations. Mark them by hand and confirm." A quote that lists stations ("2,3", "2, 3 and 5", "2/3", "2-4", "two, three") states each of them (`numbersStatedIn` in the shared number evaluator). The model also reports what it could not place: besides the numbered exceptions its answer carries `unresolved: [{ quote }]`, the note's own words for any remark about a station's condition, access, activity or service it could not tie to a station number and one status ("I couldn't check the back corner station"); the prompt forbids dropping such a remark. Code guesses nothing: an `unresolved` quote counts only when it is in the note word for word, any that does makes the read `failed` / `unresolved` (the verified numbered exceptions still pre-marked), and an answer without the `unresolved` key is a failed read, never an empty one. The server answers `stationRead: 'failed'` with detail `roster_changed` (no read) when the sheet's roster is not the registry's active stations of the program (a station retired or added since the sheet loaded); the sheet then loads the registry again. The completion is bound to the roster too: the sheet sends `stationRosterSeen` (the ids it checked; the full form never sends it) and `/complete` compares it, with the same roster rule as the typed-facts route (`stationRosterMatches`), under the visit row lock; a station retired or added since is refused with 409 `station_roster_changed` and nothing is written, and the sheet loads the stations again and reads the note again. The submitted `termiteStations` must be exactly that roster too (one check per station, none missing, extra or twice), else 400 `termite_stations_invalid` with nothing written. That check is serialized with station edits: the completion takes the station roster advisory lock (`lockStationRoster` in `termite-stations.js`, transaction-level, key `termite_stations:<customerId>:<program>`, always the last lock taken) before it reads the registry and holds it to commit; every office or sync write that creates, moves or retires a station takes the same lock. The sheet's check rows are written inside the completion transaction under that lock (the full form's sync stays post-commit). If that write fails or does not cover every station the completion aborts with a retryable 503 `station_checks_write_failed` and nothing is saved. The tech's station statuses reach the report writer as authoritative inputs under the prompt section each belongs to: a serviced station under `[COMPLETED WORK]`, bait consumption or activity, an unreachable station and the stations found OK under `[OBSERVED BY TECHNICIAN]`. A bait station visit's sheet always offers the Full form in its header (adding, moving or retiring a station and the inspection-only outcome are the full form's alone). The technician home page is unchanged. Off = the row flag is false, the route reads no stations, and station visits route exactly as before (the map-off sheet and the full form).

Pin check after a visit (dark): `GATE_PIN_PARKED_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`pinParkedCheckLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner "build guardrail" 2026-10-09 (a pin audit found customers whose map pin was 500 to 710 m from where the truck parked, so the GPS arrival detector, which needs the truck inside `gps_arrival.radius_meters`, never fired). On, a daily job (06:35 ET, `server/services/pin-parked-check.js`, job name `pin-parked-check`) reads the visits COMPLETED in the last 3 ET days (telemetry can arrive up to 12 hours late, so each visit is judged again on the next two days; the decision is idempotent) whose technician has a Bouncie vehicle (`technicians.bouncie_imei`) and compares the customer's saved pin (the visit's own `lat`/`lng`, else the customer's stored coordinates; the geocoder is never called) with the vehicle's stops that day. A stop is the gap between two trips of one vehicle (last GPS point of one trip to first point of the next, 5+ minutes, built from the `trip-data` events in `bouncie_webhook_log`, read for ONE vehicle and ONE received_at window; `mileage_log` has end coordinates but no times). It raises a suggestion only when no stop was within the arrival radius, the closest stop was farther than the radius and at most 1500 m away and lasted 10+ minutes, the customer's review is not `verified` (pin unchanged) or `outside_area`, the stop is not the vehicle's home base (its usual first start of the day in `mileage_log`), not inside an active business, personal or supplier `geo_fences` row, and not within the radius of another customer's visit the same technician completed that day, the stop is inside the service-area box, and staff have not dismissed a suggestion for the same pin. Each visit is judged on the truck's stops for EVERY ET day it used (scheduled, en route, arrived, completed), read in one paged pass per vehicle over their union; a visit with a day more than 7 days back, or a vehicle whose log cannot be read, is skipped (no suggestion, nothing closed from it). The decision is made once per CUSTOMER from all of their visits in the window (every technician's truck): a stop within the radius of the pin on ANY of them means the pin works (any open suggestion is closed and none is created); only when none has one is the suggestion made, from the newest qualifying visit. A truck whose log cannot be read makes no new suggestion for its customer that day. The bell is posted, and every close (apply, dismiss, supersede) is made, under the same per-customer advisory lock, so a settled pin never keeps a live bell. It stores ONE open row per customer in `customer_pin_suggestions` (partial unique index; a re-run never duplicates; closed rows stay as history: `applied`, `dismissed`, `superseded`) and posts ONE admin notification (`Customers — check the map pin for <name>`, keyed on the suggestion id). A verified or changed pin, a deleted customer, or a later visit with a stop inside the radius closes the open row as `superseded` and its notification with it. `GET /api/admin/customer-geocodes/:customerId` adds `pin_suggestion` and the address review panel shows it with "Use the truck's spot" (fills the existing `verify_pin` form with source `site_visit` and evidence text; staff still tick the confirmation) and "Dismiss" (`POST /api/admin/customer-geocodes/:customerId/pin-suggestions/:suggestionId/dismiss`). Applying goes through the existing `verify_pin` action only (the resolve body may carry `pin_suggestion_id`; after the pin is saved the suggestion is marked `applied`). It NEVER changes a pin by itself and sends nothing to a customer. Needs `GATE_GEOCODE_REVIEW` on too (verify_pin is the only way to apply a suggestion). Off = the endpoint adds no field, the dismiss route answers 404 and the panel shows nothing new. Rollback is clean: the daily run still ticks and, seeing the gate (or address review) off, reads nothing but the open suggestions and retires up to 500 of them (superseded, their bells closed; any rest goes at the next run); an ordinary `verify_pin` still closes the customer's open suggestion and its bell with the gate off. A customer merge retires the loser's open suggestion (superseded, bell closed) instead of moving it, and `customer_pin_suggestions` has a collision handler in `UNIQUE_COLLISION_HANDLERS` as a backstop, so two open suggestions never abort a merge; the next run raises it again for the survivor if still warranted. The suggested stop and both distance limits (175 m to 1500 m) are measured from the effective saved pin (the pin the suggestion replaces); a stop near the visit's own stamp still counts as "a stop at the pin". The stored and shown date is the ET day the truck stood at the stop, not the day the visit was closed out. A visit day that starts before the technician's current tracker mapping began (`technicians.bouncie_imei_changed_at`; NULL = always mapped) is not judged. Every path (create, ring, apply, dismiss, supersede, the gate-off sweep, the merge retire) locks the customer row FOR SHARE first and the per-customer advisory lock second, the same order a merge or verify_pin's row lock implies, so none can deadlock against them. The neighbour exclusion also loads the same technician's other completed visits on every evidence day the judged visits use (never past the 7-day cap), whenever they were completed; the home base counts only trips after the day the tracker mapping changed; coordinates outside latitude -90..90 / longitude -180..180 are not pins, and a distance that cannot be measured matches nothing. Just before a suggestion is written the visit and its technician's tracker mapping are read again under the customer's locks, and a changed technician, destination, status or mapping skips it (`visit_changed`). A customer merge whose full retire of the loser's suggestion fails falls back, inside the merge, to superseding it and closing its bell directly; if that fails too the merge aborts. A skipped scheduler tick (no lock connection) is recorded as a failed run in job_health. A vehicle whose stops or home-base lookup cannot be read is unknown: no suggestion and nothing closed from it. Rollback = unset the variable; the table keeps its history.

Trip link (dark): `GATE_TRIP_LINK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`tripLinkLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner "TRIP LINK" and "BOTH" 2026-10-26: real drive minutes, drive miles and GPS minutes on site per visit for the per-technician job cost, and a business or personal SUGGESTION per Bouncie trip for the mileage records. Shadow data only. On, a nightly job (01:40 ET: yesterday, then the day before again because a Bouncie trip event can arrive up to 12 hours late, then the worked day of any visit closed out yesterday up to 7 days back; job name `trip-link`, `server/services/trip-link.js`) and the script `server/scripts/trip-link-backfill.js --from YYYY-MM-DD --to YYYY-MM-DD [--dry-run] [--force-shadow]` (at most 120 days per run; the dry run prints the summary and writes nothing; a write with the gate off is refused unless `--force-shadow`) take each technician with a Bouncie vehicle (`technicians.bouncie_imei`; a day that starts before `bouncie_imei_changed_at` is not judged and its visits read `no_vehicle`) and read that vehicle's trips and stops for the ET day from `bouncie_webhook_log` (the same trip-data read and 5 minute stop rule as the pin check, but starting 12 hours early so a trip across midnight is read whole; a trip belongs to the day it ENDS, the day of the stop it reaches, so a drive across midnight and its stop stay on one day; `server/services/bouncie-truck-stops.js`). Each COMPLETED visit worked that ET day (its arrival stamp, else its completion stamp: a visit closed out on a later day belongs to the day the truck was there; one physical visit per `visit_id` group; destination as the pin check resolves it, `server/services/visit-gps-context.js`) is matched to the stop inside the GPS arrival radius (`gps_arrival.radius_meters`, 175 m default) of its destination that overlaps the visit window, from 120 minutes before the arrival stamp (else the completion stamp) to 30 minutes after completion: the greatest overlap wins, a tie goes to the stop that began nearest the arrival stamp, and two still equal are `ambiguous`; none is `no_stop`, no pin is `no_destination`, no vehicle (or no technician on the visit) is `no_vehicle`. Visits that match the same stop split its minutes and carry `shared_stop_count`. `visit_gps_legs` (one row per completed scheduled service) stores the stop's arrival and departure, the GPS minutes on site, and the drive leg from the END of the vehicle's previous stop (the day's first trip start for the first stop) to the stop's start: minutes, miles (the sum of the `mileage_log` distances of the trips in between; NULL when any of them has no `mileage_log` row) and what the leg came from (`visit`, `supplier`, `business`, `personal`, `home`, `day_start`, `other`); grouped members of one visit share one leg. `trip_links` (one row per Bouncie trip) stores where the trip ENDED (`visit`, an active fence type, `home`, `other`) and `suggested_purpose` (visit, supplier and business fences = `business`; personal fence = `personal`; home and other = `unclassified`). A re-run replaces the day (upsert per scheduled service and per trip, one transaction per technician-day). It NEVER writes `mileage_log`, `scheduled_services`, `job_costs`, customer pins or alerts and sends nothing. Off = the job reads nothing and writes nothing (it still ticks and records its job health) and `GET /api/admin/trip-link/summary?from=&to=` (staff only; at most 120 days: counts by status, matched %, medians of GPS and stamped on-site minutes, drive minutes and drive miles, trips and miles by suggested purpose and by end kind) answers 404. Rollback = unset the variable; the two tables are derived data and the migration's `down` drops them.

Auto lunch (owner 2026-10-25): `GATE_AUTO_LUNCH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`autoLunchLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, paid hours leave out the unpaid meal in `server/services/time-tracking.js` (rule in `server/utils/unpaid-meal.js`, constants in `server/constants/staff-time.js`): for one ET work day, `recordedMeal` is the sum of the day's completed `break` entries that each last 30 minutes or more (a shorter rest break stays paid); `auto` is 30 minutes when the day's shift total is over 6 hours and the day's `no_lunch` flag is false; the day's `unpaid_meal_minutes` = min(shift total, max(recordedMeal, auto)). The weekly regular/overtime split and the per-day overtime allocation use paid minutes (shift minus unpaid meal), so a 4x10.5-hour week reads 40 regular and 0 overtime. `total_shift_minutes`, utilization and revenue per man-hour stay on shift minutes. Migration `20261025181500_auto_lunch_unpaid_meal` adds `time_entry_daily_summary.unpaid_meal_minutes` and `no_lunch` and `time_weekly_summary.unpaid_meal_minutes`. A tech taps "No lunch today" with `POST /api/tech/timetracking/no-lunch {noLunch}` (own current ET day only); an admin sets it with `PUT /api/admin/timetracking/daily/:technicianId/:workDate/no-lunch {noLunch, edit_reason}`; both refuse while the gate is off (409, nothing written), refuse an approved day or week (409), recompute the day and week under the week lock, and reset the week's tech sign-off when the flag changes. The weekly payroll export adds an "Unpaid Lunch Hours" column after "Total Hours". Off = every stored and exported number equals the pre-gate arithmetic (unpaid meal 0). Pays nobody and sends nothing to a customer. Rollback = unset.

Shift close review (census H8 + M7, owner 2026-10-25): `GATE_SHIFT_CLOSE_REVIEW` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`shiftCloseReviewLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: (1) a shift the 11 PM job (`services/time-tracking-crons.js`) or the 14-hour check (`autoClockOutCheck` in `services/time-tracking.js`) closes ends at the technician's last real activity, the later of their latest completed visit (`scheduled_services.completed_at`) and the end of their latest finished job, drive, break or admin entry in the shift; with none after clock-in it keeps the forced time. A timer still running that started after that moment is voided. (2) The shift is marked on `time_entries` (`auto_closed_at`, `auto_close_reason` `cron_11pm` or `over_14_hours`; migration `20261025231500_time_entries_auto_close_review` adds those plus `auto_close_reviewed_at` and `auto_close_reviewed_by`). (3) An admin clears it by editing the clock-out (`PUT /api/admin/timetracking/entries/:id`) or tapping Confirm clock-out on the Timesheet Approvals tab (`POST /api/admin/timetracking/entries/:id/confirm-auto-close`, changes no time, works on a locked week); the Approvals row and week detail show the flag. (4) `evaluate()` in `services/payroll-runs.js` lists a W-2 technician whose week holds an unreviewed automatic clock-out as blocked ("An automatic clock-out needs a real time"), so the run cannot be finalized; minutes are not recomputed. (5) The 9 PM reminder and 11 PM notice stop going through `TwilioService.sendSMS(technicians.phone)` with no message type: the owner gets an internal text on `ADAM_PHONE` (`internal_alert`, `allowOwnerSms`); every other technician gets a Today card (`tech_clock_out_reminder`, `tech_auto_clock_out`) plus a push and no SMS, the same routing as the 7 PM open-visit nudge. Off = `clock_out` is the forced time, no flag, no payroll hold, the same texts as today. Texts only the owner's own phone. Rollback: unset it.

Staff guards (census M12 + M6, owner 2026-10-25): `GATE_TECH_STAFF_GUARDS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`techStaffGuardsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: (1) M12, an inbound text or call FROM the phone of an ACTIVE technician (`technicians.employment_status` `active`, last 10 digits, cached 60 s by `server/services/staff-sender-phones.js`) is a staff sender. A text to an office line (`routes/twilio-webhook.js`, after the spam check) STAYS in the office inbox as today: the unified inbox row (unread), the legacy `sms_log` row, the activity row and the owner's unknown-sender text forward (one per sender per 4 hours) all run, and the thread still shows the number (no technician name). Only the customer and lead side is skipped: the solicitation screen and its shadow, the estimator draft and agent, the scheduling shadow and the tracking-line new-prospect bell. A STOP/START/HELP keyword, a text to a technician line and a Waves-owned number keep today's handling. A call (`services/call-recording-processor.js`, `firstExternalPhone`) is transcribed and logged but no customer or lead is keyed on the caller, the same as an env staff phone; the missed-call text-back (`services/missed-call-text-back.js`) skips it. A number that is ALSO on a live customer record (primary, secondary or service-contact phone) stays a customer, and one log line counts such numbers (no name, no number). The env staff list (`staffForwardLast10`), the owner phone set in `services/twilio.js`, `routes/tech-line.js` and every outbound send are unchanged: the set answers only "is this inbound sender staff". (2) M6, a technician's En Route or On Site tap (`routes/tech-track.js`) on a voice-agent or outbound-callback booking the office has not reviewed (still pending, or a voice-agent booking a move left 'confirmed' with customer_confirmed false) no longer confirms or advances it, checked again under the transition lock: the tap answers 409 `outbound_review_unconfirmed` and `services/tech-unreviewed-booking-alert.js` raises ONE Schedule needs-you notice per visit ("review <customer>'s booking before the visit", subject the visit; raised under a visit-row lock only while the booking still waits for review; a second tap rings nothing). The notice closes when the booking is confirmed (the confirm hook) and, every 10 minutes, when its visit is confirmed, cancelled, skipped, completed or gone by any path (`closeResolved`, scheduler). `runOutboundReviewConfirmHook` closes it when the office confirms. An admin login still auto-confirms. A cancelled visit does not close the notice by itself. Off = today's behavior byte for byte. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback: unset it.

Bid kit (dark, admin only): `GATE_BID_KIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidKitLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: Sarasota County Schools bid 24-0118 (May 2024) rejected 3 of 5 bids, the lowest included, for a missing business license copy, state employee ID cards, the certified operator's certificate and renewal, a notarized statement that the certified operator works full-time for the bidder, and the product list; the papers every bid asks for sit in no one place. On, (1) the admin page `/admin/bid-kit` (nav entry `Bid kit`, shown only while the gate is on through the `bid_kit` flag of `GET /api/admin/feature-flags`) holds one row per paper or fact from the catalog in `shared/bid-kit-catalog.cjs` (papers that sank bids, insurance, registration and tax, plans and company, references, facts) in the new table `bid_kit_items`: its private file, limits (whole dollars), source document, checked-on date, expiry, and the owner's sign-off; (2) status is computed, never stored, first match wins: missing, expired (expiry before today in America/New_York), needs expiry (a catalog paper that expires and has no expiry date), needs permission (a reference with no permission date), needs sign-off, expiring (complete and signed off, but expiring within 30 days), ready; the summary counts ready and expiring together as ready (both are valid on a bid today) and shows the expiring-soon count beside it; (3) any change to the value, file, limits, details, source document, checked-on date, expiry or permission date clears the sign-off in the same update, and a sign-off is refused (400, in plain words) while the item is missing, expired or needs an expiry date, and for a version that changed since the owner looked (`expected_updated_at`, answered 409; an archive (`DELETE /:id?expected_updated_at=`) is fenced the same way, 400 without a version, one atomic UPDATE); (4) a file (PDF, PNG, JPEG or DOCX, at most 15 MB, bytes checked against the type) goes to private S3 under `bid-kit/<item id>/<random>.<pdf|png|jpg|docx>` (the original name is never in the key; a file name that carries a tax ID or SSN is refused) with no public ACL, (a replacement must send the version the page loaded as `expected_updated_at`, else 409, like a save or a sign-off) and opens only through `GET /api/admin/bid-kit/:id/file`, a signed link good for 5 minutes; no route returns a stored key; (5) `GET /api/admin/bid-kit/facts-sheet` gives the fact values and the numbers and expiry dates of the papers (never a file, key or link; archived rows left out) for the facts sheet view with a copy button for each value; (6) once a day in the 6:05 AM ET compliance slot (`server/services/bid-kit-expiry.js`, inside the credential expiry cron) one admin notification per item that expired or expires within 30 days, deduped per item for 7 days (dedupe key `bid-kit:expiry:<item id>`); the bell closes when the item is renewed (its date moves out of the 30-day window, closed at once on the save) or archived, and the daily run closes every open kit bell whose item no longer qualifies. A run raises at most 3 new per-item bells (expired first, then soonest expiry); the rest are one quiet standing count on the Activity feed (docs/admin-notifications.md rule 3), closed when it reaches zero. The activity log names a custom item only as "custom item" and lists changed field names, never a label, value or detail. A FEIN, EIN or SSN is never stored: one detector (`detectTaxId` in `shared/bid-kit-catalog.cjs`) refuses the SSN shape, the EIN shape (any run of space, hyphen, en dash, dot, underscore or slash between the groups) and exactly nine contiguous digits with or without a label (a nine-digit number with no letters cannot be stored), and nine digits in any other grouping when a tax phrase (EIN, FEIN, TIN, ITIN, SSN, taxpayer, tax id, tax identification, tax number, tax no, tax #, federal id, federal tax, employer id, employer identification, social security, W9, W-9) appears anywhere in the same text, with no distance rule, in every typed field, every reference detail, every pair of fields read together as stored, and every uploaded file name (where any nine-digit run is refused); the W-9 file is the only place one lives. A document counts only with a file (a typed number alone is missing); a check or permission date cannot be after today in Eastern time. It has no link to `business_credentials` and never reads or writes it, and it does not touch the public credentials feed (the FDACS license number is a fact the owner types and signs off). No AI call, nothing public and nothing sent to an agency, customer or anyone else. Off = every `/api/admin/bid-kit` route answers 404, the nav entry is hidden and the daily job does nothing. Rollback: unset the variable; the table keeps its rows, and `down()` of `20261023120000_bid_kit_items.js` drops it.

Bid kit Product List sync (dark): `GATE_BID_KIT_PRODUCT_LIST_SYNC` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidKitProductListSyncLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); needs `GATE_BID_KIT` on too. Owner 2026-10-25: "if they are bought from siteone, they should auto sign off in the bid section". Once a day in the 6:05 AM ET compliance slot, right after the kit's expiry check (`runExclusive('bid-kit-product-list')`), `server/services/bid-kit-product-list.js` rebuilds the Bid kit `product_list` paper as a PDF (`server/services/pdf/product-list-pdf.js`) from every product in `service_products` whose visit (`service_records.service_date`, Eastern) is in the last 365 days (the visit date, not when the line was written: editing an old recap rewrites its lines with a fresh `created_at`); visits on the internal test accounts (`INTERNAL_TEST_CUSTOMERS` in `server/services/internal-test-customers.js`, matched by first and last name like the business metrics; owner 2026-10-26: "adam m is a dummy account") never count, with active ingredient, EPA Reg. No. (a real number, by `server/services/epa-reg-number.js`), Label and SDS links. A visit line with no catalog product (`product_id` null) counts as a catalog product when its name equals exactly one catalog name after `normalizeForMatch` (an active row preferred, an inactive one when it is the only match); any other such line is not printed, and its count and distinct names are in the bell's full text and the run log; its normalized names are part of the fingerprint and are stored in `details.product_list_sync.unmatched`. A name that is NOT in the previous snapshot's list (a snapshot with no such key counts as empty) blocks the automatic sign-off and raises the bell (nothing prints for it, so it is never signed off unseen); names already in it, and names that dropped out, do not block. A hash of each row (including its category) is stored on the kit row under `details.product_list_sync`; the same list = nothing happens (no file, no bell). A changed list replaces the file and clears the sign-off in the same update, except when the kit signs it off itself (`attested_by` null, `attested_at` now, activity row `bid_kit_attested` with `auto: 'siteone_purchases'`, no bell, any open bell closed): only when this job built the file now on the row, that file was signed off, the list is complete (every registered pesticide has a label and an SDS, no pesticide-category product lacks an EPA number) and every ADDED or CHANGED product has a `purchase_receipt_lines` row with `vendor = 'siteone'` and `status = 'logged'` (`best_vendor` is never used), and no product was REMOVED (a product also leaves the list when a technician takes it off a recent visit record, which says nothing about purchases, so any removal is reviewed by the owner and the bell names it). Any other change leaves the new file NOT signed off and raises ONE admin bell (`bid-kit:product-list:<item id>`, rewritten, not stacked, by a later run; it closes when the item is signed off) that names what changed. The first run (no stored snapshot) and a file replaced by hand always ask: an unchanged list is skipped only while the file on the kit is still the one the job stored, so a hand upload is rebuilt and flagged once. The bell's words are saved on the row (`details.product_list_sync.pending_alert`) in the same update as the new file and cleared after the bell is raised; a run that finds them still there raises the bell again (same key, no second ring) before anything else. It skips (no file, no bell) when the kit has no `product_list` row, when no product was applied in 12 months, or when the owner changed the row while the list was built. Never contacts a customer, an agency or anyone else. Rollback: unset the variable; the last file stays on the kit.

Purchase intake guard (dark): `GATE_PRODUCT_INTAKE_GUARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`productIntakeGuardLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-26: "fix a". Admin inventory only; nothing reaches a customer. Two parts. (1) Near-name guard: a purchase title that carries a product-line word the catalog product's own name lacks ("Dismiss NXT" vs "Dismiss", "Gentrol Complete EC3" vs "Gentrol") no longer matches by whole-word name containment (`server/services/purchase-receipts/product-matcher.js`, reviewed `VARIANT_WORDS` list; a unit word (g, gr, pt) right after a number is a size and never counts, while any other listed word right after a number still counts because a catalog name can end in a number, "PGF Complete 16-4-8"), so the line goes to the inventory agent. The agent refuses an "existing" answer when the title has such a word that the product's name, or the pre-existing alias that names it, lacks, and the line goes to the existing "Inventory agent: not added" bell with no stock moved and no "Closest guess". Alias matches are never guarded (a person confirmed them). (2) New pesticide completeness: when the agent creates a product in a pesticide category, it asks EPA's label system (PPLS, fixed EPA origins only, outside any database transaction) for the EPA registration number: first the number the listing states, accepted only if the EPA record carries a brand name equal to the product name; otherwise an exact brand-name search that must find exactly one active two-part registration whose own EPA record carries the same brand name (a distributor three-part number with the same name, or a name built from the active ingredient, fills nothing). A match fills `epa_reg_number` and `label_url`; no match, an ambiguous match or no answer leaves `epa_reg_number` blank (NULL, never "N/A") for a pesticide. `label_verified_by` and `label_verified_at` are never set, and the active ingredient stays the placeholder. The lookup evidence is saved in the line's `agent_decision`. The "Inventory agent logged a purchase" bell names what was filled and what is still missing (EPA number, label, SDS, active ingredient) and links to the new product (`/admin/inventory?tab=products&productId=<id>`). Off: name containment as before, EPA "N/A", today's bell text and link, and no EPA call. Rollback: unset the variable.

Bid Desk intake (dark): `GATE_BID_DESK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidDeskLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: in about three months the shared inbox received nine bid invites (BuildingConnected, Procore, a city RFQ, an HOA RFP, a property manager) and Waves submitted none, because the Gmail sync files each as an ordinary email or lead and nobody saw the due date. On, (1) a job every 15 minutes (`bid-desk-intake`, under `runExclusive`, `server/services/bid-desk/index.js` `runBidDeskTick`) reads new `emails` rows past a stored watermark (`system_settings` key `bid_desk.watermark`, 200 rows a tick) and files each bid email as a `bid_opportunities` row with its emails in `bid_opportunity_emails` (unique `email_id`, so a re-read changes nothing). A bid email is one from `buildingconnected.com` or `procoretech.com`; one from a bid portal (`bonfirehub.com`, `opengov.com`, `demandstar.com`, `bidnetdirect.com`, `internationaleprocurement.com`, `myflorida.com`) or a `.gov` / `.fl.us` sender whose subject has bid words; a verified VendorLink (`myvendorlink.com`) "SOLICITATION NOTIFICATION" whose agency address has a ZIP starting 335 to 339, 341 or 342 (the SAM.gov reader's area; VendorLink sends notices from any agency in the country, and its "Vendor Commodity Code Changed" catch-up lists never count); a verified Blue Book Network ONETEAM invite, reminder or addendum (`thebluebook.com`, body line "You've been invited to bid on" or "Bid is due by"; source `bluebook`; the network's own "Project Notification" never counts); an OpenGov (`opengov.com`) "has invited you to" or "has just released" notice whose title names our trade (pest, termite, mosquito, rodent, lawn, turf, weed, fertilization, landscape, grounds, mowing, vegetation, tree, shrub and the like; OpenGov sends both kinds by registered category, so another trade's title does not count, reason `outside_trade`, unless the subject has bid words, which file it as before). Gmail files every Blue Book invite as spam, so a Blue Book email whose DKIM/SPF aligns with its own domain is read past Gmail's SPAM label (never past our own `spam` classification); every other sender in Gmail Spam is still skipped; or any sender whose subject matches RFP / RFQ / ITB / IFB / ITN, invitation to bid, bid invite, request for proposal / quote / qualifications, addendum or pre-bid. Our own mail from `contact@wavespestcontrol.com`, subjects starting `FIX:` / `ACT:` / `FYI:` / `OK:` and GitHub notifications never count. (2) Fields (GC, project, location, job walk, lead, bid due date) are read ONLY from the fixed BuildingConnected, Procore, VendorLink, Blue Book, OpenGov and Charlotte County Purchasing templates (OpenGov and Charlotte County mail is read as a template only when it passes the STRICT sender check: a resinfo DKIM/SPF pass or Google's own `dmarc=pass` for the From domain, never the loose whole-string match; OpenGov: agency and title; Charlotte County: division, bid or quote number, title and address, so each addendum, which Charlotte County sends in its own thread, groups with its bid; VendorLink: agency, bid number and title, agency address, purchasing agent email, and the opening due date/time; Blue Book: contractor, project and place, trade, and the due time moved from the zone the email names to ET), in America/New_York; every other email leaves them null. A date read this way is `due_confirmed = false` and keeps the exact line it came from (`due_source_line`). A date with no time is stored at 23:59 ET. No AI call anywhere. (3) Emails group by `gmail_thread_id`, else by sender org + normalised project title (a new solicitation joins only an open bid; an addendum or a reminder with no open bid to join, the project's single open package bid included, joins the newest bid with its key even after it was decided, and rings nothing there). A later addendum or a differing date attaches to the bid, sets `needs_date_confirmation`, and NEVER overwrites a due date (it may fill an empty one, still unconfirmed). (4) Admin notifications through `raiseAdminAlert` (category `lead`, Estimates area, each keyed so it rings once): one per new non-historical bid, one per addendum on an open bid, and reminders 7 and 2 days before a due date the operator CONFIRMED on a `new` or `bid` bid (recorded in `reminder_7d_sent_at` / `reminder_2d_sent_at`; a bid first seen inside 2 days gets only the 2-day one). An unconfirmed date never reminds. Nothing is ever sent to a buyer, a contractor or a customer. (5) `/api/admin/bid-desk` (admin only): list, detail, `PATCH` (typed due date in ET = confirmed, confirm the date as read, status new / bid / no_bid / submitted / won / lost, note) and `POST /from-email` (mark an email as a bid by hand, source `manual`, no bell). The page is `/admin/bid-desk`; its Sales nav entry shows only while `GET /api/admin/feature-flags` carries `bid_desk` (added only while this gate is on). One-time backfill: `node server/scripts/backfill-bid-desk.js` (dry run) then `--execute` files the last 180 days as `historical = true` rows that are listed but never notified or reminded; it needs `GATE_BID_DESK=true` in the shell it runs in, so run it right after the gate is on; it is safe to repeat. Off = the job and reminders return before any query, every `/api/admin/bid-desk` path answers 404, the feature-flags response is unchanged and the nav entry is hidden; the two tables stay empty. Kill = unset the variable; rows already filed stay. Leads, the email classifier and `email-sync.js` are untouched.

Bid Desk SAM.gov reader (dark): `GATE_BID_DESK_SAM` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidDeskSamLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_BID_DESK=true` and `SAM_GOV_API_KEY` (the public API key from the SAM.gov account's Account Details page; it expires every 90 days, and a missing key makes the job skip). Why: federal pest control and grounds bids (VA Bay Pines, Sarasota National Cemetery, MacDill) post on SAM.gov, the only bid source with an official API; the website itself forbids scraping, and county and city portals (DemandStar, OpenGov, Bonfire) have no vendor API and reach the Bid Desk only as alert emails. On, a job at 7:25 AM ET (`bid-desk-sam`, under `runExclusive`, `server/services/bid-desk/sam-gov.js` `runSamGovPoll`) calls `https://api.sam.gov/opportunities/v2/search` once for each NAICS code (561710 pest control, 561730 landscaping) with `state=FL`, for notices posted since a stored cursor (`system_settings` key `bid_desk.sam_cursor`; first run 30 days back; the cursor moves only after every call succeeds and steps back one day), then re-reads open SAM.gov bids by notice id, closed ones included so an unarchive is seen (`noticeid` over the API's whole one-year range; in notice-id order, rotating through all of them via `refresh_after` in the same cursor). Every run stays inside a call budget, `SAM_GOV_DAILY_CALLS` (default 10, the daily quota of a personal key with no role; raise it for a role-backed key): discovery is spent first (a discovery that would pass the budget fails the run before the cursor moves) and the re-read gets what is left, at most 25; a refused or failed re-read (HTTP 429, outage) stops for that run without losing the discovery results and records a failed `bid-desk-sam` run in job health; after a 429 the next run retries the same bid, after any other failure it resumes past it, so one bad notice cannot hold back the rest, so an archive or change to an older notice is seen even when it was not reposted. An open bid whose by-id read returns nothing (the notice was deleted, or was posted over a year ago and the API can no longer search it) is flagged once ("SAM.gov no longer returns this notice", bell `bid-desk:addendum:<id>:sam:unreachable`) and leaves the refresh. A notice is filed as a `bid_opportunities` row with `source = 'sam_gov'`, `external_id` = its notice id (unique with the source, so a re-read changes nothing) and `external_url` = its sam.gov page, when it is a solicitation, combined synopsis, presolicitation or sources sought, is active, its response deadline is in the future (or absent; an offset-bearing value is read as given, a wall time with no zone in Eastern time, a date alone as 11:59 PM Eastern), and its place of performance ZIP starts 335, 336, 337, 338, 339, 341 or 342 (Tampa Bay to Southwest Florida). The deadline is the API's `responseDeadLine`, stored unconfirmed with the raw value as `due_source_line`, so reminders still need the operator to confirm it. A republished notice (same id, SAM.gov serves only its latest version) refreshes the title, agency, solicitation number, location and link; a deadline different from the one SAM.gov last showed (`source_due_at`, migration `20261023020000_bid_desk_source_due_at`; a date the operator typed is never re-flagged) replaces an unconfirmed date, never a confirmed one (a removed deadline clears an unconfirmed date), and always sets `needs_date_confirmation` (pausing reminders); a deadline the notice no longer lists, or a notice that closes on SAM.gov (inactive, or no longer a solicitation-type notice such as an award; `source_active`, migration `20261023030000_bid_desk_source_active`) flags its bid the same way, once, and a notice active again flags it once more (`...:sam:reopened`). A notice closed on SAM.gov never reminds, even after the operator confirms its date (`reminderDue` and the reminder query skip `source_active = false`). The type, area, active and deadline rules decide only whether a notice creates a NEW bid: a notice already filed is refreshed whatever they say now. Both gates on with no `SAM_GOV_API_KEY` records a failed `bid-desk-sam` run in job health. Bells are owed on the bid (`owed_alert_kind` 'new' | 'addendum', `owed_alert_key`; migration `20261023010000_bid_desk_bid_owed_alerts`) and delivered by the Bid Desk's shared owed-bell sweep (`deliverOwedAlerts`, every 15 minutes and at the end of each SAM.gov run): one per new bid (`bid-desk:new:<id>`, same copy as an email bid) and one per changed deadline (`bid-desk:addendum:<id>:sam:<deadline>`, closed when the operator confirms the date); every bell on a notice closed on SAM.gov (`...:sam:inactive`, `...:sam:unreachable`, or a deadline move while closed) asks for a decision instead and stays open, owed or delivered, until the bid is decided; a decided bid never rings. A stored cursor older than a year is clamped to the API's one-year window. The Bid Desk page shows the source as SAM.gov with a link to the notice. No AI call; nothing is sent to an agency, contractor or customer; the API key is never logged (errors name the HTTP status only). Off = the job returns before any request. Kill = unset the variable; rows already filed stay. Migration `20261022190000_bid_desk_sam_gov` adds the source value and the two columns.

Bid Desk checklist (dark): `GATE_BID_CHECKLIST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidChecklistLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; it also needs `GATE_BID_DESK=true`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: a bid is lost on the details, not the date: a missed question deadline, a mandatory job walk, one unsigned addendum, one missing paper. On, each bid on the Bid Desk also carries (1) its solicitation type (quote, ITB, RFQ, RFP, ITN, federal, GC subcontract, other) and whether it is scored or pass/fail, (2) a questions-due date and a job-walk date with a mandatory flag, (3) a link to its estimate and proposal (`estimate_id`; the page opens `/admin/estimates/:id/proposal`), (4) its documents: the attachments of every email linked to the bid, listed by reference and downloaded through the existing email-attachment route (no file is copied), (5) a per-bid checklist (`bid_checklist_items`) started from `shared/bid-checklist-templates.cjs` (the type's stop checks (go / no-go), then ten base rows, then rows for the quote (also used for RFQ), ITB, RFP (also used for ITN), GC subcontract or federal type; the operator can add lines with the quote or page from the solicitation, edit, reorder, tick and archive them; `POST /api/admin/bid-desk/:id/checklist/start` is idempotent and `?add=missing` adds only lines the bid lacks), and (6) a submission record (`submitted_at`, `submission_confirmation`). The list shows a progress chip such as 7/12. New reminders, admin bell only through `raiseAdminAlert`: 14 days before a CONFIRMED due date (before the existing 7 and 2), 2 days before `questions_due_at`, and 2 days before `job_walk_at` (named "mandatory" when `job_walk_mandatory`; it needs `job_walk_confirmed`: a date the operator typed is confirmed, a date read from an invite is not until the operator presses "Confirm site visit date", `jobWalkConfirmed: true`). Each fires once for the date it was computed for; the date is in the dedupe key and a changed date clears its sent stamp (`reminder_14d_sent_at`, `questions_reminder_sent_at`, `job_walk_reminder_sent_at`). The same invariants as the due-date reminders hold: nothing for a historical bid, a status other than new or bid, a notice closed on SAM.gov, or a bid flagged `needs_date_confirmation`; an unconfirmed due date never reminds. Nothing is ever sent to a buyer, general contractor or agency. Off: `PATCH /api/admin/bid-desk/:id` refuses `solicitationType`, `scored`, `questionsDueAt`, `jobWalkAt`, `jobWalkMandatory`, `jobWalkConfirmed`, `estimateId`, `submittedAt` and `submissionConfirmation` (400), the checklist and estimate-search routes answer 404, the list and detail replies carry no new keys, the page hides the new sections and chip, and only the 7-day and 2-day due-date reminders fire. Migration `20261023130000_bid_desk_checklist.js` adds the columns and the table (its `down()` drops only what the operator typed there). Doc: `docs/bid-desk-checklist.md`.

Bid Desk dates and auto-close (dark): `GATE_BID_DESK_AUTO_DATES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidDeskAutoDatesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; it also needs `GATE_BID_DESK=true`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: on 10-29 the Bid Desk held 22 bids, no date had ever been confirmed, no reminder had ever been sent, and nothing closed a bid whose due date had passed. On, two things change. (1) A bid filed for the first time from a provider email template that carries a due date (BuildingConnected, Procore, OpenGov and the other fixed templates), or from a SAM.gov notice that carries a response deadline, is inserted with `due_confirmed` true, so the 7-day and 2-day reminders (and the 14-day one with `GATE_BID_CHECKLIST`) start by themselves. A bid whose first email is an addendum, a date that arrives on a later email, an addendum, or a SAM.gov deadline move still flags the bid for the operator exactly as before; a confirmed date is never overwritten. The backfill (history) never auto-confirms. (2) Every Bid Desk tick (15 minutes) closes a bid that is still `new`, has a due date, has no submission, and whose due date is more than 1 day past (30 days past if it is flagged `needs_date_confirmation`): status `no_bid`, `decision_note` "Closed by itself: the due date (<date>) passed with no decision.", and its open bells close the same way an operator decision closes them (`closeDoneAlerts` in `server/services/bid-desk/close-alerts.js`). A bid with no date, or marked `bid`, never closes. A bid the operator sets back to `new` keeps that note and never closes itself again. Admin portal only: it sends nothing to a buyer, contractor, agency or customer, rings no new bell and needs no migration. Off = every bid is filed with an unconfirmed date and nothing closes itself, exactly as before.

Bid Desk Charlotte County due dates (dark): `GATE_BID_DESK_CHARLOTTE_DATES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidDeskCharlotteDatesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; it also needs `GATE_BID_DESK=true`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: Charlotte County Purchasing's emailed notices ("Addendum Notification for Bid 26-674") carry no due date, so those bids were filed with none and never reminded or closed. On, a job (`bid-desk-charlotte`, hourly at :40 from 7:40 AM to 6:40 PM ET, under `runExclusive`, `server/services/bid-desk/charlotte-county.js`) first checks the database for an open (`new` or `bid`) Charlotte County Purchasing bid that has a bid number and no due date. Only when one is waiting does it read the county's own public bid list, one GET of `https://purchasingbids.charlottecountyfl.gov/ContractsCatalogs/GetContractData` (a fixed address; no cookies, no login; 15-second limit; a non-2xx answer, a non-JSON answer or a body over 5 MB is a failed run and writes nothing). A bid whose number is on the list exactly once, not awarded, with a real due date, gets that date: `due_at`, `due_source_line` "Charlotte County bid list: due <date and time ET>", `needs_date_confirmation` false, the sent-reminder stamps cleared, and `due_confirmed` true only while `GATE_BID_DESK_AUTO_DATES` is also on (otherwise the operator still confirms it, as for any source date). The 14 / 7 / 2-day reminders and the automatic close then work as for any confirmed date; bells the date answers close as an operator date confirmation closes them. An existing date is never overwritten; a decided bid, a status, a title, a decision and every bid from another sender are never touched; a number not on the list is left alone. Admin portal only: it sends nothing to a buyer, contractor, agency or customer, rings no new bell and needs no migration. Off = no call to the county and nothing changes, exactly as before.

Bid Desk not our work (dark): `GATE_BID_DESK_NOT_OUR_WORK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`bidDeskNotOurWorkLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; it also needs `GATE_BID_DESK=true`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: owner ruling 2026-10-29, "we are a lawn care, as in herbicide, micronutrients, fertilizer, lawn pest control, we dont mow" and "no mowing, edging, trimming, etc". Charlotte County files every notice by registered codes, so grounds jobs ("Lot Mowing for Code Compliance", "Facilities Grounds Maintenance") arrived as new bids with a review bell. On, a NEW bid is checked once, when it is first filed (an emailed invite or addendum, or a SAM.gov notice). The title is the bid's project title plus package name (else the email subject; for SAM.gov the notice title). If the title names grounds upkeep and names none of our work, the bid is filed as `no_bid` with the note "Not our work: mowing, edging or trimming (owner 2026-10-29)." and rings no new-bid bell. Upkeep words: mowing, edging, trimming (string trimmer, tree trimming, tree removal), weed eating, leaf blowing, litter and debris removal, pressure washing, pruning, mulching, sod, planting, hedges, grounds or lot maintenance, landscape or lawn maintenance, right-of-way maintenance, janitorial, irrigation repair. Our-work words (any one keeps the bid): herbicide, pesticide, insecticide, fungicide, weed control or spraying, spray, chemical, fertilizer, nutrients, pest, termite, mosquito, rodent, rat, exterminate, fumigate, insect, fire ant, chinch, grub, mole cricket, IPM, vegetation control, aquatic weed, turf or lawn treatment. A title with neither kind of word ("Hurricane Repairs at Darst Park", "Lawn Care Services") is filed as always. A bid a person marks by hand is never declined. A later addendum joins the declined bid and rings nothing, as for any decided bid. Existing bids are never changed; no backfill and no migration. Admin portal only: it sends nothing to a buyer, contractor, agency or customer. Off = every bid is filed as before.

Call applicant handling (dark): `GATE_CALL_APPLICANT_HANDLING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`callApplicantHandlingLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: on 10-29 a pest control operator called about a job. The call pipeline saw `call_nature` `job_applicant` and made no customer, but the call was labeled `no_action_needed` (the model's recommendation won over the nature default), the office got customer cards (missing service address, email unverified), the staff promise to meet him was stored as `schedule_visit` (a customer SLA kind), and no Careers record existed. On, for `job_applicant` and `vendor_or_partner` calls with a valid V2 extraction: (1) a model recommendation of `no_action_needed` gives way to the nature default `vendor_logged` (`decideDisposition(..., thirdPartyNatureDefault)`; spam, wrong number, complaint and every other recommendation are unchanged); (2) no customer-only review card is filed (`thirdPartyCustomerOnlyCards` in `server/services/call-triage-flags.js`: service address, name, email read-back, SMS consent capture, unconfirmed visit; `callback_number_needed` and `caller_phone_missing` stay, because the office needs a number to reach the caller back); the flags, route decision and routing verdict keep everything; (3) what Waves promised on the call is stored as kind `other` with no stated due time (the stated time moves into the description), so neither the pager (`SLA_KINDS`) nor the daily overdue watchdog counts it; (4) a `job_applicant` call files ONE `job_applications` row (`createJobApplicationFromCall` in `server/services/job-applications.js`): role `technician`, status `new`, `contact_snapshot` from the V2 caller (the call's number when no number was spoken), `source` `{channel: phone_call, call_log_id, organization_name, call_summary}`; keyed by `call_log_id`, so a reprocess never files a second row, and skipped while an open application (new, reviewed, interview, offer) with the same last 10 digits exists. Sends nothing to the applicant: no text, no email, no interview invite, no AI screen, no staff bell. Off = every call is handled exactly as before.

Call email checks (dark): `GATE_CALL_EMAIL_CHECKS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`callEmailChecksLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Why: the 2026-10-29 call-agent audit found the contact dictation decoder runs only on Gemini, and with Gemini over its spend cap from 10-24 it returned nothing with no log, so the owner's 2026-10-05 spelled-email rule never fired and every email heard on a call got a read-back card and a first-touch hold (144 holds retired unsent in 90 days); a domain with no mail server was saved and mailed (two transactional emails failed, nothing alerted). On (owner 2026-10-29 "yes build"): (1) the decoder runs through `dispatchWithFallback` (Gemini, then the OpenAI extraction model, each leg on the old single-call budget) and, when every model fails, logs it and writes one engineering row a day to the Activity feed (`contact-decoder-down`); (2) the domain of an email heard on a call gets a DNS check (the quarantine arbiter's `gatherEmailDomainEvidence`, via `server/services/call-email-checks.js`): an authoritative no-mail answer moves the address to `email_raw` before the upserts and files an `email_invalid` card that names the domain and the read-back question; a resolver hiccup never blocks; (3) a SendGrid bounce whose reason says the domain has no mail server (filed as "blocked") is a bad address everywhere in `server/routes/webhooks-sendgrid.js` (`isProviderBlock`): no provider retry, and it goes to people, never to an automatic correction or resend (AGENTS.md call-pipeline rule): the bounced-contact alert and the recording re-check card on every send path (tracked, automation, newsletter, untracked), with no bounce recovery and no transcript rescue (both can repair a domain on their own); a hard bounce keeps its own path; a temporary DNS failure (timeout, SERVFAIL, "try again") stays on the retry rail (`isNoMailServerEvent` in `server/services/email-bounce-recovery.js`, `isNoMailServerReason` in `server/services/call-email-checks.js`; suppression is unchanged); (4) every email read-back card shows the in-place Confirm email form to an admin (`POST /api/admin/triage/:id/confirm-email` accepts any email card). It adds no new kind of customer message. A no-AI spelled-letter trust rule was built and dropped in review: corrections said many ways kept defeating it, and with the decoder fallback the 10-05 rule runs through the decoder.

Invoice follow-up ladder through Day 90 (dark): `GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time in `server/services/invoice-followups.js` (`followupSteps()`). On, the ladder runs Day 3/10/17/30/60/90 after the invoice is sent (`stepsThrough90` in `server/config/invoice-followups.js`; the first four keep their step ids, so `step_index` and the ledger keys stay stable), and Day 90 is the only final notice (owner rulings 2026-09-27). A sequence that ran past the Day 30 end still owns its invoice: `hasActiveSequence` counts those `completed` rows, so the balance workflow no longer picks the invoice up afterwards (the handoff behind most customers reminded by two systems within a week). A payment finish before Day 30 does not: a dispute-reopened invoice with a low-step `completed` sequence is revived at the step it finished on, re-anchored to the reopen, after re-reading the invoice under its row lock (a payment that settled it meanwhile leaves the sequence completed). An invoice the retired checker ever contacted (`collections_contact_ledger` source `late_payment_checker`) is never revived: it may already have had its 60- and 90-day tiers, so it is logged for a person to settle. A sequence finished at the Day 60 or Day 90 step on a still-open invoice resumes at that step (the legacy Day 30 finishes, and payment finishes a dispute reopened). A touch stored on the legacy Day 7 or Day 14 waits for its Day 10 or Day 17, and goes out the same run when that day is today; a step already past its send day is passed over, never sent late. The annual-prepay reminder's same-day suppression reads the day the touch really fires (`liveNextTouchAt`). Turning the gate off hands an active row the ladder moved past Day 30 back to the legacy Day 30 cadence end (pauses and autopay holds keep holding), and moves a touch the ladder scheduled for Day 10 or Day 17 back to its legacy Day 7 or Day 14 while that day is still sendable (the gate-off batch read also picks those rows up, up to the cadence gap early). The Day 60 and Day 90 emails are never re-sent from a stored copy (`SENDER_RENDERED_TEMPLATES`). The Day 60 and Day 90 templates (`invoice_followup_60day`, `invoice_followup_90day`, `invoice.followup_60_day`, `invoice.followup_90_day`) are seeded with owner-approved wording by migration `20260928050000_invoice_followup_day60_day90_templates.js`, but it is insert-only and skips a key that already exists — before the owner flips the gate, confirm all four rows exist in that environment and carry the approved wording. Unset = byte-identical to before.

Seven-day overdue-reminder spacing, SHADOW ONLY (dark): `GATE_DUNNING_SPACING_SHADOW` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time in `server/services/collections/contact-policy.js` (`dunningSpacingShadowLive()`). Sequenced behind the ladder (`GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90`) and orphan adoption, which remove the handoffs behind most double contacts, so this gate only needs to observe. On, every `evaluate()` call for an overdue-reminder purpose (`late_payment` / `invoice_followup` / `balance_reminder`) additionally checks `server/services/collections/dunning-spacing.js`'s `lastOverdueReminderWithin7d` — a strict 7×24-hour window (not calendar days) from the previous DELIVERED (or send_failed-but-later-delivered) overdue-reminder ledger row from any of the five dunning rails' sources (`invoice_followups`, `late_payment_checker` (history only: that checker was deleted 2026-10-29), `previsit_balance_reminder`, `balance_reminder_late_payment_check`, `balance_reminder_workflow`) plus `invoice_followup_replay` (a follow-up text delivered after the send window, grouped with its touch by `notificationEventKey`; bank-verification re-nudges carry `verification_renudge` and are skipped; replay rows from before the key existed are left out and counted separately by the replay script). Only a caller that names one of those rails as its `source` is observed (voice and sweep checks are not), and the shadow needs `GATE_COLLECTIONS_POLICY` on too (rail-guard warns once otherwise) — and, if it would have held, logs ONE `[contact-policy] dunning_within_7d SHADOW would hold` line with the customer id, channel, purpose, the previous send's source, hours since it, and the verdict the policy actually returned. It never changes that verdict: no denial reason is added, no lock is taken, no send is held. This is the owner's evidence (also `server/scripts/dunning-spacing-replay.js`, a read-only historical replay) before an enforcing PR. Unset = byte-identical to before — it only logs.

Orphan invoice adoption (dark): `GATE_DUNNING_ADOPT_ORPHANS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time in `server/services/invoice-followups.js` (`adoptOrphanInvoices`, called first in `runPending`). On, each Tue–Fri run gives a sequence to every delivered (`sent`/`viewed`/`overdue`), homeowner-billed, not-withdrawn open invoice with a balance, no active payment plan, NO `invoice_followup_sequences` row and **no legacy checker contact at all** (`collections_contact_ledger` source `late_payment_checker`), through `scheduleForInvoice`'s adoption mode (all its guards and autopay-hold handling apply). It reads autopay eligibility fail-closed, and under the ACH webhook's own per-customer `ach.escalation` lock it leaves any customer with unresolved ACH failures (last 90 days) for a person, with no counter seeding. The row is inserted already on its first step whose send day has not passed, dated no earlier than the next run, in one statement, so an adopted row never sends in the run that adopted it. The live sweep selects and adopts under the `late-payment-check` cron lock (`runExclusive('late-payment-check')`, so two pods never sweep at once); lock held = refused for that run. A sweep failure is logged and never stops that run's due touches. Never adopted, and listed by the dry-run script for a person to settle: `has_legacy_history` (a checker contact in `collections_contact_ledger` OR its older `activity_log` `late_payment_reminder` rows), `past_final_step`, `ach_failure_history`. Read-only production count first: `server/scripts/dunning-adopt-orphans-dry-run.js`. It prints the gate state it ran with and warns when the ladder gate is missing from its environment (`railway run --service Postgres` does not carry the web service's gates; export it for the run). `--execute` adopts, and exits 1 on refusal (the cron lock is held). Unset = byte-identical to before.

Pre-visit balance reminder 5-day window (dark): `GATE_PREVISIT_BALANCE_5DAY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time in `server/services/previsit-balance-reminder.js` (`leadDays()`). On, the balance note's lead window widens from 3 to 5 days before the visit (owner decision 6, dunning unification 2026-09-27), ahead of the 72-hour appointment reminder (`appointment-reminders.js`). The unchanged one-per-appointment claim on `scheduled_services.balance_reminder_sent_at` guarantees no visit is ever sent twice, even on the first gated-on run, which also claims previously-unclaimed 4–5-day-out visits. Unset = byte-identical 3-day window.

Customer-level overdue reminders (dark; engine wired live behind its gate): `GATE_DUNNING_CUSTOMER_SCHEDULE_SHADOW`, `GATE_DUNNING_CUSTOMER_SCHEDULE` and `DUNNING_CUSTOMER_SCHEDULE_ALLOWLIST` — **both gates ship DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `dunningCustomerScheduleShadowLive()` / `dunningCustomerScheduleLive()` / `dunningCustomerScheduleAllowlist()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; the `gates.dunningCustomerSchedule*` map entries are for `logGateStatus` only). The dunning-consolidation plan (`customer_dunning_schedules`, migration `20260930010000`): a customer with 2+ actively-dunned open invoices gets ONE schedule row that owns the reminder cadence, so a touch advances one row instead of one per invoice; the per-invoice `invoice_followup_sequences` rows keep every lifecycle hook and stay control flags and membership state. **Wiring (`runPending`, every run, in this order):** the kill switch `customer-dunning/wiring.js` `releaseIfDark(now)` releases every OPEN schedule the live gate does not reach (gate off → `released_gate_off`, `GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90` or the pay-page balance gate off → `released_prereq_off`, a customer outside a configured allowlist → `released_gate_off`), landing each surviving member on its own ladder at its first non-stale step no earlier than the next run, never repeating a step (the current step's ledger evidence is read first: a step that already reached an invoice is not sent to it again, a delivered final notice completes the invoices it named and an unreadable one pauses them for a person; a member past its final step is paused and alerted; a PAUSED schedule's members stay paused with its reason and admin; with `GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90` off a member past Day 30 keeps that step, which hands it to the legacy checker); under the shadow gate a dark schedule's shadow verdict is logged before it is released; a schedule with a send in flight is left for the next run, and a release failure (unreadable delivery evidence, or a current-step leg whose outcome is unconfirmed while members remain, included: nothing is handed back; admin release answers 409 `OUTCOME_UNCONFIRMED`) is logged and raised to the office (`raiseAdminAlert`, Billing, needs-you, person), while a failed read of the open schedules is raised only when the engine is reachable (live gate on, or this process's last read saw open schedules) and otherwise only logged — the per-invoice run always goes on. Then, live gate only, `schedule.promote(now)` (never sends in its own run); then the per-invoice batch, which excludes every customer with an open schedule (`NOT EXISTS customer_dunning_schedules … status IN active/held/paused/autopay_hold` — no rows, nothing excluded); then `runner.runCustomerSchedules(now)` when live, else the write-nothing `shadowRun(now)` under the shadow gate (full verdicts only for customers already on a schedule row and within the allowlist; an unpromoted customer only gets `would promote|absorb`). With the live gate off and no schedule rows the run's effect is unchanged (one read of the schedule table). **Ownership fence:** `fireStep` takes the customer's dunning advisory key SHARED (`pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtext('customer-dunning:<id>'))`) BEFORE its invoice `FOR UPDATE`, re-reads ownership under it and never claims or fires an owned row; the engine takes the same key EXCLUSIVELY for promotion, its claim and every close/release, in the order key → schedule row → member invoice rows (id order) → sequence rows, so the two never lock in opposite orders (proven by `customer-dunning-live-wiring-postgres.test.js`). **Office controls:** the invoice follow-up send-now (`POST /api/admin/invoices/:id/followup/send-now`, `sendNextTouchNow`) for a customer on an open schedule sends the schedule's CURRENT step instead (operator channels; never while the schedule is dark) and returns `{ routedTo: 'customer_schedule', scheduleId, … }` — only when the body confirms that step (`{ combined: true, scheduleId, stepIndex }`, what `GET /api/admin/invoices/:id/followup`'s `customerSchedule` showed: id, customer id, status, step index and label, invoice count, next touch, controllable, paused reason; the invoice panel shows it, names it in the confirm, and offers Pause combined / Resume combined buttons that post to the customer routes below; release is not offered there, because the next run re-promotes a released customer who still has two active invoices): without it 409 `COMBINED_CONFIRM_REQUIRED`, a schedule that moved past that step 409 `SCHEDULE_CHANGED`, and a confirmation for a customer no longer on a schedule 409 `COMBINED_SCHEDULE_CLOSED` (the invoice's own step is never sent in its place); `POST /api/admin/customers/:id/dunning-schedule/{send-now,pause,resume,release}` (admin only) control the open schedule — 404 none open, 409 `IN_FLIGHT` ("The reminder is sending right now. Try again in a minute."), 409 `SCHEDULE_NOT_LIVE` / `SCHEDULE_CHANGED` / `EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE`, and a send-now that sent nothing (held, paused, autopay hold, closed, or a paused schedule) is 409 `NOT_SENT` with a plain-English "Not sent: …" reason; only a send that reached the customer (advanced / completed / told) is 200. Every press of these four controls that reaches a schedule, and every invoice send-now routed to one, writes one `activity_log` row on the customer (`combined_reminders_{send_now,pause,resume,release}`, `admin_user_id` = who pressed it, the outcome in the description and metadata, refusals included; best effort, never fails the press). The invoice panel calls pause and resume only; they are refused (409 `SCHEDULE_NOT_LIVE`) while the live gate does not cover the customer, and the panel hides them then (`customerSchedule.controllable`). An invoice with no sequence of its own gets `customerSchedule` only when the combined balance names it. A paused schedule reports why (`pausedBy` staff or system, `pausedReason`), shown before Resume. **Promotion alert (owner 2026-10-29):** every new schedule raises ONE office alert after its promotion commits (`alertCombinedStarted` in `schedule.js`, through `alertStaff`: Billing, needs-you, person, rings): headline "combined reminders started for <first name + last initial>", why "N invoices, $X total; first reminder <weekday, date>; pause it from the invoice panel if wrong", deduped by `customer-dunning-started:<schedule id>` (a later episode is a new schedule with its own alert; a refused or lost-race promotion raises nothing). Promotion still sends the customer nothing; it dates the first touch at least one run ahead (`seed.js`), so the alert always lands before the first combined reminder. The alert's date is the schedule's next step, worded "unless held" because a customer still on Auto Pay parks the schedule at that step: `markAutopayHold` then raises ONE office alert per hold episode (`alertAutopayHold`, Billing, needs-you, person, "charge the card on file for <first name + last initial>"; the office charges the card or takes the customer off Auto Pay so reminders run), only when the row was not already parked, deduped by `customer-dunning-autopay-hold:<schedule id>:<episode>:<time it parked>`, so the daily revisit stays quiet, a schedule that resumes and parks again rings once more, and the shadow run raises nothing; nothing is sent either way. The Auto Pay hold timeout (`releaseStaleAutopayHolds`) no longer treats a customer the live engine covers as owned: with no allowlist it releases a stale hold for everyone who has no OPEN schedule. **Cross-rail:** the pre-visit balance note skips a customer whose schedule itself touched them (a `last_touch_at` after the row was created, never the members' touches promotion copied in) within its 72-hour recent-touch window; `invoice_followups_customer` is an overdue-reminder source for the 7-day spacing shadow (a touch's legs share one `notificationEventKey`, one event); `handleAutopayFailure` deliberately leaves an `autopay_hold` schedule to the engine's daily revisit (the ACH escalation it follows moves the customer off bank autopay — `needs_verification` at the second failure, disarmed or switched to a fallback card at the third — which `customerOnAutopay` reads; releasing it would only be re-promoted next run). **Customer merge:** `executeMerge` (`customer-dedupe.js`, every merge path) first releases any open schedule of either customer through the engine as `released_merge` (members land as above; a release the engine refuses — a send in flight, an unconfirmed or unreadable current step — aborts the merge with a 409 `DUNNING_SCHEDULE_BUSY` before anything moved), then, first in its transaction, takes both customers' dunning keys, refuses a schedule that opened meanwhile, and renumbers the loser's episodes above the winner's (journaled as `dunning_episode_renumbers`); the next run promotes the merged customer as one. `revertMerge` takes the same keys and moves the closed history back by id. **Manual release:** `server/scripts/dunning-customer-schedule-release.js [--customer <id>] [--execute]` (dry run by default in a `READ ONLY` transaction, ids only; `--execute` releases each open schedule through the engine as `released_admin` and refuses without `GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90=true` exported, as the web service has it). Releasing while the live gate is on lets the next run promote the customer again.
