It adds the table (open episodes unique per customer through the partial index `customer_dunning_schedules_open_uniq`, which is the ownership predicate), the byte-identical combined-template migration `20260928060000_invoice_followup_combined_templates.js` (12 keys, md5 pinned by a test; the email-library `rowsFromVariable` feature is deliberately NOT ported, so on main the combined email shows count + total only; the 12 keys are protected email templates and sender-rendered, and `invoice.followup_combined_90_day` is a final notice), `server/services/customer-dunning/` (`constants.js` key builders, `balance-set.js` `resolveDunnableSet`, `seed.js` the promotion seed), the `onDegrade(reason)` observer on `pay-combined.js` `combinedEligibleSiblings` (`gate_off | payer_anchor | payer_unresolved | incomplete | over_cap | none`; `database` now reaches the payer resolve), `invoiceCreditWouldFullyCover` moved into `pay-combined.js` (its only import path; `pay-v2.js` no longer exports it), the cadence helper exports on `invoice-followups.js`, and the read-only `server/scripts/dunning-customer-schedule-dry-run.js` (ids only, every customer in its own `READ ONLY` transaction; it warns when `GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90` is missing from its environment). `resolveDunnableSet` is a pure read that re-runs the pay page's own authority (`openBalanceInvoices`, `combinedEligibleSiblings`, pay-v2's anchor predicates) and returns `multi | single | empty | hold`; any failure is a `hold`, never a send. The engine NEVER applies account credit (owner ruling 2026-09-30, superseding the older credit-draw design): a customer with ANY unused account credit gets `hold` / `account_credit_available` (the full set still attached), the live path holds the schedule and raises ONE office alert ("Apply customer account credit"; an office hold reason, deduped by `hold_alerted_at` per hold and by key `customer-dunning-held:<schedule>:<episode>:account_credit_available`), and no customer-facing message goes out; the shadow run only logs the hold. The later live gate additionally requires `GATE_DUNNING_LADDER_90` and `GATE_PAY_INCLUDE_BALANCE` on; the allowlist (comma list of customer ids, empty = everyone) only narrows it for a canary. Unset = byte-identical to before. **The live gate and the allowlist are the owner's flips** (one-customer allowlist canary first, after reviewing the dry-run and shadow logs); turning the live gate off is the rollback, released by the next run's kill switch.

Quiet overdue invoices bell (dark): `GATE_QUIET_OVERDUE_LIST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`quietOverdueListLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-24, after an audit found open self-pay invoices that no reminder reaches: a follow-up sequence paused with no end (or past its `paused_until`: `runPending` selects only `active` rows, so nothing resumes a pause), stopped, finished at its last step, or held for Auto Pay that never charged, or no sequence at all (orphan adoption leaves legacy-history and past-final-step invoices for a person and only logs them). On, a weekday 11:47 ET cron (`scheduler.js`, after the 10:16 dunning run, inside `runExclusive('quiet-overdue-invoices')`) runs `runQuietOverdueList` (`server/services/quiet-overdue-invoices.js`): a published (`sent`/`viewed`/`overdue`), homeowner-billed (no `payer_id`, not withdrawn), unarchived invoice with money due, no active payment plan and no open customer-level schedule (that engine alerts on its own holds) is listed when its sequence has been on Auto Pay hold 7+ Eastern days (from the later of the row's `updated_at`, which every writer stamps when it sets `autopay_hold` and nothing moves again except a failed Auto Pay charge, and the due date) or, in any other quiet state, once it is 14+ days past due. The list is ONE needs-you Billing bell row (`dedupeKey` `quiet-overdue-invoices`, category `billing` with `bellDefault`, so `GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY` admits it unless the owner silenced billing): the headline counts the invoices, the why gives the amount owed with no overdue reminder scheduled and the oldest age, "Show full text" lists each one oldest first with the reason. The row refreshes every weekday, rings again only when an invoice joins the list (or the list comes back after it was empty, through `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`), and closes itself done when the list is empty (`closeAdminAlertKeys`). A person's own done stays done until a new invoice joins. With `ALERT_EPISODES` killed it raises through `raiseAdminAlert` and never closes. Sends nothing to a customer and changes no invoice or reminder. Rollback: unset the gate (the standing row stays until marked done).

Unbilled visits bell (dark): `GATE_UNBILLED_VISITS_LIST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`unbilledVisitsListLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-25 (Air Jobs Plan step 3): it replaces the c02 "Unbilled completions" check that ran on the owner's MacBook Air, an Aug 25 SQL copy of the Billing recovery leak query that missed the later fixes (the consultation fee rule, prepay and sibling coverage, stale billed-elsewhere rows). On, a daily 07:23 ET cron (`scheduler.js`, inside `runExclusive('unbilled-visits-list')`) runs `runUnbilledVisitsList` (`server/services/unbilled-visits-list.js`), which reads the Billing recovery page's own list (`listUninvoicedLeaks` in `server/routes/admin-billing-recovery.js`, the code behind `GET /api/admin/billing-recovery/leaks`) for the last 30 days, both the one-click leaks and the needs-review rows. The list is ONE needs-you Billing bell row (`dedupeKey` `unbilled-visits`, category `billing` with `bellDefault`, so `GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY` admits it unless the owner silenced billing): the headline counts the visits (one visit names its customer), the why gives the amount and the oldest visit's date, and "Show full text" lists each visit oldest first with its next step. The row refreshes every day, rings again only when a visit joins the list (or the list comes back after it was empty, through `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`), and closes itself done when no visit in the window waits (`closeAdminAlertKeys`). A person's own done stays done until a new visit joins. With `ALERT_EPISODES` killed it raises through `raiseAdminAlert` and never closes. Bills nothing, sends nothing to a customer and changes no visit or invoice. Rollback: unset the gate (the standing row stays until marked done).

One-hour follow-up pager (dark): `GATE_FOLLOWUP_SLA_ALERTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, needs `GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS`. Every 15 minutes 8 AM–8:45 PM ET, a Waves promise from a call (callback, quote, a time to come out) with no follow-up within one hour of 8 AM–8 PM ET time (owner ruling 2026-09-26) lands on ONE rolling bell listing every miss from the last 24 hours, uncapped — re-posted to the top when a new miss joins, rewritten in place when items drop off, retired when empty. Followed up = the commitment's fulfillment proof, staff dismiss/snooze, or a later visit, outbound call, or staff-typed text. Internal only. See `server/services/followup-sla-watcher.js`.

Address review alert: every 15 minutes while `GATE_GEOCODE_REVIEW` is on, customers blocked in the staff address-review queue (needs a pin, address incomplete, possibly outside the service area — the queue's own `listReviewQueue` read) land on ONE rolling bell ("Address review: N customers can't book online", linking to `/admin/customers`). Item keys are customer + status, so it rings when a customer joins or changes problem, updates quietly as they are resolved, and retires when the queue is empty (owner request 2026-09-29). Kill: `GEOCODE_REVIEW_ALERT_DISABLED=1`; email fallback recipient `GEOCODE_REVIEW_ALERT_EMAIL` (internal inboxes only). Internal only. See `server/services/geocode-review-alert.js`.

Promises close on proof: `PROMISE_EVIDENCE_CLOSE` — **DEFAULT ON; off only when set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `promiseEvidenceCloseLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`) — the one canonical reader (owner ruling 2026-09-28, "close it, show proof"; live kill, no redeploy). On, `refreshFulfillment` in `server/services/call-commitments.js` closes an open Waves promise nobody has touched (no `human_state`: a claimed, snoozed or edited callback card keeps only its own direct proof) on an association proof exactly like a direct one (status `fulfilled`, the proof kept on the row), for kinds `other`, `callback`, `send_estimate`, `send_appointment_confirmation`, `schedule_visit`, `send_report` and `send_paperwork` (a technician follow-up, photos and payments keep an association as a hint); adds follow-up evidence that MATCHES the kind of the promise (owner audit 2026-10-05; a booking or the customer reaching Waves is never Waves keeping its word): `send_estimate` and `callback` take none beyond their own lookups (an estimate sent; a call or text a person placed to the caller), `schedule_visit` takes a visit completed, `send_report` and `send_paperwork` a service report delivered, and `other` is decided by its CHANNEL alone (one table in `call-commitments.js`, `CHANNEL_MEDIA`; the wording is never read, and an estimate never keeps it): `sms` is kept by a text to the caller (a person's delivered text, or the booking lane's link text once the provider accepted it, each fenced to the call's customer), `call` by a call a person placed to the caller (phone-matched for an unlinked caller; a completed Call Log callback-card customer leg for the source call counts, inside the 14-day window), `unknown` or absent by no record alone (only the model-judged contact check may close it, on a text or a call), and `email`, `in_person` or anything else by nothing automatic: a person closes it. The lapse scan reopens any `other` close (deterministic or model-judged) whose proof type the promise's current channel no longer allows, and the contact check offers only the witness types the channel allows; a booked visit closes only `schedule_visit`, and the customer phoning in closes no Waves promise (the lapse scan reopens earlier closes on the wrong evidence: a visit on a non-scheduling promise, an inbound call, an estimate on a callback or an `other` promise); the callback's own direct proof, a staff call back or a person's text, now reads the texting lane's provenance and delivery rules from `server/services/staff-contact.js` (`personCallBack`: staff-bridge source, live conversation; `operatorReply` + `smsDelivered`: composer stamp / sending admin / staff draft queue, delivered — never a bare `manual` type or an automated collections call; candidates are read in keyset pages until one passes, so a long run of refused ones hides nothing); an estimate sent on a lead reused from an earlier call is only ever a hint); counts an association only from a later stated time that is not a deadline (the follow-up pager's rule; direct proof may keep a promise early) and only inside the 14-day window from the call (a later start never extends it); never closes a `schedule_visit` promise for a slot the call confirmed on anything but a booking for that slot (any other visit stays a hint, `slot_bound`); and dismisses such a promise whose customer is churned now (the live `pipeline_stage = 'churned'`, on a churn date after the promise — a reactivated customer's stale `churned_at` is not leaving, and neither is a soft delete: a merge soft-deletes the duplicate profile). Each close records the customer the call had when it was judged: every refresh of a call re-judges what it closed on its own (a reprocess of the call refreshes it at once), and the watchdog sweep refreshes any call whose customer no longer matches, or whose promise a reprocess gave a stated time at or after its proof (closes from the last 30 days; older ones are history), so a relink to another customer, or a later stated time — even one the refresh never saw — reopens a promise that evidence no longer keeps. Customer promises are unchanged; nothing is sent. The Owed tab lists what closed in the last 7 days (`GET /admin/call-recordings/commitments/auto-closed`, pages of 100 with Load more, each with the promise itself and its proof, by the close time stored on the proof, `closed_at` — never `updated_at`, which a reprocess rewrites; the lapse scan reads it off the partial index `call_commitments_evidence_closed_idx`) with a one-click Reopen; a reopened promise is the office's and never closes on its own again. Off = byte-identical to before (association proof stays a "possibly kept" hint).

Promises close on a person's contact: `PROMISE_CONTACT_CHECK` — **DEFAULT ON; off only when set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `promiseContactCheckLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; live kill, no redeploy; owner ruling 2026-09-29). An open Waves "other" promise made on a call ("I'll check and let you know") closes only when a MODEL judges that a person's later delivered text or call back to that customer DELIVERED the promised thing — any contact alone never closes it, and "Thanks!" or an unrelated text is not the promised thing (the texting lane's rule 19: a promise Waves made is never closed by a later reply; the model judges it). A 15-minute tick (`runPromiseContactCheck`, `server/services/call-commitment-contact-check.js`, `runExclusive('call-commitment-contact-check')`; never inside `refreshFulfillment`, which runs on every Call panel open) does nothing unless this switch, `PROMISE_EVIDENCE_CLOSE` AND `GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS` are all live. Candidates: open, untouched (no `human_state`), AI-recorded (not entered by hand) `other` promises whose call has a customer, inside the 14-day window from the call's end; oldest call first, every candidate read page by page (a promise already judged costs only reads, so it never crowds a newer one out), at most 25 model calls a run (the rest wait for the next tick). Witnesses: only records linked to the call's CURRENT `customer_id` (never a phone alone), after the promise's evidence floor (the promise call's EXACT end — the booking lane's `callEndFor`, so a text sent during an outbound promise call is not later — or a renewal of the obligation, or a later stated non-deadline time) and inside the window: an outbound text that passes the shared `operatorReply` + `smsDelivered` rules (`staff-contact.js`; no automated text, no undelivered one, no unresolved send reservation, no proactive draft) or an outbound staff-bridge call that passes `personCallBack` (no collections call, no voicemail, never the promise's own call, never a sandbox call; its witness text is the call's stored transcript, `call_log.transcription`, and its time is when the customer conversation ended, `callEndFor`: a bridge's signed customer-leg end); a source that fails, truncates (25 per channel, 20,000 characters each) or cannot be scrubbed settles the verdict as `uncertain` before a provider is asked. Contract: `TEXT_POLICIES.fastStructured` (waves-llm's workload rule: a verifier whose verdict code consumes runs on the fast tier) through `dispatchWithFallback` with a 60-second hard deadline for both providers together (the first failed call ends the run's model calls, so a stalled provider never pins the run's lock), switchboard lane `call-commitment-contact-check`, the texting helper's `{verdict: fulfilled|open|uncertain, record_ref, quote}`; `record_ref` must name an offered witness and the quote (at least 3 characters, normalized) must be a substring of that witness's text, else `uncertain`; on a call only Waves' own words count: the quote must sit in an Agent turn of the transcript's labels, and a transcript without Agent/Caller labels never grounds a close; payment data is scrubbed (`scrubSegments`, `stringifySmsEvidence`) before a provider sees a byte. The verdict is cached per row by evidence hash in `call_commitments.contact_check` (a provider or schema failure retries after an hour). A grounded `fulfilled` closes the promise in one transaction that locks the promise, the call's customer and the witness, re-reads the witnesses (they must hash as the model saw them), and writes through the same guards as `refreshFulfillment`'s association write: status `fulfilled`, proof `kind: person_contact`, `basis: model_judged_person_contact`, `closed_by: promise_evidence`, the judged customer and the quote; a lost race writes nothing and the next run judges again. A kill stops NEW checks only: `refreshFulfillment`'s re-judge KEEPS a model-judged close while its witness still stands (deterministic, no model call: the record exists, has the call's customer and the judged customer, still passes `operatorReply` + `smsDelivered` or `personCallBack`, is still after the floor and inside the window, still says exactly what the model read: the md5 of its raw text, stored on the proof as `witness_md5`, and the promise is still the one the model judged, `promise_md5`: a reprocess that rewrites its description, quotes or due time reopens it) and reopens it otherwise, so a re-transcribed call is judged again; the watchdog's lapse scan lists such a close when its witness is gone, relinked to another customer, no longer counts, or its words changed. The Owed tab's "Closed automatically" list shows "Kept: staff text" or "Kept: staff call back" with the quote and a one-click Reopen. Internal ledger writes only: no customer message of any kind.

Call reschedule apply (dark): `GATE_CALL_RESCHEDULE_APPLY` — when a matched existing customer (call linked at ingest AND calling from the phone on file) and the agent agree to move a visit already on the books (V2 `scheduling.status = reschedule_requested`, `confirmed_start_at`, scheduling_window confidence ≥ 0.8, and the extraction's own judgement that the agent committed — `agent_committed_booking` — AND the caller accepted that final slot — `caller_accepted_slot`, schema 1.16.0), the processor moves that visit through `SmartRebooker.reschedule` (keepStatus, CAS-pinned), appends the caller's access request to the visit's `internal_notes`, writes a `call_reschedule_applied` activity_log row (also the reprocess idempotency marker), and resolves the call's `reschedule_or_cancel` / `existing_appointment_coordination` cards as `auto`. The code never reads agreement out of the conversation itself (owner decision 2026-09-27): `server/services/call-reschedule-agreement.js` only checks that the extraction's pinned quotes — the agent's commitment, the caller's acceptance, and the moved appointment's date when given (`moved_appointment_date`) — appear word for word in a turn of their speaker, and that the words the extraction recorded for the moved date (`moved_appointment_words`, schema 1.17.0) sit in that quote. The slot itself is the booking step's accepted slot (owner 2026-10-27, the way the make-up move `GATE_CALL_MAKEUP_MOVE` did it in #6437): the extraction's `confirmed_start_at`, which must be a real future instant exactly on the hour and is moved only with the grounded agent commitment and the grounded caller acceptance. The recorded `agreed_slot_words` {day, hour, period} no longer have to sit word for word in a quote (they were empty on 10 of 12 calls on Oct 24, so 0 of 22 reschedule calls would have moved); a missing slot, a missing caller acceptance or an ungrounded commitment still refuses. The one exception is a RELATIVE date (`relative_date_used`, "next Thursday"): its recorded words are the only check of the day the extraction resolved it to, so the old words check still applies there. The extraction also judges the promise's language (schema 1.20.0, prompt v19; owner direction 2026-09-30, after word-list review rounds did not converge): `definite_commitment` (false for could/might/probably/upon X/once Y/if Z), `relative_date_used` and `moved_appointment_relative_date_used` (next week, the following Thursday, eight days away — the extraction resolves them to the absolute date in `confirmed_start_at` / `moved_appointment_date`); the module only verifies them — a missing flag fails closed, a flagged relative date must be future, within 60 days, and consistent with its words: a bare weekday must match the resolved date's weekday, and only a relative form WITHOUT an exact computed offset ("next/this/the following Thursday") must also not be the nearest such weekday; a pinned clause with an exact closed-set offset (in N days/weeks, N days/weeks from now/today/away/out, tomorrow, the day after tomorrow) is computed by the code and the resolved date must agree with it (a weekday takes its first occurrence on or after the offset date, even when that is the nearest); any offset-shaped span the code cannot compute, or a bound or alternative around an offset (at least, within, or three, to three), fails closed; an unflagged date must be the nearest one. A new hour said with no AM/PM or part of the day reads as business hours (7–11 morning, 12 and 1–6 afternoon; owner decision 2026-09-28, prompt v15; since prompt v18, owner decision 2026-09-29, the extraction reads a committed and accepted exact hour of a NEW booking the same way — e.g. "can we plan on 2 o'clock?" / "Sure." is 2 PM — and a stated period that conflicts blocks confirmation); any other unstated hour never moves a visit. Fail-closed: exactly one live, ungrouped, non-dispatch-owned upcoming visit of the service the call names, on the moved appointment's date when the extraction grounded one, within 14 days of the target, else the card stays open with a `reschedule_apply.skipped` breadcrumb in its payload. Sends NO customer communication. See `server/services/call-reschedule-apply.js`.

Call make-up move (dark): `GATE_CALL_MAKEUP_MOVE` — an existing customer's recurring visit was missed (status still `pending`/`confirmed`, dated in the last 30 days, with an OPEN `customer_noshow` row in `reschedule_log` for that same date and window, and either a person's "this was a miss" or no field work and no service record), the customer calls and a booking is about to be inserted. The decision runs INSIDE the booking transaction at its fresh insert (`planCallMakeupForBooking`), after every booking guard (this call's own booking reused, the ±1-day attach, the same-day hold, the re-service checks, the slot-elapsed recheck), and judges the booking's own row: its customer, property and slot. No missed visit of the call's line at that property: the row is inserted as always. Exactly one, and none of the holds fires: nothing is inserted, and after the transaction `applyCallMakeupMove` moves THAT visit to the booking's slot through `SmartRebooker.reschedule` (keepStatus, CAS-pinned, reason `ai_call_makeup`, default series policy so the cadence follows; the rebooker settles the `customer_noshow` row as `rebooked`), stamps `source_call_log_id` on it, and writes a `call_makeup_move_applied` activity_log row. Any hold (`MAKEUP_HOLDS` in `server/services/call-reschedule-apply.js`: V2 not `scheduling.status = confirmed` with `caller_accepted_slot`, its `confirmed_start_at` not the booking's slot, confidence under 0.8, not `follow_up_existing_service` / `existing_customer_scheduling`, a specialty category instead of `pest_general` / `lawn_care` / `mosquito`, secondary categories, a named service of another line, several or placeholder candidates, a visit moved after the call, a promised visit 2 or package follow-up, a re-service booking, a booking that would go in pending for an address check, this pass's disclaimed-number hold, a caller not on the account's own `phone` (a secondary or service-contact number holds) or not STIR-A attested inbound, `GATE_CALL_AGENT_COMMIT_TRUSTED_LABELS` off; then a staff-handled card, this call's own earlier booking, an open portal request or reschedule-options text, a live visit landing on the agreed day, a changed row, or a rebooker refusal) holds the booking as `missed_visit_makeup_needs_review` and never inserts a visit beside the missed one. A reprocess of a call whose move applied is a no-op while the live call and visit still match the marker (`priorCallMakeupDecision`), else it holds. Sends NO customer communication.

Commercial dictated booking (dark): `GATE_CALL_COMMERCIAL_DICTATED_BOOKING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callCommercialDictatedBookingLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; owner ruling 2026-09-30, call-booker gates review item 8). A commercial job the owner or staff book on the call itself auto-books instead of always going to the office. **INBOUND calls only for now** (owner ruling: outbound speaker labels have swapped; outbound waits until staff identity on an outbound recording is established independently of the labels), and it also needs `GATE_CALL_AGENT_COMMIT_BOOKING` (the kill switch of the commercial exception) and `GATE_CALL_AGENT_COMMIT_TRUSTED_LABELS` — the processor combines them at both `canAutoRoute` sites. It is a SECOND path beside the 2026-09-24 agent-commit demotion (`hasAgentCommittedEvidence`, untouched) that clears ONLY `commercial_requires_quote` in `canAutoRoute` (the flag rides `failedOpenFlags`, so the office still gets the advisory card). **The extraction judges the language, the code only verifies** (owner direction 2026-09-30, same as reschedules; schema 1.21.0, prompt v20): `service_request.price_offered_by_staff` (staff offered the amount as Waves' own quote, not a question or a competitor's), `price_accepted_by_caller`, `price_is_final` (no later correction), `scheduling.staff_accepted_proposed_slot` (staff's very next turn accepted the caller's exact proposal as a whole) and `scheduling.selected_day_words` (the day the caller selected when the final time turn omits it), each with its quote pinned; a missing judgement fails closed. The code (`groundNewBookingAgreement` in `server/services/call-reschedule-agreement.js`, beside the untouched `groundRescheduleAgreement`, reusing its turn parser, quote grounding and slot checks, via `server/services/call-commercial-dictated-booking.js`) checks that every pinned quote is word for word in a turn of its required speaker, in order (acceptance after the offer; staff's reply the entire turn immediately after the caller's proposal; the caller's short acceptance the whole turn directly after staff's commitment; the selected-day quote before the time turn), and the deterministic parts: the offer quote states the booked amount, in digits or spoken words (`spokenFiguresIn`; a dollars-and-cents compound reads as one amount), the exact on-the-hour slot, date resolution, adjacency. The code does NOT scan for other figures: a later correction or added charge, in any wording, is the extraction's `price_is_final` judgement (owner ruling 2026-10-01, after four number-phrasing rounds); do not restore a figure scan. No affirm/hedge word lists here: do not grow one. Price: `quoted_price_usd` (the field booking consumes; an accepted price entry alone is not enough) AND an accepted `price`/`prices` entry for exactly that amount whose spoken unit is `one_time`, `per_application` or `unknown` (a missing entry or unit fails closed: `resolveCallAgreedPrice` would otherwise synthesize a unitless term), the quote must survive the catalog-aware booking price resolver for every view of the call's service (V1 before V2-primary adoption, merged, V2 booking view; the audits rebuild the V1 view from `ai_extraction.pre_adoption_service_fields`, and hold a V2 row without it), a confirmed on-the-hour start, and a NEW visit (an extraction that also moves an existing appointment is a reschedule). Address validation, unit checks, capacity, HOA approval, `caller_not_authorized` and every other hold still apply. Off = byte-identical to before. Decision versions: no gate-specific tag; a pass after a human reviewed the decision writes the gate-agnostic `+r1` revision of the same base version (`routeDecisionFamilyVersions` in `server/services/call-routing-gates.js`).

Call extraction system prompt (dark): `GATE_CALL_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read once per call via `callExtractionSystemPromptLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, call extraction V2 sends its rules, the bookable catalog and the output contract as one static system part and only the call's own facts (phone, date, time, known caller, caller ID name, direction, prior call) and transcript as the user message, so the provider caches the rules across calls instead of billing about 24,000 input tokens in full on every call. Same rules in a different order and channel; the two rule lines that named the call date point at the date line of the user message. Its calls are their own prompt-version cohort: `s` inside the leading token (`v25s-…`), or `b` with the agent-proposed-slot block; `v2-promotion-readiness` follows the gate. Off = the one-message prompt and its version, byte-identical. Rollback: unset the variable. Before a flip, run the reviewed-call replay with the gate on and compare with gate off. See `server/services/prompts/call-extraction-v1.js` (`buildExtractionPromptParts`).

Collapsed-spelling trigger (dark): `GATE_CALL_SPELLING_COLLAPSE_TRIGGER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callSpellingCollapseTriggerLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). The diarized primary transcript sometimes collapses a spelled name ("Serov, S-E-R-O-V") into the plain word ("Serov, Serov"); every letter-run pattern in `detectContactDictationSignals` then returns false, so the spelling-preserving second transcription pass and the contact decoder never run and the name-spelling review card cannot catch that error. While on, `spellingCollapseSignals` (`server/services/contact-dictation.js`) also buys the pass on these marks: (a) a capitalized name token (two letters or more) said twice in a row across punctuation or a speaker label, with name context in the SAME speaker turn before it (or in the turn just before it when that turn is a question): "last/first/full name", "name" (not "service/product/company/street/business name"), "spell", "it's", "this is", "I'm", "I am", or the token equals the extracted first or last name; a greeting alone ("Hi, I ...") is not context, and everyday vocabulary (fillers, yes/no, weekdays, months, US states, service-area cities) never counts; (b) a phrase that announces a spelling: "spelled" / "spell that" with no letter run within 60 characters after it, or a single-letter announcement ("that's S", "with a C", "S as in") that ends the thought (punctuation, end of text, "and", "then", "as in", "like in") or sits next to name context in the same turn, so "with a C corporation" stays quiet; (c) at the decoder gate only, the extracted last name one or two letters from the stored customer's last name, same first letter (one letter for names of four letters or fewer; two-letter names count). Signals (a) and (b) read the primary transcript, so they gate the second pass in `transcribeRecording`; signal (c) needs the extraction, so the processor runs one late second pass on a fresh download of the recording. The download is length-checked like the primary one (a short or missing CDN read runs no pass). Inbound calls only: the name-spelling card never files on an outbound call, so the name-only trigger buys no pass there; the old email/address path is unchanged. Nothing runs when `CONTACT_DICTATION_ENABLED=false`. **Passes per call:** at most one extra pass is paid and used. When the wrapper already tried its pass (even if it returned nothing) the late gate runs only for the near miss, and when the wrapper's pass produced a transcript the late gate never runs. The late pass is saved like the normal one (`transcript_structured.contact_pass_transcript` merged into the current value, plus `contact_pass_model` / `contact_pass_chars` merged into the current metadata, through the token-fenced write); a lost claim abandons the pass and a failed write aborts processing. A late pass that is the first to hear a card number goes through the same `quarantineCardRecording` path (Twilio delete, URL stripped, `pan_detected` and `pan_count` stamped) and decodes nothing. **Cost:** each call the new trigger matches pays one extra transcription pass (`gpt-4o-transcribe` by default) and a decoder call it would not have run. **Measure it:** the log line `[call-proc] spelling collapse trigger (second_pass|decoder): <signal> for <masked sid>` appears only when the new trigger is what buys the pass; a call the old detector already covered logs nothing. The downstream path (decoder, grounding, name-spelling card) is unchanged and still files a card only for a spelling the transcripts hold as a whole letter run. Sends nothing to a customer and writes no name. Off = byte-identical. Rollback: unset the variable.

Commercial assessment booking, no price (dark): `GATE_CALL_COMMERCIAL_ASSESSMENT_BOOKING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callCommercialAssessmentBookingLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; owner ruling 2026-10-06). A commercial Waves Assessment that Waves staff book on the call with NO price discussed auto-books, on OUTBOUND callback calls (`lead_auto_bridge`) as well as inbound, instead of always going to the office (the priced lane above needs a price agreed AND an inbound call, so these always went to the office). It is a mode of the same block in `canAutoRoute` that the priced lane uses and clears ONLY `commercial_requires_quote` (the flag rides `failedOpenFlags`, so the office still gets the advisory card). **What must be on:** `GATE_CALL_COMMERCIAL_ASSESSMENT_BOOKING`, `GATE_CALL_AGENT_COMMIT_BOOKING` (its kill switch) and `GATE_CALL_AGENT_COMMIT_TRUSTED_LABELS`; it does NOT need `GATE_CALL_COMMERCIAL_DICTATED_BOOKING`, and turning it on never opens the priced lane. **No price at all, on every view:** the extraction JUDGES it (schema 1.24.0, prompt v24: `service_request.price_discussed`, over the whole call and both speakers, a bare amount from either side counts; the price_is_final precedent) and the lane requires exactly `false` (true, null or missing goes to the priced path or the office); the code keeps the checks below as an extra fail-closed layer. The V2 extraction has no quoted total, no price entry with an amount, no price judgement at all (a false one counts as price talk; only null means none), and no `quote_requested` / `quote_promised` true; every V1 view (the merged record and the one before V2 adoption) has no quoted price, price amount or entry, and neither `quote_requested` nor `quote_promised`; (while the lane is live the processor persists the V1 pre-adoption price fields as their own `pre_adoption_price_fields` record on the canonical extraction, never inside `pre_adoption_service_fields`; the offline audit holds a V2 row that has no such record, reason `pre_adoption_price_unknown`, and the live lane is unaffected), and no turn of the transcript has a price noun (price, cost, charge, fee, total, quote, rate, pay, payment, invoice, bill, deposit) or a dollar figure, "dollars" or "bucks" ("free" and "no charge" are not price talk; "estimate" and "quoted" count); and no AGENT-labeled turn carries any number at all, digits or number words, so a bare amount ("it'll be 149", "one forty-nine") also goes to the priced path (caller turns are not screened; the only exemption is the recorded hour, day and period words and ordinal dates of the grounded slot turn itself) (`priceDiscussed` in `server/services/call-commercial-dictated-booking.js`); any price sends the call to the priced lane, unchanged. **The service:** every view of the call's service (the V1 record before V2 adoption, the merged fields, the V2 booking view; `commercialAssessmentBookableFor` in `call-recording-processor.js`, the same views the priced lane's catalog check reads) must resolve to the Waves Assessment catalog row (`isAssessmentServiceRow`, `server/services/assessment-booking.js`); it books at the catalog price. **The agreement** is grounded exactly as in the priced lane (`groundNewBookingAgreement`: the staff commitment and the caller's acceptance word for word in the right speaker's turns), plus one more shape that only this lane reads (`allowAgentProposed`): STAFF propose the one exact day and on-the-hour time ("How does noon on Thursday sound?"), the caller's very next turn accepts it as a whole ("Perfect."), and staff's very next turn commits without a slot of its own ("I'll book you for that, and we'll see you then"). The extraction's `agent_committed_booking` stayed null for that shape (its rule wants one agent sentence that states both the day and the time), so while this gate is on the extraction prompt carries an extra per-call block for it (rendered only while the gate is on, and the persisted `ai_extraction_prompt_version` gets an `a` cohort mark inside its leading version token then (`v22a-<hash>-cat.<hash>`, 30 characters; its hash is taken from the gate-on prompt, so any edit to the gated text changes it, and the readiness section matches only the exact live gate-on catalog version; the columns are varchar(30), so a suffix would overflow), so those calls are their own cohort (`v2-promotion-readiness.js` keeps its main cohort on the unsuffixed versions exactly as before and, while the gate is on, runs the SAME checks (schema pass rate, routing agreement, consent, phantom routes, fallback leg) on the `-aps` rows alone, first, and its main verdict requires that run to pass too; gate off: output identical to before); the block is for NEW bookings only and never overrides the reschedule rule, and the lane refuses any extraction that names an existing appointment being moved; off = the prompt and its version are byte-identical). **Outbound eligibility, what must be on for an outbound call:** the three gates above PLUS `GATE_CALL_OUTBOUND_BOOKING` and V2 routing in enforce mode (`CALL_EXTRACTION_V2_ENABLED=true` and `CALL_EXTRACTION_V2_DRIVES_ROUTING=true` or `CALL_TRIAGE_ENFORCE_V2_GATES=true`), the same prerequisites the processor's outbound creation path needs (`outboundAutoBookingEnabled`, one predicate for routing, creation and the audits); this gate never authorizes outbound creation by itself. An outbound call qualifies only as a lead callback bridge (the server-written call `metadata.type` is `lead_auto_bridge`); any other outbound call stays excluded, inbound always qualifies, and the live lanes and the audit builder read the same predicate (`commercialAssessmentBookingActive`). **Outbound proof:** speaker labels are LLM-inferred and have swapped on outbound recordings, and recordings are single-channel, so an outbound call also needs staff identity from the words: an Agent-labeled turn opens with a plain first-person "this is <name> with|from|at Waves" (optional greeting first; not a question, a negation or reported speech) and no Caller-labeled turn says it anywhere (`outboundStaffIdentityProven`); otherwise it holds (`outbound_staff_identity_unproven`). The proof sits inside the grounding function, so the live lane, the shadow pass and the audit reconstruction share ONE predicate. The confirmed on-the-hour start, capacity, address validation, unit checks and every other hold still apply. Off = byte-identical, outbound stays excluded. Rollback: unset the variable.

Whole-structure calls, no unit hold (dark): `GATE_CALL_WHOLE_STRUCTURE_NO_UNIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at process start through `isEnabled('callWholeStructureNoUnit')` (owner ruling 2026-09-30, call-booker gates review item 7). On, a call whose resolved service is on the explicit allowlist in `call-triage-flags.js` (`wdo_inspection`, `termite_pretreatment`, `termite_slab_pretreat`, `termite_trenching`, `termite_liquid`; the call must resolve a bookable catalog row with one of those keys, a coarse label alone never waives) is not held on `address_unverified` when Google's ONLY complaint is the missing unit number (a duplex or building-level job). `wholeStructureUnitWaiverForCall` (`call-recording-processor.js`) rewrites the in-memory Address Validation verdict once, after the shadow row persisted the original, so the enforce gate, the shadow bridge and the audit all read one verdict. Never waived: any other address problem (other missing component, out of area or unknown county, unconfirmed or replaced components), a property typed anything but single_family / multi_family / townhouse / mobile_home, condo or apartment wording in the call, commercial or HOA common-area calls (they still hold on `commercial_requires_quote`), or any service off the list (interior pest, bed bugs, spot/foam termite, a unit-level inspection). An open `missing_unit_number` card from an earlier pass of the same call keeps the hold (that card is a human verdict nothing auto-resolves). The waiver is judged on the V1 service before V2-primary adoption, at the gate, and as the approved booking will book it; the pass stamps `wholeStructureUnitWaived` on the persisted `ai_address_validation` so the promotion audits rebuild the verdict. Off = byte-identical (the same verdict object). No gate-specific decision tag: the base version `v2-1.50.0` stands and the route_decisions write refreshes the decision on conflict.

Business whole building, no unit hold (dark): `GATE_CALL_BUSINESS_WHOLE_BUILDING_NO_UNIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at process start through `isEnabled('callBusinessWholeBuildingNoUnit')` (owner ruling 2026-10-06; the owner accepted the risk of a strip-mall caller who has a suite). On, a call whose Address Validation verdict is "PREMISE resolved, only subpremise missing" is not held on `address_unverified` / `missing_unit_number` when ALL of these hold: Google's `addressUse.business` is true and `residential` is false (unknown residential keeps the hold); the V2 `property.property_type` is `commercial`; the V2 extraction judged BOTH `property.whole_building_occupancy` true (the caller states they own, bought, lease or occupy the ENTIRE building) AND `property.whole_building_occupancy_final` true (schema 1.23.0, prompt v23: over the WHOLE call the caller never hedged about occupying the whole building, never corrected it to a floor / suite / space / storefront / side, never shared it with another tenant, and the claim was neither a question nor a condition); the pinned quote (`/property/whole_building_occupancy`, speaker `caller`) is word for word inside a CALLER turn of a fully labeled two-speaker transcript; and the QUOTE TEXT itself carries no negation, hedge, uncertainty (I think / probably / maybe / might / may / should be / kind of / not sure ...), open condition or question (punctuation or an opener like "do we" / "is it"). **The extraction judges the language, the code only verifies the pinned quote** (owner ruling 2026-10-01; the same design as `service_request.price_is_final` in `call-commercial-dictated-booking.js`, #5377): a chatty caller turn with a hedge about a side detail ("I think the owner bought it a couple weeks ago, but we're just moving in") is NOT rejected by word lists. Two hard vetoes remain, for EXPLICIT signals only: a unit designator followed by a number or letter (suite 4, ste 12, unit B, bay 3, apt 2B, # 12) in any CALLER turn, and strip mall / plaza / shopping center / mall / office, business or industrial park / office, apartment or business complex wording in any turn. On an OUTBOUND call whose labels look swapped (a Caller-labeled turn opens with a staff self-introduction "this is <name> with|from|at Waves" and no Agent-labeled turn does) the roles are swapped before grounding; both or neither introducing keeps the raw labels (`orientTranscriptForOutbound`, direction threaded from the processor and the audits). `applyBusinessWholeBuildingUnitWaiver` (`call-triage-flags.js`) is the pure rule and `businessWholeBuildingUnitWaiverForCall` (`call-recording-processor.js`) calls it at the same site, behind the same open-`missing_unit_number`-card guard, as the whole-structure waiver (that rule runs first); no service allowlist, inbound and outbound alike. The pass stamps the same `wholeStructureUnitWaived` marker plus `reason: 'business_whole_building'` on the persisted `ai_address_validation`, so `reconstructWaivedAddressValidation` and the audits rebuild the verdict (the replay and shadow-path audits recompute the rule against a fresh extraction's own fields, pin and the transcript through `waiverCarriesToCandidate` instead of carrying the waiver over on matching scalar inputs; the whole-structure waiver keeps its scalar-input transfer). Not waived: any other address problem, a residential or mixed-use verdict, a non-commercial property type, a missing or ungrounded quote, `whole_building_occupancy_final` not true. The commercial quote rule (`commercial_requires_quote`) and every other hold still apply. Off = byte-identical (the same verdict object); the schema bump to 1.23.0 and prompt v23 are additive and start a new shadow cohort. Rollback: unset the variable.

Call-address route-spelling retry (dark): `GATE_CALL_ROUTE_SPELLING_RETRY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `callRouteSpellingRetryLive()` (owner 2026-10-03, "do a small fix pr"). On, street recovery (`server/services/address-validation/recovery.js`) first makes ONE extra Address Validation request when the spoken street names a numbered state, US or county route in a non-canonical order ("14360 East State Road 64" → "14360 SR 64 E", via the property lookup's `normalizeCountyStreetLine`). The verdict is adopted (`recovery_method: route_spelling`, advisory `address_recovered` read-back card) only when Google accepts a premise with the spoken house number, the caller's ZIP or city, and a street that reduces to the same route key. A bare "Highway N", a street line that carries a unit, and a line already in canonical order are not retried. Off, recovery is byte-identical. Rollback: unset the variable.

Call first-name advisory (dark): `GATE_CALL_FIRST_NAME_ADVISORY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callFirstNameAdvisoryLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; owner ruling 2026-10-02). On, a caller who gave only a last name still becomes a customer when the call has a phone, is not a voicemail or non-customer nature, and has a validated in-service-area premise address (`customers.first_name` is NOT NULL, so it is stored as `''`); `validatePhoneCallAppointmentCustomer` treats a missing first name as advisory like the last name, and a `missing_first_name` (`name_review`) card asks the office for it. Greetings fall back to "there" (`getTemplate`, the call confirmation, `automation-runner`). Off, byte-identical to before.

Promised reschedule link (dark): `GATE_RESCHEDULE_LINK_ON_PROMISE` (`shadow` | `true`, needs `GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS` on too) — when the agent promises to text a caller a link to move an appointment they already have, the worker (`server/services/reschedule-link-promises.js`) texts the actual `/reschedule/:token` link once the promise's own grounding checks (subject, date, channel) and the visit's own self-service eligibility all clear; `shadow` records what it would have sent without texting anyone. `RESCHEDULE_LINK_PROMISE_ACTIVATED_AT` (an ISO instant), when set, is the live-activation boundary and always wins: GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS keeps extracting these commitments regardless of this gate, so a bare flip with no boundary set would otherwise stage days of pre-existing history as live sends the moment it goes on. Unset, the boundary is READ FROM `system_settings` (key `reschedule_link_promise_activated_at`) — never this process's own start time, which would move the boundary forward on every restart and cancel a commitment created between the last sweep and a routine deploy. The first live sweep anywhere to find nothing stored writes `now()` there; every sweep after, on this process or any future one, reads the same instant back. A commitment recorded before the boundary is cancelled with `last_error: 'pre_activation'` and raises no card — a historical observation, not a live promise to keep. The boundary is established and enforced ONLY in live mode (`true`): `shadow` never reads or writes the stored value and never cancels anything as pre_activation, since it only observes — establishing the boundary during a shadow trial would fix it weeks before anyone actually went live. Date selection uses persisted `subject.date_claims` (current appointment, requested new date, delivery timing, or unresolved); legacy/incomplete claims park for review until re-extracted. `call_commitments.due_type` distinguishes a delivery floor from a deadline; missing types and human-edited times remain floors.

Automatic booking-link text after a call (owner ruling 2026-09-26): `GATE_CALL_BOOKING_LINK_TEXT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`** (also requires `GATE_LEAD_INSPECTION_LINK` live). A NEW lead — not an existing customer, inbound or an outbound return call to someone who contacted us first — who wanted someone to come out (look at a problem, an in-person quote, or a recurring plan) and ended a real two-way conversation with nothing booked gets the existing free-consultation `/inspection/:token` link (`lead-consultation-link.js`, unchanged) texted 2 hours later, or at 8 AM ET the next morning for a call ending at/after 6 PM ET — staff get the first shot at a callback. `server/services/call-booking-link-text.js` stages every V2-extracted call once, stamping the decision on `call_log.metadata.call_booking_link_text`: a lead linkage, `call_nature`, residential/in-service-area, `service_intent`, and the V2 `triage_flags` enum together stand in for the owner's never-list (commercial, a third-party caller, an explicit refusal/DNC/STOP suppression/disclaimed number/non-consented spoken destination — a bare missing opt-in to the caller's own number is fine, owner ruling 2026-09-28 — an already-promised quote, …); `call_log.customer_id` alone is NOT "an existing customer" — the legacy call-created-customer path mints a customers row directly for a first-time caller and stamps `metadata.created_customer_id` alongside `customer_id` in the same transaction, so only a `customer_id` that PREDATES this call (no matching marker) counts as the owner's already-a-customer never-rule; an outbound call additionally needs the shared `hasPriorContact` probe (`outbound-call-reason.js`) to confirm real prior contact before the call started — a qualifying inbound call or text, a non-call customer-originated lead, or a customer that predates the call; manual and cold-call-created leads never count (a cold outbound dial to a lead THIS call just minted is never a "return call to someone who contacted us first," whatever the transcript's content classifies as). Staging waits until the row has gone quiet — `processing_token IS NULL` and `updated_at` past a short grace window, not `created_at` (which is fixed at ring time and can already be stale for a long call) — so a sweep can never catch the row between `v2_extraction_status` flipping valid and a separate lead-linkage write landing. Staging also only considers calls that STARTED at or after this lane's own first live activation (mirrors `reschedule-link-promises.js`'s `activationBoundary`: `system_settings` key `call_booking_link_text_activated_at`, env override `CALL_BOOKING_LINK_TEXT_ACTIVATED_AT`) — flipping the gate on never picks up days of pre-existing valid-but-unstaged calls and texts them all in one burst; staging also skips a call outright (`stale_at_staging`, terminal, logged in its own metadata like every other staging skip) when its computed send_at is already more than 60 minutes in the past at the moment staging looks at it — an off→on re-enable, long worker/deploy downtime, or a genuine processing backlog is never a reason to burst-text a pile of hours-stale follow-ups the instant staging catches up, while a call from an ordinary short gap (its send_at still ahead) stages and sends on schedule. The cap applies ONLY at staging; a call already staged and deferred at dispatch time (outside the send window, a retryable send outcome) keeps its own advancing send_at and the separate 24h original_send_at bound. A 5-minute cron sweep (`scheduler.js`, same cadence as `reschedule-link-promises`) claims and dispatches whatever delay has elapsed, re-checking every condition fresh — the call's OWN current lead linkage still matching what was staged (an attribution correction/merge since staging skips rather than silently restaging), booked since the call, the lead no longer open, an estimate linked (`leads.estimate_id` — a priced job keeps its own Book button), and an actual SMS delivery (not just a link mint) to this lead in the last 14 days — before minting the link and sending through the canonical `sendCustomerMessage` (`purpose: 'missed_call_followup'`, `audience: 'lead'`), so the existing STOP/consent pipeline and `buildLeadConsultationSmsLine`'s own STOP-line template apply unchanged. Landing outside the 8 AM–8 PM ET window at dispatch time re-queues as 'pending' at the next window open rather than losing the send. Every terminal send-time decision (sent or skipped) also gets an `activity_log` row; the much larger stage-time "not eligible at all" population lives only in the call's own metadata. This lane never touches call routing/disposition and reads no V2_DECISION_VERSION-gated field for its OWN decisions. Immediately before the actual provider request, the send-time recheck (`neverSendRecheck`) locks the `leads` row FOR UPDATE, then the `call_log` row FOR UPDATE (same order the call processor's own writers use — its own `leads` → `call_log` order, never reversed), and re-runs readiness/lead-linkage/never-send checks against that fresh, locked row — closing a race where a forced reprocess could reclassify the call mid-handoff. The one durable pre-provider marker this creates lives in its own table, `call_booking_link_text_handoffs` (migration `20260927160000`, keyed by `call_log_id`), not on `call_log` itself — a marker on that row would deadlock against the row lock the handoff now also holds; `recoverAbandonedClaim`/`recoverStaleClaims` read that table to tell a pre-handoff crash (safe to retry) from a post-handoff one (ambiguous, never resent), and a live sweep prunes rows older than 7 days.

Consultation page reuses the lead's own intake profile (owner 2026-10-31): `GATE_INSPECTION_REUSE_LEAD_SHELL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`inspectionReuseLeadShellLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = off = kill, no redeploy) by `resolveOrLinkCustomerForLead` in `server/routes/inspection-public.js`. Before this gate, every web-form (unverified) lead that booked its consultation got a second customer row (`lead_source` 'lead_pipeline'), because the page never trusts `leads.customer_id` for an unverified contact; in October that made 8 duplicate pairs. On: the booking lands on the lead's linked customer only when it is provably the lead's OWN untouched intake profile (`leadOwnIntakeShell`): active, `new_lead`, created at most 10 minutes before the lead, this lead the first live lead on it, no billing, visit, login or merge history (`loserAutoBlockers`, merge journal), the same full phone identity and email as the lead, no other lead's consultation provenance naming it, the primary and only live profile of its own account, a complete stored street, city and ZIP, and the same unit as the booked address (shared normalizer `unitLineValueKey`; no unit stored vs "Apt 4" booked is not the same); a profile filed under another household's account, a partial address, a stored street that affirmatively differs from the booked address, a busy comms fence, or an unsettled location falls back to the old new-prospect path. The reuse writes an outright `consultation_prospect` provenance row and changes nothing on the profile except to fill missing map coordinates (as every reused profile does). Off = every unverified lead books onto its own new prospect, as before. Sends nothing to a customer.

Review asks in the technician's voice (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_TECH_VOICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `isEnabled('reviewAskTechVoice')` (owner rulings 2026-09-30 / 10-01: no general review texts). On, every review-cadence TEXT, the Day-0 SMS included (the fixed `day0_ask` control steps aside), is drafted by `review-ask-drafter.js` `draftTechVoice` in the voice of the technician who did the visit, from the visit's service report (recap, the customer's concern, observations, conversation notes, tech tips; never the treated-areas list, products or billing), the customer's texts, calls and transcripts, the customer's own emails (their own words only: quoted history, signatures and inherited "Re:" subjects cut by `email/email-strip.js`), and the messages this cadence already sent. Two SMS segments allowed; every ask says "Google review". The model cites the record line behind each detail and `verifyTechVoiceDraft` rejects a draft whose cited line is not in that record or shares no words with the detail it cites, a pest, part of the property or problem named anywhere in the text that the record never mentions, any repair, result or outcome claim (fixed, sealed, solved, gone, reduced, better, settling, working, "took care of"), any health or money topic (surgery, illness, rent, bills, payments — even when the record holds it), or promise / future visit ("I'll", "be back", "next time", "tomorrow", "appointment") — both refused outright, since word matching cannot tell a request or an observation from finished work and the writer sees no verified schedule, a capitalized name absent from the customer's own words and the report, a satisfaction condition or reply-instead-of-review steer, office phrasing, termites on a non-termite visit, or any existing compliance rule. A draft that passes is then fact-checked (owner ruling 2026-10-01): a second model on `TEXT_POLICIES.fastStructured` (switchboard lane `review_ask_fact_check`) quotes the record line behind EVERY sentence, the record shown without anything Waves texted or this cadence already sent, and also marks any sentence touching an off-limits topic as a class (health, money, products/chemicals, who was home or let the tech in — refused even when record-backed), and code confirms each verdict names the sentence being sent, each quote is in the record, and a sentence marked a bare review request holds nothing but request words; an unbacked sentence or a malformed answer is a rejection, and an unavailable checker sends nothing drafted. One redraft, then the fixed template. A cadence with no visit of its own (the admin page's manual start-sequence) sends the fixed copy with no AI call. History is scoped to the visit (30 days before through the visit day); only the customer's own texts, labeled caller turns and authenticated emails from their own address count as their words. Review EMAIL touches keep the fixed company-voice email under the switch (owner ruling 2026-10-02: a tech-voice email with its own closing and sign-off comes later). Recorded as `<template>_tech_voice`. Holds (owner rulings 2026-10-01; each recorded on the sequence with its reason, `decision.detail` carrying what it saw): a drafted later text that repeats an earlier touch of the cadence (same subject or question, judged by `TEXT_POLICIES.fastStructured`, lane `review_ask_repeat_check`; code confirms the sentence is in the draft and the quote in an earlier touch) is HELD, never reworded: nothing is sent and the cadence moves to its next step (`ask_held_repeat`); an unavailable or unconfirmed check sends the fixed template. Before an ask, `review-ask-holds.js` holds the ask while the customer has an open overdue bill of their own (`open-balance.js` `openBalanceInvoices`, overdue by `account-anchor.js` `invoiceDaysOverdue`) or an overdue-payment reminder went out in the last 3 days (`dunning-spacing.js` `lastOverdueReminderWithin7d`, any row not a confirmed failure; a failed read holds); `askHold` decides, the runner applies it: it is retried daily (or when the reminder's 3 days end) and dropped after 3 days from the first hold (`payment_hold` → `ask_dropped_payment_hold`). Every writer outcome (drafted with the record lines the fact check cited per sentence, held as a repeat, or the reason it fell back to the fixed text) is recorded in `review_ask_drafts` (migration `20261003010000`, written by `draftTechVoice` and, for a dropped payment hold, the runner, both through `review-ask-drafts.js`, best effort) and shown with the cadences waiting on a payment hold on the Reviews page's Outreach → Tech-voice texts tab (`GET /api/admin/review-requests/tech-voice-drafts?days=`, admin only; newest 200, `truncated` says when the window holds more; a text counts as sent by its request's stamp or the sender's own delivery evidence). Off = today's personalized drafter (`GATE_REVIEW_ASK_PERSONALIZED`) and the fixed Day-0 ask, byte-identical, and no hold is read.

Fixed same-day review text (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_FIXED_DAY0` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `isEnabled('reviewAskFixedDay0')`, and only matters while `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_TECH_VOICE` is on (owner 2026-10-22, "fixed line for all"). On, the SMS Day-0 and day-after review touch in `review-ask-drafter.js` sends one fixed line with no model call: "Hi <first>, it's <tech first name> from Waves. Thanks for having us out today. A Google review would really help: {review_url}" (no first name = "Hi,"; no tech = "it's Waves Pest Control"; day-after drops "today"). Why: the writer recited report findings ("a moderate level of cockroach activity" from the activity gauge label), read customers' words back, and had only booking talk to work with. Follow-up texts keep the tech-voice writer; review emails stay the fixed company-voice email, as before. A same-day AI draft saved before the flip is never reused on a retry (`review-request.js` retry reuse skips step 0 under this gate). Off = today's writer, unchanged. Rollback: unset the variable.
Exact quotes for the review-text fact check (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_EXACT_QUOTES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `isEnabled('reviewAskExactQuotes')`, and only matters while `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_TECH_VOICE` is on (owner 2026-10-05, closing #5893: "prompts" — fix it in the prompts, keep the code checks as they are). On, three things change in `review-ask-drafter.js`: the fact checker is asked for the bare words of one record line for each claim (no "Visit report:" label, source name, date, quotation marks or "..."; it often answered with such a frame, which is not in the record, so a true sentence fell back to the fixed text); the writer is asked to say each fact in its source's own words; and a cited quote held by several record lines is dated by the newest data line that holds it (the thread is oldest first, so words a customer sent twice were dated by the older message and a true "today" was refused); one line per quote either way, so its date, weekday and time of day come from the same message. Not gated: a number in a sentence or a cited detail (digits, or two through twelve as a word) must be in its quote, so "I treated 2 mounds" never rides on "We treated 3 mounds" (this only refuses more drafts; a refused draft falls back to the fixed text). Off = today's prompts and dating. Rollback: unset the variable.

Review ask after the report (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_AFTER_REPORT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `reviewAskAfterReportLive()` in `feature-gates.js` (owner ruling 2026-10-22). On, the Automatic same-day (Day 0) review-ask text is due `REVIEW_AFTER_REPORT_DELAY_MINUTES` (10) after the report text, for every service line (pest, lawn, mosquito, tree and shrub, WDO, the rest), instead of the smart send window. `enrollPostService` takes a `reportTextAnchor` `{ status, at }`: `sent` = max(now, send time) + 10 min; `paid` (an unpaid completion invoice holds the ask, the 10 minutes run from the payment) = now + 10 min. Only a completion text that went out as a text (SMS/MMS) at completion anchors the ask (`reportTextAnchorFromNotes`: `completionSmsStatus` `sent`, no `completionSmsDeferredTo`, not routed to the customer App). A report the 8 AM-8 PM window held for the morning enrolls on the smart window; when its replay is accepted as a text (SMS/MMS, known on the replay's first pass), `pullAskAfterHeldReport` (from the `dispatch_completion_deferred` finalize hook) re-plans the untouched Day-0 ask still planned on that window (decision `smart_window`, not customer-requested, not claimed) to 10 minutes after the delivery (a recovered finalize-only retry passes the stored acceptance time, `sms_log.created_at`; never in the past), in one conditional write (earlier, or later when a delayed replay leaves less than 10 minutes). The channel is the replay's own on the first pass, or read from the accepted Twilio SID (`SM…`/`MM…`) on a finalize-only retry, so crash recovery applies it too; a re-run finds the row already `after_report` and does nothing. It also needs `GATE_REVIEW_SEQUENCES`. The sender also enforces the floor itself: it holds such an ask (untouched Day-0 `smart_window`, enrolled under 24 h ago) while its record's `completionSmsStatus` is still `deferred` (re-check every 5 minutes) and until 10 minutes after `completionSmsDeferredDeliveredAt` (not after an App replay: the finalize stamps the replay's channel as `sentSmsChannel`, and `push` keeps the smart window), with the reason kept `smart_window`, so worker downtime or a pull that lost the lock race cannot send it right after its report. A replay to the customer App (no SID), no provider proof, or a decision another deferral rewrote leaves the smart window. A combined-visit summary held by quiet hours anchors to its 8 AM text (the replay is a plain text, and the packet enrollment waits for it); when an unpaid invoice holds that enrollment until a later payment, the ask goes 10 minutes after the payment, the same as a report texted at completion (the summary is a confirmed text either way). Every other report keeps the smart send window, exactly as with the gate off: one sent by the Waves app, failed, blocked, skipped, no phone, not requested or unknown; a single-visit paid invoice whose held report already went out before the payment (its replay channel is not stored, so it is not a confirmed text at payment time). The packet path anchors on its `completion_sms` visit effect when it is `sent`; an email-only completion keeps the smart window. **Cadence mode only (needs `GATE_REVIEW_SEQUENCES`):** the legacy (cadence-off) path ignores this gate entirely — no anchor, no +10, the caller's old default (120) as before — and the send-time preview reports `afterReport: false` there. The ask goes at the first `:14`/`:44` review send on or after that time (so about 10 to 40 minutes after the report text); a target after 8 PM waits for the 8 AM window, as every review text does. No new cron. Unchanged: the 8 AM-8 PM `GATE_SMS_SEND_WINDOW` hold, 72 h ask spacing, click guard, manual-ask-recent, ask holds, opt-outs, and every explicit operator timing (Tomorrow 8 AM, custom time, customer asked for the link), which still wins. The completion panel's Automatic hint (`GET /admin/reviews/send-time-preview`, `afterReport: true`) names the first `:14`/`:44` send at least 10 minutes after the report text, that a target after 8 PM waits for the morning, and that any report not texted right away keeps the smart send window. Off = new enrollments use the smart window exactly as before; an ask already planned by the gate keeps its planned time (at most about 10 minutes after its enrollment). Kill switch: unset it (`server/services/review-request.js`).

First review ask lock (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_FIRST_ASK_LOCK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `reviewFirstAskLockLive()` in `feature-gates.js` (owner ruling 2026-10-26, "YES GO", option B; unset = kill, no redeploy). A customer is "never asked" when no `review_requests` row has `sms_sent_at` or `sent_at` set and `customers.has_left_google_review` is not true (`ReviewService.customerNeverAskedForReview`, the one reader). On, for a never-asked customer: the Complete Service panel and the Fast Complete Wrap-up label the review box "First review ask", start it on and keep it on (`GET /api/admin/reviews/send-time-preview?serviceId=` adds `firstReviewAsk`, a re-service visit is always false); the tech can turn it off only by confirming the one reason "Complaint on site" (body key `reviewOptOutReason: 'complaint_on_site'`). The server enforces it where a completion saves the review choice (`complete-scheduled-service.js`, through `ReviewService.firstAskLockChoice`, and the visit-closeout packet's enrollment check; `PUT /admin/schedule/:id/status`, which no UI completes through and which carries no reason, keeps the posted choice): an explicit `requestReview: false` on a completed visit stays on unless the reason rides along, and the record's structured notes get `reviewFirstAskLock: { neverAsked, forcedOn, optOutReason }`. Left as before: asked-before and already-reviewed customers, re-service (`is_callback`) visits, the fixed re-service text, backdated and system closeouts, incomplete, concern and declined visits, a sheet that pins every customer text off, the ask text, timing, quiet hours, cap and cooldown, the unpaid or void invoice hold and the 09-07 invoice-closeout quiet rule. Off = byte-identical: no extra query, no new response key, no new record key. On, a visit where a tech used to switch the ask off now sends a review ask to a customer, so the owner flips it. Kill: unset.

Review sender every 5 minutes (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_SENDER_EVERY_5_MIN` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at boot into the gates map as `reviewSenderEvery5Min` (the Railway restart applies it; owner ruling 2026-10-22, "faster"). The review cadence sender (`processReviewSequences`, the `review-sequences` job) runs on every fifth minute of its own offset (:04, :09, :14 ... :59) instead of :14/:44 only. The cron is registered on those twelve minutes either way (an explicit list: node-cron 3 reads `4-59/5` as minutes divisible by 5); its body runs only on the minutes `reviewCadenceTickMinutes()` names (a callback pushed past its minute still counts), so the Reviews page ticks and the completion panel preview (`cadenceTickMinutesOfHour`) always match the runs. Same job, same lock, same 25-row batch, so nothing runs side by side. With `GATE_REVIEW_ASK_AFTER_REPORT` the Day-0 ask goes about 10 to 15 minutes after the report text; every other due row (Tomorrow 8 AM, a custom time, Day 3/4) also goes within 5 minutes of being due. The 8 AM-8 PM window, spacing, holds and opt-outs are unchanged. Off = :14/:44 exactly as before. Kill switch: unset it (`server/services/review-request.js`, `server/services/scheduler.js`).

Tech visit notifications: `GATE_TECH_VISIT_NOTIFICATIONS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = live kill). On, the assigned field technician gets a tech-home card plus a one-line push when a visit is assigned to them, taken off them, moved, or cancelled (`server/services/tech-visit-notifications.js`, hung on `assignDispatchJob`, the rebooker's single-visit move, and `transitionJobStatus` → cancelled). Staff-only, never a customer channel; silent for the actor's own change and for non-assignable recipients. Route-order shuffles and series-scope moves are deliberately not covered.

Auto-dispatch summary push: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_PUSH_SUMMARY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill; needs `GATE_TECH_VISIT_NOTIFICATIONS` on too). On, an auto-dispatch run's visit cards are still written one per visit, but their per-visit pushes are held and the run sends ONE push per tech after it finishes: "Auto-dispatch moved N visits", opening `/admin/today` (owner ruling 2026-10-03). Off, every auto-dispatch move pushes on its own, as before; turned off mid-run, moves already held still get that run's one summary push (their own push never went out). Read in `server/services/tech-visit-notifications.js` (`deliver`, `pushAutoDispatchSummary`), called from `server/services/auto-dispatch/index.js` after `completeRun`.

Auto-dispatch far double bookings quiet: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_FAR_CONFLICT_QUIET` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill; `server/services/auto-dispatch/needs-person-notice.js`). Owner 2026-10-22 (auto-dispatch audit D1). On, a visit the nightly run leaves in conflict (an overlap or a closed day) more than 14 days out does not ring: it is a line on one standing Activity row (ops digest `auto-dispatch-far-conflicts`, audience fyi: the Agents Activity feed, never the bell, outside the shared 10-a-day ring allowance) that the run refreshes and that retires on a run with none. Within 14 days the conflict rings as the ordinary needs-a-person notice. The list changes only after a complete conflict scan, keeps a conflict until its ordinary notice stands, and its visits are re-read each run even when the scan no longer loads them. A near conflict on the list (its notice waits for the allowance or a retry) is titled "not alerted yet", never "more than 2 weeks out"; an internal test customer's conflict is never listed. Needs the in-app Activity feed (`GATE_OPS_DIGESTS_IN_APP` + `GATE_AGENT_ACTIVITY`); without it, and with the gate off, every conflict rings as before, and a list left from before keeps only the conflicts whose notice is not written yet, then retires. Sends nothing to a customer; never emails.

Bundled tech pushes: `GATE_TECH_PUSH_BUNDLE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill; needs `GATE_TECH_VISIT_NOTIFICATIONS` on too). On, a visit change from any mover other than auto-dispatch (which keeps its own run summary above, and pushes per visit when that summary is off) still writes its card at once, but its push is held; an every-minute sweep sends each tech ONE push once no new change has landed for 60 seconds, or once the oldest has waited 5 minutes (a crash mid-send adds at most the 3-minute claim lease). Per visit it announces only a change that still stands and that the tech has not cleared, re-read right before sending; a change in between composes the push again on the next tick. One visit gets that visit's usual push; more get one count, e.g. "17 visits on your route moved", opening `/admin/today` (owner 2026-10-22: "the dispatch alerts need to be bundled in one alert"). A failed push is retried each minute, and a card is dropped after an hour of failures. Off, every change pushes on its own, as before; cards held before a flip still go out on the next sweep. Cost: a single change reaches the tech about 1 to 2 minutes later. Read in `server/services/tech-visit-notifications.js` (`deliver`, `flushBundledPushes`); the sweep is in `server/services/scheduler.js`, registered before the `GATE_CRON_JOBS` return so held pushes go out whether or not cron jobs run.

Auto-dispatch move-check-down notice: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_CHECK_DOWN_NOTICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill). On, a nightly run in which the AI move check was asked and no answer could be used (every check broke: the provider refused, timed out or rejected the key, an answer could not be read, or a read failed) raises ONE System notice, "System — restore the auto-dispatch move check", naming the cause and how many planned moves stayed put. It rings once per outage (a later broken night rewrites it quietly) and closes itself the first night a check answers; a later outage rings again. A dry run, or a night the tool does not run, changes nothing (only a usable answer proves the check works again); the reopen goes through `admin-alert-episodes.raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`, under the key's lock. One ring per outage, counted in the auto-dispatch ring allowance but never held back by it (owner audit 2026-10-22, finding 1: Oct 15-19 the tool moved nothing for five nights and no notice named it). Off, or the check off: a standing notice closes, also on nights auto-dispatch does not run (the scheduler's gate-off upkeep path). Read in `server/services/auto-dispatch/check-down-notice.js`, called from `server/services/auto-dispatch/index.js` at the run's end; the tally (`answered`, `brokeCause`) is kept in `proofreader/nightly.js`.

Plan visits on a taken hour: `GATE_PLAN_TAKEN_HOUR_HANDOFF` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill; `server/services/scheduling/plan-taken-hour.js`). Owner 2026-10-22 (auto-dispatch audit D4). On, the plan writers that copy the plan's hour onto a new visit — the follow-up seeder (`recurring-appointment-seeder.js` `seedFollowUpsForParent`) and the series extensions (`routes/admin-schedule.js` `cadenceSlotHandoffFields`: the nightly top-up and the completion-time extend through `walkExtensionCandidates`, and the plan-alert extend/convert actions) — write a visit whose hour another stop already holds WITHOUT a time, with its date as `recurring_dispatch_due_date`, so auto-dispatch places it within three days of that date (the hand-off shape a series move gives a deferred occurrence). Only four or more days out; nearer visits keep the hour as before. "Taken" is the night tool's own double-booking rule: the shared plan-writer probe (`window-rules.js` `seriesCandidateDateClashRows`, tech-blind until the schedule is technician-scoped) with the move writer's statuses (no cancelled, skipped, no-show, rescheduled or completed row) and the owner's booked interviews, where the same customer's row counts unless it is at the same place as the new visit itself (its own address with the plan's template address applied, as the insert gets it; `auto-dispatch/current-conflict.js` `samePlaceIdsAt`). Each extension reads the visit's technician once and inserts with it. Off: no hand-off read and no hand-off; an extension still books its cadence date, logging the overlap. Sends nothing to a customer. Gate on or off, a series extension never skips a cadence date because another visit is in the slot.

Call follow-up on a free hour: `GATE_CALL_FOLLOWUP_FREE_HOUR` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill; `server/services/scheduling/plan-taken-hour.js` `callFollowUpWindow`, called from `call-recording-processor.js` `ensureCallFollowUpVisit`). Owner 2026-10-22 ("fix", after a call follow-up landed on another customer's 10 AM). The call pipeline's visit 2 copies visit 1's hour when the call set no time. On, when that hour is taken on visit 2's date (the same rule as `GATE_PLAN_TAKEN_HOUR_HANDOFF`: the night tool's own double-booking rule), visit 2 takes the nearest whole hour that day where its whole span fits the shift (8 AM to the 6 PM close) and no other stop holds any of it, the later of two equally near hours; with none it keeps the copied one. The span is the planned window, or the job's estimated duration when longer: a moved visit 2 is written with that span, so a long job is never squeezed into one hour. The night tool does not place one-off visits, so the hour is chosen at booking. A time set on the call, and a two-treatment package's visit 2 (visit 1's time, owner 2026-10-04), keep theirs.
