The check runs after the call booking's fence on visit 2's date (`occupancy.js` `fenceBookingDay`), so two fenced call bookings cannot pick the same free hour; a missed fence reads unfenced, as the insert already does. The reads run in their own savepoint: a failed read keeps the copied hour and never fails the booking. The idempotency key stays on the copied hour. Visit 2 stays pending for the office to confirm, as before. Off: no read, byte-identical. Sends nothing to a customer.

Tech out today (dark): `GATE_TECH_OUT_REDISTRIBUTE` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time (unset = kill; off, `/api/admin/tech-out/*` answers 404 `{enabled:false}` and the drawer section hides). On, a dispatcher marks a technician out for a date from the dispatch-board tech drawer (`server/services/tech-out.js`, `technician_absences` row, reasons sick / emergency / no_show / other) and every open stop on that tech-day (en_route included, on_site left alone, uncommitted estimate holds — no customer + `reservation_expires_at` — skipped; a grouped visit is ONE unit) is parked as a `tech_out_overflow` dispatch alert ranked "bump first" (recurring `is_recurring` before one-time, unconfirmed before confirmed, later window first; a grouped unit ranks by its MOST protected member; `payload.bump_order` / `bump_reason` / `visit_member_ids`) for a human to reassign or quick-move through the existing board actions — **nothing moves on mark-out itself**. Auto-assign (`GATE_TECH_OUT_AUTO_MOVE`, also dark, needs this gate on too, read at call time) is dispatcher-triggered from the drawer (`POST /api/admin/tech-out/:techId/auto-assign`, `server/services/tech-out-auto-move.js`): the open alerts ARE the queue, most-protected first, each moved through `SmartRebooker.reschedule` at the SAME date + window onto the best-fitting eligible tech (`expect`-pinned, capability `moveGuard`); a refusal leaves the alert open with `payload.auto_attempt.reason`. Selection runs the mover's own read-only commit probe first (`previewMoveConflicts`, no exclusions — the absent tech's other stops count too) — that probe is tech-blind, so any other live stop overlapping the window parks it as `window_occupied`. Only a plain `confirmed` visit moves; bookings awaiting office review stay parked (`office_review_pending`). Grouped visits and live (en_route / on_site) stops are never auto-moved. No customer communication. Mark-out is ONE transaction under the tech-day fence — its ONLY lock (the technician row is read, never `FOR UPDATE`: writers read that row `FOR SHARE` at different points relative to their own fences, so a row lock here cycled with each of them in turn; a writer whose check ran outside the fence may land a stop after the absence commits, and that is the bounded window the sweep covers). Writers that fence first are strictly serialized; the series rebooker fences every swept source and destination tech-day up front on EVERY series move (`lockTechDays` after the date-occupancy locks, no longer only under `expectConflictSnapshot`), pinned by `scheduling-occupancy.test.js`. Independent of the gate, `assertAssignableTechnician(techId, { conn, date })` rejects a tech with an uncleared absence on `date` and every assignment writer threads its destination date (board drag, schedule edit, rebooker date moves that keep the tech, lead / booking / IB / voice creation), so a marked-out tech cannot receive work for that day from the canonical writers, and a spawned recurring child whose date is an absence day is seeded unassigned (`assignableRecurringTemplateTechnicianId` with the child date; the booking / conversion follow-up seeder `seedFollowUpsForParent` applies the same per-child-date rule via `absentTechDays`); the safety net for every other writer is `sweepAbsentTechDays` (same 5-minute cadence as tech-late-detector, gate-read at call time): any open stop that later lands on an uncleared absent tech-day and has no open overflow alert is parked with `payload.late_arrival: true` and folded into the absence's stored `redistribution` on the same transaction, and any OPEN overflow card whose stop is no longer an open stop on that tech-day (reassigned by hand, moved, completed…) is closed as a systemic resolution (`closeStaleOverflowCards`) — a manual reassignment never resolves the card itself (every overflow alert carries `payload.absence_id`; a card a dispatcher dismissed BY HAND for that same absence — resolved without `payload.superseded_at` — still covers the row it opened so it never grows back, but NOT its grouped siblings (`visit_member_ids`): "Open job" reassigns and detaches one row, so siblings left on the absent tech get their own card on the next tick; a system auto-resolve or a previous absence's dismissal covers nothing). Slot discovery (`scheduling/find-time.js` on every path, estimate slot availability, the non-capacity `reserveSlot` hold) skips absent tech-days through `absentTechDays` (technician-eligibility.js) so a customer is never offered a slot the commit-time guard would refuse. The board roster carries `out_today` (Out pill, drop target disabled); mark-out and clear each drop the public estimate slot cache (`invalidateAllEstimates`) and emit `dispatch:tech_absence` to `dispatch:admins` after commit and every open board re-reads the roster on receipt (`useDispatchBoard.refreshTechs`), so no tab keeps a stale Out pill. "Tech is back" clears the absence and auto-resolves that day's overflow alerts in one transaction. No customer communication, and mark-out itself never changes a customer's date, window or technician; only the dispatcher-triggered auto-assign below changes the technician (never the date or window).

Per-tech Twilio lines: `GATE_TECH_LINES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time by the number registry (unset = live kill; off, a tech line is reported like an unassigned office number — nothing dropped). The registry's `fieldTech` bucket (`server/config/twilio-numbers.js`, mirrored by `client/src/constants/techLines.js`) says which numbers are tech lines; `technicians.twilio_number` (Team tab picker, one holder per line) says who answers. On: a text to the line still rings the office bell / inbox thread AND lands as a `tech_line_sms` tech-home card + push for the holder; a call rings the holder's cell first (`?stage=tech_line`, 20 s, press-1 screen) and continues into the office list from `/call-complete`, voicemail only after both; the digital customer card / vCard carries the line instead of the office number. Never a From number for automated texts (owner ruling), and no auto-reply fires from it. Sending from the line out of the tech portal is a later PR. See `docs/technician-provisioning-runbook.md` § Tech line.

Cross-provider routing: `MODEL_OPENAI_REPORT_WRITER` (Sol), `MODEL_OPENAI_BALANCED` (Terra), `MODEL_OPENAI_FAST` (Luna), `MODEL_OPENAI_FAST_INTERACTIVE` (Luna; the Fast Complete fact readers a technician waits on, which do not follow `MODEL_OPENAI_FAST`), plus legacy `MODEL_OPENAI_BEST` as a Terra-compatible override. Knowledge embeddings: `MODEL_OPENAI_EMBEDDING` (default `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536-dim) behind `GATE_HYBRID_KNOWLEDGE`; MCP read tools at `/api/mcp` behind `GATE_MCP_READ_TOOLS` + `MCP_SERVICE_TOKEN` — single-provider BY DESIGN (embedding spaces don't cross providers; unavailable → search degrades to full-text), and changing the model requires re-embedding the corpus. Completed-service reports are Sol-first, Opus-second, and return deterministic safe copy if both miss. Generated text must use a two-provider `TEXT_POLICIES` entry; a same-provider fallback is rejected by the dispatcher. No permanent shadow/parallel model calls. Gemini vision/image/video and call transcription keep their specialized provider ladders; V2 call extraction routes `CALL_EXTRACTION_PROVIDER`/`CALL_EXTRACTION_MODEL` (default `openai`/`gpt-5.6-sol`, Claude Opus fallback, kill = `CALL_EXTRACTION_PROVIDER=gemini`).

Photo ID second look: `PHOTO_ID_ESCALATE_BELOW` (a number with 0 < value <= 1, default `0.80`, read per call; anything else falls back to the default). `pest-identification.js` (website pest identifier, SMS photo triage, admin assessments, the customer app) reads each photo with Gemini first and sends the same photo to `OPENAI_FRONTIER` through `TEXT_POLICIES.photoIdVision` when Gemini misses, scores its answer below this value, or lists a runner-up of different risk (owner ruling 2026-09-26; no Claude leg). Lower it to escalate less (e.g. `0.5`); a Gemini miss or a risky runner-up still escalates at any value.

Plant/tree/shrub/palm photo ID referee (`plant-engine.js`, owner ruling 2026-09-28 — the pest engine's `photoIdVision` ladder above is unchanged): the plant engine's own second opinion moved from Astra to `TEXT_POLICIES.plantIdVision`'s `OPENAI_PLANT_ID` (`MODEL_OPENAI_PLANT_ID` override, default GPT-6 Sol), and `GATE_PLANT_ID_REFEREE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `'true'`**, read at call time in `runReferee()` — adds a deciding look from Claude Fable 5.1 at effort `high` (`MODELS.ROUTES.plantIdReferee`, `MODEL_PLANT_ID_REFEREE` override). Owner ruling 2026-09-29 narrowed what it may decide: **plant-NAME tie-breaks only, identify mode only** — it fires ONLY for an identity lane (turf/weeds for a lawn, host for tree_shrub/palm) where Gemini and Sol's escalation DISAGREED; a workup (problem check), a missing second opinion, and a low-confidence AGREEMENT never draw the call. The referee's own top either matches one side of the disagreement (that side goes first, capped at `likely`, never `pretty_sure`) or it doesn't — anything else (a third name, no usable answer) leaves the lane exactly as the escalation left it, no partial credit (see `docs/photo-id/plant-engine.md`). Costs roughly 20¢ per referee call (Fable, effort `high`, thinking-floored tokens) — it never fires on an ordinary clean read or on a workup. Off, or unset: byte-identical to the Gemini → Sol ladder, no third call, no redeploy needed to flip it back off.

Lawn visit assessment name referee (`services/lawn-visit-referee.js`, called from `lawn-visit-assessment.js#analyzeVisit`, owner ruling 2026-09-29 — `TEXT_POLICIES.lawnVisitAssessment`'s Gemini → Sol chain is unchanged): `GATE_LAWN_ASSESSMENT_REFEREE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `'true'`**, read at call time via `lawnAssessmentRefereeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). ONE gate covers both extra calls. On, when Gemini itself answered (never the OpenAI fallback) and its read is *unsure or serious* — any finding at confidence low/unknown, any finding with severity moderate/severe, or `grass_type` `unknown` — GPT-6 Sol (the policy's OpenAI leg alone, same prompt, photos and schema) re-reads the visit. Only if Gemini and Sol then disagree on a NAME does Claude Fable 5.1 at effort `high` (`MODELS.ROUTES.lawnAssessmentReferee`, `MODEL_LAWN_ASSESSMENT_REFEREE` override, 60 s cap) get one small a / b / neither question per disputed item. **Names only**: the grass type, and what a finding IS (`safeConditionLabel`'s cause catalog: chinch, grub, caterpillar, large/brown patch, gray leaf spot, dollar spot, weeds, drought, overwatering; a generic "fungal" name agrees with a specific fungal one, symptom-only / clean / negated / multi-cause names never dispute, and an ambiguous photo pairing draws no call). Scores, `severities{}`, finding severity and urgency, and every other field stay exactly as Gemini read them. Merge is a tie-break only: Fable matching Sol's side takes that name (with Sol's wording and confirmation step) and caps the finding's confidence at `moderate`; matching Gemini's side keeps Gemini and caps at `moderate`; a third answer, no usable answer, timeout or error leaves the result exactly as Gemini's, per item. Nothing throws out of `analyzeVisit`. Diagnostics ride only on the returned `referee` object when the gate is on (`{ triggered, outcome: settled|no_majority|unavailable|skipped, reason, secondOpinion, disputes, ambiguous, usage }`): internal, never persisted as a column, never in customer copy; their token usage is added to the run's `tokens_*`. No migration. Cost: no extra call on a confident read; a Sol re-read (~2.7¢/photo) on an unsure-or-serious one; a Fable call (~20¢) only on a name dispute. Off, or unset: byte-identical to today, no extra call, same return shape.

Typed decisions (TypeSafe Jev, dark): `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, read at call time via `typedDecisionsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Jev is a decision-only model (yes/no `noul`, `choice`, `score`; never free text) called through `callTypeSafe` / `dispatch(ROUTES.typedDecision)` (`server/services/llm/call.js`, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`). Production PINS `MODEL_TYPESAFE_JEV` (default `jev-1.13.0`): the adapter refuses any alias such as `jev-latest` (`typesafe_unpinned_model`) before the network. The route is single-leg by design (nothing else answers typed questions; never a `TEXT_POLICIES` leg), so a caller falls back to its existing path on `ok:false`. Questions live in immutable, versioned packages (`server/services/typed-decisions/packages.js`, ids `<capability>.v<n>`, hashes pinned in `server/fixtures/typed-decisions/package-hashes.json`: edit a published package = ship a new version); `askPackage` (`typed-decisions/jev.js`) is the only caller. Shadow evidence lands in `decision_reviews` (meaning columns kept apart from `outcome_evidence`; one row per provider per subject and question: `provider`, default `typesafe`, is in the unique key since migration `20261002010000` (expand then contract: `20261002005000` adds a second five-column unique (`decision_reviews_subject_question_legacy_uniq`) BEFORE 010000 drops the original and `20261002050000` restores the original at the end, so a pre-provider process can still upsert at every commit of a rolling deploy and through a code rollback; `20261002201000`, shipped with the Clef shadow leg (the second writer), drops BOTH five-column keys so two providers' rows for one case coexist under the provider key alone; its down locks the table, re-adds them and refuses while another provider has rows), the closed set is `DECISION_PROVIDERS` in `packages.js`, the random-audit draw is keyed on the subject and a caller recording two providers passes each write the other's answers (`siblingAnswers`), so a case where they differ queues both rows and the same cases get labeled for each; the queue, the daily item and the Typed tab name the provider whose answer a row holds, `providerLabel`: Jev or Clef); `server/scripts/export-decision-review-fixtures.js` exports ids + labels only, never message text. Lane `typed_decisions`, maturity M0. Nothing sends to a customer.

Typed decisions shadow (same gate, `typed-decisions/shadow-recorder.js`, `sms-shadow.js`, `daily-review-item.js`, `subject-hash.js`): with the gate on, the nightly call self-audit (`call-self-audit.js`) puts each sampled call to `call_judge.v5` (v4 until 10-29: v5 adds the day/time conflict rule of extraction prompt v32, so a booking the caller accepted for one day is not drift when staff's closing line named another; v3 until 10-12, v2 until #5994; v4 added three V2-only confirmation rules v3 lacked: missing AM/PM, staff hedges, caller-proposed time; the bare-time rule is left out because no judge is given the call's clock; a call whose stored answer the V1 extractor wrote, or that carries no `v2_primary_adopted` stamp, is still asked v3) (also when the deep judge fails, against production alone) and to `call_gate_checks.v1` (three yes/no questions recorded beside three dark call gates' OWN decisions as `production` baselines, read by `gateCheckBaselines`: `service_unclear` = the v2 extraction's `ambiguous_pest_or_service` flag (GATE_CALL_UNCLEAR_SERVICE_ASSESSMENT), `reschedule_committed` = the v2 extraction's committed reschedule the caller accepted (`caller_accepted_slot`, as the apply path requires; GATE_CALL_RESCHEDULE_APPLY), `promise_open` = a non-stale AI-extracted Waves `call_commitments` row of a kind the chaser acts on (`SLA_KINDS`: callback, send_estimate, schedule_visit; GATE_PROMISE_CHASER_BELL); no valid v2 extraction or commitments off = no baseline, never a false one; asked only when the whole transcript fits the 5,000-character span the models and reviewer see (94% of calls; longer ones counted as `skippedLong`); tallied apart under `jev.gateChecks`; the same 03:40 run also puts EVERY inbound voicemail (not a sample; `shadowVoicemails`, ~44 a month; it runs first, on its own gate, even when GATE_CALL_SELF_AUDIT is off or no Anthropic client exists) to `voicemail.v1` (`callback_requested`, `needs_attention_today` judged as of the day it was left, `is_vendor_or_spam`), in two idempotent steps over every terminal, quiet voicemail (`voicemail`, or `processed` / `spam` / `lead_creation_failed` with the extraction's is_voicemail, or `extraction_failed` when the voice webhook's `answered_by` / `call_outcome` says voicemail; no processing claim held and the row unchanged for 30 minutes; never a rejected transcription) whose row changed in the last 7 days: ASK each enabled provider until its answer on the CURRENT transcript (`subject_hash`) is recorded (a labeled or held-out answer is never re-asked; a retried leg is handed the stored current answers), then REFRESH with no model call: every unreviewed answer's production baseline is rewritten from what production shows now and its cohort recomputed with the recorder's own `sampleFor` (so a baseline is never frozen at ask time: a retry, a same-transcript reprocess or a late callback claim shows up next pass). Baselines: `callback_requested` production = production put it in front of a person (the callback alert's durable claim `call_log.voicemail_callback_alerted_at`, stamped before delivery; a lead minted from its call; or a triage item for it); `is_vendor_or_spam` production = spam status, the extraction's is_spam, or the v2 `call_nature` `vendor_or_partner` unless its `spam_verdict.is_spam_content` is false (a cleared partner; a job applicant is not a vendor); urgency none. Evidence only, no bell or priority changes) and the inbound SMS webhook (`twilio-webhook.js`, registered before the consumed-reply returns, runs on response finish) puts each customer text to `sms_courtesy.v1` / `sms_reschedule.v1`, and each text from an UNKNOWN sender (exactly what the GATE_SMS_SPAM_CLASSIFIER screen sees: not `complianceEligible`, no reaction, no media; whatever that gate's mode; help and opt keywords skipped) to `sms_solicitation.v1` (`shadowUnknownSenderSms`: baselines `rules` = the screen's `isSolicitationPitch` marker, `production` = the classifier's own verdict only when its model read the text; evidence for that gate's flip pack, nothing silenced); `recordDecisions` upserts one `decision_reviews` row per question (Jev answer + the rule / production / deep-judge baselines; ids and yes/no only, never message text; for a call, `subject_hash` = sha256 of the transcript span Jev was given; a re-record merges answer columns, `sampled_for` and `subject_hash` onto unlabeled, non-heldout rows) and samples it as a disagreement or a 10% random audit drawn from a stable hash of the row key. Outcome evidence was DROPPED from this lane (owner 2026-10-01): `outcome_evidence` stays unwritten and the reviewer's label is the only ground truth. At 8:05 AM ET `daily-review-item.js` raises ONE `typed_decisions` admin item (up to 8 disagreements + 2 spot checks still unreviewed from the last 14 days, via `raiseAdminAlert`; a null alert is a failed run) and closes standing items once nothing is waiting (also after the last label). The Typed tab (`/admin/agents?tab=typed`, shown only when the hub probe reports the gate on) and `routes/admin-typed-decisions.js` (404 while the gate is off) list the queue (subject text read live for display, never stored; a call whose live transcript no longer matches `subject_hash` is flagged and cannot be labeled, 409 `subject_changed`) and write labels (`jev_right` / `jev_wrong` / `unclear`, bound to the Jev answer and transcript version shown via `seen_answer` / `seen_subject`, audit-logged, a confirmed label needs `force: true` to replace; the Claude labeling runner (owner 2026-10-02) signs in instead with header `X-Labeler-Token` = `TYPED_DECISIONS_LABELER_TOKEN` (unset or under 32 characters = off): its own router (`routes/typed-decisions-labeler.js`, mounted above cors() and the global limiter, in front of the admin router; allowlisted in `server/config/public-route-allowlist.json`) opens ONLY `POST /reviews/:id/label`, never with `force`, only on rows still `unreviewed` (409 `already_labeled` otherwise), stamped `labeled_by` `claude-labeler`, audit actor `system`). `GET /api/admin/typed-decisions/status` (`services/typed-decisions/eval.js`, `?days=` default 90) turns those labels into the §9 status per capability, package version and served model (keyed by provider since migration `20261002010000`; two providers' labels on the same subjects report side by side once the Clef shadow leg writes): labeled counts, precision and recall with the 95% one-sided exact-binomial lower bound, the tier those bounds clear (representative labels only — random audit and held-out; disagreement-sampled labels are reported, never promoted on), confident-answer coverage and the one blocker to the next tier; it reads only, and promotion stays a person's decision. Nothing acts on a Jev answer: no reply is sent or suppressed, no visit moves, no customer is contacted.

Corrections view (`corrections`, migrations `20261002100000_corrections_view` through `20261002170000_correction_reason`, each cut restating the same columns; AI acceleration scope idea D, owner 2026-10-01): one read-only VIEW over every place a person already corrects an AI decision, so the weekly corrections lane reads one query instead of five tables: `agent_decisions` (`human_verdict` corrected or dismissed, or ignored only when the operator's send parked it, i.e. a linked outbound a PERSON sent exists (persisted operator provenance, the `operatorSentSql` test: `metadata.human_authored` or `admin_user_id`; autonomous sends such as `ai_autosent` / `ai_gratitude` never count, whatever reviewer stamp recovery wrote): the after-send sweep's ignored rows (suggestions committed mid-send, never on screen) and auto-send's reviewer `auto` rows are not corrections; `corrected_by` / `corrected_at` are the displayed send's sender and time, the review stamp only when no send names one; `human_text` is what the person actually sent: the outbound text stamped `metadata.agent_decision_id` or listing the decision in `metadata.parked_decision_ids` (a reply sent instead of the suggestion), else a judged draft's `human_reply_text`, else the canned `correction_note`, which also rides in `detail`; two partial indexes on `sms_log` serve that lookup), `decision_reviews` (a typed answer labeled wrong, `detail.correct_value` the right one, `detail.subject_hash` + `detail.package_hash` the exact text and package it was labeled on), `message_drafts` (revised or rejected BY THE REVIEW ENDPOINTS: `PUT /api/admin/drafts/:id/revise` and `/reject` stamp the status they set into `flags` (a `review_verdict` key on an object, a `review_verdict:<status>` tag on an array: the house-voice drafter writes an array) and the view requires the stamp to match the row; the campaign send guard and the Agent Ops duplicate sweep also write rejected + `approved_by` and are not corrections; drafts reviewed before the stamp are not shown), `shadow_draft_judgments` (`human_better` / `draft_unsafe`: the person's own reply beside the draft; `corrected_by` / `corrected_at` are that reply's sender and time, the judge run time rides in `detail`; `version` and `model` are the drafter's, the judge's ride in `detail`; a judged draft whose Agent Review decision is shown (the same counted set) is shown once, as that decision) , `voice_profiles` (rejected) and `reply_training_examples` (the Agent Review page's Reply training verdicts edited / rejected / no_reply_needed, the AI draft beside the person's reply, `version` and `model` from the decision the draft was copied from; needs a nonblank AI draft ("no reply needed" against a decision that proposed none is an agreement); left out when the same reply is already shown for its decision: the decision's row when it counts, else the emitted judgment on the decision's draft, both sides compared canonically (the send path's GSM punctuation table, whitespace runs folded) because capture stores the folded text (one shared `decision_reply` sub-query feeds both the row and this test), so a rewrite saved beside a separately corrected decision stays its own row). Columns: `source`, `source_id`, `kind`, `surface` (sms | typed | voice), `topic`, `customer_id`, `ai_text`, `human_text`, `detail` (jsonb extras), `version`, `model`, `corrected_by`, `corrected_at`, `reason`. The one-tap reason (migration `20261002170000_correction_reason`: the column and the eleventh cut restated with a trailing `reason`): five values in `server/services/correction-reasons.js` (`wrong_fact`, `wrong_tone`, `missing_promise`, `should_have_escalated`, `other`; client mirror `client/src/constants/correctionReasons.js`, pinned equal by test), tapped as chips on the Agent Review card (`POST /api/admin/agent-decisions/:id/review` body `reason`, stored in `agent_decisions.correction_reason`, nullable, closed CHECK, never on an accepted decision) and on the Typed tab (`POST /api/admin/typed-decisions/reviews/:id/label` body `reason`, kept inside `label` beside the note, jev_wrong only); the view's `reason` is that value, NULL for the other sources. No grant (the read-only chart role cannot see it); nothing reads the view yet. It carries customer message text exactly as its sources do: in-database reads by staff tooling only, never an export.

Bad-review bell (`services/review-low-rating-alert.js`, Clef second wave idea 7, owner CW-D4 2026-10-02): `GATE_REVIEW_ALERT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `reviewLowRatingAlertLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, ONE needs-you admin item stays open for every Google review that needs an answer: 1 to 4 stars (owner ruling 2026-10-03, "4 stars or lower"; it shipped at 3), at an active location (`WAVES_LOCATIONS`, the Reviews page's own scope), no real reply by the Reviews page's own rule (`whereNeedsRealReply`: none, or an unpublished `[DRAFT]`), not dismissed, still on Google (no `missing_since`), and written at or after the lane's activation boundary (stored once in `system_settings` key `review_low_rating_alert_activated_at` at the START of the first gated sync, before its pull, two hours back on the database clock, so a review written between the gate flip and that first pull counts while turning the gate on never rings a backlog). Level-triggered: after every review sync (`syncAllReviews`, so the GBP feed and the Places sample alike) `syncLowRatingReviewAlerts` raises or reopens the item for each such review through the alert episodes (`raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`, key `review-low-rating:<review id>`, matched to an open item on either the row id or `google_review_id` so a fresh Places re-pull or a GBP adoption keeps one item; the review is re-read and share-locked in the raise's own transaction, so a reply or dismissal that committed first never rings; the linked customer is the item's version, so linking one quietly refreshes its subject; one pass at a time under the cron lock `review-low-rating-alert`, so an overlapping sync never closes an item the other just raised; with `ALERT_EPISODES` killed it falls back to a plain deduped `raiseAdminAlert` per review and closes nothing, the shared kill switch's contract) and closes every open item whose review no longer needs an answer (`closeAdminAlertKeys`; a review linked to an internal test account never needs one, so an item raised before that link closes too); a failed write is retried next sync and a reply removed later rings again. The item (`raiseAdminAlert` rules via `composeAdminAlert`: "Customers — read a 2-star Google review", the reviewer's name and the stars, deep link `/admin/reviews?responded=all&review=<id>`, done when replied or dismissed; subject the linked customer, else a check on the review; `customerId` in metadata so internal test accounts stay silent) never quotes the review (its words carry dates and exclamation marks the alert rules forbid). Category `review_low_rating` rings by default and the owner can silence it in Push settings (`DEFAULT_ON_CATEGORIES` + `OVERRIDABLE_CATEGORIES`); silenced (read only while `GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY` is on, as the notification service reads it), the pass raises nothing, not even a reopen, and closes standing items. Rules only, no model; internal only, nothing is sent to the reviewer. Off = byte-identical.

Billing email details (`services/billing-email-details.js`, owner-approved 2026-09-29 after an audit of production `email_messages`): `GATE_BILLING_EMAIL_DETAILS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `'true'`**, read at call time via `billingEmailDetailsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`, exported on its own line; unset = kill, no redeploy). ONE gate covers three things. (1) `invoice.sent` and `invoice.receipt` (and the routed `billing.notice` / `billing.receipt_notice`, when the notice is about one invoice) carry the service, service date, full street address and payment method: the invoice's own blank service or date is read from the visit, completion record, combined-visit packet or title; the receipt names the tender behind a cash / check / Zelle / ACH payment, not only a card; an unpaid invoice names the customer's saved (autopay) method as "Payment method on file" — never on a payer-billed invoice or an operator's one-off recipient. (2) `payment.failed` gets the declined card (payments row, then the saved method, then the failed PaymentIntent's `last_payment_error`), the attempt date (the row, else Stripe's event time) and the retry date ONLY when the dunning ladder armed one (`payments.next_retry_at`, billing-cron's `RETRY_DELAYS_DAYS`; a pay-page failure the ladder does not retry leaves the row blank — a date is never computed). (3) A Property row (`property_full_address`, the street address from `utils/property-display.js`, never the `profile_label` nickname) on invoice, receipt and the estimate follow-ups (`estimate.engage_*`, `estimate.payment_step_abandoned`, `estimate.deposit_abandoned`; the estimate's own address text wins over the customer's, a value with no street number falls through to the saved property). Idempotency keys are deliberately NOT part of this gate (separate follow-up). The template rows ship in migrations `20260930090000_billing_email_detail_rows` and `20260930100100_billing_email_detail_rows_fill_missing` (the second adds only rows a staff-edited template still lacks; the first: one new active version per template, read-modify-write, CAS on the active version, only the replaced version archived; skipped with a log if an admin reshaped the template or set a custom plain-text body) and are variable-driven: only the senders above fill the new variables, only under the gate, so gate off every email renders byte-identical. Every lookup fails to a blank row, never a throw or a guess. `payment.failed` needed no template change (its Attempted / Payment method / Next retry rows already existed). Off, or unset: byte-identical to today.

Typed decisions second provider (Cloudflare Clef, dark): `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS_CLEF` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, read at call time via `typedDecisionsClefLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`), and honoured only while `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS` is also live (unset = kill, no redeploy). Clef and Clef-flash are Cloudflare's decision-only models on Workers AI; they take the same `state` + typed `questions` as Jev and answer in the same shape (verified against the live endpoint 2026-10-02), so `askPackage(packageId, state, { provider: 'cloudflare' })` (`typed-decisions/jev.js`) puts a registered package to them through `dispatch(ROUTES.typedDecisionClef)` → `callWorkersAIDecision` (`server/services/llm/call.js`: `POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CF_ACCOUNT_ID/ai/run/@cf/cloudflare/<model>`, the Workers AI `{ result, success }` envelope unwrapped, never throws, never retries, a failed leg still ledgered). Credentials: `CF_WORKERS_AI_TOKEN` (a least-privilege "Workers AI - Read" token) or, when unset, the existing `CF_API_TOKEN`; plus `CF_ACCOUNT_ID`. Model: `MODEL_CLOUDFLARE_CLEF` (default `clef-flash`; `clef` is the 27B model) — Cloudflare publishes no dated ids, so the adapter accepts only an id the catalog registers as a Cloudflare decision model and records the model the provider reports serving on every ledger row. Single-leg like `typedDecision` (never a `TEXT_POLICIES` leg; a caller keeps its existing path on `ok:false`). Lane `typed_decisions_clef` (maturity M0), token-health platform `cloudflare_workers_ai`. With both gates on, the nightly call self-audit (`call-self-audit.js`) and the inbound-SMS shadow (`typed-decisions/sms-shadow.js`) put each package to BOTH providers and record one row per provider, each handed the other's answers as `siblingAnswers` (one leg's failure never blocks the other; the self-audit tallies the Clef leg under `jev.clef`); the status (`eval.js`) groups by provider so the two report side by side on the same cases. Customer text and call transcripts may go to this provider raw (owner ruling 2026-10-01, same as TypeSafe). Images (Clef only; no shipped package uses them yet): `callWorkersAIDecision` takes up to 4 `images` (data-URL strings) beside `state` and `questions`; more than 4, an entry that is not canonical-base64 JPEG / PNG / WebP whose bytes match its type (the only formats Clef takes), or a serialized body (images + state + questions) over 150 KB in UTF-8 bytes (the provider refuses a request past ~150 KB) fails the leg before any network call (`cloudflare_images_too_large` / `cloudflare_bad_images`), and the ledger text holds `[images: n, sha256 …]`, never bytes. `askPackage(id, state, { provider: 'cloudflare', images })` accepts them only for a package that declares `imageSlots` (an integer 1..4, Clef's per-request maximum, checked when packages load, covered by `packageHash` only when present, so shipped hashes are unchanged); anything else is `images_not_allowed`, and Jev never receives images. `fitImagesForClef(buffers, { reserveBytes: clefBodyOverhead(state, questions) })` (`typed-decisions/image-budget.js`) is the one server fitter, the sharp twin of the client's `fitImagesToBudget` (best rung first, first rung that fits, never upscale) with one deliberate difference: EVERY image is re-encoded from a raw raster (auto-rotated, then all metadata — EXIF/GPS/comments — discarded; no original is ever sent verbatim, so callers must not rely on byte or hash preservation), and decoding stops at 25 MP (`limitInputPixels`); call it before `askPackage`, which accepts ONLY the frozen records it returns (`isFittedImage`; a bare data-URL string or a look-alike object is `images_not_allowed`), so everything sent to Clef was decoded and re-encoded by sharp. Nothing sends to a customer.

Visit access flags, shadow leg (`typed-decisions/visit-access-shadow.js`, Clef second wave idea 5, owner order 2026-10-03): `GATE_VISIT_ACCESS_FLAGS` — **ships DARK: live only when exactly `shadow`** and only while `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS` is live, read at call time via `visitAccessShadowLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, an hourly sweep (:34, 05:34 to 19:34 ET, cron lock `visit-access-shadow`) takes today's and tomorrow's upcoming visits (`UPCOMING_SERVICE_STATUSES`, customer not deleted, internal test accounts left out; only an account PROVEN to have one premises, the primary one, is judged (`visit-property-scope.js` `customerHasOnlyPrimaryPremises`, unresolved links failing the proof), because `property_preferences`, the texts and the visit history are keyed on the customer, so a multi-property account is left out; at most 80 visits are asked per pass and the rest wait for the next, visits already answered never counting against that) and puts each to `visit_access.v1`: six yes/no reads a technician who has never met the customer would want (`dog_on_property`, `needs_code_key_or_person`, `contact_before_arrival`, `person_home_needs_notice`, `past_access_problem`, `access_fact_not_on_file`), on each enabled provider (Jev, and Clef under `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS_CLEF`), one `decision_reviews` row per provider and question under subject type `scheduled_services` (migration `20261003101500`, which rebuilds the subject_type CHECK from the values it holds plus the new one, so another migration adding a subject type the same way can run in either order). Nothing in production makes these judgments, so only two questions carry a `rules` baseline (pet count above zero; any code on file); the rest are label-only. **What leaves:** the saved codes never do; the state says only WHETHER codes are on file (`structured.has_codes`: the four saved codes, or, under `GATE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ACCESS`, a shared neighborhood gate entry by the day feed's own reader `neighborhoodGateEntriesForVisits`, flagged `structured.neighborhood_gate`). Scheduler audit segments are stripped from the visit note (`stripSchedulerAuditText`). Known limit: a customer text holding a bare word with no access context is sent as written, as every inbound customer text already is by the SMS shadow (owner ruling 2026-10-01). Every text field (the access, parking, pet, special-instruction and chemical-sensitivity notes, the visit note, the customer's inbound texts, the last technician note) passes `redactForState`: a text or note that names any access point or credential noun anywhere in it (code, key, keypad, lockbox, gate, garage, door, lock, alarm, remote), or an instruction verb a credential rides on (use, type, punch, press, enter, dial, say), or holds a sentence `completion-comms-context.js` `isAccessSentence` reads as being about getting in, is replaced WHOLE by a marker built from two closed vocabularies only (`[access detail withheld: mentions code, gate; reports a problem getting in]`), since a credential can be any word in any notation and can sit on the next line; the two fields whose purpose is how to get in (`access_notes`, `side_gate_access`) ALWAYS leave as that marker, whatever they say; a customer text sent within 24 hours after such a text, or after a Waves text that mentions access and reached the customer (queued / sent / delivered, not an internal alert; read only for this, from 24 hours before the window; a Waves text never enters the state; a truncated read withholds a full day from its oldest row), is withheld with it; in every other text, after `redactAccessCodes`, a token holding a digit is masked unless it is a one- or two-digit number, an ordinal, a clock time or a day/month date (so house and phone numbers go too), and so is a capitalised code-shaped token unless the line is shouted. The state is a function of the visit and of facts dated before it: texts run from the COMPLETION of the last completed visit on the same service line (`completed_at`, else Eastern midnight of its day; 120-day cap, at most 8, tapbacks dropped) up to the visit's own start (its window start, else 8 AM Eastern), and history (completed `scheduled_services` rows; `service_records` supplies only the last technician note) counts only days before its date, so a repeat pass over an unchanged visit builds the same digest. Each state asked about is stored, already redacted, in `visit_access_states` (migration `20261003140000`: visit id + digest + state, pruned at 180 days by the cron whatever the gate says, no grant to the read-only chart role), and the review route (`routes/admin-typed-decisions.js`, `storedVisitAccess`, one read per page) shows and labels against that stored state, so a later edit to the preferences, the note or the directory never strands a row. Note lines are in priority order (the visit note and the sensitivity first), each capped at 400 characters, never cut as a block. The visit's `customer_request` rides in the notes. The cohort refresh is idempotent and runs on every pass, unchanged ones included; in it a queued row older than 13 days restarts its `created_at`, so the daily review item's 14-day window sees a visit that moved out and came back. A visit that already holds any provider's answer for its state and retries another's failed leg draws on its own budget (40 a pass), so an outage of either provider never keeps later visits from being asked. An earlier visit the same day that finished before this one starts counts as history, and visits on one day are ordered by completion. The stored state is written before a row is asked or requeued, so a pruned one comes back. The daily review item (`daily-review-item.js`) takes rows in turn across capabilities, so this lane's volume never takes every slot. The Typed tab shows a visit subject as "Visit facts the models read". A visit that has started (now past its window start) is never re-read, so a note edited after arrival is not judged. Recruiting texts are excluded (`excludeRecruitingSmsLog`), and the text read pages until it holds eight of the customer's own texts. A provider is asked once per state (`subject_hash`); a new text or an edited note asks again and replaces the unreviewed rows; a labeled or held-out row is never re-asked; a failed leg is retried next pass with the other's stored answers beside it, and after every write the cohort of each row for the current state is settled from the answers on record (the recorder's `sampleFor`, no model call), so a retry queues both sides of a disagreement and a switched-off provider's rows for an older state never decide a new answer's cohort. About 30 visits a day. SHADOW ONLY: nothing is shown to a technician, written to a visit, a brief or a customer record, belled or sent. The card flags, their confirm / dismiss tap and the `scheduled_services.access_flags` column are the next PR.

Photo privacy shadow (Clef second wave idea 3, dark): `GATE_PHOTO_PRIVACY` — **ships DARK: off unless set to `shadow`**, read at call time via `photoPrivacyMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; `shadow` is the only value honoured and only while `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS_CLEF` is live; `suggest` / `act` are not built and read as off; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `POST /api/tech/social/publish` (`routes/tech-social.js`), AFTER the post is published and logged and only when the photo was hosted, hands the photo to `typed-decisions/photo-privacy-shadow.js` fire-and-forget: the bytes are fitted in memory by `fitImagesForClef` and put to Clef as `photo_privacy.v1` (the first package with `imageSlots`; six yes/no questions: `shows_face`, `shows_person`, `shows_address_text`, `shows_license_plate`, `shows_child`, `shows_pet`; state `surface` + the first published caption), and one `decision_reviews` row per question is recorded against the `social_media_posts` row (subject type `social_post`; `subject_hash` = sha256 of the hosted photo URL + that caption, `socialPostSubjectHash`). The baseline is `production: false` on every question (the publish path has no image check), so a Clef yes queues as a disagreement and the rest fall to the 10% random audit. Subject types: the CHECK allows `call_log`, `sms_log` and `social_post` (migration `20261003100000_decision_reviews_subject_types` widened it to six new types up front and `20261003101000_decision_reviews_subject_types_social_post_only` narrows it to the one with a writer and a reviewer; `SUBJECT_TYPES` in `shadow-recorder.js` mirrors it, and a new type is a new migration shipped with its writer and reviewer); the review route reads a social post back as the hosted photo + caption (the Typed tab shows the image) and refuses a label on any subject type it cannot read back (409 `subject_changed`). SHADOW ONLY: no post is held, edited or removed and the technician sees nothing; a hold is a later PR with its own mode.

Lawn Jev timing check (owner 2026-10-28/29, dark): `GATE_LAWN_JEV_TIMING_CHECK` = `off` | `shadow` | `enforce` — **ships DARK: off unless set to `shadow` or `enforce`** (anything else reads as off), read at call time via `lawnJevTimingCheckMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and honoured only while `GATE_TYPED_DECISIONS` is live. It adds a meaning check to the model-written lawn DIAGNOSIS summary, the contract's `customer_summary` that three writers store in `lawn_diagnostics`: `routes/public-lawn-assessment.js` (website photo tool), `routes/tech-lawn-diagnostic.js` persist (only a summary restored from the verified model run; a technician's typed `aiSummary` is never checked or changed) and `services/photo-assessment-create.js` (the Communications Analyze photos button). Each calls `checkDiagnosisSummary` (`server/services/service-report/lawn-jev-timing-check.js`) just before its insert: every sentence goes to TypeSafe Jev in parallel as `lawn_result_timing.v1` (`states_result_timing`: does the sentence say or imply WHEN a treatment's result will be seen), bounded by one 3000 ms step (`JEV_TIMING_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`), and the answers fold into one (largest `p`; `yes` = that `p` >= 0.5; `confident` = every sentence confident). A failed or late sentence call gives no verdict and the text stays. `shadow` stores the row unchanged and adds no wait; after the insert it records the verdict in `decision_reviews` (subject type `lawn_diagnostics`, migration `20261029100000`; one row per diagnosis; `subject_hash` = sha256 of the trimmed stored summary, `lawnDiagnosisSubjectHash`; baseline `production: false`, so a Jev yes queues as a disagreement and the rest fall to the 10% random audit; the review route reads the subject back from `lawn_diagnostics.report_contract.customer_summary`). `enforce` waits (bounded) and drops the sentences Jev flags from `customer_summary` before the row is stored (`withoutResultTimingSentences`, nothing left = the generic low-confidence summary), so `report_contract.customer_summary` and `ai_summary` hold the same final text; a kept text is recorded as in shadow. The read-time egress word list (`safeCustomerSummary`) still runs after this. Replay behind the decision: the word list missed 5 of 16 new timing claims, Jev caught 16 of 16 with 1 false flag in 32 sentences, and the two together missed none. Out of scope: `lawn-visit-summary.js` (fixed reviewed phrases, no model text) and the treatment narrative (not reached for lawn while `GATE_LAWN_REPORT_COPY_FIXES` is live). Nothing sends to a customer; the contract entries are in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`.

AI incidents (correction loop, shadow data): `ai_incidents` is the general ledger of adjudicated correction evidence, one row per piece of evidence, `area` = the lane family (`sms` first), `incident_key` = the unit of AI work it is about (for sms the `message_drafts.id`). Dispositions are a closed list: `confirmed_mistake`, `lead`, `not_a_mistake`, `duplicate` (the nightly job writes only `confirmed_mistake`, `lead` and `duplicate`: one reader's clearance is a lead, rule `model_cleared`, and a confirmation naming an unknown failure mode is read as a lead). The nightly 04:30 ET job `adjudicateHumanBetter` (`server/services/sms-pathology-ledger.js`, lane `sms_pathology`, gate `GATE_SMS_PATHOLOGY_LEDGER`, `PATHOLOGY_ADJUDICATE_BATCH=0` stops it) reads the shadow judge's `human_better` verdicts on drafts produced in the last 45 days and confirms a mistake ONLY under the two-model rule in `server/services/ai-incidents/sms-adjudication.js`: two models on DIFFERENT providers (the `fastStructured` legs; the second is pinned to the leg that did not answer first) each read the same evidence blind, both must return `confirmed_mistake` for the same failure mode, and each must quote the unsupported claim in words the draft really contains. The job builds no Anthropic client itself, so a missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` fails only that leg. Nothing deterministic confirms: the pattern predicates, the person's conflicting weekday or date, and the judge's safety score are stored as signals in `adjudication` and never vote (text matching cannot prove the facts do not support a claim). The readers see the facts through the judge's section-aware `sanitizeFactsForJudge`, so the calls and thread at the tail of the block are not cut. A second reader that cannot be reached leaves the judgment un-adjudicated for the next run. Everything else is stored as a lead and never counted. A partial unique index allows one confirmed row per (area, incident, cell). Recurrence is attributed by `produced_at` (when the draft was written), never by when it was judged. Nothing reads the table at runtime; the classic weekly patch proposer still counts `sms_pathology_entries` alone. Not granted to the read-only chart role. Fix tracking (`ai_fix_proposals`, `server/services/ai-incidents/fix-proposals.js`): Sundays 04:45 ET `proposeSmsFixes` (same gate; `PATHOLOGY_FIX_PROPOSAL_MIN` default 5, `PATHOLOGY_FIX_PROPOSAL_MAX_CELLS` default 3, 0 stops it) gives a cell with that many DISTINCT confirmed incidents on the live prompt version, adjudicated since the cell's last proposal, one `pending` row with its `fix_kind` (from the surface) and a dev/holdout split fixed per incident by hash; no model call, no bell. Fresh evidence on a pending proposal supersedes it (carrying its incidents only on the same version); an `accepted` or `pr_open` fix is left alone. One open proposal per cell (partial unique index on pending / accepted / pr_open). Status and stamps change only through `transitionProposal` (legal moves, required stamps: `pr_open` needs the PR, `shipped` the PR, the Codex-clean commit and the shipped version, `reverted` the revert PR; the table CHECKs the same; every change appends to `history`), driven from the terminal by `ops/agents/fix-proposal-link.js` (dry run unless `--execute`). Replays (`ai_replay_runs` / `ai_replay_results`, `server/services/ai-incidents/replay-runs.js`) make NO provider call (owner ruling 2026-10-02): `ops/agents/correction-replay.js export` writes a proposal's frozen dev or holdout cases, customer identifiers redacted (the customer's names, then the shared corpus redactors, then invoice and order references), with the drafter's stored intent, scheduling flag and, for a gratitude draft, the rebuilt approved reply, and the drafter's system prompt under each draft's stored voice profile to the lane's scratchpad (never the repo; owner-approved 2026-10-02 as an exception to the ops-artifact rule, since other people's names can survive redaction, and deleted by `record --execute --delete-export` once the run is stored); each case lists what the replay leaves out (few-shot exemplars, the verify/revise loop, the mixed-thread hint), and only prompt-wording cells (`prompt_discipline`, `other`) replay: facts-block-gap, few-shot-leak and verifier-miss cells are refused (the new fact, the exemplars and the verify loop are not in the frozen inputs); replays are recorded only on an open proposal; Claude Code subagents re-draft and grade them, and `record` stores the run (`method` subagent, `exact_production_model` false; any reproduction fails it, an unjudged or missing case makes it inconclusive, a clean holdout under 5 cases is underpowered; a fix's holdout run needs a passed dev run on the same `code_ref` and prompt version) and stamps the proposal; a `recurrence` check (dev cases only, no prerequisite, never stamps the proposal) re-checks an open proposal on a newer version; the holdout is exported only after the proposal's current dev run passed on that checkout's commit and prompt version. A facts-block fix is proven by its own synthetic fixture test and by new incidents after it ships (a past draft's full context is not stored), so it is never carried across a version bump by a replay. `carry` moves a pending or accepted proposal to the live prompt version, with its incidents and split, only when a recurrence check of its dev cases on that version still reproduces (owner ruling Q2). The Monday brief is `ops/agents/correction-loop-report.js` (READ-ONLY; recurrence per cell per house-voice prompt version by when the draft was produced, with the reviewed share beside it).

Call incidents (correction loop for calls, dark): `GATE_CALL_INCIDENTS` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, read at call time via `callIncidentsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`), honoured only while `GATE_CALL_SELF_AUDIT` is on. On, a 04:10 ET job (`adjudicateCallFindings`, `server/services/call-incidents.js`, lane `call_incidents`; `CALL_INCIDENT_BATCH=0` stops it) turns each new self-audit field disagreement (`call_audit_findings`, `audit_source` self_audit, the last 14 days; the self-audit rewrites a finding in place when it re-audits a call, so the evidence id is the finding id plus a fingerprint of everything it says (values, excerpt, full detail), and a rewritten finding is new evidence) into ONE `ai_incidents` row (`area` calls, `incident_key` the call, surface `call_extraction`, failure mode `<field>_missed` / `<field>_false_positive` over the five audited fields, unversioned, since the audited answers come from `ai_extraction`, which can be V1, V2-adopted or a mix per field, and `ai_extraction_prompt_version` is the V2 shadow's provenance only; `produced_at` = when the call happened). It is a confirmed mistake only when a second model on the OTHER provider from the one that answered the audit (the self-audit records `detail.auditor_provider` at audit time, since the deep call can fall back; the catalog resolves `detail.auditor_model` only for older rows), reading the transcript blind under the auditor's own prompt plus one ask, the exact words behind its answer for the disputed field (`field_excerpt`), reaches the auditor's answer for that field AND that field quote is words the transcript contains. The auditor's single excerpt backs its most important judgment, not necessarily this field, so it is a signal only. These stay leads with no second call made: the auditor gave no boolean for the field; the exact input the auditor read can no longer be rendered from the call (`detail.audit_input_hash` covers the audit prompt, the direction instruction and the transcript text, so a prompt change, a re-transcription or a replaced recording all count); the auditor's provider is unknown; the call is longer than the 5,000 characters both readers are shown. An unreachable second reader stores nothing and is retried, and the nightly batch reads newest first, so findings that keep failing never block newer ones. The typed-decision answers (Jev, Clef) for the same call and field are stored as signals only. About one fast-tier OpenAI call per finding (roughly three a day). Sundays 04:50 ET `proposeCallFixes` opens fix proposals for calls on the unversioned cohort, fresh by the proposal watermark (`CALL_FIX_PROPOSAL_MIN` default 5). The Monday brief lists every area. Shadow data only; nothing reaches a customer.
Call-ingest completeness watchdog: `GATE_CALL_INGEST_WATCHDOG` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, boot-read in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (`callIngestWatchdog`); ON in production. On, a cron at :07 and :37 every hour (`runCallIngestWatchdog`, `server/services/call-ingest-watchdog.js`, scheduled in `scheduler.js`) diffs Twilio's own call ledger against `call_log`: an INBOUND parent call, status completed, 20 s or longer, that STARTED more than 60 minutes ago (the grace is measured from Twilio's start time, not the end: a 50-minute call can be classified 10 minutes after it ends), with no member of its call family (parent SID or any child dial-leg SID) in `twilio_call_sid` / `call_sid` / `recording_sid` is a miss. Why: a 2026-07-11 reconciliation found 391 completed Feb–Mar calls never ingested and nothing alerted, because `call_log` can only report on calls it received. One admin bell per missed call (`bell: true`, since category `alert` is silenced under `GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY` unless allowlisted; added in #6267, before that the bell was written but never rang), deduped forever on the notification `dedupeKey`; MORE than 3 fresh misses in one run (4 or more) collapse into one aggregate bell per hour (ingest is down). Read-only against Twilio; writes nothing but admin notifications. Off: no diff runs; an ingest break (webhook outage, misrouted number, signature failure) is invisible until someone looks. Kill: unset the variable and redeploy.
Call-processing stall watchdog: `GATE_CALL_PROCESSING_STALL_WATCHDOG` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, boot-read (`callProcessingStallWatchdog`); ON in production. On, a cron every 7 minutes (`server/services/call-processing-stall-watchdog.js`, scheduled in `scheduler.js`) rings an admin bell for a `call_log` row with a real recording 11 s or longer (or a PAN-quarantined masked transcript, which has no duration floor), older than the 20-minute grace, whose `processing_status` is still NULL / `pending` / `processing`; a `processing` claim counts once its heartbeat is 8 minutes quiet (`CLAIM_STALE_MINUTES`, just under the processor's own reclaim window) OR once the claim is older than the absolute ceiling (`alertCeilingMinutes()` in `server/utils/claim-ceiling.js`: the processor's full provider budget from the `CALL_PROC_*_TIMEOUT_MS` variables plus headroom), so a pass that still beats but has run past the budget rings too. Terminal states (`processed`, `voicemail`, `spam`, `no_transcription`, `extraction_failed`) never ring: they have their own lanes. Why: 2026-08-31 a hot lead call sat unprocessed 18 minutes after a pass died and the manual retry was silently refused; one row had been wedged in `processing` since 07-10. One bell per call per DAY (dedupeKey); MORE than 3 in one run (4 or more) collapse into one aggregate bell (the processor itself is down). 7 minutes and not 5 so the check never phase-locks to the 5-minute sweep and a crash-reclaim loop cannot hide. Off: a stalled call waits until a person notices. Kill: unset and redeploy.
Unrecorded-call watchdog: `GATE_UNRECORDED_CALL_WATCHDOG` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, boot-read (`unrecordedCallWatchdog`); ON in production. Not a cron of its own: it is the "Twilio has no recording either" step of the 5-minute missing-recording sweep (`recoverMissingRecentRecordings` in `call-recording-processor.js` calls `server/services/unrecorded-call-watchdog.js` on each `no_completed_recording` result, AFTER the Twilio lookup, so a recording recovered in the same pass can never race a bell). Rings for an inbound completed call 60 s or longer, 30 minutes after `created_at + duration_seconds` (the call's end when `created_at` is the `/voice` ingest time; for a row first written by the terminal `/call-status` fallback, `metadata.source` `status_callback`, `created_at` is already after the call, so that row rings about one call length later), that Twilio holds no recording for; voicemail (`<Record>` lane) and the AI relay session are exempt, PAN-quarantined rows never reach it. Why: 2026-08-29 a human-answered 4:17 call produced no recording (DB pool exhausted by the :30 cron fan-out, Railway 502, Twilio fell back to the number's static voice-fallback TwiML, a plain `<Dial>` with no `record`); the ingest watchdog saw a known SID and nothing rang; the caller became a bare number in Communications. One bell per call (`bell: true`, deduped forever); MORE than 3 fresh misses in one pass (4 or more) collapse into one aggregate bell. The sweep's candidate ORDER also reads this module's thresholds so alert-eligible rows get the 25-row window first. Off: the sweep still asks Twilio every 5 minutes and stays silent forever on `no_completed_recording`. Kill: unset and redeploy. Open follow-up (audit 2026-10-09): the static voice-fallback TwiML on the Twilio number has not been verified to carry `record`.
Callback spam closes the parent voicemail (dark): `GATE_CALLBACK_SPAM_CLOSES_PARENT` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, boot-read via `isEnabled('callbackSpamClosesParent')` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, when an office callback (an OUTBOUND `call_log` row with `source` admin-callback and `metadata.relatedCallId`, the admin "Call back" action on a voicemail writes both) lands a spam verdict, two existing lifecycles settle the parent. Cards: `closeParentOnCallbackSpam` (`server/services/call-recording-processor.js`, right after the callback's fenced terminal write on both spam paths) takes the shared per-call triage lock first (`lockTriageCall`, `server/utils/triage-locks.js`), fences (the callback row must still read `processing_status` spam, the calling pass's `processing_generation`, no live `processing_token`; else `verdict_superseded`), checks eligibility (the callback was placed by an admin: `metadata.placed_by_role`, stamped by the call route from the verified session, never from the request body, so a technician's callback settles nothing, `not_admin_placed`; `resolution_source` auto, `resolution_rule` callback_spam), syncs `review_status` through `syncCallReviewStatus` and stamps `metadata.callback_verdict`. Cards that judge on-file data stay (on_file_* conflicts, missing_unit_number, email_unverified, caller_not_authorized, out_of_service_area, property_role_confirm), and so does callback_number_needed (the caller said the inbound number was not theirs). The nightly triage auto-resolve sweep (`server/services/triage-auto-resolve.js`, rule `callback_spam`; its evidence loader applies the same voicemail / number eligibility and answers to this gate alone, not to GATE_TRIAGE_AUTO_RESOLVE_EVIDENCE; with GATE_TRIAGE_AUTO_RESOLVE off the sweep still runs for this one rule under this gate, `sweep({ only: 'callback_spam' })`, so turning the master gate off does not stop these re-closes; turn this gate off for that) re-closes a moot card a later reprocess of the voicemail filed again. The callback promise: the processor only asks `refreshFulfillment` (`server/services/call-commitments.js`) to run now; its callback resolver reads the spam callback as a `callback_spam` proof (`callbackReachedSolicitor`, consulted only while this gate is on; and, under the same gate, the connected-call proofs `cardConnectedCall` / `returnedOutboundCall` count a callback only once settled: no `processing_token`, and a status that is neither spam nor one a later pass may still turn into spam (`UNSETTLED_CALLBACK_STATUSES`: pending, processing, extraction_failed, no_transcription; a never-processed row counts only without a recording), so a solicitor call mid-pass is never recorded as a kept promise, and the lapse scan `listLapsedEvidenceClosedCallIds` lists a call-proof close whose call no longer meets that condition, an evidence close or a promise kept on resolveCallback's direct proof alike (index `call_commitments_direct_call_proof_index`, migration 20261010300000), so `refreshFulfillment` judges it again (`keptOnCall`) and dismisses it on the spam callback: source admin-callback, linked to the promise or its call, dialed to the caller's number, after the promise's evidence boundary, so a promise staff renewed after the attempt is never touched) and dismisses it like a customer who left, closing the promise's open admin reminders in the same transaction as the dismissal, as a staff action on its card would, and closing a rolling missed-follow-up list that names it (marked emptied with the remaining members, so the SLA watcher's next tick posts an accurate list) (`closeCallbackReminders`, done by `callback:spam`) (the promise's call must itself be an inbound voicemail, and the dismissal is written under a share lock on the callback row only while it still reads spam, so a refresh that raced a correction writes nothing; the lookups use the partial index `call_log_admin_callback_spam_related_call_id_index`, migration 20261010270000); the commitments watchdog retires its reminders as for any closed promise. Correction (it runs with the gate OFF too: a rollback blocks new settlements and never strands cards or promises the feature closed; it retires whatever the callback settled whether or not the parent still qualifies today, and a promise owed again is refreshed at once so the corrected call can keep it): every fenced terminal write of an office callback goes through `settleParentForCallbackVerdict` (spam/voicemail, veto, rejected-transcript and main paths); any non-spam verdict runs `reopenParentOnCallbackCorrected` (a no-op `no_verdict` when nothing was settled; when the parent itself was since reprocessed to spam its cards stay closed on its own verdict but the promise is still judged, `parentSpam`), which recomputes the parent's verdict from every linked callback: while another eligible spam callback still stands (same number, after the call's end; read FOR SHARE so no pass can claim it before the correction commits) the cards stay closed, the stamp names it and each promise this callback dismissed is judged again with the full proof from its own evidence boundary (`rejudgeCallbackSpamDismissals` runs `callbackReachedSolicitor`: a standing callback placed for that promise or for the call, after the call's end or the staff reopen / edit that renewed the promise, keeps it dismissed on its evidence; a sibling promise's callback, or one from before the renewal, keeps nothing, so the promise is owed again); otherwise one canonical card per reason reopens (the newest callback_spam row, only where no open / in_progress row for that reason exists), the stamp goes, `review_status` follows and, in the same transaction, `reopenCallbackSpamDismissals, each reopen an `audit_log` `callback_spam_reopen` event the promise-chaser bell versions its dedupe key on` reopens the promise that callback dismissed (a card staff confirmed or edited included, the same scope the dismissal could reach; a card staff dismissed stands). `rejudgeCallbackSpamDismissals` reads each promise FOR UPDATE and writes only the row it read (status, human state, evidence, `updated_at`), so a staff ledger action that landed first stands. Durability: the callback's terminal write commits before the correction runs, so every commitments-watchdog tick first runs `reconcileCorrectedCallbackVerdicts` (this gate alone, before the watchdog's own GATE_CALL_COMMITMENTS check, under its own cron lock): every source reads only callbacks or parents changed in the last 30 days (`updated_at`, indexed by migrations 20261010310000 and 20261010320000); it runs every five minutes under this gate when callback cards are off (the scheduler's cards tick otherwise, and the 7:20 AM daily sweep always); it finishes a settlement lost before the stamp (a recent admin-placed spam callback whose parent has no stamp and still has a moot card or a callback promise: `closeParentOnCallbackSpam` again) and one whose promise refresh was lost (a recent stamp, the callback still spam, a callback promise still open that predates the callback and was not renewed since: `refreshFulfillment` again) and it finds every callback that no longer reads spam while a parent is still stamped with it, every spam callback whose parent was re-read as something other than a voicemail (stamp or dismissal retired), a promise still dismissed on it, or a card the sweep closed on it is still the newest row for its reason (that source applies lockCallbackPair's eligibility in SQL, so an ineligible callback never fills the batch) (partial indexes, migrations 20261010280000 and 20261010290000) and runs the same correction. The parent's `processing_status`, lead and customer are never touched. Nothing is sent. Fail-soft: a failure is one warn line and the callback's own verdict stands.
