Call extraction V1 backup provider (dark): `GATE_CALL_EXTRACTION_V1_FALLBACK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callExtractionV1FallbackLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; `callExtractionV1Fallback` in the gates map is for `logGateStatus` only). Incident 2026-10-21: the V1 extractor (`extractCallData` in `server/services/call-recording-processor.js`) called Gemini only; Gemini answered HTTP 402 "prepayment credits are depleted" from about 04:00 ET and 19 of 19 recorded calls failed three attempts to `extraction_failed`, so no voicemail alerts, leads or promises. On, when the Gemini leg fails for a PROVIDER reason (non-2xx HTTP including 402/429/5xx, a network error or timeout, `GEMINI_API_KEY` missing, or invalid JSON after the existing two parse attempts), the SAME prompt goes through the house dispatcher (`dispatchWithFallback`, `server/services/llm/call.js`, route `callExtractionV1Backup`): Claude first (`MODELS.CALL_EXTRACTION_ANTHROPIC`, the pinned model the V2 Claude leg uses; override `MODEL_CALL_EXTRACTION_ANTHROPIC`), then OpenAI (`CALL_EXTRACTION_MODEL`, default `gpt-5.6-sol`, the pinned V2 OpenAI leg). Each leg is a pinned model, never a tier alias. The answer goes through the same `normalizeCallExtraction` tail as the Gemini answer, so the output shape is identical. The provider that served it is stamped as `extraction_v1_provider` (plus `extraction_v1_model`, `extraction_v1_fallback_reason`) in `call_log.metadata.processing_timings` and a `[call-proc] V1 extraction served by ...` warn line is logged; the dispatcher also files its usual ledger rows (lane `call_extraction_v1`) and, with `GATE_LLM_DISPATCH_METRICS`, an `llm_dispatch_log` row. A content problem that is not a provider failure keeps today's behavior. When every backup leg fails the call takes the same path as before: the Gemini error rethrows into the `extraction_failed` path (attempt counter and triage unchanged), or the invalid-JSON stub is returned. A call that Gemini served never calls a backup provider. Off = Gemini only, byte-identical. Sends nothing to a customer; each fallback call costs one Claude (or OpenAI) extraction. Rollback: unset.

Callback spoken-number link (dark): `GATE_CALLBACK_SPOKEN_NUMBER_LINK` — **ships DARK: off unless set (strict `=== 'true'`)**, read at call time via `callbackSpokenNumberLinkLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner audit 2026-10-20. An office callback (an OUTBOUND `call_log` row with `source` admin-callback and `metadata.relatedCallId`) dials the voicemail's caller ID, but the caller may have SPOKEN another number to ring back (stored in the voicemail's `ai_extraction.phone`) that is already a customer's, for instance from a quote form filed minutes after the voicemail. The pass looked up the dialed number only, found nobody and created a duplicate customer. On, `findCustomerViaCallbackSpokenNumber` (`server/services/call-recording-processor.js`, called in Step 3 right after the normal phone lookup) runs ONLY when that lookup found no customer and no ambiguous shared number, the call has no operator link override, the related call is an inbound VOICEMAIL (`isVoicemailParent`: `call_outcome` / `answered_by` / `processing_status`; a Call Log "Call back" on an ordinary call also writes `admin-callback`) whose caller ID is the number this callback dialed, and its spoken number is a usable external number that differs from the dialed one by more than two digits (one or two digits off is a misheard digit, the `phoneNearMissOfAni` rule). It then looks up live customers whose PRIMARY phone (`customers.phone`, never a slot) is the spoken number and whose first name agrees with the callback's extraction (`sameSpokenFirstName`; the last name is ignored, transcribers misspell it), and links only when exactly one customer matches (a household number with two members of the same first name links no one). The voicemail's extraction is read only once that voicemail is settled (`isSettledParent`: no pass holds its token, not in a retryable state such as `extraction_failed`, no adopted recording waiting); while a reprocess or retry is replacing it, the callback stays on its capped `extraction_failed` retry instead of acting on the old spoken number. The card is decided before the pass's authoritative contact-number lookup; if that lookup then links the call or finds a shared number, the pass retires the callback card (`retireCallbackSpokenNumberCard`, same lock and token fence). The match is a SUGGESTION, never a link (Codex #6419 r2: anyone can name another person's number in a voicemail and answer the callback with that person's first name). It rides the EXISTING advisory `family_account_candidates` card as a new basis, `callback_spoken_number` (`matchCallbackSpokenNumberAccount` in `server/services/call-family-name-link.js`, tried after the family and contact-phone bases and before the caller's-own-account bases; the card shows the account, the number said in the voicemail as the account's "has the number", and the number the callback dialed), so it inherits that card's whole lifecycle: a reprocess refreshes the open card or retires it when the match is gone (an in_progress card is never touched), admin-only, Resolve / Dismiss bound to the version staff saw, call review status sync, not a call verdict. Staff confirm and use the call's relink action (`metadata.customer_link_override`), which is also how they undo a wrong suggestion. The basis exists only while the pass's own lookup on the contact number (`findCustomerForCallContact`, with the same address-disambiguation inputs, built once as `contactLookupOpts` and shared by Step 3 and the card) finds nobody and no ambiguous shared number; the card checks that for open cards too, so a card is retired once the dialed number links normally. The pass sets its own read-only match flag after that lookup, so a failed card write never turns into a new customer (the next reprocess files the card again). The card's callback number is the number the office dialed (`call.to_phone`). While the card suggests it, the pass keeps the call customer-less exactly as in the shared-phone case: no customer is created, nothing is written to the matched customer (no email or address backfill, no phone-match mark, no property record), nothing is sent to them, the workable-lead path treats the number as unclaimed-only, and the call does not close as customer_creation_failed. The contact number used for texts and confirmations stays the dialed one. The path FAILS CLOSED AND RETRYABLE: a failed lookup of the voicemail or its owner is unknown, not "no match", and a match with no durable card (the write failed, or no card was filed, refreshed or already held by an operator; a card a person closed by hand ends the suppression instead) is not finalized either; both throw `CALLBACK_SPOKEN_NUMBER_UNRESOLVED` (reason code only, no phone or name) into the pass's outer guard, which stamps the existing capped `extraction_failed` retry (and its blocking card at the cap), and no customer is created meanwhile. The owner must be an active, not soft-deleted account (any pipeline stage, like the contact-phone basis; a quote-form customer is still a lead stage). A card an operator closed by hand is not reopened by a reprocess, and the pass then behaves as it did before this gate. Off: byte-identical to before (no extra query). Kill: unset `GATE_CALLBACK_SPOKEN_NUMBER_LINK`; cards already filed stay open until staff resolve them (a reprocess with the gate off retires an open one).

Estimate image analysis (`satellite-analyzer.js`, `property-lookup-v2.js`) uses `TEXT_POLICIES.estimateVision`: Gemini 3.8 Flash → GPT-6 Sol only. `MODEL_OPENAI_ESTIMATE_VISION` overrides the Sol fallback; generic `OPENAI_MODEL` / `OPENAI_VISION_MODEL` pins do not affect these image lanes. The separate property-record web-search trio is unchanged.

Good / Better / Best on a pest + lawn estimate (owner 2026-10-05; reworked onto the opt-out rail the same day, after the first design — precomputed tiers on a one-time-flag row, #5921/#5929, reverted here — mispriced the pest-only tier and needed tier-specific handling on every surface): `GATE_ESTIMATE_OFFER_TIERS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `estimateOfferTiersLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_ESTIMATE_SERVICE_OPT_OUT` (live). The picker is a VIEW over the service opt-out rail (`server/services/estimate-offer-tiers.js`): **Best** = the estimate as quoted (pest + lawn), **Better** = lawn removed through `PUT /api/estimates/:token/service-opt-out` (the canonical engine re-price: the pest plan at its own tier and setup fee), **Good** = the one-time choice on that pest-only row. The stored row is always an ordinary valid estimate, so accept, slots, card holds, the text agent, admin and emails need no tier handling, and turning the gate off leaves every row in a normal state. What is new: (1) `POST /calculate-estimate` marks a result the office may offer tiers on (`offerTiersAvailable`: residential, recurring program exactly pest + lawn, no member evidence) and the estimate tool defaults its "Offer Good / Better / Best" checkbox on; the save stamps `estimate_data.offerTiersRequested` when asked and eligible (a marker only — the one-time option stays OFF on the row). (2) `/data` carries a top-level `offerTiers` block for a marked, accept-active row when the rail itself would allow the move: `state` (`best` | `pest_only`) plus `good` / `better` / `best` figures, the other state's numbers being the rail's OWN dry run (`buildOfferTiersBlock`). (3) The rail's commit sets `show_one_time_option` on a marked row from the lawn line (`oneTimeOptionUpdateForMixChange`): ON when lawn is removed — by the customer or by the live "lead with one service" send-time park — and the delivery validator allows it on the repriced row; ALWAYS OFF when lawn is added back, gate or no gate, because the one-time toggle drops companion programs at accept. Tree & shrub is not a tier companion (the rail refuses its removal). Off, or unset: no marker is stamped, no block is served, the rail never turns the option on, and every payload is byte-identical to today.

Lawn report coverage on default zones (owner 2026-10-06, after a local test of the first 3 open lawn visits): `GATE_LAWN_COVERAGE_HIDE_DEFAULT_ZONES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnCoverageHideDefaultZonesLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The verdict is FROZEN at completion, never computed at render. While the gate is live, the lawn write gate (`finalizeLawnReportSynthesis`, `lawn-report-write-gate.js`, post-commit, after the technician's zone writes for the visit) decides once whether the visit's coverage zones are only the schematic defaults (no active `property_zones` row keeps a technician satellite mark, a non-empty `geometry_image`, after drift resolution) and freezes `structured_notes.lawnCoverageVerdict = { v: 1, defaultsOnly, frozenAt }` (`lawn-coverage-verdict.js`), first writer wins, in a guarded statement of its own. A failed zone or geometry read at completion freezes nothing. A LAWN report render with the gate live returns `serviceCoverage: { enabled: false }` (no Lawn Coverage section) ONLY when the frozen verdict says `defaultsOnly: true`; it never reads zone rows to decide. A visit with no frozen verdict (every visit completed before the flip, a freeze made while the gate was off, or a failed freeze) renders exactly as with the gate off, so older reports are unchanged and a later zone write never flips a report. The defaults are stock rectangles named after the chipped areas ("Front/Rear/Left/Right perimeter") under a satellite photo captioned as marked on site by the technician, which nobody did; the product card already says the whole lawn was treated. A visit with marked zones keeps its section, and every other service line is unchanged. The cached lawn PDF key carries `:covhide=1` only while the gate is live AND the record's frozen verdict is `defaultsOnly: true`. Off = byte-identical payload and key.
Lawn report facts frozen at completion (owner 2026-10-08, after the three stage-1 test reports; `server/services/service-report/lawn-report-facts.js`, `lawn-report-write-gate.js`, `reentry.js`, `lawn-visit-summary.js`): `GATE_LAWN_REPORT_FACTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnReportFactsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The gate controls ONLY the freeze; a render and the PDF key read what the record already carries and never the gate (lesson of #6087 and #6089: a decision made at render time races the stored-PDF cache). While live, the lawn write gate (`finalizeLawnReportSynthesis`, post-commit, BEFORE the first report build so the v6 copy's first freeze already sees it) reads the visit's `service_products` rows with their frozen product facts, the linked assessment's reviewed run and the technician's treatment-guide taps, and freezes `structured_notes.lawnReportFacts = { v: 1, frozenAt, reentry, productUse, ties }`, first writer wins, in a guarded statement of its own (a failed product or catalog read freezes nothing). (1) **Ready to re-enter is a condition**: each product gets a rule only from facts the visit froze (never a name, never the method alone, and never weaker than the label floor the report shows today): a product with NO approved frozen facts, or whose frozen label is not plainly "until dry" (a stored positive `rei_hours`, a re-entry text that states hours or cannot be read, or no text at all, because a catalog NULL freezes as 0), has no usable fact and is marked `source: 'default'`; a second accepted label is the standard granule sentence "Stay off treated areas until the product has been watered in and the turf is dry." (recognized narrowly in `lawn-report-facts.js`, no digit or time word, no stored hours; the shared SMS parser does not read it), which gives `watered_in_and_dry` ONLY with a frozen water-in watering rule (hold, none or missing: default); otherwise a frozen water-in watering rule means `watered_in_and_dry`; a granule whose rule is hold or none, and a bait, mean `dry`; a granule with no frozen watering rule has no usable fact (default); any spray or spot spray means `dry`; a row with no recorded method defaults. The visit takes the strictest (dry < watered_in_and_dry); one defaulted product marks the visit `default` and it keeps today's 30 minute clock. There is no timed rule: a product with label hours defaults. A record with a real rule prints "Ready to walk on once the application has dried — your technician confirms timing." (the clause is the approved idiom's own: `REENTRY_SAFE_COPY`, `social-media.js`; nothing is stored as text, so the wording applies to every read) (every `dry` product: spray, spot spray, bait, or a granule that is not watered in; method-neutral) or "Ready to walk on once today's treatment has dried and, after you water it in, the grass is dry again — your technician confirms timing." (granular or mixed) and "Keep people and pets off the lawn until then.", with no clock time and no seconds countdown, in the Ready to Re-enter card, the status chip and hero result, the PDF, the report email, the Ask Waves facts and answers, the AI summary facts and the aftercare card (`reportV2.aftercare.reentry`); all read `dynamicContext.reentry` (`condition`, `customerSummary`, `petAdvisory`, `targets: []`). An admin correction of the re-entry minutes (`reentry_adjusted`) keeps the clock for that record. The tech completion panel's re-entry steppers stay as they are (seeds 30 / 0): a stepper override on a record that carries a frozen condition does not change what the customer sees (the condition wins), and on a `default` record it works exactly as before. (2) **A spot product says where it was used** (only for a completion from the lawn Fast Complete sheet, the one surface that sends the `lawnFast` echo; the re-service sheet and the full form record the location themselves, so their spot rows get no override and the recorded application area renders as it always did; on the sheet, a row with an explicit recorded location beyond the default plan areas keeps it too, the place being more precise than the extent): a `spot_treatment` row freezes its area ONLY when the technician recorded one as the spot's extent (the sheet names those rows in `lawnFast.spotAreas`, frozen as `structured_notes.lawnSpotAreaRecorded` while the gate is live; a row sized by a typed amount, or whose `areaValue` is the planned or whole-lawn fallback, is not named), and the card, the PDF and the fixed "what was applied" answer read "Spot treatment, about 250 sq ft" (5 sq ft steps under 100, 10 under 1,000, 50 above) or "Spot treatment" when no area was recorded (`applications[].areaUse`); whole-lawn rows keep their zone text. (3) **A finding is tied to what was applied** (live only while `GATE_LAWN_VISIT_SUMMARY_V2` is also live, one helper `lawnReportTiesLive()`: the Visit Summary writes the sentences and the v6 copy, always live, prints the curative "What to expect" line; with the Visit Summary dark no tie is frozen and the standing chinch tap records nothing new; the re-entry condition and the spot text need neither): fungal findings and a fungicide, weed findings and a herbicide spot, insect findings and an insecticide spot, drought stress and the wetting agent (kept reviewed findings of the visit's own run, label to kind by `KIND_BY_LABEL`); the technician's chinch bugs, caterpillars or fungus tap (`lawnTreatmentGuide` card `checked: 'found'`, `taken: true`, read through `guideTakenFindings`) is a finding too, but only after it is VERIFIED at completion (the echo comes from the client): the card's product ids must be applied on the visit, of the card's kind, and staged program rows of that kind (`verifyGuideFind`: a fungicide row, the caterpillar row, a chinch rung), a fungus or caterpillar card must match a finding on the confirmed assessment (the guide's own thresholds), and the standing chinch tap (offered every month) is checked against its rungs alone; an unverified find stays on the technician record and never becomes a customer tie; a product the expectations engine locks to preventive (Acelepryn) never counts as treating a finding, so the tie and the "What to expect" line cannot disagree; the Visit Summary's six-sentence cap counts individual sentences and drops whole parts (results line, next-visit line, area read, then the second tie), never half a tie, and the standing "Chinch bugs found at the edge of damage" tap is now recorded as a `chinch` card with `checked: 'found'`, `taken: true`. A PHOTO tie never says that spot or that area was treated (no place is recorded for a spot row yet): "Today’s photos showed {label} in one area. Today’s visit included {a fungicide treatment | a spot treatment for weeds | a spot treatment for insects | a wetting agent treatment}." (or, hedged, "...showed what may be {label} in one area, and today’s visit included {...}."); only the technician's own find says "Your technician found {...} and treated that spot today." The facts are frozen BEFORE anything can render or queue a render: `freezeReportFactsOnly` runs in the completion path ahead of the report-token mint and the PDF render queue (the lawn write gate's own call later is a no-op), so no report is built or cached without the block. One attempt decides: if the attempt FAILS (a product, catalog, assessment, run or program read, a find whose verification read failed, or the write), a MARKED block `{ v: 1, failed: true, productUse: {} }` is recorded instead, with no re-entry rule (the report keeps today's default clock, never anything weaker), no spot text and no ties; every later reader and attempt (the write gate's own call, a resumed completion, the v6 copy, the summary, the PDF key) agrees with it, so nothing can freeze different facts after copy has frozen. A write that answers null (the swallowed write error) is a failed attempt too, so the marker is attempted before anything renders. If the marker write ALSO fails nothing is on the record: the completion path then holds the PDF pre-render (no render before the facts are decided), and the write gate's later call freezes no tie once the v6 copy or the Visit Summary exists. Ties are also never frozen once the v6 copy or the Visit Summary has already frozen without a block. A completion that resumes after the gates changed writes the Visit Summary version its record's frozen tie block calls for (v4 when the record holds ties for the assessment); the live gate decides only whether NEW facts may be frozen. An incomplete closeout returns before the report path (no token, no delivery, no lawn write gate), so no facts are frozen for it and its report is never sent to the customer. The Visit Summary freezes version 4 (`lawnVisitSummary[assessmentId].v === 4`) with the ties in `slots.ties`; version 3 entries still render exactly as frozen. A matched PHOTO tie prints only while the report's own card for its topic shows a concern (`watch` or `needs_attention`: fungus and insects read the damage and disease card, weeds the weed pressure card), the same check the ordinary findings sentence uses, decided once at freeze from the same card reads (`matchedTiePrints`); a minor read on a healthy card prints no tie and no curative line, so the report never says "No clear stress patterns" and "Today’s photos showed gray leaf spot" together. A technician's own find stays authoritative whatever the card shows, and a drought photo tie has no card to check. A tied product's "What to expect" line reads curative (`lawn-expectations.js`, `tiedFamilies`; fungicide and insecticide rows; `frozenTiedFamilies` applies the same card check from the render's own diagnosis). A finding with no matching product says "We will check it by hand at the next visit." and only on a recurring plan visit with a real next visit, while the report's own card for that topic shows a concern; a treatment is never promised. The lawn PDF key carries `:rf=<hash>` only for a record that holds a frozen decision. Off = identical frozen notes and payload. Rollback: unset the variable (a record already frozen keeps its decision, by design).
Lawn report month detail (owner 2026-10-06: "add more detail here ... use the labels, seasonality"): `GATE_LAWN_PROGRAM_DETAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnProgramDetailLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Needs `GATE_LAWN_EXPECTATIONS` (it rides beside the v13 month sentence and only where that sentence shows; only the lead layout mounts the card); strict `'true'` only (`1` / `on` do not enable it). On, `buildLawnReportV2` adds `snapshot.seasonalDetail` = `{ whyNow }` from `lawn-program-line.js` `PROGRAM_DETAIL_V13` for the visit month, and the lead layout's "This time of year" card renders "Why now" under the sentence. Copy restates each v13 month step by category (no product, brand, active ingredient or rate; a test enforces it) plus Southwest Florida seasons (dry Nov-May, rainy Jun-Sep, summer nitrogen limits). No watering advice rides in it (the Water This Week card and label aftercare own that); a conditional step such as the weed barrier keeps "where it fits the property". Off = byte-identical payload.

Lawn protocol v13 (owner 2026-10-05, PRs 2 and 3 of the 3-way split of #5942; plan `~/lawn-program-scope-20261001/v13-app-load.html`, program `protocol-v13-20261005.md`): `GATE_LAWN_V13` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lawnV13Live()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, one universal lawn program (the same 12 month steps for every grass; 9x plans run the same step for their months, except April: a visit on a 9x plan takes LESCO Dimension 0.21% 18-0-10 at 2.78 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.5 lb N) in place of the 12x plan's April bag, chosen from the recipe's `cadenceVariants` by the visit's plan, read from the booked catalog service then the visit's service name (`lawnVisitsPerYear`); an unknown plan keeps the 12x step and warns `lawn_v13_plan_cadence_unknown`; the plan's cadence ranks the cadence-specific catalog service, then the series recurrence (`recurring_pattern` every_6_weeks / monthly / bimonthly, or a custom 42-, 30- or 60-day gap), then the service name; the tank sheet reads the same from `?scheduledServiceId=` (the Schedule page sends its visit id) and takes `?visitsPerYear=` as an override, and with neither keeps the 12x step and warns; the material-cost audit prices each plan's own step and the lawn-outline facts count the 9x product against April; the 9x extras stay a tech choice from the visit note) replaces the old four-track program with three tracks (`st_augustine`, `bermuda`, `zoysia`; no `bahia`, see below) wherever the portal reads the lawn recipe for planning (a lawn whose recorded grass names no track of its own, such as mixed, unknown or free text, plans from the `st_augustine` copy of the one program, `lawnV13AnyGrassTrack()`, instead of blocking with `missing_protocol_visit`; planning only, in the plan engine's `selectProtocolVisit`; `loadCustomerGrassContext`, which also feeds historical report context, keeps such a lawn untracked, and a blank grass keeps its old handling): `server/services/lawn-program.js` `lawnProtocols()` returns `server/config/lawn-protocol-v13.json` instead of `protocols.json` `lawn` for the plan engine (job card, mix sheet, Fast Complete prefill), the admin protocol routes (tank sheet, programs, completion actions), the protocol reader and IB tool, inventory references and the material-cost audit; the Protocol reference tab shows the track's own `safety_rules`. The same recipe feeds the service outline (stamped `lawn-v13` instead of `lawn-v4`, so a flip shows older outlines as updated; its season-focus bullets name treatment categories only, such as pre-emergent weed control, micronutrients, insect control, disease control, weed spot treatment and wetting agent, and never a product name or rate), the KB sync and the knowledge index (both persist what they read; the lawn KB entries (one per track the live program holds: three under v13, four under the old program) carry a `lawn-v13` tag while they hold v13, and `reconcileLawnProtocolKnowledge`, a 15-minute tick in `scheduler.js` that takes the nightly `knowledge-index-sync` lock (and records its own job health as `lawn-knowledge-reconcile`), rewrites those entries and the `protocol` and `kb` index corpora as soon as the gate and the stored program disagree, either way (the entries' tags and one `system_settings` marker per corpus are what it compares; `syncCorpus` writes the marker for the `protocol` and `kb` corpora, so the reconcile and the 02:40 nightly both maintain it, from the program the corpus loaded and only after a sync that really ran (never a skipped one), so a failure or a skipped corpus after the entries were rewritten is retried on the next tick; the marker names the program and, for v13, its sorted track set (`v13:bermuda,st_augustine,zoysia`), so a recipe that gains or loses a track marks an already-indexed corpus stale and the next tick rebuilds it (v13 dropping bahia removed the bahia text from the protocol and kb indexes this way); an absent marker is unknown and reads as stale; each corpus is checked only while it has chunks of its own, so the first tick after deploy syncs each populated corpus once; a partial set of the program's entries is stale, an entry for a track the program lacks (the old bahia entry once v13 is live) is stale until the lawn sync deletes it (auto-sync entries only), and the lawn sync throws before touching the corpora when an entry could not be written; the pricing knowledge entry's `Tracks:` line follows the live program the same way), so unsetting the gate reverts them within one tick; the index chunks re-embed on the nightly run), and the program line: `lawn-program-line.js` uses the v13 month sentences when `GATE_LAWN_EXPECTATIONS` is also on and the visit's plan resolved the staged v13 version (the closeout's completion ledger row, else the scheduled visit's pin); a visit with no recorded version (completed before protocol assignment existed) or one pinned to an older version gets no program line and keeps the season note (the retired per-grass sentences were removed; one named soil tests, which Waves does not run), so a past report is never rewritten with a program the visit did not run. `getActiveLawnProtocol` (`lawn-protocol-operating-layer.js`) resolves ONLY the staged version `2026.10-v13` for a visit with no assignment, and only for a PLANNING caller (`planning: true`: the plan engine, tank sheet, pre-visit brief, live lawn assessment, `/admin/protocols/lawn/active` and `/lawn/window`); a historical reader, the public service report context included, never passes it and keeps the pre-gate resolution (the record's own ledger row or pin, else the active version), so a legacy completed record never reads as having followed v13 (the public report payload shape is unchanged, so `docs/public-route-contracts.md` needs no entry). With no staged row (migrations not run, or a key with no active baseline) a planning lookup returns nothing, never the old active version. The plan resolves a visit's pinned assignment whatever `GATE_LAWN_COMPLETION_DEFAULTS` and `GATE_LAWN_PROPERTY_HISTORY` say, and a visit whose structured protocol is not the staged v13 one (no staged row, or pinned to an older version, since the recipe is v13 for the whole portal) is blocked (`lawn_v13_protocol_missing`) with no calculated products at all: `mixCalculator.items`, `conditionalOptions`, `protocol.base` and `protocol.conditional` are empty, so no panel or job card shows an amount; a visit already pinned to the staged v13 protocol while the gate is OFF is blocked the same way (`lawn_v13_gate_off`, no calculated products) whatever the completion-default gates say; each plan item carries the v13 row's `gates` and `gateNotes` (required notes, such as Tetrino's 25 ft from water, also show as plan warnings `lawn_v13_product_gate`; an apply-alone product selected beside another product blocks with `lawn_v13_apply_alone`, offers no mixing order and withholds every quantity of the selected products, in the plan and on the tank sheet alike); the tank sheet answers 409 `lawn_v13_protocol_missing`, and for a visit-less sheet applies the same gate notes, warnings and apply-alone rule through the shared helpers (`blocks`, an empty `mixingOrder`, and every quantity of the selected products withheld; the Protocol reference tab shows the block as an alert); the live lawn assessment reads the visit's own protocol key and version, not only its window key; the material-cost audit refuses to run. The tank sheet narrows a `sunnyTurfOnly` row (Tetrino) to the half the plan assumes without a turf profile, and `/admin/inventory/lawn-outline-facts` lists the v13 recipe's own products (exact catalog names) instead of the legacy list. Needs the PR 1 migrations (`20261005120000` .. `20261005160000`, plus `20261006140000` the prodiamine yearly cap, `20261006150000` the 9x April product row, `20261006160000` its rollback reconcile, `20261006170000` the caps at the catalog's verified annual label maximum (65 WDG 0.83 oz, 4FL 1.1 fl oz; the granulars keep the derived cap because their stored maximum is per application) and `20261006180000` the ownership record that makes a rollback leave a Dimension row the window already held untouched: staged protocol, catalog rows and links, rollback order and EPA numbers, then the round-3 migration that restores the product safety gate keys and classes the two combination pre-emergents as herbicide pesticides). With the gate on, every matched v13 line goes through ONE decision (`v13LineState`) in the plan and on the tank sheet: it keeps its protocol product (a saved substitution is never applied; the plan warns `lawn_v13_substitution_ignored`), reads its own staged row, and is UNAVAILABLE (no amount, `unavailable` on the item, plan warning `lawn_v13_line_unlinked`) when no row is linked to the matched catalog product, never the catalog default; the plan also reads `product_limits` through the application-limits reader over the customer's own history for each selected v13 product (a yearly cap shared by every formulation of one active ingredient, prodiamine: `annual_max_rate` rows with `match_type` `active_ingredient`, one per product in that product's own unit per 1,000 sq ft, migration `20261006140000`, adds Prodiamine 65 WDG, Stonewall 4FL and the Stonewall granulars as shares of the 1.5 lb ai/acre label cap and counts the planned application with them, judged on applications up to the visit's own date and, when the visit has a property, on that property's ledger rows only (a row whose property is unknown still counts, and with no property the whole customer counts); the tank sheet opened with `?scheduledServiceId=` applies the same limit decision as the plan; after a completion that crosses it the response's `completionAdvisories` carries the message and dispatch gets one `application_limit` alert, the completion itself never blocked), and a hard limit (an annual cap such as Celsius, an interval, a blackout) blocks that selection with no amount and the limit's own message (`lawn_v13_annual_limit`), while a warning-level limit (for example a minimum interval set to warn) becomes a plan warning with the limit's own message (`lawn_v13_limit_warning`) and leaves the dose alone; with the gate off no v13 field (`gates`, `gateNotes`, `spot`, `unavailable`) is added to any item, so the payload is the old one; `/admin/protocols/completion-actions` lists lawn products with no catalog rates while the gate is on and points to the visit plan's completion defaults for amounts; the recipe's lines match catalog products by FULL catalog name only (a missing product leaves the line unmatched; no partial-name stand-in); a v13 SPOT row (backpack work: Arena, Artavia, Velista, Gravex, Acelepryn, Talak, Celsius, Certainty, Blindside, Dismiss, Dispatch, the surfactant) and a label-rate row (Dylox 6.2 G) get NO calculated quantity anywhere (plan, tank sheet, material-cost audit, completion defaults): the item stays selectable and carries `spot` (a label-rate reference, or the label concentration for the surfactant, plus "Spot: enter the area treated and the amount used."), while the whole-lawn rows (Stonewall 4FL, Nutra-TECH, Dimension 2EW, Tetrino on sunny turf, the spreader bags) keep their amounts on the rig or window carrier; a matched v13 protocol row's `rate_per_1000` is the planned rate (`rateSource` `protocol_rate`), a `lb_n` row derives from the visit's nutrient target, and `sunnyTurfOnly` (Tetrino) scales the whole-lawn amount by the turf profile's sun exposure; the tank sheet and the material-cost audit read the same rows as the plan. A staged v13 protocol serves only while the gate is on, so unsetting it fails closed for visits pinned to v13. Known limit: no stored field says a lawn is on reclaimed water, so the recipe's half-nitrogen rule for reclaimed-water lawns is a tech adjustment the app does not make (the plan prefills the full N target). October's spreader step is LESCO Dimension 0.21% 18-0-10 at 4.04 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.73 lb N, 0.40 lb K2O), swapped in for the discontinued Stonewall 15-0-15 by migration `20261007120500`: 4.04 lb is the EPA 10404-87 commercial label's Coastal South rate for pre-emergence on high-cut turf, under its 5.46 lb per-application maximum (16.38 lb and 3 applications a year, at least 2 to 4 months apart); the 9x April step is unchanged. The migration resolves the Dimension product id once (it fails when none exists), sets the catalog `max_label_rate_per_1000` to 5.46 only where it is empty or the old 5.48, and adds, only where the product has none, the 3-a-year and 60-day product limits (hard block) and the yearly dithiopyr cap rows (`annual_max_rate`, `active_ingredient`: granular 16.38 lb, Dimension 2EW 2.2039 fl oz); it never changes an existing limit row. Its rollback leaves a protocol that a visit or completion references. The limit reader counts a product's history for the treated property only, up to the visit's date and without the visit's own ledger rows (the pre-visit brief passes the same scope), and the plan counts the 9x April step's derived rate against the cap. Pricing is untouched. December's spreader step is LESCO 10-0-22 50% PolyPlus OPTI45 50% YaraRega 2% Fe 2% Mg KMAG MOP SOP (SiteOne 511289) at 4.5 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.45 lb N, 0.99 lb K2O; slow-release N exactly 50%), on every plan and grass, in place of the 24-0-11 (owner 2026-10-08), by migration `20261008130000`: it inserts the catalog row only where no name or alias spells it (pending pricing, no price written; the watering rule is the 24-0-11's, 0.25 inch within 24 hours; approved for the service report), fills only the empty analysis, slow-release and watering fields of a row that exists, and swaps the staged December row (still a `lb_n` row, `targetN` 0.45 and `targetK2O` 0.99); its rollback leaves a protocol that a visit or completion references, a changed row and a referenced or priced catalog row. The same migration retires (gates.retired, the Dismiss mechanism) February's Certainty, surfactant and Blindside rows (February weed spots are Celsius alone: the Certainty label says it may delay green-up) and the May and October Blindside rows (Blindside is a November-through-March product until its full label is read; April through October there is no weed spray once the Celsius cap is reached); the recipe states chinch bugs as found at the edge of a damaged patch (float test only if unsure), not a count, and the staged trigger key `chinch_20_to_25_per_sqft` keeps its name. Arena 50 WDG for chinch bugs is 0.147 oz per 1,000 sq ft (6.4 oz per acre, the low end of the label's turf range of 6.4 to 12.8 oz per acre; the staged Arena rows state `rate_per_1000` 0.147 `oz` and `gates.minIntervalDays` 56): up to 2 applications per lawn per year (the label's 12.8 oz per acre, 0.4 lb clothianidin per acre, yearly limit) and, under the gate, a synthetic hard-block `min_interval_days` of 56 days between applications on a lawn (`config/lawn-v13-count-caps.js`, by product id, no stored row; a stored product-level interval row is raised to it, never lowered). The 56 days is the company's own rule, not a label interval. The label's limit is an amount, so under the same gate the code also adds a synthetic hard-block yearly amount of 0.294 oz per 1,000 sq ft (12.8 oz per acre) for Arena (`annualAmount`, `match_type` `v13_amount`, read in `application-limits` by product id): the lawn's recorded Arena rates this year (an unreadable rate counts as the old 0.29 oz) plus the planned rate must fit it; the closeout flag audits the same amount. No stored row and no migration: the gate-off reader is unchanged. Migration `20261008131000` (data only; `20261008130000` is frozen) fills the 4.5 lb catalog rate and `lb` unit on a pre-existing 10-0-22 row where empty and coherent, and adds the inserted `active`, `needs_pricing`, `content_status` and `customer_visibility` values to the frozen migration's catalog audit snapshot so its rollback keeps a row staff changed. Migration `20261008132000` is a rollback guard (its `down()` runs first): while any v13 protocol is referenced by a scheduled visit or a completion it neutralizes the frozen catalog audit row (originals under `keptLive`, as 20261007187000 does), so the frozen rollback keeps the 10-0-22 row and the fields it filled even for a referenced protocol with no December swap log; its `up()` puts a neutralized row back. `server/data/pricing.csv` carries the 10-0-22 row (SiteOne, 50 lb, $31.81) for the bundled pricing import. A spot row's plan payload carries its rate and its own carrier (`spot.ratePer1000`, `spot.carrierGalPer1000`), which the job card's product-search dose uses (Arena: a 4-gallon fill is 1,000 sq ft and 0.147 oz); the compliance summaries report all three Arena limits with real usage and status from the same evaluators (the interval: days since the latest application, exceeded inside 56; the amount: oz per 1,000 sq ft used on the busiest lawn, warning from 75%, exceeded at the cap). The yearly amount is per lawn everywhere: a reader with no treated property judges the busiest property of the customer, never the sum across properties. A ledger row the ledger itself cannot size (no recorded rate, no quantity over area) counts at the cap's FIXED 0.29 oz, never at the catalog default, which an admin can change. A proposal check that names no dose (`POST /api/admin/compliance/check-limits`, `opts.proposal`) counts the program's dose for the product (the highest rate a staged v13 row states by product id: Arena 0.147 oz; none stated, the fixed 0.29 oz); the plan's limit check (`v13Limits`, which only ever sees selected, to-be-applied products) is a proposal too: a product with no row in the visit's window (Arena on an October visit, a search-added product) counts the same staged dose, so it is blocked with a typed `annual_max_rate` block when it would not fit. A named dose is `{ ratePer1000, unit }` (what the plan sends; `rateUnit` is read too) and is the only dose counted; an unreadable one is the fixed 0.29 oz. status reads (the compliance page, reads after the ledger write) add none. The catalog default rate stays 0.29 oz (the label's chinch rate) for use outside the v13 program. **No bahia program (owner 2026-10-06):** the v13 recipe has no `bahia` track, because the Celsius label says "DO NOT use this product on bahiagrass" and Blindside is not labeled for bahia. With the gate on: (1) a lawn recorded as bahia, by grass type, by track key (either field, whichever other track the other field names) or by the legacy lawn text when no profile is recorded, never takes the any-grass fallback; the plan engine's `selectProtocolVisit` ends the lookup with no track and the plan blocks `lawn_v13_bahia_no_program` (the visit's work is entered by hand) while a mixed or unknown lawn keeps the fallback; (2) planning readers never serve the staged bahia protocol rows (`swfl_bahia_10_10`, kept in the database for the history that points at them; no migration): `getActiveLawnProtocol` skips them, so `/admin/protocols/lawn/active` and `/lawn/window` answer 404 for `?grassTrack=bahia`, and a visit pinned to that version plans from no protocol; a historical reader keeps its old resolution; (3) `/admin/protocols/completion-actions` answers 404 `lawn_v13_bahia_no_program` for a bahia lawn (never St. Augustine chips), `get_protocol` answers that bahia has no v13 program and no longer tells callers to ask for it (the Intelligence Bar prompt and the customer guide row follow the live program too; the bahia aliases `bahia`, `d`, `d_bahia` stay for the old program); (4) pricing: a NEW recurring bahia lawn plan is review-only (`priceLawnCare` adds the manual-review reason `lawn_v13_bahia_no_program`, so the line carries `requiresManualReview` and the enforced `requiresCustomQuote`, and the office reviews it before it is sold; the table price stays for the reviewer); the estimate tool stops offering Bahia as a new lawn choice (`/admin/pricing-config/lawn_pricing_v2` reports `subFeaturesAvailable.bahiaOffered`; a reopened estimate that already carries bahia still shows it) and the public recurring lawn price range stops sweeping bahia; (5) estimates already issued are honored: a stored estimate replayed as sold (`extractEngineInputs`, the persisted-replay recompute) keeps its price (`savedEstimateReplay`), and one-time lawn pricing is unchanged; but a service line added by the customer add-service rail (`addedServiceKeys`) was never sold and is reviewed (the add is refused as `add_unavailable`), and an estimate never issued (status draft, scheduled, sending or send_failed with no `sent_at` and no `viewed_at`), saved before the gate went live or not, is reviewed on its send snapshot and refused at the send guard (`LAWN_V13_BAHIA_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, 400) in every stored shape (engine inputs, V1 form inputs, a saved request, stored results), until staff author a proposal. The bahia lawn keeps its track IDENTITY (`loadCustomerGrassContext` `trackKey` `bahia`, so the historical readers (the service report context, analytics, the wiki) still know the grass and an unassigned report keeps its bahia guidance across the gate flip), while live availability is a separate flag, `noProgram`, that every planning consumer asks (the plan engine, the pre-visit brief, the live lawn assessment, the Schedule page through the turf-profile route's `lawn_v13_no_program`, `completion-actions`, `/lawn/active` and `/lawn/window`). Other pricing is untouched. Off = every output byte-identical to before (the matcher's `exact_catalog_names` flag and the `staged` status are inert). Follow-up PR (after the flip holds) archives the old versions, activates v13 and deletes the old recipe and this gate. April on the 12x plan is LESCO 44-0-0 100% PolyPlus OPTI120 Turfgrass Granular Fertilizer (SiteOne 511333, 50 lb, available by request) at 2.27 lb per 1,000 sq ft (1.0 lb N, 100% polymer coated, releases over about 3 to 4 months into the June 1 to September 30 nitrogen ban) in place of the 24-0-11 at 0.5 lb N (owner 2026-10-22), by migration `20261022195000`: it inserts the catalog row only where no name or alias spells it (pending pricing, NO price written: the line plans, mixes and reports with no cost and the cost summary counts it unpriced; the watering rule is the 24-0-11's, 0.25 inch within 24 hours; approved for the service report; a row that already matches by name or alias, in any state, makes the migration throw and write nothing: it only inserts, so staff remove or rename that row first), swaps the 12x April row of every v13 protocol (name, product id, `gates.targetN` 1.0 lb N) and leaves the 9x Dimension row, February, November and the North Port nitrogen block as they were. A recipe cadence variant may carry its own `notes` (`visitForCadence`), because the visit's N target is read from the notes: the 12x notes state 1.0 lb N and the 9x variant's notes 0.5 lb N. The 12x year is 3.68 lb N per 1,000 sq ft (was 3.18). Its rollback is all or nothing: it does nothing when any visit or completion references a v13 protocol or when any April row it wrote was edited; otherwise it restores every April row and deletes only the catalog row it inserted, and only if that row is unchanged, unpriced and unused.

Estimate-page consultation offer ("Want us to come look first?", consultation-first lane, owner ruling 2026-09-23): `GATE_ESTIMATE_CONSULTATION_OFFER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`estimateConsultationOfferLive()`, `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Requires `GATE_LEAD_INSPECTION_LINK` ALSO live — the offer builder (`server/services/estimate-consultation-offer.js`) checks both, and either dark keeps the field off. On, the public estimate page's `/data` payload carries an optional `consultationOffer: { url }` for the estimate's one linked recurring-intent lead (`leads.estimate_id` pointing at it, or a stamped `lead_id` with `lead_linkage` `sid`/`stamp`; ambiguous → none; the lead must still be the estimate's contact — same customer, or same phone or email) whose estimate is in an open, customer-actionable state (never accepted/declined/expired/staff-preview) on a quote-first estimate (never one drafted from a visit, never a grouped one), when the `/inspection/:token` page's probe finds an open slot at the estimate's own property (the address it resolved must match the estimate's, and after the probe what that address resolves from — the lead's own address, its trusted customer's — must be unchanged and the page's lead-wide state must still allow a booking) — composed on the first page load only (the slot probe is time-boxed at 3 s and capped at 3 in flight per process — either bound means no offer), never on an internal refresh or the Intelligence Bar projection — the React page then renders a compact "Want us to come look first?" section with a "Pick a time" link to that SAME `/inspection/:token` page the recurring-lead new_lead email already offers (the estimate-email link is the separate gate below). The URL carries NO delivery-channel claim (unverified — never `'sms'`/`'email'`) and the GET makes no write of any kind to produce it (no short-code mint, no DB insert). Off, or any ineligibility/error, omits the field entirely and the page renders byte-identical to before. The Intelligence Bar estimate-detail projection drops the field (the URL is a booking bearer). No customer communication either way — this is a link on a page the customer already opened, not a send.
Estimate-page assessment first ("Book a free Waves Assessment first"): `GATE_ESTIMATE_ASSESSMENT_FIRST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`estimateAssessmentFirstLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-26, "OK GO" on decision page choice 3A: "Offer it on every open estimate, residential and commercial: 'Book a free Waves Assessment first' opens a booking page. That page must work from the estimate itself, because today's booking link belongs to the lead." On, `/data` adds `assessmentFirst` for an open estimate the customer is viewing (never a staff, draft or document render) whose customer account sits at the estimate's property (inside the service area, and never an excluded locality), is not a property group or a visit draft, and has no open Waves Assessment (`assessmentFirstFor` in `server/routes/estimate-assessment-public.js`); the page then shows a glass **Book a free Waves Assessment first** card with a gold **Pick a time** link to `/estimate/:token/assessment`, the consultation booking page keyed by the estimate token, and the lead-only consultation offer (`GATE_ESTIMATE_CONSULTATION_OFFER`) is not built for that page. Booking a time books one free Waves Assessment for the estimate's customer (the assessment catalog row and its per-customer lane dedupe, never billed, never linked to the estimate, so the estimate stays open), re-checked inside the booking transaction (`estimateGuard`), with an office note naming the estimate. Routes and guards: `docs/public-route-contracts.md` (`/api/public/estimate-assessment/:token`). **The owner flips it**: it books visits and sends the booking confirmation text. The estimate's follow-up emails stop after an assessment is booked from it: `estimate-follow-up.js` and `estimate-engagement-engine.js` call `customerConvertedSince` (`estimate-conversion-guard.js`), which suppresses the sends once any live visit is booked after the estimate was created. Off: the API answers the generic 404, `/data` carries nothing new and the consultation offer behaves as before. Rollback: unset the variable; booked assessments stay booked.

Estimate-email consultation offer ("Rather have us come look first? Pick a time for a free consultation →", owner ruling 2026-09-26, decision 2 of the estimate-email consultation-offer lane): `GATE_ESTIMATE_EMAIL_CONSULTATION_OFFER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`estimateEmailConsultationOfferLive()`, `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy) — a SEPARATE gate from the estimate page's own `GATE_ESTIMATE_CONSULTATION_OFFER` above, since the two surfaces ship independently. Requires `GATE_LEAD_INSPECTION_LINK` ALSO live, checked inside the same shared `estimateConsultationLead` eligibility the page uses (never re-derived). Covers `estimate.engage_gone_quiet` ONLY (the engagement engine's `viewed_gone_quiet_72h` rule) — every other `estimate.engage_*` rule never calls either step below. This is never a new send: `server/services/estimate-email-consultation-offer.js` computes ONE extra payload variable, `consultation_url`, for the one gone-quiet email the engine (`server/services/estimate-engagement-engine.js`) sends anyway, in two steps split around the engine's own send checks. `probeGoneQuietConsultation` — the shared eligibility with the page's own `isEstimateAcceptActive` verdict (an estimate held off the customer surface — linkage invalidated or pending, reprice hold, unverified address — never carries the link) and the slot probe — runs only for a gone-quiet job that has passed every engine check (no probe, and no time under the follow-up lock, for a job about to be skipped or deferred); the engine then judges that job once more from the top on state read after the probe, reusing the probe's result, so every check and payload field of the send is post-probe. Shadow jobs never probe, and with this gate off no job probes or takes the second pass. A batch spends at most 10 s probing while it holds the follow-up lock (`ENGINE_LIMITS.offerProbeBatchBudgetMs`; a probe starts only if the budget still covers its full 3 s ceiling); past that, its remaining gone-quiet sends go out without the offer, in one pass. After the claim (a lost claim never mints), `mintGoneQuietConsultationUrl` mints the short link; then, as the last step before sending, the engine judges three things from ONE read-only REPEATABLE READ snapshot (so no guard reads a different instant from another): `goneQuietConsultationStillValid` (the probe-free shared eligibility, `reconfirmConsultationLead`, and the lead's-own-inbox rule against that send's actual recipient), the estimate row, and the customer's email opt-out. If the row changed at all besides `updated_at` (recipient, customer, status, address, price, services, or the follow-up counters a concurrent send moves) or the customer opted out since, it gives the claim back and retries the whole job on fresh state, where the normal checks decide it; a failed offer check drops only the link. Sends that probed no offer skip both steps and are byte-identical to before. `consultation_url` renders as a text link right after the template's existing primary CTA button (`email-template-library.js`'s `cta`/`variant:'link'` block; migrations `20260926010000` → `20260926010100` → `20260926010200` → `20260926010300` (preceded by the read-only preflight `20260926005000`, which checks every template-shape condition a later chain file aborts on, before any of it publishes) leave exactly one, directly after the first non-link CTA — and only when that CTA is guaranteed to render (a static `url`, or a `url_variable` in the template's `required_variables`); if the first non-link CTA is optional, `010300` fails the migration for manual review rather than anchor the link above the real button. Their rollback never rewrites the curated template) ONLY when it is non-blank; blank (gate off, no eligible lead, or the send's recipient does not match the linked lead's own email — the SAME lead's-own-inbox rule the new_lead consultation email enforces) drops the block and the email renders byte-identical to today. The URL is channel `'email'` (never `'sms'`) and is ALWAYS short-wrapped before it rides the email (`lead-consultation-email-block.js`'s `shortWrap`, reused verbatim) with a short-code TTL matching the 14-day consultation token; `createShortCode` throwing yields `''`, never a broken send. Any other ineligibility or error in either step also fails closed (no link) and is logged, and the shared slot probe is bounded (3 s, then no offer; at most 3 in flight per process) — it never blocks the gone_quiet email itself.

Commercial suite sizing (`server/services/commercial-suite-size/`): `GATE_COMMERCIAL_SUITE_SIZING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `commercialSuiteSizingLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); off = byte-identical to before. When on, an estimator-engine call draft for a commercial tenant in a multi-tenant building (unit scope `commercial_suite`, e.g. a restaurant in unit 102 of a plaza) is priced off the SUITE's own square footage, never the whole building and never a $0 manual quote: caller/tech-stated size (source-arbitration.js, unchanged) → an active FL DBPR permanent food-service license naming that suite (`dbpr-food-license.js`: public CSV extract, 24h in-process cache, bounded fetch + 10-minute failure backoff; seats → sq ft) → a type default keyed off `commercialRiskType`/`commercialSubtype` only (`type-defaults.js`). A license size parks the draft yellow ("confirm on site"); a type default also prices LOW confidence (`footprintSizeEstimated`, applied once in `generateEstimate` to every commercial line), so the low-confidence delivery gates apply. Requires `GATE_UNIT_SCOPE_GUARDRAILS` (on in prod) — that apply is what clears the building size a suite is sized in place of; with guardrails off the engine skips suite sizing and logs a warning. `COMMERCIAL_SUITE_WEB_SEARCH` — default ON, read at call time; `0`/`false`/`off` disables the business-name web-search leg (`web-search-leg.js`, via `services/llm/call.js` `callAnthropic`), which is NEVER a size source (AGENTS.md: an LLM proposes intent, it never reaches a price/size field) — it only names the business in the draft notes when the license has nothing. The admin estimate tool reads the same gate: opt-in via `performPropertyLookup({ commercialSuiteSizing: true })`. **Every production caller declares its scope decision once in `server/services/property-lookup/lookup-callers.js` (`lookupOptionsFor(callerId, extra)`; address-match PR 7):** only `admin_estimate_tool` (the panel asks and answers) and `estimator_engine` (the composer answers; an unresolved scope goes red) opt in; the legacy admin GET lookup, the Intelligence Bar lookup tool (no answer surface), the area editor, the call cache warm, and every public or customer surface (`public_property_lookup`, `public_quote`, `customer_pricing_ai`, the report cross-sell and its warm) never do, so they see no business identity, no suite candidate, no resolver call, and no `suiteSize`/`suiteBuildingTotalSqFt` fields at all. The call site cannot override the decision, and `lookup-callers-guard.test.js` fails on a call of `performPropertyLookup` that does not go through the registry (and on an undeclared direct `lookupPropertyFromAITrio` caller; the two WDO prompts are declared bypasses that read home facts only). A resolved suite size is persisted on the cached `property_record` (`_commercialSuiteSize`, tagged with the unit it sized) so a cache hit reuses it with zero network; a DBPR-sourced stamp expires after 30 days and re-resolves; a type default is never persisted (a later lookup may find a license). `suiteBuildingTotalSqFt` is deliberately NOT named `buildingSqFt` — that name is a genuine pricing alias elsewhere (`resolvePestFootprint`'s explicit-footprint override, several IB agent-tool fields) that must never pick up this unverified whole-building total as a measured footprint.

Condo unit folio (`server/services/property-lookup/ai-property-lookup.js` `aggregateUnitDesignatorMatch`): `GATE_CONDO_UNIT_FOLIO` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `condoUnitFolioLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); off = byte-identical to before (a typed Apt/Unit on a stacked condo aggregate drops to the address search). When on, the typed unit is matched against the stacked building's own county unit rows (`unitDesignatorRows` from `county-parcel-gis.js` `buildStackedAggregate`: labeled `UNIT/APT/#` situs or a bare trailing unit number); ONLY a unique exact match on a row that is one dwelling with its own living area resolves to that unit's roll row — never the building's figures. Repeated unit numbers (BLDG A/B under one street number) stamp `_unitFolio.status = 'multiple_unit_matches'` on the cached record and raise a HIGH sq-ft field-verify flag; anything else degrades to the address search as before. With the gate on, a cached unit-address row (labeled Apt/Unit/#, or a bare number after the street suffix) without `_unitFolio` misses once and is then stamped; "no stacked building" is stamped only when the county roll answered for the point, otherwise `county_unavailable` retries after 24 h. Kill: unset the gate — every cached row carrying `_unitFolio` then misses once and re-runs the pre-feature lookup, and the ambiguity flag stops rendering.

Intelligence Bar cancel_appointment card-confirm (ib-cancel-pinned-effects lane, owner ruling 2026-09-28, "bare visits only" — supersedes that lane's earlier "simple visits only" ruling): `GATE_IB_CANCEL_APPOINTMENT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `ibCancelAppointmentLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Off, `cancel_appointment` behaves exactly as before this lane: both the proposal site (`proposePendingWrite`) and `/confirm-action` in `server/routes/admin-intelligence-bar.js` refuse every cancel with `CANCEL_NOT_CARD_CONFIRMABLE_MESSAGE`, pointing the operator to the Dispatch screen — this also covers a pending row minted while the gate was on and then turned off before Confirm. On, the proposal computes the deterministic pre-commit impact (`server/services/appointment-cancel-impact.js` `computeCancelAppointmentImpact`) fresh for the target appointment: not found refuses ("Appointment not found — nothing was proposed."); a throw (any rail unreadable) refuses ("The cancellation effects could not be verified right now — nothing was proposed."); a terminal appointment (completed/cancelled/skipped/no_show) refuses ("This appointment is already `<status>` and can't be cancelled.") — a fresh proposal is never the commit-time idempotent-replay path; a non-bare visit — **the bar cancels BARE visits only** (owner ruling 2026-09-28) — refuses with the same `CARD_CANCEL_REFUSED_MESSAGE` wording `tools.js` also uses, naming the Dispatch screen, when `card_cancel_refusals` is non-empty: a card fee agreement or hold (`card_fee_agreement`), a card payment on an invoice (`card_payment_on_invoice`), an invoice that would still hold money after the void even though it isn't itself voidable (`invoice_holds_money`, `fee.blocked_by_invoice`), a legacy estimate deposit (`estimate_deposit`), a possible plan make-up visit (`plan_makeup_visit`), a grouped visit (`grouped_visit`, row.visit_id set — cancelling one member can detach or dissolve the group via `visit-groups.js`'s `handleChildTerminal`, a side effect this card does not disclose), a follow-up child (`followup_child`, row.followup_source_service_id set — cancelling one re-parks the source visit's follow-up obligation as a fresh dispatch alert, `job-status.js`'s `maybeReparkFollowupObligation`) — **plus two ANY-STATUS checks added for "bare visits only": `invoice_linked` (ANY invoice on record for this visit at all, whatever its status — paid, void, refunded, draft — via the new `invoice.js#anyInvoiceLinkedToVisit`, the same direct-or-through-service-record linkage `voidOpenInvoicesForCancelledService`/`previewInvoiceVoidForCancelledService` use, minus their voidable-status filter) and `inspection_credit` (broadened: refuses not only a REDEEMED offer this cancel would reverse, as before, but ANY inspection-credit offer tied to this visit at all — as the inspection that sourced one or the booking that redeemed one, open/expired/void included — via the new `inspection-credit.js#anyInspectionCreditOfferForVisit`)**. Otherwise the impact is pinned onto `params._frozen_cancellation_impact` and mirrored onto `preview.cancellation`, so the confirmation card renders the exact effects — plus a comms line and `notifies_customer: true` whenever `customer_notice` is `'may_send'` (the existing `GATE_CANCEL_NOTICE_HOOK` cancellation-text hook, `job-status.js#previewCancellationNoticeVerdict`'s read-only mirror: `'none'` ONLY when that gate is off, since every DB-backed condition is mutable and never grounds a `'none'`) — plus a `technician_notice` verdict (`'may_notify'` when `GATE_TECH_VISIT_NOTIFICATIONS` is live AND the visit has an assigned technician different from the confirming actor — `tech-visit-notifications.js#notifyVisitCancelled`, already wired unconditionally into every `transitionJobStatus` cancel, is disclosed here rather than left a silent side effect) — plus a human-readable appointment window and the visit's effective service address (falling back to the customer's primary address for a legacy unstamped row) — plus a full whole-row identity hash (`identity_fingerprint`, `appointment-cancel-impact.js`'s `computeRowFingerprint` — every `scheduled_services` column bar a tiny denylist of columns that churn for unrelated operational reasons) — plus, ONLY for a legacy row with no stamped service address, a SEPARATE narrow `legacy_address_fingerprint` over the customer's raw address columns (that address lives on `customers`, never `scheduled_services`, so `identity_fingerprint` — deliberately scheduled_services-only — cannot catch it drifting; the proposal and the locked recheck below hash the exact same column set) — and the authorization contract's hash covers all of it (`pinned_cancellation`; `cancel_appointment` is also always in `IRREVERSIBLE_TOOL_NAMES`). `/confirm-action` dispatches a `cancel_appointment` pending action only when the gate is live AND the stored action still carries that frozen pin. The dispatched executor (`services/intelligence-bar/tools.js` `cancelAppointment`) recomputes the SAME impact immediately before transitioning the appointment and refuses on any drift from the frozen one. That final identity check runs a SECOND time INSIDE the mutation transaction itself: the tool locks the `scheduled_services` row `FOR UPDATE`, recomputes the whole-row fingerprint from exactly what that lock sees, and refuses before transitioning anything on a mismatch. The SAME locked read also explicitly re-derives, from the row about to be transitioned rather than only inferring from the fingerprint match: the plan-reseed (`cancelMayReseedPlan`) and grouped-visit verdicts (as before), the follow-up-child refusal, a fresh existence check against `invoices`/`inspection_credit_offers` for THIS visit (neither lives on `scheduled_services`, so only an explicit re-query under this lock — never the fingerprint — can catch one created in the gap between the pre-check, outside any lock, and this lock; verified against `inspection-credit.js#redeemSpecificOffer`, the one writer that could mint a credit against this same visit concurrently — it locks this SAME row FOR UPDATE, inside its own transaction, before minting, so whichever transaction reaches the lock first serializes the other safely either order), and — for a legacy unstamped row — a FOR SHARE re-read of the customer row, refusing if its address fingerprint no longer matches the frozen one. Because a bare visit has nothing to void or reverse, this lane runs the SAME shared post-commit cleanup seam every other cancel surface does — `transitionJobStatus`'s own UNPINNED `voidOpenInvoicesForCancelledService` seam (`job-status.js#maybeReparkFollowupObligation`) is no longer suppressed, and this tool's own follow-through call (`runVisitCancellationFollowThrough`) runs unpinned too, exactly as a Dispatch cancel does — there is no bar-owned pinned invoice/credit plumbing left to race it. The tool also appends the operator's reason with a SQL-side `concat_ws`/`NULLIF` against the LIVE `notes` column (never a value read before the transaction opened, so a concurrent note survives). State that moves between proposal and Confirm can never settle a different verdict than what the operator approved. Also refused: `prepaid_coverage` — money committed outside any linked invoice (a positive `prepaid_amount`, live annual-prepay coverage, or at the estimate level an unapplied deposit or a payment-pending prepay invoice), decided by the schedule route's own canonical readers (`admin-schedule.js` `findBillingCoveredVisits` + `findEstimateScopedCommitment`) at proposal and again on the cancel transaction under the lock. Also refused: `card_rail_present` — ANY `estimate_card_holds` / `appointment_card_requests` row for the visit, whatever its status or current fee eligibility (a fee-exempt request can become chargeable when a Bill-To payer is cleared). The card discloses, as a standing conditional effect, that the cancel closes any open overdue-family dispatch alert (`tech_late` / `unassigned_overdue`) for the visit — alert creation does not lock the visit, so no count is frozen. A visit that goes terminal just before the lock chain (`SCHEDULED_VISIT_NOT_LIVE`) returns `preview_changed`. Kill = unset `GATE_IB_CANCEL_APPOINTMENT` — every cancel goes back to Dispatch, byte-identical to before this lane.

Intelligence Bar cancel of a visit with an invoice, credit or linked visit (owner decision 2026-10-12, adopted recommendations 2026-10-14): `GATE_IB_CANCEL_WITH_EFFECTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`, and live only while `GATE_IB_CANCEL_APPOINTMENT` is also on**, read at call time via `ibCancelWithEffectsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Off, the bar refuses every visit with an invoice, credit or linked visit exactly as before (`CARD_CANCEL_REFUSED_MESSAGE`, code `cancel_with_effects_unsupported`); a card minted with effects and then switched off before Confirm refuses at `/confirm-action`. On, `computeCancelAppointmentImpact(id, { withEffects: true, notifyCustomer })` (`server/services/appointment-cancel-impact.js`) stops treating these refusal codes as blockers: `invoice_linked`, `card_payment_on_invoice`, `estimate_deposit`, `inspection_credit`, `linked_followup`. The impact then also carries `with_effects`, `notify_customer`, `customer_text` (the rendered `appointment_cancelled` text, `appointment-reminders.js#previewCancellationText`, read-only), `linked_invoices` (every invoice on the visit, any status) and `linked_visits` (the follow-up visits the cancel takes with it); all of it is frozen into the card and the contract hash. The card lists each invoice voided or kept, each credit restored, each linked visit cancelled and the customer text, with a `notify_customer` choice (default true; the operator asks for "cancel without a text" and a new card shows no text). Still refused with the gate on: a fee due (`card_fee_agreement` / `card_rail_present` with a fee or an unreadable lane) with code `cancel_fee_due_unsupported`; money the bar never refunds or charges (a card rail with no fee, `prepaid_coverage`, `invoice_holds_money` = a paid, processing or statement-held invoice) with code `by_owner_rule`; and `plan_makeup_visit`, `grouped_visit`, `followup_child` or a linked follow-up that has an invoice of its own (`linked_followup_billed`) with code `cancel_with_effects_unsupported`. The scope is always this visit only (`scope: this_only`, never the series). Confirm (`tools.js` `cancelWithEffects`) recomputes the impact and refuses with `preview_changed` on any drift, then replays the Dispatch handler in-process: `admin-dispatch.js#cancelServiceFromBar` runs the same `PUT /:serviceId/status` handler (`serviceStatusHandler`) with the carded body only (status `cancelled`, scope `this_only`, the reason as notes, `notifyCustomer` as carded; no `waiveCardHoldFee`, no coordinates), `techRole` admin and the confirming operator as `technicianId`. Inside the handler's cancel transaction, right after it locks the visit, the shim's `beforeCommit` recomputes the impact once more and aborts with `preview_changed` on any difference. What that handler then does: `transitionJobStatus` (cancel, history row, tech cancel notice), `handleCancellation` (the customer text only when `notifyCustomer` is not false), `runVisitCancellationFollowThrough` (void open invoices and restore applied credit or deposit credit, cancel an open PaymentIntent, reverse a redeemed inspection credit, tracker cancel, cancel the linked follow-up visits) and the counted-plan reseed. It never refunds and never charges a card; a paid invoice or a payment in flight is skipped and the office is alerted, which the bar refuses up front. The text and the linked visits are pinned, not just previewed. The card's `customer_text` holds the recipients (`appointment-reminders.js#resolveNoticeContacts`, the same resolution `safeSendAppointment` sends with) and, per recipient, the body rendered by `renderCancellationBody` (the same renderer `handleCancellation` sends with), from ONE weighted template variant picked at proposal (`template_body`; a re-check re-renders that pinned variant, so the check is stable). Confirm passes the approved bodies to the handler (`handleCancellation` `approvedNotice`), which sends exactly those and refuses a recipient the card did not approve; a text the card could not compose is not sent. Send-time holds (opt-out, landline, quiet hours) are not previewed. The linked visits the card lists are passed to the shared cascade (`call-booking-catalog.js#cancelCallFollowUpsForParentCancel` `approvedChildren`, through `visit-cancellation-followthrough.js` and `track-transitions.js#cancel`; all opt-in, every other caller unchanged): the cascade re-reads each child under its own `FOR UPDATE` lock and cancels it only if it is still a live linked follow-up with the carded status, date and service and no invoice of its own; a child that changed, or one not on the card, is NOT cancelled and comes back as `linked_visits_skipped` in the receipt. The lock-time check also row-locks the linked visits inside the handler's cancel transaction, and makes no Stripe call under the lock: PaymentIntents are looked up before the lock and reused from a cache (`previewInvoiceVoidForCancelledService` `piCache` / `piCacheOnly`); a payment attempt that appeared since counts as a change (`preview_changed`). Each linked visit also pins its assigned technician (id, name) and whether that technician would get a cancel notice (`technician_notice`, the parent's rule); the card has one line per notified technician, and a child reassigned before the cascade is skipped and reported (`technician_changed`). An approved text send is never left to the cancellation sweep: if it fails, its claim is finalized as terminal `suppressed` (the sweep would render the live template for today's recipients, not the approved ones), the receipt warns that the text did not go out and must be sent by hand. The money is pinned too: after the cancel commits, the follow-through runs on the card's frozen money effects only (`visit-cancellation-followthrough.js` `pinnedEffects`, the existing pinned path, forwarded by `cancelServiceFromBar` `approvedMoney`): it voids only the invoices the card listed, at those amounts (and, for an invoice with an open card payment attempt, only when it is still the PaymentIntent the card named, `payment_intent_id`; each is re-checked under the invoice row lock), reverses only the credits the card showed as taken back, and runs NO card fee rail (a rail that appeared is never run; the office is alerted). Anything approved that was not carried out comes back as `moneySkipped` in the reply and as a `money_skipped` / warning in the receipt; a linked visit that failed to cancel for any reason (drift, a database or transition error, or the cascade not running) is in `linked_visits_skipped`. The shared status writer's own unpinned invoice void / credit reversal seam (`job-status.js`, `transitionJobStatus` `moneySeam: 'caller'`) stands down for this replay, so nothing runs on live money state before the pinned follow-through; an approved cascade also texts no linked visit. Dispatch's own cancel passes none of this and is unchanged. Codex #6377 r2 narrowed the card to the plain case (refuse over pin): with effects the bar also refuses (code `by_owner_rule`) a credit REDEEMED on the visit (`inspection_credit_redeemed`; a failed pinned follow-through would leave the hourly sweep to void unpinned), an invoice carrying an estimate deposit credit (`estimate_deposit`), any deposit row or annual-prepay term on the visit's source estimate (`estimate_money`), any GROUPED linked visit (`linked_followup_grouped`, `visit_id` set: a package follow-up can be grouped automatically, and cancelling one runs the group hook; the cascade's under-lock recheck skips and reports one grouped since as `grouped_changed`), and any linked visit with money on it (`linked_followup_money`: the same prepaid / coverage, estimate, card request or hold, inspection-credit offer and invoice checks the parent gets). The lock-time re-check reads the estimate-level and money-rail state on the handler's cancel transaction (`computeCancelAppointmentImpact` `conn`, default `db`), which first takes the estimate deposit ledger lock that deposit receipt, mint, collection and void share, so a deposit cannot land between the check and the commit. With the effects gate off, an explicit `notify_customer: false` is refused at proposal (code `gate_off`) instead of being ignored. The cascade's per-child re-check under the child's own lock now repeats the full linked-visit money check (`appointment-cancel-impact.js#linkedChildMoneyReason`: prepaid or coverage, estimate deposit or annual prepay, card request or hold, inspection-credit offer, any invoice) on that child's transaction; a child that has money now is not cancelled, never reaches the shared money seam, and is reported in `linked_visits_skipped` as `money_added_<kind>`. A PaymentIntent that also rides another invoice (a combined payment covering other visits) is refused (`combined_payment`, code `by_owner_rule`: cancelling it would clear the stamps on invoices the card never listed) in the preview (`previewInvoiceVoidForCancelledService` flags it) and again in the pinned sweep, which leaves it open (the sibling check, the Stripe cancel and the stamp clear run under the per-customer `pay.combined.customer` advisory lock the combined setup takes, so a session cannot be stamped in between); Dispatch's unpinned sweep is unchanged. The approved customer text is protected through a crash or a transient database failure without a migration: when the card carries an approved text and `GATE_CANCEL_NOTICE_HOOK` mints a durable claim, the cancel transaction mints it as `pending_approved` (`transitionJobStatus` `cancelNoticeApproved`; no caller-intent outbox is written for it, and if the marker cannot be written the cancellation aborts rather than committing without it), a `cancellation_notice_state` value that NO sweep, late-claim fallback or outbox lists (they read only NULL, `pending`, `pending_notify`). Only the approved send itself adopts it (`handleCancellation` with `approvedNotice`), keeps it through the send and finalizes it as `sent` or terminal `suppressed`. Any earlier exit leaves the marker, so nothing sends the live template for it; the receipt then says the text was not confirmed and must be sent by hand (a restored visit sheds the marker like any other). With the hook gate off no claim exists and nothing else sends. An invoice whose void has downstream billing effects is refused too (`invoice_downstream_effects`, by_owner_rule): a rodent setup-fee line or claim (the void would restore the obligation to the series or re-bill it), an annual-prepay term's prepay invoice, or a membership-dues invoice; only a plain visit invoice is carded. The pinned void repeats that check on the locked invoice row (an invoice edited since the card can keep its amounts and still gain such an effect): on drift the void is skipped and reported in `money_skipped`.
