If preparing the combined-payment lock fails, its manual transaction is rolled back and the candidate is left open. The pinned sweep releases its combined-payment lock right after the void commits, before the post-commit follow-up stop (which takes the same customer lock itself). For an approved text, if the claim touches no row because an older pending / pending_notify claim already sits on the reminder, the cancellation aborts (only a terminal, already-marked or absent reminder row is accepted). KNOWN LIMIT (fails closed, refuses more): `findBillingCoveredVisits` (the schedule route's prepaid-coverage reader, reached through `prepaidCommitmentReason`) treats an invoice with account credit or an open PaymentIntent as prepaid coverage, so those visits are refused today (`prepaid_coverage`, by_owner_rule); the credit-restore and open-payment-cancellation lines on the card apply once that reader is split (follow-up). Kill = unset `GATE_IB_CANCEL_WITH_EFFECTS`. CRASH RECOVERY (follow-up to #6377, owner ruling 2026-10-22 option A; NO gate of its own: the rows exist only after the gated card path ran, so with the gate never on the sweep reads an empty table): the cancel transaction also writes ONE row to `ib_cancel_effect_bundles` (`server/services/ib-cancel-effect-bundles.js`, written from `cancelServiceFromBar`'s `beforeCommit` right after the lock-time re-check, so it commits or rolls back with the cancel; a failed write aborts the cancel) holding exactly what the card approved: the pinned invoices and credit offers, the approved text per recipient or the no-text choice, the approved linked visits, the pending action id, the actor and the notes. The request takes a 10 minute `request` lease, records its text outcome when `handleCancellation` returns, and marks the row `complete` when the follow-through returns. A row still `pending` 10 minutes after it was written (the request is dead) is finished by `sweepIbCancelBundles`, a cron every 5 minutes under `runExclusive('ib-cancel-effect-recovery')` that queries by AGE, not by tick (a dropped tick only delays it): it claims one row at a time with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a lease token (only the holder writes), checks the visit is still cancelled with no later restoration (else the row is `abandoned` and reported), then runs the SAME pinned calls the request runs: `runVisitCancellationFollowThrough` with `pinnedEffects` / `moneyReport` / `linkedChildren` (same lock-time rechecks and fail-closed skips; an invoice already void or a linked visit already cancelled counts as done, not as changed), then the approved text. The approved text is sent ONLY when the reminder marker is still `pending_approved` (nothing reached the provider handoff), through `handleCancellation` with the approved bodies and never the live template, only inside the 8 AM to 8 PM ET window (otherwise the money work runs now and the text waits, using no attempt) and only if the visit date has not passed; a marker `sent` with no provider-accepted audit row is recorded UNCERTAIN for office review and is never sent again; a text step the request already recorded is never redone. Each step's result is saved the moment it ends, so a crashed sweep resumes without repeating a step. The sweep records a receipt on the pending action (only if it has none; the request's own receipt wins) and raises an office alert (`raiseAdminAlert`, Schedule, subject = the visit; needs-you with the full list when anything was skipped, uncertain or not sent, a quiet row when all is done). RESTORE FENCE: a standalone check is not enough, so every mutation the sweep makes re-proves the cancellation INSIDE its own transaction (`server/services/cancel-generation-fence.js`, passed as `cancelFence` through `runVisitCancellationFollowThrough`, the invoice void under the invoice row lock, the inspection-credit reversal, `trackTransitions.cancel` and the per-child cascade as `parentFence`): `FOR SHARE NOWAIT` on the visit row (a restore is an UPDATE of that row, so it either committed first or waits for the short transaction; a restore in flight fails at once with `visit_busy`, so no lock-order deadlock), then the visit must still be `cancelled` and its restoration COUNT (job_status_history rows leaving `cancelled`) must equal the count the cancel transaction pinned in the bundle (`restorations_seen`, read with the visit row locked). No time is ever compared: `transitioned_at` defaults to the transaction START, so a restoration that began before the bundle was written but committed after it carries an older timestamp; the history table is append-only and a restore inserts its row in the same transaction as its status UPDATE, so under the share lock the count is exact, and a cancelled, restored and cancelled-again visit always has a higher count, so a different cancel is never mistaken for the approved one. A refusal is pushed to `fence.hits`: a visit that changed abandons the bundle with an office alert saying some steps may already have run; a merely busy visit saves nothing and retries on the next pass. The request itself is not fenced (it runs right after its own commit, as the Dispatch cancel does), and `liveFinish` only flips the bundle row's status, so a restore racing it changes nothing. The recovered text's claim is bound to the same generation in its own small transaction (`AppointmentReminders.claimApprovedNoticeForGeneration`, reached through `handleCancellation` `cancelGeneration`): it takes the visit's `FOR SHARE NOWAIT` lock and proves the pinned restoration count FIRST, then claims only the untouched `pending_approved` marker, so while the lock is held no restore can change the visit and no newer cancellation can replace the reminder's marker between the proof and the claim (a single UPDATE with generation subqueries was not enough: PostgreSQL re-checks only the updated tuple after a lock wait, so a replaced marker passed an older snapshot); a restore or re-cancel in flight makes it fail at once and the text retries on the next pass; every later step is fenced by the token that claim mints), and delivery is proven per approved recipient by that recipient's own phone (`approvedCancellationNoticeStatus` `recipientKeys`: each approved `recipient_key` must resolve to a contact on the customer and have a provider-accepted audit row whose `to_hash` is the hash of that contact's normalized phone; a count of destinations is not proof, because an accepted SMS followed by an email fallback to the same person is two destinations and one person). `delivered` needs every approved recipient proven; some but not all, an email-only fallback, a recipient no longer on the customer or unreadable preferences is `partial`; no accepted audit row at all is `uncertain`; none of them is ever sent again. RECOVERY WRITE INVENTORY (every write the sweep can reach; a new one must be added here): FENCED IN ITS OWN TRANSACTION: the invoice void and its same-transaction restores (deposit and account credit, statement rollup, rodent setup), the credit rebind and the credit reversal (each in its own transaction, before its offer update), the "inspection credit could not be reversed" office alert (its transaction asserts the fence before it stamps the offer's `reversal_alerted_at`, so a restore after the point-in-time check raises no alert for a live booking), the tracker flip, the technician-state cleanup (visit share lock, then tech_status NOWAIT; also on the already-cancelled retry path and after a lost tracker race, where the winner may have died before clearing tech_status), each linked child's cancel (parent proof plus the child's own pinned restoration count under the child lock, so a child the dead request cancelled and an operator restored is not cancelled twice), the reminder close and the text claim. FENCED BY A RECHECK: the Stripe PaymentIntent triage (a point-in-time proof right before it; NOT a share lock held across the network call, which would invert the lock order against the invoice-first credit application; the void itself is proven under NOWAIT in its transaction, so a restore in that instant leaves a cancelled PaymentIntent on an open invoice, which the next payment attempt replaces), the fee step's office alert and the tracker-failure dispatch alert (each written in the same transaction that proves the generation, via `notifyAdmin({ trx, dedupeKey })` / `createAlert({ trx })`; a refusal writes nothing and lands on `cancelFence.hits`, which also skips the tracker cancel), the stale cancelled-refresh broadcast, the pre-dispatch stamp before the provider handoff, the finalize of the text claim (token-fenced, a restore clears the marker). OWNERSHIP IN THE FENCE: the cancel fence every sweep effect passes also carries `bundleId` and `leaseToken`; `assertCancelGeneration` first takes the bundle row `FOR SHARE NOWAIT` in the effect's own transaction and requires status `pending`, `lease_owner` = the runner's token and a live `lease_until` (database clock), else the effect is refused with `lease_lost` (or `bundle_busy` when an update is in flight, a retry) before any write. A runner that paused past its lease (another worker claimed it, or it expired and the office was told nothing more would run) is therefore stopped at its next effect, including the text claim and the pre-dispatch stamp (now proof + stamp in one transaction); the sweep turns `lease_lost` into a lost lease (no receipt, no alert) and the text marker is left as it was. TEXT IN FLIGHT: the provider handoff cannot be held under a lock or un-sent, so a send that was stamped (the reminder marker `sent`) and then paused can still land after its bundle is terminal. Every terminal report (expiry, abandonment, rebuilt receipt) therefore reads the reminder per approved recipient (`reportedTextState`): a stamp with no accepted audit row is reported as `customer_text_uncertain` with the line "may be going out right now, check the message history, do not send it again", never as part of "nothing more will run" (that sentence names only the steps listed as not confirmed), and an audit row found later reports the text as delivered. `claimUnactable` also skips, for `IN_FLIGHT_GRACE_MS` (15 minutes), a bundle whose approved text was stamped that recently with no outcome recorded, so the stale send can land and the report is written from the evidence. REQUEST SIDE: the request's own post-commit work obeys the same ownership. After the text step it renews its lease and, if the bundle is no longer its own (a sweep took it, possibly abandoning it after a restore), it runs NO money, linked-visit or tracker step; otherwise the approved text (its claim and its pre-dispatch stamp) and then the follow-through run under one fence carrying the bundle and the `request` lease (`liveFence`), with the bundle's own pinned copies of the linked visits, and any refusal stands the request down after the text outcome it already knows (partial or uncertain delivery) is saved (`liveStandDown`: the reply says the recovery owns the outcome, the request lease is released, the bundle stays pending for the sweep). TEXT EVIDENCE IS BOUND TO ITS CANCELLATION: the claim transaction appends its claim token to `approved_money.notice_claim_tokens` on the bundle (before any stamp or handoff; the migration is unchanged and the follow-through reads only invoices and credit offers from that column). An abandonment, a rebuilt receipt and the delivery evidence an abandonment saves judge the text ONLY by accepted audit rows carrying one of those tokens (`approvedCancellationNoticeStatus(..., { claimTokens })`), never by the reminder's current marker, which after a restore and a new cancel belongs to the NEWER cancellation: no token stored = the text is reported as not confirmed (check the message history, do not send it again), never delivered. The rule is one function (`noticeStatusFor`): the current reminder is read only if, checked AFTER the read, the cancel still stands (same restoration count, still cancelled); otherwise only this bundle's tokens count. It covers the request's own bookkeeping (`settleRequestNotice`, so a newer cancellation's delivered text never turns an old request's not-sent into sent), the sweep's text status reads, abandonment and every report. NO-TEXT CHOICE: a card that chose no text runs its reminder close and terminal suppression under the same fence, in one transaction, so a delayed request cannot suppress the marker of a newer cancellation. RECEIPTS AND ROLLBACK: the /confirm-action result save passes `keepRecoveryFinal`, so a request that paused past the receipt-gap window never replaces a `recovery_final` receipt (a plain first write is unchanged); and the window-held rollback of the pre-dispatch stamp runs in the bundle + generation fence transaction and must hit exactly the row under its own claim token, so a stale worker restores no approved marker behind a terminal bundle (`lease_lost`: no rollback, no park). Lock order everywhere: caller's rows -> bundle row (share, nowait) -> visit row (share, nowait); the finalizing transaction takes bundle FOR UPDATE then the visit share lock, the same order, and both fence locks are NOWAIT so nothing waits in a cycle. The lease is renewed between steps. REQUEST SIDE: when `liveStart` reports that the bundle is no longer the request's (the sweep holds or finished it, it expired, or the heartbeat could not be written) the request runs NO post-commit effect (no text, no follow-through): the sweep owns them and its receipt is the record. REMINDER ROWS: a visit can have several reminder rows; the approved text's status is read across EVERY row (all untouched `pending_approved` = ready; any row sent = delivered/partial/uncertain judged on every sent row's own claim token; else suppressed/other), and the claim (fenced or the request's) adopts a row only while no sibling row was touched, so an untouched sibling can never be sent a second time. A rebind that fails for ANY reason under the fence (deadlock, dropped connection) stops that offer as a `credit_rebind_error` hit and never falls through to the reversal. LIVE PATH: the request marks the bundle `complete` only when the text step has a terminal outcome on the row (or the card chose no text). If the card approved a text and no outcome was recorded (the reminder step threw before reporting, or reported not-sent while the approved marker is still untouched), `liveFinish` records the follow-through as done and leaves the bundle PENDING with the lease freed, so the sweep runs only the text step; the request's reply flags `textRetryScheduled` and the receipt says the system is retrying (no "send it by hand"). The post-commit-failure branch never calls `liveFinish`, so its bundle also stays pending. CHILDREN: a linked visit classified as already cancelled (an unlocked read) is re-read under its own row lock and checked against the restoration count pinned with the bundle; one restored since is a `child_restored_since` linked skip, never recorded as done. SEND WINDOW: when the 8 PM ET cutoff passes before the FIRST recipient is reached, the fenced send reverts any pre-dispatch stamp to the untouched approved marker, flags `windowHeld`, and the bundle parks to the next window (no attempt used); a partial fan-out keeps the terminal handling. DELIVERY EVIDENCE for the approved send is bound to its claim token, not a time window: the send writes `cancellation_notice_token` (the claim's timestamp token, ISO) into its audit rows' metadata, and the status read, the reconcile and the finalizer match audit rows by equality with the reminder's own `cancellation_notice_at`. The token is taken in the fenced claim transaction of one generation, so it can only appear on rows that send wrote; `job_status_history.transitioned_at` (a transaction START time) is no longer consulted for the approved send. A text that reads not-sent while the approved marker is still untouched (a database error before the claim; nothing reached the provider handoff) is retried on the next pass, not recorded as uncertain. TERMINAL PROOF: a bundle past the hard stop or out of attempts is first checked against the visit: a restored visit gets the abandonment result (saved outcomes and text evidence kept), never an expired report about a cancelled visit; the `expired` write and the `recovered` write both carry the proof. The bundle's terminal `recovered` status is written in the same transaction that proves the cancellation generation (visit share lock, NOWAIT); a restore found there abandons the bundle (the transaction wrote nothing, so there is nothing to replace), a busy visit retries. A tracker cancel that answers `ok:false` without throwing: `cannot_cancel_complete` (cancelled parent whose tracker already reads complete) is a reported skip (`tracker_already_complete`, dispatch alert kept); any other reason is a `tracker_rejected` retryable hit. The technician-state event (`dispatch:tech_status`) of a cleanup on a caller's transaction is sent after the commit (nothing on a rollback). SWALLOWED FAILURES (audit; a recovery step that fails must never be counted as done): in a fenced recovery every unexpected failure that the step used to log and swallow is recorded as a retryable fence hit instead (`money_step_error`, `invoice_void_error`, `credit_reversal_error`, `credit_check_error`, `tracker_error`, `tech_state_error`, `cascade_error`, `child_cancel_error`), so the bundle stays pending and is retried (at most 5 attempts, then reported with what it saved); unfenced callers keep their best-effort behavior. Deliberate verdicts stay reported skips: a money review verdict (`MONEY_REVIEW`), a Stripe lookup/cancel failure on an invoice (the invoice is left open and listed as not voided), a spent credit (its own office alert), a linked visit that changed (`LINKED_CHILD_CHANGED`). An exhausted bundle reports what it saved (skipped lists, text state; every step finished when none is open). A complete bundle that still owes a receipt is reconciled at any age (a late one raises a needs-you alert) and is never pruned. NO DEFERRED REPLAY: the fenced recovery send never queues a recipient held by the 8 PM cutoff on the generic scheduled rail (that replay carries no generation or visit-date constraint); a held recipient is reported as not reached, so the receipt says partial and not to resend to those reached. A technician-state cleanup that fails for a reason other than a fence refusal is recorded as a fence hit (`tech_state_error`), so the sweep retries the bundle instead of saving the follow-through as finished (unfenced callers stay best-effort). OFFICE ALERTS REACHABLE FROM THE SWEEP (audited): the inspection-credit alerts, the fee alert and the tracker-failure alert are fenced in their own transaction; the membership-dues "rebill the month" alert follows a void that was itself fenced, so it states a fact that happened; the cancellation text path raises no alert of its own. DELIBERATELY UNFENCED: the bundle row's own lease and result writes (its own table), the receipt on the pending action and the office alert about the recovery (informational, written after the work, and truthful about what stopped), the provider handoff itself (cannot be un-sent; the request has the same window), the post-commit side effects of a fenced child cancel or void (they follow a write that was fenced). A text parked for the send window sets `next_attempt_at` to the next opening and the claim skips the row until then, so other bundles' money and linked work never queue behind it. A row older than 24 hours, or out of 5 attempts, is NOT acted on: the sweep first CLAIMS it (the same `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` pattern, a `report:`-prefixed lease token, no attempt counted; a row a live request lease still holds is not claimable), and only the holder records the receipt, raises the alert and sets `expired`, each guarded on the claim; while ANY sweep holds a live lease on a row (this claim or a recovery claim), the request's `liveNotice` and `liveFinish` write nothing, so a finishing cancel is never reported as exhausted and a request that woke up after its own lease ran out cannot overwrite or discard what the sweep records. A request whose bookkeeping write changed no row (the sweep holds or finished the bundle) flags it (`req.ibCancelBundleLost` -> `recoveryOwnsOutcome` -> `recovery_owns_outcome` in the tool result with a pointer warning); `/confirm-action` then saves that result only if the action has none (`onlyIfEmpty`), and the sweep's receipt replaces such a pointer (`replaceRecoveryPointer`) but never a real receipt; the normal path is unchanged. An inspection-credit rebind refused by the fence aborts that offer (the fence error propagates instead of returning false and falling through to the reversal). An abandoned recovery reports the outcome its own run saved before the restore was found, including text delivery evidence: when one approved recipient was already reached and a later recipient's proof sees the restore, the partial/uncertain state is saved to `notice_outcome` and carried into the receipt and alert ("do not send it again to those reached"). SWEEP OUTPUTS ARE FINAL AND TRANSACTIONAL: for every terminal outcome (recovered, abandoned, expired, and the late receipt reconcile) one transaction locks the bundle row and checks the lease token, proves the cancellation generation when the outcome claims a standing cancel (visit share lock, NOWAIT), writes the receipt (marked `recovery_final`) and the office alert on that same transaction, and sets the terminal status last. So the receipt and alert exist exactly when the status does; a worker whose lease was taken over (a pause longer than the lease) fails the owner check and writes nothing, so it can never replace a terminal receipt or refresh the alert; a restore found at the proof rolls everything back and the abandonment is reported instead; a crash leaves the bundle pending and unwritten, so there is no half-done window to reconcile. `recordResult` replaces only an empty result or a request's `recovery_owns_outcome` pointer, never a sweep receipt. A request send that read "not sent" only because the sweep had stamped the text is re-read and reported delivered, partial or uncertain (never "send it by hand"), in its stored outcome and in its own receipt. RECEIPT RECONCILE: the request marks the row `complete` before the route saves the card's receipt, so a crash between the two would lose the receipt and the money/linked warnings. `liveFinish` stores those warnings on the row in the same write as `complete`, and the sweep reconciles: a `complete` row finished by the request 10 minutes ago or more (and inside 24 hours), whose pending action still has no result, gets the receipt rebuilt from the stored outcome (saved only if still empty) and the office alert raised from it (a skipped or unconfirmed step rings; a clean outcome leaves a quiet row); a receipt that exists is the request's own and is left alone; the row is then marked (`finish_note` `request+receipt`) so it is not checked again. A text outcome the request never recorded is reported as uncertain, never as sent. No schema change. A receipt save that reports failure, or an office alert that notifyAdmin could not save (it returns null), THROWS: the row is not marked recovered, abandoned, expired or receipt-checked, its lease is freed, and the next pass retries it (a deliberate suppression is a success; the alert dedupe key keeps a retry from doubling a row that did land). Finished rows are deleted after 90 days (they hold the approved text). The table has no foreign keys and no customer column, so it never blocks a customer merge or delete.

Stamped-$0 bills nothing, every lane (`server/services/billing-lane.js` `hasAuthoritativeZeroPrice`): `GATE_STAMPED_ZERO_FREE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `stampedZeroFreeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); off = byte-identical to before (a bare stamped 0 with no `primary_line_price` base stays indistinguishable from a never-priced row and keeps falling through to `per_application_fee` / `monthly_rate`). When on, a `scheduled_services.estimated_price` stamped exactly 0 — never NULL, never `''` — is the visit's own authoritative price in EVERY billing lane (per-application, per-visit, monthly_membership, legacy-null, annual prepay; owner ruling 2026-09-28, waves-billing skill invariant #8, superseding invariant #6's monthly-fallback note while the gate is on): `completionInvoiceAmount` and everything already routed through it (completion auto-invoice, Charge Now, the schedule preview, closeout, sibling-coverage eligibility) inherit it for free, and a handful of sites that computed a visit's charge WITHOUT going through the resolver (billing recovery's leak query and bill route, project completion, job-costing revenue, the completion-charge-verdict cap anchors) now check the same predicate, each explicitly gated so they stay byte-identical off. A callback's own bare $0 is unaffected (it is already free via the isCallback exclusions, not this rule). Restoring a voided invoice (`assertUnvoidableLinkedVisit`) refuses onto ANY visit now stamped $0, not just a callback conversion, including a combined-visit packet invoice where any billed member is stamped $0, and an invoice linked only by `service_record_id`. A static guard test (`stamped-zero-charge-fallback-guard.test.js`) fails CI if a new file reintroduces a "price > 0, else fee/rate" fallback outside the reviewed allowlist. Kill: unset the gate or any non-`'true'` value.
Plan-rate ledger nightly reconcile (`server/services/plan-rate-ledger-reconcile.js`): `GATE_PLAN_RATE_LEDGER_RECONCILE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`, and live only while `GATE_PLAN_RATE_LEDGER` is also on**, read at call time via `planRateLedgerReconcileLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, a daily 6:47 AM ET job (`server/services/scheduler.js`, `runExclusive('plan-rate-ledger-reconcile')`, recorded in job_health, re-run once if a deploy kills it) finds every live customer (`whereLiveCustomer` in `server/services/customer-stages.js`: active, pipeline stage `active_customer`, `won` or `at_risk`, not deleted; an inactive account is not billed by the dues run and is checked again the first night after it is reactivated) whose `customer_plan_rates` lines add up to a different figure than `customers.monthly_rate` by a cent or more (a NULL rate counts as zero; a customer with no lines is not a gap) and judges each one again in its own transaction under the customer-comms lock (rung 6) and then the customers row lock, the order every ledger writer uses; the locked read applies the same live rule, so an account deactivated, churned or deleted since the scan is left alone. A shortfall (bill above the lines) is parked in the customer's `unattributed` line: inserted with source `invariant_repair`, or added to the existing line, whose source, `source_estimate_id` and stamps are kept (the cancellation engine reads a human-source line's `updated_at` as its manual-override cooldown). An overshoot (lines above the bill) is never deleted or shrunk. Each distinct gap raises one Billing needs-you alert for a person (category `billing`, dedupe key `plan-rate-invariant:shortfall:` or `plan-rate-invariant:overshoot:` + `<customer>:<bill cents>:<line sum cents>`; composed by `composeAdminAlert` and raised through `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen` in `server/services/admin-alert-episodes.js`, or the plain `raiseAdminAlert` while `ALERT_EPISODES` is killed), written on the repair's own transaction so a lost alert rolls the repair back. An overshoot alert closes itself (done, with what changed as its resolution) once its gap no longer stands: the lines were corrected or cleared, the bill changed, or the account stopped being live; the same gap coming back rings again, and a person's own dismissal of a gap that still stands stays dismissed. A shortfall alert is closed only by the person who checks the repair. A customer name the alert rules refuse rings as "a customer"; at most 5 new alerts a run, the remaining customers wait untouched for the next run. It never changes `customers.monthly_rate`, never charges and never messages a customer. A customer that cannot be reconciled is logged, the others still run, and the run reads as failed in job_health. Off (either gate) = the tick returns before the cron lock: no query, no write, no alert, no job_health row. First-run sizing, production 2026-10-24 (read-only): 0 of 236 live customers with lines diverge.
Stamp-time price check for every annual prepay (`server/services/annual-prepay-renewals.js` `recordMintVisitPrices` / `holdPriceDriftedRows`, owner 2026-10-05, follow-up to #5387): `GATE_PREPAY_MINT_PRICE_HOLD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `shadow` or `true`**, read at call time via `prepayMintPriceHoldMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). #5387 holds a repriced visit out of coverage only for a term picked on the /secure card page, because only that mint records one sold per-visit price. With this gate in `shadow` or `true`, every other NEW term (staff invoice, Customer 360, invoice editor, on-site switch, estimate accept) writes one `activity_log` row (`annual_prepay_mint_visit_prices`: term id and each covered visit's `estimated_price` in cents) when it is created; a covered visit with no price of its own (a WaveGuard membership visit) is named under `unpriced` with the plan's per-visit price (`seededVisitPriceForTerm`: the prepay invoice's coverage money over the sold visits, the price the term seeds new visits with; with no prepay invoice such a visit is left unnamed; before this an unpriced visit was never named, so three WaveGuard prepays created 10-05 to 10-24 recorded nothing); the estimate accept writes it after its own visit price writes. `true`: when the term stamps coverage (activation, refresh, late payment, nightly re-stamp, completion reconcile, the pay-after-first-visit hold), a visit whose price no longer equals its recorded price (a price cleared to NULL included; for a visit recorded `unpriced`, any price of its own other than the plan's, while having no price stays covered) is not linked or stamped, bills normally, and raises the existing 'Annual prepay: repriced visit left uncovered' alert once per term and visit; the schedule editor allows the edit back to the recorded price. `shadow`: the row is written and a visit the check would hold is only logged (`[annual-prepay] shadow: term … would hold visit …`); stamping is unchanged, and a failed read or write of the row never stops a stamp or a mint. Under `true` both fail closed: a failed read stops the stamp, and a mint that cannot write its row rolls back. Not judged in any mode: a visit the row does not name (booked, seeded or pulled into coverage after the mint), a term created while the gate was off, termite annual plans and their renewals, and a /secure pick (it keeps its own #5387 baseline). Off = byte-identical to before: nothing written, nothing read. Rollback: unset the variable; rows already written are inert.
Pay after first visit (owner ruling 2026-09-30, "customers should save card, and then pay after first visit, throughout"): `GATE_PAY_AFTER_FIRST_VISIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `payAfterFirstVisitLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); needs `RECURRING_CARD_ON_FILE`. **Copy only**: the server-rendered estimate page (`estimate-public.js` `handleEstimateView` → `renderPage` `opts.payAfterFirstVisitCopy`, decided by `RecurringCards.payAfterFirstVisitCardRail(policy)`) says "nothing is charged today … billed at your first visit" ONLY for a customer on the card rail (capture required, `saved_method_consented`, `autopay_already_active`); every exempt customer, and the setup-only shape, keeps today's wording. The money paths are NOT changed by this gate: the per-application self-pay accept already saves the card and charges the attached first-visit invoice at completion; the setup-only invoice (unattached, pay link delivered) and annual prepay (charged at accept) are unchanged because completion cannot take them (see the PR body). Off = byte-identical. PR-C (`GATE_PAF_SETUP_FEE`, needs the master gate): the monthly-tier (setup-only) accept on the card rail stamps the WaveGuard setup fee on the first visit's series parent (`scheduled_services.pending_setup_fee`, the same durable claim the secure plan-choice lane uses) instead of minting a payable unattached invoice; the first PERFORMED completion adds it as a line of the visit's own invoice (one invoice, one saved-card charge, claim-backed cap allowance), `setup-fee-obligation.js` reads a live claim (or the consumed claim's record) as "deferred" so the first visit is not parked, the combined-visit packet sends a still-queued deferred claim to the office, a no-show/declined first visit bills nothing and keeps the stamp, a cancelled series never bills it, and it falls back to today's payable invoice when no series parent can carry the stamp. Consent is recorded as `after_visit_card`; `/data` carries `recurringCardPolicy.setupFeeAfterFirstVisit` (present only when true). PR-D (`GATE_PAF_PREPAY`, needs the master gate and `GATE_PREPAY_CARD_AND_CHARGE`): an in-lane annual prepay accept charges nothing at approval. The quote still binds the exact cents and method, names the `after_visit_prepay` authorization (`quote.chargedAfterFirstVisit`, `quote.consentVariant`), and the resubmit must attest it (`prepayChargeConsentVariant`); the durable job (`estimate_data.prepayAutoChargeJob`) is stamped `awaiting_first_visit` with `deferred_to_first_visit`, the year invoice stays an unsent draft, and `annualPrepayCoversVisit` holds the plan's visits (no per-visit bill) while the term is payment_pending (`pafDeferredPrepayCoversVisit`, keyed off the job's frozen flag, not the live gate). Completion stamps a visit the waiting year holds with that term at closeout (`scheduled_services.paf_held_term_id`); the release, the cancelled-year office alert and a closeout resumed after the year is paid read the stamp, never the live hold (owner ruling 2026-10-02, "stamp + narrow"). The first performed visit of a still-unpaid year gets the neutral completion text `service_complete_annual_prepay_after_first_visit` ("Your plan payment is processed after this first visit - you'll get a receipt.", no amount; owner ruling 2026-10-03); every other covered visit keeps `service_complete_annual_prepay`. The earlier `service_complete_annual_prepay_first_charge` seed is unused. A year minted to, or resolving to, a third-party payer at approval is never deferred: the normal job routes it to the payer. `server/services/paf-prepay-release.js`, run at the start of every prepay sweep, releases the job to `pending` after the first PERFORMED visit (invoice due that day) and the sweep charges the bound method with the acknowledged total as a ceiling (lower when credit applies, owner R1); a decline delivers the pay link, raises one office alert and keeps later visits held (owner R2); no performed visit 14 days after approval raises one office alert (owner R8); a voided or cancelled year before any visit resolves `cancelled_before_visit` and charges nothing. PR-E: `/data` `recurringCardPolicy.prepayAfterFirstVisit` drives the React page's after-visit wording, capture/confirm consent text and attestation, and the `after_first_visit` success copy. PR-A plumbing (no behavior change): per-item sub-gates `GATE_PAF_EXISTING_CUSTOMERS` / `GATE_PAF_SETUP_FEE` / `GATE_PAF_PREPAY` / `GATE_PAF_TERMITE` (readers `pafExistingCustomersLive()` / `pafSetupFeeLive()` / `pafPrepayLive()` / `pafTermiteLive()`; each also requires the master gate); `RecurringCards.payAfterFirstVisitInvoiceRail(policy)` is the one shared "invoice rides the card lane" predicate (estimate-public.js's accept, renderer pick and `/data` all call it); `/data` `recurringCardPolicy.payAfterFirstVisit` (present only when true; no client reads it yet); consent variants `after_visit_card` / `after_visit_prepay` (card + ACH) under the `v12_2026-09-30` label (`consentVersionForVariant`) with the global `CONSENT_VERSION` left at v11 — server `payment-method-consent-text.js`, client mirror `paymentMethodConsentText.js`. PR-F (`GATE_PAF_TERMITE`, needs the master gate; owner clause approved 2026-10-03): the termite annual agreement's BILLING clause (migration `20261003130000`, draft v3 body only while unpublished) says the setup + first annual fee are charged to the payment method on file after the station installation is completed. The timing is decided by the SIGNED text, never by the gate: an agreement signed on that wording records `estimates.annual_plan_signature_charge = {status:'awaiting_installation'}` at signing (no charge, no pay link) and the daily termite sweep (`chargeInstalledTerms`) charges it once the plan's installation visit is completed, with the same claim, consent record, frozen-total cap, drift hold and bells as the signing charge; an agreement signed on the at-signing wording keeps the charge at signing. The gate controls ISSUE only: with it off, an active annual template carrying the after-installation wording parks the accept for manual prep (same bell as an inactive template), so no customer is handed that text. Payer-billed invoices never enter the wait. Owner ruling 2026-10-03 ("stamp the visit"): the closeout stamps the installation visit with the plan's term (`scheduled_services.paf_held_term_id`, through `pafDeferredHoldingTerm` → `termite-annual-activation.js deferredInstallHoldingTerm`), the same stamp the deferred prepay year uses. That stamp is the installation's identity: the plan covers the visit (no completion bill beside the plan invoice), the charge release reads it (a stamped, completed visit whose newest closeout is performed and not a backfill), and the visit sends the neutral `service_complete_annual_prepay_after_first_visit` text while the plan is still unpaid. One stamped visit per plan. An installation billed to a payer, paid another way, closed as not performed, or a backfill is never stamped, so it never releases the automatic charge; the 14-day office alert covers it. A plan still waiting 14 days after signing with no completed installation raises one office alert. The accept payload carries `annualChargeAfterInstallation: true` (present only when true) for the sign-agreement card. Rollback: unset the gate (new accepts park); agreements already signed on the wording still charge after installation, as signed.

SMS portal-link wrap (`server/services/messaging/sms-link-wrap.js`): `GATE_SMS_LINK_WRAP` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `smsLinkWrapLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); off = every SMS body byte-identical to before. On, `sendCustomerMessage` rewrites every owned-portal-host link in a customer/lead SMS body (full https or scheme-less; recognition is `ownedPortalLinkSpans` in `composer-customer-links.js`, the same host-exact run judgement as the bearer fences) that is not already `/l/` into a tracked short code (`kind 'other'`, `entity_type 'portal:<family>'`, `purpose 'sms_link_wrap'`), immediately before `countSegments` so the audit body, segment count and provider text agree. After an accepted send, codes are stamped `message_ref = 'sms_log:<id>'` (or `twilio_sid:<sid>`); a blocked, held or uncertain attempt leaves its code unstamped (an inert redirect nobody was sent; codes are never deleted) and a retry mints its own. Log lines carry the link family and an error code only — never a URL, token or raw error message. Never blocks a send: any mint failure keeps the original link and logs a warn. Never touches internal/applicant audiences, MMS bodies, non-portal hosts, the bare portal home, links already short, `/reschedule/`, `/inspection/` and `/rate/` links (their own senders mint the entity linkage `reschedule-link-promises.js`, `call-booking-link-text.js` and the review-link fence read), or `review_request` / `missed_call_followup` sends (they stamp their exact body and later search the provider for it, `TwilioService.findOutboundMessageSince`). Kill: unset the gate or any non-`'true'` value.
Email links that open the app (`server/services/messaging/email-link-policy.js`): `GATE_EMAIL_APP_LINKS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `emailAppLinksLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, `sendOne` (`server/services/sendgrid-mail.js`) marks anchors to customer pages on the portal host `clicktracking=off`, so SendGrid leaves them unwrapped and iOS universal links / Android App Links open them in the Waves app; off = every email link goes through SendGrid's click host (`click.wavespestcontrol.com`) and opens the browser, as before #7229. Keep OFF until the app lands on the tapped page: on 2026-10-31 a tapped `/?tab=billing` and `/book` link opened the iPhone app (1.7) on Home. Kill = unset; takes effect on the next send, no redeploy.

Admin alert relevance (`server/services/admin-alert-relevance.js`): `ADMIN_ALERT_RELEVANCE` — **ships LIVE: on unless set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `adminAlertRelevanceLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); off = byte-identical to before (the env is a pure kill switch, no redeploy). An unread admin bell clears itself when the visit, series move or lead it is about has moved on (owner ruling 2026-09-28, rule 14: auto-applied, no bell): a 10-minute sweep (`runAdminAlertRelevanceSweep`, scheduler.js) marks read every matching unread row (no age cut-off: a refreshed bell keeps its first `created_at`) and stamps `metadata.retired = {by, reason, at}` — each retirement judged on a fresh read right before the write, written only onto that exact version of the bell (category, link and metadata: a bell an emitter refreshed in between is left for the next sweep), and judged once more after it on the bell as it then stands, putting it back when a change landed in between or that check could not finish (a person's own read, or a refresh that rang it again, always wins); a retirement holds only while its rule does — the emitters in the table are one-shot, so each run first judges again what it retired in the last 14 days and puts back, unread, any row whose subject is relevant again (a booking cancelled, a visit reopened) — only while the row's read is still the one the sweep wrote (the stamp's `at` is that `read_at`), so a person's later read is never undone — and older retirements are final; no row locks ever, since invoice settlement takes the visit `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` and a sweep holding a lock would fail that payment. A bell always rings as its emitter wrote it; the sweep clears it within minutes. "Moved on" is judged from what the bell itself is about, never the customer's account, and only the classes in the module's `CLASSES` table, whose emitter never re-raises the alert on a stable dedupe key: stale visit (its own condition ended — the visit left on_site/en_route, was moved to today or later, or is gone; the emitter was removed in #5223), series move (settled item by item: each windowless conflict given a time, closed or gone; each preserved occurrence closed or gone; any item whose day has passed; a card-only pass for a superseded move stores only its own conflicts), promise marks (`visit-promise-marks:<visit>`, raised when a technician's Done or Partly mark never reached the office's promise list: settled once every promise it names is closed, gone, or acted on by the office after the bell, and closed by its emitter when a resumed completion saves the marks), new lead (the intake bell, `metadata.triggerKey = 'new_lead'`, only — a direct `new_lead` notice such as a repeat submission filed as a duplicate is fresh work — and judged ONLY by what happened after the bell: the lead deleted, a quote sent (the one it points at, or any to its customer — a newer draft can take over `leads.estimate_id` without un-sending one), or a live visit booked for its customer, never a system-generated child or one that did not run; a status carries no time and the lead's state can predate the bell, e.g. a website submission attached to a lead already quoted; `converted_at` is not evidence, since booking the lead stamps it and cancelling that visit never clears it). An alert whose emitter re-raises a stable key (the first-application split, the schedule watchdog's price / prepay / plan reviews, the estimate hot view) is its emitter's to clear with its own recurrence rules — a retire from outside would keep the key and swallow a comeback, or free it and fight the emitter's dedupe. Customer-contact bells (`inbound_sms`, `inbound_email`, `voicemail_callback`) are in the table only behind `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE` (the next paragraph); a missed-call bell is not in the table at all (`missed-call-bell.js` owns it); `review` bells and payment-owed/failed/refund alerts never are. Two other customer-contact bells are in the table by owner ruling (2026-10-03), each closed only by the record that answers it: the promise-chaser bell (`promise_chaser:<promise>:…`) once the promise it chases is closed (kept, dismissed, or dismissed by staff; a promise row that is gone is not judged; this retirement is final, `rearm: false`, like the close the emitter itself writes inside its 30-minute window — a promise reopened later is the promise list's and the SLA pager's to surface), and a portal chat hand-off whose stored `metadata.topic` is `add_service` once any estimate is handed off to that customer after the bell, judged by the promise lane's handoff witness (`handedOffWithin` + `whereEstimateCustomerOwnership` in `call-commitments.js`: a real delivery or the customer's acceptance, never `sent_at` alone; the bell records the topic, not the service asked about; every other topic, and a bell written before the topic was stored, stays a person's to close). A call last-name suggestion (`call-last-name-suggestion:<customer>`, category `customer`, owner 2026-10-08) is in the table too: it closes once its customer has a non-blank last name or is gone (deleted or soft-deleted); a live customer with a blank last name keeps it, and a name blanked again inside the 14-day window puts it back. A retire is a pure `read_at` + `retired` stamp, so it reads like a human dismissal to anything else. A new alert class joins the table with its own rule; it is not a new hook.

Customer-contact alerts close themselves once a person answers (`server/services/admin-alert-relevance.js`, witnesses in `server/services/admin-alert-contact-witnesses.js`): `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE` — **ships DARK, three states, read at call time via `alertContactCloseMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`): unset or anything but `shadow` / `true` = off, `shadow` = judge and RECORD, `true` = close**. Owner 2026-10-24 ("most of these should close automatically ... text sent, agent confirms resolved, appt booked, rescheduled"), approved 2026-10-26; it replaces the old line that kept customer-contact bells out of the sweep. Off = byte-identical to before: the three relevance classes are not in the candidate query, nothing is read for them and the new-lead bell keeps only its own reasons. `shadow` = the sweep judges them and writes ONE `audit_log` row per bell per class per Eastern day (`action` `notification.alert_relevance.would_close`, `resource_type` `notification`, `resource_id` the bell, `metadata` `{class, reason, judgedAt, etDay}`) and changes nothing on the bell (no metadata stamp: emitters compare metadata on a refresh and the retire's version fence reads it); list them with `SELECT created_at, resource_id, metadata FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'notification.alert_relevance.would_close' ORDER BY created_at DESC`. `true` = the sweep's normal retire (`done_by` `relevance`, the reason as the resolution, `metadata.retired` stamp, judged on a fresh read, landing only on the version judged, judged once more after). Rollback: unset the gate; the next sweep's re-arm pass also puts back, unread, whatever the contact classes closed in the last 14 days (a rollback restores the bell), and `ADMIN_ALERT_RELEVANCE=off` stops the whole sweep. The classes, each judged only by events AFTER the text, call or email the bell is about, each witness the repo's existing definition and `read_at` never evidence: **text** (`inbound_sms`, trigger `sms_reply`; a known sender's `sms-thread:<customer>` row only. An unknown sender's text bell, with no customer on file, is NOT judged at all: it stays a person's to close and the 30-day retention closes it) closes when `loadPendingSmsConversations` (the Messages "needs a reply" reader) no longer counts that number (reasons "Answered by text", "Answered by a call", else "Answered, or no reply needed": a courtesy text or an assistant reply); **voicemail callback** (`voicemail_callback`, trigger `customer_voicemail_callback`) closes when a person called back and spoke (`personCallBackSql`), the customer called in and a human answered (`answered_by = 'human'`), a person's text reached them (`operatorReplySql` + `smsDeliveredSql`, minus proactive drafts), a visit was booked (the new-lead class's top-level live-visit read) or a quote was handed off (`handedOffWithin` + `whereEstimateCustomerOwnership`), matched by customer id or phone identity (`phoneIdentitySql`) so an unknown caller works (the call's anchor is its real start, `callStartedAt`, since a row inserted after the call was over carries a post-call `created_at`; a call is judged by when it ENDED, `callEndedAtSql`, the Messages reader's definition); **missed call** (`missed_call`, trigger `customer_missed_call`) has ONE owner, `missed-call-bell.js` `retireCalledBackMissedCalls` (the 2-minute call-alert cron, closing through `supersedeMissedCallAdmin`, no relevance stamp, never re-opened): its existing proof (`calledBackSql`, a later answered call, an alerted voicemail or our dialed callback) and `GATE_MISSED_CALL_VISIT_UNDERWAY` are untouched, and this gate adds three clauses, each with its own resolution and each anchored on the call's START: a person's text reached the caller (`operatorReplySql` + `smsDeliveredSql`, by the call's customer or the caller's phone) — "A person texted the caller after the call"; a visit was booked for the call's customer (the live top-level booking predicate) — "A visit was booked after the call"; a quote was handed off (`handedOffWithin` + `whereEstimateCustomerOwnership`) — "An estimate was sent after the call". Off = none of them runs; `shadow` = the same `audit_log` rows (class `missed_call`), nothing retired; `true` = retired. The promise chaser, repeat caller and Sandy hand-off bells keep their own owners. **email** (`inbound_email`, trigger `customer_email_received`) closes on a person's Gmail reply in its thread (`personSentFilter` + `resolveEmailCustomerLink`, a SENT row that reaches that customer) or any call witness above; **new lead** gains "Lead was contacted" (a person's text or call back after the bell, by the lead's customer or phone). On a SHARED phone (another customer is tied to the number by a live `customers` row, or a text, call or thread row carrying a different customer id) the Messages reader's phone-level verdict is not used at all: a text bell closes only on this customer's own evidence by customer id (a person's reply to them, sent or delivered, or a person's call with them), never "Answered, or no reply needed". A new text from a known sender rewrites the sender's one thread row and rings it again, and the refresh now also drops the `retired` stamp (a ringing refresh clears the done fields) so the sweep judges the row again; an Witnesses that fail to load are no verdict: nothing closes and the re-arm pass leaves closed rows as they are. Sends nothing to anyone.

A staff action answers a text (`GATE_SMS_STAFF_ACTION_ANSWERS`; owner 2026-10-29, decision page "Stuck Alert Fixes", F1: "A staff action answers a text"). **Ships DARK, three states, read at call time via `staffActionAnswersMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`): unset or anything but `shadow` / `true` = off.** The real cases: a customer texted "remove that spot" and the office booked a Lawn Care Re-Service eleven minutes later; a customer texted "I will Zelle you $108" and the office recorded the Zelle payment four minutes later. The system's own confirmation, invoice and receipt texts are automatic types, so the Messages reader never counted them as an answer and both texts stayed "needs reply" (and the evening Comms digest listed one again every day). A STAFF ACTION for the text's customer, BY CUSTOMER ID only (never the phone), after the text and within 24 hours of it, now answers it. The one definition is `server/services/sms-staff-action-answers.js`: (a) a visit a person created in the admin: `scheduled_services.created_at` in (text, text + 24 h], `recurring_parent_id` IS NULL (never a series top-up), status not in the never-ran statuses, and `source_action` in `STAFF_VISIT_SOURCE_ACTIONS` (`admin_manual`, `admin_ib`, `admin_new_caller`; automatic sources such as `voice_agent`, `ai_call_pipeline*`, `package_followup_auto` are not staff actions); (b) a payment a person recorded: `invoices.payment_recorded_by` is set and is not the Zelle notice reconciler's `zelle-notice-reconciler`, `payment_recorded_at` in (text, text + 24 h] (a card or Auto Pay payment stores no `payment_recorded_by`). Reasons: "A visit was booked" and "A payment was recorded". `shadow` = the admin text alert (class `inbound_sms`, inside `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE`) RECORDS the would-close (`notification.alert_relevance.would_close`) and nothing else changes; the Messages reader's SQL and output are byte-identical to off. `true` = the alert closes with the action named, AND `loadPendingSmsConversations` (`server/services/sms-pending-conversations.js`) counts the text as answered, like `answered_inbound`, so the Messages Unanswered filter, the badge, the evening Comms digest and the alert agree. On a shared phone the customer-id action closes only that customer's alert. In `true`, the action is named before the plain "Answered, or no reply needed" fallback. Rollback: unset the gate; the reader lists the text again and the next sweep's re-arm pass puts back, unread, the alerts it closed in the last 14 days.

Two admin-alert relevance rules with their OWN gates (`server/services/admin-alert-relevance.js`; owner 2026-10-29, decision page "Stuck Alert Fixes", F3 and F5), so a new reason can run in shadow while `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE` is `true`. Both ship DARK, three states, read at call time: unset or anything but `shadow` / `true` = off, `shadow` = judge and RECORD one `audit_log` row per bell per class per Eastern day (`notification.alert_relevance.would_close`, nothing on the bell changes), `true` = the sweep's normal retire (`done_by` `relevance`, reason as the resolution, `metadata.retired` stamp). Rollback for each: unset it; the next sweep's re-arm pass puts back, unread, whatever it closed in the last 14 days. **`GATE_VOICEMAIL_VISIT_UNDERWAY`** (`voicemailVisitUnderwayMode()`): one more reason on the `voicemail_callback` class, "The customer's visit went ahead after the call" (the missed-call lane's wording, `VISIT_UNDERWAY_RESOLUTION` in `missed-call-bell.js`). The voicemail's customer, BY CUSTOMER ID only (never the phone), has a visit with `completed_at` after the voicemail's real start (`callStartedAt`) on the same America/New_York date, in a status that is not one that never ran (cancelled, canceled, no_show, skipped); any visit counts, not only a top-level booking, and the missed-call rule's invoice-paid clause is NOT copied. Voice items only (an email bell never gets it), and only when no person's contact witness (call back, answered call, text, booked visit, handed-off quote) closes the bell first. It never closes more than `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE` allows (that gate off = the class is not judged; `shadow` = the visit reason is recorded only). **`GATE_LEAD_CONTACTED_CLOSE`** (`leadContactedCloseMode()`): a new `lead_contacted` class, the whole class under this gate and independent of `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE` (off = not in the candidate query, no witness read). It matches category `lead` with `metadata.doneWhen = 'lead_contacted'` and a lead id (`metadata.leadId` or the link's `?lead=`): the bells of `lead-call-text-followup.js`, `lead-call-reply-ring.js`, `sms-lead-extraction.js` and `lead-unverified-hold.js`. The repeat-form alert shares that doneWhen but keeps its own class (`lead_repeat_form`, always on, matched first); a bid-invite Leads bell (`doneWhen` `bid_decided`), an FYI and a customer-only bell never match. It closes only on facts AFTER the bell's latest event: the later of `created_at` and `metadata.rungAt` (a refresh that changes content rings and stamps `rungAt` but keeps `created_at`, so a reply before the refresh never settles the new request): "Lead was contacted" (a person's text or call back, the same witnesses as the new-lead `lead` contact kind), "A visit was booked" (a live top-level visit for the lead's customer, the new-lead class's read) or "Estimate was sent" (the promise lane's handoff witness, `handedOffWithin` + `whereEstimateCustomerOwnership`, never `sent_at` alone). A lead row that is gone is unknown. Sends nothing to anyone.
**`GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_ANSWERED_CLOSE`** (`portalChatAnsweredCloseMode()`, owner 2026-10-31, approved Portal inbox plan: "a chat item closes itself when someone texts, calls or emails that customer after the request"): a portal chat hand-off bell (`server/services/ai-assistant/assistant.js` `notifyTeamOfEscalation`: category `alert`, dedupeKey `portal-chat-escalation:<escalationId>`, `metadata.doneWhen` `customer_answered`, a `metadata.customerId`) closes once a PERSON reached that customer after the bell's latest event (the later of `created_at` and `metadata.rungAt`, so a re-rung bell is judged from its re-ring). Three states, read at call time, dark by default: unset or anything but `shadow` / `true` = off; `shadow` = judge and record one `audit_log` row per bell per Eastern day (`notification.alert_relevance.would_close`), the bell is unchanged; `true` = the sweep's normal retire (`done_by` `relevance`, reason as the resolution). It rides on `GATE_ALERT_CONTACT_CLOSE` too: the weaker of the two wins, and that gate `off` means no portal chat bell is judged. Reasons, in order: "A person called back", "A person answered their call", "Answered by text", "Answered by email" (a person-sent Gmail row received after the bell in ANY thread that `resolveEmailCustomerLink` links to the customer; read only for rows whose To/Cc/Bcc carry the customer's own address). A visit booked or an estimate is NOT a reason here. The add-a-service chat (`portal_chat_add_service`) keeps its "Estimate was sent" rule and also closes on this contact. The confirmed-email-change bell (`portal-chat-email-change:`, `doneWhen` `email_changed`) is never judged. With the gate `off` the class is not in the candidate query, no witness is read, and the next sweep's re-arm pass puts back, unread, whatever it closed in the last 14 days. Sends nothing to anyone and calls no paid API.

Alert episodes (`server/services/admin-alert-episodes.js`: `closeAdminAlertKeys` / `openAdminAlertKeys` / `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`, shared by the schedule-integrity watchdog and the hot-estimate alert — `first-application-sibling-split.js` keeps its own copy of the pattern): `ALERT_EPISODES` — **ships LIVE: on unless set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `alertEpisodesLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); off = the pre-episode behaviour (no close pass, no reopen, the same `notifyAdmin` calls; pure kill switch), except that a suppressed internal-test alert never takes a slot of the per-run cap in either mode. The watchdog's four classes (unpriced series, lawn-email gap, prepay coverage, accepted plan) now clear themselves when the problem is fixed and ring again on a comeback, the first-application split's pattern: each run raises the class's complete live set (the per-run cap of 10 counts only rows newly created or re-rung, never a silent dedupe onto a standing row) and marks every open bell of the class whose key is absent read + `autoCleared` (read rows too, so a person's read never blocks a comeback); a raise onto an `autoCleared` row bumps `recurrenceGeneration` and re-rings, while a standing row is never re-versioned (rows written before this carry no `dedupeVersion`). A prepay-coverage review whose visit COMPLETED (or was rescheduled) is never closed by the pass — completion is when the prepay billing mistake happens, and the scan no longer sees the visit — so it stays for a person to clear, as before episodes; a superseded prepay key (matched per visit and issue) or lawn-email key closes only once its replacement was delivered this run (a cap-held replacement leaves the old bell up). Under episodes an authoritative $0 (`hasAuthoritativeZeroPrice`, `GATE_STAMPED_ZERO_FREE`) is a price for this class, upcoming, overdue or completed: the visit's own stamp, or its parent's for a child that inherits the parent's price. An unpriced series stays LIVE while it has an overdue unpriced visit, or a visit that COMPLETED (its own `completed_at`; a backfilled completion without one never counts, since `updated_at` moves on any later edit) since its bell first rang (the earliest of the bell's `created_at` and `metadata.episode_started_at`, the run's pre-scan time, so a completion racing the first insert counts; a later reopen never moves it) still unpriced by its own row (the scan's rule; an authoritative $0 under `GATE_STAMPED_ZERO_FREE` counts as a price): such a held series keeps its existing bell, and a bell auto-cleared meanwhile (priced, then the price removed) reopens and rings; it never starts a new bell, since the class pages upcoming visits only. Whether a completed visit was billed right is a person's call. A series has ONE bell, composed from everything the run knows about it: it leads with the most urgent fact (a visit that completed without a price, then one past due, then the next visit) and names the others; its text follows the series through a quiet refresh (`ringOnRefresh` false) that never re-rings it, so a person's read stands; a reopen always rings. The standing-row read in `raiseAdminAlertWithReopen` takes a row lock (`forUpdate`), newest row first (`notifyAdmin`'s own lookup reads the newest row too), so a person's dismissal is never overwritten by a refresh. A fifth class, `churned-live-work:<customer id>`, pages a customer churned OUTSIDE the app's cancel steps: live `pipeline_stage` `churned`, not soft-deleted, and no `churn_episode_id` (the cancel processor mints one on every whole-account churn and every reactivation path clears it; what the cancel steps leave on purpose, like paid visits kept to `term_end`, visits parked for review or a refund owed, is never residue). It pages the work those steps would still clean up: a live visit the sweep would pull (`whereVisitRowLive`, minus the visits an end-at-term lapse keeps by the cancel's own identity, its term's `coverageRowsForTerm` set through `term_end`, not rescheduled), a `recurring_ongoing` series anchor, an undecided paid prepay term still covering (a decided lapse is the renewal machinery's outcome), an unpaid prepay invoice, and an invoice the cancel would void that never reached the customer (draft / scheduled, no delivery stamp, not parked on the Text/App-accepted email retry, not a third-party payer's, and linked by invoice.js's visit link to a visit the sweep would pull or one already cancelled; an invoice for finished work is an earned receivable and never counts). It clears once that work is cancelled or voided (or the customer returns) and rings again if it recurs, its text follows the work that is left through a quiet refresh, and it rings after every other class so it never starves the money pages under the cap. A class whose check failed is never closed. While episodes are on, a visit covered by a first-application invoice no longer pages as an unpriced series — the anchor by its own live invoice that bills its base application, a sibling by billing-lane's `siblingInvoiceCoverageVerdict` (`covered` only; it follows a voided combined invoice to its live replacement, and `needs_review` / `none` / `error` keep paging); if the invoice is voided with no replacement the series is live again and rings. Killed, there is no coverage lookup and such a visit pages as before. The hot-estimate alert (`server/services/estimate-hot-view-alert.js`) closes when its estimate is accepted, declined, expired or archived (checked every 5 minutes by the engagement tick, only while `GATE_ESTIMATE_HOT_VIEW_ALERT` is on) and re-rings on a new hot streak.

Accepted-plan bell rings on a changed finding (owner 2026-10-29, "go"): `GATE_ACCEPTED_PLAN_RING_ON_CHANGE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `acceptedPlanRingOnChangeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The schedule-integrity watchdog's "Accepted recurring plan needs schedule review" bell (key `accepted-schedule:<estimate id>:<service family>`, the daily 06:40 ET run) carries a `dedupeVersion`; off, that is the finding's `evidenceKey`, which hashes every visit row's revision (`xmin`) and date, so any routine edit to a visit in the plan re-rang the same standing gap: unread again, no longer Done, and never idle long enough for the 30-day expiry (production 2026-10-29: 18 open, all unread, 11 rang again in 7 days). On, the version is `finding:<findingKey>` (`server/services/recurring-schedule-audit.js`: a hash of the issues, the accepted pattern and the planned and recorded application counts, the facts the bell's text states), and its `ringOnRefresh` rings the standing row only when it moves from one finding version to another. A row still on an evidenceKey version takes the finding version quietly, so the first run after the flip rings nothing; a refresh that leaves the finding as it was is quiet too, so a person's read and Done stand; a fix followed by a comeback still rings through the alert episodes' reopen (`raiseAdminAlertWithReopen`). The bell's `appointment_ids` metadata (no reader) updates only when the finding changes. Sends nothing to a customer and changes no visit. Off = byte-identical. Rollback: unset the variable (the next run moves each standing row back to its evidenceKey version, which rings it once, within the run's cap of 10).

Customer alerts ring (owner 2026-10-29, "small" E1 of the admin bell rebuild): `GATE_CUSTOMER_ALERTS_RING` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `customerAlertsRingLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and only while `GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY` is on (the policy it changes). An admin alert can declare that it is a customer contact (`contact: true`: a customer reached us) or a promise we owe a customer (`promise: true`): a `TRIGGER_REGISTRY` type in its `rule` (10 contact types incl. `bundle_quote_requested`, 3 promise types; `server/tests/admin-alert-catalog-contract.test.js` pins the sets), a composed alert in its spec (`composeAdminAlert` stamps the flag in metadata, also on the fallback path), a raw call in its metadata (the estimator's and the call processor's quote bells: promised = `promise`, asked for = `contact`). On, `bellAllowed` (`server/services/notification-bell-policy.js`) rings a declared alert whatever its later steps say (the trigger lists, the owner's category switch, the category lists; a site's explicit `bell: false` still wins), and a customer's failed invoice payment at checkout (`bill_payment_error`) rings beside `payment_failed` under the owner's 2026-09-11 ruling. `triggerNotification` hands the type's rule to the policy and, when it let a declared type through, tags the bell write `bell: true`, so the bell and the phone push agree. Newly ringing (muted before): a customer's failed invoice payment, a customer's bundle quote request, and a quote a customer asked for or that we promised (category `lead`); every other declared alert already rang. Declarations are data: off, what rings is byte-identical, and composed and quote rows carry the flag in metadata. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback: unset the variable.

Portal chat self-serve (`server/services/ai-assistant/assistant.js`, `tools.js`): `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE` — **ships LIVE: on unless set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `portalChatSelfServeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, the portal's Waves Assistant (`POST /api/ai/chat`, channel `portal_chat`) runs its own prompt and two button tools: `offer_reschedule_link` (a Reschedule button per upcoming visit the self-serve `/reschedule/:token` page accepts, by that page's own GET verdict `pageEligibility`) and `open_portal_section` (a button that opens Billing, upcoming visits, completed visits and reports, My Plan, Documents or Refer); the reply carries them as `actions` and the model never writes a link. A reschedule ask no longer hard-escalates. A hand-off rings ONE admin bell (`raiseAdminAlert`, Comms, needs-you, person, key `portal-chat-escalation:<id>`, the customer's words in `detail`) and the reply says the team was told only when that bell exists (`teamNotified`); otherwise it says the request is saved and gives the phone number. No account data reaches the model. SMS (`channel: 'sms'`) is untouched. Killed = portal chat byte-identical to before.

Portal chat payment card (`server/services/ai-assistant/tools.js` `show_recent_payments`, `services/portal-payment-history.js`): `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_FACTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `portalChatFactsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); needs `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE` live. On, a portal chat question about a charge, payment or receipt shows the customer a server-rendered CARD of their last three payments (date, amount, description, card or bank, status, Waves receipt link) built from `listPortalPayments`, the same read as `GET /api/billing` (third-party-payer exclusions and receipt rules included), plus an Open Billing button; the reply carries it as `cards`. The model is told only that the card was shown and the status words, never an amount, date, description or card (owner ruling 2026-10-01 on money content: nothing money-shaped for the model to misstate, and no regex checker). A scheduled Auto Pay row (`upcoming`) shows as Scheduled, or Processing once its date has passed, the Billing tab's own rule; a payment status the card cannot label (anything else, or a refund that has not settled) means no card at all and the model is told to hand off; a read failure shows nothing. Off = the `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE` behavior alone, byte-identical.

Portal chat past-visit answers (`server/services/ai-assistant/tools.js` `get_recent_visits`, `services/portal-service-history.js`): `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_VISIT_FACTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `portalChatVisitFactsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); needs `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE` live; independent of `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_FACTS` (the two compose). On, a portal chat question about what was done at a visit, when the last visit was, or where a report is reads the customer's last three completed visits from `listPortalServiceHistory`, the same read as `GET /api/services` (typed-report shadow suppression, reviewed-text-only notes and report-link rules included), and the model answers from the structured facts only: date, service, technician first name, kinds of product applied (categories, never names). This is the one place account data reaches the portal model. The reviewed visit summary is free text (it can name a product or a price), so it never reaches the model: it shows on a server-rendered `visits` card (capped at 600 characters) with a View report link (`/report/<token>` only), and the reply carries it as `cards`. The Open completed visits button is added on every exit. The portal prompt also gains the owner-approved company facts block (`sms-company-facts.js`, unedited). Plan-tier contents are NOT covered (the My Plan tab derives them client-side; there is no server read to share). Off = byte-identical.

Portal chat free re-service offer (`server/services/ai-assistant/tools.js` `offer_reservice`): `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_RESERVICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `portalChatReserviceLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); needs `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE` live, plus `GATE_RESERVICE_SELF_SERVE` and `GATE_RESERVICE_STREAMLINE` (the /reservice page and the Schedule tab's hand-off to it); independent of the other portal chat gates. **Pest only unless `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_RESERVICE_LAWN` is also on** (the next entry; it adds the lawn line): on, a customer reporting household pests back between visits makes the model call `offer_reservice` (service line `pest`); with the lawn gate off, a lawn problem is escalated with topic `pest_problem`. The customer's own message that turn (never the model's reading of it, and never an earlier message carried forward past a later "they're gone now") is classified with the texting AI's shared classifier (`reportedReserviceLanes` / `reportedReserviceExcludedSpecialty`): a separately priced specialty (rodents, termites, mosquitoes, tree and shrub) in it, or no ACTIVE pest report (`isActivePestReport`, the SMS flow's predicate) in it, means no free offer ("Do you cover ants?" reports nothing). The token must pass the page's own `TOKEN_RE`. A turn that also hands off drops the booking button. The server alone decides, from the /reservice page's own verdict for the customer's token (`reservice-public` `_internals.pageLaneState`, the GET's customer load, lane catalog, coverage and open re-services, plus its `reserviceLocationReviewRequired` address hold): bookable and not on an address hold → one "Book your free re-service" button to `/reservice/<token>`; already booked (`openReserviceCallbacks`, read on its own as the page does, so a visit booked under earlier coverage still shows) → the visit's date and window to the model, and a Reschedule button only when the reschedule page's own verdict (`loadById` + `pageEligibility`) would move that visit; anything else (no plan, a lane the page does not hold, an address hold, a tokenless row, a read failure, either re-service switch off) → the model is told not to offer a free visit and to hand off with topic `pest_problem`. The prompt lets the model state that one plan fact. The button is withheld when the portal session is scoped to a secondary saved property (`isSecondarySelection`, read in `POST /api/ai/chat` only while `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE`, this gate and both re-service page switches (`reservicePageSwitchesOn`) are live; a failed scope read withholds it), because the page books at the primary address. The model never writes the link and never decides a visit is free. Portal chat (this gate or not) reads its history newest-first (the last 20 messages, put back in order, starting at a customer turn); SMS keeps the original oldest-first read. Off = byte-identical apart from that history read.

Portal chat free re-service offer, lawn line (`server/services/ai-assistant/tools.js` `offer_reservice` `lawnReportRefusal`): `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_RESERVICE_LAWN` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `portalChatReserviceLawnLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); honoured only while `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_RESERVICE` is live. On, `offer_reservice` also takes service line `lawn` with two more fields. **The model judges the language, the code only verifies** (owner ruling 2026-10-03, after the code-side lawn word list did not converge in #5651; the same pattern as call reschedules): `current_problem` must be exactly `true` (a question about lawn care, a what-if, a past or fixed problem is false) and `customer_quote` must be the customer's own words about the lawn, word for word from that turn's message (case, spacing and curly quotes folded; at least 8 characters) and name a lawn subject (`reservice-scheduler` `RESERVICE_LAWN_SERVICE_WORDS`, grass, yard). There is no list of lawn-problem wording here: do not grow one. A separately priced specialty in the message (`reportedReserviceExcludedSpecialty`: rodents, termites, mosquitoes, tree and shrub) still refuses, and everything after the report check is the pest line's path unchanged (open re-service read, the /reservice page's verdict, address hold, secondary-property withholding, the same button). The pest line keeps the server's own `isActivePestReport` and ignores the two fields. Off = the pest-only offer, byte-identical.

Portal chat email change (`server/services/ai-assistant/tools.js` `request_email_change`, `assistant.js` `escalate`): `GATE_PORTAL_CHAT_EMAIL_CHANGE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `portalChatEmailChangeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`); needs `PORTAL_CHAT_SELF_SERVE` live; independent of the other portal chat gates. An email change is a confirmed hand-off, never a write (owner ruling 2026-10-02: no self-serve email edit; staff make the change). On, the model calls `request_email_change` with the address the customer typed and `customer_confirmed` false, and is told to read it back; after the customer confirms it calls again with `customer_confirmed` true. **The model judges whether the customer confirmed, the code only verifies** what can be checked: the address is email-shaped (taken as given: no character is stripped or corrected) and at most 150 characters (`customers.email`; a longer one hands off, never read back), is one the customer typed in this chat, is not already the email on the account, and was read back in the PREVIOUS turn: that turn's own logged `request_email_change` result (`agent_messages` role `tool_use`, `read_back`) names the same address and the assistant's reply that turn shows it as a whole word, so this turn's message answers it. One definition of an address (`EMAIL_ADDRESS` in `tools.js`) serves every check: typed, shown, and left out of the keyword match. The address sent to the office is that logged read-back, character for character. Anything short of that returns the read-back instruction again. There is no list of confirmation wording here: do not grow one. A verified confirmation ends the turn as a hand-off: one `ai_escalations` row and ONE admin bell (`raiseAdminAlert`, Customers, needs-you, person, done when `email_changed`, key `portal-chat-email-change:<conversation id>:<address>`, so a confirmation the portal sent twice lands on one bell; saved with reason `account_change`; link to the customer record) whose full text carries the email on file, the confirmed new one and the customer's message; a same-turn `escalate` call adds no second bell: its topic and reason ride on the email bell's full text and the saved row (always, since another account change shares the topic), a gap it flags is filed under its own reason, and such a hand-off rewrites a bell already standing on the key (`refreshOnDedupe`) keeping every request line the standing bell already carries (`standingRefresh`, under the key's lock), so a duplicate confirmation adds a request and never removes one. The reply is a fixed sentence naming the new address and saying the team will update it (or, when the bell did not ring, that the request is saved, with the phone number); it never says the email was changed.
