The email on file never reaches the model, and nothing writes the customer row. Under the gate, email addresses in a message are left out of the keyword hand-off match (an address containing "owner" or "adam" is not a request for the owner). A keyword hand-off ("yes, and cancel my service") runs before the model, so nobody judged the confirmation: when that message answers a read-back, the ordinary hand-off's saved row and bell text carry the email on file and the read-back address marked not yet confirmed. A failed read hands off through `escalate` with topic `account_change`. When the tool sends an email request to the team this way (a failed read, or an address over 150 characters) and the same reply already holds an `escalate` call for another request, that hand-off's bell text and saved row say the customer also asked to change their email. Under the gate an `account_change` hand-off is saved with reason `account_change`. An `escalate` call in the same response as a first read-back is answered, not run, so the customer sees the read-back. Known limit: a confirmation the portal sends twice at once makes two `ai_escalations` rows (one bell) until the turn coordinator makes the turn idempotent. Off = byte-identical.

Lawn draft timing check (`server/services/service-report/lawn-draft-timing-check.js`): `LAWN_DRAFT_TIMING_CHECK` — **ships LIVE: on unless set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `lawnDraftTimingCheckLive()`; it checks the lawn v6 copy, which is always live (owner 2026-10-03). On, a lawn technician report draft (`/admin/schedule/generate-report`) that passes the pattern screen gets one `TEXT_POLICIES.fastStructured` call (lane `lawn_draft_timing_check`) that answers, per sentence, whether it says WHEN a result will show; a yes rejects the draft like any other screen (retry, then the other provider), and the deterministic last-resort copy is checked too. Fails open: an unavailable or unusable answer, or no budget left in the report chain, accepts the draft and is logged; a draft over 20 sentences is refused. Killed = the pattern screen (`lawnResultTimingViolation`) alone, no extra model call.

Admin body guard (`applyAdminBrevityGuard` in `server/services/notification-service.js`): `ADMIN_BODY_GUARD_ALL` — **ships LIVE: on unless set to `off`, `false` or `0`** (case-insensitive), read at call time via `adminBodyGuardAllLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, an admin notification body over 110 characters in EVERY category is cut to one sentence (first line of a multi-line list, else a word-boundary cut) and the full original text is kept in `notifications.detail`, so nothing is lost. Killed = the earlier behaviour: only `ops_digest` bodies are cut and every other category is stored whole. The full text is read from the bell's "Show full text" on any non-digest row and from the Agents → Activity feed for digests; titles are never cut. A code path that rewrites a standing admin row directly must write `body` and `detail` together (`NotificationService.adminBodyColumns` / `normalizeAdminText`) and read the full text from `detail` when it has one.

Manatee permit detail collection (address-match round 2, PR R2-A; `server/services/property-lookup/manatee-permit-detail.js`, run by the Monday 7:41 AM ET permit cron right after `syncPermits`): `GATE_PERMIT_DETAIL_SYNC` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `permitDetailSyncLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); independent of `GATE_PERMIT_SYNC` (the report sync that fills `construction_permit_records`). **Collection only: nothing reads it for a lookup or a price yet, nothing is sent to anyone.** On, a slow sequential pass reads each new-home permit's public Accela record page (anonymous; the ACA search by permit number, then the linked `CapDetail` pages, a plan-revision record first and the real one next) for FIVE building facts only (Total Square Footage (Under Roof), Square Footage (Conditioned), Number of Stories, Bedrooms, Bathrooms) into new nullable columns on `construction_permit_records` (migration `20261002220000`: `conditioned_sqft`, `under_roof_sqft`, `stories`, `bedrooms`, `bathrooms`, `detail_status` ok / no_fields / not_found / error, `detail_fetched_at`, `detail_co_date`). Contractor contact, owner and every other field on the page are never parsed or stored. Candidates: `type_of_work` New Single Family, New Townhouse or New Townhouse/Duplex (trimmed, case-insensitive; New Villa and New Duplex are left out until a spot check shows the same fields), not canceled / withdrawn, never read, or a CO date the last read did not see (re-read at CO; an ok read whose re-read fails keeps its facts), or a failed read past its retry window (error 1 day, not_found 14, no_fields 30); newest issued first. Politeness: strictly one request at a time, at least `PERMIT_DETAIL_SYNC_MIN_GAP_MS` between any two (default 2500, floor 2000), `PERMIT_DETAIL_SYNC_CAP` permits per run (default 400) and `PERMIT_DETAIL_SYNC_BUDGET_MS` wall clock (default 3600000); it never runs from a customer lookup. Fail open: a parse or HTTP failure records the permit's `detail_status` and the run moves on; five consecutive `no_fields` (the page structure changed) or five consecutive request failures (Accela is down) end the run with ONE warning. Logs (`[permit-detail-sync]`) carry counts and elapsed time only, never a permit number, address or parcel. `findPermitBuildingFacts({ parcelPin, looseKey })` is the read helper the lookup will call later (newest ok row, source `manatee_permit_detail`, parcel tier before loose-key tier like `findConstructionActivity`). Off = no network and no DB read.

Listing suite size (address-match round 1, PR 5b; owner ruling 2026-10-02 "price it automatically"; `server/services/commercial-suite-size/listing-size.js`): `GATE_LOOKUP_LISTING_SIZE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lookupListingSizeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); needs `GATE_COMMERCIAL_SUITE_SIZING` live (it is a rung of that resolver) and the DataForSEO vendor (`GATE_SEO_INTELLIGENCE` + `DATAFORSEO_LOGIN`/`PASSWORD`; without them the search returns nothing and the rung is a miss). **Off = no search, no page fetch, and the sizing ladder is byte-identical.** On, `resolveCommercialSuiteSize` tries, before the DBPR license and the type default and only when no caller/tech-stated size exists (`source-arbitration.js`, unchanged), a size a public listing publishes for THIS suite: **no model anywhere** — plain code runs up to three Google queries through DataForSEO's organic SERP (`"<street number>" <street> "suite <unit>" <city> FL`, first `site:loopnet.com`, then `site:crexi.com`, then an open query only when those gave nothing; desktop, Bradenton location) and reads each result's title + description; LoopNet, Crexi, Showcase, CityFeet, CommercialCafe, 42Floors, PropertyShark, CommercialSearch, Catylist, Ten-X and Zillow refuse every server fetch (probed 2026-10-05, robots.txt included), so their text is read from the snippet only and their pages are never requested; up to three results on other hosts (a broker's site, a leasing page) are fetched once each, HTML only, 1.5 MB and 6 s each, within the leg's budget (12 s default, capped by the lookup's `deadlineAt`; skipped under 2 s), and read the same way. **A listing size needs a suite the operator typed: with none typed the leg returns nothing and runs no search, and a unit known only from the Places listing (staff answered "suite" with no typed unit) never starts it.** The text is read in blocks (a sentence, a list item, a table cell). A figure counts only when the typed street number followed by the full street (county spelling, suffix canonicalized, contiguous and ending there (only the typed city, a state or a ZIP may follow; "Test St Ext" is another road), a stated direction agreeing; a numbered route by its number: "SR 70", "State Road 70", "FL-70") precedes it within reach with no other street address in between (a word or ordinal street, with or without a direction; a one-digit house number with a street-type word), a ZIP in postal position on that anchoring block (if any; ZIP+4 on its first five digits) is the typed one, the figure is 150–100,000 sq ft, it is not a range endpoint, a bound ("up to", "from"), an estimate ("approx.", "1,350 ± SF", "1,350 SF +/-", "1,350 SF minimum", before or after the figure) or a total (a building / lot / site word before it; or the noun phrase after it, however long, naming a center, plaza, complex or other total: "25,000 SF grocery anchored neighborhood shopping center"), what follows the figure is nothing or words that describe a space ("retail space", "warehouse suite"; any other qualifier such as "per floor" or "each" is refused), hidden page content (script, style, template bodies, comments) is never read, and the figure's block names exactly one suite, this one, and the figure DIRECTLY follows a mention of it: only punctuation (and this address's own city, state and ZIP) may sit between them ("Suite 103 — 1,350 SF", "Suite 103, Bradenton, FL — 1,350 SF"); any other word in between ("Suite 103 is housed inside this 25,000 SF warehouse", "Suite 103 — parking 4/1,000 SF"), a neighbor's "Suite 105 2,000 SF", a block naming two suites, or a combined "Suite 103/104" never counts. A listing naming another city or state (abbreviated or spelled out) with no confirming ZIP is another locality's. Figures within 10% of each other are one size; two different sizes for the same suite are a conflict and the rung returns nothing. The result is `suiteSize.source` `listing_verified_text`, confidence medium, with `url` (the page the size was read from) and evidence; the admin estimate tool shows "from a public listing for this suite" with the link, the lookup pushes a MEDIUM `homeSqFt` verify flag naming the link ("confirm on site before pricing"), the engine draft parks yellow with "suite size read from a public listing: N sq ft (url) — confirm on site" (`draft-builder.js`; measured for the measured-only guards like a license size, never `footprintSizeEstimated`), and the engine reuses the lookup's listing size instead of re-resolving. Persisted on the cached `property_record` (`_commercialSuiteSize`) like a license size and re-checked after 90 days (`SUITE_SIZE_STAMP_MAX_AGE_MS`); a persisted listing stamp is reused only while the gate is on, and the pricing boundary (`translateV2CallToV1Input`) refuses a profile that still carries a listing size with 409 `LISTING_SIZE_OFF` until the lookup is re-run, so unsetting the gate stops cached and open-tab listing sizes at once. Page fetches refuse private IP literals, localhost and intranet names before any request, on every hop, through the shared `isBlockedHostname` guard. The DBPR license still runs beside a listing hit for classification only: a license at the suite makes the listing size `licenseBacked` (restaurant subtype and cadence, the license's business name), whichever source sized it; a `licenseBacked` stamp ages on the license's 30 days, not the listing's 90; a cache hit on a row whose listing stamp (for the requested unit) aged out re-reads the listing once (`listingRefresh`) instead of dropping the size, and a refresh that finds nothing marks the stamp (`refreshCheckedAt`) so the search is not repeated for 30 days; the license record behind a `licenseBacked` classification rides in the result's evidence beside the listing's; the result says whether the license list really loaded (`licenseChecked`), and the estimator engine runs the license check once more (with the call's phone, the tie-breaker when several licenses share a suite, or whenever the license leg never answered) for the classification only, appending the license's evidence. Known limit: the admin tool does not retry an unanswered license check on its own before the stamp ages out. The cache-hit path (`skipWebSearch`) and `skipListing` never run it. Fail-open: a vendor error, a timeout, an unreadable page or nothing found falls to the license rung. Logs carry counts only, never an address, business name or URL. Cost: about three DataForSEO SERP calls (≈ $0.002 each) per fresh commercial suite lookup with no stated size. PDF brochures are not read (no PDF text parser in the dependency set). Kill: unset the gate.
Permit building facts in the property lookup and estimator engine (address-match round 2, PR R2-B; `server/routes/property-lookup-v2.js` `stampPermitBuildingFacts` / `permitBuildingFactsEstimate`, `server/services/estimator-engine/source-arbitration.js`): `GATE_LOOKUP_PERMIT_FACTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lookupPermitFactsLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Reads what `GATE_PERMIT_DETAIL_SYNC` collects (R2-A): the home's own Manatee building permit's conditioned and under-roof square footage, stories, bedrooms and bathrooms in `construction_permit_records`. **Off = no table read, no stamp, and a byte-identical lookup, profile and draft.** On, every fresh lookup with a record and every non-cache-only cache hit calls `findPermitBuildingFacts` once (one indexed local query; parcel tier only with a Manatee parcel pin, loose address key otherwise, so an address outside Manatee simply finds no row) and stamps the newest permit's facts on the record as `_permitBuildingFacts` (`null` = checked, nothing on file; absent = the read could not run; fail-open, error recorded on the lookup). The enriched profile exposes `permitBuildingFacts` (conditioned / under-roof sq ft, stories, bedrooms, bathrooms, permit number, issue and CO dates, `sourceLabel` "Manatee building permit <no>, issued <Mon YYYY>") with the same three states and withholding as `subdivisionMedian`: `undefined` no stamp, `null` withheld (home sq ft already on the record, unit lookup, commercial profile, unconfirmed address, implausible area outside 400–15,000 sq ft, or gate off), object otherwise — **only ever beside an EMPTY `homeSqFt`; `homeSqFt` itself never changes and no measurement is written.** A permit story count (integer 1–4) fills an EMPTY record count: `stories` becomes the permit's and `storiesSource` is `'permit'`; a looked-up or verified count never moves. The `homeSqFt` verify flag (HIGH) names the permit, the plan figures and "confirm the size with the customer before pricing", and does not need a lot size (the new-plat miss has no county record). The admin estimate tool (`client/src/lib/lookupPrefill.js`) prefills home sq ft from the record first, the permit plan second, the plat median third, shows "From building permit" with the permit line in the lookup panel, and refuses to save the untouched prefill as a tech-verified measurement. The estimator engine (`gatherPropertySignals`) takes only the profile's exposed object (never the raw record stamp) and `resolveHomeSqft` ranks it as `permit_plan`: below county and the caller, above the plat median and the lookup estimate, confidence medium, and in `FALLBACK_SQFT_SOURCES` so a draft sized from it parks yellow with "home/building sqft from fallback source (permit_plan)". The engine does not take the permit's story count (stories provenance fails closed to the review rail without a source URL). **Public routes never carry it:** `/api/public/estimator/property-lookup` strips `permitBuildingFacts`, returns a permit-filled story count to the default and swaps the `homeSqFt` flag prose for the shared vacant-parcel copy on both the response and the lead snapshot (`publicEnrichedProfile`, documented in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`), the same treatment as `subdivisionMedian`. Nothing is sent to a customer. Logs carry no permit number, address or parcel. Kill: unset the gate — stamped rows stop exposing the estimate on the next read.
Address status line in the admin property lookup (address-match round 1, PR 4; `server/services/property-lookup/address-status.js`): `GATE_LOOKUP_ADDRESS_STATUS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lookupAddressStatusLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); needs `ADDRESS_VALIDATION_ENABLED` (the same Google Address Validation provider the call pipeline uses, `server/services/address-validation/`). **No scope effect: it changes no measurement, verify flag, cache row or price, and nothing is stored.** Off = no validation call and a byte-identical response. On, the admin estimate tool's own lookup route (`POST /property-lookup`; no other caller of `performPropertyLookup`, and no public route) asks Address Validation beside the lookup (never ahead of it) and adds `meta.addressStatus = { state, corrected?, use: { business, residential }, checkedAt, countyRoll }`: `state` is `confirmed` (resolved to a premise in the service area; `corrected` when Google rewrote a typed component), `unit_missing` (a premise in the service area whose ONLY missing component is the unit), `needs_confirmation` (incomplete, unconfirmed or ambiguous), `outside_service_area`, or `unavailable` (validation off, no key, a 4 s cap at which the provider call is aborted, a provider error, or a resolved premise whose county reverse-geocode failed: never an address failure, and not remembered); `use` carries Google's own `result.metadata.business` / `.residential` booleans (`deriveStatus` now returns them as `addressUse`; this is Google's classification, NOT USPS data — `uspsData` is a separate field nothing here reads; null when Google gave none; display only, no status reads them); `countyRoll` (`countyRollAnswer`) reads the typed number's audit first: `not_found` (the audit ran for a county and has no exact match, even when a record for another house number came back), `found` (an exact audit match, or with no completed audit a county-backed record) or `unknown` (no audit and no record, an audit that could not run, or only a snapped-record marker: never shown as a miss), from the lookup's own evidence, kept apart from the address state (an address Google confirms can still be missing from the roll). One call per address per 24 hours (in-process memo of 500, keyed on the trimmed lower-cased address); a second lookup of the same address while the first is still asking joins that call. The panel (`PropertyLookupResult.jsx`) shows one line under the address ("Address confirmed · Google: business address · Not on the county roll") and, when the lookup's existing `address` verify flag is up, says "We could not confirm this address" only for `needs_confirmation` / `outside_service_area` (or no status, as before); for a confirmed or unavailable address it names the county roll instead ("no record" only when `countyRoll` is `not_found`; a record that was found but may belong to another house number gets a mismatch line), and for `unit_missing` with no record it asks for the unit. Logs carry the state only, never the address. Cost: one Address Validation call (plus its county reverse-geocode) per distinct address per day from the admin tool. Kill: unset the gate.
Business identity in the property lookup and estimator engine (address-match PR 5-1; `server/services/property-lookup/business-identity.js`, `business-scope.js`): `GATE_LOOKUP_BUSINESS_IDENTITY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `lookupBusinessIdentityLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy); needs `GATE_COMMERCIAL_SUITE_SIZING` live too and the same opt-in (`options.commercialSuiteSizing`: the admin estimate tool's lookup route and the engine's `gatherPropertySignals`; public routes never reach it). **Off = no Places request and a byte-identical lookup, profile and engine draft.** A storefront with its own street number inside a plaza parcel whose situs is a different address has no county record (the situs guard dropped the point parcel), so it used to price off the satellite or the whole building. On, for a COMMERCIAL lookup or one with no county record, one Google Places (New) `places:searchNearby` call (60 m circle at the geocode point, 20 results, field mask limited to id, display name, primary type, types, business status, address components and location: no reviews, phones or hours; 2.5 s default timeout, `LOOKUP_BUSINESS_IDENTITY_TIMEOUT_MS`; fail-open to no signal) reads which OPERATING business sits at the typed street number, its subpremise, how many operating places share the number and how many others are nearby; results are ranked nearest first (`rankPreference: DISTANCE`), and a lookup with a deadline gives the call only what is left after the response margin (skipped under 300 ms). **Nothing from Places is stored**: Google's Places policies allow keeping a place ID and nothing else, so the answer lives for one request, is never stamped on the cached record, a cache hit asks again (`cacheOnly` never asks), and the admin tool shows the listed name with a "Google Maps" attribution and strips it from the pricing call and the saved estimate; `saveLookup` drops `businessIdentity` from the stored `enriched_snapshot`. If the CSR answered the question and the re-run cannot reach Places, the answer is not dropped: the profile stays `scope_unresolved` (question open, no price) until an answered lookup succeeds. Everything after the call is plain code (a place-type table to the existing commercial subtype vocabulary, string and number comparisons): no model reaches a size or price. **Places only suggests; staff confirm (owner 2026-10-03).** A listed business never changes the profile by itself: `resolveBusinessScope` returns `scope_unresolved` with the question "Are we treating just your space or the whole building?" and a display-only `serviceScopeSuggestion` (`suite` for a typed suite, the place's own subpremise, two or more tenants at the number or county part-building evidence; `building` for a county-recorded stand-alone building with no neighbors; else null — neighbors alone never suggest a suite), the classification and sizes stay the base ones, and there is **no price until staff answer** (HIGH flag marked `source: 'google_places'`; pricing boundary 409 `COMMERCIAL_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED`). Staff answer on the admin lookup body field `occupancy`: `suite` → `commercial_suite`, `building` → `entire_commercial_building` (both make the lookup COMMERCIAL with the business's type, `commercialDetectionSource` `staff_confirmed_business`; a residential record type is never asked or flipped), `none` → "not this business", base profile, pricing allowed. Association jobs and own-unit condo folios are never asked. The admin-only fields `serviceScopeDecision`, `serviceScopeQuestion`, `serviceScopeSuggestion`, `occupancyAnswer` and `businessIdentity` (name, type, matched-by, tenants) appear only with an identity; `businessIdentity`, the suggestion and `google_places` flags are dropped from the stored snapshot, the pricing call and the saved estimate, and an unanswered snapshot also drops the open question. The estimator engine never sends an answer and never promotes a lead on a listing: a commercial lead, or a residential one whose caller does not say they live there, goes red with `commercial_scope_unresolved`; a caller who lives there stays residential with a review reason. **Parent parcel (PR 6, same gate):** when the situs guard drops a point-in-parcel hit (the parcel's situs is another address), `ai-property-lookup.js` keeps WHICH parcel it was as `_parentParcel` on the record (parcel id, county, situs, use code, edge distance; never lot or building figures) if `GATE_COMMERCIAL_SUITE_SIZING` is live too, the geocode is ROOFTOP, the point is at least 5 m inside the parcel line, the parcel is DOR major 11–27 (stores, offices, restaurants; never apartment, condo, residential, mobile-home park, hotel or industrial), the typed address names no dwelling unit, and the roll did not resolve the typed address itself. When no fact provider returns a record, the lookup returns a facts-free `_contextOnly` record with it, which is never cached, counts as record-less for the attempt status, and is returned only to an opted-in caller (admin tool, engine). Every live lookup through the property-lookup route keeps the context (`retainParentParcel`) so the shared cache row does not depend on who filled it; a direct caller of `lookupPropertyFromAITrio` never gets it; the route strips it from every non-opted caller's response. A live lookup also stamps `_parentParcelChecked`; an opted-in, non-cache-only lookup treats a cached row with no county evidence and no such marker as a miss, so rows cached before the flip are re-run once. Its only effect is on the suggestion: it counts as part-building evidence, so the panel suggests `suite`. A commercial profile (the lookup's own read, or the category a staff scope answer resolved) on a county parcel the roll lists under several addresses (`_raw.multiSitusParcel`) and did not positively identify as a mobile-home park gets neutral wording on its `parkParcel` verify flag ("one of N addresses on a single county parcel") instead of the land-lease-community wording, with or without this gate; several addresses on one parcel alone never change the suggestion. A suite known only from the staff answer (no unit typed) never applies an address-wide verified size (flagged for reconfirmation instead), and a whole-building answer withholds a verified size (blank, HIGH flag) until staff enter the building's. Logs carry counts and elapsed time only, never a business name or address. Kill: unset the gate — new lookups stop asking Places, and the pricing boundary refuses a profile that still carries a business scope with 409 `BUSINESS_IDENTITY_OFF` until the lookup is re-run. Campus parcel context (2026-10-23): when the kept parent parcel is in Manatee, the lookup also reads that parcel's PAO building table (one request, 4 s, beside the AI legs, fail-open) and the admin route returns `meta.campusParcel` (parcel address, land use, buildings grouped by type and size); the panel shows it and the address flag names that parcel instead of asking for a house-number fix. Display only: no size or price field reads it.

Two-treatment package visit 2 (owner rulings 2026-10-04): `GATE_PACKAGE_FOLLOWUP_AUTOBOOK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `packageFollowupAutobookLive()`. On: booking visit 1 of a catalog `cockroach_control`, `flea_tick` or `bed_bug_treatment` job (admin Schedule create, estimate acceptance incl. one-tap, Leads schedule-appointment, and a self-book row that carries a catalog `service_id`) also inserts visit 2 in the same transaction via `services/package-followup-booking.js` — scheduled the catalog row's `follow_up_interval_days` (14) after visit 1 with no weekend roll, same technician/window/address, status `confirmed` (customer_confirmed false; nobody has to confirm it), `estimated_price` 0 + `followup_included`, `parent_service_id` + `followup_source_service_id` = visit 1, `source_action` `package_followup_auto`. The catalog row is read from `service_id`, else `service_key_snapshot`; a label is never read. **Not covered:** the two customer self-serve writers that store only a label — the public `/book` funnel (its row is the funnel label, e.g. `Pest Control`) and `availability.confirmBooking` (the customer assistant's `book_appointment`, the estimate's `service_interest`) — book no visit 2 until they carry the accepted estimate's catalog identity; the closeout card is the path for those. The call pipeline plans the same visit 2 for these rows without the caller having to mention it and writes it in the same confirmed shape (it keeps the call's linkage and number hold; a date agreed on the call still wins, and visit 2 is always at visit 1's time — owner ruling 2026-10-04, "same time"). A voice-agent or outbound-callback booking is a pending office-review request and gets no automatic visit 2 in this change (booking it at office activation is a follow-up change); the closeout card covers it. A slot clash still books and rings a Schedule needs-you card after commit. Moving visit 1 to another DATE (Schedule page, rebooker) shifts visit 2 by the same number of days while the customer has not confirmed it and it has no reschedule of its own (no `reschedule_log` row); visit 2 keeps its own time of day, so a time-only change of visit 1 does not move it (the shared shift hook is date-only for every linked follow-up). Cancelling visit 1 always cancels a live visit 2, and so does marking visit 1 skipped or no-show (call-booking-catalog shift/cancel hooks, `job-status.js`). The Intelligence Bar does not book visit 2 (its confirm card shows one visit), and its cancel, reschedule and batch-move cards refuse a visit with a live package visit 2; those move or cancel from the Schedule screen or Dispatch. No confirmation text for visit 2; the reminder self-heal sweep arms 72h/24h reminders; the customer sees it and can reschedule it. Off: byte-identical to before — visit 2 is booked from the closeout card or a call that discussed it. Kill = unset; already-booked children stay on the schedule.

Visit not closed out (Action Queue worklist, dark): `GATE_NOT_CLOSED_OUT_QUEUE` — **off in prod unless exactly `true`**, read at process start through `isEnabled('notClosedOutQueue')`. The 6 PM missed-appointment check logs `reschedule_log` `customer_noshow` for every visit still open at that hour; production (60 days to 2026-10-03) showed all 74 such rows came from the check, 64% later cancelled and 27% later completed, so the row means "not closed out", not "we missed it" (owner rulings 2026-10-03, scope `~/sms-missed-visit-link-scope-20261003.md`). On, each flagged visit also raises ONE Action Queue card (`dispatch_alerts` type `visit_not_closed_out`, one open card per visit by partial unique index; `server/services/not-closed-out.js`) where a person decides: Open job to rebook or close it out, "This was a miss" (`POST /api/admin/dispatch/not-closed-out/:logId/confirm-miss`: stamps `miss_confirmed_at`, the row stays open, the card is replaced by a confirmed one), or "Not a miss" (`…/dismiss`: resolution `dismissed`). Independent of the gate, the decision is recorded on the log row (`resolved_at` / `resolution` / `resolved_by`, migration `20261003120000_reschedule_log_resolution`, which also marks every existing row `backlog` so the list starts empty): a rebooker move settles it `rebooked`, a status change to completed settles it `completed`, to cancelled or skipped `dismissed` (`job-status.js`, `rebooker.js`; savepoint-confined, never blocks the move or the transition); a person-marked dispatch no-show is a confirmed miss from the start and stays open until rebooked. One customer-facing reader: the texting AI's MISSED VISIT fact (`visit-loops-facts.js` `loadMissedVisit`, under `GATE_SMS_REAL_ANSWERS`) lists a visit only when a person pressed "This was a miss" on the card and nothing has settled the row (`miss_confirmed_at` set, `resolved_at` NULL), never for a dispatch "No-show" (the customer's absence). With this gate off no card exists, so no row qualifies. The worklist itself sends no customer contact. Off = the check logs as before and raises no card. A confirmed miss is settled by **Done** on the card (`handled`): a `no_show` visit is terminal, so its rebooking is a new appointment. With the gate on, the repeated-miss outreach task (2 in 90 days) counts person-marked misses only and is evaluated when a person confirms, not by the nightly check; the nightly check also repairs every open flagged row (`reconcileOpenRows`): a row whose visit already closed or moved is settled from the visit (gate on or off), and a row with no card gets one (gate on). "Not a miss" after "This was a miss" settles the row as `not_a_miss` (its own value: it never counts toward the outreach, gate on or off), recounts the customer's misses and cancels a pending outreach task that no longer has its two. Every outreach count-and-write runs in one transaction under a per-customer advisory lock, and the nightly check repairs a failed raise or withdrawal (`reconcileOutreach`). With the gate on the nightly repair also retries five cases where one write failed once (owner ruling 2026-10-03, the known limits of #5769; all are skipped with the gate off, which keeps the old behavior): (1) `reconcileOutreach` withdraws a pending outreach task whose customer lost its second miss over the last 90 days (the count window) instead of 7; (2) it also evaluates a customer with a no-show Quick Move (`reschedule_log` `new_date` set) in the last 7 days, once per customer and never beside a task already in those days; (3) `settlementFromVisit` settles a moved visit as rebooked also when it has since reached `en_route`, `on_site` or `no_show` (a person-confirmed row on a `no_show` visit still waits for **Done**); (4) it cancels a pending outreach task raised before the queue (no `metadata.source`, subject `Recommended outreach: N missed appointments in 90 days`) when the customer has fewer than 2 person-marked misses; (5) `reopenUnconfirmedNoShows` reopens a row settled as `not_a_miss` or `backlog` and never confirmed when a person marked the visit `no_show` in the last 14 days AFTER the row was settled and the visit is still that no-show (a later "Not a miss" stands), checked again under the visit and row locks; the replacement card counts in the repair's `raised`.

Fast Complete voice fill: `GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_VOICE_FILL` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`fastCompleteVoiceFillLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy needed for the routes, and the schedule row's `fastCompleteVoiceFillEnabled` takes the sheet's part away on the next schedule load). On, the Fast Complete sheet fills product rows from what the technician said, always through our own transcriber (`gpt-transcribe`, override `OPENAI_VOICE_FILL_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`) primed with the sheet's product names, and every filled row is a suggestion the technician confirms before Complete. Three surfaces: (1) the report flow (`GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_REPORT`): every untyped pest visit (a regular visit or a re-service) and every specialty visit that sheet reads a record for (a lane under `GATE_LANE_VOICE_FILL`, a typed form under `GATE_TYPED_VOICE_FILL`; on those each row takes the way said for it, and a sheet that opens with no product reads the note for products before it writes the report): the note's mic sends its clip to `POST /api/admin/dispatch/:serviceId/fast-complete/voice-fill/dictation` and the words land in the note box; when the report is written, `POST .../fast-complete/voice-fill/products` reads the products the note names (amount, unit, a non-spray way, the words each stood on) and the sheet lands them as rows to confirm, with Checks for what it could not settle; both hold Complete & send. (2) the lawn re-service sheet (with `GATE_LAWN_RESERVICE_FAST_COMPLETE` also on): the same note mic, and a "Fill products from my note" button that sends the note to the same `.../voice-fill/products` route, read against the lawn sheet's own catalog and ways; a suggestion tile is turned on, a product added, an amount or a way set, each to confirm. (3) the older pest re-service sheet (shown only where the report flow is off): `POST .../fast-complete/voice-fill/clip` fills products, visit taps and both notes from one clip. Nothing is stored by any of the three routes; audit lines carry sizes and counts only. Off = each route answers 404 `{enabled:false}` and the sheet is as it was. Code: `server/services/fast-complete-voice-fill.js`, `client/src/components/tech/FastCompleteVoiceFill.jsx`.

Fast Complete for an already-invoiced visit: `GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_INVOICED_VISITS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`fastCompleteInvoicedVisitsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy needed; the schedule row's `invoicedVisitFastCompleteEnabled` carries it to admin Dispatch on the next schedule load). On, admin Dispatch opens a visit that is already invoiced or returning from the payment flow (its row carries `completionInvoiceAlreadySent`, `checkoutInvoiceId` or `checkoutInvoiceToken`) in its Fast Complete sheet instead of the full form: pest, specialty (lane and typed), lawn, lawn re-service and tree & shrub. Before, every sheet rule refused such a visit because no sheet sent the invoice field the full form sends. Now each sheet builds its `/complete` body with the same helper as the full form (`client/src/lib/completion-invoice-fields.js`): a visit with `completionInvoiceAlreadySent` posts `invoiceAlreadySent: true`, so the server sends no second pay-link text, opens no second in-person payment prompt, holds the review ask while the invoice is unpaid and records the completion as invoice-handled. A visit with only the door-charge markers posts no invoice field, exactly as the full form does: the server finds that invoice by the visit and reuses it, and a paid invoice stays paid. The sheets post to the same `POST /api/admin/dispatch/:serviceId/complete` as the full form, so no new server path exists and no new billing rule. Off: routing and request bodies are as before. The day and week row builders in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js` both carry the flag. Rollback: unset the variable.

Same name, different phone and address: `GATE_DUPLICATES_SAME_NAME` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at request time (`duplicatesSameNameLive()`, `server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, `GET /api/admin/customer-duplicates` also returns `sameNameGroups` and the admin Duplicates page shows a third section: live customers whose normalized first AND last name are equal (both at least two letters; placeholder names like Unknown and N/A never match) that the shared-phone list and the same-address list do not already show, are not profiles of one account (`account_id`) and are not a dismissed pair. Different or missing phone and address are the point; each card shows both phones and both addresses. Review-only: `findSameNameGroups` is not read by the auto-merge cron and `executeMerge` refuses mode `auto` for the kind. `POST /merge` and `POST /link-as-property` accept `kind: 'same_name'` (merge keeps the kept customer's address; link-as-property also saves the other address as a second property); an address difference is not a refusal for this kind, but the executor's own refusals (two Stripe profiles, two third-party payers, billing-mode conflicts, a red pair) still apply. The merged-away record's phone follows the same-address carry rule: it lands in the kept customer's first free service-contact slot, held from automated texts until it consents. Nothing is sent to a customer. Off = the API, the page and every refusal are byte-identical to before (a `kind: 'same_name'` request takes the shared-phone path and refuses `not_in_queue`). Rollback: unset the gate; a merge already done is undone from Recent merges as usual.

Capacity mode: `GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` — **off in production since 2026-10-05**, read at call time through `capacityEnabled()` (`server/services/scheduling/policy.js`). On, booking checks the whole route (08:00 to 18:00) instead of a fixed hour grid. **What it plans (owner 2026-10-30): 35 minutes for a recurring pest or recurring lawn visit, on every booking path and for the visit being placed too** (`server/services/scheduling/planning-minutes.js`: one-time pest 45, re-service 15, assessment 30, rodent and termite 30; combined pest + lawn rows and unnamed services keep the window/estimate rule). A stored estimate above 60 minutes is real work and never plans shorter, and neither does a placed visit whose allowance is above 60 (add-on minutes, dead-rodent attic 90, pest + termite 120). **A written row always keeps the one-hour promise** (owner 2026-09-25: "a one-hour arrival window is a promise about when the truck arrives, not how long the work takes"): the office form default end is 60 in both modes, and the catalog policy `services.scheduling_duration_policy` with `source: 'owner_2026_09_09'` (the 30-minute routine allowance that wrote 30-minute rows before the 2026-10-05 switch-off) is ignored by `service-library.js` — the column and its data stay, and a version-1 policy from another source still applies. With the gate off the route rows are unchanged, including the night auto-dispatch arrival search (`planningMinutes: false`, no placed-visit table). A `reservation_policy_version` 2 hold keeps the capacity rules it was offered under after a rollback.
Staff route insertion (dark): `GATE_STAFF_ROUTE_INSERTION` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/arrival-route.js` (`staffRouteInsertionLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-25 ("go", then "save order"). Applies with capacity mode OFF only (`GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` keeps its own insertion and commit). On, a staff arrival check of a MOVED visit (another day, technician or start than its saved row; `staffPlacement`, from the context's `placedAt`) tries it at every place in the technician's stored order instead of after the last numbered stop (a moved visit has no `route_order`, so `currentOrder` used to put it last on every hour). A stale stored order (a gap, a duplicate, a null, or a later window numbered ahead) also tries the promised-window order, the 2026-09-25 capacity rule. That fallback also covers a visit checked where it is saved (owner 2026-10-26, "fix both"; live test: a leftover number made the visit's own 5 PM drop out of the times box while 4 PM and 6 PM fit): its own hour reads like every other hour; it keeps its place in each order, and nothing is written for it. The gap tool's hand-built context (no saved place) keeps the saved order. A route number the office typed into the edit (a pending `route_order` other than the stored one) is checked where it puts the visit, and a whole shared stop keeps today's rule. An in-between place counts only when every later stop still arrives `INSERTION_MARGIN_MINUTES` (15) before its window closes (the drive model is off by about 4 min a leg); a day whose only fits are tighter answers `arrival_margin`. The times box (`findArrivalWindowSlots`), the picked-hour verdict, the save probes (`checkArrivalPlacement`: Save-anyway warnings, the Rain Out / Quick Move options, tech-out auto-move) all use the same rule. The staff SAVE then numbers that technician's day in the certified order (`placeMovedVisit`, audit `schedule.route_order_placed`): Edit appointment (`update-details`, a date, start or technician change the office did not number itself), the rebooker single moves and every occurrence a series move shifts, for staff callers (`adminWindowRules` + `overlapAdvisory`), and Quick Move and tech-out auto-move (`placeInRoute`, since their options come from the same check). It plans from the office like every commit-time check (the save probes do), runs in the save transaction under a savepoint and never fails the save; an uncertifiable day keeps today's behavior. Never changes a customer's time or sends a message; the board, the tech app and the tracking page's stops-ahead follow the new numbers. Customer booking, the Intelligence Bar time search, the gap tool and auto-dispatch do not use this check and do not change; New Appointment's open-times box uses it only under `GATE_NEW_APPT_ROUTE_TIMES` (a new stop tries every place), and its save writes the order only under `GATE_NEW_APPT_STOP_ORDER`; a phone agent booking writes it only under `GATE_CALL_BOOKING_STOP_ORDER`. Off: byte-identical.

Combo route check (dark): `GATE_COMBO_ROUTE_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/arrival-route.js` (`comboRouteCheckLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). A visit shared by two or more services (lawn + pest at one stop) answers `route_unverified` on every arrival check, because certifying one half alone would under-count the work at the stop. On, a caller that moves the WHOLE visit passes `unit: true` to `loadArrivalRouteContext`: the visit's live members leave the day's rows and ride the target as ONE stop whose work is the members' summed `workDuration` (the sum `groupRouteStops` already uses for every other stop; exempt from owner planning minutes like any target), with `memberIds` on the target. Members that are not one clean stop (a different technician, different or missing coordinates, another day, a member en route / on site, or members promised different arrival times) keep `grouped` and today's `route_unverified`. The staff availability box passes it: the hint route marks its existing-visit request (`arrivalWindow.unit` in `admin-schedule-find-time.js`), `find-time.js` forwards that mark on both the capacity and the non-capacity path, and the picked-hour verdict in `find-time-hints.js` asks for it directly, so with the gate on the box shows real hours for a combo instead of "Can't check the route" on the screens that opt into arrival-window routing: Edit appointment, the manual reschedule and the reschedule confirm. The Rain-out picker does not opt into arrival-window routing (before or after this gate), so it is unchanged. Edit appointment sends its Together / Separate choice with the request (`moveScope`): `separate` is checked as that one service alone (`alone: true`, the same gate), since the save splits it off first; that applies to a two-service visit only (with three or more, the remainder is still a shared stop and the answer stays unverified). Read-only and advisory: no save is blocked or changed. The whole-stop SAVES (rebooker capacity check, rain-out, tech-out auto-move, the update-details save probe) do not pass it yet, so a combo move still saves with "Could not verify arrival windows"; that is the next PR. Customer `/book`, estimate pickers and auto-dispatch never pass it. Off, or a caller without `unit`: byte-identical. Scope: owner 2026-10-03, combo visits (`visit-groups.moveVisitAsUnit`).

Best-times road times (dark): `GATE_BEST_TIMES_ROAD_TIMES` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/hint-road-times.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). The admin availability strip's best-times chips (`summary.best`: 4 hours on the picked date, 4 date + hours in the 7 days from today) and the picked hour's verdict get their drive-in and added-drive numbers from Google's traffic-aware route matrix (`computeRouteMatrix`) instead of the straight-line model. Only the shown chips are priced (3 legs each), on the picker's own allowance (`hintTravelBudget` in `route-optimizer.js`: 600 legs per 15 min, never customer booking's; staff only, a technician's chips keep the model, and every chip lookup is counted against the pickers' durable `PICKER_ROAD_*_CAP_CENTS` ceilings, see `GATE_PICKER_ROAD_CHECK`), with a 6-hour process cache per pin pair, date and departure minute and a 2.5 s deadline. Which hours fit is still the model's answer. Under `GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` the chips show the capacity simulation's model numbers as estimates ("~"); only gap-mode chips are re-priced. A chip whose legs do not all come back from Google keeps the model numbers (`drive_source: estimate`). Google bills per leg.

Open-times box (dark): `GATE_OPEN_TIMES_BOX` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/routes/admin-schedule-find-time.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy; needs `GATE_BEST_TIME_HINTS`; `GATE_BOARD_OPEN_TIMES` also allows the same search for the Dispatch grid). Owner 2026-10-25 (layout A, "all staff" + "start"): the staff time picker on New Appointment, Edit appointment, the Reschedule dialog, the drag-and-drop confirm and admin Quick Move draws the open-times box instead of the availability strip. The box lists only open times: 15 dates of the next four weeks, each the best hour of that date (least added drive, the sooner date on a tie) with the technician under the date and "adds N min" (over 30 min in amber), a Best / Soonest switch at the top, Morning (8-11) / Afternoon (12-3) / Evening (4-7) filters, and a new Date field value shows that day's open times with "All dates" to go back. No verdict sentence: Edit's Save never reads "anyway", and the route warning of the slot check is dropped (the double-booking notice stays). Edit and New Appointment rank every technician's route (a row books its technician; a Tech list shows once two technicians have open times); the other three screens keep the visit's own route. The pickers ask `GET /api/admin/schedule/find-time/ui` once per 10 minutes (`{ openTimes }`), then send one `summary` search with `openTimes: true` from today for 28 days (`OPEN_TIMES_MAX_DAYS`; the strip's cap stays 14), plus that one day when the picked date is later. With the gate on, that search answers `summary.open_times` (`{ from, to }`) and per-technician hours, scores no picked hour, builds no best-times rows (no road pricing: "~" model numbers) and, for a booking `GATE_BOOKING_RAIN_RANK` reads, gives each hour its `rain_tier` so Best puts an outdoor job's wet hours last. Slow log: `[find-time] open times search slow` past 3 s. Off: the request is answered as the strip's summary and the pickers draw the strip as before.

Board open times (dark): `GATE_BOARD_OPEN_TIMES` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at boot into `boardOpenTimes` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` and carried to Dispatch as `boardOpenTimes` on the admin schedule day view (`GET /api/admin/schedule`); the find-time route also reads it at call time to allow the open-times search (needs `GATE_BEST_TIME_HINTS`). Owner 2026-10-26 ("start step 4"): while a visit is dragged on the Dispatch day grid or the 5-day / week grid, the hours that fit it light up — each with "adds N min" (what it adds to the day's driving, "~" = the straight-line estimate), amber (`warn` tokens) over 30 min, and the best one tagged "Best" (least added drive; an outdoor job's wet hours last, the box's rain tiers). The day grid searches that day on every technician's route (a drop can change the technician) and the lit hours replace the grey Open blocks while they show; the week grid searches the shown days on the visit's own route (a drop keeps it), and an unassigned visit lights nothing. One `summary` + `openTimes` find-time search per drag (`client/src/components/schedule/BoardOpenTimes.jsx`), the visit's service sent so an unqualified technician is left out. Display only: the drop and its confirm save exactly as before. Off: a drag asks nothing and lights nothing.

New Appointment route times (dark): `GATE_NEW_APPT_ROUTE_TIMES` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/routes/admin-schedule-find-time.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-26 ("fix both", after the live test: New Appointment's open-times box used the older gap check, which offers no start after 4 PM and called Oct 26, 27, 30 and 31 full for a test customer the Edit box placed at 8 AM). Needs `GATE_BEST_TIME_HINTS`, `GATE_OPEN_TIMES_BOX` and `GATE_ADMIN_ARRIVAL_WINDOWS`. On, a summary search with `openTimes` and `arrivalWindows: true` but no `serviceId` (New Appointment; the client always sends the flag) runs `findArrivalWindowSlots` on a prospective stop at the searched address (`loadArrivalRouteContext({ prospective: { lat, lng, estimated_duration_minutes } })`, the shape the capacity path already uses for customer booking): the same arrival-window route check as Edit appointment and the board, with `GATE_STAFF_ROUTE_INSERTION`'s every-place rule for a new stop. The strip (box gate off) and every other caller keep the gap check. Suggestions only: the New Appointment save is unchanged (it never blocks on an overlap; it books with an advisory warning) and writes a stop order only under `GATE_NEW_APPT_STOP_ORDER`. Off: byte-identical.

Picker road check (dark): `GATE_PICKER_ROAD_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `pickerRoadCheckLive` (`server/services/scheduling/arrival-route.js`), which the find-time route (`server/routes/admin-schedule-find-time.js`) and `checkArrivalPlacement` both call (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-26 ("we need to run Google inside the scheduling check itself"; "Next 7 days"; "His current stop") and 2026-10-27 ("the dispatcher needs to run every time we create, reschedule, etc, we just have to make sure costs are appropriate"). Needs `GATE_BEST_TIME_HINTS` and `GATE_ADMIN_ARRIVAL_WINDOWS`; stays off under `GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` (the pickers then list the capacity engine's hours, which this check does not drive; `pickerRoadCheckLive` in `arrival-route.js`). On, three changes to the staff pickers' route check (`findArrivalWindowSlots` in `server/services/scheduling/find-time.js`): (1) admin Quick Move (`RainOutSheet`, `quickMove: true` on the find-time request) uses the route check Edit appointment uses instead of the older gap check (no start after 4 PM, straight-line drive); (2) that check, for Quick Move, Edit, Reschedule, the drag-and-drop confirm, the Dispatch grid's lit hours (`GATE_BOARD_OPEN_TIMES`, the days on screen) and New Appointment (with `GATE_NEW_APPT_ROUTE_TIMES`), drives the road days on Google inside the fit check itself (`createPickerTravel` in `hint-road-times.js`): today and tomorrow (`PICKER_ROAD_TRAFFIC_DAYS`, default 2) traffic-aware at three departure times a day (09:00 for a leg leaving before 11:00, 12:00 before 14:00, 16:00 after; today never before the next whole hour; Google Route Matrix "Pro", $10 per 1,000 lookups); the next days (`PICKER_ROAD_PLAIN_DAYS`, default 5) road times without traffic (`TRAFFIC_UNAWARE`, "Essentials", $5 per 1,000), one lookup per pair of places whatever the hour (24-hour process cache); later days the model, with the "~". Measured 10-27 on real routes (replay, one technician): about 31 traffic-aware + 50–90 plain lookups, ~61 cents, for a new search (the first cut, every hour for seven days plus a re-check of later days' best hour, was ~500 lookups, ~$5). Spend is bounded per process (its own `pickerTravelBudget` in `route-optimizer.js`, 600 requests / 1,500 lookups per 15 min, apart from the chips'), per request (one budget for the list and the picked-hour verdict, and one for each batch of staff slot checks: 150 traffic-aware + 300 plain lookups, claimed before any purchase so concurrent checks neither oversubscribe it nor buy a shared leg twice; a picker that closes aborts its request: nothing more is reserved and no queued Google request is sent) and by durable ceilings shared by every process (`server/services/scheduling/picker-road-spend.js`, table `picker_road_spend`, one row per bucket and Eastern day, the account and each staff user): `PICKER_ROAD_DAILY_CAP_CENTS` (default 1000 = $10 a day), `PICKER_ROAD_USER_DAILY_CAP_CENTS` (default 1000) and `PICKER_ROAD_MONTHLY_CAP_CENTS` (default 20000 = $200 a month), Google's list price before its monthly free usage; each lookup is reserved before it is asked (lookups the Google source then never sends, stopped by its burst allowance, its deadline or a closed picker, are given back), a crossed ceiling rolls the reservation back and the search uses the model ("~") until the next day (or month); no counter (a database error) also means the model (fails closed). Each purchase logs one `[picker-road]` line: lookups sent and how many Google answered (a sent lookup is paid even when an error or a timeout keeps the model); `[picker-road-spend]` logs each reservation against the day's ceiling and a refusal (paused). (3) Today's route under way (one stop en route or on site) continues from that stop, after its job (on site: arrival + job length; en route: departure + modelled drive + job length), instead of reading "could not check"; two stops under way still read unverified. The staff live checks that share `checkArrivalPlacement` (the edit/save probe, the staff slot check, the picked-hour verdict) follow the same rule, so a listed hour is not flagged the moment it is picked; the staff slot check (admin callers) and the staff picked-hour verdict also drive their one placement on the same road days and cache (`roads: true` + `roadSpender`, opt-in), while a technician's check and the edit save probe (inside its transaction, so no Google under a lock) stay on the model. Drive clock (dark): `GATE_DRIVE_CLOCK` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/drive-clock.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-28 ("add drive clock if its free"). Scheduling math under-counts real drive time. Measured from our own GPS only (`visit_gps_legs`, 100 visit-to-visit legs, Aug 27 - Oct 27 2026, Theil-Sen fits): GPS minutes = 4.11 + 1.70 x GPS road miles, so a Google road time (curb to curb) misses about 4 minutes of pulling out, parking and idling per drive; GPS minutes = 7.88 + 2.20 x straight-line miles, against the calibrated estimate of 4.25 + 2.35 (`GATE_DRIVE_TIME_CALIBRATION`; per leg, GPS minus estimate: median +1.9 min, p75 +7.6). Nothing is fitted or derived from Google answers (Google Maps terms). On: (1) estimate legs (`milesToDriveMinutes`, and the model fallback of `createSchedulingTravel`, both in `route-optimizer.js`) use `DRIVE_CLOCK_FIXED_MINUTES` (default 7.9, allowed 0-30) and `DRIVE_CLOCK_MINUTES_PER_MILE` (default 2.2, allowed 0.5-6) in place of the calibrated pair (only the calibrated branch; the legacy branch stays; same-place legs stay 0 and the fallback floor stays); (2) a leg whose minutes came from Google gets `DRIVE_CLOCK_PARK_MINUTES` (default 4, allowed 0-20) added when it is READ, once, in `createSchedulingTravel` lookups and in the pickers' lookups and cached reads in `hint-road-times.js` (the best-times chips, the route check, and the save check's cache-only read); no cache holds the added minutes, so turning the gate off restores Google's own numbers at once; a model, unverified or same-place leg never gets them; (3) the day-quality `drive_model` label reads `drive_clock`. A setting that is not a finite number inside its bounds uses the default. Does not change Google's own route ordering (`optimizeRoute`), GPS mileage or job cost, or any message; it moves the drive minutes that slot ranking, route fit checks, auto-dispatch, arrival windows and the day-quality numbers use, so more days read as full. Off: byte-identical. Rollback: unset `GATE_DRIVE_CLOCK`.

External job heartbeat watch (dark): `GATE_EXTERNAL_HEARTBEAT_WATCH` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/external-job-heartbeat-watch.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-28 ("the sweep writes a heartbeat, and the portal rings if no complete run lands by 07:00"). A job that runs outside the portal (first entry: `appt-sweep` on the office Mac) upserts ONE `job_health` row at the END of each run (never "running"): a complete run sets `last_status` `success`, `last_success_at`, `last_finished_at`, `last_duration_ms` and `consecutive_failures` 0; a failed or partial run sets `failed`, `last_error` and `consecutive_failures` + 1 and leaves `last_success_at` alone. On, an hourly cron (`external-heartbeat-watch`, `5 7-22 * * *` ET in `scheduler.js`) reads each registered job's row (registry `EXTERNAL_JOBS` in the service: job name, `dueBy` ET time, label, log location, admin link). "Complete today" = row exists, `last_status` `success`, and the ET date of `last_success_at` is today (ET). Complete: every open alert of that job is closed. Not complete and past `dueBy`: ONE admin bell (category `system`, title "FIX: ... did not finish today", link `/admin/schedule`), keyed per silence episode `external-heartbeat:<job>:<last_success_at ISO or never>` so a multi-day outage keeps one standing bell; older episode keys of the job are closed. Before `dueBy` with no complete run: nothing raised, nothing closed. Writes only admin notifications (no row locks, no customer data, no customer messages). Off: the cron is a no-op. Rollback: unset `GATE_EXTERNAL_HEARTBEAT_WATCH`.

New-caller booking by address (dark): `GATE_NEW_CALLER_BOOKING` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at boot into `newCallerBooking` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` and carried to the page as `newCallerBooking` on the admin schedule day view (`GET /api/admin/schedule`), which Dispatch hands to the New Appointment modal. A reminder or text failure after the link answers 200 with a warning; the link stands. The processor's booking branch then reuses the linked visit and sends nothing. A pass that leaves the visit unlinked (no customer on the call, or a refused link) rings `new-caller-visit:<id>` (category `schedule`, `bellDefault`, Area Schedule, the link opens the visit on Dispatch), which the link closes. After a link, one check bell `new-caller-visit-check:<id>` (same category and link) lists what to check: an address on the call that differs from the booked one (only for a customer this call created; spelling, suffix, directional and ZIP+4 forms, and a unit or ZIP only one side gives, are ignored; the visit keeps the booked address), a confirmed time in the extraction that differs from the booked one (the visit keeps the booked time), a held or unsent confirmation text, failed reminders, or a plan price the call agreed (D8 bell first, owner 2026-10-27, `server/services/booking/new-caller-plan-check.js`: the booked service, every agreed price as said (a price per visit and a yearly total only when those prices give one answer), the prepay choice, whether the WaveGuard setup fee was said, the call's own words and which of the six checks pass; a Waves Assessment first or a one-time job at a one-time price gets none; it sets no price and sends nothing, so the office sets the plan up by hand, as before; the row's `metadata.plan_check` feeds a two-month count of the calls that pass all six). A ten-minute sweep (`services/booking/new-caller-visit-bells.js`, scheduler job `new-caller-visit-bells` under `runExclusive`) rings the `new-caller-visit:<id>` row for what no pass reports: no call picked at Book, a recording not processed 90 minutes after the call, a finished pass that left the visit unlinked with no bell (a voicemail or spam verdict ends the pass before the link step), and once more within 24 hours of the visit's start unless the row last rang inside that day (the visit stays on the route; the office links it). The processor never books a second visit for a call the office booked by address (`findNewCallerVisitForCall` in `call-recording-processor.js`, not gated, linked or not): when the reuse lookup misses it (no customer yet, or linked to another customer), it holds the booking with the `ambiguous_existing_appointment` review card. Kill switch: unset (the button reads Schedule appointment and needs a customer, as before; the agent links nothing).

Booking rain rank (dark): `GATE_BOOKING_RAIN_RANK` — **ON in production since 2026-10-07 (owner); off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/find-time-hints.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-06. The New Appointment best-times rows (`summary.best`) rank by rain fit before drive, from the NWS hourly chance (Open-Meteo when NWS fails; the picker caps NWS at 1.2 s inside a 2.5 s wait so the backup can answer). Rules live in `server/services/scheduling/rain-fit.js`: an hour is wet when any hour from the visit start through 2 h after its end reads 60% or more, for the next 3 dates only. A service is classified by identity: New Appointment sends each selected row's catalog key (`serviceKeys`, parallel to `serviceTypes`), and the find-time route resolves key + name to the catalog key and findings type a visit would have (`service-completion-profiles.js`; at most 12 distinct services, read one at a time), and `rain-fit.js` checks the key against `RAIN_OK_KEYS`, the explicit rain-OK list (assessments, inspections, bed bug, German roach, the rodent bait-station check, rodent monitoring, trap follow-ups and checks, attic sanitation; pinned by a snapshot test, and none may be a spray lane in `service-report/trace-eligibility.js`). Billing riders and `general_appointment` are left out; every other catalog identity is outdoor, including trap setup, station installs, exclusion and `waveguard_initial_setup`. A name with no catalog identity takes the word rules in `rain-fit.js` (assessment, estimate, inspection, WDO, interior, bed bug, German cockroach, rodent/trap checks; exterior, exclusion, mesh, sealing, remediation, treatment, liquid, spot, application, spray, fumigation, foam and the "Accepted estimate" placeholder are outdoor). A booking is rain-OK only when every service in it is: rain moves only what the forecast knows: an outdoor booking sorts a wet hour last and an hour inside the 3 days that the forecast cannot read just before it; a rain-OK booking sorts a wet hour first; a dry hour and any date past the 3 days compete on drive alone. A booking with more than 12 distinct services is outdoor. Which hours fit is unchanged. Off: drive-only order, and the forecast is read alongside the road prices as before.

Truck check (dark): `GATE_TRUCK_KIT` — **ships DARK: off unless set to `true`**, read at call time by `truckKitLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`) in `server/services/truck-kit.js` and `server/routes/tech-truck-check.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). A check writes one `equipment_checks` row (idempotent per page key, `client_key` from `20261023000040`); a missing or damaged item opens a `maintenance_alerts` row (`tool_missing` / `tool_damaged`, shown on Equipment → Maintenance with Found / Lost or Repaired / Retired, admin only, an outcome is required to resolve one, and Lost and Retired also set the item's status; the resolve takes the truck's advisory lock so it never interleaves with a running check, and a stale resolve of an alert a check already closed answers 409; an item with an open tool alert cannot move to another truck or leave its truck until the office resolves it, and handing a truck to another technician takes the same lock, so a check in flight on it writes nothing) and the check rings one office bell per truck (category `truck_kit`, area Inventory, link to that tab; rings by default through `bellDefault` and the owner can silence the category in Settings) that closes itself once every tool alert on the truck is resolved; an item marked present on a later check closes its own alert. Kit keys (PR 2): a row's `equipment.kit_key` names what the tool is (`moisture_meter`); checklist items carrying the same key (seeded by `20261023000020_equipment_kit_key.js`, the termite flashlight-and-probe item split into `flashlight` + `probe` by `20261023000030_termite_probe_kit_key.js`, editable in the checklist JSON) are that service line's required tools; a combined job ("Quarterly Pest + Termite Bait Station") requires every line its name mentions (`serviceLinesFor`), so with the gate on the Schedule readiness strip adds a `Truck lacks …` hold for a visit whose assigned technician's truck has keyed rows but not the key, and the technician's Today page says `Not on your truck: …` on that stop (`gaps` on the same `GET`); a truck with no keyed row is never judged. The Assets dialog shows the Kit key field only when `GET /api/admin/equipment/kit-keys` answers `enabled: true`. Off: `GET` and `POST /api/tech/truck-check` and `GET /api/admin/equipment/kit-keys` answer 404 `{ enabled: false }`, the readiness poll reads nothing from the kit, nothing renders, nothing is written. Technician reach: the `own-truck` bucket in `server/middleware/technician-scope.js` (the truck is resolved from the login, never the body). PR 3 (same gate): (1) **receipt link**: when the receipt inventory agent classes a purchase line as equipment (`agent_equipment`), its bell names the ONE open tool alert whose item name the line's title contains (`matchReceiptToOpenAlert`, catalog-name words only, no model) and links to that row's Assets dialog, else to a new-row dialog with the name filled in (`?tab=assets&new=1&name=…&receipt_line=<line id>`); the save carries `receipt_line_id` and files the line under the row (`purchase_receipt_lines.equipment_id`, migration `20261023180000`), claimed under `FOR UPDATE` before the write (a line that is gone, not an equipment line, or already filed under another row answers 409 and writes nothing); off, the agent rings its plain bell and `receipt_line_id` is refused 400; (2) **Intelligence Bar reads**, no write tool: admin `get_truck_kit` (one truck by technician name, or the fleet overview) and `get_tool_issues` (every open tool alert) on the procurement / inventory contexts (`/admin/equipment` now reads as procurement) and tech `get_my_truck_kit` (the login's own truck); every one answers `integration_disabled` with the gate off. Sends no customer communication and never changes an item's status by itself.

Equipment tax de minimis (scope decision 7, owner and accountant; not a gate): `EQUIPMENT_TAX_DE_MINIMIS_USD` — default **0** (unset, 0, negative or not a number = every priced row is judged, the behavior before the variable existed), read at call time (`taxDeMinimisUsd()` in `server/services/equipment-reconciliation.js`). An active `equipment` row with a `purchase_price` at or under the threshold and no tax-register link raises no `equipment_missing_tax_link` finding on `GET /api/admin/equipment-systems/reconciliation` and is not counted in `summary.equipment_without_tax_link`; the summary carries `tax_de_minimis_usd` and `equipment_below_tax_de_minimis` instead. Ads capacity by work day (dark): `GATE_ADS_CAPACITY_WORK_DAYS` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `adsCapacityWorkDaysLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill). Ads gap-fill rule (dark): `GATE_ADS_GAP_RULE` — **ships DARK**, `shadow` | `true`, read at call time via `adsGapRuleMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset, `false` or anything else = off, byte-identical to today). The 2-hour budget job (`BudgetManager.adjustBudgets`) stops checking one day and counts the technician's open stops over the next 7 ET days starting tomorrow: per day, the limit is technicians × the weekday, Saturday or Sunday limit (defaults 9 / 8 / 6, kept in `ad_targets.metadata.gap_rule`), minus the distinct customers already booked. Open stops at or above `run_at_open` (6) put the Google campaign at its base budget; below `stop_below_open` (3) put it at the 1% floor; in between it keeps its state. `shadow` leaves the old rule in charge and writes what the new rule would do to `system_settings` key `ads.gap_rule.last` (history in `ads.gap_rule.history`, last 120). `true` makes the new rule decide for every active Google Ads campaign, with every existing push, persist and rollback safety kept. The owner can hold a campaign at base or stop until a chosen date (`ad_campaigns.metadata.budget_hold`, `POST/DELETE /api/admin/ads/campaigns/:id/hold`); the job honors a hold in shadow and live only. Routes `GET /api/admin/ads/gap-rule`, `PUT /api/admin/ads/gap-rule/settings` answer 404 `gap_rule_off` while off. Changes ad budgets only; sends nothing to a customer. Rollback: unset `GATE_ADS_GAP_RULE`.

Technician "Can move visits" switch (dark): `GATE_TECH_MOVE_SWITCH` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/tech-move-permission.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy needed beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-25, the way ServiceTitan gates technician rescheduling. Each staff row has `technicians.can_move_visits` (migration `20261025163000`: every row on file when it ran was set true, so today's staff keep moving visits; a row added later starts false). The Team tab edits it ("Can move visits", PUT/POST `/api/admin/timetracking/technicians` `canMoveVisits`). On, a non-admin whose switch is off gets 403 `{ error: 'Ask the office to move this visit.', code: 'move_not_allowed' }` from every route that moves a visit or lists its moves: `GET/POST /api/tech/services/:id/rain-out(-options)` (tech app Quick Move) and `GET/POST /api/admin/dispatch/:serviceId/rain-out(-options)` and `GET .../reschedule-options` + `POST .../reschedule` (Dispatch Quick Move and Reschedule). A technician with no row is refused too (fail closed). Admins are never refused. Stop reordering (`/reorder`) is not a move and is unchanged. Nothing is sent to a customer. Technician login privacy (dark): `GATE_TECH_LOGIN_PRIVACY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `techLoginPrivacyLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-25, before the second technician starts: a login with the technician role sees only its own customers' alerts and promises, by the same rule the Communications routes use (`technicianServicesCustomer` / `technicianCustomerIdsSubquery` in `server/services/technician-visit-scope.js`: an assigned visit that is not dead and sits inside the 7-day window). On: (1) **Alerts.** A customer-scoped tech-visible alert (SMS reply, reschedule intent, voicemail callback, service report and completion text failures, Twilio failure, job complete, follow-up bells) is pushed to a technician (`triggerNotification` in `server/services/notification-triggers.js`) and listed, counted and marked read or done on the non-admin bell (`scopeAdminFeedToRole` in `server/services/notification-service.js`, fed by `GET /api/admin/notifications` and the unread count) only when its customer is on that technician's route. The customer is read from the event payload (`customerId`, `customer_id`, or `threadId` for an SMS reply) or the row metadata. An alert with no customer keeps today's routing. A failed scope lookup drops the technician (fail closed). (2) **Promises.** For a technician `GET /api/admin/call-recordings/proposals`, `/commitments/open`, `/commitments/auto-closed` and `/commitments/sms` list only own-customer rows (a promise on a call with no customer is hidden), and `PATCH /commitments/:id`, `POST /calls/:id/commitments` and `POST /proposals/:id/(preview|apply|dismiss)` answer 404, writing nothing, for a promise, call or proposal outside that set. `GATE_TECH_MOVE_SWITCH` still governs apply. (3) **Account-deleted push.** The "Customer deleted their account" push (`server/routes/auth.js`) goes to admin-role devices only (`sendToAdmins(..., { adminOnly: true })` in `server/services/push-notifications.js`). Admin logins and office staff see everything as before. Sends nothing to a customer. Off: byte-identical to before.
Technician work days (dark): `GATE_TECH_WORK_DAYS` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `techWorkDaysLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Waves AI tools are office paths and do not block. Day length is out of scope. Sends nothing to a customer. Off: `work_days` is ignored everywhere, no editor, no extra read, responses byte-identical. Technician job type from the catalog (dark): `GATE_TECH_JOB_TYPE_CHECKS` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `techJobTypeChecksLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change).
