The capability checks (find-time and estimate slot offers, `pick-technician`, tech-out auto-move, auto-dispatch candidates and apply, the save-time fences in `technician-capabilities.js`, the Team tab list of future visits a turned-off category affects) used to read a visit's job type from its NAME (`auto-dispatch/service-category.js` regex, no match = general pest), so "Palm Tree Nutritional Treatment", "Semiannual Palm", "Palm Fert" and "Top Dress" read as general pest and a technician set to Off for Lawn could still get them. On: `categoriesForServices` (`technician-capabilities.js`) resolves the category from the service library first (the visit's `service_id`, else its service key or `service_key_snapshot`, to `services.category`), mapped onto the five capability categories by the table the service-line map uses (`CATALOG_CATEGORY_LINES` in `service-category.js`: pest_control = general, mosquito, lawn_care and tree_shrub = lawn, rodent, termite and wdo = termite; inspection, specialty, other and unknown name no category), and falls back to the name regex only when the catalog names none or cannot be read. Callers pass `service_id` / `service_key` where they hold them (visit rows, arrival-route member services, the call booking catalog row, the new job's `serviceKey` in find-time); a name-only caller (the estimate service mix, slot-reservation) still classifies by name. A `review_required` category still counts as allowed (owner 2026-09-05: every hire may treat every service); only Off removes a technician. Also on: office saves add one plain line such as "Tech One is set to Off for Lawn, tree & shrub work." (`capabilityOffWarningsFor` in `technician-eligibility.js`, same `warnings` list and never a block) when the chosen technician is Off for the visit's category: schedule create and edit (technician changed), board assign and drag and Dispatch assign (`dispatch-assignment.js`), lead booking, and Dispatch New Appointment. Rebooker admin moves, the follow-up override, the Intelligence Bar assign tools and tech-out redistribute add no such line yet. Setting a hire's Lawn and Termite to Off at hire setup stays data, not code. Sends nothing to a customer. Off: name-only classification and no extra warning or read, byte-identical. Rollback: unset `GATE_TECH_JOB_TYPE_CHECKS`.

Second technician census lows (dark): `GATE_SECOND_TECH_LOWS` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `secondTechLowsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-25, second technician census lows L1 and L3; both are admin-only and send nothing to a customer. (L1) The admin dashboard tech utilization tile (`computeCoreKpis` in `server/routes/admin-dashboard.js`) used to divide billable hours by `active technicians x 8 x every calendar day`, which counted office staff (active but not field-dispatchable) and a technician's days off, so utilization read low. On: only assignable field staff count (`applyAssignable`: active and `field_dispatchable`), and each counts only the days of the labor-hours window (the period start through its end date, each date once; the old count rounded the period up a day and always ran to today) that are in their `work_days` (`normalizeWorkDays`; no list = every day), at 8 hours a work day. A failed read still gives a null count and a logged error. (L3) Four Intelligence Bar schedule-tool sites (`optimize_tech_route`, `assign_technician`, `swap_tech_assignments` for both names, and the `find_available_slots` technician filter, in `intelligence-bar/schedule-tools.js`) picked a technician with an unordered `whereILike('name', '%x%').first()`: no assignable filter and no ambiguity check, so two matching rows (or an office row) could bind the wrong person and the confirm card named them. On: each uses `resolveTechnicianByName` (`intelligence-bar/tools.js`): assignable technicians only; no match keeps the tool's existing "not found" error; a name that fits two technicians returns the tool error `Multiple technicians match that name...` with the candidates and writes nothing. Off: the old first() match and the old dashboard count, byte-identical. Rollback: unset `GATE_SECOND_TECH_LOWS`.

Admin alert retention (owner 2026-10-26, "ok go"; `server/services/admin-alert-retention.js`): `GATE_ALERT_RETENTION` — **ships DARK, three states, read at call time via `alertRetentionMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`**: unset or any other value = off, no query; `shadow` (trimmed, any case) = judge and record, change nothing; `true` = expire. A nightly 1:32 AM ET job (`admin-alert-retention`, deploy-kill retry) walks the open admin rows oldest first in pages of 500. Rule 1: a bell row not done whose last activity is more than 30 days old is marked done, read or unread. Rule 2: an FYI row (`metadata.severity = fyi`, or an `ops_digest` row of audience `fyi`) idle more than 7 days is marked done. Last activity is the latest of `created_at`, `metadata.rungAt`, `metadata.observedAt` and `metadata.lastFailureAt`, so a row its emitter still refreshes with a ring is kept; a quiet refresh leaves no stamp. Rows in the Activity feed that are not FYI are left alone (no bell to leave) and the query never returns them. A run reads at most 20,000 candidates; a run that stops on that budget saves a continuation cursor (`system_settings` key `admin_alert_retention_cursor_<mode>`) and the next run resumes behind it, and a run that reaches the end clears it. The write is `done_at`, `done_by = retention`, a plain `resolution` ("Expired: no action in 30 days" or "FYI expired after 7 days") and `metadata.retention = {run, rule, at}`; `read_at` is not touched; nothing is deleted; no row locks (a 2 s lock timeout skips a batch, the next run takes it). Re-ring: emitters that pass `dedupeOpenOnly` raise a fresh row when their condition still holds; the shadow summary counts, per emitter, the rows that could ring again, the emitters a sweep raises again with no new event (cancelled-root price guard, SMS draft canary) are capped at 10 rows per run, and an overdue-promise row whose promise is still open is skipped. `shadow` writes one `audit_log` row (`admin_alert_retention.shadow`); `true` writes one per run (`admin_alert_retention.expire`). Undo one run: `node server/scripts/undo-admin-alert-retention.js --run <run id>` (dry run; `--execute` writes). Rollback: unset the variable, no redeploy. Sends nothing to a customer.

Admin alert catalog, watch mode (owner 2026-10-29, "ok go" on admin bell rebuild step D1; `docs/admin-notifications.md` section 6): `GATE_ALERT_CATALOG` — **ships DARK, two states, read at call time via `alertCatalogMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`**: unset or anything but `watch` (trimmed, any case) = off, byte-identical: no read, no write. `watch` = when the 08-28 bell policy (`GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY`) silences an admin alert, which writes no row (inside `NotificationService.create`, or in `triggerNotification` for a registry event, which checks the policy itself and returns before create), the service writes ONE `audit_log` row per Eastern day per distinct muted alert (`auditBellPolicyMuted`): `action = notification.bell_policy.muted`, `resource_type = notification`, `metadata = {category, triggerKey, titleStem, etDay}`, plus, when the alert declared them, `area`, `severity` and `who` (a composer alert) and `kind` (its dedupe key's class prefix, ids as `#`), where `titleStem` is the title with every digit run as `#`, whitespace collapsed, cut at 80 characters. The day's dedupe is in memory, so a restart may write a second row for the same alert that day. The write uses the module's own database handle, never the caller's transaction; a failure logs a short error summary with no title text and never changes `create()`'s return (`{id: null, suppressed: true, reason: 'bell_policy'}`). Watch mode refuses nothing and changes no bell, push or preference. The registry side needs no gate: every `TRIGGER_REGISTRY` type carries a `rule` (area, severity, who, and `doneWhen` + `closedBy` or `expiryDays`), checked by `server/tests/admin-alert-catalog-contract.test.js`. Count muted alerts with `SELECT metadata->>'category', metadata->>'triggerKey', count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'notification.bell_policy.muted' GROUP BY 1, 2`. Rollback: unset the variable, no redeploy. Sends nothing to a customer.

SMS courtesy tail (owner 2026-10-29, fix F2 "Stuck Alert Fixes"; `isCourtesyOnly` in `server/services/sms-intent.js`, inbound webhook `server/routes/twilio-webhook.js`): `GATE_SMS_COURTESY_TAIL` — **ships DARK, three states, read at call time via `courtesyTailMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`**: unset or any other value = off, `isCourtesyOnly` is byte-identical to before; `shadow` (trimmed, any case) = every result unchanged, the webhook stamps `metadata.courtesyTailWould: true` on the inbound `sms_log` and `messages` rows when the new rule would newly call the text courtesy-only; `true` = `isCourtesyOnly` applies the new rule, so the webhook (already read, no bell, no AI auto-reply, no lead) and the Messages needs-reply reader (alert and evening digest close) both use it. The rule (all must hold, doubt = false): the strict rule says false and our last text asked nothing; the text has no `?`, digit, `@`, URL or non-ASCII symbol and is at most 80 characters; no scheduling or reschedule/away signal; the text splits at the first `.` `!` `,` ` - ` or line break into a HEAD that passes the strict courtesy grammar alone (a bare "ok" head does not count) and a TAIL of 1 to 6 words with no request, contrast, problem, pest, service, money or access word (`COURTESY_TAIL_BLOCK_WORDS`). "Perfect. Go browns" closes; "Great, but the gate is locked" and "Thanks, I paid the invoice" do not. Rollback: unset the variable, no redeploy. Sends nothing to a customer.

Auto Pay hold timeout (owner 2026-10-26, "OK FIX"; `releaseStaleAutopayHolds` in `server/services/invoice-followups.js`): `GATE_AUTOPAY_HOLD_TIMEOUT` — **ships DARK, four states, read at call time via `autopayHoldTimeoutMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`**: unset or any other value = off, no query; `shadow` (trimmed, any case) = record, change nothing; `true` = release; `charge` = charge the saved Auto Pay card or bank first (see "`charge` mode" below; it moves money, so the owner flips it). Why: an invoice reminder sequence starts in `autopay_hold` when the customer is on Auto Pay, and only `handleAutopayFailure` (3 failures) released it. Auto Pay never charges some invoices (an annual-prepay invoice staff created after a visit: Auto Pay charges only at visit completion, monthly dues and stranded accept-time prepay charges), so such an invoice never failed and sat held forever with no reminder and no charge. The sweep runs inside the `invoice-followups` job (`scheduler.js`, 10:16 AM ET Tue-Fri) under the same `runExclusive` lock, once per run, before due touches; a sweep failure is logged and does not stop the touch run. A candidate is a sequence in `autopay_hold` whose `updated_at` (the hold start; every hold writer and every failure-counter bump stamps it) is more than 3 days old (`AUTOPAY_HOLD_TIMEOUT_DAYS`), with no `stripe_invoice_charge_attempts` row for the invoice at all (any age, any state: an attempt means Auto Pay acted, and an unresolved one still needs its reconciliation), no `payments` row for the customer (any status) created since the hold start that Auto Pay or the pay page could have written, and no failed `payments` row for the customer still on the Auto Pay retry ladder (`next_retry_at` set; billing-cron retries after 2 and 4 days). A manual tender does not count as that evidence (owner 2026-10-29): a `payments` row that is `paid` with no `processor`, no `stripe_charge_id` and no `stripe_payment_intent_id` (`OFF_GATEWAY_PAID_TENDER`) is money a person took. `recordManualPayment` writes exactly that for cash, check, Zelle, Venmo, PayPal and other, and so do the prepaid-credit rows and the check/cash branch of the payment reconcile; before this a cash or check payment the office recorded froze that customer's other held invoices for good, with no reminder and no charge. Every Auto Pay and pay-page writer (`stripe.js`, `pay-combined.js`, the Stripe webhook, `estimate-card-holds.js`) sets `processor` `'stripe'` or a Stripe id, and billing-cron's deferred or failed monthly rows are not `paid`, so they still block. Only a customer the customer-level reminder engine OWNS (an open `customer_dunning_schedules` row: status `active`, `held`, `paused` or `autopay_hold`) is skipped, in the select and again inside the guarded release UPDATE (a promotion that lands between the read and the write keeps the hold). The engine's coverage is not a skip any more: `GATE_DUNNING_CUSTOMER_SCHEDULE` live with `DUNNING_CUSTOMER_SCHEDULE_ALLOWLIST` unset covers every customer, and the engine promotes only `active` rows (`promotionCandidates`), never an `autopay_hold` row, so skipping covered customers would stop the sweep for everyone and leave a single uncharged Auto Pay invoice held for good. What happens now: a customer with ONE held invoice has it released to its own per-invoice ladder, and the engine never touches it (promotion needs two active invoices). A customer with TWO OR MORE held invoices that all time out gets them released together; the same job's `runPending` then promotes the two active rows into one combined schedule (the old worry: a released row promoted back into a hold). While the customer is still on Auto Pay the engine parks that schedule as `autopay_hold`, silently, and revisits it daily; an open schedule is the engine's, so this sweep does not release it again. The first-promotion alert below is then the office's only notice, and a person must charge the card or take the customer off Auto Pay. Every held row is read, in id-keyset pages of 500, so skipped rows never hide later ones. An invoice that is terminal, not schedulable, payer-billed or withdrawn, or has an active payment plan is skipped. An invoice linked to a visit (`scheduled_service_id`) whose status is not in `TERMINAL_SCHEDULED_SERVICE_STATUSES` is also skipped: Auto Pay charges when the visit closes, so an upfront invoice is waiting for that charge. No linked visit, or a closed one, stays eligible. `true` releases each candidate with the same fields as `releaseFromAutopayHold` (status `active`, next touch from the anchor), except that the first touch is dated no earlier than the NEXT send-window run (`adoptionLanding`, the rule promotion and adoption use: steps whose day passed are walked over, a step already due lands on the next Tue-Fri 10 AM), so the release run's own `runPending` never sends it and the office has a day to charge the card first, in one guarded UPDATE that re-applies the SQL rule and requires the hold's `updated_at` unchanged since the read (compared as text, to the microsecond), so a failure bump, payment, retry, plan, visit change or schedule that lands in between keeps the hold; it logs one count line. Each release raises ONE office alert through `raiseAdminAlert` (`alertAutopayHoldReleased`, Billing, needs-you, person; headline "charge the card on file for <first name + last initial>", why "Auto Pay did not charge invoice <number> ($X); reminders start <weekday, date>", or "no reminder steps are left to send" when every step's day has passed), deduped by `autopay-hold-timeout:<invoice id>:<hold stamp>`, so one alert per invoice and hold episode and none on a re-run. `shadow` writes no alert and one `audit_log` row per would-release invoice (`invoice_followup.autopay_hold_timeout_shadow`, metadata `sequence_id`, `held_since`, `days_held`), at most one per invoice per Eastern day. No migration, no customer copy changed; a released invoice follows the normal reminder ladder. Rollback = unset (a released row stays released). **`charge` mode (owner 2026-10-28, "Charge the saved card"; values: `off` / `shadow` / `true` / `charge`).** Selection is the `true` rule set (same skips, same id-keyset paging) with six charge-mode changes (the sixth, below, narrows what `charge` may charge: owner 2026-10-29, option B). (1) **Payments:** a customer's settled payment for a SIBLING invoice no longer blocks (charging one held invoice would otherwise disqualify the customer's other holds for good). Two rules replace the customer-wide one: no non-failed payment for THIS invoice since the hold (matched by `metadata.invoice_id` or the invoice number in the description), and no `processing`/`pending` payment for the customer since the hold (any invoice). The same rules apply on the recheck before each charge and, since the hold stamp, after a charge that failed cleanly. (2) **Dispute holds:** a customer with an active collections dispute hold (`disputeHoldExistsSql`, the same test the charge refuses on) is not selected, and a hold that appears before the quote, or a hold-check failure, defers the invoice quietly (no marker, no attempt, no release, no alert; retried next run). A charge that still throws `COLLECTION_HOLD_ACTIVE` or `COLLECTION_HOLD_CHECK_FAILED` (a race) is `deferred`: the hold is kept, one office alert says a dispute hold stopped the charge, and the final row outcome is `deferred`. The attempt rows such a refusal leaves (`failed`) are ignored by the attempt rule once a final `deferred` row follows them, so the invoice is charged once after the hold clears; every other attempt row still excludes the invoice. (3) A timeout release in charge mode raises no second alert (the charge-mode alert is the one). (4) **Annual-prepay term rails are never charged here:** an invoice an `annual_prepay_terms` row references (`prepay_invoice_id`, the one column every dedicated rail charges through: `termite-annual-renewal-charge.js`, `termite-annual-signature-charge.js` and the deferred prepay in `recurring-card-on-file.js`) is governed by that rail's signed-agreement cap, surcharge rule and renewal gate, which this generic call does not carry. In charge mode these invoices are selected in a separate pass and released exactly as `true` releases them (the `true` rule set and recheck, the `true`-mode office alert `alertAutopayHoldReleased`, counted in `released` and `true_released`), never quoted, never charged; the charge pass excludes them in SQL. (5) **Bank methods wait for the invoice due date (ACH consent: a debit "on or after its due date"):** a bank method (`ach` / `us_bank_account`) on an invoice whose due date (an ET date-only string, `etCalendarDayOf`) is after today (ET) is skipped quietly (no quote, marker, attempt, release or alert; counted `not_due`; retried next run). The Auto Pay billing day the customer may have chosen is an earlier alternative and is ignored (waiting for the due date never exceeds the consent). A bank method on an invoice with NO due date has no authorized debit date, so it is released as `true` releases it (counted `true_released`). Cards are unchanged. The charge also passes `requireBankDebitDue: true`, which re-checks the same rule against the locked invoice before any credit apply or Stripe call and refuses with code `BANK_DEBIT_NOT_DUE` (message "Bank debit date has not arrived..."); the sweep treats that as `not_due`: the hold stays, no alert, the final row outcome is `deferred` (reason `not_due`) so the attempt rule lets the next run charge it once it is due, and recovery reads an unfinished attempt with that message the same way (final row `deferred`, reason `bank_debit_not_due`, no alert, no release). (6) **Visit bills only, inside the visit-completion rail's own authorization (owner 2026-10-29, option B: "inside the cap: charge the card; outside: office alert, no charge").** An invoice bound to no visit (`scheduled_service_id` null) is released as `true` releases it and never charged (it has no agreed price to cap it). A visit-bound invoice gets a verdict (`visitBillVerdict` in `invoice-followups.js`) BEFORE the quote and before the start marker, built from the completion route's own read-only functions (`completion-charge-verdict.js`: `resolveAppointmentCardLane`, `resolveExtendedLane`, `resolveCompletionChargeCap`, strict, so a lookup failure keeps the hold and the next run retries, counted `skipped`): the visit must be `completed` and its latest `service_records` row a performed closeout (`closeoutPerformedForCharge` in `visit-outcomes.js`, the predicate `requirePerformedVisit` uses; an inspection-only, declined or incomplete closeout, or a manual backfill, is not performed); a payer on the invoice or on the visit/customer (`payer.resolveForInvoice`) is never charged; a visit that carries a cash/Zelle prepayment the bill does not show (`visitCarriesUnappliedPrepayment` in `billing-lane.js`: `scheduled_services.prepaid_method` other than `annual_prepay_invoice` with `prepaid_amount` > 0 and no paid `payments` row with `metadata.source` `scheduled_service_prepaid` for this invoice and visit; a backfill closeout skips applying it) is never charged, on any lane; the bill must fall in a completion lane (per-application, appointment-card one-time, or the extended Auto Pay lane) and its pre-tax subtotal net of discounts must be inside the lane's cap ceiling (the visit's accepted price, else the customer's per-application fee or dues rate); Auto Pay must be active (`customerOnAutopay`, as completion reads it) for a charge. **Order:** these review conditions (payer, not performed, unapplied prepayment, over cap, no cap) run BEFORE every release decision: a bound bill that fails one is an office review even when the customer has no Auto Pay method or the bank invoice has no due date. Only a bound bill that passes all of them is released for no method, no due date, an inactive Auto Pay or no lane. The charge also passes `requireNoUnappliedVisitPrepayment: true`, which re-runs the prepayment test under the visit lock (refusal code `UNAPPLIED_VISIT_PREPAYMENT`, an office review). **A visit the issued-invoice closeout job closed after its bill was sent counts as performed FOR THIS CHARGE ONLY** (owner 2026-10-29, "charge late visits"): `chargeInvoiceWithSavedCard` takes `allowIssuedInvoiceCloseoutFor: invoice.id`, which, together with `requirePerformedVisit`, lets a latest record that is completed, `visitOutcome` `completed`, `backfill` true and carries `structured_notes.issuedInvoiceCloseout.invoiceId` equal to the invoice being charged count as performed; a manual backfill without that marker, or a marker for another invoice, still refuses. The completion route and every other caller are unchanged (backfill closeouts never move money automatically there). `GATE_COMPLETION_AUTOPAY_CHARGE` and `GATE_APPT_CARD_COMPLETION_CHARGE` are read exactly the way completion reads them, inside the shared verdict functions: both are boot-time values (`gates.completionAutopayCharge`, `isEnabled('apptCardCompletionCharge')`), so a change needs a restart; with both off, only a per-application customer's visit bill is admitted, and any other visit bill is released as `true` releases it. The verdict's outcomes: inside the cap = charge (below); **over the cap, no agreed price on file (no visit price and no dues rate), not a performed visit, or a payer = office review**: the hold is kept, nothing is charged, no marker or attempt is written, no reminder goes to the customer, ONE office alert (`autopay_hold_charge:review:<invoice id>`) says why, and a final audit row with outcome `review` is written carrying a `fingerprint` (an md5 over the invoice's subtotal, discount, total and payer, the visit's price, payer and prepayment stamp, and the customer's per-application fee, dues rate, billing mode and payer: `chargeFactsFingerprintSql`). The charge-mode candidate rule excludes a hold whose newest final row is a `review` with the SAME fingerprint (`chargeModeUnreviewedRule`), so the next run is silent; a changed bill or visit price is a new fingerprint and is evaluated once more, at most one new alert (the alert is deduped while its row is open; a row marked done re-rings only on a new fingerprint: kind `event` in `admin-alert-retention.js`). No annual-prepay office-review state is re-derived: the extended lane's `requireExtendedCompletionAnchor` refuses a visit under annual-prepay coverage under the locks, which is a review. For each candidate the sweep re-checks that the hold is unchanged (no lock), finds the method Auto Pay itself would charge (`getChargeableAutopayMethod`, card or bank), runs the verdict above, quotes it (`quoteInvoiceSavedCardCharge`) and calls `chargeInvoiceWithSavedCard(invoice.id, method.id, { ...the completion route's own option set for the lane (maxAuthorizedSubtotal: the cap ceiling, requireAutopayForCustomerId, requireSelfPayScheduledServiceId, requireOneTimeLane, requireNoAppointmentCardLane and requireExtendedCompletionAnchor for the extended lane, maxAuthorizedChargeCents for the extended lane), requireInvoiceScheduledServiceBinding, refuseWhenDunningStopped, requireCompletedVisit, requirePerformedVisit, allowIssuedInvoiceCloseoutFor: invoice.id, requireBankDebitDue: true, maxAuthorizedTotalCents: round(quote.total*100) })` (the quote total includes any card surcharge and is the ceiling on the charge; there is no exact-total demand, so a lower total is allowed; the default collections dispute-hold guard stays on, no operator override). Outcomes: **paid, processing (bank) or covered by account credit** = the hold is NOT released; a paid or credit-covered invoice closes its follow-up sequence through `stopOnPayment` (the charge path calls it; the sweep calls it again as a no-op safety net) and a bank charge closes it when the webhook settles it; the normal receipt comes from the charge path and the sweep sends nothing. **A real card decline (the charge path stored a decline code) or no chargeable method** = the hold is released exactly as `true` does it (so the reminder ladder starts) and ONE office alert (category billing, key `autopay_hold_charge:declined:<invoice id>`) names the customer, invoice, amount and reason. **A guard refusal before anything reaches Stripe** (`PAYER_BILLED_GUARD`, `VISIT_NOT_COMPLETED`, `COMPETING_CARD_CONSENT`, a stopped sequence, a cap, lane or anchor error with no code, a refused quote) is never a release (a released payer debt would send the homeowner the payer's pay link): it is an office review, with the hold kept, a `failed` attempt row with no decline code (when the charge was called), and a final `review` row with the fingerprint. The attempt rule lets such an invoice back in once its newest `review` row no longer matches the bill (one retry after the office changes it). **Ambiguous** (`STRIPE_AMBIGUOUS_OUTCOME`, `STRIPE_CHARGED_DB_FAILED`, `STRIPE_CHARGE_IN_PROGRESS`, a reconciliation flag, or an unresolved charge attempt after any other error) = the hold is NOT released, nothing is retried, and ONE office alert (key `autopay_hold_charge:ambiguous:<invoice id>`) says to check Stripe before anything else. One `audit_log` row per attempt (`invoice_followup.autopay_hold_timeout_charge`; metadata `sequence_id`, `outcome`, `reason`, `error_code`, `amount_cents`, `method_type`, `released`; no card numbers, no names). The durable `stripe_invoice_charge_attempts` claim the charge makes keeps the clause from picking the invoice again; a release when no charge was called (no method) uses the original guards in full, hold-stamp equality included; a release after a charge call that failed cleanly exempts only the `failed` attempt and `failed` payment that charge wrote (any other attempt, or any non-failed payment since the hold began, keeps the hold) and drops only the age and hold-stamp checks. A method lookup that throws keeps the hold, alerts nothing and counts as `skipped`; the next run retries. **Recovery (charge mode only, never charges):** right before the charge call the sweep writes an `invoice_followup.autopay_hold_timeout_charge_started` audit row (sequence, customer, hold stamp, amount; if it cannot be written, nothing is charged), and the per-attempt `invoice_followup.autopay_hold_timeout_charge` row is the LAST write of a finished attempt. The office alert goes FIRST: if it cannot be filed nothing else is done (no release, no final row, counted in `errors`) and the next run's recovery retries it; after a filed alert come the release, stopOnPayment and then the final row. At the start of each charge sweep, a start marker with no later final row on a sequence still in `autopay_hold` is finished from the `stripe_invoice_charge_attempts` rows created at or after the marker: all `failed` (and none with decline code `authentication_required`, which is read as ambiguous because the customer can still complete that PaymentIntent, and which also blocks the own-charge release itself) with a decline code = release with the narrowed own-charge guards, the declined alert (same dedupe key) and a final row with reason `recovered`; all `failed` with no decline code (a refusal before Stripe) = the review alert, the hold kept and a final `review` row (reason `refused`); any other attempt on a paid or prepaid invoice = `stopOnPayment` and a final row `charged`; any other attempt otherwise = the check-Stripe alert and a final row `ambiguous`; no attempt at all = a final row `abandoned` and the hold stays for the normal rule next run (not charged in the same run). The normal stale rule still rejects every attempt row, so an invoice is never charged twice. The sweep returns `{ mode, candidates, released, recorded, charged, declined_released, true_released, review, ambiguous, deferred, not_due, skipped }` (`released` = `declined_released` + `true_released`; `candidates` includes the term-rail pass) and logs one `autopay hold timeout (charge)` count line. `off`, `shadow` and `true` are unchanged. Rollback = unset or set `true`.

Promise record evidence (owner 2026-10-29, fix F4 on "Stuck Alert Fixes"; `server/services/sms-commitment-fulfillment.js` and `refreshSmsCommitment` in `server/services/sms-operational-actions.js`): `GATE_PROMISE_RECORD_EVIDENCE` — **ships DARK, three states, read at call time via `promiseRecordEvidenceMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`**: unset or any other value = off, byte-identical; `shadow` (trimmed, any case) = record, change nothing; `true` = apply. Why: three prod promises rang the "Comms — follow up" bell although the records answered them. (1) A staff promise ("I'll adjust the payment terms"): an `invoice` Waves sent this customer after the promise was loaded but never admissible, so the annual prepay invoice that carried out the promise did not count. (2) A `send_estimate` ask: estimate evidence was only a hand-off after the ask, so an estimate sent before the ask and accepted by the customer after it did not count. (3) A waves promise whose answer was a visit booked an hour after the bell rang. `true` does three things. Rule 1: for a staff promise (`other`, basis `promise`) an invoice with `sent_at` after the promise text, not void, cancelled or refunded, is a witness type; the model alone judges it (never a no-model close), and its text now carries invoice number, title, total, send date, whether it is an annual prepay invoice and up to five line descriptions, and the prompt gains one sentence naming it. Rule 2: for `send_estimate` an estimate with `accepted_at` after the ask (up to now) is loaded and admissible, same customer ownership and the same property scoping as any estimate; the model judges it; `accepted_at` on or before the ask never counts. Rule 3: a waves-party row (basis `promise` or `request`) of kind `other`, `callback` or `technician_follow_up`, past its due time, whose customer has a live visit (status not cancelled, no_show or skipped; `recurring_parent_id` null; at the promise's property when it names one) created after the promise text whose scheduled day is within 14 days of the promise's due date (Eastern day), and whose window end (`window_end`, else `window_start` + 60 minutes, Eastern) is still ahead, does not ring the overdue bell (nor the kept-late bell) until that window end. The row stays open and the visit-progress rule (R1) is unchanged; once the window end passes the bell rings as before. A promise kept by the model or the visit still closes. The fulfillment fingerprint carries policy 26 only when the gate is `true`, so cached verdicts are rechecked once (one model call per still-open row on its next tick); off keeps policy 25 and today's hashes. `shadow` applies nothing: when the normal check leaves a promise open and the extended evidence holds a new admissible record (an invoice, an accepted estimate), the model runs once more on the extended evidence and ONE `audit_log` row `sms_commitment.fulfillment.shadow` records it (metadata `commitment_id`, `kind`, `new_records`, `shadow_verdict`, `evidence_hash`), at most 10 such extra model calls per run and never twice for the same evidence hash; when rule 3 would skip a ring the ring still happens and one `sms_commitment.on_track.shadow` row per promise per Eastern day records the visit and window end. No migration, no customer copy changed. Rollback = unset.

Service-line map (dark; `shadow` records, `live` also places new work): `GATE_SERVICE_LINE_MAP` — **`shadow` and `live` are the only values that do anything; anything else, `true` included, is off**, read at call time via `serviceLineMapMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (exactly `shadow` or `live`, trimmed, any case). Owner 2026-10-25: a second technician starts early 2027; the new technician is the home tech for general pest, rodent and mosquito, and the owner is the home tech for lawn / tree & shrub and termite / WDO and covers every gap. `service_line_techs` (migration `20261025220000`) holds one row per line (`general`, `mosquito`, `lawn`, `rodent`, `termite`) with a home and a gap technician, edited on the Team tab "Service lines" card (`/api/admin/timetracking/service-lines`, shown while the gate is `shadow` or `live`; the card says which). On `shadow` and `live`, after each of six choice points commits (/book confirm, phone live booking, after-call booking, estimate accept, an office create left on Auto, the auto-dispatch night run) `server/services/scheduling/line-technician.js` writes one `service_line_pick_shadow` row: the technician actually chosen, the one the map would pick (`would_reason`), the line and whether it came from the service catalog or the name. Read-out: `/api/admin/timetracking/service-lines/shadow-summary`. The recorder never changes a booking and sends nothing to a customer or staff member; a recorder failure is swallowed. **`live` (build 4, owner 2026-10-30)** adds the pickers, for NEW work at these sites only: (1) /book offers (`buildBookingAvailability` `serviceLines`, passed by `buildFunnelAvailability` from the funnel service key; /availability, /find-slots, the capture-intent revalidation and the pin readers) keep only the line's home and gap technician's slots, the home technician claiming a start both have (`lineOfferRanking`); a two-service booking needs a technician who is the home or gap technician of every mapped line; (2) the phone booking recheck (`relay-booking.js` `revalidateSlot`) passes the booked service's line the same way, so a start only another line's technician had answers slot_gone and the saved technician is the line's; (3) the after-call booking (`call-recording-processor.js`, fresh and reused visit): the visit's own service and day pick the home technician, else the gap technician, else the visit saves unassigned (`pickLineTechnician`, no free-time check; the overlap probe still flags a clash); visit 2 copies visit 1; (4) `pick-technician.js` `pickTechnicianForVisit` (when its own gate is active) and (5) the office "Auto" choice (`office-auto-technician.js`, behind `GATE_UNASSIGNED_VISIT_GUARD`; reasons `line_home`, `line_gap`, `line_none`) let the line decide among the technicians that may take the visit. (6) the estimate time picker (`estimate-slot-availability.js`): only the home and gap technicians of the line(s) the held visit carries are offered: the primary program's line (`primaryProfileService`, the rule the hold stamps), or every program's line for a combined capacity hold, so only a technician on every line is offered. The home technician wins a date and start both have; the gap technician fills the starts the home technician has none for; everyone else is dropped. Each time keeps its own technician's first name. A ranked list is not cached. (7) the estimate accept (`estimate-converter.js` via `scheduling/promoted-unit-line.js`): a program added to the customer's picked trip (not a combined capacity member) whose line has a technician set no longer copies the reserved visit's hour and technician when the line's technician is someone else: it books the same day with no time on the line's technician (unassigned if nobody can take it), and its customer-visible note says its time will be set separately; the schedule watchdog's combined-booking check (`GATE_SCHEDULE_INTEGRITY_WATCHDOG`) flags the visit with no time for the office. The same technician keeps today's copy. A line with no technician set adds no rule, so `live` with an empty `service_line_techs` behaves as `shadow`. The night run still places only unassigned visits. Not covered: a Waves Assessment (the free sales visit, catalog key `lawn_inspection`) is never routed by the map at any site and keeps today's choice (`liveServiceLine` / `pickLineTechnician` reason `assessment`: which line an inspection belongs to is an open owner decision); also the assessment link, public reschedule and re-service offers, commercial first visit and the phone agent's find_slots offers. Rollback = `shadow` or unset.

Territory routing (dark): `GATE_TERRITORY_ROUTING` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `territoryRoutingLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-30 ("go" on question 4 of the Waves Territory Map page): each technician has a territory drawn as a ZIP list in `territory_zips` (migration `20261031000000_territory_zips.js`; 52 ZIPs, 7 areas, `technician_id` NULL until a handover run assigns it). On, the service-line map (`services/scheduling/line-technician.js`) lays the territory over a pest, mosquito, rodent or termite / WDO line: the technician who owns the visit's ZIP becomes that line's home technician, and the line's own home (else gap) technician covers that technician's gaps. Lawn / tree & shrub keeps the line map. The ZIP comes from the visit's ZIP, else its map position (`server/data/territory-zip-shapes.json`, Census 2020 ZIP areas), else the customer row's ZIP or map position (`services/territory.js` `territoryTechnicianFor`). A ZIP with no territory technician, or outside the 52, adds no rule. It acts only where `GATE_SERVICE_LINE_MAP` acts: `shadow` rows record the territory pick, `live` picks follow it. Off = the line map exactly as before, no territory query. Sends nothing to a customer or staff member.

Territory night run (dark): `GATE_TERRITORY_NIGHT_RUN` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `territoryNightRunLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). A visit that already has a technician, a lawn / tree & shrub visit, or a ZIP with no territory technician adds no rule; an unreadable territory adds none either. Territory read-out (dark): `GATE_TERRITORY_READOUT` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `territoryReadoutLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-30 ("go" on question 4 of the Waves Territory Map page, build 3): the Team tab shows a Territories card (`client/src/pages/admin/TerritoryReadoutCard.jsx`) with stops a week per technician and area, booked over the next 4 weeks (pending / confirmed) and done over the last 4 (completed); a stop is one customer at one appointment slot, so sibling service rows count once, and a customer-portal reschedule placeholder (`rescheduled`) or an unclaimed estimate hold is not a stop, from `GET /api/admin/timetracking/territory-readout` (admin only; `?weeks=` 1-13, default 4). Each stop takes one ZIP, a sibling's stamped service ZIP before its customer's ZIP, and its area comes from `territory_zips` (`services/territory.js` `territoryReadout`); a ZIP outside the 52 reads as no area. Unassigned-visit guard (dark): `GATE_UNASSIGNED_VISIT_GUARD` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `unassignedVisitGuardLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-25 (census H5 + M13): a second technician starts early 2027, and a visit with no technician shows on no field app. Two changes. (1) The office create modal's "Auto" technician choice (`POST /api/admin/schedule`, `assignmentMode: 'auto'` with no technician named) used to ask `services/tech-matcher`, which does not exist, so Auto always saved the visit unassigned. On, `server/services/scheduling/office-auto-technician.js` resolves a real technician from the existing rules: the technicians assignable for that visit and day (`technician-eligibility.js`: active and field-dispatchable, not absent, not off that day while `GATE_TECH_WORK_DAYS` is on; `technician_capabilities`: not Off for the visit's service line, read through `line-technician.js` `serviceLineFor`). Exactly one: that technician. Several: the existing `scheduling/pick-technician.js` pick when it is active (`GATE_MULTI_TECH_CONFIRM`, in hour mode or capacity mode) and the visit has a window; otherwise the visit stays unassigned for the office to place. The response carries `autoAssign: { result: 'assigned' | 'unassigned', reason }` and the modal shows a plain warning that the visit was saved with no technician; a save is never blocked (a technician marked out on a later date of a recurring series leaves the series unassigned with reason `absent_on_series_date` instead of refusing it). A recurring series resolves once for the parent; children copy it. The `GATE_SERVICE_LINE_MAP` shadow log call (`office_auto`) is unchanged. (2) `server/services/unassigned-timed-visits-check.js`, daily 6:10 PM ET (`scheduler.js`, `runExclusive` key `unassigned-timed-visits`): one standing Schedule row, "Schedule — assign a technician to N visits", for timed visits (`window_start` set) from tomorrow through 3 days out with no technician and a live status (not an estimate hold, not an internal test customer, and not a visit the combined-booking check already rings for). It carries `count` and `itemKeys`, rings only when a new visit joins, refreshes quietly when one leaves, closes itself (done) at zero, and links to the schedule board on the earliest day. Dedupe key `unassigned-timed-visits`; category `alert`. Off = Auto behaves exactly as before (the old failing require stays on that path) and the check returns before any query. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback = unset.


Customer rain rank (dark): `GATE_CUSTOMER_RAIN_RANK` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/customer-rain-rank.js` (unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-08. The rain-fit rule of `GATE_BOOKING_RAIN_RANK` on the customer booking surfaces: `buildBookingAvailability` (`routes/booking.js`: `/book`, the inspection link, public reschedule) stamps a rain tier on each candidate, and `compareRankedSlots` and the per-day best fit sort by it before route score. The booking's services come from the visit's own catalog identity when the caller has one, else from the funnel labels. The public re-service profile (`GATE_RESERVICE_RANK_AFTER_NEW`) keeps its own order. Order only: which hours are offered, the full day list, signed offers and commit checks are unchanged; `rain_tier` never leaves the server, and a curated slot whose tier is above 0 carries `display_tier`, which the picker sorts by first (contract in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`). Nothing is read until a candidate inside the 3 dates exists; the point must be inside the service area's coarse box, and at most 60 reads start per minute per process (past that: today's order). Fail open (gate off, neutral booking, no forecast): every candidate is tier 0, today's order. The estimate page's slot list (`estimate-slot-availability.js` `selectCustomerFacingSlots`) takes the same gate: behind the soonest-opening first card and a scarce first day's pinned cards, slots are reordered by rain fit before the display slice (`slotRainTierOf` / `demoteByRainTier`); a slot moved behind drier ones carries `display_tier`, never a lead card. Only the services this appointment performs are classified (`appointmentServicesFor`: a recurring estimate's primary service; every line of one-time work or a combined allocation), each by its catalog key (frozen on the line, resolved under the capacity gate, or looked up here), and an estimate with more than 12 such rows is outdoor.

Call booking rain flag (dark): `GATE_CALL_BOOKING_RAIN_FLAG` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/call-booking-rain-flag.js` (unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-08. The call pipeline (`call-recording-processor.js`) books the time a person agreed with the caller and never chooses one, so the rain ranking does not reach it (90 days: 35 of 39 such bookings from calls a person answered, 30 of 39 inside the 3-day horizon). After a FRESH phone-booked visit is written, `flagCallBookingRain` raises one admin alert through `raiseAdminAlert` on the `schedule` channel (headline "Schedule — check <name>'s visit for rain", severity `needs-you`, subject the visit, link to that visit on the dispatch schedule, `dedupeKey call-booking-rain:<visit id>`) when the visit is outdoor work by `rain-fit.js`'s classification (catalog identity from the pipeline's catalog row), its date is inside the next 3 dates, the booked property's point is inside the service area (the `lat`/`lng` the pipeline stamps on the visit; a visit tied to a property with no stamped point gets no forecast; only a visit with no property uses the customer's point), and the NWS hourly chance (Open-Meteo when NWS fails) is 60% or more from the start through 2 h after the end, where the end is the later of the stored window end and start + `estimated_duration_minutes`. It only tells: no visit is moved, no customer is texted, no triage card is created. The alert closes itself through the relevance sweep (`admin-alert-relevance.js` class `call_booking_rain`) once the visit is closed, gone, moved off the booked date or start, or past its date. Fail open: any miss or error is no notice.

Lead service names (dark): `GATE_LEAD_SERVICE_DISPLAY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time by `leadServiceDisplayLive()` in `server/routes/admin-leads.js` (unset = kill, no restart). Owner 2026-10-09. On: the lead list and lead detail responses carry `service_display`, the lead's service named the way the booking catalog names it (`server/utils/lead-service-display.js`): website, quote-wizard, call and email wordings land on one name ("Recurring Pest Control" → "Quarterly Pest Control Service"), a lead is recurring OR one-time, an unstated frequency reads "Waves Assessment (Pest + Lawn)", and a one-time request is never an assessment. The Leads screen shows it and keeps the stored text as a tooltip and a "From the lead" line. Read-only: `leads.service_interest` is never rewritten, so every reader of that text (estimate drafts, recurring intent, service lines, search) is unchanged. Off: the field is absent and the screen shows the stored text.

Collective series anchor: `GATE_COLLECTIVE_SERIES_ANCHOR` — on only when exactly `true`, read at call time. On: moving a recurring visit to another date shifts its whole future series (`server/services/rain-out.js`), so `POST /api/admin/dispatch/:id/rain-out` refuses that date change to a non-admin, and `GET /api/admin/dispatch/:id/rain-out-options` offers a non-admin on a recurring visit today's options only (`days: []`, `sameDayOnly: true`; the Quick Move sheet then keeps its custom date on today), or a 403 `admin_required` when that visit is overdue (dated before today), since every option would change its date. The tech route `/api/tech/services/:id/rain-out` is not fenced this way: it calls `RainOut.commit` without `requireAssignedTechnicianId`, so a technician's date change on a recurring visit there takes the series-shift branch and can move the whole future series. Off: no series shift, every date offered.
Reschedule next-visit date (dark): `GATE_RESCHEDULE_NEXT_VISIT_DATE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time in `server/routes/reschedule-public.js` (`nextVisitDateActive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-09 ("show every plan shift before the customer confirms"). On the customer reschedule page (`/reschedule/:token`), a recurring visit under `GATE_COLLECTIVE_SERIES_ANCHOR` gets a `nextVisit` key on the GET payload: the next plan visit's current date and, for each offered date, the cadence date the move would give it (`SmartRebooker.projectNextVisitDates`, the same projector as `rescheduleSeries`). The page shows one line under Confirm ("Your next visit moves too…"). The key is omitted when the customer's move would not write that date on the next visit (the rules are in `docs/public-route-contracts.md`), when the pick is the same date, or on any read failure. `find-slots` and the `SLOT_TAKEN` refresh carry the key too. Confirm pin: the commit body carries `disclosed_next_visit_date` and `disclosed_next_visit_current_date`; the series mover hands `moveGuard` its own verdict for the next visit under its locks, and the commit is refused `409 SCOPE_CHANGED` (the page reloads) when that differs from what the page named. No other move, text or charge changes. Rollback = unset.

Customer last start 16:00 (dark): `GATE_CUSTOMER_LAST_START_16` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/customer-windows.js` (`customerLastStart16Enabled()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-09 ("last start 16"). While on, `customerWindowAdmits` and `customerOfferGrid` admit no start after 16:00, so the estimate slot picker, `/book`, the public reschedule page and the public re-service page, and the assistant booking engine (`services/availability.js` `getAvailableSlots` + `confirmBooking`: the portal assistant's tools and text open-time drafts) stop offering and committing the 17:00 hour (a 5-7 PM arrival window). The grid constant, `booking_config.day_end` and the customer day close do not change. Staff, optimizer, auto-dispatch and voice callers do not call the admission rule and keep 17:00. A 17:00 slot offered before the flip is refused when the customer tries to take it (`createSelfBooking` at `/book` confirm, after its idempotent-replay lookup, so a retry of a 17:00 booking that already committed still replays; `customerWindowAdmits` in the commit rebuild on reschedule and re-service; `reserveSlot` on the estimate picker) and the customer picks again. The estimate slot cache key carries the gate state, so a flip does not serve cached 17:00 offers. An estimate hold that already exists on 17:00 is honored: a repeat `/reserve` for it returns the hold, and acceptance commits it. Rollback = unset.

Customer route check (dark): `GATE_CUSTOMER_ROUTE_CHECK` — **ships DARK: unset or any other value = off; `shadow` or `true`**, read at call time via `customerRouteCheckMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-29 ("start the builds", Route Check Everywhere build 3). Runs the dispatcher's 2-hour arrival-window route check (`server/services/scheduling/arrival-route.js`) over the time lists customers see, as a DROP-ONLY filter in `server/services/scheduling/customer-route-check.js` (`filterOfferedSlots`). Surfaces: `/book` (and the texting assistant's open times), public reschedule, public re-service, the inspection link, the commercial first visit and the phone agent (`buildBookingAvailability` in `server/routes/booking.js`), and the estimate page slot list and its ASAP windows (`estimate-slot-availability.js`, inside the cached builder: a cache hit does not recompute or log). The estimate page runs ONE check per request over its final eligible pool (route list and ASAP windows together, after the time-of-day, lead-time, season and zone-day filters), so the floor, the time budget and the route reads are shared and the floor is judged on what the customer could be shown: a morning-only search never ends with an empty picker. The reschedule list routes skip the check while a late-move limit holds the page back (the limit drops days after the build). It needs `GATE_ADMIN_ARRIVAL_WINDOWS` (or capacity mode) on; with that off the helper does nothing. Each offered slot is checked at its own date, start minute and technician, for the duration the old engine used. `shadow` = compute and log one `[customer-route-check] surface=... mode=... offered=... removed=... kept_unverified=... kept_other=... target_late=... baseline_late=... day_end=... floor_kept=... timed_out=... first_stop_hour=... ms=...` line (plus up to 5 lines for slots it would remove) and serve today's list. `true` = remove an hour ONLY if, at every placement that keeps the new customer's own 2-hour window, a customer who is on time without the new visit would arrive late. Stops already late before the new visit never count, a late day end alone never removes an hour, and a customer who is newly late removes the hour even on a day that is already late elsewhere or runs past the day end (the evaluator's `explain` diagnosis, `evaluateArrivalPlacement(..., { explain: true })`, tries the visit at every position of the day and reports `lateness.newlyLateStopIds`; a placement that saves the others only by missing the new customer's own window does not count). If one placement keeps every promise, the start stays. Also kept: a new customer who cannot be reached in their own window anywhere (`target_late`), a day that is only past the day end (`day_end`), a day that is only already late (`baseline_late`), route_unverified, return_time, arrival_margin, day_overcommitted, any error, a missing diagnosis and any slot not yet checked stay; the summary line counts `target_late`, `baseline_late` and `day_end` (KEPT slots only) separately from `kept_other`; a removed slot on a mixed day counts as removed, and its removed-slot line adds `mixed=baseline_late,day_end`. Without `explain` the evaluator returns exactly what it always did. Floor: if the removals would leave nothing dated today to today+6 (ET), the whole list is served unchanged. Budget about 1500 ms a request; slots not yet checked stay (`timed_out=true`). The phone agent is never filtered (its 3-second tool limit): its check runs after the answer, detached, in shadow only. Order and slot shapes never change. Drive times are the default route-optimizer estimate (the GPS-fitted clock under `GATE_DRIVE_CLOCK`); it never buys Google road times and never touches a commit, confirm or reserve path, a message or a limiter. Off = byte-identical: the helper is never called. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback = unset.

Assistant route times (dark): `GATE_ASSISTANT_ROUTE_TIMES` — **ships DARK: unset or any other value = off; `shadow` or `true`**, read at call time via `assistantRouteTimesMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-29 ("start the builds", Route Check Everywhere build 3c, "drive clock"). The portal assistant's `check_availability` (`server/services/ai-assistant/tools-expanded.js`) and the text drafter's city-based OPEN TIMES fallback (`server/services/sms-shadow-drafter.js`) asked the old by-city zone finder (`server/services/availability.js` `getAvailableSlots`: city to zone, `booking_config` day grid, overlap plus a straight-line travel gap). With the gate on they read the customer pages' list (`buildBookingAvailability` in `server/routes/booking.js`, through the pin reader `availabilityForPin`, so `GATE_CUSTOMER_ROUTE_CHECK` applies as on `/book`), for the customer's STORED pin only (`customers.latitude` / `longitude`, the pin `/book` commits at; a customer without one is never geocoded and gets the old list, in every mode), through the adapter `server/services/scheduling/assistant-route-times.js`. `shadow` = serve the old list, then (detached, 5 s cap, the reply never waits) build the new list and log one `[assistant-route-times] surface=<assistant|sms_drafter> mode=shadow old=<n> new=<m> both=<k> only_old=<a> only_new=<b> ms=<t>` line (`new=- reason=<no_stored_pin|no_service|no_customer|unavailable|timeout|error>` when the new list did not build). `true` = serve the new list in the old response shape (one slot per distinct start); no pin, a list not built inside the cap (1.5 s assistant, 3 s text quote) or any error serves the old list. Quote and recheck use one list: a text quote built on the new list stamps `open_times_snapshot.lookup.source = route_times` (plus `serviceKey`), the send-time recheck (`openTimesStillOffered`, called by `scheduler.js`, `agent-decision-send-checks.js`, `sms-auto-send.js` and `sms-scheduling-decide.js`) asks the new list for that source, and a snapshot with no source is rechecked on the old finder, whatever the gate says at send time. A `route_times` snapshot is an unknown offer kind in the offer ledger and never a suggestion card, exactly like the old finder's. With `GATE_MULTI_TECH_TEXT_TIMES` on, that gate's website-engine fallback keeps the city fallback and this gate does nothing for the drafter. For the assistant (not the text drafter) the new list is filtered against `confirmBooking`'s own commit constraints before it is served (`filterByCommit`, 1 s budget, calling the same functions: `isBlackoutDate`, `violatesSelfServeNotice`, `pastCustomerLastStart`, the zone occupied set through `loadZoneOccupied` (the loader `confirmBooking` itself calls: zone visits, unlinked legacy self-bookings, live estimate holds) and the technician-blind `findConflictingVisits` probe with interviews and the travel gap), because the customer pages offer per technician and the commit does not: a start one technician has free but another technician's visit overlaps is dropped, so every offer is bookable (a filter that fails or is slow, or that leaves nothing, serves the old list: owner ruling, never an empty picker when times exist, logged `fallback=old_empty`); shadow adds `commit_dropped=N` (and `fallback=old_empty` when it would fall back) to its line. The drafter's route quotes are not filtered: no automatic booking commits them (the offer ledger kind is unknown) and a person books them with the technician-aware staff tools. `confirmBooking` (the assistant's `book_appointment`) keeps its own conflict checks and is unchanged; with the gate `true` it also calls `placeMovedVisit` (source `assistant_booking`) on the new visit inside its transaction, which numbers the visit only when it has a technician and `GATE_STAFF_ROUTE_INSERTION` is on. The lead-response availability tool (`lead-response-tools.js`) and the estimate converter's first service day (`estimate-converter.js`) read the same old engine but are not covered by this gate (they follow `GATE_MULTI_TECH_TEXT_TIMES`). Drive times are the default route-optimizer estimate (the GPS-fitted clock under `GATE_DRIVE_CLOCK`); the pin reader is called with `providerTravel: false` (`availabilityForPin` and `buildBookingAvailability` pass it to find-time, whose capacity mode then builds its travel source with a zero request allowance), so even with `GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` on, shadow and true never draw on the paid Google allowance customer booking shares; every other caller keeps today's allowance. The same call passes `appendOnly: true` (`buildFunnelAvailability` then hands find-time `capacityPlacement: false`): the assistant's offers are append-only even with `GATE_BOOK_CAPACITY_COMMIT` on, because `confirmBooking` stores an unassigned visit with no certified route order, so a mid-route insertion offer could not be honored; `/book` and every other caller keep the gate's value. No Google purchase, no message to a customer, no template change. Off = byte-identical. Rollback = unset.

Review name match (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_NAME_MATCH_V2` — **ships DARK: unset or any other value = off; `shadow` or `true`**, read at call time via `reviewNameMatchMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). After each hourly review sync (`scheduler.js` :56), `server/services/review-name-match.js` scores every live Google review against every live customer with the evidence rules in `review-link-evidence.js` (names, first known contact, taps, recent visits and asks, "I left a review" texts) and records the decision on `google_reviews.name_match_*`: link / link_confirm / pause / household / queue / reject for an unlinked review, `disputed` for a linked review whose customer's first contact came after it. `shadow` = score and log the counts, write nothing; `true` = write the decisions that changed. Probable-reviewer guard (dark): `GATE_REVIEW_PROBABLE_REVIEWER_GUARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `reviewProbableReviewerGuardLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-31 (review matching plan PR 4, E1 A).
