Reschedule move limits (dark): `GATE_RESCHEDULE_MOVE_LIMITS` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/scheduling/customer-move-limits.js` (`moveLimitsEnabled()`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-09 ("limit yes", "no quota, first visit 2"). Scope: the public reschedule page only (`routes/reschedule-public.js`: GET, `find-slots`, Confirm). (1) Late-move limit: a plan visit moves online no later than its due date plus 21 days (quarterly), 14 (every other month), 10 (every 6 weeks) or 7 (monthly). The plan is read by its nominal gap in days (`intervalDaysForPattern`): 76-100 days = 21, 50-75 = 14, 36-49 = 10, 28-35 = 7, so `monthly_nth_weekday` and a `custom` plan with a 42-day interval get the same allowance as the named pattern; shorter and longer gaps (weekly, semiannual, annual), the Feb-Oct season and one-time visits have none; earlier dates are never limited; there is no count limit and no customer quota. The due date is the `original_date` of the visit's first `customer_self_serve` `reschedule_log` row since Waves last placed it, else its current date. The history starts again on: a slot-changing log row from any other initiator (staff, weather, dispatch, the phone or text agent); a visit that is not on the date and start the customer's last move gave it, or a customer move that does not start where the one before it ended (the staff edit screen writes no log row); and the customer's rebook of a missed visit (that row sets the appointment and is not a move). To let a customer past a limit, the office moves the visit. (2) First visit: a customer with no `completed` visit gets 2 online moves of a visit (a pick inside 15 minutes of the one before it is the same move, and the customer may correct for 15 minutes after the second); after that GET answers `not_reschedulable` / `move_limit` and the page shows "let's find a time that works" with Text and Call. (3) No rule empties the picker: the late-move limit is applied only when it ends before the booking range does and 3 or more times remain inside it, counted over the whole booking range, so GET, the search and Confirm reach one answer. GET, `find-slots` and the `SLOT_TAKEN` refresh add `moveLimit: { laterByOffice, noTimeSoon }` for the list they return (no date is sent; the page says later dates go through the office); `noTimeSoon` is true when no time is open in the next 7 days and the page says to text or call the office. Confirm refuses a date past an applied limit, or a blocked first visit, with `409 MOVE_LIMIT` after its idempotent replay; the page reloads. A missed visit (rebook) has no limit. Fail open: an unreadable history applies no limit. No customer message is sent and nothing is written. The staff pickers, `/reservice`, `/book`, and the text and phone agents do not read it. Rollback = unset.

Auto-dispatch rain pass (dark): `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_RAIN_PASS` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/auto-dispatch/rain-pass.js` (unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-08. The 04:10 auto-dispatch run never moves a visit inside 72 hours (`route-tiers.js`) and the hourly forecast is good for 3 dates (`rain-fit.js`), so the run cannot see rain. The pass runs every hour at :30 from 05:30 to 18:30 ET (`scheduler.js`, `runExclusive('auto-dispatch-rain-pass')`; a run that cannot finish fails the job) over every `pending`, `confirmed` or NULL-status visit on the next 3 dates, one row per physical stop (the route model's own `physicalStops` of `auto-dispatch/route-model.js`: a `visit_id` group or a legacy co-visit is one stop with the model's minutes; only those live rows and their add-ons make the stop). A stop is flagged when it is outdoor work by `rain-fit.js`'s classification (catalog identity) and the hourly chance of rain reaches 70% (`MOVE_PCT`; the booking ranking uses 60%) in any hour from its start through 2 h after its end, at the point where the work happens (`loadPoints`: the point stamped on the visit; else its linked property's own point while the property address still matches the visit's stamped address; else, only for a visit with no property link, the customer's primary home while the stamped address does not diverge from it; each a whole non-zero pair with its own ZIP; inside the service area by `isInServiceAreaBox` with that ZIP). For a flagged stop the pass looks for the start nearest its own on the same date, inside the service day Quick Move offers (`find-time` `DAY_START_HOUR`..`DAY_END_HOUR`), where every hour of the stop and its drying time reads below 40% (`DRY_PCT`, every hour read) and Rain Out's occupancy probe (`loadOccupancy` / `conflictsForTarget`) finds no other stop of that technician. It then raises one admin alert through `raiseAdminAlert` on the `schedule` channel (headline "Schedule — move <name>'s visit out of rain", severity `needs-you`, subject the visit, link to that visit on the dispatch schedule, `bellDefault`, `dedupeKey rain-pass:<visit_id of a grouped stop, else the row id>:<date>:<start>`), naming the service that needs dry weather (on a shared stop or a visit with add-ons, the outdoor one), the chance and the dry hour, or that there is none. The pass owns the notice from first ring to close (`docs/admin-notifications.md` section 2; no relevance class): it rings once; a later run that reads another chance or dry hour rewrites it without ringing (`refreshOnDedupe`); every run closes each standing notice whose stop is not wet at that slot any more (`closeAdminAlertKeys`, reason `no_longer_in_rain`: the forecast dried, the work is no longer outdoor, or the visit moved, was parked, cancelled, started or passed), and only an unread forecast keeps one; a closed notice rings again when its stop is wet on that slot again, at most once an ET day for one notice. At most 10 rings an ET day over all runs (`MAX_NOTICES_PER_DAY`, the budget of `docs/admin-notifications.md`, counted from the ring day each first ring or comeback stamps on its row, `metadata.rang_on`); the rest ring on a later day. A visit that starts within 2 hours is left to `storm-watch.js`. It only tells: nothing is moved and no customer is contacted. A phone-booked visit can carry both this notice and the `GATE_CALL_BOOKING_RAIN_FLAG` notice when both gates are on. Rollback: unset the variable.

Auto-dispatch conflict moves (dark): `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_CONFLICT_MOVES` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js` (`conflictMovesEnabled`; unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-09. The 04:10 run only moves a visit for a score gain, so a recurring visit that shares its hour with another customer's stop, or sits on an owner blackout day, stays there. On, `auto-dispatch/current-conflict.js` reads each evaluated visit's conflict: `closed_day` (`blackout-dates.js` `isBlackoutDate`) or `overlap` (the rebooker's read-only `probeMoveConflicts` for that date, expanded by `occupiedRows`; the visit's own group does not count, and its rows give the unit's full occupied span; the same customer's other row does not count only when it is at the SAME place — the same linked property, or the same effective premise including the unit — so a second property or a second unit in the hour IS an overlap; another technician's row is excluded only once the schedule is technician-scoped, `techScopedConfirmActive()`, and until then any overlapping row counts). A visit in conflict skips the score bar and the day-move drive floor (`move-rules.js`) and applies before ordinary route gains in pass 2; an overlap takes a free hour on the same day first, then the slot that adds the least modeled drive. A slot that adds more than `AUTO_DISPATCH_CONFLICT_MAX_ADDED_DRIVE_MINUTES` (default 15, owner 2026-10-09) is never taken: the visit stays and its audit row reads `CONFLICT_NO_NEAR_SLOT`. One exception: with `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_SHARED_MODEL` off, a visit with a live grouped sibling has no usable current detour (`detour_group_blind`), so the ceiling cannot be measured and does not apply to it; keep the shared model on for the bound to hold for every visit. A dry run recommends one visit of an overlapping pair (the other logs `CONFLICT_PARTNER_MOVES`), or both when the second would also move on the ordinary rules (that second row is an estimate scored before the first move, and says so; apply mode evaluates the visit again after the first move); a grouped visit counts as one. The closed-day read is strict here: a failed read fails that visit's evaluation, it is never read as an open day. At apply the move guard re-reads the conflict on the move transaction, holding the other stop's row, the interview's row or the closure-state lock to commit, and refuses when the conflict is gone. Every other guard is unchanged: eligibility, the 73-hour and reminder freeze, person-placed, customer-confirmed, the flex window (±5 days), portal preferences, the per-run cap and the writer's own overlap check on the destination. The audit row carries `constraints_checked.conflict` (kind, date, row ids) and reads "Moved off an overlapping stop" or "Moved off a closed day". Moves are silent like every auto-dispatch move. Rollback: unset the variable.

Auto-dispatch move proofreader (model): `MODEL_AUTO_DISPATCH_PROOFREADER` — the model of `ROUTES.autoDispatchProofreader` (default Claude Opus 5.5 since 2026-10-12, owner "go with the better agent"; Anthropic only, effort high; lane `auto_dispatch_proofreader`). Owner 2026-10-09 ("proofreader yes"): one model call reads the full customer record before an automatic move and answers allow / hold / unknown. `server/services/auto-dispatch/proofreader/record.js` builds the record with code (every stored text, email, call transcript and note written before the move, access codes redacted; a source it cannot read, a recording with no transcript, or an entry whose access-code mask also hid a time or a day (`time_masked`) makes the record incomplete); `index.js` judges the answer (a hold counts only with a quote found word for word in the entry it names; an allow on an incomplete record, a failed call or a malformed answer is unknown; unknown never reads as allow). Two callers: the nightly run behind `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_PROOFREADER` (next row) and the read-only replay `node server/scripts/auto-dispatch-proofreader-replay.js [--days N] [--limit N] [--hard-only] [--models provider:model,...]`, which runs the hard cases with a known answer (`proofreader/hard-cases.js`) and then every `changed` row of `auto_dispatch_audit_logs` in the window, each on the words that existed before that move. It moves nothing and sends nothing; its output files hold customer words, so keep `--out` outside the repository.
Website content writers (model): `MODEL_CONTENT` — the model of `TEXT_POLICIES.websiteContent` (blog-writer post drafts and idea lists, lane `blog_draft`; OpenAI `OPENAI_BALANCED` backup), the Codex remediation fix on content PRs (`content/codex-remediation.js`, lane `codex_remediation`) and the content Managed Agent configs (writer, refresher, meta rewriter, legacy content engine). Default Claude Opus 5.5 (owner 2026-10-24: "make them all claude opus 5.5"). Effort on the two direct paths follows `MODEL_ANTHROPIC_EFFORT`. A registered Managed Agent keeps the model it was registered with, so moving one also needs a `POST /v1/agents/{id}` update (done 2026-10-24: writer v3, meta rewriter v2, content engine v2; the refresher was already on Opus 5.5). Drafts written in the terminal (`GATE_CONTENT_WRITER_TERMINAL`) use the terminal session's model, not this one. Rollback: set `MODEL_CONTENT` to another Anthropic model, e.g. `claude-opus-4-8`.
AI credit key pool: `GATE_AI_CREDIT_KEYS` + `ANTHROPIC_CREDIT_KEYS` / `OPENAI_CREDIT_KEYS` (owner 2026-10-29) — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read once at boot (a flip or a key change needs a redeploy). Each Claude Max / ChatGPT Pro plan's monthly API credit lands in its own API organization, so the portal needs one key per organization. The two key variables hold comma-separated API keys of credit-only organizations (no payment method), in the order to use them; an empty entry, a duplicate or the main key itself is ignored. On, `server/services/llm/credit-key-pool.js` (installed in `server/index.js` right after `instrument.js`) wraps `globalThis.fetch` once, so every Anthropic SDK client and every raw OpenAI fetch goes through it. A call moves to a credit key only when it is a POST to `api.anthropic.com` `/v1/messages` or `/v1/messages/count_tokens`, or to `api.openai.com` chat completions, embeddings, moderations, images, audio, or `/v1/responses` with `"store":false`; it carries the main key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`); its body can be sent twice; an Anthropic body names no `file_id` or `container`; and an OpenAI body has no `encrypted_content` (encrypted reasoning only decrypts in the organization that wrote it, so the Intelligence Bar OpenAI loop and Sandy's voice relay stay on the main key for every turn). Everything else (Managed Agents sessions, files, batches, streamed bodies, other keys) stays on the main key untouched. Credit keys are tried in order, then the unchanged main-key request. A credit key is paused in memory per process: 6 h on Anthropic "credit balance is too low" / "reached your specified API usage limits" or OpenAI `insufficient_quota`; 1 h on 401; 1 h for that model only on 403, an OpenAI `model_not_found` or an Anthropic `not_found_error`; the `retry-after` time (default 60 s, cap 300 s) on any other 429. Any other answer (other 400s, 5xx, 529, a 2xx stream) goes back to the caller as-is; a network error is rethrown. Log lines `[credit-keys] ...` name keys by position only, never by value. Cost is unchanged per call (same models); the call ledger records the same model and tokens. Off, or on with no credit key = nothing wrapped, every call as before. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback = unset the gate (or the key variables) and redeploy.

Auto-dispatch move proofreader, nightly (dark): `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_PROOFREADER` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js` (`proofreaderEnabled`; unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-12 ("go with the better agent, and for moves it is unsure of moving forward create admin notifications for these"). On, the 04:10 run in apply mode asks the proofreader about each move right before the write (`auto-dispatch/proofreader/nightly.js`, pass 2 only: after every fixed rule, the road check and the per-run cap). **Allow**: the visit moves, on the slot the model read and no other (a proofread move has no `SLOT_TAKEN` fallback; a taken slot is logged `APPROVED_SLOT_TAKEN` and the next run tries again). **Hold** (`PROOFREADER_HOLD`): the visit stays; the audit row carries the verdict, never the quote. **Unknown** (`PROOFREADER_UNSURE`): the visit stays where it is booked and nobody is asked (owner 2026-10-29, "i dont want to have to approve every move"); the next run asks again. Until then an unknown a person could settle from the record (the model was unsure, or part of the record could not be read) raised one admin notice per visit and placement (key `auto-dispatch-proofreader:<visit>:<date>:<time>:<technician>`); every run now closes the ones still open. A failed model call moves nothing; so does an allow whose record changed while the model read it (the record is read again after an allow). `AUTO_DISPATCH_PROOFREADER_MAX_CALLS` (60) is the most model calls one run makes (a record that cannot be read or is too long asks nobody and spends none); and no call starts later than `AUTO_DISPATCH_PROOFREADER_DEADLINE_SECONDS` (300) into the run, because the 04:10 run holds the writer lock the 04:20 route reorder needs; past either a move is logged `PROOFREADER_NOT_ASKED` and waits. A check that broke (a failed or malformed model call, an unreadable record) moves nothing and ends the run `completed_with_errors`. **A notice a person marked done before 2026-10-29 still holds its visit**: while the visit is on that placement, no automatic move of it is asked about or made (`PROOFREADER_PERSON_HELD`). **A grouped stop (two or more open services in one visit) does not move while the gate is on** (`PROOFREADER_GROUPED_STOP`, nobody is asked, no notice; owner 2026-10-12: grouped stops are being removed). It can only stop a move, it sends the customer nothing, and a dry run does not call it. Rollback: unset the variable; the next run then closes every proofreader notice, the done ones too.
Auto-dispatch road check (dark): `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_ROAD_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js` (`roadCheckEnabled`; unset = kill). **Needs `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_SHARED_MODEL` on** (the legs it measures are that model's; with it off the road check stays off). Owner 2026-10-09 ("drive time yes"). The 04:10 run scores every slot on a straight-line drive model. On, `auto-dispatch/road-check.js` measures an ordinary move's drive saving again on Google's traffic-aware route matrix before the visit moves: the three legs the model's own detour is made of (stop before to visit, visit to stop after, and before to after), on the day the visit has and on the day it would take, at the hour of each placement. A move whose real-road saving is under `AUTO_DISPATCH_MIN_DAY_MOVE_DRIVE_SAVING_MINUTES` (6) does not happen; the next-best slot is measured instead, at most three for a visit; when all fail the audit row reads `NO_ROAD_DRIVE_SAVING` with both numbers. It can only stop a move, never cause one. Not checked: a visit that must move (no arrival time yet, or in conflict; its 15-minute ceiling stays on the model), and the legacy grouped shape. A leg Google does not answer (outage, no key, a departure not in the future, the cap spent) keeps the model's answer (`road.source: 'estimate'`). Each checked row's `routeMetrics.road` holds `saving_minutes`, `current_detour_minutes`, `candidate_detour_minutes`. Spend: one reader for the whole run (pass 2 re-asks nothing), six legs when the best slot passes, at most `AUTO_DISPATCH_ROAD_CHECK_MAX_ELEMENTS` legs a run (default 600, 0 = buy nothing), on a budget of its own (never customer booking's); the run's log line ends `road_legs=<n>`. Dry runs are checked too. Rollback: unset.
Auto-dispatch road check at apply (dark): `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_ROAD_CHECK_AT_APPLY` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js` (`roadCheckAtApply`; unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-28 (the Google cost is "way too high"). Acts only when `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_ROAD_CHECK` is on and the run applies moves; a dry run keeps today's behavior, road numbers included. Today pass 1 buys the road legs for every visit that qualifies, then the per-run change cap holds most of them (10-27: 44 moves checked, 254 legs, 34 held by the cap of 10). On, pass 1 judges on the model alone (no Google call), and pass 2 buys the road check only for a move about to be written, in its live re-evaluation (`holdBeforeRoadCheck` in `auto-dispatch/index.js`). A move the cap already holds is logged `recommended` / `MAX_CHANGES_REACHED` with no re-evaluation and no road legs. A move still needs its real-road saving to pass, so one that fails there is `NO_ROAD_DRIVE_SAVING` and takes no cap slot. Unchanged: the leg budget (`AUTO_DISPATCH_ROAD_CHECK_MAX_ELEMENTS`), fail-open on a leg Google does not answer, move order, every audit field. Rollback: unset.
Auto-dispatch arrival search: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_ARRIVAL_SEARCH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `shadow` or `true`**, read at call time (`autoDispatchArrivalSearchMode()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`, resolved once per run as `config.arrivalSearch` in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js`; any other value or unset = off, the kill). **Needs `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_SHARED_MODEL` on** (its `slot_taken` filter drops a slot the writer's one-stop-per-hour probe refuses; without it the mode reads off). Owner 2026-10-24 ("build"; scope page 58XT2mGs). The 04:10 run's candidate search (`auto-dispatch/candidate-slots.js`) asks find-time for the arrival-window engine (`findCapacitySlots`, `opts.arrivalSearch`) for its own call only: each stop on the day must still be reached inside its 2-hour promise, instead of one-hour blocks with drive time on both sides (a day of 4-5 stops read as full: 104 visits had no valid slot on Oct 24; a read-only replay of that run found 36 moves on 28 distinct hours, none refused at the write). Every booking surface keeps today's search, and `GATE_SCHEDULING_CAPACITY` stays as it is. For that call find-time passes `preserveCapacity` (the existing per-call switch older booking holds use), `planningMinutes: false` (the stops keep their window/estimate length, as the 04:20 route pass plans them; `planning_exempt` on each row), and the tech's start point; it makes no Google call (`providerTravel: false`) and offers no insertion between stops (`capacityPlacement` stays with callers that persist the route order). The score bar, drive floor, move check, road check and the writer's hour probe are unchanged. `shadow`: the run decides on today's search and also records, for each visit it leaves where it is, what the arrival search would do (`constraints_checked.arrival_search`: `would` = `move` with date, hour, technician, improvement, drive saving, or the reason it would not; `ms` = that search's own time, since a shadow night runs both searches); no road check for the shadow, nothing moves. `true`: the run searches and moves on it, in pass 1 and in pass 2's re-check. The slower search can push the move check past `AUTO_DISPATCH_PROOFREADER_DEADLINE_SECONDS`: a night where no check answered because the deadline came first now raises the check-down notice (`GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_CHECK_DOWN_NOTICE`). Rollout: shadow nights, then `true` with `AUTO_DISPATCH_MAX_CHANGES_PER_RUN=10` for a week. Rollback: unset (moves already made stay at their new hours).
Auto-dispatch day rules: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_DAY_RULES` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time (`autoDispatchDayRulesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; resolved once per run as `config.dayRules` in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js`; unset = kill). Owner 2026-10-24 ("dont skip sundays", "think sundays should be a last resort", "sundays all", "yes build the 7:30 depature, and make this ediatble in the admin portal"; decision page 4gjHYcDnhm8WUJ6Zryj3i3). **Sundays:** the 04:10 run's candidate search asks find-time for Sundays too (`includeWeekends`); `move-rules.js` ranks a Sunday slot after every qualifying Monday-Saturday slot, so a Sunday is taken only when no other day qualifies (a free hour on an overlapping visit's own day still comes first). "Skip weekends" now covers Sunday as well as Saturday, in the candidate filter and the writer's grouped-member guard (`isWeekendDay`). At most `AUTO_DISPATCH_MAX_SUNDAY_MOVES_PER_RUN` (default 2; 0 = none) visits move onto a Sunday in one apply run: past it a Sunday move is held as `SUNDAY_CAP_REACHED` (action `recommended`, before the move check), and no SLOT_TAKEN fallback slot is a Sunday; a re-time on a visit already on a Sunday does not count. **Departure:** the van leaves its start point at the Settings → Scheduling → Day start time (`server/services/scheduling/departure-time.js`, system_settings `schedule_departure_time`, a JSON "HH:MM" 06:00-08:00 in 15-minute steps, default 07:30 before any save; a broken saved value or a failed read = 08:00). Read once per run by the night tool (`config.departureMinutes`, in the run snapshot) for the arrival search (`vanDepartureMin` on the route context, capacity path only), once per run by the 04:20 route pass (`chooseWindowSafeOrder` `dayStartMin`, the stale-order baseline, `computeChronologicalRepair` and the nightly `measureDayQuality` snapshots), and by the day reports (`getScheduleQualityMeasurements` `modeledDepartureMinutes`, `analyzeGapCandidate`; the scorecard divides stops/hour by each measurement's own `assumptions.departureMinutes`, saved plans by `plannedDepartureMinutes`). No visit starts before its window opens: a gap-candidate window never opens before 08:00 from the Settings time (an explicit `departure_time` input keeps its old meaning). A stop with no window at all starts when the van arrives. Booking pages, the staff Optimize button and the Intelligence Bar route tools keep 08:00. **Staff strip:** `loadSummaryDayFacts` marks Sundays `last_resort` instead of `closed` (a closure on a Sunday is still closed); the strip offers a last-resort day only when no other day has room, and the best-times week row leaves it out. **Staff day lists:** the Reschedule window's suggested days and the Quick Move day buttons (`SmartRebooker.findRescheduleOptions`) list a Sunday after every Monday-Saturday day, on the route-checked list (`route-ranked-days.js` `sundaysLast`, checked and unverified days alike) and on the old score list, so a Sunday shows only when fewer than three other days are offered (owner 2026-10-24 "sundays all"; route-dispatcher audit 2026-10-29). Off: every reader keeps 08:00, Sundays are not searched, the strip calls Sunday closed, and the day lists rank a Sunday like any other day. Turn on together with `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_ARRIVAL_SEARCH=true` after the shadow nights. Rollback: unset (moves already made keep their new day and hour).
Auto-dispatch keeps each visit on its own technician: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_KEEP_TECH` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `autoDispatchKeepTechLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (resolved once per run as `config.keepTech` in `server/services/auto-dispatch/config.js`, carried on the run's `ctx`; unset = kill). An unassigned visit (`technician_id` NULL) is handled exactly as before, including the one-assignable-technician rule. Sends nothing to a customer. Auto-dispatch 5:00 AM catch-up run: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_CATCH_UP` — **ships DARK: strict `=== 'true'`**, read at call time via `autoDispatchCatchUpLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (the 05:00 cron in `server/services/scheduler.js`; unset = kill, the job returns before any database read). A deploy that restarts the server during the 04:10 run cuts it off (2026-09-03 and 2026-10-26: the run moved nothing, nothing re-ran it, and its `auto_dispatch_runs` row stayed `running` until the next run's 60-minute stale check). On: at 05:00 ET the job (needs `cronJobs` and `autoDispatch` on, like the 04:10 job) takes the `auto-dispatch-catch-up` lock and, inside it, the same `auto-dispatch-recurring` writer lock the 04:10 run and the 04:20 reorder use. If today (ET) has no `cron` or `catch_up` run with status `completed` or `completed_with_errors`, and no `catch_up` run at all, it first settles every `triggered_by = 'cron'` row still `running` to `failed` (a held lock means no cron run is alive), then runs the night tool once with `triggered_by = 'catch_up'`: same mode, same guard, same rules and caps as 04:10 (`server/services/auto-dispatch/catch-up.js`). At most one catch-up a day. A skipped lock or a run that is not `completed` fails the job health row `auto-dispatch-catch-up`. The 04:20 route reorder does not run again after a catch-up.
