Auto-dispatch move limit: `AUTO_DISPATCH_MAX_MOVES_PER_VISIT` — default `2`, `0` = no limit (not a gate; **live on deploy, no flag**). Owner 2026-10-09: "at most two automatic day moves for one visit, both inside the ±5-day window". `server/services/auto-dispatch/move-limit.js` counts a visit's automatic moves from the durable `reschedule_log` (rows written with `reason_code='auto_dispatch'` and `initiated_by='auto_dispatch'` where the date or window changed), never from the `auto_dispatch_change_count` stamp. Day moves, same-day re-times and forced moves all count. Read in pass 1 (one bulk read, skip `MOVE_LIMIT_REACHED` before any candidate search; an unreadable log skips every visit as `MOVE_COUNT_UNKNOWN` and ends the run `completed_with_errors`), in the pass-2 recheck, and on the move transaction (`makeMoveGuard`, and `makeMemberGuard` for grouped siblings: a unit moves only if every member is under the limit). A visit that must move (an unplaced due date, or in conflict) and is at the limit is not moved. For one in conflict, `needs-person-notice.js` raises one `schedule_conflict` admin notice per visit and date at run end (key `auto-dispatch-needs-person:<id>:<date>`); a visit with no arrival time is told by the existing recurring-placement alert (`recurring-dispatch:*`), not a second bell. The same notice covers EVERY loaded visit still in conflict (an overlap, a closed day) when the run ends, whatever path left it there: no near slot (`CONFLICT_NO_NEAR_SLOT`), no valid slot (`DRIFT_ANCHOR_STALE` included), a grouped sibling's guard, the per-run cap, a refused, failed or partial write, a dry run. The run keeps one ledger of the visits it read in conflict and decides once, at its end (`index.js` `settleConflicts`); it always reads each of those conflicts again first, so a visit that is now clear (the run's own move, its group's, the partner's, or a person's change during the run) raises nothing; the same read covers every loaded visit a guard skipped before evaluation (a freeze, a person-placed visit), a group member a partial move left behind and every visit with an open notice, so a person's own fix closes the notice. Only that final read is proof, never an earlier one in the run. A notice also closes when the visit loses its arrival time, and one key rings at most once in 24 hours. The lane spends the shared auto-dispatch ring allowance of 24 hours (`audit.ringsLeft`, 10 for all lanes and runs together), soonest date first; a standing notice is refreshed free. A notice closes (title `Visit placement alert resolved`) when its visit is cancelled or leaves the date, or when a run has proof the conflict is gone: it read the visit with the conflict read on and found none (at evaluation, or at the end-of-run re-read). A visit the run skipped, failed on or never loaded keeps its notice; a fixed visit that conflicts again reopens it. Same change: a visit that overlaps another stop also gets every whole-hour start on its own date from the slot finder itself (`find-time.js` `everyStepStart`, one technician, one date), so each added hour has passed the finder's drive, time-off and closed-day checks. Same change: a same-day re-time must also save the drive floor (`AUTO_DISPATCH_MIN_DAY_MOVE_DRIVE_SAVING_MINUTES`) and its gain leaves out the default-time credit; the closed-day reads on the auto-dispatch path (`current-conflict.js`, the destination-day filter in `find-time.js`, the rebooker's commit check for `initiated_by='auto_dispatch'`) are strict: an unreadable list blocks instead of reading "open" (`blackout-dates.js` `{ strict: true }`). Rollback: set `AUTO_DISPATCH_MAX_MOVES_PER_VISIT=0` (the closed-day and same-day changes have no switch).

Auto-dispatch re-date anchor: `GATE_AUTO_DISPATCH_REDATE_ANCHOR` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`/`1`/`on`**, read at call time (unset = live kill; `server/services/auto-dispatch/route-tiers.js` `loadAnchorMap` / `resolveAnchor`). Owner 2026-10-22 (auto-dispatch audit D2: "the new date becomes the planned date"). The ±5-day drift budget is measured from the visit's date before its first auto move. On, a visit that something other than auto-dispatch re-dated after an auto move (a person, a script, another automatic mover) has its budget restarted at that date: the current date when the visit is no longer where the newest auto move left it, or the origin of a later auto move that started somewhere else. Off, the old date stays the anchor, so a visit re-dated more than 10 days away gets no day moves (`DRIFT_ANCHOR_STALE`) and one re-dated 6 to 10 days away can only move back toward the old date. Read only from the tool's own move rows in `reschedule_log` (written inside every auto move's transaction); an incomplete history (an audit move with no such row, or a row without a date) restarts nothing. A visit a person placed stays protected first (`PERSON_PLACED`, `eligibility.js`), and the per-visit move limit (`AUTO_DISPATCH_MAX_MOVES_PER_VISIT`) still counts every auto move. Sends nothing to a customer.

Lead call-reply ring (owner 2026-10-24, "ring my cell, like we had before"): `GATE_LEAD_CALL_REPLY_RING` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('leadCallReplyRing')` in `ringForCallReply` (`server/services/lead-call-reply-ring.js`), which the SMS webhook calls after the ack for every inbound text the intake machine did not consume. On, a bare CALL (`parseCallTextReply`) between 8 AM and 8 PM ET rings Adam's cell from the lead-alert line (`INTERNAL_ALERT_CALLER_ID`) with the press-1 bridge (`placeBridgeCall`, `call_log.source` `lead-call-reply-ring`): "{First} asked for a call back. Calling {First}. Press 1 to connect." Press 1 dials the lead from their home line. The staff leg rings 20 s, so the cell's voicemail does not answer first. It rings only for a `+1` ten-digit sender, and only when this phone got a "Reply CALL" text in the last 7 days with a real Twilio sid and no failed/undelivered/canceled status, the customer row is not in `active_customer`/`won`/`at_risk`, no ring went to the phone in 24 h, and no outbound call went to it in 10 min; `lead_intake_status` is not read. A ring that ends without press 1 (no `bridged_at`), a call Twilio refused outright (including 429), or an uncertain create that still has no CallSid 3 minutes later (in-process check), raises one `lead` bell through `raiseAdminAlert`: "Leads — call {Full Name} back", why "Missed call request: {First} replied CALL to our lead text and nobody pressed 1.", linked to the lead, done when the lead is contacted. It is claimed by `metadata.missed_bell_at`, tried 3 times over ~12 s, and the claim is released when no try lands; the generic Twilio failure bell does not fire for these rings. A night CALL and any TEXT do nothing here. Off, nothing rings and the bridge call is byte-identical. Rollback: unset `GATE_LEAD_CALL_REPLY_RING`.

Lead call/text follow-up (owner 2026-10-24, wording approved word for word): `GATE_LEAD_CALL_TEXT_FOLLOWUP` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('leadCallTextFollowup')` in `handleLeadReply` (`server/services/lead-call-text-followup.js`), which the SMS webhook calls after the ack beside the CALL-reply ring. Same lead rule as the ring (`leadTextBlocker`: a `+1` sender who got our "Reply CALL" text in 7 days and is not `active_customer`/`won`/`at_risk`). A bare TEXT, at any hour, gets "Great, we can handle it by text! What service(s) are you interested in?" and a NULL or `awaiting_address` `lead_intake_status` is set to `awaiting_service` (a drafted quote is left alone; only once the question sent), and an open or booked call request for the phone is cancelled. A bare CALL from 8 PM to 8 AM ET gets "Got it! What time tomorrow works best for us to call you?" (never "closed"); the lead's next text, read by `parseCallTime`, books the first free 15-minute slot at or after that time (8:00 AM to 7:45 PM, one booked call per slot) and sends "You're all set. We'll call you tomorrow at 10:00 AM." ("today" when the answer came after midnight). An unclear answer, a time outside 8 AM-8 PM, no free slot, or one of our texts that did not send raises one `lead` needs-you bell instead. A daytime CALL is left to the ring and closes an open time ask. One follow-up of each kind per phone per 24 h; rows in `lead_callback_requests`. Entry point `lead_call_text_followup` is a customer action in the send window. A booked call (part 2b, `server/services/lead-callback-scheduler.js`, every minute under `runExclusive`): 15 minutes before, the owner gets a `lead` bell "Leads — call {Name} at 10:00 AM" and the lead gets "Hi {First}, Adam from Waves here. I'll call you in about 15 minutes." (never before 8 AM); at the time, Adam's cell gets the CALL ring's own press-1 ring (`placeRing`), one lead ring at a time, and a ring more than 30 minutes late becomes a bell instead; at 8 AM, a time question never answered raises "Leads — call {Name} back" and nothing rings. Each step is claimed once on the row (`reminded_at`, `ring_claimed_at`, `no_answer_at`). Rollback: unset `GATE_LEAD_CALL_TEXT_FOLLOWUP`.

Lead repeat form (owner 2026-10-24, "A: both parts"): `GATE_LEAD_REPEAT_FORM` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('leadRepeatForm')` in `isRepeatFormFromLead` (`server/routes/lead-webhook.js`). A web quote form whose phone matches a live customers row takes the existing-customer branch: a note ("Form submission (existing customer)"), no lead row, no text, no draft and no new-lead bell. On, when that row is still a lead (`pipeline_stage` new_lead, contacted, estimate_sent, estimate_viewed, follow_up or lost): an open intake state (`awaiting_service`, `awaiting_address`) is kept instead of cleared, so the lead's next bare CALL / TEXT still gets its note and label and a service reply still drafts a quote through `lead-intake.js`; and one Leads alert rings through `raiseAdminAlert` (category `lead`): "Leads — call {Name} about the quote form", "{First} sent the quote form; on file as a lead since {Mon D}.", linked to the lead the form attached to, else the newest live lead, else the customer. One open row per lead (dedupe `lead-repeat-form:<customerId>`, open rows only); each form is a new `dedupeVersion`, so a form while the row is open rings it again and moves its time to that form (`refreshOnDedupe` + `bumpOnRefresh`). The relevance sweep (`server/services/admin-alert-relevance.js`, class `lead_repeat_form`, every 10 minutes) closes it once, after its latest form, a staff text reached the customer (`deliveredTexts`, message types `manual` / `ai_approved` / `ai_revised`), an estimate was handed off to them (`handedOffWithin` + the estimate-ownership fence, never `sent_at` alone: a suppressed send stamps it), a live visit was booked for them, or the lead was deleted. A call alone does not close it (a dialer bridge row is written before Twilio dials and does not prove the lead answered), and a lead marked handled before the form does not close it; a person marks it done. Quotes, bookings and texts are read for the alert's own customer, with or without a lead row. That close is final, and the lead's next form rings a fresh row. A second submit inside the 5-minute duplicate window keeps the state and rings nothing. Any other stage (a customer) or intake state: cleared and note only, as before. Nothing is sent to the lead; an address ask still parks for approval. An alert failure is logged by customer id and the form response is unchanged. Off, byte-identical to before. Rollback: unset `GATE_LEAD_REPEAT_FORM`.

Lead draft real size (owner 2026-10-24, "A, my recommendation: build the fix"): `GATE_LEAD_DRAFT_PROPERTY_LOOKUP` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`server/config/feature-gates.js` `leadDraftPropertyLookupLive`, read by `server/services/lead-draft-measurements.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Does nothing while `GATE_LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTOMATION` is off (no lead drafts). On, a website lead draft whose form and customer row give no home or lot size is no longer priced on the 2,000 / 8,000 sq ft defaults when the county record has the real ones: the webhook reads the property-lookup cache before its phone lock (caller `lead_draft`, cache-only, writes nothing) and the draft builder (`buildAutomatedLeadDraftEstimate`, `server/services/lead-estimate-automation.js`) prices on it, as does a triage rebuild (which reads the cache itself); a draft still on the defaults gets one live property lookup in the background after the estimate row commits (same caller, scheduled from `server/routes/lead-webhook.js`; the website's answer never waits), and the draft is re-priced through the same builder with the submission's own inputs. Sizes count only when both home and lot are county-assessed (`resolvePropertyFacts`, source `county_assessed`) for a record labeled `Single Family` (the raw label: the pricing normalizer reads a county `Multifamily` building as `single_family`) at an address with no unit, the lookup did not land on a different premise (wrong-premise flag or snapped record), the parcel is not new construction, and home 400–10,000 / lot 1,000–435,600 sq ft; anything else keeps the defaults. The re-price writes only a draft nobody has written since it was created (`updated_at` = `created_at`, same `estimateEditVersion` before and after the lookup, under `FOR UPDATE`), never one archived, sent or price-locked; a staff member with the draft open gets the existing stale-version refusal on send or save. The webhook's AI triage rebuild of the same draft (it rewrites a generic service label) waits up to 3 minutes for that in-flight lookup (`pendingLeadMeasurements`) and prices with its sizes, so a triage write that lands first never discards them. A county-sized draft carries `sizeSource: 'county_assessed'`, `measurements` and the review reason `property_measurements_from_county` (in place of `property_measurements_defaulted` on the intake record too), so the auto-send lane still parks it unless `LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND_ALLOWED_REVIEW_REASONS` names that reason. The sizes stay on the draft's engine input: nothing is written to the customer or property rows. Logs `[lead-draft-measurements] estimate <id>: <outcome>` (repriced, no_trusted_size, changed, not_rebuilt, lookup_failed), ids only. Off: drafts price on the defaults with `property_measurements_defaulted`, as before.

Lead estimate auto-send created-after cutoff (fix-first, owner 2026-10-27, "OK DO THIS"): `GATE_LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND` — **off unless exactly `true`**, and the 5-minute job in `server/services/scheduler.js` also needs `GATE_LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTOMATION`; with it off nothing runs and nothing changed. On, the job (`processLeadEstimateAutoSendBatch`, `server/services/lead-estimate-auto-send.js`) sends up to `LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND_LIMIT` (10) website-lead draft estimates per scan, oldest first, once a draft is `LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND_DELAY_MINUTES` (5) old. **A draft now qualifies only if it was created strictly after `LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND_CREATED_AFTER`**, a required setting: ISO 8601 with an explicit zone (`2026-10-28T12:00:00Z` or `…-04:00`); set it to the moment the owner turns the gate on. **Fail closed:** unset, blank or unparseable (no zone, date only, not a date) = the scan reads no candidates, sends nothing, and logs `[lead-estimate-auto-send] sending nothing: LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND_CREATED_AFTER is not set` (or `is not an ISO 8601 timestamp…`) once per change. The cutoff is a `created_at > cutoff` bound in the candidate query plus an eligibility check (`created_before_cutoff` / `created_after_cutoff_unset`); a cutoff skip is never stamped blocked, so lowering the cutoff later re-opens those drafts. `GET /api/admin/estimates/lead-auto-send/preview` (read-only) applies the same cutoff from the environment only (no query override) and reports `config.createdAfter` / `config.createdAfterProblem`, so its `wouldSend` rows are exactly who would get a text. Every other rule is unchanged: source `lead_webhook`, generated draft, SERVER price stamp, not quote-required, no authored proposal, a phone or email, every review reason on `LEAD_ESTIMATE_AUTO_SEND_ALLOWED_REVIEW_REASONS` (empty by default; the production value still names `property_measurements_defaulted`, which is the owner's to change before the flip), delay, limit. Stale-claim recovery is not a send and still runs when the cutoff is missing.

Text-thread lead reader (owner 2026-10-23): `GATE_SMS_LEAD_EXTRACTION` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('smsLeadExtraction')` in the 5-minute cron (`server/services/scheduler.js`) and in `sweepSmsLeadCandidates` (`server/services/sms-lead-extraction.js`). On, every 5 minutes the sweep takes each number whose newest customer-facing inbound text (`inbound`, `domain_lead`, `van_lead`; not the tech line or internal alert line) is from the last 24 hours and at least 5 minutes old, and that has no customer record and no lead except one this reader made. US/Canada (`+1`) numbers only; phones match on the full digits with or without the leading 1, never on the last 10 digits alone, so an international sender never shares a US contact's thread. One model call (lane `sms_lead_extraction`, policy `routineAnswer`) reads the last 48 hours of the thread (30 texts at most). A new service request for a service Waves offers, at confidence 0.8 or more, goes through `createLeadFromExtraction` with `channel: 'sms'` (lead_type `inbound_sms`, first_contact_channel `sms`; the writer fills empty fields only) and raises one Leads bell per lead (dedupe `sms-lead:<leadId>`, rewritten in place when a later text adds a name, address or email). A thread a spam screen silenced, a known customer, someone else's lead and any other kind are recorded and skipped. Each read is one `sms_lead_extractions` row, unique on number + newest inbound text; a failed read retries up to 3 times. A lead written before its bell was raised stays `created_unrung` / `updated_unrung` and the next sweep raises it (same dedupe key, 3 tries, then `bell_failed`). The writer re-checks at write time and writes nothing when a customer or another lead (any phone format) now holds the number. Nothing is ever sent to the texter. Off, the cron returns before taking its lock and nothing changes. Rollback: unset `GATE_SMS_LEAD_EXTRACTION`; leads already made stay.

Reply outcome signals (owner 2026-10-24): `GATE_SMS_REPLY_OUTCOMES` — **off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('smsReplyOutcomes')` in the 30-minute cron (`server/services/scheduler.js`, :13 and :43) and in `sweepReplyOutcomes` (`server/services/sms-reply-outcomes.js`). On, each outbound reply to a customer text (`manual`, `ai_approved`, `ai_revised`, `ai_autosent`, `ai_gratitude`; US/Canada numbers only, matched on the full digits) gets one `sms_reply_outcomes` row 72 hours after it was sent, up to 200 per tick, 30 days back. The row records what the customer did next: a confused or repeated text within 30 minutes (small regex, no model), an opt-out within 72 hours (the opt-out detector), an inbound call within 1 hour, a thanks / ok / thumbs-up as the first text or tapback within 4 hours (the courtesy detector), or silence; AI replies also carry `draft_id` and `prompt_version`. No message text is stored or logged. `summarizeReplyOutcomes` and `ops/agents/sms-reply-outcomes-report.js` (read-only) print counts and rates per prompt version and per reply source. Measurement only: it sends, changes and holds nothing. Off, the cron returns before taking its lock. Rollback: unset `GATE_SMS_REPLY_OUTCOMES`; rows already written stay.

SMS prompt patches (owner 2026-09-27 "the texting AI should improve with NO human approval steps", 2026-10-24 "do all"): `GATE_SMS_PROMPT_AUTOPROMOTE` — **three modes, read at call time** through `smsPromptAutopromoteMode()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`): unset or anything else = off, `observe` = record-only (the drafter stays unpatched), `true` = the ONE active row of `sms_prompt_patches` applies. With `true` and `GATE_SMS_REAL_ANSWERS` on, the drafter (`server/services/sms-shadow-drafter.js`) appends the active block under `LEARNED REPLY RULES` and every patched draft stamps `prompt_version` with one extra uppercase letter (`sms_prompt_patches.version_tag`, handed out once per base prompt identity, never reused, 26 per base; for example `house_voice_v12_real_answers26_n+bcA`), so graduation cohorts and exam coverage restart on the patched version, and the longest identity (39 characters before the letter) still fits 40. A patch applies only on the base prompt identity it was examined on; one whose tagged identity would pass 40 characters, or whose stored block fails its hash or the text guards in `server/services/sms-prompt-patch.js` (no prices, discounts, promised visits, refunds or credits, complaints, billing, chemical, medical, legal or cancellation topics, no instruction-shaped text), is not applied. The snapshot of the active row loads at boot and is re-read every minute (`startPatchRefresh`, started before the `GATE_CRON_JOBS` early return in `server/services/scheduler.js`). The sealed exam (`server/services/sms-sealed-eval.js`) can draft a run with a candidate block under the candidate's own identity (`sms_sealed_eval_runs.prompt_patch_id`; exam-only, the live drafter never sees a candidate), and an automatic baseline never picks such a run. No active patch, or a mode other than `true` = prompt and version byte-identical to today. Daily 6:12 AM ET in `observe` or `true` (`server/services/sms-prompt-autopromote.js`; off returns before taking a lock): the newest pending `prompt_discipline` proposal on the live prompt version (failure modes a prompt rule can fix, never the money or hand-off ones; 21 days old at most) becomes ONE candidate rule. One cheap model call distills it, and the same guards screen it; a refused rule is stored `rejected` so the proposal is not tried again. One candidate at a time, at most one new candidate a week; in `true` a new rule stacks on the active patch's rules (5 at most). **Exam runs spend real LLM API calls**: at most one candidate exam a week, never above the nightly sweep's cap (`SEALED_EXAM_AUTO_MAX_ITEMS`, 150 active items; a resume of a paid run is exempt) and never under 20 items; the sealed exam (anthropic leg) drafts, verifies and judges every active frozen item WITH the candidate block, plus a baseline run of the current prompt when none is under 3 days old; a failed sitting is resumed and the second failure rejects the candidate. The bar: 20 or more items pair, unsafe verdicts do not rise net of improvements (so no McNemar regression), the paired mean overall score gains 0.2 and actions 0.1, and both runs share one model and voice profile. Every step writes `sms_prompt_patch_events` (numbers and codes only). In `observe` the decision is only recorded; a would-promote decision is acted on if the gate flips to `true` within 14 days, then expires so the loop moves on. In `true` a candidate that clears the bar goes live at once: activation re-checks that its parent is still the active patch and that its base identity, exam model and voice profile still match the live ones, retires the previous active patch (one active at a time) and raises one admin bell (area System, category `agents`, `bellDefault` so it rings unless the owner silences the category). Daily 6:42 AM ET the rollback monitor (database reads only) retires the active patch, and puts its parent back, when live judged drafts (read with graduation's judge ruler), `sms_reply_outcomes` (confusion, opt-outs) or a sealed exam on the live version (20 or more items on both runs, compared only when graded by one judge ruler) get worse past set margins over a minimum sample; a base identity change retires it without restoring a parent; each rollback raises one admin bell. Auto-send is off in production, so an active patch changes the drafts a person reviews. Rollback: unset the gate or set it to `observe` (the prompt returns to today's at once); a bad row can also be retired with `UPDATE sms_prompt_patches SET status = 'retired' WHERE status = 'active'` (the drafter drops it within a minute).

Unverified lead hold (owner 2026-10-04): `GATE_LEAD_UNVERIFIED_HOLD` — **default ON: on unless exactly `false`**, read through `isEnabled('leadUnverifiedHold')` in `server/routes/lead-webhook.js`; it only acts while `GATE_LEAD_TURNSTILE` is enforcing. ON: a lead form that posts to `/api/leads` with no Turnstile token (the visitor's background check did not finish in time), whose token fields are genuinely absent (not a non-string value) and whose browser-set Origin or Referer header names a fleet site (`SPOKE_SITE_KEYS`), is held by `server/services/lead-unverified-hold.js`: one customer-less `leads` row (`extracted_data.stage = 'lead_webhook_unverified'`, `first_contact_channel 'form_unverified'`; `phone` and `email` stay NULL and the submitted contact is kept in `extracted_data.unverified_contact` and on the activity note, so no audience, spam-blocker or consent reader treats it as a known contact; the office adds them after confirming with the person), one lead activity and one Leads bell, and the form gets its normal success answer. A held lead creates no customer, no draft estimate, no text, no email, no Lead Response Agent run and no bridge call; a repeat from the same phone inside 24 hours adds no row and no bell. The visitor's message is kept on the lead (`extracted_data.message`, and quoted on the lead activity). A token Cloudflare rejected, an oversized token and a tokenless post with a foreign or absent Origin/Referer still get the 403, and so does a submission with no usable phone. OFF (`false`): every enforced Turnstile failure answers 403 and saves nothing, as before. Kill: set `GATE_LEAD_UNVERIFIED_HOLD=false`; leads already held stay on the Leads page.

Service report plan + upcoming visits merged, with a Reschedule button (owner 2026-10-06; `server/services/service-report/report-data.js` and `client/src/pages/ReportViewPage.jsx`): `GATE_REPORT_PLAN_RESCHEDULE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`reportPlanRescheduleLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). It only acts when `GATE_REPORT_UPCOMING_VISITS` is on, which supplies the visits. On: `upcomingVisitsCard` on the live `/api/reports/:token/data` payload carries `merged: true` and each visit carries `rescheduleUrl` (the visit's self-serve `/reschedule/:token` short link from `buildRescheduleLink(id, { customerId, reuseExisting: true })`, reused so a repeat view makes no new short-link row; `null` when the visit is too close to move, no link applies, or the build throws). The report page then shows ONE "Your plan" section (member line, visits-completed line, the upcoming visits each with a Reschedule button, the between-visits line) instead of two cards; with no plan summary the section is titled "Your upcoming visits". The link is a bearer credential: anyone holding the report can move that visit, the same class as the report link itself. The field exists only on the live view (never the `/ask` build, PDF, static or text-preview renders). OFF: the payload has no `merged` and no `rescheduleUrl`, and the page keeps the two separate sections. Rollback: unset `GATE_REPORT_PLAN_RESCHEDULE`. Sends nothing to a customer.
Lawn report clarity (owner 2026-10-08; `server/services/service-report/report-data.js`): `GATE_LAWN_REPORT_CLARITY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`lawnReportClarityLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). One gated change left on a lawn report: "Your plan" on a LAWN report: `upcomingVisitsCard` (needs `GATE_REPORT_UPCOMING_VISITS`; merged into the plan section with `GATE_REPORT_PLAN_RESCHEDULE`) lists ONE visit, the next upcoming lawn visit at the report's property, with its Reschedule button when eligible. With no upcoming lawn visit the card is `{ visits: [] }` and the plan section names no next visit, never another line's visit. Other service lines are unchanged. OFF: payloads and pages are byte-identical to before. Rollback: unset `GATE_LAWN_REPORT_CLARITY`. Sends nothing to a customer. The ruling's watering half is PERMANENT and reads no gate (owner 2026-10-09, "permanent code change, no gate"; `server/services/service-report/{lawn-watering-instruction,report-data,lawn-report-lead}.js`, `server/services/lawn-fast-complete.js`, `client/src/components/report/lawnV2/LawnReportV2.jsx`): a water-in instruction BUILT AT COMPLETION (the build that is then frozen under `structured_notes.lawnWateringFreeze`, and the Fast Complete preview of it) for a customer with no irrigation head type and no measured rate on file (the `generic` basis only) states the amount and no minutes: "Water in today’s treatment with about ½ inch by Fri 8 PM." then "Run it even if it is not your usual day." (hold-then-water-in: "After that, water in today’s treatment with about ½ inch by …"); the instruction records `amountOnly: true`. Hold text, and the `measured`, `head_type`, `mixed_heads` and `unknown_heads` bases (minutes from the customer's own portal setup), are unchanged. An instruction already frozen renders as written, and a render that has to regenerate (nothing frozen) prints the generic minutes as before, so the lawn PDF cache key is unchanged. The live banner adds `banner.setupLine` ("Add your sprinkler setup and we’ll give you minutes for each zone.", a link to the portal property tab) under a frozen `amountOnly` water-in or hold-then-water-in; it is live-view only (deleted by `stripLiveOnlyScheduleFields`, never in `lines`, so the PDF, the watering text, the hero task and Ask Waves do not carry it).

Waves Assessment Fast Complete (owner 2026-10-09; `client/src/components/tech/FastCompleteAssessmentSheet.jsx`, `client/src/lib/assessment-fast-complete.js`, `client/src/lib/dispatchCompletionRouting.js`): `GATE_ASSESSMENT_FAST_COMPLETE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`assessmentFastCompleteLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: the schedule payload (`GET /api/admin/schedule` day and week rows, `loadProjectCompletionContextByServiceId` in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js`) carries `assessmentFastCompleteEnabled: true` for a visit whose completion profile service key is the assessment key (`ASSESSMENT_SERVICE_KEY` in `server/services/assessment-booking.js`; no profile or a failed profile read is never flagged), and admin Dispatch opens the one-screen sheet for it instead of the full form (`fastCompleteSheetFor` returns `"assessment"`, after the lawn sheet). The sheet asks for a talk note (with the mic), photos (staged by the photo manager and promoted at completion), how it went (warm, cold or lost, and why when lost) and what is recommended (the interest chips of `ConsultationOutcomeSheet.jsx`, whose options and payload builder it imports), and the $75 inspection credit toggle only where the full form shows it (inspection profile, `inspectionCreditAvailable`, profile read answered). Complete needs a note and an outcome pick. It also shows an optional "Call back on" date (`followUpApplies`, `followUpPayload` and the blank-date default of `ConsultationOutcomeSheet.jsx`; none for a lost outcome) and the customer's estimate, read-only and never a price input (owner 2026-10-09: the estimate sets the price): whether the estimate went out and when ("Estimate sent Oct 3", "Estimate draft, not sent yet"), with NO amount (the stored totals are annualized accounting figures, not the price a per-application or one-time-option estimate states, and no single function states that price), and an "Open estimate" link to the staff Estimates page (`adminEstimateHref`), or "No estimate yet" with a "Create estimate" link. Both links render only for a login that can reach `/admin/estimates` under the admin shell's own rule (server-returned role, `isPathAdminOnly`); a technician sees the line without a link. The line is read again when the tab is shown or focused again (`useVisiblePageRefresh`), so an estimate made or sent in the other tab appears without closing the sheet; nothing typed is touched. The estimate comes from one new read, `GET /api/admin/consultations/:id/estimate` (`server/services/assessment-estimate-summary.js`; 404 while this gate is off, same own-visit rule as the outcome read, no estimate token returned; the estimate's id and number go to an admin only, a technician's answer names no estimate): the estimate linked to the visit by `estimate_data.scheduled_service_id`, the visit's `source_estimate_id`, or the estimate the estimate-sent sweep pairs with it (`estimateForAssessment`); the visit must be a Waves Assessment (`isAssessmentBooking`; any other visit is 404, for admins too) and the route is on the technician own-visits allowlist (`server/middleware/technician-scope.js`); the current estimate is judged as the customer payload judges it, the call-side verdict first (`callSideBlockForEstimateData`) and then `isEstimateCustomerViewable` (archived, held, expired, or past `expires_at` is never the price; an unsent draft counts for staff; declined does not), the sent date is the last real handoff (`latestHandoffAt`, so a suppressed send reads "Not sent yet"), and more than one live candidate shows nothing. The sheet never writes the estimate's figure into the outcome row. The completion is still ONE write: the read of the visit rides the `POST /api/admin/dispatch/:id/complete` body as `consultationOutcome` (the payload `ConsultationOutcomeSheet.jsx` builds; a recorded soft quote and follow-up date ride through unchanged; a converted consultation sends none), next to `{ visitOutcome: 'completed', technicianNotes, offerInspectionCredit (only when its toggle was shown), sendCompletionSms: false, requestReview: false, expectedVisit }`. `completeScheduledService` records it through `recordOutcome` inside its own transaction, under the visit lock it already holds, after its `expectedVisit` check (`server/services/completion-consultation-outcome.js`), so the read commits and rolls back with the completion; the outcome rules are `recordOutcome`'s own, except that the arrival-window refusal is skipped on this path (the technician closing the visit is the stronger fact; a future calendar day, a dead status and an unassigned technician are still refused, and the office route is unchanged). A consultation that converted (won) keeps its read and the completion goes on. The field is accepted only for a completed assessment visit while the gate is live, else 422 `consultation_outcome_not_allowed` and nothing is written; the server's `internal_only` posture is unchanged (no products, no rating, no texts). A visit with companions, a grouped stop or visit closeout, a closed visit, a visit returning from the payment flow and a week-list row with no `propertyId` key keep the full form; the sheet's Full form button covers the incomplete and no-show outcomes. OFF (unset or any other value): the flag is always `false`, the assessment opens the full form, and no request differs from before. Rollback: unset the variable.

Service report Ask Waves AI answers (owner 2026-10-05, "use sonnet 5.5"; `server/services/service-report/report-ask-ai.js`, called by `POST /api/reports/:token/ask`): `GATE_REPORT_ASK_AI` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`reportAskAiLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: the route still builds the fixed-rule answer (`routeServiceReportQuestion`), then asks Claude Sonnet 5.5 to write the answer from a fact sheet built from the report data: service, date, technician first name, weather, pest pressure label, the customer's concern, the reviewed report sections, every recorded finding (up to 200), the serviced-area labels (never on a pest report), each applied product's name, active ingredient, approved plain wording (`report_copy`: how it works, "labeled for N+ pests", pets and kids), label precaution and re-entry text (fixed re-entry minute figures stripped, compliance screen applied), inside or outside from the recorded application area (`shared/treatment-area-scopes.json` plus the Fast Complete "Inside" / "Outside" / "Garage" chips), the re-entry status (never the appointment). A question that names one product gets only that product. The fact sheet also carries the Waves summary (headline and body) when the report has no summary text, never the technician recommendations (typed text that can hold a customer's name). The model never receives application rates, totals, units, EPA numbers, per-product target pests or prices. Privacy: the question and every free-text string of the fact sheet (report sections, findings, summary, concern, required lines, product wording) pass through one scrub (`scrubFreeText`, applied to the whole sheet in `scrubFacts`) that masks phone numbers, emails, access codes, a house number before a street (up to six words and any USPS Publication 28 street type, any case; the street name itself passes), lockbox and keypad shorthand ("lockbox 42") and any digit run of 3 or more. Only the fixed company and contact lines, the calendar dates and the product names skip it. The scrub cannot detect a customer's name written in prose, or a street name without a number and suffix; those can still reach the model in report text. The answer is 1 to 4 plain sentences and is screened (no "safe" in any form, "non-toxic", "harmless", "free", prices, guarantees, amounts, percentages, EPA, links, another phone number, a product's target pest the customer did not name (singular or plural), amounts, prices and product counts spelled as words such as "ninety dollars" or "twelve bait stations", plus result promises and friendly-safety claims, plus the shared owner report-writer screen `writerRulesRejection` called with its `skip` option so the re-entry, timeframe, date, gauge and active-ingredient rules a short answer to a question needs are left out, plus the report copy guards: `validateCustomerCopy`, `findBannedCustomerCopy`, `complianceLanguageIssues`). Model path: `MODELS.TEXT_POLICIES.reportAsk` through `dispatchWithFallback` (Anthropic leg `MODEL_REPORT_ASK`, default `claude-sonnet-5-5`, effort low; OpenAI backup leg `MODEL_OPENAI_REPORT_WRITER`), switchboard lane `report_ask`, one call-ledger row per leg. Budget about 8 s for the whole chain, first leg capped at 5 s. A failure, timeout, empty or rejected answer returns the fixed-rule answer; the reply shape `{ answer }` and the recorded `report_question_asked` event (`question_length` and `topic` only) do not change, and the question text is never stored or logged. Each AI answer is one model call behind the existing `/api/reports` limiter (20 requests a minute per IP) and a daily paid-call budget (`reportAskBudgetFor` in `server/routes/reports-public.js`): 40 model answers for a report and 120 for an IP in 24 hours. It is one atomic, shared reservation: before a model call a transaction takes an advisory lock for the report and one for the IP hash, counts the last 24 hours of `report_ask_model_call` rows in `service_report_events`, and writes this call's row when both are under their cap, so every replica shares the count, a restart keeps it and concurrent requests cannot share the last slot (no migration; `event_name` is free text and readers filter by name). It is taken only when a call is about to reach the model; past it the fixed-rule answer stands, with no 429. If the transaction fails, the call is not made and the fixed-rule answer stands (fail closed). Off = the fixed-rule answer alone and no model call, except for the always-on symptom and exposure answer: a question that reports a symptom, an ingestion or eye/skin contact ("the spray made me dizzy", "my dog ate the bait") gets one fixed Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) / 911 / veterinarian answer on every report whether this gate is on or off (`medicalExposureAnswer`, checked in the route before the gate and before any model call; owner-approved copy). A question that mentions spray plus a person, a pet or a body part from the cue list (`exposureSafetyLine`) and no symptom keeps its normal answer with a fixed Poison Control line in front, gate on or off (owner 2026-10-05, option A). Customer-visible text, so flip it only after the owner has read sample answers (`node scripts/dev/report-ask-prompt.js <report-data.json> "<question>"` prints the exact prompt, the topic, the `requiredLines`, why the question would skip the model if it would, and the fixed-rule `ruleAnswer` for a saved report). Scope (narrowed 2026-10-05): the AI answers only Pest, Lawn and Tree & Shrub reports (`data.serviceLine` is `pest`, `lawn` or `tree_shrub`), on the `applied`, `findings`, `summary` and `unrouted` topics only: `next_visit`, `next_steps`, `reentry`, `watering` and `results` keep the fixed answer, and so does any question about results, scores, trends, pest pressure or weather in other words (owner 2026-10-08, "fixed answers"), and never on a photo, blog-card, lawn-size, grass-type, legacy lawn progress, mowing-hold or (lawn and Tree & Shrub) product-location question (that text is not on the sheet, and footage never reaches an answer); care-permission questions ("can I mow now?") count as `next_steps`, and re-entry keeps the fixed answer because it is the safety instruction word for word (Codex security P1 #5964 r59). Next-visit questions keep the fixed-rule answer, and an AI answer may not state a calendar date, weekday, clock time, month or relative day of its own (required lines keep theirs; "today", the visit itself, and "this week" are allowed). An answer with required lines may not grant unconditional permission on their subject ("pets can go out right away"). Pest names are checked against the canonical target vocabulary (`server/config/treatment-target-vocabulary.js`). Every number the model writes must be a fact-sheet number of the same kind (a score out of 100, an inch figure). While watering is held, no model sentence may tell the customer to water. Termite, rodent, mosquito and specialty reports, any report a typed snapshot drives (`data.typedReport`) and any report with a customer-visible companion section (`data.companionReports`) keep the fixed-rule answer with no model call, because those pages have more than one source of truth (the reconciled termite dashboard, count-bearing results, typed detail fields, companion sections) that the fact sheet does not reproduce. The check is `ruleAnswerReason` in `report-ask-ai.js`, called at the top of `answerReportQuestionWithAI`. Required lines (owner 2026-10-05, "ok go"): the fixed-rule answer for a question states recorded customer instructions word for word (a lawn watering hold or water-in task and the weekly plan, a pet precaution and the ready-at summary, the once-dry line, technician recommendations, the rinse caution). `routeServiceReportQuestion` returns them as `requiredLines` entries `{ text, source }`, collected by the same rule functions that build the rule answer (`answerReentry`, `answerNextSteps`, `answerFindings`, the two watering answers and the plan branch), so there is no second derivation. `source` is set where the rule function collects the line, never guessed from its words: `system` for text the portal wrote from a template or a product record (the pet and re-entry summaries, the rinse caution, the watering aftercare and weekly-plan text), `tech` for anything a person typed or approved (technician recommendations, the primary next step, a finding's recommendation, lawn recommendation cards). The default is `tech`. Technician free text rule: if any required line for the question is `tech`, the AI skips the model and the customer gets the fixed-rule answer, because a customer's name in prose cannot be detected and the line must be repeated word for word. They go to the model as `required_lines` and the answer screen rejects any answer in which a line is not one whole sentence of the answer, word for word (whitespace and curly quotes aside; several-sentence lines as that run of whole sentences), or in which the sentence just before it ends with a colon, or which holds a dismissal anywhere, before or after the line (ignore, disregard, not true, no longer, outdated, you can skip). A required line that itself trips the screen (an em dash, "safe", a percent sign, a fixed re-entry minute figure) keeps the fixed-rule answer for that question, which states it, with no model call. Required lines pass through the same scrub as the rest of the sheet; a line the scrub changes keeps the fixed-rule answer too, with no model call, so the customer is still told the original. Generic filler, the next-visit line and the per-product watch line are not required. Line facts the sheet carries: the lawn assessment summary, findings, watch items and the four scores plus overall as numbers out of 100 (never a percent sign). Tree & shrub reports carry the plant-health score out of 100, what we are watching, the one homeowner task, the insight cards, the diagnosis rows, the plant-group cards, the landscape water card and the score trends from `reportV2` (never the treatment block; card text is scrubbed like the concern). Not carried: the lawn expected-improvement window, application rates, EPA numbers and per-product target lists, so a question only those answer is told the report does not say and offered text or call. While the visit's aftercare holds or reviews watering, free text that changes watering (an "increase irrigation" line in a section, summary, finding or recommendation) is left out of the sheet, the same way the rule answers withhold it.
Pest report in one voice (owner 2026-10-22, "rewrite pest"; `server/services/service-report/pest-report-voice.js`, chosen in `selectReportCopyPrompt` (`lawn-report-copy-prompt.js`) for `POST /generate-report` in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js`): `GATE_PEST_REPORT_VOICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`pestReportVoiceLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and only with `GATE_REPORT_WRITER_RULES` on. On, the dedicated pest report writer (recurring, one-time and re-service pest visits) gets one prompt in one voice (`pest_report_voice_v1`: every owner rule in one list, the owner prose rules, three example reports) in place of its stacked blocks (owner rules, v4 hard constraints, pest module, re-service modifier, fill-in block). The inputs, the provider chain and every output screen are unchanged. Off, the pest prompt is byte-identical. Lawn, tree & shrub, palm and the remaining-service writers are untouched either way. Rollback: unset it; reports already written keep their text.

Pest report quiet visit (owner 2026-10-24, "ok go" on the pest report relevance page after "it always says tech noted nothing, this is lame"; `pest_report_voice_v2` in `server/services/service-report/pest-report-voice.js`, inputs in `POST /generate-report` in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js`): `GATE_PEST_QUIET_VISIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`pestQuietVisitLive()`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and only where the one-voice pest prompt serves (`pestVoiceServes`: `GATE_REPORT_WRITER_RULES` and `GATE_PEST_REPORT_VOICE` on, the dedicated pest writer). On, the writer gets v2: v1 with a new first example (a quiet visit opens on what we saw and where we worked) and two rules (never say what the customer did not mention; never claim we talked unless the note says so); the route sends no "Observations: None noted" or "Customer concern: None" line for an empty field and leaves out the sheet's customer-home choice (it opens on "home — spoke with them" every time, and the visit timeline prints it). Recorded observations and a recorded concern still reach the writer. Output screens are unchanged. Off, the v1 prompt and inputs are byte-identical; the stacked pest writer and the remaining-service writers are untouched either way. Rollback: unset it; reports already written keep their text.

Estimate accept-card phone (owner 2026-10-04): `GATE_ESTIMATE_ACCEPT_PHONE` — **default ON: on unless exactly `false`**, read through `featureGates.isEnabled('estimateAcceptPhone')` in `server/routes/estimate-public.js`. An estimate with no phone and no linked customer cannot become a customer: the card step and the accept refuse it with "call the office". ON: `/api/estimates/:token/data` reports `contactGaps.phone` for such an estimate, the "Confirm your details" card on the estimate page asks for a mobile number, and `PUT /api/estimates/:token/contact-phone` saves it on the estimate (E.164, guarded update) before the card step and Accept unlock. A typed number that already belongs to any live customer is never saved or attached: the customer sees the standing "call the office" message and the office gets one Estimates bell with the number. OFF (`false`): `contactGaps.phone` is always false, the field never shows, the route answers 404, and a phone-less estimate behaves as before. Kill: set `GATE_ESTIMATE_ACCEPT_PHONE=false`; phones already saved stay on their estimates.

Price Match shipping estimates: `PRICE_SCAN_DEFAULT_SHIPPING_USD` (default `15`) and `PRICE_SCAN_BULK_FREIGHT_USD` (default `25`), read at call time in `server/services/price-scan/shipping-rules.js`. The weekly Price Match scan compares delivered prices (sticker + shipping) against the SiteOne baseline. Shipping is firm only on two paths: vendors that ship free on everything (SiteOne, Veseris, Amazon, DoMyOwn, Chemical Warehouse, DIY Pest Control), and Gemplers when the item price is at least $149 (its published free-shipping threshold) or its weight, taken from the listing, falls in an exact band of Gemplers' published weight table (17 bands, 0-5 lb to 350-400 lb) and the listing has no hazardous, oversize or truck freight tag. Every other case is an estimate: Gemplers items with a special-freight tag, an estimated weight or a weight over 400 lb, and every other vendor (GCI Turf, Intermountain, Seed World, Forestry, Keystone, Solutions, Golf Course Lawn Store, SeedBarn whose free-shipping promo is time-limited, and unknown hosts). An estimate is the default per order plus the bulk freight figure for a single item of 40 lb or more, labelled "shipping estimated" in the email to the SiteOne rep. The scan never reads "free shipping" from page copy or markup. A missing, non-numeric or negative value falls back to the default. No gate; set to `0` to compare sticker prices for estimated vendors.

Server dictation for every staff mic (owner 2026-10-06; extends the 2026-10-03 voice-fill ruling "always our transcriber"): `GATE_SERVER_DICTATION` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`serverDictationLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy needed). On, every voice-to-text mic in the portal (`client/src/hooks/useSpeechDictation.js`: the Intelligence Bar, chart prompt, schedule notes, photo captions, project and invoice fields, the Fast Complete note mic, the customer text composer) records a clip on every browser that can record and posts it to `POST /api/tech/dictation` (admin and technician logins; `GET /api/tech/dictation/availability` tells the client whether the gate is on, cached per session) instead of the browser's speech recognition, which on iPhone is Apple dictation and mishears customer, product and pest names. The server hears the clip with the voice-fill transcriber (`gpt-transcribe`, override `OPENAI_VOICE_FILL_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`, lane `voice_fill_transcription`) primed with a word list it builds itself (`server/services/dictation-word-list.js`): the named customer (from a customer or visit id the client may send in the query string; a technician's ids are checked against their own visits and customers first, and one that fails is dropped, never a 403), active technicians, catalog products and their aliases (the voice-fill source), service names, then pest and lawn words; capped at 1800 characters in that priority order; the client never sends prompt text. One microphone records at a time app-wide: starting a mic stops the one that holds the microphone and sends its clip. Send, Ask, Generate and Save actions wait while any mic is recording or transcribing. Same 15 MB clip policy and hallucination guard as field dictation, 40 clips per 15 minutes per staff bucket. Nothing is stored; the audit line (`[server-dictation]`) carries sizes and counts only. The trade-off: words appear after the mic stops, not live. Off = availability answers `{available:false}`, POST answers 404, and every mic keeps today's browser behavior (a browser that cannot record always does). Rollback: unset the gate. Code: `server/routes/tech-dictation.js`, `server/services/dictation-word-list.js`.

Customer names in the staff mic (owner 2026-10-20, after the Intelligence Bar heard a customer surname as a common word): `GATE_DICTATION_CUSTOMER_NAMES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `dictationCustomerNamesLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy needed). Needs `GATE_SERVER_DICTATION`. On, the word list (`buildDictationHints` in `server/services/dictation-word-list.js`) adds "Customers who may be named" right after the named customer, full names "First Last", best first: the customer on screen, customers with a pending, confirmed, en-route or on-site visit today or tomorrow (ET), customers who texted or called in the last 48 hours, then recently updated active customers. A technician login gets only the names of its own stops (the texting and recent-customer groups are admin-only). Products shrink from 750 to 400 characters and the names get 350; the prompt stays at 1800. The surnames of the names that fit also go to the transcriber as extra `keywords[]` (`opts.keywords` on `transcribeWithOpenAI`, merged after the shared place-name hints, at most 50, 40 characters each; OpenAI's own limit is not documented in this repo, so that bound is unverified). The name list is cached in memory for 5 minutes per login scope and ET day. The Intelligence Bar mics (desktop and phone) now send the page's customer id as dictation context. Nothing is stored or logged. Off = the word list and keyword hints are exactly as before (the bar's customer id still names the on-screen customer in the existing section). Rollback: unset the gate. Code: `server/services/dictation-word-list.js`, `server/routes/tech-dictation.js`, `client/src/components/admin/GlobalCommandPalette.jsx`.

Dictated dollar amounts (owner 2026-10-21, after "sixty-one thirty-three" came back as 6133, $60.33 and $61.33): `GATE_DICTATION_MONEY_NORMALIZE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `dictationMoneyNormalizeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy needed). Needs `GATE_SERVER_DICTATION`. On, `POST /api/tech/dictation` runs the transcript through `normalizeSpokenMoney` (`server/utils/spoken-money.js`) and answers `{ text, money: { changes, ambiguous } }` (clients ignore unknown keys). The `text` is ALWAYS the transcript exactly as heard: the parser only suggests (`changes`) and flags (`ambiguous`); it never rewrites, because a misread phrase must not change what the operator said. It acts only where a money cue (a `$`, or price, charge, cost, dollars, bucks, rate, a month, per visit, invoice, pay, paid, total, amount, quote, fee) sits within five words in the same sentence: "sixty-one thirty-three" and "61 33" become `$61.33`; "sixty one dollars and thirty three cents" becomes `$61.33`; "a hundred and five" and "six thousand one hundred thirty three dollars" become `$105` and `$6,133`. The dollar part of a pair must be 10 or more ("one fifty" could be $1.50 or $150, so it stays as heard); spoken years, decimals ("sixty one point thirty three"), gate/door/lockbox codes, cents and percentages are left as heard. A run-together four-digit amount over 2,000 (`$6133`, `6133 dollars`, "6133 a month") keeps its digits and is listed in `money.ambiguous` as `{ heard, candidates: ['$61.33', '$6,133'] }`. Phone numbers, street numbers, times, dates, ZIPs, invoice, ticket and unit numbers and numbers followed by a unit (oz, gallons, sq ft, lbs) are never touched. The parser reads at most the first 20,000 characters (a 20,000-character worst case runs well under 100 ms; the cap keeps a huge typed prompt from blocking the server). Numbered streets ("6133 15th Street East") are addresses, not amounts. The Intelligence Bar mics do not pass amounts back: when any dictation went into the message, the palette sends one flag, `dictation_used: true` (cleared after an answered question or New chat). With this gate on and the flag set, the bar re-runs the parser over the whole question on the server and adds up to three lines to the system prompt, unclear amounts first: "ask with offer_choices between $61.33 and $6,133 before using it" for each ambiguous four-digit amount, and "may mean $X ... read it back" for each clear reading. No client-supplied amount or heard text is read. A typed message (no flag) gets no note. The saved task keeps only the flag. Off = the transcript and the bar prompt are exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate. Code: `server/utils/spoken-money.js`, `server/routes/tech-dictation.js`, `server/routes/admin-intelligence-bar.js`, `client/src/hooks/serverDictation.js`, `client/src/components/admin/GlobalCommandPalette.jsx`.

Area add-on treatments (`server/services/pricing-engine/service-pricing.js` `priceAreaAddOn`, table `AREA_ADDONS` in `constants.js`; owner rulings 2026-10-08): `GATE_AREA_ADDONS` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `gateEnvValue` inside `assertAreaAddOnsEnabled()` (the deepest chokepoint, like `GATE_BERMUDA_SUPPRESSION`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The six add-ons are `bed_pre_emergent`, `lawn_insect_spot` (St. Augustine only), `fire_ant_yard`, `lawn_insect_preventive`, `hardscape_weed` and `web_sweep`; the price comes only from the cost formula (60% target margin at the top of each area tier, no recurring-customer perk, no WaveGuard percentage, never counted toward the WaveGuard tier). **Version 1 sells ONE application per add-on per estimate** (a second application is a new estimate; recurring add-ons are a later PR): there is no application count anywhere, a caller that sends `applications` is refused (400), and the yearly limits are enforced (next sentence). **Yearly limits (owner ruling 2026-10-08, add-on-only; `server/services/pricing-engine/area-addon-limits.js` pure rule, `server/services/area-addon-limits.js` history and enforcement):** `AREA_ADDONS.items[key]` is the one source of `maxPerYear`, `minDaysApart` and `limitProduct` (the pricer, the catalog payload, the job card line and the recheck read it; a test pins the protocol `area_addon` label text to it): bed pre-emergent (Snapshot 2.5TG) 4 in 12 months and 60 days apart, lawn insect spot (Arena 50 WDG) 2 and 56 days apart (the v13 lawn program's own Arena cap is unchanged), fire ant yard (Topchoice) 1, yearly preventive (Acelepryn) 1, hardscape weed (Roundup QuikPro SC) 2, web sweep none. The check counts applications of the same PRODUCT at the treatment PLACE, whoever the customer record is (Codex round 18: a label limit is about the property, so two estimate links at one address with two phones share one history): the place is the treated property widened to every `customer_properties` row of the same `address_key` (any customer), or, with no property id, the estimate's address parsed to that key (`parseEstimateAddress` + `addressKey`, the parse the accept links properties with); it counts the FDACS ledger `property_application_history` (the known customer's rows scoped to the treated property the way application-limits scopes it, other customers' rows only when provably at the place, so program and add-on applications both count), the add-on visits already booked and not done of any customer at the place (`scheduled_services` / `scheduled_service_addons`, not cancelled or completed; a visit with no property id is placed by its source estimate's address; the estimate being accepted left out) and the live holds at the place, and only ever blocks or holds the ADD-ON, never a program visit; no `product_limits` row exists for it. The engine never queries: the estimator's calculate and save read the history for the verified customer and property (`options.existingCustomerId`, `options.propertyId`, `options.address`; a customer with two properties and none named counts the whole customer; a new lead with no customer but an address at a property that has history is read too, for an admin requester only) and inject `services.areaAddOnHistory`; a posted copy is dropped. A limit reached becomes an unpriced custom-quote line (`area_addon_yearly_limit_reached`, staff detail with the last application and the next allowed day), an unreadable history the same line (`area_addon_history_unavailable`), a new lead with no customer and no address on file prices normally. The accept, the reserve and the booking also take transaction advisory locks on the PLACE (address, property and canonical `place:<address_key>` keys, a named customer included), so two different people at one address cannot both pass; the public accept (inside its transaction, after the customer lock), the reserve (inside its transaction), Mark Won and the schedule's booking from a linked estimate recheck it and refuse with 409 `AREA_ADDON_YEARLY_LIMIT_REACHED`, or `AREA_ADDON_HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE` when the read fails (fail closed for the chemical add-ons); gate off = no read at all. The job card shows "Application 1 of 2 in 12 months; last applied 2026-08-01." beside the label limit. On, `generateEstimate` accepts `services.areaAddOns` = a list of `{ key, areaSqFt }` (one entry per key; a repeated key is refused) plus ONE group visit `services.areaAddOnVisit` (`standalone` default | `sameTripAddOn`) and adds one non-discountable one-time `area_addon` line per entry; the visit is chosen once for the group (a per-entry `visitContext` is refused, 400, so an old client cannot double-charge): on their own visit the add-ons share ONE 20-minute drive, carried by the first priced add-on (`carriesVisitDrive` on its line and row), and on a same visit none carries one; the $8 booking-and-invoicing cost (`adminPerJob`) is one job's cost too: the first priced add-on carries it (`carriesJobAdmin`, own visit or same visit) and every other add-on prices with no admin, so a second add-on on the same visit costs $50 to $60 less than the first of its tier (price table: `server/services/pricing-engine/README.md` section 5a); the line and the mapped row carry the add-on's own catalog key (`catalogServiceKey`, `area_addon_<key>`), its family (`addOnCategory`: web sweep = pest control, the other five lawn care), the tier and the engine on-site minutes. `v1-legacy-mapper.js` emits each as its own named one-time row; an area above the table is an unpriced custom-quote row. A commercial property gets the commercial manual-quote line instead of a price. `areaAddOnVisit: 'sameTripAddOn'` (no drive on any add-on) needs a priced service that is not an add-on on the same estimate, else a 400 `PricingError`. Estimator: the admin estimate tool posts `options.areaAddOns` (same shape) and one `options.areaAddOnVisit` to `POST /api/admin/estimator/calculate-estimate`; `translateV2CallToV1Input` turns it into `services.areaAddOns` and, like the Bermuda option, a request while the gate is off fails closed (400 `AREA_ADDONS_GATED`); a malformed envelope is a 400 `AREA_ADDON_INPUT_INVALID`; `lawn_insect_spot` prices only for a grass the operator chose ON ITS ROW (the estimator row carries a required Grass select with no default and sends it as the entry's own `grassType`, `unknown` until chosen); an entry's own grass wins over the estimate's, and an empty or unknown one is a custom quote, never the form's or the translator's St. Augustine default. An add-on-only estimate (no other service) needs no home or lot size. `GET /api/admin/pricing-config/lawn_pricing_v2` (the read that carries `subFeaturesAvailable.bermudaSuppression`) also returns `areaAddOns: { enabled, visitContexts, items[] }` so the screen never hardcodes the table. Booking: each add-on has a `services` catalog row (migration `20261008200000`, `area_addon_<key>`, generic completion lane, taxability row that follows dethatching: commercial taxed, residential not; web sweep is pest control, the rest lawn maintenance). The one-time accept books ONE appointment that carries the whole one-time service mix, stamped with the primary service's catalog id by the exact `catalogServiceKey` (pest control first, else the first), and the one-time total as its price; every other sold area add-on becomes a `scheduled_service_addons` row on that appointment in the accept transaction (`server/services/area-addon-visit-rows.js`, called from `commitReservation` and from the adopt-existing-appointment branch; staff booking from a linked estimate builds its own lines in the schedule modal), so the job card, the completion invoice (primary line = total less the add-on rows, equal to the one-time total), closeout (license, application log and notice requirements fold in every area add-on row: `service-closeout-requirements.js`) and the trace readers see every add-on. The slot is sized to at least the sum of the add-ons' engine on-site minutes whatever `GATE_VISIT_COMBINED_CAPACITY` says (`oneTimeVisitDurationMinutes`). The completion screens decide by the visit's catalog key, not its name: an area add-on is never the lawn fast-complete sheet, the pest recap / pest report flow or the recurring lawn form (`isAreaAddOnCatalogKey`, `isAreaAddOnVisit`). A normal pest or lawn visit that carries an attached add-on row (a same-trip add-on) keeps its OWN full completion form (the lawn assessment, plan and calibration, lawn defaults and coverage for a lawn host; the pest form for a pest host) and gains the add-on fields beside it; only an appointment whose own service is an area add-on takes the generic lane. The lightweight shortcuts are off for the host: the schedule feed (`loadProjectCompletionContextByServiceId`, one batched read, `areaAddOnSoldByVisit`) turns every lightweight flag off for it (`LIGHT_COMPLETION_FLOWS_OFF`: pest report flow, recap, lawn, lawn re-service, Tree & Shrub and typed report flows) and lists the add-ons in `areaAddOns` (key, name, sold area, tier, area label, grass); the server authority is `resolveEligibility` (`hasAreaAddOnRows`, fail closed), which the pest recap, the lawn, lawn re-service and Tree & Shrub contexts and the voice fill all read; the client shortcut predicates use `carriesAreaAddOnWork`, and the completion form's lane uses `isAreaAddOnVisit` alone. The add-on fields (`AreaAddOnFields`, "Add-on treatments on this visit") name each attached add-on with "Sold: up to 5,000 sq ft of lawn area"; a chemical add-on's product is chosen there and lands in the visit's ordinary product list as a row tagged with the add-on, where the treated square feet are entered (a lawn-family area rule on that row whatever line the host is; every other row keeps the host's own rules), so the server saves it like any other application row; the web sweep records no product. The generic form of an add-on visit records the add-on's product and treated area as an ordinary product row: a lawn-family add-on asks for the treated square feet on a broadcast or granular product (`areaAddOnRowServiceType`). A recurring-mode accept or reserve of an estimate that carries add-ons is refused (409 `AREA_ADDONS_ONE_TIME_ACCEPT_ONLY`), because the recurring conversion has no step that books a sold one-time add-on; the office books those by hand. Staff Mark Won (`markEstimateManuallyAccepted`, before any status write) and the schedule accept-on-book preflight (`admin-schedule.js`, before the appointment commits) refuse the same estimate with the same 409 code and a staff message (remove the add-on from the estimate and sell it on its own one-time estimate); an add-on-only estimate still marks won. The other writers of `accepted` are the one-tap purchase (its own generated estimate, never an add-on) and termite annual activation (runs after an accept that already passed these gates). Off = any `areaAddOns` entry (and `priceAreaAddOn` itself) throws a 400 `AREA_ADDONS_GATED` with `failClosed`, so nothing is silently dropped; no `areaAddOns` input = byte-identical to before; the catalog payload answers `enabled: false`. Off is also a kill switch for ALREADY SAVED estimates, enforced the way `GATE_BERMUDA_SUPPRESSION` is (one detector, `estimateDataCarriesAreaAddOns`, and one guard, `estimateAreaAddOnsGated`, both in `v1-legacy-mapper.js`): a stored estimate that carries an add-on in its engine inputs, mapped rows or engine lines is refused with `AREA_ADDONS_GATED` at send/publish (409, `admin-estimates.js`), public accept (409), manual accept (409), booking from a linked estimate (409, `admin-schedule.js`), every slot route including the locked extend recheck and both card-intent routes (409), the annual prepay suggestion (blocked whenever the estimate carries an add-on, gate on or off), and re-price (400 failClosed); a deposit paid gate-on and recorded gate-off is unrecordable (`area_addons_gated`) so the stale-deposit rail refunds it. Public view stays readable (as for Bermuda: it serves stored rows and takes no money). A manual estimate discount never touches an add-on row (engine, mapper, and the pest one-time choice rows `applyManualOneTimeDiscountToChoiceRows` keep the engine's price). The technician's job card shows each chemical add-on through the governed `area_addon` one-time program in `server/config/protocols.json` (five visits routed by catalog service key: `MATCH_RULES` in `protocol-matcher.js`, `ADDON_PROGRAMS.lawn_care.keys` in `job-card.js`, so the recurring lawn or pest program's lines never apply and a display name never routes a service here): the catalog product with the label facts (rate, area basis, yearly limit, safety line) beside it, what the estimate sold ("Sold: up to 2,000 sq ft of bed"; for the insect spot "Grass on the estimate: St. Augustine", and the 2(ee) rate is withheld, with the reason, when the visit carries no St. Augustine evidence) and no tank amount (the search is closed to these lines). The sold scope (`areaSqFt`, `tierSqFt`, and the grass for a grass-bound add-on) is stored in `scheduled_services.area_addon_scope` (the add-on that IS the appointment) and `scheduled_service_addons.area_addon_scope` (each row) by `area-addon-visit-rows.js`, migration `20261008230000`. The schedule's Update Details save (delete and re-insert of the add-on rows) keeps each stored scope on the row of the same catalog service, server-side (`readAreaAddOnScopesToCarry` / `restoreCarriedAreaAddOnScopes`): a posted line cannot set, widen or drop a scope, and a removed add-on takes its scope with it; the visit's own scope is cleared when an edit moves the visit to another service (`clearOwnAreaAddOnScopeOnServiceChange`). No other writer copies or regenerates a scope (recurring spawns skip one-time rows). Completion prefill offers none of these products (the visits carry no `completionDefaultProducts`), so the catalog default rate (Arena 0.29, Acelepryn 0.05) is never seeded; the web sweep shows no product. **Governed rate on the completion form (Codex round 8):** `area_addon` `labelFacts` also holds each rate as numbers (`ratePer1000`, `rateUnit`), read by `area-addon-governed-rate.js`. The schedule feed carries it on each attached add-on (`areaAddOns[].governed`) and, for the add-on that IS the visit, as `areaAddOnOwn`; the form prefills it for the add-on's own product (never the catalog default), computes the amount from the treated area and uses it as the row's ceiling. The server holds the rate back (with a reason) for the wrong grass or an unverified label, as the job card does; any other product on an add-on row starts with no rate. **The add-on's product is found by catalog identity, once (Codex round 12):** `resolveGovernedProducts` in `area-addon-governed-rate.js` resolves the protocol's product hint against every catalog name and alias (the plan matcher's rule), so a product renamed in the Service Library with its old name kept as an alias is the same product everywhere: the job card line, the feed's verified-label read, the completion picker and rate prefill, the wrong-product and over-rate checks at completion, and the yearly-limit history (`area-addon-limits.js` no longer has a second lookup). The feed sends the product's ID (`governed.productId`, also on `areaAddOnOwn`) and the form filters, offers and prefills by that ID, never by name; the picker offers only that one product and never the whole catalog. Of duplicate-named rows the ACTIVE one is selected; the history counts every row of the product, active or not. When every row of the product is inactive (`productStatus: inactive`) or no row matches (`unresolved`), the add-on has no selectable product: the feed sends no `productId` and the plain sentence `productNote` ("<product> is not an active product in the Service Library, so no product can be chosen for this add-on. Ask the office."), the form shows it in place of the picker, the job card shows it under the add-on, the rate is held back, and a product recorded anyway is flagged to the office by the existing wrong-product rule (never blocks); the closeout keeps the add-on's application fact pending. A failed catalog read sends no product and "could not be confirmed right now"; the yearly-limit reader still fails closed on an unresolved product. **A host's card and an add-on's card of one product are separate cards (Codex round 12):** the job card keys a card by product AND, for an add-on riding a host visit, the add-on (`rowId`, the same identity as the completion rows: `<productId>` or `<productId>::<area_addon_key>`; the add-on that IS the visit has no host and keeps the product alone), so Snapshot on a Tree & Shrub visit and the Bed Pre-Emergent add-on's Snapshot are two cards, each with its own plan line or governed text, sold scope, source label and yearly-count line; the add-on card has no tank amount and asks no carrier rate on the dispatch strip, and the host card keeps its plan amount. At completion `service_products.area_addon_key` (migration `20261009200000`) records which add-on a row belongs to, kept only for an add-on the visit carries (its own scope or a `scheduled_service_addons` row; an untagged row on an add-on visit is that add-on's; a forged tag is dropped), and a tagged row recorded above the governed rate (same product and unit) is flagged on the completion and sent to the office like every other over-limit application; it never blocks. **Closeout is per add-on:** the closeout requirement lists the chemical add-ons that each need an application row (`areaAddOnApplicationKeys`, with `hostApplicationLog` for the host's own log), frozen into the snapshot; `closeout-status` reports the application fact pending (or failed when a row was retracted) naming the add-ons with no row, and done only when each has one. A COMPLETED visit is refused without them (round 45, below; an incomplete outcome still saves); a snapshot frozen without the list, and a visit with no chemical add-on, keep the one-boolean verdict; requirements read from the live catalog (not frozen) count per add-on only once a row of the visit carries a tag, so a visit completed before rows were tagged never turns pending afterwards. The closeout alert names the add-ons with no record (`closeout-alerts.js`). The yearly limit recheck reads the customer an unowned estimate resolves to (booking customer, linked appointment, estimate group, phone match). The Acelepryn "April" is advisory only: the limit is "Once in 12 months." Customer copy lives in `server/services/estimate-one-time-copy.json` (`area_addon_*` entries); the service-details packet is unchanged and add-ons unlock no guide. Rollback: unset the gate (the migration rows stay; `down` retains any row a visit references). The price knobs (target margin, admin per job, per add-on material, setup minutes, minutes per 1,000 sq ft, tiers) are the `pricing_config` row `area_addon_pricing` (migration `20261010110000`, Pricing Logic panel One-time tab, bounded, a malformed row leaves the code defaults); the yearly limits, grass and product stay in code. The governed rate, unit, yearly count and interval of the five chemical add-ons are also rows in the DB protocol store (`lawn_protocol_products`, protocol key `area_addon`, migration `20261010120000`), pinned equal to `protocols.json` and `AREA_ADDONS` by a test. The six `area_addon_*` catalog keys are in `WAVEGUARD.excludedFromPercentDiscount` (and `service_discount_rules`, migration `20261010100000`): no percentage discount applies to an add-on on any path. **The gate stops NEW quotes and sales only (Codex round 11):** the pricer, the estimator input, the stored-estimate refusals (send, accept, Mark Won, linked booking, slots and card intents, re-price) and the limit recheck read it; every reader of add-on data that already exists - the job card, closeout requirements and status, completion tagging, the rate and actuals checks, the schedule feed, Fast Complete eligibility and the duplicate-application audit in `application-limits.js` - keys on the data and works with the gate off (`area-addon-gate-readers.test.js` pins the complete list of files that read it). A fresh completion of a row tagged to a chemical add-on is refused (400 `area_addon_actuals_required`) without a positive rate and unit, treated square feet and amount (the amount is filled from the rate and area when the client sends none), and closeout counts such a row as the add-on's record only with all three. A tagged row with a blank, zero or negative rate, or a unit with no safe conversion to the governed unit, is flagged to the office (`area_addon_rate_unchecked`); a convertible unit (lb/oz/g, gal/fl oz/ml, per 1,000 sq ft or per acre) is compared in the governed unit. The replay stamp (`pricingKnobs`) also carries `laborRate` and `driveMinutes` (`global_labor_rate`, `global_drive_time`), so a sent estimate keeps its price when either is edited. **Stored rows (Codex round 17):** every reader of an estimate's add-on rows (the persisted-gate detector `estimateDataCarriesAreaAddOns`, `soldAddOnKeys` for the limit recheck and booking, the knob replay, the one-time breakdown normalizer, the service-interest inference) goes through `storedAreaAddOnRows` (`server/services/estimate-result-container.js`), which reads the authoritative result container only, so a stale `engineResult` left behind by a revision neither keeps a clean estimate gated nor gets an add-on rechecked or booked; the replayable inputs stay fail-closed at the gate boundaries. An add-on-only estimate saves `service_interest` as the add-on names (`Fire Ant Yard Treatment + Web Sweep`) with the add-on's family (`lawn` / `pest`) as its service line.
