Mosquito misting system pricer (`server/services/pricing-engine/service-pricing.js` `priceMosquitoMisting`, table `MOSQUITO_MISTING` in `constants.js`; scope `~/mosquito-misting-scope-20260924.md` sections 4.3 and 6): `GATE_MOSQUITO_MISTING` — **ships DARK: off unless `1`/`true`/`on`**, read at call time via `mosquitoMistingLive()` (unset = kill, no redeploy). On: `generateEstimate` accepts `services.mosquitoMisting` (or `mosquito_misting`) and prices an install (tier price plus nozzle and riser overage) with a plan of 12 monthly applications at $59 per application; refills (`standard`, `natural`, `premium`) are billed per refill application and are NOT in the plan annual; more than 80 nozzles or more than 80 risers is a manual quote, and a quote-required request never waives the pest setup fee. The legacy mapper emits a recurring `mosquito_misting` plan line and a one-time `mosquito_misting_installation` item, and the public price ranges add the rows `mosquito_misting_install` and `mosquito_misting_plan`. The line is not a WaveGuard tier service and takes no percent discount (`excludedFromPercentDiscount.mosquito_misting`). All prices are DRAFT and DB-authoritative. Owner 2026-10-24: the system is the Pynamite system built at retail sale prices until dealer pricing arrives (tier keys `essential` and `smart` kept; labels `Compact system (10-gallon)` 2,795 with 10 nozzles and `Standard system (55-gallon)` 4,195 with 30 nozzles; 0 risers included at 75 each; install 2 techs x 6 hours; migration `20261025090000` moves the pricing_config row from the 10-23 seed only while no admin has edited it). The pricing_config row `mosquito_misting_pricing` (Pricing Logic panel, Mosquito tab) overrides them on every sync, and the constants are the fresh-environment seed. Off = the `services.mosquitoMisting` key is ignored and every estimate and the range feed are byte-identical. No customer text, email or charge starts from this gate. Conversion (misting PR 2a, #6543): an accepted priced misting estimate converts. Migration `20261023100000` adds the catalog rows `mosquito_misting_install` (one-time install, base 4,595 at the 10-23 seed; migration `20261025090000` moves it to 4,195 with the range minimum at 2,795, only while the seeded values are unchanged), `mosquito_misting_service` (monthly, 12 applications a year, 59 per application) and `mosquito_misting_refill` (a catalog row, Standard base 129 as a placeholder only; linked as an add-on by misting PR 2c), with completion profiles, tax rows and percent-discount exclusions. The plan converts to a monthly series under `mosquito_misting_service` with no WaveGuard setup fee and no tier count; the stored install figure is a named line (`<tier label> Installation`) on the acceptance invoice (standard first invoice and annual prepay) and ONE office bell (dedupe key `misting_install_schedule:<estimateId>`, dispatched after the accept commits) tells the office to book the install day after the design visit and before the first plan application. No install visit row is created: a scheduled install visit with a proper billed-on-invoice link is a later PR. The install invoice line carries `kind: 'misting_installation'` and `service: 'mosquito_misting_installation'` in `invoices.line_items`, and the prepay coverage readers (`seededVisitPriceForTerm`, the term's `prepay_amount` basis) subtract lines by that marker, never by description, so gap-filled visits do not inherit an install share. The converter's annual-prepay coverage line carries `kind: 'annual_prepay_coverage'`; for such an invoice the per-application basis is that line's amount over the sold visits (nothing is subtracted), and for legacy invoices without the kind the subtraction path never reads the coverage wording ("... 12 months prepaid (setup fee waived)") or a marked one-time line as setup. The install figure (`frozenMistingInstall`) resolves from the authoritative stored result in this order: an authored itemized proposal's priced install line, a mapped `mosquito_misting_installation` item, then the raw engine `mosquito_misting` line's `installation.price` (the shape an engine-origin estimate stores at `engineResult.lineItems`), so every quote shape bills it; an authored proposal that sells an install per building bills every priced install line (one marked invoice line each; previews show one summed row), never summed with a mapped or raw copy of the same install; an unpriced or oversize line bills nothing. The quoted annual-prepay total and the operator preview add the install through the one helper `frozenPrepayOneTimeLines` (rodent setup plus install), so the quote equals the minted invoice. The customer previews carry the install too: the pricing payload's `mistingInstallFee` row (label `<tier label> Installation`, from `frozenPrepayOneTimeLines`, omitted when no install was disclosed), the legacy page's due-today and prepay totals, and the client's payment choices (`extraInvoiceRows`, kept out of the after-completion extras), so the previewed total equals the invoice. The install office bell is armed by an explicit caller flag (`mistingInstallBilled`): the public standard, invoice-mode and annual-prepay accepts and a manual annual-prepay accept pass it; a manual Mark Won that bills nothing and a one-tap purchase do not. Refill billing (misting PR 2c): migration `20261024100000` links `mosquito_misting_refill` as an add-on of `mosquito_misting_service` (`addon_price` NULL). One resolver, `resolveRefillAttachment` in `server/services/misting-refill.js`, prices every staff attach: a new booking (`buildAppointmentPricing`, behind `POST /api/admin/schedule` and `POST /api/admin/schedule/preview`) and an Update Details save (`normalizeUpdateDetailsAddons`, behind the save and its preview). The price is the per-application price of the solution on the customer's ACCEPTED misting estimate for the property (the visit's own source estimate when it is one, else the property's newest accepted misting estimate; the stamped `refillSolution` of its stored plan, else its engine inputs), read from the LIVE `mosquito_misting_pricing` table when the refill is attached. The posted catalog price (the Standard placeholder) is ignored and staff cannot type over it; a line discount still applies. The line is named `Mosquito Misting System Refill - <solution label>` (the visit invoice prints that name) and written with `recurring_pattern` `one_time`; the key is also one-time-only in `isOneTimeOnlyAddonKey`, so a series child, top-up or extension never copies it. A refill is refused (400/409, stable code `MISTING_REFILL_*`, staff-readable text) when there is no accepted misting estimate for the property, the solution is unreadable, the live table has no price for it, the visit is not a Mosquito Misting Service Plan visit, the refill is the visit itself, or the booking is a series (its prepay-on-book total, per-visit price times planned visits, would multiply it: add the refill to the one occurrence after the series exists); a read failure is a retryable 503. A refill a visit already carries keeps its stored price when it cannot be priced later, so an unrelated edit never fails. The price must come from the applied `mosquito_misting_pricing` row (the sync keeps the in-code defaults when the row is missing, refused or leaves the sold solution out, so `mistingRefillPriceIsFromRow(solution)` gates it) after a due db-bridge refresh; a failed refresh is a retryable 503 (`MISTING_REFILL_PRICING_STALE`), and a sync that fails after applying the row restores the refill provenance together with the in-code constants, so restored prices never read as the row's own. A refill is priced for one house and never moves with it: an Update Details save that changes the address is refused while it posts a refill or any visit it moves stores one (`MISTING_REFILL_ADDRESS_MOVE`, judged by the shared `applyAppointmentAddress` for every mover, Update Details, the Intelligence Bar property switch and the geocode review's grouped moves alike, and only on the rows the move re-addresses, so a refill on a completed series parent never blocks moving the future occurrences), a service change cannot make the visit the refill or leave a refill on a non-plan visit (on the edited visit or, for `following`/series scope, on a later occurrence), and a move by another editor after the price was set is a retryable conflict under the row lock. `POST /api/admin/schedule/preview` returns `mistingRefills` (solution, label, per-application price) or the refusal as the group error, and the Create Appointment modal previews a refill group, shows the amount and binds the create POST to the previewed price. On an annual-prepay covered occurrence the refill is the add-on owed on top of the coverage (`annual-prepay-addon-billing`, gated by `GATE_ANNUAL_PREPAY_ADDON_BILLING`; with that gate dark the Update Details repricing guard gives a refill on a covered occurrence no exemption, because the completion would not bill it, and an occurrence the term has not yet stamped never gets one, since its prepay may still await payment); the term's per-visit coverage basis reads the prepay invoice's coverage line only. With `GATE_MOSQUITO_MISTING` off none of this runs and booking, preview and Update Details are unchanged. Rollback guard `20261023110000` keeps operator-edited discount rules: its down() runs before the catalog migration's and strips the insertion marker from a misting rule whose pricing fields were edited, so the catalog down() leaves it (the rule is keyed by a plain string, so it survives even when the service row is removed). The misting program's safety rules (weather shutdown, nozzle placement, exposure response) reach the technician SOP and its text download as a Safety section of the procedure (`procedure.safety`); the barrier mosquito program and the other programs keep their procedures unchanged. Install resolution fails CLOSED: a stored quote with a priced misting plan whose install amount cannot be read is refused with `MOSQUITO_MISTING_INSTALL_UNRESOLVED` (same endpoints and customer text as the accept-pending refusal, after it in precedence, before area add-ons; staff text: re-send the estimate so the install is frozen), while an engineInputs-only estimate carries the replayed engine's install into the accepted data and is not refused. The code-owned `MOSQUITO_MISTING_CONVERSION_READY` in `constants.js` is `true`, so the `MOSQUITO_MISTING_ACCEPT_PENDING` refusal (accept, reserve, slots, card intents, manual acceptance, deposit recording; view and staff send are never blocked) no longer fires; the constant stays so the refusal remains reachable. The gate-off refusal (`MOSQUITO_MISTING_GATED`) is unchanged. Admin estimator inputs and the Pricing Logic panel are misting PR 2b. Staff estimator (misting PR 2b): the admin estimator (`EstimateToolViewV2`) shows a "Mosquito Misting System" toggle with system, nozzles, risers, refill solution and refills-per-year inputs only while `GET /admin/pricing-config/mosquito_misting_pricing` says `featureAvailable` and `misting.enabled` (labels and limits come from that read, never a price), posts `selectedServices: ["MOSQUITO_MISTING"]` with `options.mosquitoMisting` exactly as typed (blank fields take the engine default, `translateV2CallToV1Input` refuses the key with `MOSQUITO_MISTING_GATED` while the gate is off), and the Pricing Logic panel lists the `mosquito_misting_pricing` row in the Mosquito tab like any other row, with the server's validation error shown on a refused save; a saved misting estimate replays from the server-derived `mistingPricingKnobs`, never from the posted options.

Misting layout designer, step 1 (owner 2026-10-26, "build staff version"; `client/src/components/admin/MistingLayoutDesigner.jsx`, geometry in `client/src/lib/mistingLayoutGeometry.js`): `GATE_MISTING_LAYOUT_DESIGNER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `mistingLayoutDesignerLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). On: the `misting` block of `GET /admin/pricing-config/mosquito_misting_pricing` carries `layoutDesigner: true` (the key is absent when off, so the response is then byte-identical), and the staff estimator shows a **Design on map** button beside the misting Nozzles input. The button opens a modal over the property's Google satellite photo (same Static Maps loader as the Treatment Zone Mapper); staff draw eave and fence lines, nozzles are placed at the corners and about every 10 ft along the line (never above 10 ft apart along it, never closer than 3 ft; a corner within 5 ft along the line of the previous nozzle or of the line's end is dropped, so a 3 to 6 ft jog gets one nozzle), and **Use counts** writes the nozzle total into the Nozzles input. Staff screen only: nothing is saved, no risers, no PNG export, no customer message, no price logic change (the price still comes from the nozzle count staff confirm). The map carries the label "Concept layout — final placement at the design visit and install." Step 2 adds risers, the pump and no-mist zones (staff screen only). Step 3 (migration `20261026170000_misting_layouts.js`; routes in `server/routes/admin-estimate-misting-layout.js`, service `server/services/misting-layouts.js`, validation `server/services/misting-layout-validate.js`): **Save layout** composes a branded sketch PNG in the browser (aerial photo, lines, nozzles numbered 1 to N in walking order, risers as triangles, the pump as a labeled cabinet, no-mist zones as labeled circles, nozzles inside a zone drawn amber with a legend row "In a no-mist zone: N (aim away or move)", a small feet scale bar; the picture is the plain drawing, with no title, counts, legend or note on it, and Google's own attribution in the static image is never covered) and sends it with the geometry to `PUT /api/admin/estimates/:id/misting-layout` (multipart: `snapshot` PNG up to 8 MB checked by its PNG signature, `payload` JSON). `GET` on the same path returns the saved layout and a 15-minute signed picture link, or `{ layout: null }`. Admin only; with either gate off both routes answer 404 before the upload is read. One current layout per estimate in `misting_layouts` (unique `estimate_id`, deleted with the estimate): the payload is validated server side (bounded counts, finite in-map coordinates, known kinds, zoom 15 to 22, map 1280 by 960) and the counts and line length are derived, never trusted. The picture is stored under `service-photos/misting-layouts/<estimateId>/` (the prefix the deployed IAM policy grants), the row is upserted, and the replaced picture is deleted afterwards, best effort; a failed row write deletes the picture just uploaded. Reopening the designer on a saved estimate restores the saved center, zoom, lines, final nozzle positions (as the usual manual-edit overlay), risers, pump and zones; changing the lines then re-places the nozzles and clears the edits with the existing notice and Undo. An unsaved estimate shows "Save the estimate first". Estimate document: `GET /:token/data` carries `mistingLayout` ({ imageUrl: a 20-minute signed link, address, counts }) for the document render pass only, and only with both gates on, a saved layout, a misting system in the estimate (the accept guards' own reader), and a layout drawn for the estimate's current address (an estimate moved to another property omits the old sketch, and the designer then opens blank with a notice instead of reopening it); `EstimateProposalDocument` then prints a "Proposed misting layout" card (sketch, counts, legend, concept note) in the place of the satellite photo (the "How your price was built" block; the photo is not shown or counted then) and counts a failed sketch image in `window.__WAVES_PDF_IMAGE_FAILURES`. With the gate off, no layout, or no misting in the estimate, the key and the card are absent and the document, satellite photo included, is unchanged. The pdfkit fallback has no layout section. The layout never changes a price; the nozzle and riser counts still reach the estimate only through Use counts and the estimator's own inputs. **Spray direction (follow-up, same gate, no migration).** The photo opens as close as the Treatment Zone Mapper's (zoom 21, then 20, then 19) with − and + steps (out to zoom 18, in to the closest photo there is; a saved layout reopens at its saved center and zoom, which is its closest). A zoom step scales everything staff placed (lines, manual edits, risers, pump, zone centers; zone radii follow from feet) about the photo center so it stays on the same ground, and a zoom in is refused, with the reason shown, while any point would leave the 1280 by 960 frame. The look is the pest report's: the Treatment Zone Mapper's brand blue `#0A7EC2` for the layered glow of a traced eave or fence line (a fence dashed on the top stroke), the spray puffs and the still mist wedges (blue radial gradients); near-water nozzles stay amber and no-mist zones red. **Pump, bed lines and risers (Pynamite's published FAQ and owner's manuals: nozzles and risers about 10 ft apart (the manual; owner 2026-10-26 overruled the FAQ's 8 ft for risers), nozzles 2 to 15 ft high on the first-story eave and along fences, a Cube Pro pump runs 60 nozzles and 120 with a Zone Kit; constants in `client/src/lib/mistingLayoutLimits.js`).** The pump is required: it is drawn as its cabinet (a tan box with a darker lid line), `Save layout` stays off with "Place the pump first" until it is placed, and the server answers 400 to a payload without one (an older saved layout without a pump still reads). Once it is placed, a "Pump spot (Pynamite manual)" checklist of four boxes (a 120V, 15 amp GFCI outlet within reach of the cabinet's cord with no extension cord, firm level ground, out of flooding and irrigation spray, not a stucco wall or Pynamite's stucco steps noted) shows outside the photo, and `Save layout` stays off with "Confirm the pump checklist" until all four are ticked; moving the pump or placing a new one clears the ticks (a zoom step keeps them). The ticks are saved inside the pump jsonb (`checks: { outlet, level, dry, stucco }`, no migration), the server answers 400 unless all four are true (an older saved pump without them still reads and reopens unticked), and the public `geometry` keeps the pump as `{ x, y }`. The designer counts show "Pump to nearest line: N ft" (straight line to the nearest eave, fence or bed line) and "Pump load: N of 60", where the load is nozzles plus risers (each riser carries a nozzle): above 60 an amber notice "Over 60 nozzles: needs a Pynamite Zone Kit (up to 120)", above 120 a red one "Over 120 nozzles: needs a second system"; the estimate document's card prints the same notice under its counts line from the saved nozzle and riser counts. No price changes and no line item come from any of it. A new **Bed line** tool traces a landscape bed edge; risers go along it automatically about every 10 ft, one at each end and no gap over 10 ft (the nozzle placement engine at 10 ft nominal, 5 ft minimum), and a bed line gets no nozzles and adds no eave or fence length. Bed lines are drawn thin, dashed and copper, not as the blue mist trace. Staff can move or delete any bed riser (an edit overlay cleared, with the usual notice and Undo, when the lines change) and still drop single risers with the Riser tool (those stay when the lines change). Every riser sprays: it gets the same default aim and throw as a nozzle and a mist wedge or puffs, with no arrow and no manual aim. Saved lines gain the kind `bed`; saved risers carry `source` (`bed` or `manual`, the server accepts only those or none) and a bed riser also its bed line's `lineIndex` (dropped when it points past the lines), and reopening re-derives the bed risers from the bed lines and puts the moves and deletions back exactly; a riser saved without a source reopens as a manual one. The saved counts take every riser (`risers`), and `linearFt` leaves bed lines out. The drawing is plain, in the designer and in the saved picture: the satellite photo with the lines, numbered nozzles, aim arrows, spray (animated in the designer, still mist wedges in the picture), risers, pump and no-mist zones with their labels; no panel is ever drawn over the photo. In the staff designer the tools, the Spray and Directions switches, the counts (with "Near water: N"), the legend and the concept note sit outside the photo in the admin's normal UI. On the estimate document, the "Proposed misting layout" section is the estimate template's card (`estimateCard` / `estimateInnerBox`): the title, the plain picture in the inner box, the counts line, an HTML legend (nozzle, near water or no-mist zone, arrow = spray direction, riser, pump, no-mist zone) and the concept note. Every nozzle has an aim, a compass heading in degrees [0, 360): `client/src/lib/mistingLayoutAim.js` derives it, never stores it: away from the house (the normal of its line segment, away from the centroid of the eave-line points, or the map center without one), 10 ft of throw; within 30 ft of the edge of a water or pool zone it aims along its line, away from the nearest such zone, at 5 ft of throw, and counts as near water (amber). A manual aim (Edit nozzles: drag the tip of a nozzle's arrow, which is kept inside the photo with room for its ring even for a nozzle at the edge pointing outward; Reset aim clears one) is the only thing saved: an optional finite `aim` in [0, 360) inside each entry of the existing `nozzles` jsonb, validated by `misting-layout-validate.js` (anything else is a 400), carried for manually aimed nozzles only and kept on reopen. A line change that re-places the nozzles clears manual aims with the other manual edits, under the same notice and Undo. Spray animates soft mist along each aim on a canvas (requestAnimationFrame, stopped when the designer closes and while the tab is hidden); with `prefers-reduced-motion` it never animates and each nozzle shows a still mist wedge instead. The picture is 1280 by 960, the photo full frame. The public payload is extended by the customer page follow-up below. **Customer estimate page (follow-up, same gate, no migration; owner 2026-10-26, "this should take place of the other satellite image we have for residential estimates").** `GET /:token/data` now carries `mistingLayout` on the normal page load too (not only the document render pass), under the same conditions (both gates on, a saved layout, a misting system in the estimate, a layout drawn for the estimate's current address), with a `geometry` block added: center, zoom, map size, lines (kind and points), nozzles (position, kind, lineIndex, manual aim only), risers, pump and zones, projected field by field, so no S3 key, staff id, line id or price is published. `EstimateViewPage` shows a "Proposed misting layout" card (picture, counts line, pump notice over 60, legend, "Concept layout — final placement at the design visit and install.") in the Waves AI card in place of the satellite photo, with a canvas over the picture that animates the blue mist from every nozzle and riser along its effective aim (the same engine as the staff designer, `client/src/lib/mistingSprayEngine.js`, scaled from the 1280 by 960 map to the rendered width). It pauses while the card is offscreen or the tab is hidden and does not animate with `prefers-reduced-motion` (the picture already shows still mist wedges). A picture that fails to load puts the satellite photo back. With the gate off, no layout, or no misting in the estimate, the key and the card are absent and the page is unchanged. The emailed-PDF fingerprint still reads the layout `revision`, not `geometry`. Rollback: unset `GATE_MISTING_LAYOUT_DESIGNER` (saved rows stay, unread); the migration's `down()` drops `misting_layouts`. Remove the gate in a later PR once the staff have used it.
Misting system records (owner 2026-10-30, "yes"; migration `20261030120000_misting_records.js`, routes `server/routes/admin-misting-records.js`, service `server/services/misting-records.js`, math `server/services/misting-calibration-math.js` and `client/src/lib/mistingCalibrationMath.js`, panel `client/src/components/admin/MistingRecordsPanel.jsx`, product label numbers in `shared/misting-products.json`): no new gate; the records ride `GATE_MOSQUITO_MISTING` (read at call time via `mosquitoMistingLive()`, ships DARK). On: Customer 360 shows an admin-only **Misting system** panel and `/api/admin/misting-records` answers; off: every route answers 404 `{ error: 'Not enabled' }` before any database read and the panel renders nothing. Two append-only tables. `misting_calibrations` is the install calibration (wiki/protocols/mosquito-misting-systems.md step 7): the staff-measured nozzle flow, cycle, mist times, product, mix and treated volume, with the daily output and the label's daily cap computed and stored by the server (the client preview uses the same formulas, both tested against `shared/misting-calibration-cases.json`); a re-calibration is a new row and the newest non-voided row per property is current (a calibration always stores the real property id, the primary's included; a NULL property_id only follows a deleted property row, lists under "Removed property" and is never current; the same holds for a property the office retired with active = false, and a refill against it is refused with 409 `MISTING_PROPERTY_RETIRED`; `currentCalibration` and `currentCalibrationForCustomer` in the service define "current" for the staff panel and the customer-app card). Every calibration is stamped with its property's address (migration `20261030150000_misting_calibration_install_address.js`); a customer move edits the same property row, so once the row's address no longer matches the stamp (`premiseStampConflicts`, formatting-blind; a missing stamp is unknown, not different) that calibration is history and takes no refill. The save is refused (422) when the schedule puts out more than the label allows (`MISTING_OVER_LABEL`), when the three install checks are not all ticked (`MISTING_CHECKS_INCOMPLETE`), or, for a known product (Sector, EPA Reg. No. 1021-1834), when the entered limit is above the label's 9.5 fl oz per 1,000 cu ft a day (`MISTING_LABEL_LIMIT_MISMATCH`) or the mix is outside the label's 64 to 128 fl oz in 55 gal with 2% slack (`MISTING_MIX_OFF_LABEL`); a stronger mix divides the daily cap by the strength factor, a weaker one never raises it; an unknown product keeps the limit staff enter. The table's CHECKs refuse an over-label row even from outside the service. `misting_refills` is one row per tank refill (product, EPA reg. no., concentrate, water, level before, counter reset, who, when) and must be logged against the current calibration (409 `MISTING_CALIBRATION_NOT_CURRENT`), with the same product (422 `MISTING_PRODUCT_CHANGED`) and a mix within 10% of the calibration's (422 `MISTING_MIX_CHANGED`), inside a known product's label mix range (422 `MISTING_MIX_OFF_LABEL`), and the system's daily output must still fit the daily cap at the refill's mix (422 `MISTING_REFILL_OVER_LABEL`). Rows are never deleted: an admin voids a row with a reason, and a calibration with open refills cannot be voided. Writes for one customer run one at a time under a transaction advisory lock. Admin only; technicians do not get these routes. Nothing here changes a price or sends a customer message. The customer app's Home card (`client/src/components/portal/MistingSystemCard.jsx`, read from `GET /api/misting-system` in `server/routes/misting-system.js`) reads both tables behind the same gate: off, or a household-contact login, answers `{ system: null }` with no database read. Rollback: unset `GATE_MOSQUITO_MISTING` (rows stay, unread); the migration's `down()` drops `misting_refills` then `misting_calibrations`.
Dead Rodent Removal & Odor Treatment (owner approved 2026-10-26, prices 2026-10-29; `server/services/pricing-engine/service-pricing.js` `priceDeadAnimalRemoval`, table `RODENT.deadAnimalRemoval` in `constants.js`, DB row `pricing_config.rodent_dead_animal_removal`): `GATE_DEAD_ANIMAL_REMOVAL` — **off unless `1`/`true`/`on`** (shipped dark; production on since 2026-10-29), read at call time via `deadAnimalRemovalLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js` (unset = kill, no redeploy). **NEW QUOTES ONLY.** Off: the estimator hides the choice (the staff screen reads `featureAvailable` from `GET /admin/pricing-config/rodent_dead_animal_removal`), and `generateEstimate` refuses a `services.deadAnimalRemoval` input with a 400 `failClosed` `PricingError` (`DEAD_ANIMAL_REMOVAL_GATED`, thrown before the commercial hand-off, so nothing is dropped silently). **An estimate already saved with the line stays a normal estimate**: send, accept, booking, completion and invoicing read the stored row and never call the pricer, so they work like any rodent line with the gate on or off; only a fresh engine run (a re-price or edit that sends the service again, or the replay of an engine-inputs-only estimate that has no stored result) is refused while the gate is off. Estimates saved from the staff estimator store their priced result, so they never replay the pricer. On: `services.deadAnimalRemoval = { tier }` with `tier` one of `reachable`, `attic`, `in_wall`; one fixed price per tier: reachable $199, attic $299 (owner 2026-10-29; other rodent work on the estimate does not lower it, staff discount on the estimate itself; the lower "riding" price was retired the same day, and the retired `riding` key never prices anything: a row may still carry it, ignored, and a Pricing Logic save strips it); could not find it (owner 2026-10-30): the customer pays the full price, and the estimate and the not-found service report carry the odor treatment and one free 14-day recheck; booked as indoor work (rain-OK); `in_wall` or no tier is a custom quote; a commercial property is a manual quote. One-time, takes the 15% recurring-customer perk like other rodent one-time lines, never counts toward the WaveGuard tier. Not on the public quote menu and not in the public price feed (`public_quote_selectable` false). Catalog row `rodent_dead_animal_removal` (migration 20261029130000) completes on the `rodent_sanitation` form and needs no pesticide application (no application log; license mirrors `rodent_inspection`). Sends nothing to a customer by itself. Rollback: unset the gate; no data changes.

Courtesy reply after an automated visit text (owner 2026-10-14; `server/routes/twilio-webhook.js` `lastOutboundAskedQuestion`, reader `smsCourtesyAfterTemplateLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`): `GATE_SMS_COURTESY_AFTER_TEMPLATE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = kill, no redeploy). Today a bare "Ok" after a booking confirmation rings the admin bell, because the template carries a "reply"/"confirm" line and so counts as a question. On: when Waves' last text on that thread (same Waves number, last 24 hours, queued/sent/delivered, not `internal_alert`) has a `message_type` in the automated visit list AND delivery evidence (`sent` or `delivered`; a `queued` row has not reached the phone, so the earlier question check still applies), the thread is not awaiting an answer. The list is `confirmation`, `appointment_confirmation`, `appointment_reminder`, `appointment_reminder_72h`, `appointment_reminder_24h`, `reminder_72h`, `reminder_24h`, `tech_en_route`, `tech_arrived`, `service_complete`, `service_complete_with_invoice`, `service_complete_paid_receipt`, `service_complete_prepaid`, `service_complete_annual_prepay`, `service_complete_annual_prepay_after_first_visit`, `service_report_v1` and `service_report_v1_with_invoice`; a test scans `complete-scheduled-service.js` and `service-report/delivery.js` so a new completion type must be classified. A closer ("Ok", "Thanks", "Great thank you", 👍) is then marked read with no bell, push or owner forward. Tapbacks follow a stricter rule: an affirmative tapback (Liked/Loved or an acknowledgement emoji such as 👍 or ❤️, in the iOS "Reacted ..." or the Android "<emoji> to “...”" shape) is quiet when the last Waves text on the thread is in that list AND the tapback's quoted text EQUALS that last text in full (whitespace and case ignored). A truncated, partial or different quote rings, so a 👍 on an earlier staff text stays loud; ❓, 👎, "Disliked" and "Questioned" stay loud, and a failed lookup stays loud. Anything else still rings: questions, digits, dates, times, yes/no, cancel/stop/reschedule words, and every reply after a `manual` or AI-approved text (a person asked). A reply is still logged and still passes the reschedule-reply and lead-intake steps; only the bell is skipped. Sends nothing to a customer. **Not gated:** the Android `<emoji> to “...”` recognizer in `server/services/sms-intent.js` is a permanent parser fix. With the gate off, an affirmative Android tapback on a text that does not ask for a reply is quiet, the same as an iPhone "Liked ..." today; the reaction recognizers also return false for a body over 4000 characters. The gate covers only replies and tapbacks after automated texts. Gate off = those replies and tapbacks behave as before this change. Rollback: unset `GATE_SMS_COURTESY_AFTER_TEMPLATE` (the parser fix stays; revert the PR to remove it).

Bare YES as a reply (owner 2026-10-29, weekly sweep #5007 finding B3; `server/routes/twilio-webhook.js`, decision in `server/services/messaging/bare-yes-reply.js`, reader `smsBareYesReplyLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`): `GATE_SMS_BARE_YES_REPLY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (unset = kill, no redeploy). Today a bare "YES" (any case, trailing punctuation ignored, a tapback quoting it included) from a compliance-eligible sender is handled exactly like START, because YES is one of Twilio's opt-in keywords: the webhook clears suppression, confirms recipient asks, sets `notification_prefs.sms_enabled = true`, replies "You've been re-subscribed to Waves Pest Control SMS." and returns before the reply bell and every inbound consumer, so a customer answering "Reply YES to …" is never heard. On: a bare YES stays an opt-in only while it can restore something: an active `messaging_suppression` row for the number, `notification_prefs.sms_enabled = false` on the matched customer, or a recipient ask this YES would confirm (`yesWouldConfirmAsk` in `server/services/recipient-optin.js`, sharing its predicate with `markRecipientOptin(…, 'confirmed')`: an ask that went out or a declined one, never `ask_failed`, not confirmed yet; or an undispatched pending row whose own ask `sms_log` shows accepted). Otherwise it takes the ordinary inbound path: no re-subscribe reply, no consent writes, and the usual courtesy rule decides the bell (a YES after a Waves text that asked something rings; a YES after a text that asked nothing is a closer, marked read). The decision is made once, before the recruiting lookup, and every later keyword check reads it: a YES called a reply takes the ordinary recruiting lookup (fail-closed for a plausible applicant), is a staff text from an active technician's phone (`GATE_TECH_STAFF_GUARDS`), and reaches the visit-technician relay (`GATE_CUSTOMER_TEXT_TO_VISIT_TECH`). The webhook logs `[sms-optin] bare YES from <masked phone> handled as a reply`. A failed or incomplete lookup keeps the opt-in. START, SUBSCRIBE, UNSTOP, OPTIN and OPT IN are unchanged, and so is whatever Twilio does with the keyword on its side (the Messaging Service opt-out settings, untouched here). Sends nothing new to a customer. Off = a bare YES is START, byte-identical to before.

Fast Complete Wrap-up on the lawn visit, Tree & Shrub and pest report-flow sheets, and on the pest and lawn re-service paths (owner 2026-10-10, PRs 1 to 3 of 4)): `GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_WRAP_UP` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`fastCompleteWrapUpLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/lawn-fast/context`, `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/tree-shrub/fast-context` and `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/pest-recap/context` and `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/lawn-reservice/fast-context` carry `wrapUp: true`, and each sheet shows an always-open "Wrap-up" section after its last form section: adjust time on site (admin only), re-entry countdown steppers, send completion text, include payment link, send review request with its timing and the next scheduled visit with a "Needs adjustment?" note box (owner 2026-10-12, "store it", no gate of its own: it fixed a silent loss; a typed note, at most 300 characters, posts as `nextVisitAdjustmentNote` beside `nextVisitId`, and `completeScheduledService` appends one `[From M/D visit] <note>` line to that next visit's staff-only `scheduled_services.notes`, once, in the completion transaction; the full Complete Service form posts the same two keys). The rows follow the full Complete Service form's rules (shared in `client/src/lib/completion-review-timing.js` and `completion-invoice-prediction.js`), including its submit-time checks on the review send-time preview. The section's choices ride the sheet's `/complete` body (`sendCompletionSms`, `includePayLink`, `requestReview`, `reviewTiming`, `reviewDelayMinutes`, `reviewScheduledFor`, `timeOnSite`, `reentryExteriorMinutes`, `reentryInteriorMinutes`), fields the endpoint already takes; untouched, the body is the customer-text values each sheet always posted (the lawn and Tree & Shrub sheets the four flags; the pest report flow, which covers recurring, typed, specialty and bait station visits, `sendCompletionSms`, `includePayLink` and `requestReview` with no `reviewTiming` until the tech picks a timing other than Automatic). The pest section sits on the report step before Complete & send. The Tree & Shrub and pest sheets also show the Time on-site clock. **This gate changes a customer text (owner 2026-10-10, "show on"): with it on, a pest or lawn re-service asks for a review by default.** On the pest re-service paths (the report flow's re-service or callback, and the short re-service form) and the lawn re-service sheet, the review switch is shown and starts on, where today a re-service sends no review request. Untouched, those sheets post what they posted before plus `requestReview: true` (and no `reviewTiming` until the tech picks a timing other than Automatic). The pest re-service's fixed text carries no pay link, so its section has no payment-link row and `includePayLink` stays false; the lawn re-service keeps its pay-link rule (a free callback invoices nothing, so no row). The fixed text itself (`GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_RECAP`) is unchanged and carries no review line: the review goes as its own message through the normal review scheduler, subject to every other blocker (unpaid invoice, client or typed customer-comms suppression, consent, STOP and opt-out, review cadence rules). With `GATE_FAST_COMPLETE_RECAP` off the short re-service form sends no customer text today, and shows no Wrap-up. The re-service sheets mark that ask with `wrapUpReviewAsk: true` beside `requestReview: true`; the server refuses a marked ask unless this gate is live when the completion runs, so unsetting the gate stops the new re-service asks even from a sheet that was already open (rollback), and a fixed-text request that is not honored sends no review ask either. The full form posts no marker and asks as it always did. Gate off, a fixed re-service text never asks for a review, exactly as before. Off = no `wrapUp` key and the sheets render and post exactly what they did. Rollback: unset the variable.

Pet-named line in the completion text (WaveGuard perk, owner 2026-10-31 perks round 4 and 2026-11-01 "continue working on"; `server/services/pet-name-line.js`, wired in `server/services/complete-scheduled-service.js`): `GATE_PET_NAME_TEXT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`petNameTextLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: the closeout's completion text adds one sentence, as its own paragraph after the template body and before the bundled review line, that names the customer's dogs and cats and says when they can go back out, e.g. "Biscuit can go back out once the spray has dried." The sentence is one row of a closed table, picked by the re-entry decision the visit's service report already prints (`buildReentryContext` in `server/services/service-report/reentry.js`, read from the record the closeout just wrote): a frozen lawn condition (dry, or watered in and dry), or the stored until-dry advisory of a pest, mosquito, lawn, tree and shrub or palm visit with an outside and/or inside re-entry target. Bait or station work, a visit with no re-entry on its report and an advisory not in the table get no sentence. No time or minute figure and no "safe"; the finished sentence still goes through `customerCopyViolations`. Names come from `property_preferences.pets_structured` (the customer app's Pets editor): dogs, cats and pets with no type only, one to three names (none, or four and more, = no sentence), an indoor pet left out of an outside line and an outdoor pet out of an inside one. Never on Fast Complete's fixed re-service text (it carries its own pets line) and never on an inspection-only, declined or incomplete visit. A failed read costs only the sentence, never the text. Off: no extra read, and every completion text is byte-identical.

One on-the-way and one arrived text per customer, address and day (owner 2026-10-12/13, dark): `GATE_ONE_TEXT_PER_CUSTOMER_DAY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `oneTextPerCustomerDayLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, when a customer has two or more services at one saved address (`scheduled_services.property_id`) on one ET day and the technician named in the text is the same person, the second and later visits send no second "on the way" text and no second "arrived" text (`sendTrackTextOnce` in `server/services/one-text-per-day.js`, called from `track-transitions.js`). **It does not change appointment reminders**: two services at the same start time already get one reminder from the existing same-slot merge (`registerVisitReminderInTx` and the reminder sync trigger). The rule never reads or writes `visit_id`, `service_visits` or `visit_effects`. Coverage is "named = covered": the delivered proof records the ids of the visits the text named (`named_service_ids`) and only those visits are covered. The arrived text names the sender plus the other live visits of that customer, address, day and technician that have no text of their own (one merged label); the on-the-way text names no service, so it stands for the same set as of its delivery. The merged label reaches only the text template, so an arrived notice delivered by email alone names only its own visit and covers only it (the on-the-way text and email name no service and keep the whole set). A visit added later, a visit assigned to a different technician, or a failed label lookup is not named and sends its own; a proof written without the list covers nothing. Coverage is decided only from a recorded delivery: the `track.one_text_per_day.delivered` audit row, written as a critical write only after the sender returned success, records customer, property, ET day, kind and the technician the text named; another visit covers the later one only when its row matches all of those and that visit still exists and is not cancelled, skipped, no-show or rescheduled. There is no lock and no transaction around the send, so no database connection is held across the provider call. Standing down needs a delivered row that only a completed send writes, so two texts can never both stand down; but two taps at the same instant can both find no row and both send: an accepted duplicate (the fail-open direction, and what happens with the gate off). If the proof write fails it is retried once; if it still fails, this visit is not re-sent and the next same-day visit sends (a possible duplicate, never silence). The caller's complete attempt fence is checked right before the send: a visit moved, re-armed or changed meanwhile sends as without the rule and records no proof. The one arrived text names every service it covers (labelled by the existing per-visit label builder; the tracker page stays per visit). A text the provider reports undelivered stops covering other visits: the Twilio status callback records the bounce by message id (one `track.one_text_per_day.bounced` row, only for an on-the-way or arrived text, decided from the send's audit/SMS log row), and a delivered proof all of whose provider ids (one per contact; one delivered contact, or a delivered on-the-way email, keeps the cover) have a bounced row, or a `failed`/`undelivered` status on its `sms_log` or `messages` row (written by the same callback first, so a bounce row that failed to write loses nothing), is void when read, whichever was written first; nothing is re-sent retroactively. The proof is written only if the visit still matches the attempt's fence after the provider call. A legacy NULL visit status counts as live. A covered visit gets its guard stamped and a `track.one_text_per_day.en_route` / `.arrived` audit row. The per-row guards `track_sms_sent_at` and `arrival_sms_sent_at` are never treated as proof. Fails open: any read or write error sends the text as with the gate off. Off = `track-transitions.js` behaves exactly as before.

One-tap report on the recurring pest report sheet (owner 2026-10-17, PR 1 of the one-tap report): `GATE_ONE_TAP_REPORT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`oneTapReportLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/pest-recap/context` carries `oneTap: true` for a visit of a recurring series or a re-service (the pest re-service or a free callback under a regular key; `scheduled_services.is_recurring`, sent as `service.isRecurring`; a one-time visit and a plan's booster or add-on keep today's sheet; the sheet echoes `isRecurring` in its `expectedVisit`, so `/complete` refuses a visit taken out of its series since the sheet opened, `visit_identity_changed`), and the plain pest report sheet that opens with the house mix on it (no lane or typed record; a first cleanout, which opens with no products, keeps the note's products read) changes the sheet as below (items 1, 2 and 4; item 3 is the stock rule every pest sheet follows). (1) The 1-5 pest activity tap starts the AI report writer in the background once the Generate holds clear, while the visit step stays shown; the footer button stays live and only opens the report step, and a later change makes the report stale as before. (2) The note is no longer read for products (no `POST .../fast-complete/voice-fill/products`, no confirm or check holds); the note's mic and the voice-facts read (where, pests, spray, sweep) stay. (3) A product at 0 in stock holds nothing: `/complete` takes a pest visit's stock below zero and records the shortfall, and the sheet names the product and offers Check stock (`stockAdvisory: true` in the context). (4) The trace is optional: a perimeter spray with no saved trace at all asks for a whole number of feet ("Feet sprayed", never copied from an earlier trace or visit) and `/complete` carries it as `areaValue` with `areaUnit: 'linear_ft'` on the perimeter rows (a saved trace's feet win); the Auto-trace button and trace section stay offered. A saved trace that gives no feet (an outline, an old trace with no length) keeps today's trace hold. Photo and trace read holds, the dictation hold, promises loading, missing amount, the rating-required hold and every lane, typed, station, re-service and prepare path are unchanged. Off = no `oneTap` key and the sheet renders and posts exactly what it did. (5) The photo and trace reads hold nothing (the scope page's "Loading photos" and "Check the trace" holds and their Full form escapes): a photo or trace read still loading, or failed, no longer holds Generate or Complete & send and no longer opens the header Full form (a writer outage still does; the read's own retry button stays). The body then omits that read's `photoCaptionsSeen` / `traceSeen`, so `/complete` skips that check instead of refusing a mismatch (an answered read still sends it, and every flow off the gate holds until both reads answer, so it sends both; the one exception, in every flow, is a photo read outside the note box that failed, which never held: it now leaves `photoCaptionsSeen` out instead of sending an empty list that saved photo descriptions would refuse). A perimeter spray whose trace read did not answer shows the Feet sprayed box; a saved trace the sheet could not read still shows on the report, and the typed feet go on the record. A photo change still being saved, and "Loading promises…", still hold. The lawn re-service sheet (PR 3: `GET /admin/dispatch/:id/lawn-reservice/fast-context` carries `oneTap: true` while the gate is live) reads no note for products: no "Fill products from my note" tap and nothing to confirm; the note's mic stays. The lawn visit and Tree & Shrub sheets have no AI writer and no products read, so they are unchanged. Rollback: unset the variable.
Pest rain outlook (owner 2026-10-24; `server/services/service-report/pest-rain-outlook.js`): `GATE_PEST_RAIN_OUTLOOK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`pestRainOutlookLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: a pest visit's completion (`detectServiceLine(service_type) === 'pest'`, the same `shouldCaptureApplicationConditions` test as the weather capture, never a backfill) also fetches the property forecast for the 48 hours after completion (rounded out to whole hours, so a shower in the partial hour at either end is counted), in parallel with the weather fetch, and freezes a compact summary in `service_records.structured_notes.rainOutlook` (`{ v, source, fetchedAt, completedAt, windowHours, totalIn, firstRainAt, complete }`). It never goes into `service_records.conditions`, which is copied into the FDACS application ledger. A forecast that is unavailable, or errors, stores nothing. The pest report's Weather call card then reads that frozen summary. The headline stays, and so does the page's weather icon. The outlook takes the place of a body that only says the weather was written down (the two wind bodies and the default one, "…noted with today's record"), and follows a body that states a fact ("Good treatment window", "Recent rainfall noted"). The outlook is "When we finished, the forecast showed dry weather for the next two days." when the window total is under 0.05 in and no rain falls in the hour that holds the completion, or "When we finished, the forecast showed rain on Sunday morning." plus one sentence when the total is 0.25 in or more, the first rain is at least 4 hours after completion, and every outside spray is fipronil (a soil-binding line) or a pyrethroid (a tighter soil, mulch and plant-binding line). An outside spray is a `perimeter_spray` row that is not a dust (Delta Dust goes into voids, and the pest method fallback can record it as a perimeter spray) and whose recorded area does not name only inside places (controlled chips in `shared/treatment-area-scopes.json`; garage and entry points decide nothing beside a room or an outside place). Surfactant rows are passed over. Each active of a mixed product is classed on its own and must be exactly fipronil or a listed pyrethroid (bifenthrin, cypermethrin and its alpha and zeta forms, lambda- and gamma-cyhalothrin, deltamethrin, cyfluthrin and beta-cyfluthrin, permethrin, esfenvalerate). One dissolvable active (dinotefuran, imidacloprid, thiamethoxam, clothianidin, acetamiprid), any other active (Gentrol's hydroprene, a synergist, a growth regulator, prallethrin) or no outside spray gives the card as it is today, as do light rain, rain inside 4 hours and an incomplete or missing outlook. Rain before 5 AM is named as the night before ("Saturday night"). No line says rainproof, waterproof, rainfast or won't wash off, names days, or asks the customer to call, text or report. Off, no forecast call is made, no key is written, and the card is unchanged. The pest PDF cache key gains `-rain1` while it is on. Rollback: unset it; records keep the frozen summary, unread.

The writer uses it only for a pest you name in the note"; `server/services/service-report/label-pest-facts.js`, read by `productFactLines` in `server/services/service-report/report-writer-records.js`): `GATE_PEST_LABEL_FACTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`pestLabelFactsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and only under `GATE_REPORT_WRITER_RULES` on the pest line. On: `buildReportCopyContext` reads which pests the technician named today (the redacted note and observations `POST /generate-report` passes as `visitTexts`, plus the pests tagged on the product rows), and each reviewed product whose `labelPests` (its current EPA label's pests, owner-reviewed, in `server/config/report-product-copy.js`) names one of them gets "its label lists <pest>" in the writer's PRODUCT FACTS, with one header line: the writer says it once in WHAT WE DID AND WHY, as a treatment "labeled for" that pest, and never that it kills it, keeps it away or works on a pest not listed (a permissive "may" went unused in the 2026-10-24 replay, 0 of 4; the instruction used it in 3 of 4). A species the label names is said as the species ("german cockroaches", with a small g: owner 2026-10-25); a species the label covers only as a group is said as the group. Termite, cockroach, rodent and mosquito reports in one voice (owner 2026-10-24, "yes build voice" to "should the termite, cockroach, rodent and mosquito reports get the same plain voice as pest reports?"; `server/services/service-report/specialty-report-voice.js`, chosen in `selectReportCopyPrompt` (`lawn-report-copy-prompt.js`) for `POST /generate-report` in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js`): `GATE_SPECIALTY_REPORT_VOICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`specialtyReportVoiceLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), and only with `GATE_REPORT_WRITER_RULES` on. Annual prepay chosen on a call (dark, owner 2026-10-29): `GATE_CALL_PREPAY_CHOICE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`callPrepayChoiceLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`). The V2 call extraction carries `service_request.billing_choice` (`annual_prepay`, `per_application` or null: the plan the CALLER chose). On: (1) a call that was NOT booked carries it in the scheduling payload the office sees (`scheduling_window.billing_choice`, `services/call-routing-gates.js`) and in its held-visit row (`services/call-held-visits.js`); the Dispatch strip says "Caller chose annual prepay" and Book it opens the New appointment form with Annual prepay preselected when the customer's linked estimate is prepay-eligible (the save still runs the server's own eligibility and pricing checks); (2) for a call the pipeline or the Phone agent DID book, a sweep every 10 minutes (`services/call-prepay-choice.js`, `scheduler.js`) files ONE admin-only Needs Review card per call (reason `call_prepay_choice`, advisory, category `billing_review`) when the call's customer has a live visit BOOKED from the call (the call's id AND a source_action only a call writes: `ai_call_pipeline`, its follow-ups, the voice agent's or an outbound callback's booking; a visit the call was only attached to, booked earlier or by a person during the call, stays in the existing-plan check) and a newest open estimate (sent or viewed, owned by the customer) that `prepayBookingEligibility` accepts and whose quoted cadence matches the booked visits, at the same property (`completion-pricing.js` `propertyMatches`: property ids, else the quote's address against the visit's stamped address), with no payment already recorded on the visit; the card's tap `POST /api/admin/triage/:id/accept-call-prepay` (admin, version-bound) runs `markEstimateManuallyAccepted` exactly as the New appointment form does for "Billing on acceptance: Annual prepay" (billingTerm `prepay_annual`, term anchored to the booked date, coverage from the booked series), links the booked visits to the estimate and resolves the card. It creates a DRAFT annual prepay invoice that is NOT sent plus a payment-pending term; visits bill per application until it is paid. It refuses with a plain message when the estimate was accepted, expired or became ineligible, the visit is gone, or the customer changed. The sweep never accepts, invoices or texts; a termite estimate gets no card: its accept can send the state termite notice (`GATE_MANUAL_ACCEPT_CONSUMER_NOTICE_SEND`) and the program agreement (`GATE_TERMITE_PROGRAM_AGREEMENT_AUTOSEND`), so the office accepts those from the estimate; every other annual prepay accept sends the customer nothing (the manual accept skips the welcome text and the membership email). The tap must carry the terms token the card showed (`call_prepay.preview_token`: estimate row version, booked visits, amount, coverage), so a re-price after the list loaded asks for a fresh look; the accept pins the estimate row and the booked visits (`expected` `estimateVersion` + `bookedVisits`), and its last step inside the transaction (`beforeCommit`) locks the call and then the booked visits until the commit, re-checks that the call is still this customer's and still shows annual prepay and that the visits match with no add-on line, then links the visits to the estimate; any change since the check rolls the whole accept back (no invoice, no term). The sweep also dismisses (auto) an open card whose estimate was accepted or closed or whose visit is gone. Off = no field on any payload or row, no card, the accept route answers 404, and the form opens as before. Rollback: unset.
Cancel notice (dark, owner 2026-10-30): `GATE_CALL_CANCEL_GUARD` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`callCancelGuardLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`). `GET /api/admin/schedule/cancel-call-notice?customerId=` (`server/services/call-cancel-guard.js`) answers the customer's latest real conversation (voicemails and spam skipped) from the last 14 days when the newest cancellation card on that call was not dismissed, and New Appointment shows "Canceled on a call" with the card summary and an admin-only "Open the call" link under the chosen customer. Closing the stale cards automatically was dropped in #7152 review: address, service scope and caller authority are the office's call.

Held visit strip (dark, owner 2026-10-12): `GATE_CALL_HELD_VISIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('callHeldVisit')` in `server/services/call-held-visits.js` (`listHeldVisits`), served by `GET /admin/schedule/held-visits?date=` in `server/routes/admin-schedule.js` (admin only) and shown on admin Dispatch by `client/src/pages/admin/HeldVisitsStrip.jsx` ("From calls, not on the calendar"). On = Dispatch's day view lists, above the stops, each two-party, non-spam call of the last 30 days (never a voicemail or a sandbox call) whose stored V2 extraction either confirmed a slot on that ET date (`confirmed`, shown "Promised on a call" with its time) or asked for, was offered, or left ambiguous exactly that day with no time (`day_only`, shown "Day discussed on a call" / NOT CONFIRMED / "Time not set"; `processed` calls only, never a spam / wrong-number / vendor disposition or a call that ended with nothing to do per `callEndedWithNothingToDo`). A `reschedule_requested` call is a `confirmed` row too when there is no visit to move (call audit 2026-10-13): a linked customer, staff committed to the new slot (`agent_committed_booking`, or `definite_commitment` with no explicit `agent_committed_booking: false`), the caller accepted it (`caller_accepted_slot`), and that customer has no other visit from the call's ET day on (live, or parked at `rescheduled`); a customer with such a visit stays with the reschedule card. A `reschedule_requested` call is a third kind, `move_day_only`, when staff and an existing customer agreed to MOVE a visit to a new day with no time (owner 2026-10-19, call audit 2026-10-19; call-reschedule-apply skips it because that apply needs an exact hour): a linked customer, no explicit refusal (`agent_committed_booking` is not `false` and `caller_accepted_slot` is not `false`; null or missing passes, because the extractor fills those fields only for a timed slot and the row is display only and NOT CONFIRMED), `moved_appointment_date` naming the visit to move, a one-day range on the row's day that is today or later, no timed slot on the call, a processed two-party call that is not spam, a dropped disposition or `callEndedWithNothingToDo`, and a live visit of that customer on the old day. It shows on the NEW day as "Move discussed on a call — from <old day>, time not set" (NOT CONFIRMED · not moved) with an Open the visit button instead of Book it (a link to the Schedule on the old day, opened on that visit; no new write). It clears when the customer has no live visit on the old day (moved, cancelled or rescheduled), has a live visit on the new day at any time, a visit carries the call, the office closed the call's cards, or the new day has passed. Nothing moves and no text goes. A row clears when ANY of these holds: a visit carries the call (`source_call_log_id`, or a `Call ID: <call_log id>` or `Call SID: <sid>` marker in the visit's `notes` or `internal_notes`; `rowCarriesCall` in `call-booking-miss-watchdog.js`), on any date and under any customer; the call's customer has a live visit on that day, created before or after the call (live = pending, confirmed, en_route, on_site, completed, or a legacy NULL status; a confirmed slot also needs the visit inside the watchdog's 2-hour window tolerance); the watchdog's namesake rule (confirmed slots only); or the office closed the call's triage cards (`officeClosedCall`). Nothing is inferred from a phone number or an address. Book it opens the New appointment modal on that date with the linked customer and the `Call ID:` marker in internal notes; with no agreed whole-hour time the modal opens with no time selected and cannot be saved until one is picked. Open call links to the call. The tech Today page shows the same rows for today to an admin login only (`client/src/pages/tech/TechHeldVisits.jsx`, with a Book in Dispatch link); a technician login never requests them, because a held row belongs to no technician and the route is admin-only. The strip is display only: it writes no visit, no customer and no message. It does not change `GATE_CALL_BOOKING_MISS_WATCHDOG` paging, except that the watchdog's `rowCarriesCall` also reads the two markers in `internal_notes`, so a visit booked through Book it stops the bell. Off = the route returns `{ heldVisits: [] }` and the page looks as before. A failed load also returns an empty list. Rollback: unset the variable.

Overdue promise rings once (owner 2026-10-14): `GATE_ALERT_RING_ONCE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `alertRingOnceLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, an overdue promise bell (SMS and email, `ringOverdueBell` in `server/services/sms-operational-actions.js`) makes no new row and no ring while the promise has an open row (`done_at` empty, at any age; the `dedupeOpenOnly` option of `notifyAdmin` makes the dedupe probe skip closed rows): it only rewrites that row's text without a ring (read state, done state and push stay) and still closes stray older rows of the same key; a promise with no open row (first time, or a person marked it done and it is still overdue) gets one fresh row and one bell, even inside the old 24 hours. The kept-promise auto-close is unchanged. The call booking-miss watchdog (`GATE_CALL_BOOKING_MISS_WATCHDOG`) skips its two-hourly repeat rings; its first ring stays. The one-hour follow-up pager, the daily overdue-count summary and the promise-chaser bell are not touched. Sends nothing to a customer. Off = byte-identical to today (a 24-hour rolling dedupe, a new row and bell each day, repeat booking-miss rings). Rollback: unset the variable.

Claude's own queue (owner 2026-10-26, "ok go"; `docs/admin-notifications.md` section 5): `GATE_ALERT_CLAUDE_QUEUE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `alertClaudeQueueLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy), applied by `stampClaudeQueue` (`server/services/admin-alert-routing.js`) inside `NotificationService.create` and `notifyAdmin`. On, an admin row that is a reminder from a Claude job on the owner's Mac (`metadata.opsJob` set, `metadata.opsWho` not `person`) or one of our engineering faults (the `CLAUDE_QUEUE_CLASSES` table: category `system` with dedupeKey `sms-draft-canary:` or `ops-reminder-broken:`, category `review` with `metadata.reason` `gbp_sync_degraded` or `metadata.opsKey` `gbp-sync-health`) is written Activity-only (`metadata.feed` `activity`) and stamped `who` `claude`, `severity` (`broken` for a fault; `needs-you` for a job `ask`, `fyi` for a job `fyi`) and `claudeQueue` (the class). It no longer rings, so the bell policy (`GATE_ADMIN_BELL_POLICY`) does not silence it: the row is still written. A refresh of the keyed row (`refreshOnDedupe`) keeps it Activity-only, with or without a ring. `needs-me --who claude` lists it (an `fyi` row is never listed). Never routed: `inbound_sms`, `inbound_email`, `missed_call`, `voicemail_callback`, `new_lead`, a row with a `triggerKey`, a row tied to a customer (`customerId`, `customer_id`, `threadId`, top level or in `payload`), an `ops_digest` row, an owner ask. Rows already open move once with `node server/scripts/reroute-claude-queue-rows.js` (dry run; `--execute` writes; it only changes `metadata`, never read or done state, and refuses to run while the gate is off). Sends nothing to a customer. Off = every row lands as before, byte for byte; rows already moved stay in Activity (undo: remove the `feed`, `who`, `severity` and `claudeQueue` keys from their metadata). Rollback: unset the variable.

Name matcher v2 (dark, owner ask 2026-10-19, a dictated surname heard as a common word): `GATE_NAME_MATCH_V2` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `nameMatchV2Live()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `query_customers` ranks a dictated name with the v2 matcher (`server/services/intelligence-bar/name-match.js`, `server/utils/double-metaphone.js`): Double Metaphone keys (same key 0.9, other reading 0.85), a tolerant key ("pf" said "f", an initial "st" or "sch" may drop its s, d/t b/p g/k v/f z/s and p/f equal, one or two dropped final consonants) 0.8, a shared ending of three or more letters, words run together ("Mac Donald" = "McDonald", "Anne-Marie" = "Annemarie"), and a possessive ("Richard's dump") with no extra word. Up to 8 results. A first word that matches exactly keeps a customer at 0.6 or better. Ranking bonus +0.15 for the customer on screen, +0.10 with a visit today or tomorrow (ET), +0.05 contacted by text or call in the last 7 days; any bonus lowers the floor to 0.65. When the exact search finds exactly one customer for a name-like search, the result also carries `alternatives` (sound-alike matches, each with `score` and `reasons`) and `exact_hit_match` (`rank`, `score`, `reasons` of the exact hit among them), and a `note` that tells the model to offer choices (`offer_choices`) when the top two are close or the exact hit is not the best context match; an empty exact search still returns `approximate` rows, now ranked the v2 way. Work cap (Codex #6367): one name index of every live customer (words plus sound, first/last-three-letter and one-typo keys) is built once and kept in memory for 5 minutes, whatever the search filters are; a customer-scoped task reads its own small query and skips the cache. A call looks up only candidates that share a key with the search (rarer keys count more) and ranks up to 5,000 of them, walked in ten chunks of 500 ids: for each chunk the database applies the search's filters and scope (one id-only read) until 500 allowed survivors are found. The three context tables are read only for the survivors, even a sole survivor (context lowers the floor to 0.65), and only the survivors are scored. Limits: a typo is found when it is one wrong, missing or extra letter, or leaves a shared sound, start or end; a double slip with none of those can be missed, and a very common key (hundreds of customers) keeps the best 500 by key weight. The first call after a restart or after 5 minutes pays the build (about 0.2 to 0.5 s for 20,000 customers). Several exact hits keep the same rows but each row that fits the name gets `match`; without a sort_by the best fits come first and the note says so, with a sort_by the requested order is kept and the note says `match.score` shows the name fit. Exact-hit reranking and alternatives run only for a name search: they are skipped when the text has an address word (street, avenue, unit, FL...) or an exact row matched it on its address or city (the same rule as the admin customer pickers' sound-alike pass, `shouldSearchSoundAlike`). The call bonus counts only a call that reached someone (`whereCompletedCall` in `server/services/missed-call-text-back.js`: a bridged outbound call or a handled inbound one, never a Sandy bake-off call). Final rows are scored again by their current names, so a customer renamed inside the 5-minute index window drops out unless the new name still fits. The index is dropped when `create_customer`, `update_customer` or `bulk_update_customers` runs in the Intelligence Bar; a customer created or renamed anywhere else (booking, admin screens) appears in name search when the index expires, up to 5 minutes later. Candidate rows and the three context reads stay inside the task's customer scope (the context sets are only used for rows the scoped query returned). Read only: nothing is written or sent. Off: the original five-result sound-alike fallback that runs only on an empty exact search.

Sound-alike rows in the admin customer pickers (dark, owner ask 2026-10-21, "Orlan damp" must find "Orlan Stompf"): `GATE_CUSTOMER_SEARCH_FUZZY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `customerSearchFuzzyLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `GET /admin/customers?search=` and `GET /admin/schedule/list?search=` (the customer pickers: new appointment, Customers search, Schedule client search, estimate, invoice and Communications pickers) add up to 8 `approximate: true` rows (with `matchReasons`) AFTER the exact rows, on page 1 only, when the exact search found fewer than 3 rows and the text reads as a name (no digit, no `@`; `server/services/customer-name-search.js`, ranking from `server/services/intelligence-bar/name-match.js` v2 with its shared 5-minute name index). The exact rows, `total` and the paging do not change; the response also carries `approximateCount` (rows at the end that are approximate). The sound-alike customers are read back through the same filters and the technician's assigned-visit scope (a technician never sees a customer outside their own visits); the schedule list adds at most 25 upcoming appointments of those customers. The web pickers show the approximate rows under a "Did you mean" divider (New Appointment customer search, Customers page, Schedule client search); other pickers show them as ordinary rows. Read only: nothing is written or sent. Off: the exact search only, byte for byte. Limits: a double spelling slip with no shared sound, start or end can be missed; the first search after a restart or after 5 minutes builds the index (about 0.1 s for 20,000 customers); a service-type search with fewer than 3 hits can show similar-named customers.

Day-only agreement shadow (dark, owner 2026-10-20, PR 1 of 2): `GATE_DAY_AGREEMENT_SHADOW` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('dayAgreementShadow')` by the `*/10` cron tick in `server/services/scheduler.js` (job `day-agreement-shadow`, under `runExclusive`; an off gate takes no lock and leaves no `job_health` row) and again by `runDayAgreementShadow` in `server/services/day-agreement-shadow.js`. On = every 10 minutes the sweep judges, once each, (a) two-party calls (never a voicemail, spam or voice-agent sandbox call) whose pipeline verdict landed in the last 3 hours and whose valid V2 extraction has `scheduling.status` `requested`, `reschedule_requested`, `ambiguous` or `offered`, and (b) phones whose latest inbound text is under 3 hours old, holds a day word (weekday name, today, tomorrow, m/d date, ordinal) (or a day-less latest reply that follows a delivered Waves text with a day word sent in the 3 hours before it) and whose thread has had no text either way for 30 minutes; a customer's own day-word text answered by a delivered Waves text before a day-less reply also counts; each text candidate is rechecked right before its model call and left unjudged if it is no longer the latest inbound text or no longer quiet (only inbound texts and Waves texts that went out count; app-only push deliveries and recruiting `job_*` texts are ignored, in the probe and in the thread the model reads). A source with no linked customer is recorded as a skip without a model call. Each judged source costs ONE model call (`TEXT_POLICIES.deepAnalysis` (the DEEP judge tier, 4096 output tokens), lane `day_agreement`, prompt `day-agreement-v1`; at most 4 calls and 4 threads a tick; an unusable answer fails its leg so the OpenAI backup gets a turn). The model names each agreement moment (a day agreed for one visit, or a move of one, with no clock time); deterministic rules (`server/services/day-agreement-rules.js`) then keep it only when `act` is true with no blocker listed and confidence 0.7 or more (for a text, the moment's time must be readable and be the minute of a message in the thread, else `at_ungrounded`), the day is after today ET, the source is linked to a customer, staff have not already created or moved a visit of that customer onto the day since the agreement, a move has exactly one pending or confirmed visit on the old day, and the customer has no live visit already on the day. Visits changed after the agreement are left out of the context the model sees, with a count. The model's kind, days and daypart are stored only in their vocabulary (else null), and an answer with a confidence outside 0 to 1, or an action with a bad kind, day or daypart, is unusable (the backup model gets a turn). A sweep with an error or a model outage ends as a failed run in `job_health`. A new visit also needs ONE catalog service: the model is shown the bookable service names and copies one, and the sweep resolves it through the call booking resolver (`call-booking-catalog.js`); a missing, unknown, multi-service or generic service (the anything-appointment, the assessment) is recorded as `service_unresolved` and the picker is never asked. A new visit for a customer with more than one active service property is recorded as `property_ambiguous` (the conversation names no property); a failed or empty catalog read leaves the source unjudged, to be retried on the next tick. A move keeps the moved visit's own service and pin. For a passing moment the sweep asks `findAvailableSlots` (`server/services/scheduling/find-time.js`; service identity and catalog length passed the way other new-booking callers do, so a technician switched off for that kind of work is not offered) for that one day, keeps whole-hour starts inside the daypart, and records the first slot it would take, or `no_slot`. Every moment is one `day_agreement_decisions` row (`would_book`, `would_move` or `skip` with its reason; never a transcript or a message). SHADOW ONLY: it books nothing, moves nothing and texts no one; the act step is a later PR. A week of rows is scored against what staff did by a read-only query. Off = byte-identical to today. Rollback: unset the variable; the table stays.

Missed-call bell robodialer wave (dark, owner 2026-10-20 "yes" after the call audit, narrowed after Codex #6392 r2): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_SPAM_WAVE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('missedCallSpamWave')` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js`. The 60-day call audit found a robodialer wave: from 2026-09-30, 18 different 941-236-xxxx numbers called only the Google Business Profile lines, each hanging up near 24 s with no voicemail, and rang 11 missed-call bells. A wave call = an unknown caller (no customer on the call and the number on no customer phone slot) on a `gbp_tracking` line, under 30 s, whose 6-digit number block (area code + exchange) sent 3 or more different unknown numbers inside 14 days, the call itself included and itself a wave member (no recording, unanswered, not AI-handled, not called back). **A wave quiets the push and keeps the bell; it never stops a text.** Why (Codex security): a caller can prime a number block with a few fresh numbers so a genuine first-time prospect matches, and real people who hang up at the voicemail beep cluster on one length, so no spam rule may remove delivery evidence. **On:** the bell row is still written, no push is sent (`beforePush` returns false), the call is stamped `missed_call_spam_wave: 'block_quiet'` and settles normally once the row is written. The push is quieted only when this pass wrote the bell row and the quiet marker was stored; otherwise it goes as usual (fail open). The push-check retry (`GATE_MISSED_CALL_PUSH_CHECK`) and its daily alert do not fire for it: a skipped push is not "reached no phone". The 30-minute re-push (`GATE_MISSED_CALL_REPUSH`) skips a `block_quiet` call too. **Off (default, shadow):** the bell and push go exactly as before and the call is stamped `missed_call_spam_wave_shadow: true`, so a week of shadow can be read before the flip. **Text-back:** this gate never stops a text; `server/services/missed-call-text-back.js` only stamps `missed_call_text_spam_shadow: 'block'` (or `'burst'`) on the call, whichever spam gates are on, so the pattern stays measurable. (A caller who failed the press-1 screen is skipped by `GATE_MISSED_CALL_TEXT_SKIP_FAILED_SCREEN`, a separate rule.) Customers on file always ring. Bell push only, no customer comms. Kill: unset or set anything but `true`.
Missed-call bell robodialer burst (dark, owner 2026-10-20 "ALL", narrowed after Codex #6392 r1): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_SPAM_BURST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('missedCallSpamBurst')` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js` (`isRobodialerBurst`). The second robodialer pattern: rotating number prefixes, so no 6-digit block repeats (on 2026-10-16 five numbers called one Bradenton GBP line, 53-54 s each, none ever called again). A burst member = an unknown caller (no customer on the call, the number on no live customer phone slot, full-country keys), North American number, FIRST call ever from that number (no earlier `call_log` row on the same phone key), unanswered by the bell's own rule, no recording, not AI-handled, 15 s or more. A call is a BURST when, on the same `to_phone` line (last 10 digits) in the previous 24 h with the call itself included, 3 or more different member numbers have a length within 1 s of this call's, the call itself is a member, and each passes `calledBackSql({ retire: true })` (nobody later got through). Any line type.
