The 60-day production backtest found exactly those 5 calls: 0 got through, 0 texted, 0 became customers. **A burst quiets the push and keeps the bell; it never stops a text.** Why (Codex security): the rule is a pattern, not proof. A caller can prime a line and a length with two fresh numbers so the third genuine first-time prospect matches, and real people who hang up at the voicemail beep cluster on one length. So no spam rule removes delivery evidence. **On:** the bell row is still written, no push is sent (`beforePush` returns false, composed with the supersession check), the call is stamped `missed_call_spam_wave: 'burst_quiet'` and settles normally once the row is written. The push is quieted only when this pass wrote the bell row and the quiet marker was stored; otherwise it goes as usual (fail open). The push-check retry (`GATE_MISSED_CALL_PUSH_CHECK`) and its daily alert do not fire for it: a skipped push is not "reached no phone" The 30-minute re-push (`GATE_MISSED_CALL_REPUSH`) skips a `burst_quiet` call too. **Off (default, shadow):** the bell and push go exactly as before and the call is stamped `missed_call_spam_burst_shadow: true`. **Text-back:** this gate never stops a text; a burst is stamped `missed_call_text_spam_shadow: 'burst'` whether the gate is on or off, so the pattern stays measurable. (A caller who failed the press-1 screen is skipped by `GATE_MISSED_CALL_TEXT_SKIP_FAILED_SCREEN`, a separate rule.) If a call is both a block wave and a burst and both gates are on, it is stamped `block_quiet`. Customers on file always ring. Any classifier error fails open. It never adds a customer text, email or call. Kill: unset or set anything but `true`.
Missed-call text-back skips a failed press-1 screen (dark, owner ruling 2026-10-24 "this should be fixed": no text-back to robocalls): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_TEXT_SKIP_FAILED_SCREEN` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('missedCallTextSkipFailedScreen')` in `server/services/missed-call-text-back.js` (`precheckRow`). The pre-connect screen (`GATE_CALL_PRECONNECT_SCREEN`, `server/routes/twilio-voice-webhook.js`) asks an unknown caller on STIR/SHAKEN attestation B to press 1 and stamps `call_log.metadata.preconnect_screen` `'failed'` when no key came and the call fell to the voicemail recorder. **On:** such a call gets no text-back; it settles `missed_call_text_outcome: 'skipped:screen_failed'` and takes no claim. Only the explicit `'failed'` stamp counts: `'passed'`, `'gated'` (a lost pass/fail write), `'would_gate'` (screen off) and no stamp text as before. Production evidence (2026-10-24): in the 4 weeks before, 17 of the lane's 27 texts went to failed-screen callers (16 in the Oct 14-16 robocall bursts: 37-38 s empty voicemails and 53 s calls with no voicemail; 8 of the 17 were delivered); over 90 days, 229 failed-screen calls came from 212 numbers and no text-back case among them was a real prospect (the 3 real callers were under 15 s or left a spoken voicemail, which this lane never texts). Unlike the robodialer pattern rules above, a caller cannot be primed into it: a real person passes by pressing 1. The missed-call bell, the voicemail lane and the voicemail quote-link text are unchanged. It never adds a customer text, email or call; it only withholds the text-back. **Off (default):** byte-identical to before. Kill: unset or set anything but `true`.
Estimate PDF on the email (owner ask 2026-10-19: "attach a pdf version of the estimates to all outgoing emails for customers who can't open the estimate"; and "I don't want the glass UI for the pdf"): `GATE_ESTIMATE_EMAIL_PDF` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true` in production** (on in dev and test), read through `featureGates.isEnabled('estimateEmailPdf')` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`), which snapshots the environment at boot like the other gates: a Railway variable change restarts the service, and that restart applies it. Needs `GATE_ESTIMATE_DOC_PDF` ALSO on (live): the attachment is the browser-rendered work-order document only, never the pdfkit commercial "Proposal" and never the glass page, so with either gate off nothing attaches. On, an open-estimate email carries `Waves-Estimate-<estimate number>.pdf` (no customer name in the file name; the number is `estimate_slug`, else a short id) and a one-line note under the button, the payload variable `estimate_pdf_note` added by migration `20261019200000_estimate_email_pdf_note` as a block directly after the first button of 14 templates; migration `20261019210000_estimate_email_pdf_note_paragraph` then retypes that block from `small_note` (13px) to `paragraph` (15px) on every template that carries it, because customer copy has a 14px floor. Covered: the delivery email (`estimate.delivery`, non-proposal only; a commercial proposal keeps its own PDF path), the follow-ups and engagement nudges (`estimate.unviewed_followup`, `viewed_followup`, `followup_final`, `expiring_notice`, `engage_unopened`, `engage_gone_quiet`, `engage_expiring`, `engage_expiring_unseen`, `engage_high_intent`, `engage_return_visit`, `engage_return_after_dark`; one explicit allowlist in `server/services/estimate-email-pdf.js`, used by `sendDualChannel`), the extension email (`estimate.extended`). The auto-renew notice (`estimate.extension_notice`) carries NO PDF (one send path fewer: the live automation executor path never could, and the direct path was dropped); its template still holds the note block, which renders blank. Never covered: `estimate.deposit_abandoned`, `estimate.payment_step_abandoned`, the accepted-estimate emails. A follow-up attaches only when a fresh row read shows the estimate still open (`sent` or `viewed`, not archived, not past its expiry). Rate-review disclosure evidence for this customer-emailed copy follows the documented rule that a missed marker costs a frozen document its line while an extra marker would give it a line the customer never saw: before the render `buildEstimateEmailPdfAttachment` only CHECKS (on clones of the row, `documentPrintsRateReviewTerms`; unknown, such as a failed check, means no attachment: the browser renderer cannot withhold the line and this copy has no pdfkit fallback), and `estimate_data.rateReviewTermsServed` is written by `recordRateReviewTermsServedOutcome` only AFTER the provider accepted the email that carried the file (the delivery send, the follow-ups and the extension email; the write is SQL-guarded and never touches a frozen estimate). A failed render, a fence veto or a provider rejection therefore leaves no marker. A cancel or reschedule of the linked appointment between the render and the handoff vetoes a document that says "Confirm appointment / your appointment stays as scheduled" (the acceptance contract is part of the compared payload); an unrelated scheduled-services change does not. The fence refuses any estimate that is in a multi-property group at the handoff, whenever the group formed (it never records a group verdict as its baseline); the delivery review records its PDF decision on SMTP-fallback previews too (no note line there; the SMTP content hash is unchanged) and a reviewed or scheduled SMTP send attaches the file only when that decision is true. Once a follow-up (or the delivery send) has passed eligibility and starts rendering, the send always carries a provider-boundary fence: when the render returns nothing (after the busy waits), the email goes out with no file and no note but behind a fence WITHOUT a document fingerprint (open state or the claimed `sending` state, expiry, address, call-side checks), so an accept, decline or address correction during the wait vetoes it like any other fence abort (the stage is released when no text went out); paths that return before any render (gate off, not allowlisted, closed, grouped) are unchanged. The row fingerprint also covers `satellite_url`, `estimate_slug` and `created_at`, the other columns the document projects. The delivery send's whole PDF step (decision, address check, fence, render) is `prepareDeliveryPdfCopy` in `estimate-email-pdf.js`. The handoff-fence fingerprint is taken from the row as the database returned it, so a billing resolution that mutates its input cannot make the fence veto its own send. The document's action button and Next steps copy follow the server's acceptance contract (`estimate.acceptance.mode`) with EstimateViewPage's wording: standard Accept & pick a start date, existing appointment Confirm appointment, invoice-only Accept + send invoice, commercial site confirmation Approve estimate, and call/email only for contact-office, quote-required, inspection-request or any other mode; Next steps text is 14px. An already-ACCEPTED estimate keeps the "See your visit details" wording only for the standard and existing-appointment modes; every other mode (invoice-only, office-only, commercial site confirmation, ...) reads "View your estimate" and "This estimate has been approved. Your estimate at <link> has the details.", with no visit promise. The decisions live in a pure resolver, `resolveDocNextSteps` in `client/src/pages/estimateDocumentNextSteps.jsx`, not in the document component. The render drives `/estimate/:token?mode=pdf` with a signed pin (no view count, no "viewed" alert), waits and retries up to 3 times (8 s apart) while the render capacity is busy, and returns nothing on any other failure: the email then goes out exactly as today, with no file and no note, and the delivery channel result carries `pdfAttached: false` plus a warning (`pdfAttached: true` when attached). The delivery review preview shows the note when the gate is on, so a reviewed `messageVersion` covers it; the reviewed `contentHash` is the template-version hash and the note is a payload variable, so it is unaffected. A review made before the gate flipped goes stale ("review again"). The SMTP fallback path attaches the file but has no note. SendGrid-sent rows record `has_attachments`, which keeps a bounced PDF email out of the body-only bounce-recovery replay. Grouped (multi-property) estimates carry no PDF copy and no note, on the delivery send and on the follow-ups: an estimate whose `estimate_group_id` has any other non-archived member is skipped (`estimateInMultiPropertyGroup`, the one definition the review preview, the send and the follow-ups share), because the shared link renders the whole group but the document is one property's. The delivery review records its PDF decision (`messages.email.pdfCopy`, present only when true) with the review and with a schedule built from it; at send time a decision that no longer matches (gate flipped, estimate joined a group) rejects the send as `ESTIMATE_REVIEW_STALE` so the office re-reviews, and a review with no stored decision (an old schedule, a review made with the gate off) means no PDF and no note and is never stale. The delivery fence also requires the row to still be in its claimed `sending` state (a decline, accept or release during the render vetoes the send). The notes are mode-neutral (they also go to existing-appointment, invoice-only and office-only estimates): delivery "Can't open the link? A PDF copy of this estimate is attached. Reply to this email or call (941) 297-5749 with any questions or to go ahead.", follow-up "Your estimate is attached as a PDF if the link won't open. Reply or call (941) 297-5749 with any questions."; migration `20261019220000_estimate_extension_notice_pdf_note_fixture` blanks the sample note in the `estimate.extension_notice` preview fixtures (the auto-renew notice carries no file). Migration `20261019230000_estimate_email_pdf_note_fixture_copy` replaces the old seeded sample notes in the delivery and 12 follow-up preview fixtures with the current text (exact old value only; admin edits kept). The handoff fence compares the document's own input instead of listing inputs one by one (codex #6343 r14, after four rounds each adding another): `fullFingerprint` is the row fingerprint (columns plus a hash of the rendered `estimate_data`) joined with a hash of the payload the headless page renders. `documentInputHash` builds that payload exactly as `GET /:token/data` serves the signed-pin pdf pass (`reconcileFrozenMembershipSnapshot` on a CLONE of the row, then `composeEstimateDataPayload` with `isPdfRenderPass` and the render pin's valid-through date), at capture and at the handoff of both the follow-up and the delivery fence; the no-file fence keeps no fingerprint. The projection keeps what `EstimateProposalDocument` prints (estimate: id, token, slug, contact name, phone, email and address after the linked customer or lead fill, category, createdAt, expiresAt, satelliteUrl, licenseNumber, the guarantee flags, the acceptance contract with its linked appointment, the pricing intelligence body and metrics; plus proposal, cta, acceptance, publicOrigin, documentRender), so a staff edit to the linked customer's phone, a billing or membership change, an appointment move or a line-item edit all veto the send (`estimate_changed_since_render`). The per-request fields are left out: `estimate.askToken` (a JWT with a fresh issue time) and `meta.generatedAt`, plus the page-only `meta.cacheHit` and blocks the document never reads; two payloads of one unchanged estimate differ in exactly `askToken` and `generatedAt`. The pdf pass writes nothing (no view count, first-view flip, served-disclosure evidence, park alert or consultation probe). A failed composition is a fence read failure (no PDF at render time, a retryable check failure at the handoff); the delivery send leaves the printed date out because it persists `expires_at` later. The emailed render fails closed on a broken image: `renderEstimateDocumentPdf` takes an opt-in `failOnImageErrors` (only `buildEstimateEmailPdfAttachment` passes it) that reads the page's `window.__WAVES_PDF_IMAGE_FAILURES` counter after the render and throws `estimate_doc_image_failed` when it is above zero (the satellite snapshot failed to load), so the email goes out link-only through the usual no-file fence path; an unreadable or absent counter never fails a render, and the customer Download route keeps its map-less document. The channel result's `pdfAttached` reports what went out: `true` only for a fresh provider-accepted send that carried the file, `false` plus the warning when that send had no file, and for a deduped answer (an earlier message already covered this send) it reports that message's persisted `has_attachments` or, when the library does not return it, leaves `pdfAttached` out; the rate-review disclosure marker is never written for a deduped result. A PDF email is NOT on the provider-retry rail (`transactional-email-provider-retry.js` skips `has_attachments` rows, as on main). A failed follow-up or engagement email is retried by the sweep re-running the whole touch: with no text sent the stage claim is released, so the next tick goes through every first-send check again (follow-up SMS are off by owner ruling 2026-09-28; a stage with an active SMS template that sent its text would keep the claim and not retry the email). A failed delivery email shows as failed to the operator, like the invoice PDFs. On first sends, a PDF-bearing email passes a final fence at the provider handoff: the row unchanged since the render apart from view and charge bookkeeping (a hash of the rendered `estimate_data` content and the identity and pricing columns), still open, not expired, not invalidated or call-blocked, and the address still the estimate's current `customer_email`. A failed fence skips that send. The manual delivery send (`admin-estimates.js`) builds its PDF only when the address it is sending to equals the freshly read row's `customer_email`, and passes the same fence (`deliveryPdfFence`: address, content fingerprint without the persisted expiry, archived, invalidation and call-side checks) to the provider handoff; a veto fails the email channel with an error the operator sees ("the estimate changed ... the email was not sent"), never a silent send. Off = byte-identical to today (blank `estimate_pdf_note` drops its block; no `attachments` key on follow-up sends). Rollback: unset the variable.
Monthly average beside per-application prices (owner ruling 2026-10-20, "option A", narrowing the 2026-07-23/31 rule): `GATE_ESTIMATE_MONTHLY_AVERAGE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true` in production** (on in dev and test), read through `featureGates.isEnabled('estimateMonthlyAverage')` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`), which snapshots the environment at boot; a Railway variable change restarts the service and that restart applies it. The per-application price STAYS the price. On, a residential per-application estimate adds a second, smaller line "$X a month" and the context "Averaged over the year. You pay after each application." `$X/mo` or `$X/month` AS THE PRICE stays banned. Three surfaces: (1) the delivery email (`estimate.delivery`, non-proposal): the `price_summary` value (the Estimated price row) reads "$94.00 per application · $31.33 a month" for one service or "Priced per application · plan averages $72.30 a month" for several (the per-application prices stay the prices; the average never stands alone as the price), and the context sentence rides at the FRONT of the existing `next_step_summary` paragraph (no new payload variable, no template block, no migration: gate off, the payload is byte-identical; `moneySummary(estimate, { average })` and `estimateEmailPayload({ average })` in `admin-estimates.js`, resolved by `emailAverageParts` in `server/services/estimate-monthly-average.js` for both the review preview and the send); (2) the estimate PDF document (`EstimateProposalDocument.jsx`): "$X a month" under each per-application line, a plan line "Your plan averages (N% bundle savings included)" when there are two or more services, the context line, and "One-time charges are not in the average." when one-time lines exist; the server sends `proposal.monthlyAverage` only on the PDF pass; (3) the estimate page: `/data` carries `monthlyAverageEnabled: true` (absent gate off) and `EstimateViewPage.jsx` derives the figures from the SELECTED cadences (`client/src/lib/estimateMonthlyAverage.js`), so a cadence change restates them: "$X a month" under each card's per-application price (`PriceCard`), and for two or more services a `MonthlyAverageSummary` card with the per-service lines, a credit line when a plan credit is not itemized into the sections, and the plan line. The legacy server-rendered page (`renderPage` in `estimate-public.js`: `use_v2_view=false` rows and the GrowthBook control; the `/api/estimates/:token` mount) prints the same lines from the same builder: "$X a month" under each per-application card, a plan summary for two or more services (or a credited one), and the context sentence, only when its cards reconcile to the stored `monthly_total` and the plan is open, per-application and not commercial; a preference change or the annual-prepay choice hides them client-side rather than restating them. The email average is resolved from the row read just before the send. A review (and a schedule built from it) records the exact average copy as `messages.email.monthlyAverage` (absent = none); a reviewed or scheduled send recomputes it and refuses with `ESTIMATE_REVIEW_STALE` when it differs, including an old review with no record when the send would now add one, or a recorded one when the gate is now off, before any channel sends (SMTP reviews and text-only sends are exempt); the email build compares the exact copy it is about to hand the provider with the reviewed one a second time, and an edit that landed in between fails the email channel with the same stale text (`uncertain` false, nothing dispatched). One shared builder (`shared/estimate-monthly-average.cjs`, alias `@estimate-monthly-average`) serves all three, so they cannot differ by a cent. It never prices: the per-service average is shown per-application price x applications / 12 (the per-application prices on every surface are already NET of the WaveGuard bundle discount), the plan average is the estimate's STORED `monthly_total`, and the per-service lines are made to add up to it to the cent by moving the rounding difference one cent at a time, largest line first. A gap larger than rounding (0.05) is accepted only when a declared plan credit (`manualDiscount`) explains it, and then prints as its own negative line; any other gap (a stale stored total, a flat-monthly line, a missing service) withholds the average and the surface renders exactly as before. One-time charges never enter the average, and every surface says so when one sits beside the plan: a setup or first-visit fee, or an ADDITIVE one-time row (a flea treatment); on the PDF and email a one-time option on offer (`show_one_time_option`) makes the proposal's one-time rows the either/or alternative, so only the bundle's positive first-visit fees count then (`firstVisitFees`, else `setupFee`, the page's fee list), and the "One-time setup" wording is by identity, never by wording: it applies only when every counted dollar is the `waveguard_setup` fee (a fee, or a `waveguard_setup` breakdown row), else the email reads "One-time charges $X, not in the average." A plan credit is read from the SELECTED service-cadence combo (its own `manualDiscount` and `manualDiscountSuppressed`) on the page, the PDF and the email (the candidate the document's lines were quoted from, `perApplicationRecurringResolution`), and from the top-level frequency then the bundle root only when no combo is selected. Commercial is the canonical classifier (`services/estimate-commercial-identity.js`: the `commercialEstimatedPricing` marker, estimated-pricing commercial lines or commercial rows, or category COMMERCIAL), not the category alone. Unchanged with the gate on: commercial proposals and commercial estimates, quote-required estimates, one-time-only estimates, monthly-billed members, the annual-prepay choice, and accepted, declined, quote-required (and, on the page and the PDF, expired) estimates on every surface (the document pass follows the page's own terminal state; the email reads the row status and the stored quote requirement), and the pdfkit fallback document. The follow-up emails (`estimate-follow-up.js` `moneySummary`) are not covered. For one spaced service plus monthly services with no plan credit, the summary card shows the per-application prices, the month amounts and the average, and the payment preview row reads "First application". Rollback: unset the variable.
Monthly average in the estimate follow-up emails (owner 2026-10-21, "follow-ups too"): `GATE_ESTIMATE_FOLLOWUP_MONTHLY_AVERAGE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true` in production** (on in dev and test), read through `featureGates.isEnabled('estimateFollowupMonthlyAverage')` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`, snapshot at boot; a Railway variable change restarts the service and that restart applies it). It also needs `GATE_ESTIMATE_MONTHLY_AVERAGE` ON, because the figures come from the same resolver. Covers the four follow-up emails that render the price row: `estimate.unviewed_followup`, `estimate.viewed_followup`, `estimate.followup_final` and `estimate.expiring_notice` (`withMonthlyAverage` in `server/services/estimate-follow-up.js`, wrapped around `estimateEmailPayload` at the four senders). On, `price_summary` reads the delivery email's copy ("$94.00 per application · $31.33 a month" for one service, "Priced per application · plan averages $72.30 a month" for several; today it reads "Priced per application — full breakdown inside") and the new payload variable `estimate_average_note` carries the context sentence ("Averaged over the year. You pay after each application.", with the bundle, credit and one-time clauses). The figures come from `emailAverageParts` in `server/services/estimate-monthly-average.js`, the delivery email's own resolver and eligibility, applied to the `estimates` row read at send time (no reviewed copy exists for follow-ups, so no stale check): commercial (category or data marker), quote-required, accepted or declined rows, annual-prepay or monthly-billed plans and one-time-only estimates get no average, and the payload stays the very same object it was. The average is added only when the template's ACTIVE version (read through `loadTemplateByKey`) references BOTH `{{price_summary}}` and `{{estimate_average_note}}` in its blocks and its plain-text body is blank or references both, so a template the migration skipped never prints the average row without its context sentence. The send is pinned to the version it checked: when the average is applied the email carries that version's id to `sendTemplate` as `versionId`, so an admin publish between the check and the send cannot put the average copy into a version without the tokens (`sendTemplate` sends a pinned version even after a newer one is active; a disabled template still refuses). Without the average no `versionId` is set. The copy is also re-checked at the provider boundary: the email carries a `withProviderHandoff` (composed with the PDF fence when `GATE_ESTIMATE_EMAIL_PDF` built one, PDF fence first) whose check reads the estimate row again right before the provider request and recomputes the average text with the same resolver. A different text, an estimate that no longer qualifies or a missing row vetoes the send (`providerBoundaryBlocked`, reason `monthly_average_changed`); a read failure is `providerBoundaryCheckFailed`. Both are definite non-sends, so the stage claim is released (when no text went out) and the next sweep sends fresh copy. A follow-up carrying the average is also stamped with the category `estimate_followup_monthly_average` (`server/constants/email-replay-exclusions.js`) and is NOT eligible for the stored-copy rails, like a PDF row: `transactional-email-provider-retry.js` schedules no retry for it on a provider block, `claimDueRetries` skips it and `retryOne` stops one that is somehow scheduled; `email-bounce-recovery.js` skips it (`monthly_average_not_replayed`, staff get the suggested address). A provider rejection with no text sent returns not-attempted, the stage claim is released, and the next sweep re-runs the touch with fresh copy under the same idempotency key. Follow-ups without the average keep the retry rail unchanged. A failure resolving the average or reading the template logs a warning and sends the follow-up as it was. Unlike the delivery email, the sentence cannot ride in an existing paragraph variable (these four templates have none), so migration `20261021010000_estimate_followup_average_note.js` publishes one new active version of each template with a paragraph block `{{estimate_average_note}}` right after the details block holding the price row (the 20261019210000 pattern: template row locked, compare-and-swap on the active version, admin edits kept, a custom plain-text body or a template without the price row left whole and logged, preview fixtures gain a sample); `20261021020000_estimate_followup_average_fixture_price.js` then replaces the four templates' seeded fixture price sample `$89/mo` with the single-service price row, only where it still equals that exact value; `20261021030000_estimate_followup_average_fixture_price_restore.js` puts `$89/mo` back for any of the four whose ACTIVE version does not show the average (the note migration skipped it), only where the fixture still holds the new value. A paragraph that renders blank is dropped, so gate off the four emails are byte-identical (proved against the real shipped templates by `estimate-followup-average-note-migration-postgres.test.js`). Not covered: `estimate.extended` and `estimate.extension_notice` (no price row, no price in their payload), the `estimate.engage_*` emails (no price row), the deposit and payment-step emails. Kill switch: unset the variable. Known limit: a follow-up carrying the average that SendGrid accepts and later blocks (webhook block event) is not re-sent from its stored copy and its stage stays done, so that one reminder is lost; the next follow-up stage still sends. The same holds for PDF-bearing follow-ups (#6343).

Email schedule send (owner 2026-10-22, "build it like Gmail has it"): `GATE_EMAIL_SEND_LATER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`emailSendLaterLive()`, `server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, the admin email composer and reply box get an arrow beside Send with Gmail's Schedule send choices (tomorrow morning 8 AM, tomorrow afternoon 1 PM, Monday morning 8 AM, pick date and time; all Eastern), Email gets a Scheduled tab with Cancel send (the email comes back as a draft), `POST /api/admin/email/schedule` queues a row in `scheduled_emails`, and a once-a-minute cron (`server/services/email/scheduled-email-sender.js`, job `scheduled-email-send`) sends due rows through the same Gmail path as Send. Each row goes out at most once: a possible acceptance or a claim older than 10 minutes becomes `outcome_unknown` and is never retried; three definite Gmail refusals make it `failed`; both ring one Comms admin alert. Off = no arrow, no tab, the schedule and cancel routes answer 404 `{enabled:false}`, the list answers `{enabled:false}`, and the cron sends nothing; rows already queued stay queued, unsent, until the gate is on again. Sends customer email only at a time an office user picked; the flip is the owner's. Rollback: unset the variable.

Missed-call alert detail (dark, owner "ALL" 2026-10-20): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_ALERT_DETAIL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('missedCallAlertDetail')` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`) at each ring. On, the `customer_missed_call` bell and push body names the line the caller dialed (`call_log.metadata.location`, shortened to about 26 characters; the webhook's `unknown` placeholder is left out), the call length in seconds (only a positive length, by `callDurationSeconds`; a stored 0 means not reported and is left out) and, for a customer on file, the date of their next visit (earliest `scheduled_services` row dated today or later in ET whose status is not cancelled, completed or rescheduled), for example "(941) 555-0100 called Parrish (Pest), 12 sec, no voicemail. Next visit Thu Oct 22." The producer (`ringMissedCallIfUnanswered` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js`) adds `line`, `durationSeconds` and `nextVisitDate` to the trigger payload through `detailPayload` in `server/services/missed-call-alert-detail.js`; the trigger's `build()` formats them with `formatMissedCallBody` and prints today's sentence when none of those fields is present, so a bell rung before a flip keeps its text. A failed visit lookup leaves the visit out and never delays the alert. Admin bell and push only; nothing is sent to a customer. Off: the payload and body are today's, byte for byte ("<phone> called and did not leave a voicemail."). Kill: unset and redeploy; rows already written keep their text.

Missed-call re-push (dark, owner "ALL" 2026-10-20): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_REPUSH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('missedCallRepush')` by the 2-minute call-alert cron in `server/services/scheduler.js` (off = the sweep module is not even loaded). On, `sweepMissedCallRepush` (`server/services/missed-call-repush.js`) re-sends the push ONCE for a `customer_missed_call` bell that is still unread (`read_at` NULL) and not done (`done_at` NULL, so a bell retired because the caller got through or left a voicemail is skipped) 30 minutes after it was created and no more than 48 hours old, and only in office hours: Monday to Saturday inside the `booking_config` day window (8:00 to 18:00 ET by default) and not on a blackout day (`loadOfficeHours` / `isOfficeOpenAt`, `server/services/voice-agent/relay-context.js`; Sunday is always closed here; an unknown closure state counts as closed). The re-push uses the call's own tag `waves-customer_missed_call-<callLogId>` with `renotify: true` so the phone buzzes again instead of silently replacing the first banner, the row's stored title, body and link, the same recipients as the first push (active admins whose `customer_missed_call` preference has push on), and the bell policy check. It writes no new bell row. At most once: one atomic UPDATE stamps `metadata.repushed_at` (re-checking the row is still unread and open) inside the push service's `beforeDispatch` hook, after the subscription lookup and right before the first provider handoff (so a failed lookup never uses up the re-push), and only that writer sends; office hours and the strictly read closed-day list are rechecked at the claim and before each device, an unreadable closed-day list counts as closed, and a failed `retireCalledBackMissedCalls` ends the tick with nothing sent, so overlapping instances and later ticks never repeat it; the outcome is stamped as `metadata.repush_sent` (devices reached), and a crash after the stamp loses the re-push rather than repeating it. At most 20 bells per tick. Admin push only; nothing is sent to a customer. Off: no sweep work. Kill: unset and redeploy; stamped rows stay stamped.
Missed-call bell: customer's empty voicemail (owner 2026-10-20, "ALL", after the call audit; admin bell only, no customer text, email or call): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_EMPTY_VM_CUSTOMER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `gapOptions()` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js`. On: a customer on file (`call_log.customer_id`) who reached voicemail and left a recording the processor found empty (`isEmptyVoicemailRecording`: rejected transcription with no text, or only no-speech markers; a recording still awaiting transcription never counts) rings the missed-call bell like any other unanswered customer call. `ringMissedCallIfUnanswered` and `sweepMissedCalls` admit the row, and the claim, the re-read before the push and the post-delivery check pin the very recording, transcription status and transcription text that were read, so a newer recording or a re-transcription loses the race. Unknown callers, real voicemails (the voicemail lane) and the text-back lane (which passes its own `emptyVoicemail` option) are unchanged. Off: no bell change; the 2-minute sweep stamps `metadata.missed_call_gap_shadow = 'empty_vm_customer'` once on each call the gate would have rung, so the flip's effect can be counted first. Rollback: unset the variable.

Missed-call bell: customer call that ended with no outcome (owner 2026-10-20, "ALL"; admin bell only): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_NO_OUTCOME_CUSTOMER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `gapOptions()`. On: an inbound call from a customer on file with status `completed`, `answered_by` NULL, no recording and no `ai_handled` / `ai_transferred` outcome counts as unanswered for the missed-call bell (the `/call-status` fallback insert in `server/routes/twilio-voice-webhook.js` and `server/services/call-ingest-watchdog.js` write no `answered_by`, so such a call never rang). The same later-call rules still retire it: a redial that was answered, a Sandy-handled call or an alerted voicemail. Unknown callers are unchanged. Off: no bell change; the sweep stamps `metadata.missed_call_gap_shadow = 'no_outcome_customer'` once on each call the gate would have rung. Rollback: unset the variable.

A callback counts only when the customer answered (owner 2026-10-20, "ALL"; admin bell only): `GATE_CALLBACK_NEEDS_ANSWER` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `calledBackSql()` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js`. The "caller got through" test (`CALLED_BACK_SQL`) counted an outbound call with `bridged_at` as a callback, but `bridged_at` is stamped when staff press 1, before the customer leg is dialed, so a callback that rang out silenced the missed-call bell and retired an open one. On: an outbound call counts only with proof the customer answered: `metadata.customer_leg.status = 'completed'` with seconds above 0, or, where `customer_leg` is missing (it is written on a minority of bridged calls), a recording of the call (the bridge records from answer, so a recording exists only once the customer picked up), or, for the claim, the sweep and the re-read before the push only (never for retiring a bell, and never for the post-delivery retire), a bridged call still in flight (`status = 'bridged'`, within 15 minutes of the bridge), so no bell rings during a live callback and a callback still ringing never retires one; a bell write suppressed only by that in-flight arm releases the call instead of settling it, so the sweep rings it if the callback then rings out. The parent-leg `duration_seconds` is not used: it holds the 8-second press-1 prompt plus the 30-second ring. One switch covers the claim, the sweep, the re-read before the push and `retireCalledBackMissedCalls`. Off: the SQL is byte-identical to before. Rollback: unset the variable.
Missed-call bell skips a visit already underway (dark, owner 2026-10-21; admin bell only): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_VISIT_UNDERWAY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read through `isEnabled('missedCallVisitUnderway')` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js` (`visitUnderwaySql`, used by the claim, the 2-minute sweep, the re-read before the push, `retireCalledBackMissedCalls` and the post-delivery retire) and `server/services/missed-call-repush.js` (`callStillMissed`). A customer on file called at 1:05 PM and nobody answered; the tech went en route at 1:46, arrived at 1:59 and the invoice was paid at 2:32, and the missed-call bell still sat open. On: a call whose customer has a `scheduled_services` row with `en_route_at`, `arrived_at` or `completed_at` later than the call's `created_at`, or an `invoices` row with `paid_at` later than the call, on the SAME Eastern day as the call (the ET date of each timestamp, not the UTC date), counts as handled. The open `customer_missed_call` bell is retired by the sweep with the resolution `The customer's visit went ahead after the call` (a separate pass from the called-back retire, which keeps its own wording), a bell that has not rung yet does not ring, and the 30-minute re-push (`GATE_MISSED_CALL_REPUSH`) does not buzz it. A visit or payment before the call, on another ET day, or for another customer changes nothing, and a call with no customer on it (an unknown caller) is never affected. Admin bell and push only; it adds no customer text, email or call. Off: no clause is added anywhere and the SQL and the retire sweep are byte-identical to before. Rollback: unset the variable.

Missed-call push check (owner 2026-10-20, "ALL"; admin alert only): `GATE_MISSED_CALL_PUSH_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `isEnabled('missedCallPushCheck')` in `server/services/missed-call-bell.js`. The bell used to settle once its row was written, even when `push.sent` was 0. On: when the bell row is written, an admin push subscription existed, none was sent and none was merely skipped, the call is not settled; the lease is released and `metadata.missed_call_push_retries` is set to 1, and the next 2-minute sweep re-sends the push only (`triggerNotification` option `pushOnly`: no second bell row; the push tag is the same, so a phone that did receive the first one shows one banner). That second pass always settles. If its push also reached no phone, `raiseAdminAlert` posts "System — Missed-call push reached no phone" once per ET day (dedupe key `missed-call-push-no-phone:<ET date>`, subject `check`/`missed_call_push`). The retry follows the counter stored on the row the claim itself won (read back with RETURNING, never from the earlier snapshot), not the gate, so a concurrent pass or turning the gate off between the passes cannot write a second bell. Pass 1 also stores how many subscriptions it found (`missed_call_push_first_subs`): expired ones are deactivated, so the retry can find none, and that still counts as a push that reached no phone. Off: no behavior change. Rollback: unset the variable.

Call leads without an eager Stripe profile (dark, 2026-10-21): `GATE_CALL_LEAD_LAZY_STRIPE` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callLeadLazyStripeLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). `server/services/call-recording-processor.js`: a customer created from a call no longer gets a Stripe profile at once (the "Auto-create Stripe customer" step is skipped). The empty profile of a lead that never pays made a later duplicate merge refuse the pair (`stripe_profile_conflict`); without it the duplicate merges under today's rules. Nothing needs the profile up front: `StripeService.ensureStripeCustomer` runs on demand in `createSetupIntent`, `savePaymentMethod`, `chargeSavedPaymentMethodOffSession`, `charge`, `chargeInvoiceWithSavedCard` and the invoice pay-page save-card, payment-method and finalize paths (an invoice PaymentIntent without save-card uses no profile). Not gated: `ensureStripeCustomer` refuses a row a duplicate merge retired (`server/services/merge-retired.js`: `deleted_at` AND the `merged-` sentinel phone the merge's retire write sets) with `CUSTOMER_RETIRED` ("this customer record was merged — reload and retry"), before the Stripe call, and links the new Stripe customer with a guarded compare-and-set (`stripe_customer_id IS NULL` and the row not merged away); a profile linked meanwhile is returned instead. An archived customer (`deleted_at` only) still links, so it can pay an open invoice and save the card. Merges are unchanged: a retired row's `autopay_enabled=false` and credit opt-out are still inherited. Changes only when a call lead's Stripe profile is made; it sends nothing to a customer, and existing customers and profiles are untouched. Off: today's behavior, byte for byte. Rollback: unset the variable.

Call access codes need the caller's own number (dark, 2026-10-22; security audit run 2): `GATE_CALL_ENRICH_CODES_REQUIRE_ANI` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `callEnrichCodesRequireAniLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Applies only when `GATE_CALL_PROFILE_ENRICHMENT` is on. `server/services/call-profile-enrichment.js` `enrichFromCall`: a call writes gate, garage and lockbox codes and appends access notes to a customer's profile only when the call's caller ID (the inbound From number; on an outbound call the dialed customer number) is the customer's primary phone (last 10 digits; service-contact slot phones do not count, because the same call can file the caller as a new service contact). Why: step 3 of `call-recording-processor.js` can resolve the customer from a callback number the caller SPOKE, and these writes reach the technician's job card with no office accept. With the gate on and no match, the code and note writes are skipped and logged; pets, internal notes and the rest of the enrichment are unchanged, and the access-code candidate flow (texts only, office accept) is not used for calls. Sends nothing to a customer. Off: today's behavior, byte for byte. Rollback: unset the variable.

Strict inbound email trust (dark, 2026-10-22, security audit run 2): `GATE_EMAIL_AUTH_STRICT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `emailAuthStrictLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: (1) `hasAlignedAuth` in `server/services/email/inbox-hygiene.js` (the shared check behind spam rescue, the known-sender override, the SiteOne receipt sweep, bid desk and review-ask tech voice) reads only real method results of Google's Authentication-Results: comments and quoted strings are dropped, only a clause that starts with `dkim=pass` or `spf=pass` counts, and the header must come from authserv-id `mx.google.com`, so a quoted envelope sender such as `"x dkim=pass header.d=victim.com y"@evil.example` can no longer pass as victim.com (same parser as the Zelle check); (2) `processVendorInvoice` in `server/services/email/invoice-processor.js` books an expense only when the sender passes that aligned-auth check for its From domain, otherwise it writes `auto_action = 'invoice_detected:unauthenticated'` on the email, logs, and creates no `expenses` row for a person to review. Sends nothing to a customer. Off: today's behavior, byte for byte. Rollback: unset the variable.

Duplicate auto-merge leaves an anonymous lead's email for the office (dark, security audit run 2, 2026-10-22): `GATE_DEDUPE_NO_UNVERIFIED_BACKFILL` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time through `dedupeNoUnverifiedBackfillLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`) by `executeMerge` (auto mode) in `server/services/customer-dedupe.js`. It only matters with `GATE_CUSTOMER_DEDUPE_AUTO_MERGE` on. When on, the nightly AUTOMATIC sweep does not merge a pair in which EITHER row (the duplicate, or an older intake row the merge would keep) is an untouched anonymous web-intake row (`pipeline_stage` still `new_lead` and a `lead_source` of `website_quote` or `lead_pipeline`, a `last_contact_type` of `website_quote` or `form_submission`, or a `form_id`) when that row has an email that is not the kept customer's email, because invoice and report mail go to that address and an anonymous visitor typed it. The sweep records the pair in its summary as skipped with reason `unverified_intake_email` (ids only). The pair stays on the Duplicates page, where the office can merge it by hand. Manual (admin) merges are unchanged, and an intake row with no email, or the same email, still auto-merges. Off = the old behavior, byte for byte. Sends nothing to a customer. Rollback: unset the variable.

Tax ledger rules + inbox: `GATE_TAX_LEDGER` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, nested under `GATE_BANK_IMPORT`. Payee rules (table `tax_ledger_rules`; the merchant-pattern seeds in `server/services/tax-ledger-seed-rules.js` are written at runtime, idempotent by pattern, so the list can change without a migration) pre-fill the Bank Import suggestion on every staged bank row after a CSV upload or a Plaid sync: the Schedule C category for an expense, or personal / transfer / income / review. An Inbox tab under Admin → Tax lists the open rows with one-tap decisions (Business, Personal, Transfer, Income, Later) and an "Always" box that writes an owner rule (priority 10, so it beats every seed at 100). Income does not hide a row: a customer receipt outside the processor moves to the Income view and stays there, because nothing counts it as revenue yet (record it as a sale by hand; the return engine is a later phase). Suggestion-only: no row changes status without the operator, the expense itself is still made by `/bank-import/:id/create-expense`, and nothing is sent anywhere. Routes: `/admin/tax/bank-import/ledger/*` (status answers `{enabled:false}` when off; the rest 404). Read at call time by `server/services/tax-ledger-rules.js`. Rollback: unset the gate; the table stays and is harmless.

Commercial proposal online signing: `GATE_COMMERCIAL_PROPOSAL_SIGN` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`commercialProposalSignLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner decision 2026-10-23: a signed agreement for every commercial proposal. On, an authored commercial proposal (`normalizeProposal(estimate).enabled`, with a recurring price and structured `commercialTerms` that agree with the agreement's fixed terms: `agreementTermsConflict` (`commercial-proposal-agreement.js`) is the ONE chokepoint, used through `signEligibility` by `/data`, the route, the issuing re-check and the sign-time re-check. The template fixes a payment paragraph (Net 30, Net 60 (owner 2026-10-29; template version 2 only), or Auto Pay under `GATE_COMMERCIAL_AUTOPAY` below), a 12-month initial term that renews automatically for 12-month terms with 30 days' written non-renewal notice, 30-day written cancellation, and price adjustment at renewal or with 30 days' notice, so: `paymentTerms` must be Net 30 or Net 60 or, with `GATE_COMMERCIAL_AUTOPAY` on and Bill by invoice off, Auto Pay (required); `initialTermMonths` must be blank or 12; `renewal`, `cancellation` and `priceAdjustment` must be blank (the agreement governs) or equal, ignoring case, spacing and apostrophe style, to the agreement-aligned text in `AGREEMENT_TERMS` (the texts the builder will prefill). The field list is read from the proposal normalizer's own output, so a structured term added to the normalizer later has no rule and FAILS CLOSED (no online signing) until a rule is written. `accessRequirements` and the free-text Additional terms do not block: they add to the agreement, they do not contradict a fixed term. Any conflict gives `cta.commercialAgreement = { canSign: false, reason: 'terms_conflict', field }`, the generic 404 from the route, and a builder line such as "Online signing needs the proposal terms to match the agreement: initial term 12 months (or blank).") on an open, customer-viewable estimate shows **Accept & sign agreement** on the public estimate page; in the PDF render pass the same label is a link to that page. The tap calls `POST /api/estimates/:token/commercial-agreement` (`server/services/commercial-proposal-agreement.js`), which creates the `customer_contracts` row from the document template `service_agreement.commercial_pest` for the estimate's customer through the existing contract tables, and returns the public signing URL; the customer signs on the existing `/contract/:token` page. A second tap returns the same open agreement with a fresh link (only a link hash is stored, so a new link replaces the old one) only when the quote fingerprint is identical (normalized proposal lines, programs, corrective work, scope, terms, tax rate, totals, merge values, customer and template version); any change cancels the stale open agreement and issues a new one; a signed agreement answers 409. An estimate with no customer account answers 409 and the page says to call. Merge values: `customer.name` and `customer.address` come from the proposal's prepared-for name and property address; `service.name` is `Commercial pest control — <estimate number> — <annual price> per year, serviced <cadence>[, plus sales tax]`; `agreement.start_date` is `Set when we schedule your first visit`. The contract snapshot carries `estimate.id`, the estimate number and the proposal totals, so the signed copy ties to the quote. The signature is checked at the signing boundary too: `POST /api/contracts/:token/sign` for a contract this feature issued locks the customer row first and then the estimate row (the issuer's lock order, customer first like every customer contact write: customers, estimates, leads, call_log, contracts), refuses if the estimate no longer belongs to that customer, re-runs the locked open check, the gate, the terms and the quote fingerprint, and when any fails answers 409 `proposal_changed` ("This proposal was updated. Please open the latest proposal to sign.") and cancels the stale open contract in the same transaction, so nothing is signed, no copy is emailed and no alert rings. Signing is NOT acceptance (owner ruling 2026-09-24: staff confirm commercial): the estimate's status is never changed and no visit, invoice or charge is created. After the signature commits, `routes/contracts-public.js` calls `handleAgreementSigned`: one admin alert (`composeAdminAlert`, dedupe key `commercial-agreement-signed:<contract id>`, headline `Estimates — mark <name> won and book the first visit`; with `GATE_COMMERCIAL_FIRST_VISIT` on and an eligible proposal it reads `Estimates — watch for <name>'s first visit booking`, because the customer books it online) linking to the proposal page, plus one `activity_log` row on the estimate. The hook reads the snapshot's `estimate.source` marker, so it does nothing for a commercial agreement staff issued by hand. `GET /api/estimates/:token/data` adds `cta.commercialAgreement` (`{ canSign, state }`) and `GET /api/admin/estimates/:id/proposal` adds `commercialAgreement` (`{ state, since | signedAt }`) for the builder's read-only line, both only with the gate on. **The owner flips it**: it puts a signing link in front of a customer and the existing signed-contract email (`services/contract-signed-email.js`) then sends the customer the signed copy. The gate is re-read after the issuing locks and before any write, so a kill thrown mid-request writes nothing. Off = the route answers the generic 404 with the privacy headers from a pre-guard mounted before the global limiter (and skips its rate limit), `/data` and the admin read carry nothing new, and the page, the PDF and the sign route behave exactly as before. Rollback: unset the variable.

Commercial Auto Pay default: `GATE_COMMERCIAL_AUTOPAY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`commercialAutopayLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner decision 2026-10-24 ("autopay default"): card or bank Auto Pay is the commercial default; Net 30 by invoice stays for accounts that need it (HOA, property manager, multi-site, large monthly amounts, or an accounts-payable team that cannot use a card), and staff choose. On: the proposal builder offers **Auto Pay** as the payment term of a proposal that does not bill by invoice and prefills it on a proposal with no terms (Net 30 still needs Bill by invoice; GET `/api/admin/estimates/:id/proposal` adds `commercialAutopayEnabled`); the proposal Service terms print `Payment: Auto Pay` (React card, browser PDF, SSR card, pdfkit PDF). Auto Pay never sits beside Bill by invoice: the proposal PUT refuses it there and predicates its write on `bill_by_invoice = false`, turning Bill by invoice on is refused while the proposal says Auto Pay (and the write predicates on it), Mark won refuses the pair, and the signing chokepoint (`agreementTermsConflict` with the estimate's `bill_by_invoice`) treats it as a conflict. Auto Pay never collects a visit from a won Bill-by-invoice proposal, whatever the customer's own enrollment (owner 2026-10-30, `server/services/bill-by-invoice.js`): the completion charge (extended and per-application lanes), the closeout-sheet charge, the full-balance sweep and the Auto Pay hold sweep's charge all skip it, its reminders run instead of an Auto Pay hold, and the sheets show it as an invoice. It is due on the proposal's Net term (`proposalTermsDueDate`). An appointment card request (the customer's own card for that one visit) is not Auto Pay and keeps its lane. The Commercial Pest Service Agreement template version 2 (migration `20261025120000`) prints its payment paragraph from `{{agreement.payment_terms}}`: the Auto Pay text ("You authorize Waves to charge the card or bank account on file after each service is completed, plus applicable tax. ...", owner-approved) or the 2026-06-24 Net 30 text, both in `shared/commercial-agreement-terms.cjs`; a Net 30 agreement prints exactly what version 1 printed. After an Auto Pay agreement is signed, `POST /api/contracts/:token/sign` mints the customer's standalone Auto Pay setup link inline (`services/autopay-setup-link.js`, `GATE_AUTOPAY_SETUP_LINK`; nothing is sent) and the signing page shows **Save your card or bank account**; the existing setup page saves the method and enrolls Auto Pay, and completed visits are then charged by the existing completion auto-charge (`GATE_COMPLETION_AUTOPAY_CHARGE`, capped at the visit's accepted price). Nothing is charged at signing, and the office alert says whether a method is saved yet. **The owner flips it** (it leads to card enrollment and charges). Off: Auto Pay cannot be chosen, saved or signed; a proposal already saved on Auto Pay keeps and prints it and cannot be signed online (an open Auto Pay agreement is refused at signing and cancelled); the signing page shows no setup step. Rollback: unset the variable.

Commercial first visit picker: `GATE_COMMERCIAL_FIRST_VISIT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`commercialFirstVisitLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Owner 2026-10-26, "OK GO" on decision page choice 1B: "The customer picks the first visit from open slots, the same way residential customers do. It books by itself, sized to the real visit length." On, after the Commercial Pest Service Agreement is signed, and only while the proposal is still the quote that was signed (`signedQuoteMatches`: the agreement's frozen fingerprint; a visit length is not part of it), the proposal page shows **Pick your first visit** (the shared `SchedulePicker`) for an eligible proposal: not billed by invoice (invoice mode stays with the office), pest service programs only, one whole cadence (12, 6, 4, 3, 2 or 1 visits a year), no building line items, corrective work or one-time charge, a year of visits equal to the quoted annual price (`firstVisitPlan` in `server/services/commercial-first-visit.js`), and structured payment terms of none or Auto Pay (the win refuses any other term outside invoice mode), signed premises that are the customer's address on file (the booking and the series run there; a proposal for another building or unit stays with the office), and a per-visit tax equal to what the completion invoice will charge this customer after the win (`completionTaxMatches`: the `InvoiceService.previewInvoiceTotals` dry run of the visit price, taxed as commercial when the win will mark the customer commercial, so mixed taxable programs, another rate or an exempt customer stay with the office). Anything else keeps the office flow and its copy. Times come from the `/book` engine at the customer's pin (or the canonical geocode of the account address when no pin is saved; the commit re-derives and stamps it), sized to the visit length: the builder's new per-program **Visit length** (`visitMinutes`, whole minutes 5-480, optional; the proposal save answers 400 outside that) summed, else the estimator's on-site minutes rounded up to 5, else 60; at least 15, and a visit over 90 minutes (the `/book` commit's limit) stays with the office. Booking a time creates the visit through `createSelfBooking` as a paid internal visit (`Commercial Pest Control`, unlinked from the residential catalog, the per-visit price on `estimated_price`, invoiced on completion, linked by `source_estimate_id`, one first visit per estimate under an advisory lock), then marks the proposal won through the staff path (`markEstimateManuallyAccepted`, source `customer_first_visit_booking`), seeds the ongoing series at the proposal's cadence, and rings one office alert (`Schedule — check <name>'s first commercial visit`). The customer gets the standard self-booking confirmation text and reminders; the signing page offers "Back to your estimate"; the signed-agreement alert tells the office to watch for the booking instead of booking by phone; `/data` adds `cta.commercialFirstVisit` and an accepted proposal's page shows the booked visit's date. Routes and guards: `docs/public-route-contracts.md` (`/api/estimates/:token/first-visit`). **The owner flips it**: it books visits and sends the booking confirmation text. Off: the routes answer the generic 404, `/data` and the contract payload carry nothing new, the alert and every page read exactly as before, and the office books the first visit. Rollback: unset the variable; visits already booked stay booked.

Shared bills + home office: `GATE_TAX_SHARED_BILLS` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, nested under `GATE_BANK_IMPORT`, read at call time (`taxSharedBillsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). A bill that is part business (a phone plan with business lines, home internet) is a row in `tax_shared_bills` (normalized bank text, label, business %, optional category). When `/admin/tax/bank-import/:id/create-expense` books a staged debit whose description holds that text on word boundaries (plain text, no regex; the longest pattern wins), the expense's deductible amount is cut to the business share (after the category's own partial rule, such as meals at 50%), the category fills in from the bill only when the operator and the suggestion left none, and the notes get ` [Shared bill: <label> <pct>%]`. The home office is the simplified method, one row per tax year in `tax_home_office` (`$5 x sq ft x months / 12`, 300 sq ft at most = $1,500 a year, computed on read). The tax package adds `home-office.csv` (when the year has a row) and `shared-bills.csv`. Routes: `/admin/tax/shared-bills` (GET, POST, PUT/:id, DELETE/:id) and `/admin/tax/home-office/:year` (GET, PUT, DELETE); `/admin/tax/shared-bills/status` answers `{enabled:false}` when off, the rest 404. Admin → Tax → Rates shows the panel only while on. Nothing is sent anywhere. Off = create-expense and the package behave exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate; the tables stay and are harmless (`down()` of `20261024120000_tax_shared_bills.js` drops them).
Tax return engine: `GATE_TAX_RETURN_ENGINE` — **ships DARK: off unless set**, nested under `GATE_BANK_IMPORT`, read at call time (`taxReturnEngineLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). One row per tax year in `tax_years` (filing status, other income, estimates paid, the four carryovers IN: NOL, QBI loss, section 179, home office) and a federal return computed from the books by `server/services/tax-return-engine.js` (`computeReturn` is pure; the constants for 2024, 2025 and 2026 live in `server/services/tax-year-constants.js` with their IRS sources, and any other year answers 400 "tax constants for <year> are not loaded"). Gross receipts are the P&L's revenue (`buildPnlReport`), expenses are `expenses` rows by their category's Schedule C line at the deductible amount (rows on line 13 and 30 are left out and warned), depreciation and section 179 come from the equipment register, the home office from `tax_home_office` (simplified or, new here, actual = Form 8829). Order: section 179 capped at gross less other expenses (home office not subtracted) and at the year's dollar limit, then the home office capped at what section 179 leaves (Form 8829 line 8 starts from Schedule C line 29; actual excess carries out, simplified excess expires), Schedule SE, NOL at 80% of taxable income, QBI at 20%, then income tax from the IRS Tax Table under $100,000 of taxable income (the bracket formula at the row midpoint, whole dollars) and the bracket formula from $100,000. An election over the section 179 dollar limit counts only up to the limit and the rest is not carried. Marking a year filed freezes the numbers and the carryovers OUT in `filed_snapshot`; a carry-in left empty (NULL) takes that snapshot's carry-out, or 0 when there is none, and any number the owner types, including 0, wins (the screen shows each source); a filed year cannot be edited until it is unmarked. Mark filed sends the `fingerprint` of the return on screen; the server computes the return again and answers 409 ("the return changed since it was shown") when the books, the year's inputs or the prior year moved since then. Filing is one optimistic step: the return is computed from the year row and the prior year row as read, and the filing runs in one transaction under `LOCK TABLE tax_years IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE` that matches only those two row versions, so a save, filing or unfiling that lands meanwhile is a 409 and freezes nothing. Warnings cover a year in progress, a filed year the books now disagree with, the simplified home office on a late return, QBI over its threshold, a section 179 election over its limit, and wages in Other income (the section 179 income limit, the Social Security wage base and the Additional Medicare Tax count business income only). Routes: `/admin/tax/tax-years` (GET, GET/:year, PUT/:year, POST/:year/file, POST/:year/unfile, GET/:year/return); `/admin/tax/return-engine/status` answers `{enabled:false}` when off, the rest 404. Admin → Tax → Reports → Return appears only while on. The home office box (Admin → Tax → Rates) needs `GATE_TAX_SHARED_BILLS` too. Not modeled: credits, married filing separately, the QBI wage/property limit, the 2026 $400 minimum QBI deduction (IRC 199A(i); warned when it could apply), the section 179 phase-out, Form 172 nonbusiness add-backs. Nothing is sent anywhere and no tax is paid or filed from here. Off = nothing reads the new tables. Rollback: unset the gate; the tables stay and are harmless (`down()` of `20261024230000_tax_return_engine.js` drops `tax_years` and puts the old home-office CHECKs back, deleting any actual-method rows).
Tax package W-2 labor (census A8, owner 2026-10-25): `GATE_TAX_PACKAGE_W2_LABOR` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`taxPackageW2LaborLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Today the CPA package (`GET /admin/tax/export/tax-package`) writes `labor-timetracking-informational.csv` from `time_entry_daily_summary` for every technician, labeled as the owner's own non-deductible time with overtime forced to 0, and a W-2 hire's wages are nowhere in it. On: (1) the informational file keeps only technicians who are not W-2 employees (`technicians.employment_type` is not `'w2'`; a row with no employment type stays), same columns and per-row logic; (2) a new `w2-payroll.csv` lists one row per FINALIZED pay check (`payroll_checks.status = 'finalized'`, the predicate `payroll-runs.js` and `payroll-tax-calendar.js` use; drafts and voided checks are left out) whose `pay_date` falls in the package year: employee, week start, week end (week start + 6), pay date, regular and overtime hours (`regular_minutes` / `overtime_minutes` are decimal minutes on the check; hours = minutes / 60 to 2 places, as the pay stub prints them), gross wages, federal income tax withheld, employee Social Security, employee Medicare plus Additional Medicare, employer Social Security, employer Medicare, FUTA, Florida reemployment tax and net pay, all from the integer cent columns printed as dollars, with one TOTAL row (no SSN, bank or routing number); (3) the README lists `w2-payroll.csv` as item 7 (wages are Schedule C line 26, employer taxes line 23, totals match the portal's W-2 and W-3 figures) and says the P&L does not read pay runs yet, so payroll payments sorted into expense categories from the bank feed in `expenses.csv` and `pnl.csv` must be compared with it. It changes a file for the CPA only; it sends, files and pays nothing. Off = the package is byte for byte today's (same files, same README). Rollback: unset the gate. The separate `GET /admin/tax/export/labor` route (Taxes, Exports, Labor) builds the same time-tracking rows for its picked dates and keeps every technician: the gate does not apply to it.

P&L and Schedule C wages from pay runs (census M11, owner 2026-10-26, choice B "from the payroll the portal already runs"): `GATE_PNL_PAY_RUN_WAGES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`pnlPayRunWagesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Today `buildPnlReport` passes `laborCost: 0` and `gatherInputs` sums expense rows by `expense_categories.irs_line`, so with a W-2 hire the bank-booked payroll payments (net pay, the federal deposit, FUTA, the Florida RT-6 payment) put net pay on line 26 and the employee's withheld taxes on line 23, and the totals do not match the W-2 and W-3. On: (1) both read FINALIZED pay checks (`payroll_checks.status = 'finalized'`, the same checks `w2-payroll.csv` lists) with `pay_date` in the window, inclusive, through `server/services/pay-run-books.js`: wages = `gross_cents`, employer taxes = employer Social Security + employer Medicare + FUTA + Florida reemployment; (2) a new expense category `Payroll (counted from pay runs)` (`expense_categories.counted_from_pay_runs = true`, no Schedule C line, migration `20261026150000_expense_category_pay_runs.js`) holds the bank payroll payments; the P&L and the Schedule C draft leave rows in it out, and keep uncategorized rows; (3) the P&L labor line (inside COGS) = wages + employer taxes, the P&L JSON gains a `payroll` block (`source`, `checks`, `wages`, `employerTaxes`, `total`, `bankLinesLeftOut`, `note`), the quarterly estimate's year-to-date expenses do the same swap, and the Tax page shows one muted line under Labor; (4) Schedule C line 26 = wages and line 23 = employer taxes plus the other Taxes and licenses rows; (5) with `GATE_TAX_PACKAGE_W2_LABOR` also on, the CPA README says the P&L counts the same pay runs. A deposit paid in January for December wages stays in December (pay date rules). `expenses.csv` still lists the bank payments. Off = every output is byte for byte today's (no `payroll` key, same Schedule C lines, same README); the migration only adds a column and a category row, which nothing reads while the gate is off. Rollback: unset the gate (the column and category row stay and are harmless). It changes report figures only; it sends, files and pays nothing.

Payroll bank match (basic payroll item 8, owner 2026-10-28, "pay package is still being built, do these"): `GATE_PAYROLL_BANK_MATCH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`payrollBankMatchLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy; existing links stay). Needs `GATE_BANK_IMPORT` (the bank lines and every `/admin/tax/bank-import` route), `GATE_PAYROLL` (the pay runs) and `GATE_PNL_PAY_RUN_WAGES` (`payrollBankMatchLive()` reads both: only with that gate on do the P&L and Schedule C leave the pay-run category out and count the pay runs instead, so with it off the matcher links nothing and moves no expense; links made earlier stay, and since the match never edits a deduction they count at their own deduction). Today nothing links a bank line to a paycheck, so a payroll line categorized as wages, or left uncategorized, makes the books count payroll twice or leaves review noise. On, the bank import's own match pass (`runDeterministicMatching` in `server/services/bank-import.js`, one more candidate source in the same flow, pure rules in `server/services/payroll-bank-match.js`) pairs: (1) NET PAY: a debit on a business (`account_type = 'bank'`) account equal to the cents of a finalized, not-voided `payroll_checks.net_cents`, dated pay date minus 3 days to plus 45 days (a paper check clears late; a `bank_transfer` check plus 7), and the line auto-links only when exactly ONE unmatched check and ONE unmatched bank line pair up; a check number printed on the line (CHECK 1042) breaks a tie and a different printed number makes it a suggestion; (2) FEDERAL DEPOSIT: an IRS / EFTPS debit (USATAXPYMT, EFTPS, IRS Direct Pay, US TREASURY ... TAX PYMT) equal to a `tax_filing_calendar` row with `source_key` `payroll:941_deposit:YYYY-MM` (or its `:balance:n` row; the amount the owner recorded paying, else the amount due), dated from the first day of the month to 14 days after the due date; (3) FLORIDA RT-6: a Florida Department of Revenue debit (not one that says sales tax) equal to a `payroll:rt6:YYYY-Qn` row, dated from the quarter start to 14 days after the due date; FUTA is not matched (the calendar's FUTA row is an alert with no amount). A linked line becomes status `created_expense` with an expense in `Payroll (counted from pay runs)` (the deductible amount an ordinary bank-import expense gets, never 0: the P&L leaves the whole category out when the pay-run gate is on, and every other reader of the deductible still sums it), `match_method` `payroll_check` or `payroll_tax`, `matched_payroll_check_id` or `matched_tax_filing_id` (migration `20261029130000_bank_txn_payroll_match.js`; a unique index on each), and `suggestion.payrollMatch` (when, `auto` or `owner`, the ids) as the audit trail. The claim runs in one transaction with the bank row and the target locked and the pairing re-judged on a fresh read. An automatic claim also commits a marker (`suggestion.payrollMatch.verifyPending`) and is verified right after: the bank line and target are locked again and the pairing is re-judged on a fresh read with the claim virtually undone, because a CSV upload, Plaid sync or pay run finalization can commit a second same-amount line or paycheck between the re-plan and the commit. Still the only pair: the marker is cleared. Otherwise the line goes back to review with `suggestion.payrollUnlinked` (`reason: became_ambiguous`, the kept `expenseId`) and the candidates parked for the owner; the expense is not deleted or edited and the target is not remembered as rejected. The top of every gated pass verifies any line a crash left with the marker. The owner's own link carries no marker. Anything else (two checks with one amount, a second bank line that could be the same check, an amount one cent off, a held `manualLink` line) parks in `suggestion.payrollCandidates` with the paycheck named, and the owner links it with `POST /admin/tax/bank-import/:id/link-payroll` (`checkId` or `filingId`, plausibility judged by the same rules). Before it creates an expense it runs the ordinary matcher's own existing-expense survey (`surveyExpenseCandidatesForRow`): if an expense the owner already entered could be this payment, nothing is created and nothing is linked, and the line parks with the paycheck or tax row and the expense named (`existingExpenses`); the owner then links the paycheck to that expense (same expense, moved into the payroll category with its own deductible amount untouched; a release puts only the category back, and only while the expense is still in the payroll category) or chooses Book as new. A tax line whose pay period is still open (another run can raise the row's amount) is a suggestion unless the owner already recorded paying that amount. Every gated pass also reconciles tax links: a line linked to a calendar row whose amount (`amount_paid`, else `amount_due`) no longer equals the line, or whose row was deleted, returns to review with the expense kept (a re-categorized one gets its category back) and the evidence, with the expense id, kept in `suggestion.payrollUnlinked` (`calendar_changed` / `calendar_deleted`). Never moves money; never marks a calendar row paid (the filing calendar shows `Seen in the bank on <date>`; Mark filed / paid stays the owner's); never touches a non-payroll line. Voiding a pay run releases the lines matched to its checks (the line returns to review, the expense the match created stays untouched, `suggestion.payrollUnlinked` keeps the trail with that `expenseId`, the check is remembered as rejected; the next pass finds the kept expense in the existing-expense survey, so no second expense is made); the match never deletes an expense. When the owner deletes the created expense, the line is freed as before and the matcher does not re-book it. The Payroll tab shows `Bank: matched <date> / not seen yet / needs your pick` per final check. No admin notification: the panel status is enough. Off = the bank import, the books and every response are byte for byte today's (no payroll key in a summary, a suggestion, a transaction row, a pay run or a filing). One clean-up runs on or off: a line back in review that still carries a payroll link (made while the gate was on, then freed by a deleted or unlinked expense) loses that link at the next pass, so it never reserves the paycheck.

Tech cost rates (L11a, owner 2026-10-26: "we need real actual calculation, this ($35) was a number I just thought"): `GATE_TECH_COST_RATES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`techCostRatesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Today `calculateJobCost` (`server/services/job-costing.js`) books labor as on-job minutes x `loaded_labor_rate` ($35) and drive as `drive_cost_per_stop` ($6), both from `company_financials`. The migrations `20261026220000_tech_cost_cards.js` and `20261026230000_tech_cost_card_wage.js` add two effective-dated tables, `technician_cost_cards` (kind `w2` or `imputed`, the hourly wage a W-2 card is made with, paid hours per week and per day, health money per month, retirement %, workers' comp %, paid days off per year, the vehicle the technician drives) and `vehicle_cost_cards` (loss of value, insurance, loan interest, other fixed costs per year; fuel and upkeep per mile). A card is never updated (a trigger refuses it); a change is a new row. The card in effect on a date is the one with the greatest `effective_date` on or before it (tie: newest `created_at`, then `id`); before the first card there is no card. `server/services/tech-cost-rates.js` turns a card into labor cost per worked hour: a W-2 card adds wages (the card's `hourly_wage` x paid hours; the card keeps the wage it was made with, the technician's pay rate by default, because `technicians.pay_rate` is not dated and a raise must not re-cost old visits; a card without a wage reads `technicians.pay_rate`), health money, employer Social Security and Medicare (7.65%), FUTA and Florida reemployment tax on the first $7,000 of wages (rates read from `payroll-calc.js` `RATES`), workers' comp and retirement, then divides by worked hours (paid hours less paid days off x hours per day); an imputed card states the hourly rate. Vehicle fixed cost per worked hour = the yearly fixed lines / the summed worked hours of every technician whose card in effect names that vehicle (two drivers share one year of fixed cost), the same in costing and on the rates screen. Every yearly line rounds half up to the cent; every hourly rate rounds half up to the cent. On, AND a card in effect for the visit's technician on its `scheduled_date`: `labor_cost` = labor per worked hour x (on-job minutes + drive minutes) / 60; `drive_cost` = vehicle per-mile cost x drive miles + vehicle fixed per worked hour x (on-job minutes + drive minutes) / 60 (no vehicle on the card = 0). On-job minutes keep today's sources. Drive minutes and miles come from the visit's `visit_gps_legs` row with status `matched` when that table exists (the trip-link change creates it), divided by its `shared_stop_count` (one parking spot that served several visits), else 24 minutes and 11 miles (the 10-26 measurement); a pending visit books no drive. The members of one grouped visit share one leg: with no closeout marker, only the lowest service id of the group carries it. In a combined closeout the drive minutes and miles are charged once, to the stop's marked drive-cost owner (the `visitDriveCostAllocation` rule `drive_cost_per_stop` already follows); every member still carries labor and vehicle fixed cost for its own allocated on-site minutes. `labor_hours` stays the on-job hours. `service_records.vehicle_fixed_cost` (migrations `20261026233000` and `20261026234000`; NULL when no card applied) keeps the vehicle fixed part of `drive_cost`, written with the other financials, and the adjusted-EBITDA bridge (`/api/admin/dashboard/ebitda-bridge`) takes the month's sum of it (the same rows as its gross profit) out of the vehicle overhead line (never below zero), so that cost counts once. Keep a vehicle card's insurance out of the Insurance overhead line, or it counts twice. Off, or no card in effect (or a W-2 card whose technician has no pay rate) = `job_costs` and `service_records` values are byte for byte today's. Admin API `server/routes/admin-cost-cards.js` (`/api/admin/cost-cards`: list, add technician card, add vehicle card, rates on a date; every write audited with ids only) and the Cost cards section on Settings > Operating costs; off answers 404 (the list answers `{ enabled: false }`) and the section renders nothing. Customer prices never change: the pricing engine does not read cost cards or `company_financials`. The unbooked part of the paid day is `GATE_TECH_OPEN_TIME` (the next paragraph).
