Rollback: unset the gate; the tables and cards stay and are harmless. Past visits are re-costed only when something recalculates them (a manual recalc or the backfill), and only with the gate on. It changes cost figures only; it sends, charges and pays nothing.
Job cost standard minutes (owner ruling 2026-10-31: the dashboard Gross Margin was wrong; a read of the last 90 days found labor costed from check-in-to-report spans, one lawn visit at 528 hours, paid visits booking $0 revenue and annual-prepay visits booking the monthly rate or $0): `GATE_JOB_COST_STANDARD_MINUTES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`jobCostStandardMinutesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On: `server/services/job-costing.js` books a completed lawn care visit at 20 on-site minutes and a pest control visit at 25 (a name that also says roach, rodent, termite, mosquito, bed bug, flea, wasp, bee, wildlife, exclusion or inspection keeps its measured time), which replace measured time, time entries, backfill minutes and a combined-closeout share; an admin time-on-site correction still wins; any other measured result over 480 minutes books the visit's scheduled estimate (else 0). With no cost card the drive-owning visit books the Average Drive Time (`pricing_config` `global_drive_time`, 20 min) at the loaded labor rate (about $11.67 at $35), other members 0; a cost card still uses its own drive path. Revenue under a cost-only re-run keeps a recorded amount only when above $0; a recorded $0 falls to the visit's own price, then its share of a paid annual-prepay term (`prepay_amount` over the term's counted visits), then its linked invoice's service lines (setup, membership and onboarding fee lines and tax left out), never to `customers.monthly_rate`. Cost and margin figures only: no price, invoice, payment or customer message changes. Off = `job_costs` and `service_records` values byte for byte today's. Re-cost history with `GATE_JOB_COST_STANDARD_MINUTES=true node server/scripts/job-cost-standard-recost.js --from YYYY-MM-DD --to YYYY-MM-DD [--write]` (dry run by default: each visit costs in a transaction that rolls back; prints before and after by service type). Kill switch: unset.
Tech open time (L11b, owner 2026-10-26 "BOTH", build B: "Each visit carries only its own minutes and miles. The unbooked part of the paid day shows as one 'open time' cost for each tech and day. A visit's cost stays steady, so customer margins compare fairly. Open time shows what an empty schedule costs."): `GATE_TECH_OPEN_TIME` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`techOpenTimeLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). It needs `GATE_TECH_COST_RATES` on too; with either off, everything below is off. Migration `20261027230000_job_costs_charged_minutes.js` adds `job_costs.charged_on_job_minutes` and `charged_drive_minutes` (numeric 8,2, NULL = no cost card applied to that row). `calculateJobCost` writes them whether or not this gate is on (a visit costed with a card keeps the minutes it was charged for; a re-cost without a card clears them; no cost figure changes). Gate on: (1) **Nightly re-cost.** The 01:40 ET scheduler tick runs `recostNightly()` (`server/services/job-cost-recost.js`, job `job-cost-recost`) right after the trip link: it re-costs the completed visits whose `visit_gps_legs` rows sit on the days the trip link links that night (`nightlyDays` + `lateArrivals`), so their GPS drive minutes and miles reach `job_costs`. Only visits whose technician has a cost card in effect are re-costed; revenue is kept as recorded (`keepRecordedRevenue`); one failed visit does not stop the rest, and the job fails after the loop when any failed. The customer ad-attribution sync that `calculateJobCost` runs for a completed visit is idempotent (it re-sums the customer's completed `job_costs` rows under a lock on one row and rewrites the same funnel fields; it sends nothing). `node server/scripts/job-cost-recost.js --from YYYY-MM-DD --to YYYY-MM-DD [--write]` re-costs a back-dated range when the owner enters a first card (dry run by default, at most 400 days, `--write` needs `GATE_TECH_COST_RATES`). (2) **Open time** (`server/services/open-time.js`): per technician and ET day (never today or later), paid minutes = the day's `time_entry_daily_summary` row (`total_shift_minutes` less `unpaid_meal_minutes`; source `clock`), else on a day with a visit the card's `paid_hours_per_day` x 60 (source `card`); booked = the day's completed visits' charged on-job + drive minutes; open = paid less booked (never below 0; `overMinutes` when booked is more); open cost = the card's labor cost per worked hour x open minutes / 60, rounded half up to the cent once per technician-day. A day is left out, never guessed, when the technician has no card that day, the card gives no rate, or a completed visit that day has no charged minutes (costed before the card). Labor only: the vehicle's fixed cost for unbooked minutes stays in the vehicle overhead line; overtime premium is not modeled. (3) `GET /api/admin/cost-cards/open-time?from=&to=` (default the 30 days ending yesterday, at most 92 days; 404 with the gate off) and the Open time panel in the Cost cards section. (4) The adjusted-EBITDA bridge (`/api/admin/dashboard/ebitda-bridge`) adds one row `open_time` right after gross profit for the month's finished days (month start through yesterday) and takes it out of contribution and EBITDA; the response also carries `openTime: { amount, days, openMinutes }`. Tech pay is in no overhead line, so nothing counts twice. Off = no re-cost, the route answers 404, the panel renders nothing, the bridge rows and numbers are exactly today's. Customer prices never change. Production holds 0 cost cards and 0 time entries today, so this is inert until the owner enters a card. Rollback: unset the gate; the two columns stay and are harmless.
Tech pay stubs (payroll item 7, owner 2026-10-28: "pay package is still being built, do these"; allowed by the technician allow-list v1 ruling of 2026-10-02, which gives a technician login its own pay): `GATE_TECH_PAY_STUBS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`techPayStubsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Today only an admin can open a pay stub. On: `GET /api/tech/payroll/checks` lists the signed-in person's own checks from FINALIZED, not-voided pay runs (newest pay date first, at most 60) and `GET /api/tech/payroll/checks/:id/stub` returns the same stub the admin sees (`getStub`: hours, earnings, taxes withheld, year to date, net pay; no employer taxes) for one of them (`server/routes/tech-payroll.js`, `listOwnChecks` / `getOwnStub` in `server/services/payroll-runs.js`). Both scope by the authenticated technician id, never a client-sent id; another person's check, a draft or voided pay run, and a bad id answer 404. A Pay stubs tab appears under Time on the Staff page for every staff login; an admin sees only their own stubs there. Pay runs, W-4s, other people's checks, employer taxes and tax forms stay admin only (`/api/admin/payroll`, GATE_PAYROLL). Off = both routes answer 404 `{ enabled: false }` after the staff login check and before any pay query, the client's one request reads that 404 as off, and the tab is hidden. Pays, sends and files nothing; rollback = unset.
Tech training dates (owner 2026-10-28, Tech 2 and 3 Roadmap question 3: "Training and ID-card due dates on the Compliance page, with a reminder before each date"): `GATE_TECH_TRAINING_DATES` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`techTrainingDatesLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). The dates follow F.S. 482.091 and rule 5E-14.1421: the ID card application is due 30 days after the hire date, 5 days (40 hours) of field training under a certified operator need a written record kept 2 years, 4 classroom hours are due 6 months after the card issue date, and 2 hours of continuing training come before each yearly renewal (`technicians.license_expiry`). **On:** `GET /api/admin/compliance-v2/licenses` adds `training`, `idCard`, `classroom` and `renewalTraining` for each technician with a hire date (the owner's row has none); `PUT /licenses/:techId` also takes `id_card_applied_on`, `id_card_issued_on`, `classroom_hours_done_on` and `renewal_training_done_on`; the admin-only `GET/POST/DELETE /licenses/:techId/training-days` and `GET /licenses/:techId/training-record` (the printable 40-hour record) work; the Licenses tab shows the dates, a Training log panel and a Print record view; and a daily 6:52 AM ET sweep (`server/services/technician-training-reminders.js`, `runExclusive('technician-training-dates')`) raises one admin bell for each technician and deadline (ID card application 14 and 3 days before and overdue, classroom hours 30 and 7 days before and overdue, renewal training 30 days before the expiry) and closes it when the date is entered. **Off:** the Licenses tab, routes and responses are as before; nothing is written or raised. It sends nothing to a technician or a customer, and the Team tab's "Can be assigned field work" stays the owner's manual gate. Tables: `technician_training_days` and four date columns on `technicians` (migration `20261029120000_technician_training_dates.js`).

Slab pre-treat for a home is not taxed: `GATE_SLAB_HOME_NO_TAX` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time (`slabHomeNoTaxLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Florida taxes a pre-construction termite treatment only for a nonresidential building (Rule 12A-1.009); for a home it is residential pest control, even when the customer is a builder whose account is commercial. Today `TaxCalculator.calculateTax` taxes every commercial account, so a builder's home slab is billed 7%. On, `calculateTax` (`server/services/tax-calculator.js`) returns no tax for a service whose name says pre-slab, pre-treat, pretreatment or pre-construction and names termites, Termidor, a slab or a borate (`isHomeSlabPretreat`; the live names are Slab Pre-Treat Termite Service, Pre-Slab Termidor and Termite Pretreatment Service), unless the name says Commercial or nonresidential. No record stores the building's use, so the service name is the office's mark: book a nonresidential building's slab as a service named with Commercial (for example "Commercial Slab Pre-Treat Termite Service") and it keeps the commercial tax. A verified exemption still answers first. The calculator is the tax source for visit-completion invoices (single and grouped), invoices created without an explicit rate and the invoice preview, so they all follow it. Not changed: an explicit `taxRate` from a caller, a completion rate frozen before the flip, and invoices already created; an estimate invoice taxed before the flip is held for the office at closeout (`invoice_tax_mismatch`) instead of being adopted. The office invoice form still shows a flat 7% for a commercial account while it is filled in; the saved invoice uses the calculator. Off = slab services are taxed by the customer's property_type exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate.
Residential building use is not taxed: `GATE_BUILDING_USE_TAX` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time (`buildingUseTaxLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Florida taxes pest control only at a nonresidential building (Rule 12A-1.009), whoever pays: homes, apartments, condos and their common areas are residential. The commercial proposal builder's Building use pick (`proposal.buildingUse`, owner 2026-10-28) is written onto the customer as `customers.building_use` when the proposal is won (`recordProposalBuildingUse` in `server/services/proposal-win.js`, called from `winCommercialProposal`; written whatever the gate). On, `TaxCalculator.calculateTax` (`server/services/tax-calculator.js`, step 1b) returns no tax for a customer whose `building_use` is `residential`, after a verified exemption and before the service and county rules, including a payer-billed invoice (the use belongs to the site). The calculator is the tax source for visit-completion invoices (single and grouped), invoices created without an explicit rate and the invoice preview, so they all follow it. Not changed: an explicit `taxRate` from a caller, a completion rate frozen before the flip, invoices already created, and accounts with no recorded use (every account won before the pick existed, and every estimate that is not a builder proposal). A mixed site's later visits follow its one recorded use. A proposal win makes no invoice (PR #7115), so no bill reads a row's Taxable box: the box sets the quote and the signed agreement only, and the builder warns on any row whose box differs from the building use (owner 2026-11-01, audit fix 4); for a Residential pick it warns only while this gate is on (GET /proposal serves `buildingUseTaxLive`); a verified tax exemption is answered first (`taxExemptVerified`, from `TaxCalculator.findVerifiedExemption`). Off = commercial accounts are taxed by property_type exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate.

Tax follows the serviced property's county: `GATE_TAX_SERVICE_COUNTY` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time (`taxServiceCountyLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Florida's surtax is due in the county where the service is delivered (s. 212.054(3)(a); Rule 12A-15.003(5)(a)). On, `TaxCalculator.calculateTax` (`server/services/tax-calculator.js`, `taxZipFor`) reads the county from the serviced property's ZIP before the customer's own: `opts.propertyId` (a saved `customer_properties` row of that customer) or `opts.scheduledServiceId` (a visit of that customer, through its `property_id`); an id of another customer, a property without a ZIP, or no id = the customer's ZIP. Callers: the visit-completion rate freeze and its payer reconcile (`server/services/complete-scheduled-service.js`, the visit's `property_id`), the grouped visit-invoice tax checks (`server/services/visit-completion-invoice.js`, each member's `property_id`), `InvoiceService.create` and `previewInvoiceTotals` (`server/services/invoice.js`, the linked visit: `scheduledServiceId`, or the service record's visit), and every commercial prepay rate (`resolveCommercialPrepayTax` / `resolveCommercialPrepayBaseRate` in `server/services/estimate-converter.js`, with the estimate's `property_id`: the proposal builder's rate chip, which then names the source "(property ZIP)", Generate from estimate, the estimate page, accept, manual acceptance and conversion). On, DeSoto ZIPs map (`DESOTO_ZIPS` in `server/config/county-zips.js`), and Lee, Collier and DeSoto use their 2026 rates (6.5%, 6%, 7.5%; DR-15DSS) when no `tax_rates` row covers the county; a row added on the admin tax page wins. Not changed: an invoice whose lines name properties but that has no linked visit (the customer's ZIP, since the preview has no lines to match), an explicit `taxRate`, a completion rate frozen before the flip, and invoices already created. In 2026 Manatee, Sarasota and Charlotte all charge 7%, so the gate changes no invoice in the service area until a county rate differs (Charlotte's 1% ends Dec 31, 2026 unless extended). Off = the customer's ZIP, no DeSoto, and the flat 7% fallback, exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate.

A slab pre-treat at a business building keeps its tax: `GATE_SLAB_BUSINESS_SITE_TAX` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time (`slabBusinessSiteTaxLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). With `GATE_SLAB_HOME_NO_TAX` on, `TaxCalculator.calculateTax` bills every slab service whose name does not say Commercial as a home job, and the catalog has no Commercial slab service (only Slab Pre-Treat Termite Service and Termite Pretreatment Service), so a contractor's slab job at a business building is billed with no tax. Florida taxes a pre-construction termite treatment at a nonresidential building (Rule 12A-1.009). On, a commercial account's slab job (`isHomeSlabPretreat`) keeps the county tax when its serviced property has Occupancy "Commercial" (`customer_properties.occupancy_type = 'commercial'`, set in the customer's Properties panel). `servicedOccupancy` in `server/services/tax-calculator.js` reads the same ids as `GATE_TAX_SERVICE_COUNTY`: `opts.propertyId` (a saved property of that customer), else the saved property of `opts.scheduledServiceId` (a visit of that customer). So the visit-completion rate freeze and its payer reconcile, the grouped visit invoices, `InvoiceService.create` and its preview, and every commercial prepay rate follow it. The account's building use is not read: a builder whose won proposal marks its own office a Business building still owes no tax on its home slabs. Not changed: a non-commercial account, an account whose recorded building use is residential, a slab job with no saved property, a property of another customer or a property not marked Commercial (all keep the home-slab answer), an explicit `taxRate`, a completion rate frozen before the flip, and invoices already created. The property is read only for a slab job of a commercial account. Off = every slab job follows `GATE_SLAB_HOME_NO_TAX` exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate.

Lawn and landscape treatments are not taxed: `GATE_LAWN_SPRAY_NO_TAX` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time (`lawnSprayNoTaxLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Florida does not tax lawn spraying, residential or nonresidential (Rule 12A-1.009(6)), and taxes pest control only for an infestation of a nonresidential building, so tree and shrub and palm care is not taxed either. Today `TaxCalculator.calculateTax` taxes these services at the county rate for a commercial account: their `service_taxability` rows say taxable, and a name that matches no row is taxed too. On, `calculateTax` (`server/services/tax-calculator.js`) returns no tax for a service whose name names a lawn, turf, sod, trees, shrubs, palms, weeds, fertilizer, pre-emergent or fire ants, or dethatching, topdressing, plugging or aeration (`isGroundsTreatment`; live names include Every 6 Weeks Lawn Care Service, Bi-Monthly Tree & Shrub Care Service and Palm Injection), A combined visit (parts joined with "+") qualifies only when every part does, and a part that also names building pest work (pests, termites, rodents, roaches, palmetto bugs, bed bugs, fleas, ticks, bees, wasps, ants other than fire ants, spiders, silverfish, scorpions, crickets, WDO) or mosquitoes keeps its tax, so "Lawn Care Visit #4 + Quarterly Pest Control" is taxed as before; "lawn pest" (turf insects, as in Lawn Pest Knockdown Service) and fire ants count as lawn work. Mosquito work keeps the commercial tax: the rule names only lawns, and mosquito control is the closest of these services to nonresidential pest control. A verified exemption still answers first, and the home-slab rule runs before it. The calculator is the tax source for visit-completion invoices (single and grouped), invoices created without an explicit rate and the invoice preview, so they all follow it. Not changed: an explicit `taxRate` from a caller, a completion rate frozen before the flip, invoices already created, and the `service_taxability` rows (the gate-removal PR aligns them); an estimate invoice taxed before the flip is held for the office at closeout (`invoice_tax_mismatch`) instead of being adopted. The office invoice form still shows a flat 7% for a commercial account while it is filled in; the saved invoice uses the calculator. Off = these services are taxed by the customer's property_type exactly as before. Rollback: unset the gate.

Tax worksheets: `GATE_TAX_WORKSHEETS` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), nested under `GATE_BANK_IMPORT`, read at call time (`taxWorksheetsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). Adds Admin → Tax → Reports → Sales tax and 1099s (`server/services/tax-worksheets.js`, routes `/admin/tax/worksheets/status`, `/worksheets/sales-tax?kind=month|quarter|half|year&year=&index=`, `/worksheets/1099?year=`). Sales tax shows the Florida DR-15 lines for a month, quarter, half year or year: line A gross sales = the P&L revenue (`buildPnlReport`, the figure the return engine uses), tax collected, its taxable base (subtotal less discount) and its county surtax (the rate above 6%, line 15(d)) from the gross collected leg of `salesTaxLegsForWindow` in `server/services/pnl-report.js` (the same legs the P&L backs out; `salesTaxCollectedForWindow` now reads its net tax), tax refunded on earlier sales on line 6 (lawful deductions, at most the tax collected) and line 7 = tax due (refunds beyond the tax collected are an excess the sheet tells you to carry to the next return's line 6, never a negative amount due), gross sales = the P&L revenue plus the refunded taxable base, exempt = gross − taxable; due the 20th of the next month (a weekend or a state or federal holiday moves it to the next business day); on time = filed and paid by then (the calendar row's filed and paid dates, else today); line 11 collection allowance 2.5% of the first $1,200 of tax ($30 at most) only on time; line 12 penalty when late, 10% of the tax and at least $50. Mark filed uses the filing calendar's own `PUT /filings/:id` on the month's `dr15_sales_tax` row (quarters, halves and years have no row). 1099s lists contract labor (Schedule C line 11) and legal and professional (line 17) expenses of a year by payee (the name comes from the bank text, e.g. "Zelle money sent to <name>"), leaves out card, debit card and Fiverr/Upwork payments (a 1099-K covers them), keeps a check or Wise transfer that names no person on its own line (marked unresolved, never added to anyone else's), marks a payee at or over $600 (payments through 2025) or $2,000 (from 2026, P.L. 119-21) as needing a 1099-NEC, gives the due date (Jan 31, next business day) and counts payment-app debits still unmatched in Bank Import. Read-only; no name edits (a later phase adds payees with W-9s). Off = the routes 404 and the tabs stay hidden. Rollback: unset the gate.

SMS voice profile pin (owner 2026-10-24, "do all"): `GATE_SMS_VOICE_PROFILE_PIN` — **ships DARK: unset = today's behavior, byte for byte**; the value is a `voice_profiles.version` whole number (anything else, such as `true`, `0` or `5.5`, reads as no pin and logs once), read at call time by `smsVoiceProfilePinVersion()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). Set, the texting AI's drafter reads THAT profile in place of the newest approved one: `resolveEffectiveVoiceProfile()` (`server/services/sms-shadow-drafter.js`) asks `getPinnedVoiceProfile()` (`server/services/voice-profile-distiller.js`) first, so graduation's readiness pin, the sealed-exam run pin and auto-send's staleness check read the same profile as the drafter. Only a version that was once approved counts: status `approved`, or `superseded` WITH an approval row in `activity_log` (`voice_profile_reviewed`, `metadata.action = approve`, written in the same transaction as the approval; a profile becomes superseded when a newer one is approved, so a pin on last week's profile keeps working after the nightly run approves a new one, but a pending exception the distiller only replaced is also `superseded` and has no approval row, so it cannot be pinned). The operator kill switch reaches a pinned superseded profile too: `POST /api/admin/agents/voice-profiles/:id/review` with `action: revoke` now accepts a superseded profile that has an approval row and turns it `rejected`, after which the pin no longer resolves (the Agents hub button still shows only for the newest approved profile; unsetting the variable or `SHADOW_VOICE_PROFILE=false` also ends the pin). A `pending` or `rejected` version (`rejected` also covers a revoked profile, the operator kill switch) or a version that does not exist falls back to the newest approved profile and logs one warning per process with no customer data; `SHADOW_VOICE_PROFILE=false` still turns every profile off. The nightly distiller keeps distilling and approving; the phone agent (`relay-conversation.js`) keeps reading the newest approved profile. Each draft already records the profile it used in `message_drafts.intended_actions.voice_profile_version` (no new column). A set pin adds the tag `v` to the draft's prompt version (`house_voice_v12_real_answers26_n+v`, tags sort with the hand-off category tags, at most 39 characters), so pinned drafts form their own cohort for graduation, the sealed exam and the judge; the tag marks that a pin was set, and the version actually used stays in `voice_profile_version`. Sends nothing to a customer; rollback is to unset the variable.
SMS edit learning (owner 2026-10-24, "do all"): `GATE_SMS_EDIT_LEARNING` — **ships DARK: off unless the value is `1`, `true` or `on`** (`gateEnvValue`), read at call time by `smsEditLearningLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`). On, the texting AI learns from the owner's edits to its suggestions in two places. (1) The nightly miner (`server/services/sms-voice-corpus-miner.js`) mines `sms_log` outbound rows of `message_type` `manual` AND `ai_revised` as `sms_human_reply` examples, never `ai_approved`, and skips a `manual` send whose linked `agent_decisions` row (`sms_log.metadata.agent_decision_id`) has `human_verdict = 'accepted'`: the Comms composer sends a suggestion, edited or not, as `manual`, and an unchanged one is the drafter's own text. (2) The drafter's few-shot exemplars (`fetchVoiceExemplars`, `outcomeRanked`) drop those accepted-unchanged replies and rank by outcome instead of recency alone: first replies that resolved a decision with `human_verdict = 'corrected'` or were sent as `ai_revised`, and replies the judge scored `human_better` (`shadow_draft_judgments.human_reply_sms_id` = the example's `source_id`), then the rest, newest first within each tier. All three facts are read from the live tables when the draft is made, so examples mined before the gate went on rank too. The sealed-exam answer-key exclusion and the opt-out and complaint exclusions are unchanged. The voice-profile distiller reads the same corpus, so edited sends also feed its nightly profile. An on gate adds the tag `e` to the draft's prompt version (`...+e`, `...+ev` with a pin; only while `SHADOW_FEWSHOT` and `SHADOW_DRAFT_VERIFY` are on, since otherwise no exemplars reach the prompt), a cohort of its own. Off, the miner query, the exemplar query and the prompt version are byte-identical to before. Sends nothing to a customer; rollback is to turn the gate off.
SMS prompt B1 (owner 2026-10-24, "go b1", "yes all"): `GATE_SMS_PROMPT_B1` — **ships DARK: off unless the value is `1`, `true` or `on`** (`gateEnvValue`), read at call time by `smsPromptB1Live()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`), and only while `GATE_SMS_REAL_ANSWERS` is also on. On, the texting AI's suggestion drafter (`server/services/sms-shadow-drafter.js`) changes in one prompt version: a missed-visit text gets OPEN TIMES sized for the missed visit's own service and offers 2-3 of them to rebook (none available keeps the apology plus the follow-up wording and escalation); a covered pest re-service text gets a FREE RE-SERVICE OPENINGS facts section (the free re-service booking page's own openings, read through `reserviceOpeningsFor` in `server/routes/reservice-public.js`) and offers 2-3 of them, with a person booking the pick (no automatic booking), asking where and how many only when there are none; new deterministic checks reject a reply that says a link, text, email, report, quote, proposal or photo is being sent without carrying it, that promises the office or a teammate will confirm, cancel, add, move, call, email or send something, that pairs the follow-up wording with anything but a reply, or that opens with Hi, Hello or Hey and a name when Waves texted in the last three days; the cancel sentence (2026-10-09 ruling) no longer says the team will confirm; and the latest finished visit's customer-safe notes reach SERVICE HISTORY up to about 1,200 characters, with its findings (`context-aggregator.js`). Stamps a fresh prompt version (`house_voice_v12_real_answers27_n`, `28_n` with `GATE_SMS_OFFERS_SCHEDULER`), a cohort of its own. Off, the prompt, facts and checks are byte-identical. Suggestion cards only: staff send them; sends, schedules and books nothing. Rollback is to turn the gate off.
SMS judge v2 (owner 2026-10-24, "yes all"): `GATE_SMS_JUDGE_V2` — **ships DARK: off unless the value is `1`, `true` or `on`** (`gateEnvValue`), read at call time by `smsJudgeV2Live()`. It changes measurement only and sends nothing: the AI that grades texting drafts against what staff really sent also answers "could the person who replied have sent the AI draft instead?" (`yes`, `yes_with_edit`, `no`, stored in `shadow_draft_judgments.could_send`) and counts false promises as `draft_unsafe` (a link, text, email, report, quote, proposal or photo "being sent" that nothing sends; the office or a teammate "will confirm, cancel, add, move, call or email"; "within the hour" turned into an arrival promise). Rows carry `judge_version` `j2` (migration `20261025000000_shadow_judgments_judge_v2`; NULL = the old judge, no backfill), and with the gate on the autonomy safety backstop (`fetchLiveJudgeSignals`) counts only `j2` rows so the stricter ruler never mixes with the old one. The sealed exam summary also counts `could_send_*`, and a sealed run graded by a different judge ruler than its baseline (or a run that mixes both) gets no significance verdict. Off = byte-identical judge prompt, parser output and rows; the drafter prompt and its `prompt_version` never change.
Estimate time picker, one opening per hour (dark): `GATE_ESTIMATE_SLOT_ONE_PER_HOUR` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time via `estimateSlotOnePerHourLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-25, before the second technician starts. Today the estimate picker keys its openings on the technician too, so with two technicians open at one hour the customer sees "Tue 9:00" twice with two technician names, the "Only N openings" badge counts both, and the repeats push other times out of the short list. On: `getAvailableSlots` in `server/services/estimate-slot-availability.js` keeps ONE slot per date and start time (`collapseSameStartSlots`), the way `/book` keeps one technician per `date|startTime`. The kept slot is the one the picker sorts first (`compareCustomerFacingSlots`: route-optimal, then the shortest detour to a nearby job, then the slot id), never by list order, and it stays a whole reservable slot with its own technician, `slotId` and signature (nothing is merged from the dropped slot). The collapse runs on the collision-checked pool before the day funnel, the cut and `firstDayAvailability`, so the badge count and every cut follow the collapsed list. Every reader of that list sees it: `GET /api/public/estimates/:token/available-slots`, `/find-slots`, the 409 "slot no longer available" refresh, one-tap purchase slots, and the estimate-time text drafts (`offerableEstimateSlots`, which feeds the SMS open times when `GATE_SMS_OFFERS_SCHEDULER` is on). The admin slot debug view (`getSlotDebug`) still lists every candidate. Reserve, extend and accept are unchanged: a held slot keeps its technician. The result cache key carries the gate state. Sends nothing to a customer by itself, but a text draft that lists estimate times lists one per hour once this is on. Off: byte-identical to before.
SiteOne order by email (dark): `GATE_SITEONE_EMAIL_ORDER` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time via `siteOneEmailOrderLive()` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy beyond the variable change). Owner 2026-10-26, "OK DO OPTION B": SiteOne's website blocks the order bot (headless Chromium gets `net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR` on the first page), so an owner emails the order instead. On: an open request on the Restock tab shows "Email order to SiteOne" (admins only). It opens a preview (To, Subject, the body, "Estimate before tax"); Send email goes out through SendGrid from `SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL` (contact@) to `SITEONE_ORDER_EMAIL`, cc `SITEONE_ORDER_CC` when set, and the request becomes ordered through the same path as the tab's mark-ordered action (`updateRestockRequest`), with `metadata.emailOrder = { emailId, sentAt, po, packages, itemNumber, to }`, so Receive works as today. Routes (`server/routes/admin-inventory.js`, `requireAdmin`): `GET` and `POST /api/admin/inventory/restock-requests/:id/siteone-email`; gate off answers 404; a refusal answers 409 with a `code`. The service is `server/services/procurement/vendor-order-email.js`, the ledger is `vendor_order_emails` (one row per request, UNIQUE): claim, stamp `send_attempted_at`, send, finalize on the claim token, as `price-match-draft.js` does. A request with a sent email never sends again; a failure before the stamp sends nothing and leaves the request open; an ambiguous failure after the stamp (5xx, network, timeout) leaves the row `sending` and nothing resends it (check SendGrid or SiteOne, then set the row `dismissed`); a 4xx rejection marks it `failed` and allows a retry. Send is bound to the preview: the preview returns a `version` (a hash of recipient, subject, body, packages, item number and pack), POST must carry it, and the claim recomputes it under the request lock; a changed price row, recipient or payment setting answers 409 `preview_changed` and the admin opens a fresh preview. An `auto_reorder` request is refused (409 `bot_can_order`) while the order bot would place it for real (`canAutoOrder` true and `SITEONE_BOT_DRY_RUN` not `true`), so SiteOne is never ordered twice; turn off `GATE_AUTO_ORDER_SITEONE` first. The dispatcher's claim (`claimRequest`, order-dispatch.js) also stands down, `skipped: 'email_order'`, for any request whose email is `sending` or `sent`, under the same request row lock the email claim takes (the one dispatcher change; no request without an email row behaves differently). Receive defaults to what the emailed packages hold, in the request's unit (301 lb asked of a 50 lb pack is 7 packages and 350 lb), kept in `vendor_order_emails.ordered_quantity` and read by `emailOrderedQuantityFor` (after the bot ledger's `orderedQuantityFor`); the preview `version` covers the estimate and that quantity too. A request whose email is `sent` or `sending` cannot be cancelled from the Restock tab (409 `email_order_out`, in `updateRestockRequest` and its preview), because a cancelled request would let the reorder sweep buy the product again; to cancel it, tell SiteOne, then set the email row `dismissed`. Refuses unless: the request is `open`, SITEONE_ORDER_EMAIL is set, no bot claim is `placing` (the `assertManualActionAllowed` guard) and no automatic order is out for the product, the SiteOne vendor row (code 1) has an account number, the product has an approved active SiteOne price row with an item number and a pack the converter reads (`vendorOrderQuantity`, so 300 lb of a 50 lb pack is 6), and the result is at least one package. The email: subject `Pickup order: Waves Pest Control, account <account>, PO <po>`; body asks SiteOne to prepare the order for pickup at the branch, gives the account and the PO (`WAVES-` plus the first 8 characters of the request id, upper case), one line `<packages> x <item number> <product> (<pack>)`, the payment line, and asks for a reply when it is ready. The estimate (packages x the price row's price) is shown to the owner only. Settings read at call time: `SITEONE_ORDER_EMAIL` (recipient, required), `SITEONE_ORDER_CC` (optional, comma separated), `SITEONE_ORDER_BRANCH` (default `Lakewood Ranch #238, 5115 Lena Rd`), `SITEONE_ORDER_PAYMENT` (`pickup`, the default: "We will pay at pickup."; or `card_on_file`: "Please charge the card on file ending <last4>.", which refuses unless `SITEONE_ORDER_CARD_LAST4` is exactly 4 digits). The order bot (`adapters/siteone.js`, `GATE_AUTO_ORDER_SITEONE`, `SITEONE_BOT_*`) and the dispatcher's ordering logic are unchanged. Emails a vendor, never a customer. Off: byte-identical to before (both routes 404, no button).

- **`GATE_ANNUAL_PLAN_DOCUMENTS`** — Default off; strict `true`, read at request time by `annualPlanDocumentsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`. Adds current signed-term annual-plan summaries to authenticated `GET /api/documents` and enables `GET /api/documents/annual-plan/annual_plan_<term_uuid>` for the owning account holder. When the summary lookup fails, the list leaves the summaries out and still returns every other document; the download route answers a retryable 503. Contacts receive no list entries; the auth middleware rejects their downloads with 403 ACCOUNT_HOLDER_ONLY. For authenticated holders, malformed, foreign and ineligible IDs return generic 404. Cancelled account holders retain this read under GATE_CANCEL_FLOW_V2 when the underlying term remains eligible. Uses the existing My Plan eligibility reader, shows current saved amounts and dates, and suppresses provisional installation dates. No notice, renewal decision, payment, public share link or customer communication is created. Kill: unset; the extra list query stops and the PDF route returns 404. Existing My Plan, decline and signed-agreement reads remain independent.

Late-arrival alerts, office cards only (owner approved 2026-10-27, gate audit 10-25; `server/services/no-show-detector.js`): `GATE_NOSHOW_DETECTOR` — **ships DARK: off unless set (`gateEnvValue`)**, read at call time. Off: nothing changes; the legacy late scan (`tech-late-detector.js`) and the unassigned-overdue detector keep running. On, the detector replaces both. A visit whose promised window started with no departure or arrival recorded gets: at 45 minutes (stage 1) a ping to the assigned tech **only if `NOSHOW_TECH_PING_ENABLED` is exactly `true` (default off, read at call time)**; at 150 minutes (stage 2) a tech notice plus a critical office card on the dispatch Action Queue; and, for a visit with no active field-dispatchable tech, an office card already at stage 1. So with only the gate on, an assigned tech gets no 45-minute ping, and the office card at 150 minutes and the no-tech card are exactly as before. Staff alerts only, no customer contact. Kill: unset the gate; `cleanupAfterDisable` clears the open cards.

Undo last manual payment (owner 2026-10-29, built before partial payments go live): `GATE_UNDO_MANUAL_PAYMENT` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`undoManualPaymentLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; also checked inside the writer `undoManualPayment` in `server/services/invoice-manual-payment-undo.js`). On: `GET` and `POST /api/admin/invoices/:id/undo-payment` answer, the invoice list sends `undoPaymentEnabled: true`, and the Invoices page shows "Undo payment" on a paid invoice with an off-card tender (cash, check, Zelle, Venmo, PayPal, other) recorded in the last 36 hours. Undo works only on a payment the office recorded with Record payment (not the Zelle notice reconciler, not Stripe), on the same Eastern day, with a typed reason, and only while nothing followed it: no receipt sent or queued, no customer message about the invoice, no review ask, no visit closeout, no billing-pause clear, no later payment, credit or refund, no ad-conversion upload, no annual prepay term, no payment plan closed, no invoice edit. Every rule re-runs under the invoice row lock. It puts the invoice back to the status it had (kept in the `invoice.manual_payment_recorded` audit marker that `recordManualPayment` now writes), keeps the `payments` row as status `canceled` with the undo note, reopens payment-failed admin bells the payment closed, re-arms the reminder sequence at its stored step (no step already sent fires again) and writes one `invoice_payment_undone` activity row plus an audit row. The payment must also carry its completion marker (`invoice.manual_payment_effects_done`), which `recordManualPayment` writes as its last step, after the reminder stop, billing-pause clear, review ask, closeout and receipt; until then Undo answers "This payment is still finishing; try again in a minute." A crash during those effects, or a lost marker write, therefore leaves that payment un-undoable here (the safe direction); a failed marker write never fails the payment. A receipt send and Undo are ordered by a transaction-scoped advisory lock per invoice (`lockInvoiceReceiptClaim` in `server/services/receipt-delivery-queue.js`, taken by every operator receipt claim and by Undo, never held across a send): a sender re-reads the invoice under it and sends nothing for a reopened invoice, and Undo sees a claim that committed first and refuses. The confirm sends the payment id the page was shown; if a different payment now sits on the invoice, Undo answers 409 and writes nothing. A payment recorded before this shipped has no marker and cannot be undone here. Off = both routes answer 404, the button is hidden, and recording a payment behaves exactly as before (the marker is written either way). Kill switch: unset.

A new residential lawn 9x series books one visit in each of nine fixed rounds a year: `GATE_LAWN_9X_ROUNDS` — **ships DARK: off unless set** (`1`, `true` or `on`), read at call time (`lawn9xRoundsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, `lawnRoundsSeriesPattern` (`server/services/recurring-appointment-seeder.js`) turns a residential lawn series sold as every-6-weeks or custom 42 days into `recurring_pattern = 'lawn_rounds_9'` with no interval, wherever a series' pattern is written: office New Appointment and make-recurring (`server/routes/admin-schedule.js`), the estimate accept (`server/services/estimate-converter.js`), the online booking wizard (`server/routes/booking.js`) and the seeder's own follow-up rows; the parent and every child of one series carry the same value. Tree and shrub, mosquito, pest, commercial lawn, lawn monthly and lawn bi-monthly are never translated, and a series already on file keeps its pattern. Quotes, the catalog link (`lawn_care_6week`) and the cadence words stay every-6-weeks. Annual prepay covers a rounds series: an estimate accept with annual prepay writes the rounds series and mints a term with `coverage_cadence = 'lawn_rounds_9'`, prepay on book of a rounds series mints the same term (no downgrade), and the term's covered visits (`coverageScheduleDates` in `server/services/annual-prepay-renewals.js`) sit on `lawnRoundDate(anchor, i)`, the dates the series is seeded with; payment-time seeding and gap-fill write `lawn_rounds_9` rows with no interval. A prepay term minted from Customer 360 with the every-6-weeks cadence still seeds a 42-day series. Off = every series is written exactly as before. **Size rule for moves** (owner 2026-10-31, `lawn_rounds_9` rows only, no gate: it keys on the row's pattern, so it is inert until a rounds series exists, and unsetting `GATE_LAWN_9X_ROUNDS` does not change existing rows): a date move of 7 days or fewer, inside the visit's round, moves only that visit (no sibling shift, no re-anchor; later rounds keep their dates). A bigger move, or a short move that crosses into the next round, re-anchors exactly as before. The size is measured from the visit's regular (cadence) date (`date_exception_cadence_date` when a date exception exists, else its own date), so repeated small moves cannot walk a visit across its round. `roundsMoveIsOneOff` in `server/services/lawn-rounds.js` is the one rule. It narrows the paths that make a move a series move: the rebooker choke point under `GATE_ADMIN_COLLECTIVE_MOVE` (dispatch drag, Edit modal date edit, staff SMS reply, IB tools, call makeup), Quick Move under `GATE_COLLECTIVE_SERIES_ANCHOR` (`server/services/rain-out.js`), the customer reschedule page and its SMS offers under `GATE_COLLECTIVE_SERIES_ANCHOR` (`server/routes/reschedule-public.js`; the page discloses `roundsOneOff` and the commit pins it, see `docs/public-route-contracts.md`), and the call reschedule apply. Every other pattern keeps the collective rules unchanged, the office "Reschedule series" action (`scope: 'series'`) always re-anchors, and auto-dispatch nudges are already single.

Lawn 9x neighborhood days (owner 2026-10-31; no gate of its own, every branch keys on the `lawn_rounds_9` row pattern, so it is inert until rounds series exist): a NEW rounds series is born on its area's shared anchor date, so neighbors are treated on one day in every round. Config: `system_settings` key `lawn_round_area_days` (JSON text or jsonb), read at call time by `server/services/lawn-area-days.js`, shape `{"parrish": {"label": "Parrish", "zips": ["34219"], "cities": ["parrish", "duette"], "anchor": "2027-01-26"}}`. Key absent = the code default (Parrish, anchor 2027-01-26 (Tuesday); Lakewood Ranch, ZIPs 34202/34211/34212, anchor 2027-01-28 (Thursday)). **`{}` is the kill switch** (no areas: every series keeps its own anchor); invalid JSON or a read failure also means no areas (logged once). Matching is ZIP first (first 5 digits of the series parent's `service_address_zip`, else the customer's zip), then city (parent `service_address_city`, else the customer's city; lower-cased, spaces collapsed), so a Lakewood Ranch ZIP wins over a "Bradenton" city; no match = no area (own anchor, as before). Two areas claiming one ZIP or city: the first key wins and a warning is logged. An anchor must be a real Monday-Friday date late in its round: in-round offset 30 or more and at least 3 days before the round's end, else that area is ignored (warning). Why: the weekday snap moves a date at most 3 days, so every round's area date sits at offset 27 or more; a visit in a round is on its last day at the latest, so the area date in the next round is 28 or more days after ANY visit of the round before, and area dates are 35, 42 or 49 days apart. There is no separate first-gap rule. The anchor is STAMPED on the series parent (`recurring_round_anchor_date`) at creation, so a later config edit does not move an existing series. Writers that use it: the seeder (`seedFollowUpsForParent` and its planner `planFollowUpSeedDates`: online booking wizard, estimate accept), the office New Appointment (`POST /admin/schedule`, picked property else customer address; its date plan is the one the insert loop writes), the office make-recurring spawn of `PUT /:id/update-details` and its pre-lock planner, and the annual-prepay gap-fill that creates a new parent (the invoice schedule lists the same dates). The office Edit-appointment cadence rewrite is the office changing the lawn day and keeps the visit's own date. A reseed or top-up of a series that already stores an anchor walks from that stored anchor (`seriesRoundAnchor`), so it keeps its area day. Moves of an existing series are not covered here.

Partial payments (owner 2026-10-29): `GATE_PARTIAL_PAYMENTS` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`partialPaymentsLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; checked inside the writer `recordManualPayment` in `server/services/invoice-manual-payment.js`). On: `GET /api/admin/invoices` sends `partialPaymentsEnabled: true`, and the Invoices page Add payment sheet shows an Amount received field (default: the amount still owed). `POST /api/admin/invoices/:id/record-payment` takes an optional `amount` in dollars. The writer compares it with what is owed on the LOCKED row (`invoiceAmountDue`: total less account credit less `invoices.amount_paid`): more is refused (400); equal is today's paid flip, now fenced to that figure; less is a PART payment. A part payment inserts one off-gateway `payments` row (status paid, `metadata.partial_payment`), adds the amount to `invoices.amount_paid`, stamps `payment_recorded_at`/`_by` (the signal the void, edit and settle guards read), leaves the status and the tender alone, retires an open Stripe session exactly as a full payment does, and writes the `invoice.manual_payment_recorded` marker (`partial: true`) and the `invoice.manual_payment_effects_done` marker Undo works from. It sends no receipt and does NOT stop the reminder sequence (reminders continue for the remainder); it skips the review ask, closeout, billing-pause clear, annual-prepay activation and plan completion. Refused (409, plain English, nothing recorded) for: an Auto Pay customer (`customerOnAutopay` with `failClosed`; an unreadable answer refuses), an invoice with an active payment plan, an annual prepay invoice, a payer-billed invoice (and the live self-pay re-resolution under the lock); refused (400) when the caller is the Zelle reconciler or notice Apply (`automated`, `expectedAmountCents`, `settlementFence`, `requireSelfPay`) or any other fenced caller; the Intelligence Bar card stays whole-balance only unless `GATE_IB_RECORD_PAYMENT_PARTIAL` is also on (the route drops any `amount` the bar carries, and a bar part uses an internal marker described under that gate). The paid flip of a part-paid invoice resets `amount_paid` to 0, books the REMAINDER as the ledger row, and the receipt reads the whole bill; every other paid flip does the same (Stripe card, saved card, ACH, combined pay, reconcile): their `total` rewrite adds `amount_paid` back, and an ACH debit still clearing keeps it. Credit that covers the rest closes the invoice `prepaid` and keeps `amount_paid` (the due stays 0). While `amount_paid` is above 0 the invoice cannot be voided, cancelled or have its amounts edited; a card refund of an invoice that was also part-paid is refused; a Zelle notice never matches it (`openSelfPayInvoicesByAmountDue` skips it) and the repricing and prepay-switch guards treat it as having money on it. Undo (`GATE_UNDO_MANUAL_PAYMENT`) also undoes a part: it subtracts that payment from `amount_paid`, cancels that ledger row, restores the notes and recorded-at/by, re-arms nothing, and refuses once the customer opened a payment page or a plan was set up; undoing the final payment restores `amount_paid` from its marker. Only the latest part can be undone. Off = the amount field stays hidden, the writer refuses a smaller amount, and recording a payment behaves exactly as before. Kill switch: unset.

Same-question check (content engine, owner 2026-10-30, "all"): `GATE_SAME_QUESTION_CHECK` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`sameQuestionCheckLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; the `sameQuestionCheck` entry is for the boot log only). Before a NEW supporting blog is drafted, autonomous-runner step 2d runs `evaluateSameQuestion` (`server/services/content/topic-targeting-gate.js`) on the corpus it already loaded: the brief keyword (else working title, else slug) is reduced to its topic words (served cities, Florida and regional words, the generic words of the topic gate and the framing words in `SQ_FRAMING_WORDS` dropped, singular folded), and a live post whose title, slug or primary keyword holds ALL of them is the owner (most hits first, then URL). A one-word topic blocks only when it is not a broad pest or service word (`SQ_BROAD_TOKENS`: termite, ant, roach, lawn, ...) and at most 3 live posts hold it; a longer topic is ignored when more than 3 posts hold it. Refreshes are never judged. **Off = shadow:** the verdict is stored on `autonomous_runs.topic_targeting_result.same_question` (`mode: shadow`, `would_block`, `owner_url`, `tokens`) and the row goes on to the writer. **On:** the row is skipped by design (`topic_targeting:TOPIC_SAME_QUESTION_LIVE`) and one `same_question_refresh` row is queued for the owner page (`server/services/content/same-question-refresh.js`): a page-only `refresh_existing_page` whose `unanswered_queries` holds the question, so the refresh agent adds one answer block in ANSWER-GAP MODE. The row passes every refresh gate: protected pages (checked at queue time and by the runner), the shared page-edit lock and in-flight check, the question route fence and 28-day page cooldown in `opportunity-queue` (`AEO_QUESTION_GAP_COOLDOWN_DAYS`), the own-run PR fence, the terminal-writer flow, and the quality gates. A shadow-mode blog run (`SHADOW_MODE_NEW_SUPPORTING_BLOG`) queues nothing. One row per (owner page, question words); a done, skipped or claimed row is never reopened. Off also stops queued `same_question_refresh` rows from being claimed and releases their page reservation; they expire after 60 days. No migration (`opportunity_queue.bucket` is free text). Replay over recent runs, read-only: `node server/scripts/same-question-replay.js --days=30 [--all] [--json]`. Kill switch: unset.

Portal inbox (owner 2026-10-31, option A): `GATE_PORTAL_INBOX` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`portalInboxLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). On, Admin > Communications gets a **Portal** tab (admin only) listing what customers asked for inside the customer portal and nobody answered: portal chat hand-offs (`ai_escalations` still `pending` whose `agent_sessions` row has `channel = 'portal_chat'`; hidden once their admin bell alerts are all marked Done) and customer service requests that are not `resolved`, `closed` or `cancelled` and not made by staff (`source = 'admin'`). The tab shows the last 14 days (`GET /api/admin/portal-inbox`, count in `GET /api/admin/portal-inbox/summary`). Older open items sit under one Older line; `POST /api/admin/portal-inbox/close-older` closes them in one transaction (chats `dismissed`, requests `resolved`), closes their open admin bell alerts and writes one audit event. It sends NO email or text. Mark handled uses the existing `PUT /api/ai/admin/escalations/:id` and `PATCH /api/admin/requests/:id`; with the gate on, a chat set to `resolved` or `dismissed`, and a request that moves to `resolved`, also close that item's open admin alerts. The request PATCH still sends its usual update email. The escalation update also now answers 404 for a missing row and 400 for an unknown status, gate on or off. Off = the tab is hidden, the new routes answer `{ enabled: false }` or 404, and the two update routes close no alerts. Admin only; sends nothing to a customer by itself. Code: `server/routes/admin-portal-inbox.js`, `client/src/pages/admin/PortalInboxTabV2.jsx`. Rollback: unset.

Messenger inbox (owner 2026-10-31): `GATE_MESSENGER_INBOX` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`messengerInboxLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = kill, no redeploy). **The owner turns it on**, because it adds a customer-message path (a Facebook message from a customer becomes an admin bell and a reply leaves from the page). The Facebook API calls are free. Send an owner test message to the page first, wait 3 minutes, check the thread and the bell, then reply once from the tab. On, a `*/3 * * * *` job (`messenger-inbox`, `pollMessenger` in `server/services/messenger-inbox.js`) reads the page's Messenger conversations with `FACEBOOK_ACCESS_TOKEN` (a page token with `pages_messaging`) and `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID` into the unified `conversations` / `messages` store (channel `facebook_messenger`, thread `messenger:<psid>` on endpoint `messenger:<page id>`, message key `twilio_sid = 'fb:' + 48 hex of sha256(Graph message id)`, the Graph id kept in `metadata.graph_mid`). The cursor is `system_settings` key `messenger_inbox_cursor` (the newest conversation `updated_time` processed); the first run reads the last 183 days, marks imported customer messages read unless Facebook shows that conversation unread, and rings only those. Each later thread with a new customer message and no newer reply rings ONE admin bell (`dedupeKey` `messenger-thread:<conversation id>`, re-rings on each new message); a reply seen in Facebook or sent from the tab marks it Done. Admin > Communications gets a **Messenger** tab (`GET /api/admin/messenger/summary|threads|threads/:id`, `POST .../read|reply`; staff roles, a technician sees only threads linked to a customer on their route). A reply goes through Facebook's Send API (`messaging_type RESPONSE`) only within 24 hours of the customer's last message (`409 outside_window` after that; the tab shows a Reply in Facebook link). Attachments are stored as `[Photo]` / `[Attachment]` text; no media is downloaded. Off = the job does nothing, the summary answers `{ enabled: false }`, the other routes 404, the tab is hidden. It replaced the unused Twilio Messenger route and its `GATE_SOCIAL_INBOX` gate (both deleted). Meta ends this app's data access 2026-11-25 unless renewed. Rollback: unset.

Data hygiene review surface: `GATE_DATA_HYGIENE_UI` — **default off in production** (`true` in dev), strict opt-in `=== 'true'` in prod, read at boot into the gates map as `dataHygieneReviewUi` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`; the Railway restart applies a change; unset = kill). On, the Agents hub shows the Hygiene tab (the hub probe `GET /admin/agents/control/hub` reports `features.hygiene`) and `/api/admin/data-hygiene/*` answers admin requests. Off, the tab is absent (`?tab=hygiene` falls back to Overview) and every route on that API (list, metrics, scan, approve, reject, reveal, revert) answers 404, so to review or revert a proposal turn the gate back on. It does not touch the scanner cron, extraction, auto-apply or sensitive reveal, which keep their own gates (`GATE_DATA_HYGIENE_SCANNER`, `GATE_DATA_HYGIENE_EXTRACTION`, `GATE_DATA_HYGIENE_AUTO_APPLY`, `GATE_DATA_HYGIENE_REVEAL`). Sends nothing to a customer.

Quote wizard same-person match (owner 2026-10-31): `GATE_QUOTE_SAME_PERSON_MATCH` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`quoteSamePersonMatchLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = off = kill, no redeploy) by `findExistingCustomerByContact` in `server/routes/public-quote.js`. Before this gate, a typed phone that matched 2 or more customer rows linked nothing, so each wizard rerun inserted a new `customers` row (on 10-30 one person ran it 5 times and added 5 rows). On, a phone matching 2 to 10 live rows is resolved by `resolveSamePersonCluster` in `server/services/customer-dedupe.js` when every row has a compatible name and a matching street, unit, ZIP or city with each other row and with the typed contact (the same parsed street key, equal unit keys from the shared address normalizer (`unitLineValueKey`: Apt, Unit, Suite and # are one dwelling designator, Bldg, Floor, Space and Lot stay, so "Bldg 2" never equals "Apt 2"; inline units are peeled by `splitStreetLineUnit`), and equal ZIPs or, when a ZIP is blank, equal non-empty cities; an unparseable street keeps today's behavior). The wizard links the lead and estimate to the row the nightly duplicate sweep would keep. Any mismatch, or more than 10 rows, keeps the old result: a new row. A single phone match, the email match and the pre-pricing rodent lookup are unchanged. Sends nothing. Rollback: unset it.

Route engine summary (owner 2026-10-31, "do #1 first"): `GATE_ROUTE_ENGINE_SUMMARY` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read at call time (`routeEngineSummaryLive()` in `server/config/feature-gates.js`; unset = off = kill, no redeploy) by `server/routes/admin-route-scorecard.js`. On, `GET /admin/route-scorecard` (itself behind `GATE_ROUTE_SCORECARD`) also returns an `engine` block from `server/services/scheduling/route-engine-summary.js`, and the Day Scorecard panel on the Dispatch page shows one line above the table. The block covers the last 7 ET nights of night auto-dispatch runs (`triggered_by` cron or catch_up): per night `finished` (a `completed` run), `running` (still in progress, never shown as a failure), `with_errors`, `failed` or `no_run`; moves made (audit rows `changed`); visits the per-run cap held back (distinct visits with `MAX_CHANGES_REACHED`) and how many of those moved on a later ET night (a hold and a move in the same night, such as a cut-off run and its catch-up, does not count). Counts only: no drive-time figure, because the engine's per-move `drive_saving_minutes` is the detour it expected to avoid against a future day that was often still nearly empty (on 2026-10-31 the last 7 nights summed to 949 minutes, more than a week of modeled driving). The cap shown is `config_snapshot.maxChangesPerRun` of the latest run. A summary error is logged and the payload carries `engine: { unavailable: 'summary failed' }`; the scorecard itself still answers. Reads only; sends nothing. Off = the scorecard payload is byte for byte today's, no `engine` key. Rollback: unset it.
SiteOne deals bell (dark): `GATE_SITEONE_DEALS_DIGEST` — **ships DARK: off unless exactly `true`**, read when the server boots into `siteOneDealsDigest` (`server/config/feature-gates.js`) and checked by the cron in `server/services/scheduler.js`, which also needs `cronJobs`. Owner 2026-10-31, plan A. On: Monday 8:00 AM ET (`0 8 * * 1`) `runSiteOneDealsDigest` (`server/services/procurement/siteone-deals-digest.js`) reads the last 7 days of the `emails` table (the contact@ Gmail sync) and keeps mail from siteone.com or a product-maker domain (BASF, Envu, Bayer, Syngenta, Corteva, FMC, Nufarm, Albaugh, MGK, Zoecon, Control Solutions, Quali-Pro, PBI Gordon, Adama, AMVAC, Liphatech, Ensystex, Valent, LESCO; the exact domain or a subdomain, so `siteone.com.evil.example` never matches) that Gmail's own Authentication-Results shows authenticated as that domain (`hasAlignedAuth` strict reader; a missing or unreadable header is not a deal) and that is not quarantined, labelled SPAM or TRASH, or classified spam, and that looks like a deal: a deal word (promo, special, flyer, early order, EOP, rebate, price increase, floor pricing, cash discount, discount, % off, sale, trade-in, points, deal, offer, savings, price match) in the subject, or in the body with an attachment, or two different ones in the body. Invoices, order and cart mail, eWallet, auto-replies, statements, payment and password mail are never deals. It rings ONE admin bell (category `system`, `bell: true`, headline `Inventory — review N SiteOne deals this week`, link `/admin/communications#tab=email`) through `raiseAdminAlert`; the full text lists one line per deal, newest first: date, sender, subject, `deadline <date or not stated>`, `your products: <names or none named>` (active `products_catalog` names that the mail names, up to 6). The deadline is the earliest explicit date in the mail on or after the day it arrived and within 180 days, ignoring quoted reply history. The bell dedupes on `siteone-deals:<Monday of the ET week>` with `refreshOnDedupe`, so a rerun rewrites the week's bell instead of adding one. Zero deals: no bell, one log line. The query is bounded (Codex r2): SQL narrows by sender domain, a dkim/spf pass, and held-back rows, reads body excerpts only, and reads at most 300 emails (a warning is logged and a line is added to the bell when the cap is reached). Costs nothing: plain string rules over rows already in the database; no model call, no paid API, no network; reads `emails` and `products_catalog` and writes only the bell; sends nothing to anyone. Rollback: unset `GATE_SITEONE_DEALS_DIGEST` (or set it to `false`) and restart; an existing bell stays until someone marks it done.
